title: Convert test_agent_spec_matrix.py to an introspection-driven generator + pyagentspec capability registry
description:
Replace the hand-written CELLS dict with a mechanically-derived cross product, so the matrix's completeness stops depending on a human remembering every axis (the exact failure that missed the oracle merge_prompt cell).

Steps:
1. Build a small capability registry classifying every concrete pyagentspec node primitive under pyagentspec.flows.nodes (LlmNode, Agent, ApiNode, ToolNode, MapNode, BranchingNode, StartNode/EndNode, InputMessageNode) by its _get_inferred_inputs family: text-scan/placeholder-coupled, structural/subflow-based, or unconstrained-echo. Add a completeness assertion: the registry's key set must equal the actual set of concrete Node subclasses pyagentspec ships (walk the module), so a new primitive pyagentspec adds later fails loud instead of silently going unclassified. This registry is a SHARED artifact -- the AST guard task (blocked by this one) must reuse it, not re-derive its own copy.
2. Enumerate neograph's own axes via introspection, not hand-typed lists: Node.mode via typing.get_args(Node.model_fields['mode'].annotation); each Modifier subclass (Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator) via Modifier.__subclasses__(), and for each, its discriminating field values pulled from the field definitions themselves (Oracle's merge_fn XOR merge_prompt in particular -- this must come from reading Oracle's field/validator definition, not be copy-typed into the test).
3. Cross (1) x (2), restricted to the combinations _agent_spec.py's actual dispatch code (_lower_node, _lower_oracle, _lower_each, _lower_loop, _lower_operator) claims to support. Diff that generated set against tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py's current CELLS keys; the diff itself should be a loud assertion failure (missing cell = failing test), not a silent gap.
4. Run it. Expect NEW red/failing cells to surface beyond the two that were already xfailed (m57mn fixed those) -- e.g. Oracle(merge_prompt=...) combinations, Oracle+agent/act mode, and possibly others nobody has named yet. Do NOT fix them in this task -- that is the next task's job. This task's acceptance criterion is: the generator runs, is provably exhaustive against both closed enumerations, and produces an accurate list of every currently-red cell (record that list in this issue's notes/design field for the next task to consume).

Reference: docs/design/agent-spec-oracle-inputs-2026-07-25-architecture-retrospective.md section 4.3 and the conversation that refined it (matrix-first sequencing rationale).
design:
## Core Invariant
The matrix's completeness must be MECHANICALLY DERIVED from two closed enumerations — pyagentspec's concrete flows.nodes.Node subclass set AND neograph's own introspected axes (Node.mode Literal, ModifierCombo, Oracle merge_fn XOR merge_prompt) — with a LOUD partition/completeness assertion on EACH axis, so any new pyagentspec primitive OR new neograph combo fails a loud test instead of silently going uncovered (the failure that let the Oracle merge_prompt cell escape).

## Implementation Plan (refined post-review)

1. **Shared capability module tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py — two-tier, importorskip NOT at top (M2).**
   - Tier A (always importable, NO pyagentspec dependency): the hand-authored name-string -> family classification dict, e.g. NODE_FAMILIES: dict[str,str] mapping 'LlmNode'->'text_scan', 'AgentNode'->'structural', 'ToolNode'->'echo', ... for all 14 concrete flows.nodes classes. Pure str->str data, no import of pyagentspec. Downstream neograph-tjupj imports THIS name-only and stays always-on (pure-AST guard must not become extra-gated/skipped — north-star: a structural guard silently not running is the forbidden silent seam).
   - Tier B (lazy, pyagentspec-dependent): a function all_concrete_flow_node_classes() that imports pyagentspec inside the function body, walks recursive Node.__subclasses__() filtered by inspect.isabstract, and a assert_registry_complete() that asserts set(NODE_FAMILIES) == {c.__name__ for c in walk}. Callers (the matrix) invoke these under their OWN pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec'). Module top does NOT importorskip.

2. **Enumerate neograph axes by introspection + LOUD partition on the modifier axis (M1).**
   - modes = typing.get_args(Node.model_fields['mode'].annotation) -> ('think','agent','act','scripted') ('raw' correctly excluded — it is raw_fn-set, not a mode Literal).
   - Modifier axis: derive from ModifierCombo (12 members). Define TWO explicit sets: SUPPORTED = {BARE,EACH,ORACLE,LOOP,OPERATOR} (what _lower_construct_item lowers) and UNSUPPORTED = {PORTAL + the 6 fusion combos that RAISE}. Add a LOUD partition assertion: set(ModifierCombo) == SUPPORTED | UNSUPPORTED AND SUPPORTED & UNSUPPORTED == empty — so a future combo added to the enum forces classification (mirrors step 1's registry-completeness assertion). Do NOT hand-type a single 'exclude PORTAL/composed' expression with no completeness check.
   - Oracle config discriminator: read field names off Oracle.model_fields ({merge_fn, merge_prompt}); fails loud (KeyError) on rename. Add a code comment noting the residual drift risk (won't auto-pick a future 3rd mutually-exclusive merge_* variant added to the XOR validator — modifiers.py:445-457) (LOW).

3. **Generate the cross product with a pinned builder contract (LOW).**
   - Axes: mode x modifier x oracle-config x input-shape. SUPPORTED modifier x 4 modes; ORACLE x 4 modes x {merge_fn,merge_prompt} x {single,dict}; input-shape {single,dict,+context(Each only)}. Also emit expected-RAISE cells for each UNSUPPORTED combo (pins 'restricted to what dispatch claims').
   - Pin the generic cell-builder contract explicitly: for each (mode,shape) document the @node kwargs it emits and the prompt CONTENT each LLM mode injects to trigger/avoid _check_placeholder_inputs (think: prompt=+model= referencing an input; agent/act: tools= + input-referencing system_prompt; oracle merge_prompt: gen_outputs-referencing prompt; scripted: no prompt). Reuse register_scripted / tests/schemas.py / conftest reset; extend schemas.py only if a model is missing.

4. **Make BOTH completeness diffs loud, key-spaces reconciled (M3).**
   - Express the 8 prior GREEN CELLS as their explicit NEW-scheme cell-ids (a hand-written PRIOR_GREEN: set[str] of new-scheme ids) and assert PRIOR_GREEN <= generated-key-set (true coverage check, not an old-vs-new string coincidence that fails or passes vacuously). Confirm input-shape (single AND dict) is crossed for ORACLE too (old had oracle-single AND oracle-dict), not just mode x config.
   - Keep the per-family GREEN baseline passing; mark surfaced RED cells with xfail(strict=True) carrying the neograph-i7k7j blocker id (mirrors existing _XFAIL_EXPORT/_XFAIL_ROUND_TRIP at lines 201-203) so the suite stays green-when-run yet records every red cell. strict=True makes a later fix XPASS->fail, a correct ratchet for i7k7j. Do NOT fix red cells (that is neograph-i7k7j). Record the final red-cell list (Findings families 1-5) as the handoff.

5. **Run** uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py and confirm: registry completeness passes, ModifierCombo partition passes, PRIOR_GREEN-coverage diff passes, baseline green, red cells xfail-recorded. Also run the core suite subset for test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py WITHOUT the agent-spec extra to confirm importing the shared module (Tier A) does NOT skip the always-on AST guard.
notes:
## Findings

### Reuse targets (do NOT re-derive)
- **pyagentspec closed enumeration**: walk `pyagentspec.flows.nodes` concrete `Node` subclasses. The module's own `__all__` == the 14 concrete classes (verified): AgentNode, ApiNode, BranchingNode, CatchExceptionNode, EndNode, FlowNode, InputMessageNode, LlmNode, MapNode, OutputMessageNode, ParallelFlowNode, ParallelMapNode, StartNode, ToolNode. The completeness assertion should compare the registry keyset against the reachable-concrete-subclass walk of `pyagentspec.flows.node.Node` (recursive `__subclasses__()`, filter `inspect.isabstract`), which yields exactly these 14 — matching `flows.nodes.__all__`.
- **neograph mode axis**: `typing.get_args(Node.model_fields['mode'].annotation)` -> `('think','agent','act','scripted')` (node.py:164). NOTE: 'raw' is NOT a mode Literal value — raw is expressed via `raw_fn` being set (rejected by `_reject_unrepresentable_fields`), so the closed mode axis is exactly these 4.
- **neograph modifier axis**: `Modifier.__subclasses__()` -> `[Oracle, Each, Operator, Loop, Portal]` (modifiers.py). BUT the per-node lowering dispatch (`_lower_construct_item`, _agent_spec.py:641) only handles `ModifierCombo` values {BARE, ORACLE, EACH, LOOP, OPERATOR} and raises for PORTAL/composed combos. Portal is exported at the *construct* level to a Swarm (`_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm`), not via a per-node combo — so Portal is OUT of the per-node cross product. Use `ModifierCombo` (modifiers.py:65) + `classify_modifiers` (modifiers.py:107) to define the supported modifier axis; do not hand-type {BARE,ORACLE,EACH,LOOP,OPERATOR}.
- **Oracle config discriminator (the §4.3 missing axis)**: `Oracle.merge_fn` (modifiers.py:430) XOR `Oracle.merge_prompt` (modifiers.py:428), both `str | None`. The XOR is enforced by Oracle's model_validator (modifiers.py:445-457: "not both", "exactly one required"). Pull the two config-variant values FROM these field names / validator, not copy-typed into the test.

### pyagentspec `_get_inferred_inputs` family classification (verified from source)
- **text-scan / placeholder-coupled** (scans text/config for `{{ }}` via `get_placeholder(_properties)_from_json_object`; real inputs MUST appear as jinja placeholders): **LlmNode** (prompt_template), **ApiNode** (url/data/params/headers), **InputMessageNode** (message), **OutputMessageNode** (message).
- **structural / subflow-based** (inputs read from a nested flow's StartNode / subflow / agent — structural, not text): **AgentNode** (agent.inputs), **FlowNode** (subflow.inputs), **CatchExceptionNode** (subflow.inputs), **MapNode** (module-level `_get_inferred_inputs` -> `iterated_`-prefixed sub-flow StartNode inputs), **ParallelMapNode** (same), **ParallelFlowNode** (union of subflows' inputs).
- **unconstrained-echo** (inputs just echo self.inputs/tool.inputs/outputs; no coupling): **ToolNode** (tool.inputs), **BranchingNode** (single StringProperty branch-name), **StartNode** (self.inputs or outputs), **EndNode** (self.inputs or outputs).

### Which primitives the exporter actually constructs (dispatch claims)
- `_lower_node` (_agent_spec.py:214): mode think->LlmNode(placeholder-coupled), agent/act->AgentNode+Agent composite (placeholder-coupled via `_make_agent`->`_check_placeholder_inputs` on system_prompt), scripted->ToolNode(echo, safe).
- `_lower_oracle` (:355): variant per node.mode — think->LlmNode, scripted->ToolNode, **agent/act->raises ConfigurationError "no lowering yet" (:405)**; merge per config — merge_prompt->LlmNode(placeholder check on gen_outputs, :440), merge_fn->ToolNode(:459).
- `_lower_each`(:500)->MapNode wrapping single-node sub-Flow; `_lower_loop`(:540)->BranchingNode+back-edge over `_lower_node(body)`; `_lower_operator`(:613)->BranchingNode+InputMessageNode over `_lower_node(primary)`. EACH/LOOP/OPERATOR all delegate their inner node to `_lower_node`, so they inherit its full 4-mode dispatch.
- Exporter NEVER constructs: ApiNode, CatchExceptionNode, OutputMessageNode, ParallelFlowNode, ParallelMapNode (registry still must classify them for completeness; they are simply "not a lowering target").

### Currently-RED cells (surfaced by prototype cross-product; for neograph-i7k7j to fix — do NOT fix here)
Baseline GREEN (all scripted-mode / merge_fn, the existing 8 CELLS): none-single, none-dict, each-single, each-context, oracle-single, oracle-dict, loop-single, operator-single (16 passing = 8 x {export, round-trip}).
NEW RED families surfaced by adding the mode + oracle-config axes:
1. **think-mode + any real input -> RED**. Root cause: @node dict-form inputs give a Property title `{upstream}.{field}` (e.g. `prod.a`, _agent_spec.py:208); pyagentspec's placeholder scan can't match a DOTTED title to a jinja `{{ }}` (dots illegal in placeholders), so even a prompt literally containing `{{ a }}` still fails `_check_placeholder_inputs`. Verified.
2. **agent/act-mode + any real input -> RED**. Same coupling via `_make_agent`'s `_check_placeholder_inputs` on the system_prompt.
3. **Oracle scripted-mode + merge_prompt (with real gen_outputs) -> RED**. `_lower_oracle` merge branch builds an LlmNode and runs `_check_placeholder_inputs(oracle.merge_prompt, gen_outputs)` (:440); dotted/unreferenced output titles fail. This is the exact §4.3 / 4th-site gap.
4. **Oracle think-mode (variant) + real inputs -> RED** (variant LlmNode placeholder check, :391).
5. **Oracle agent/act-mode -> RED** (explicit ConfigurationError "Oracle+agent/act export has no Agent Spec lowering yet", :405).
Leaf LLM nodes with NO inputs stay GREEN (nothing to placeholder-couple).

- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:154 `_check_placeholder_inputs` — the single placeholder-coupling gate; reuses pyagentspec's own `get_placeholders_from_json_object`. This is the "root invariant" the retro §4.4 wants framed generally.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **CLARIFICATION (task wording vs reality)**: the task lists "Agent" as a pyagentspec node primitive, but `pyagentspec.agent.Agent` is an `AgenticComponent`, NOT a `flows.nodes` Node. The flow-node analog is `AgentNode`. The registry keyset must be the 14 concrete `flows.nodes` Node subclasses (which includes AgentNode, ApiNode, CatchExceptionNode, FlowNode, OutputMessageNode, ParallelFlowNode, ParallelMapNode — several NOT named in the task's parenthetical), or the completeness walk will not match. Not a contradiction — just resolve "Agent" -> "AgentNode" and include the full 14.
- **Shared-registry location**: it must be importable by BOTH test_agent_spec_matrix.py and the future AST guard (neograph-tjupj) — a new test-support module (alongside tests/fakes.py, tests/schemas.py), e.g. tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py, NOT inline in the matrix file. It references pyagentspec (optional [agent-spec] extra), so it (and its importers) must `pytest.importorskip("pyagentspec")` — the matrix already does (line 42); the AST guard currently reads source text only and will need to add the importorskip when it consumes the registry.
- **'raw' is not a mode Literal** — do not add it to the generated mode axis; raw is `raw_fn`-set and is rejected pre-lowering. Introspecting the Literal is the correct closed source.
- **PORTAL must be excluded from the per-node modifier cross** — it lowers at construct level to a Swarm. `Modifier.__subclasses__()` includes it; restrict via `ModifierCombo`/dispatch-supported set, or the generator produces cells `_lower_construct_item` cannot build.
- **Completeness must be a LOUD assertion, not a skip**: registry-key-set == walked-subclass-set, and generated-cell-set == CELLS-keys (missing = failing test), per steps 1 and 3. Do NOT xfail/skip the diff.
- **Do NOT fix red cells here** (neograph-i7k7j owns that). The dotted-title placeholder coupling (families 1-4 above) is the systemic red root; record it accurately, leave it red.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-00447)

Pattern: hand-typed enumeration of a closed axis (Node.mode Literal, ModifierCombo, Oracle merge_fn/merge_prompt XOR, pyagentspec node classes) copied into test/code instead of introspection/enum-derived, so completeness silently rots (the CELLS-matrix failure that missed the Oracle merge_prompt cell).

Disease shape: SYNTACTIC (grep-findable literal forms) -> single-executor scan; no multi-agent targeted scan / .claude/code-review artifact required.

Scan commands (reproducible):
  grep -rns -E '\b(CELLS|MATRIX|_CELLS|CASES)\b\s*[:=]\s*\{' tests
  grep -rns -E 'mode (in|not in) \(' src/neograph
  grep -rns -E '(BARE|ORACLE|EACH|LOOP|OPERATOR)\b.*(BARE|ORACLE|EACH|LOOP|OPERATOR)' src/neograph tests

## Architect Review (neograph-u2ncp.4, independent)

Verified against source: pyagentspec flows.nodes.__all__ (14) == recursive concrete-subclass walk of flows.node.Node (filter isabstract) exactly; Node.mode Literal == ('think','agent','act','scripted') with raw correctly excluded; ModifierCombo has 12 members; _lower_construct_item (_agent_spec.py:641-724) supports {BARE,EACH,ORACLE,LOOP,OPERATOR} and RAISES ConfigurationError for PORTAL + all 6 fusion combos; test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py currently has NO pyagentspec import (pure AST source parse, runs always-on in core suite). Reuse targets (register_scripted, schemas.py, conftest reset, importorskip) all confirmed real.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The completeness discipline is applied to ONLY ONE of the two closed enumerations the Core Invariant names. Step 1 rigorously guards the pyagentspec axis (set(registry)==walked-subclasses, loud). But step 2/3 handles the ModifierCombo axis by 'derive from ModifierCombo, exclude PORTAL/composed' with NO equivalent completeness assertion. ModifierCombo has 12 members; the plan silently uses 5 and drops 7. A future neograph combo added to the enum would be neither supported-nor-excluded and go UNCOVERED with no failure -- the exact disease this ticket exists to kill, reproduced on the neograph half of the cross product. Suggestion: add a loud partition assertion set(ModifierCombo) == SUPPORTED | UNSUPPORTED (both explicit), mirroring step 1's registry-completeness assertion, so a new combo forces classification. Bonus: generate expected-raise cells for the UNSUPPORTED combos to pin 'restricted to what dispatch claims'.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Shared-registry module design puts pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec') at module TOP (mirroring the matrix). But the downstream consumer neograph-tjupj is a PURE-AST source-parse guard that today imports no pyagentspec and runs always-on in the core suite. If tjupj imports this module to reuse the classification (the mandate), tjupj's structural guard becomes SKIPPED whenever the agent-spec extra is absent -- a structural guard silently not running is precisely the silent seam the north star forbids. The plan forces a dilemma: extra-gate the guard (weaken it) or re-derive a copy (violates reuse). Suggestion: structure the module so the hand-authored classification mapping (name-string -> family) is importable WITHOUT triggering the importorskip at module top, and confine the pyagentspec-dependent completeness walk/assertion to a lazily-invoked function. Then tjupj consumes the mapping name-only and stays always-on; the matrix calls the walk under its own importorskip.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The 'loud diff' completeness check (step 4) compares mismatched key spaces. Prior CELLS keys are old-scheme ('none-single','oracle-dict', all scripted-mode/merge_fn) while the generator emits a NEW mode x modifier x oracle-config x input-shape id. A literal string superset assertion either always-fails or, if loosely reconciled, passes VACUOUSLY -- and would not catch e.g. a dropped oracle input-shape axis (old had oracle-single AND oracle-dict). This is the reviewer-flagged 'completeness could pass while silently missing an axis' hole. Suggestion: express the 8 prior cells as their explicit new-scheme cell-ids and assert those ids are members of the generated set (true coverage check), not a format coincidence; confirm input-shape (single/dict) is crossed for ORACLE too, not just mode x config.

- [LOW] Finding: The parameterized cell-builder is the bulk of the work and is underspecified. The RED predictions depend on specific prompt CONTENT (think needs prompt=+model= referencing an input to trigger _check_placeholder_inputs; agent/act needs tools= + input-referencing system_prompt; oracle merge_prompt needs a gen_outputs-referencing prompt). The plan says 'reuse existing shapes' but the current builders are all scripted-mode with no prompt content. Suggestion: pin the generic builder's contract -- how each (mode,shape) maps to @node kwargs and what prompt content each mode injects -- so the RED/GREEN split is reproducible and not left to implementer guess.

- [LOW] Finding: Oracle XOR pair is read as {merge_fn,merge_prompt} by name off Oracle.model_fields. This fails loud on a rename (KeyError) which is good, but model_fields also carries 4 other merge_* fields and a hand-named pair won't auto-pick up a future 3rd mutually-exclusive variant added to the XOR validator (modifiers.py:445-457). Acceptable pragmatic compliance (fully deriving the XOR set from validator AST is disproportionate); just note the residual drift risk in a comment.

- [LOW] Confirmations (survived attack): xfail(strict=True) + recording the red-cell list in notes DOES satisfy acceptance ('generator runs, produces accurate red-cell list, suite stays green') -- and strict=True makes each fixed cell XPASS->fail, a correct ratchet for i7k7j; blocker id neograph-i7k7j is correct; the decision to NOT fix red cells is correct; mode axis via typing.get_args (raw excluded) is the right authoritative source; reuse of register_scripted/schemas/conftest over reinvention is sound; the task-wording 'Agent'->'AgentNode' clarification is correctly resolved to the 14 concrete flows.nodes classes.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

title: from_agent_spec(): import Agent Spec Flow/Agent -> Construct (primitive-level)
description:
Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s5, s7. Add from_agent_spec() next to load_spec in src/neograph/loader.py. Parse an Agent Spec dict/YAML (Flow: start_node, nodes[], control_flow_connections[], data_flow_connections[]) into a Construct via existing _build_construct patterns.

MAP: StartNode/EndNode -> Construct input/output ports; LlmNode -> think node; ToolNode/ApiNode -> scripted; AgentNode/Agent -> agent/act; FlowNode -> sub-Construct; MapNode/ParallelMapNode -> (primitive) node reading a collection; BranchingNode + control-flow cycles -> branch/loop primitives. DataFlowEdge(source_output->destination_input) -> Node.inputs dict entries. Handle name-based mode (data_flow_connections=None) by matching on the state-bus names.

EXPLICITLY primitive-level: no modifier (Oracle/Each sugar) recovery -- import yields the expanded form (doc s6). Layer rule: loader.py only; do NOT touch node.py/construct.py IR. Blocked by gate + type-layer tasks. Three-surface parity where applicable.
design:
## Core Invariant

`from_agent_spec()` must never silently reconstruct a modifier (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator) whose per-group `neograph/*_spec` marker no longer matches the actual flattened primitives around it -- exactly the symmetric counterpart of `to_agent_spec()`'s "never silently drop, fail loud" invariant (`_agent_spec.py` module docstring): where export fails loud rather than emit a lossy primitive, import fails loud (or falls back to primitive-level for that group, with a WARN) rather than silently reconstruct a modifier that diverges from the file on disk.

## Implementation Plan

1. Add `from_agent_spec(flow_or_dict)` as a new public function in `src/neograph/loader.py` (sibling of `load_spec`), function-locally importing pyagentspec via a guard identical in shape to `_import_agent_spec_flow_classes()` (`_agent_spec.py:59`) / `_import_agent_spec_property_classes()` (`spec_types.py:225`) -- reuse one of those two if importable without a cycle, otherwise copy the exact guard shape (do not invent a new error message format).
2. Walk `Flow.nodes` + `control_flow_connections` + `data_flow_connections` in `start_node`-reachable topological order. For each primitive node, dispatch by its Agent Spec class the INVERSE of `_lower_node`'s dispatch in `_agent_spec.py:147-188`:
   - `LlmNode` -> `Node(mode="think", prompt=node.prompt_template, model=node.llm_config.model_id, inputs=..., outputs=...)`
   - `ToolNode`/`ApiNode` -> `Node(mode="scripted", scripted_fn=node.tool.name, inputs=..., outputs=...)` (name-only; factory binds at compile/lint time, same contract `_resolve_tool` already documents)
   - `AgentNode` -> FAIL LOUD (`ConfigurationError`), symmetric with the export-side fail-loud in `_agent_spec.py:164-180`, until `neograph-i3zsh.1` defines the real shape
   - `FlowNode` -> recurse `from_agent_spec(node.subflow)` to get a sub-`Construct`, matching `_lower_construct_item`'s `Construct -> FlowNode` direction (`_agent_spec.py:431-434`)
   - `StartNode`/`EndNode` -> map to the enclosing `Construct.input`/`.output` boundary ports (mirrors doc s5's structural table), not emitted as Nodes
3. For each node's `inputs`/`outputs` Property list, call `spec_types.agent_spec_properties_to_types(properties, name)` then `lookup_type(name)` to get the Pydantic class -- reuse verbatim, do not re-walk Property trees (`spec_types.py:310`/`:398` are the monopoly, per that module's own docstring).
4. Reconstruct modifiers ONLY when the per-group marker is present AND validated against the actual primitives (doc s6a's three-way discipline: markers absent -> plain primitive import; markers present and matching -> reconstruct `Oracle`/`Each`/`Loop`/`Operator` via `item | Oracle(**oracle_spec)` etc. exactly like `loader._apply_modifiers` already does for the declarative Spec path; markers present but diverged -> WARN + primitive-level for that group only). Recognize the exact marker keys `to_agent_spec` emits (`neograph/modifier`, `neograph/group_id`, `neograph/oracle_spec`, `neograph/each_spec`, `neograph/loop_spec`, `neograph/operator_spec`, `neograph/branch`) -- do not invent new key names.
5. For `Swarm`/handoff-mode Agent Specs: **BLOCKED on the doc-vs-bead-notes contradiction flagged in Findings** -- confirm with the user/task owner which behavior is current (ratified reject-with-error in `agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md` §3a, vs. the 2026-07-14 RE-SCOPE note on this bead proposing import onto a Portal mesh) before implementing either path. Do not silently pick one.
6. For `RemoteAgent`/`A2AAgent` nodes: BEST-EFFORT lower to a name-bound scripted `Node` (factory supplied at bind time) + log a WARNING, per ratification §3b. Stash endpoint/auth metadata for potential re-export, but this is best-effort, not lossless -- no fail-loud needed here (doc already sanctions the downgrade).
7. Reconstruct `_BranchNode` sentinels (`neograph/branch` marker, or an unmarked `BranchingNode` with no modifier marker) via `_ir_branch.py`'s existing `_BranchNode`/`_BranchMeta` constructors -- the one place this task may need something beyond `loader.py`+existing IR constructors (mirrors the sanctioned-new-IR-capability precedent in CLAUDE.md, but likely no new field is needed since `_BranchNode` already exists; confirm before adding anything new to `_ir_branch.py`).
8. Assemble the final `Construct(name=flow.name, input=..., output=..., nodes=[...])` from the reconstructed item list, in Flow topological order -- exactly the tail of `_build_construct` (`loader.py:152-156`).
9. Do NOT touch `node.py`/`construct.py`/`_construct_validation.py`/`factory.py`/`modifiers.py` for this task -- every new line lives in `loader.py` (plus, if genuinely unavoidable, `_ir_branch.py` for branch reconstruction, per point 7).
10. Write/extend tests in a new `tests/test_agent_spec_import.py` (sibling naming to `test_agent_spec_export.py`) covering: plain primitive import (no markers, foreign spec), marker-present lossless reconstruction per modifier (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator), marker-diverged fallback+WARN, AgentNode fail-loud, FlowNode recursion, RemoteAgent best-effort+WARN. Full round-trip (export->import->compile equivalence) tests are `neograph-csdcl`'s job, not this atom's -- but this atom's own tests must still prove `from_agent_spec` in isolation.
notes:
Import MUST read + VALIDATE markers (doc s6a), not blindly trust them. If Flow.metadata['neograph/source'] present: deserialize, re-lower, diff vs the actual flattened Flow. Match -> reconstruct abstract modifiers (Oracle/Each/Loop) losslessly. Diverged (hand-edited) -> primitive-level import, reconstruct only groups whose per-group markers still match, WARN on touched modifiers. No markers -> plain primitive import (foreign Agent Spec).
RE-SCOPE (KEYMAKER shipped, epic neograph-t1f7z, 2026-07-14): Agent Spec Swarm/handoff import is no longer a 'reject' — neograph now has a native handoff mesh (Keymaker mode (a), Command(goto)+destinations=). from_agent_spec() can faithfully import Agent Spec handoff-mode flows onto a Keymaker mesh (v1: sibling-node peers at one construct level; cross-boundary is deferred neograph-do0d9). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md.
RE-SCOPE (export-first, 2026-07-15): from_agent_spec is now ROUND-TRIP-FAITHFUL — it reads the x-neograph reconstruction metadata that to_agent_spec (i3zsh) emits, rebuilding the SAME modifiers (Oracle/Each/Loop/Portal) that compile to LangGraph, so neograph->AgentSpec->neograph is lossless. Primitive-level import (no metadata) stays the FALLBACK for external/third-party specs. Therefore this DEPENDS ON i3zsh (export defines the contract the reader consumes). nkjv9 still required for the type layer.

Export currently FAILS LOUD on agent/act (no lossy placeholder to import back), so there is nothing to round-trip yet for that mode. ## Findings

- **Reuse target for the builder plumbing**: `_build_construct` / `_build_node` / `_build_sub_construct` / `_apply_modifiers` / `_resolve_tool` in `src/neograph/loader.py` (lines 122-283). `from_agent_spec()` should produce the SAME intermediate shape these already consume -- i.e. build a typed `Spec`/`NodeSpec`/`ConstructSpec` (or construct `Node`/`Construct` instances directly the way `_build_node` does) rather than inventing a second assembly path. Concretely: map each Agent Spec primitive node to a `Node(...)` the same way `_build_node` does (mode/inputs/outputs/prompt/model/scripted_fn/tools), then hand the list to `Construct(name=..., nodes=[...])` exactly like `_build_construct`'s tail. Do NOT re-derive fan-in/type-registry logic -- reuse `lookup_type` / `spec_types.agent_spec_properties_to_types` (see below) and `_resolve_tool`/`Tool`.
- **Reuse target for the type bridge**: `spec_types.agent_spec_properties_to_types(properties, name)` (`src/neograph/spec_types.py:310`) is the EXACT import-direction primitive nkjv9 built for this task -- converts a `list[Property]` to a registered Pydantic model. `from_agent_spec()` must call this per node's `inputs`/`outputs` Property lists and then `lookup_type(name)` to get back the class, mirroring how `_build_node` in loader.py already does `lookup_type(node_spec.outputs)`. Do not hand-roll a second Property-walker; `_property_to_field_type` is the monopoly (spec_types.py:244).
- **Reuse target for the export-side mapping (read backwards)**: `src/neograph/_agent_spec.py` (`to_agent_spec`, i3zsh, 596 lines) is the CANONICAL, already-ratified mapping table in the *opposite* direction. Every marker key/shape `from_agent_spec` must recognize is defined there: `metadata["neograph/modifier"]` in `{"oracle","each","loop","operator"}`, `neograph/group_id`, `neograph/oracle_spec` (`n`, `models`, `merge_prompt`|`merge_fn`, `merge_model`), `neograph/each_spec` (`over`,`key`,`on_error`), `neograph/loop_spec` (`when`,`max_iterations`,`on_exhaust`), `neograph/operator_spec` (`when`), `neograph/branch` (bool, `_BranchNode` sentinel marker). Copy these key names verbatim -- `from_agent_spec` is the inverse of `_lower_oracle`/`_lower_each`/`_lower_loop`/`_lower_operator`/`_lower_construct_item`, not a fresh design.
- **Import-guard pattern to copy verbatim**: `_import_agent_spec_flow_classes()` in `_agent_spec.py:59` and `_import_agent_spec_property_classes()` in `spec_types.py:225` -- both function-local `try/except ImportError -> ConfigurationError.build(hint="install with: uv sync --extra agent-spec ...")`. `from_agent_spec()` needs the identical guard (own `_import_agent_spec_flow_classes`-equivalent, or literally import the one in `_agent_spec.py` since loader.py may import from `_agent_spec.py` -- check for import-cycle risk before duplicating).
- **Docs vs bead notes CONTRADICTION on Swarm import (NEEDS USER INPUT)**: `docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md` §3a (a ratified GATE doc, ratified 2026-07-13) says: *"Swarm -- REJECT with a clear error (do NOT best-effort lower)... `from_agent_spec()` raises a `NeographError` naming `Swarm` as unsupported-on-import... No lossy lowering."* But `01i0g`'s own bead NOTES (RE-SCOPE, 2026-07-14, post-dating the ratification) say Keymaker/Portal shipped and *"Agent Spec Swarm/handoff import is no longer a 'reject' ... `from_agent_spec()` can faithfully import Agent Spec handoff-mode flows onto a [Portal] mesh (v1: sibling-node peers at one construct level; cross-boundary is deferred neograph-do0d9)."* These directly conflict: the ratified design doc says reject-with-error, the newer bead note says import-onto-Portal-mesh. **NEEDS USER INPUT: which wins -- update the ratification doc to match the RE-SCOPE, or revert the RE-SCOPE note and keep the reject-on-Swarm behavior?** Until resolved, the safe default for THIS task (research only) is to document both paths in the design below and let the implementer pick per whichever is still current at write-time -- but this must be settled before `from_agent_spec` ships Swarm/handoff handling.
- **Agent/act mode is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for now**: bead's own GATE (2026-07-22) says `from_agent_spec` must not claim round-trip fidelity for agent/act until `neograph-i3zsh.1` lands (export currently FAILS LOUD -- `_agent_spec.py:164-180` -- rather than emit a lossy `ToolNode` placeholder, so there is nothing produced on export to read back for that mode yet). `from_agent_spec` should therefore reject (fail loud) any `AgentNode` it encounters on import too, symmetric with export, until i3zsh.1 defines the real `AgentNode`+tools shape.
- **Metadata round-trip is VERIFIED, not a blocker**: `docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md` line 124 flagged `metadata["neograph/source"]`/marker survival through `to_dict`/`from_dict` (incl. disaggregation) as UNVERIFIED-blocking. It is now proven: `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::test_flow_and_node_metadata_survive_plain_to_dict_from_dict_round_trip` and `::test_metadata_survives_disaggregated_component_round_trip` (lines 108, 125) pin this. Safe to build the marker-based reconstruction on top of it.
- **RemoteAgent/A2AAgent -- BEST-EFFORT lowering per ratification §3b**: map to a name-bound scripted/raw `Node` (factory supplied at bind time, same contract as any ToolNode/ApiNode import) with a WARNING logged; endpoint/auth-shape rides in `metadata['neograph/remote_agent']` for re-export. Mirror the `_resolve_tool`/name-only pattern already in `loader.py:159`.
- **Layer discipline**: per doc §7 (also CLAUDE.md), `from_agent_spec()` belongs in `loader.py` ONLY. It must build IR via `Node(...)`/`Construct(...)` construction exactly like `_build_node`/`_build_construct` do (NOT touch `node.py`/`construct.py`/`_construct_validation.py`/`factory.py`/`modifiers.py`). `_BranchNode` reconstruction (for `neograph/branch` marker or an unmarked `BranchingNode`) is the one place that may need a helper from `_ir_branch.py` (`iter_with_arms`/`_BranchNode` are already the neutral IR home per its own docstring) -- import from there, do not hand-roll a second sentinel.
- **`iter_with_arms` (`_ir_branch.py:70`)** is the arm-aware walk `to_agent_spec` uses to iterate `construct.nodes`; there is no import-direction analog yet -- `from_agent_spec` will need to go the other way (flat Agent Spec node/edge list -> `Construct.nodes` list, reconstructing `_BranchNode` where markers indicate a Loop/Operator/plain branch). Since IR-level `_BranchNode` construction is the one place `from_agent_spec` may need something beyond `loader.py`+existing constructors, confirm with `_ir_branch.py`'s public surface before writing new IR-touching code -- if a helper is missing there, that is the ONE sanctioned exception (mirrors the Portal precedent in CLAUDE.md), not a reason to touch `construct.py` directly.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Marker STALENESS (doc s6a): if a Flow's per-group marker (`neograph/oracle_spec` etc.) is present but the actual primitives around it no longer match (hand-edited Flow), `from_agent_spec` must NOT blindly trust the marker and reconstruct a modifier that doesn't match reality -- diff first, warn and fall back to primitive-level import for that group only (symmetric with the export side's fail-loud discipline).
- Name-based (implicit) data-flow mode: when `data_flow_connections=None`, Agent Spec expects components to read/write a shared name-based variable space -- this is structurally neograph's state bus already (doc s2), so `from_agent_spec` in that mode should map node I/O names directly onto `Node.inputs`/`outputs` dict keys without needing explicit `DataFlowEdge`s, exactly mirroring the "Agent Spec's name-based mode == neograph's state bus" framing in the interop doc.
- Composed modifiers (e.g. Each+Oracle together) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for export per `_agent_spec.py:469-474` (`ModifierCombo` other than BARE/ORACLE/EACH/LOOP/OPERATOR raises); `from_agent_spec` should mirror this exclusion rather than attempt to reconstruct combos the exporter itself never produces.
- Callable-valued fields (`raw_fn`, `skip_when`/`skip_value`, callable `Loop.when`, Oracle merge hooks, `renderer`, Portal `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel`, callable `gate_tools_when`) have NO Agent Spec representation by construction (export already fails loud on these) -- `from_agent_spec` never needs to reconstruct them, only needs to leave the corresponding Node fields unset/None on import (there is nothing to recover).
- Three-surface parity is N/A here in the usual sense (this is a NEW entry point producing IR, not modifying an existing IR-consuming surface) -- but the produced `Node`/`Construct` instances must be indistinguishable from what any of the three existing surfaces would produce, so downstream compile()/validation see no special-cased shape.

title: Batch 2: State-bus Protocol + adapter — eliminate 13 Any entries from Cluster 3
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §5, §7
- docs/design/any-audit-analysis-2026-05-20.md Cluster 3 + Cluster 8 (8 is subsumed)

## Cluster 3: State-bus polymorphism (BaseModel | dict) repeated everywhere

**Entries (13)**: 12 `state` params + the duplicate `_state_get` in factory.py + _oracle.py

**Hypothesis**: State is sometimes a compiled Pydantic model (`compile_state_model` output) and sometimes a dict (sub-graph dispatch / isolated execution / fakes). Every helper that reads from state takes the union. Twelve functions repeat the same `BaseModel | dict[str, Any]` semantic with `Any`. Pattern is broad-interface-no-abstraction.

## Structural fix

```python
# src/neograph/_state_bus.py (new module)
class StateBus(Protocol):
    def get(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any: ...

def adapt_state(state: BaseModel | dict[str, Any]) -> StateBus:
    if isinstance(state, dict):
        return _DictStateBus(state)
    return _ModelStateBus(state)
```

Helpers take `state: StateBus` and never see the union. `_state_get` becomes obsolete. Single boundary `Any` remains on the return (user values, §5).

## Risk
**Highest of all batches.** State-access semantics are load-bearing across the dispatch layer. Property-based Hypothesis tests should pin adapter equivalence with current behavior.

## How to verify

**Test file**:
1. `tests/test_state_bus_adapter.py` (new) — unit tests on `_DictStateBus` / `_ModelStateBus` parity
2. `tests/hypothesis/test_state_bus_equivalence.py` (new) — property-based test: for arbitrary state shape, `_state_get(state, key) == adapt_state(state).get(key)` (current behavior preserved)
3. `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoAnyInIRPublicAPIs` — `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 13 entries

**Test type**: unit + hypothesis-property-based + structural-guard regression
**What it exercises**: adapter preserves identical semantics under both dict and BaseModel state shapes; allowlist shrinks
**Expected initial state**: write unit + property tests FIRST; remove 13 entries from `ANY_ALLOWLIST`; guard fails on 13 sites
**Persistence**: all three test sets stay in the suite

Order: write tests FIRST → fail → implement `_state_bus.py` adapter → migrate 13 call sites → re-run → all pass.

## Acceptance
- `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 13 entries
- `factory.py:_state_get` and `_oracle.py:_state_get` removed (or reduced to one-line `adapt_state` call)
- Hypothesis property tests on state-bus equivalence pass
- Three-surface parity: declarative + @node + programmatic
- `make quality` green
close_reason: StateBus Protocol + adapt_state() introduced in src/neograph/_state_bus.py; 12 helpers migrated to StateBus, 4 _dispatch.py context_data tightened to dict[str, str] | None, _state_get duplicates removed from factory.py + _oracle.py; 9 property-based Hypothesis tests pin adapter equivalence; 19 allowlist entries removed; all 1770 tests pass + make quality green

title: Verify Operator's Agent Spec HITL-pause EXPORT target against pyagentspec before to_agent_spec lowering
description:
## What
Before writing Operator's to_agent_spec() export lowering, VERIFY the real Agent Spec HITL-pause target against pyagentspec 26.1.2 itself (not the neograph repo).

## Why (from swcy1 ratification + independent review, 2026-07-13)
The swcy1 ratification corrected a real design-doc error: Operator(when=) is a conditional HITL interrupt (LOWER), NOT a DIRECT BranchingNode — grounded in _wiring.py:951-961 (single linear check node; interrupt()+HUMAN_FEEDBACK; checkpointer-required; no fork, both paths reconverge). GO on that. BUT the independent reviewer flagged: the ratification's proposed EXPORT target — 'BranchingNode(gate) -> InputMessageNode -> reconverge' — asserts InputMessageNode == interrupt()/pause semantics with ZERO grounding (InputMessageNode is an Agent Spec concept; grep of neograph finds nothing, correctly). It also contradicts master-synthesis line-78's GAP characterization. So the corrected target is itself UNVERIFIED.

## Deliverable
Verify against pyagentspec 26.1.2 (the installed package / its docs / source): what Agent Spec node ACTUALLY expresses 'interrupt the flow, checkpoint, retrieve human input, resume'? Is it InputMessageNode, a BranchingNode+InputMessageNode pair, or is there NO faithful HITL-pause primitive (=> Operator export is a documented GAP, marker-only round-trip)? Pin the real target with pyagentspec evidence, THEN correct docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md (:22, :132-137), 00-master-synthesis.md (:38, :78), and agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md §5. Do NOT apply the ratification's unverified InputMessageNode correction to the master docs until this is done.

## Scope
Blocks ONLY the to_agent_spec() EXPORT task (Operator lowering). The import path (from_agent_spec), structural mappings, Oracle/Each/Loop LOWER, Swarm-reject/RemoteAgent-best-effort, and the [agent-spec] dep decision are all RATIFIED and unblocked. Not blocking the import/type-layer children.
design:
## Core Invariant
Every Agent-Spec EXPORT lowering must be traceable to a REAL pyagentspec primitive verified against the installed package (source/docstring/reference-adapter), never asserted from the neograph side alone or from a prior design doc's unverified claim — a lowering target is only 'ratified' once grounded in pyagentspec 26.1.2 itself.

## Implementation Plan
1. Do NOT introduce a new IR node/class for 'Operator export'. Reuse the existing to_agent_spec() lowering machinery (task neograph-i3zsh scope) and, for `Operator(when=cond)` specifically, emit a **composite of two existing pyagentspec classes** already imported/available via the `pyagentspec` dependency: `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.BranchingNode` (conditional gate) feeding `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.InputMessageNode` (the actual pause/interrupt/resume node) on the pause branch, with both the post-InputMessageNode path and the bypass branch wired via `ControlFlowEdge` to a single shared reconverge downstream node — mirroring the existing Loop lowering pattern already documented for `BranchingNode` (back-edge/continue/done) in `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md` §5, since that is the closest existing precedent for 'condition -> BranchingNode -> divergent then reconverge' in this codebase's own design docs.
2. **Corrected wiring (per architect review MEDIUM finding — do NOT ship 'zero extra plumbing'-style language)**: `BranchingNode.mapping` is `{INPUT-VALUE-string : BRANCH-NAME-string}` — the mapping VALUE is a branch LABEL, not a node name, and `ControlFlowEdge.from_branch` selects on that label. The precise composite is: `BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH})` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH) -> InputMessageNode` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH) -> reconverge` (unmapped inputs fall to `DEFAULT_BRANCH`, which is exactly the bypass path — no second explicit mapping entry needed for the false case). **Explicit coercion obligation, must be stated in the doc correction, not hidden**: neograph's `Operator.when` yields a Python truthy `should_pause` (bool or message string) via a `DataFlowEdge` into the BranchingNode's input — but the mapping key is a literal string (e.g. `"true"`). Without an explicit boolean-to-string-key coercion step, a Python `True`/truthy value will NOT match the literal key and the composite would silently ALWAYS take `DEFAULT_BRANCH` (bypass), never pausing — a silent fail-soft degradation this project's North Star forbids. neograph-i3zsh MUST either implement the coercion explicitly (render `should_pause` to the exact mapping-key string before the DataFlowEdge) or the doc must mark this as a documented GAP if left unhandled — it must NOT be presented as automatic/zero-plumbing.
3. Populate InputMessageNode.outputs with a single StringProperty (its ONLY supported shape per `_validate_outputs_have_right_format`) and map neograph's `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK` to that output on import/round-trip. Interrupt-payload asymmetry to document explicitly in the doc correction: the pyagentspec reference LangGraph adapter lowers InputMessageNode to `interrupt("")` with the prompt carried by the STATIC `message:` field, whereas neograph's Operator passes `interrupt(should_pause)` — a DYNAMIC runtime value. neograph-i3zsh must treat a dynamic-payload Operator as an explicit, DOCUMENTED lossy-export edge case (flag in metadata, do not silently coerce) rather than extending InputMessageNode past its schema. Additionally: a callable `Operator.when=` is a separate export GAP (14-adapters.md already notes callable-valued fields do not serialize) — the doc correction should add a one-line annotation for this alongside the message-payload GAP, since only the string/registered-condition case is handled by the composite above.
4. Before writing the exporter code for neograph-i3zsh, update the FOUR doc locations identified by research + codebase-scan to remove the now-resolved TBD/unverified language, using the CORRECTED composite wording from step 2 (not 'zero extra plumbing'): `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md` (:22 BranchingNode row phrasing + :132-137 Operator section, replace 'Status: TBD' with the composite target + coercion-obligation note), `docs/design/agent-spec-api/00-master-synthesis.md` (:78, annotate InputMessageNode gap as import-direction-only), `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md` (:174, replace 'exact lowering TBD' with the composite target + point at this bead as the verification record), and `docs/design/agent-spec-api/14-adapters.md` (:142, same 'gated edge (exact lowering TBD)' row in the Export-lowering table -- found by the codebase-wide disease scan, NOT in the ticket's originally-cited file list; must be corrected alongside the other three or the doc set is left internally inconsistent). Do this doc correction as its own preparatory step, separate from and before the neograph-i3zsh exporter implementation, per this task's explicit scope boundary. Do NOT edit `docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:101,103` — it is a historical decision record whose proposal is now confirmed correct, not a live doc that goes stale.
5. When neograph-i3zsh actually implements the exporter, the construction call sites to copy are the pyagentspec-internal reference patterns already inspected in this research (not neograph in-repo code, since neograph has zero existing InputMessageNode/BranchingNode-into-pyagentspec call sites): `InputMessageNode(name=..., message=..., outputs=[StringProperty(title='user_input')])` per the class docstring in `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/inputmessagenode.py`, and `BranchingNode(name=..., mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH}, inputs=[...])` + separate `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=...)` wiring per `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/branchingnode.py`'s docstring example (mapping value is a branch label, per the step-2 correction — not a node name).
notes:
## Findings
- VERIFIED against real pyagentspec 26.1.2 (pip-installed in scratchpad venv, not just grepped from the neograph repo). Source: `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/inputmessagenode.py`, `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/branchingnode.py`, `pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_node_execution.py`, `pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_langgraphconverter.py`.
- **InputMessageNode IS the faithful HITL-pause primitive — now grounded, not asserted.** Its own docstring: "This node interrupts the execution of the flow in order to wait for a user input, and restarts after receiving it." More decisively: pyagentspec's OWN reference LangGraph adapter (`InputMessageNodeExecutor` at `_node_execution.py:568-576`) lowers `InputMessageNode` to `langgraph.types.interrupt("")` — the exact same LangGraph primitive neograph's `Operator` uses (`_wiring.py:1097`, `human_input = interrupt(should_pause)`). `_langgraphconverter.py:419-421` also treats `InputMessageNode` presence as the signal requiring `uses_interrupt=True` / checkpointer, matching Operator's checkpointer-required semantics. This closes the reviewer's ZERO-grounding flag from swcy1.
- **BranchingNode has NO interrupt/pause semantics of any kind** — confirmed by source: it is a pure Dict[str,str]-keyed router (`mapping: Dict[str, str]`), input value → branch name, default branch on miss. No message, no wait, no resume. This CONFIRMS (does not contradict) the swcy1 ratification's core correction that `Operator(when=)` is NOT itself a `BranchingNode` — the pause logic cannot live in BranchingNode; it can only live in InputMessageNode.
- **Corrected export target for `Operator(when=cond)`**: `BranchingNode(gate on cond)` -> true-branch: `InputMessageNode` -> reconverge node; false-branch: reconverge node directly (bypass). This is a COMPOSITE of two real, grounded primitives — BranchingNode supplies the CONDITIONAL gating (Operator's `when=` is conditional; InputMessageNode alone is unconditional/always-pauses), InputMessageNode supplies the actual pause/interrupt/resume semantics. Neither node alone is faithful; the pair is. This differs from the swcy1 ratification's literal wording ('BranchingNode(gate) -> InputMessageNode -> reconverge') only in that the wording is now CORRECT/grounded rather than asserted without evidence — no change to the shape itself is needed.
- Multiple control-flow edges converging on one downstream node (the 'reconverge' node) is a standard, unrestricted pattern in pyagentspec — `Flow`'s pydantic validators (`flow.py`) place no in-degree cap; `BranchingNode`'s own docstring example converges two branches into two separate `EndNode`s (not a shared node, but nothing structurally prevents targeting a shared node instead).
- **neograph's OWN Operator lowering is a single linear node with an in-node conditional interrupt call** (`_wiring.py:1082-1103`, `_add_operator_check`): one node `{node_name}__operator` wired via a single `graph.add_edge` (no fork, no conditional_edges), whose body does `if should_pause: interrupt(should_pause)`. This reconfirms swcy1's LOWER (not DIRECT BranchingNode) classification of Operator on the neograph-IR side; it says nothing about the EXPORT-target shape on the Agent-Spec side, which is the composite BranchingNode+InputMessageNode above.
- Currently `InputMessageNode` is NOT modeled anywhere in neograph — grep of `src/neograph` confirms zero references (matches the existing GAP-AS row in `02-flows-nodes.md`). The export lowering (task neograph-i3zsh) will be the FIRST code to construct an `InputMessageNode`, so there is no existing in-repo call site to copy; the pyagentspec docstring's own `Flow` example (in `inputmessagenode.py`) is the best available template for correct field usage (`outputs=[StringProperty(title=...)]`, `message=` for the prompt appended before pausing).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Operator's `interrupt(should_pause)` payload is the CONDITION VALUE (whatever `should_pause` evaluates to, often a bool or message string), not a fixed prompt string. InputMessageNode's `message:` field is a static/templated string (Optional[str], Jinja-style `{{var}}` placeholders via `get_placeholder_properties_from_json_object`), not an arbitrary runtime payload. If `Operator.when` needs to carry a dynamic message into the interrupt payload, that has no 1:1 InputMessageNode field — likely needs to render `should_pause` into `message` via a DataFlowEdge from the BranchingNode's condition output, or accept lossy flattening (documented GAP, not silent).
- InputMessageNode ALWAYS returns a single string output (`DEFAULT_OUTPUT = 'user_input'`, enforced by `_validate_outputs_have_right_format` — exactly one output, type=string). neograph's `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK` is untyped/Any at the interrupt() call site (`_wiring.py:1097-1098`) — if piarch's real usage of `Operator` ever expects structured (non-string) human feedback, the export loses type fidelity to a bare string. Verify against actual `Operator` call sites in piarch before finalizing the lowering's output-type contract.
- Doc contradiction to fix (not a NEEDS USER INPUT — this task's own deliverable): `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md:22` current text 'Operator compiles to check node + conditional edge' for the BranchingNode row is imprecise post-verification — Operator compiles (on the neograph IR side) to a check node with an UNCONDITIONAL edge in, and an IN-NODE conditional interrupt call, not a graph-level conditional edge (confirmed by `_add_operator_check`, which calls `graph.add_edge`, not `add_conditional_edges`). The EXPORT-side BranchingNode+InputMessageNode composite is the Agent-Spec-side reconstruction of that in-node condition, not a mirror of neograph's own wiring shape.
- `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md:132-137` ('Status: exact lowering still TBD in implementation') and `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md:174` ('gated edge vs explicit check node — TBD') are now RESOLVABLE by this research — should be updated to the BranchingNode+InputMessageNode composite, TBD removed.
- `00-master-synthesis.md:78` InputMessageNode/OutputMessageNode row ('interrupt() not first-class in neograph... GAP-AS') describes the neograph-side gap correctly (still true — neograph has no InputMessageNode-equivalent IR node) but should be annotated that the EXPORT path can still SYNTHESIZE a faithful InputMessageNode from Operator, i.e., the GAP is import-direction / native-modeling only, not export-direction.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-03djs)

  grep -rln "InputMessageNode" docs/ src/ tests/ website/

title: Low-severity catalog: describe_type recursive-ref + tuple rendering, --setup 4x re-import, dead has_llm_ref param, ConfigDict standardization, source-mutating-guard finally hygiene (review 080726_2107)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md Low table, bundled for one small molecule:
1. describe_type.py:241 — a recursive model renders a dangling 'Tree' reference with no hoisted declaration, and tuple[A,B] renders as [A] (drops the second member). Both are render-correctness bugs in the LLM-facing schema notation: TDD both (recursive model round-trip; heterogeneous tuple) and fix the hoisting/tuple arms.
2. __main__.py — the --setup module is re-imported and re-executed 4x per check run (masked by idempotency guards); import once, thread the module object.
3. verify.py:55 — vestigial has_llm_ref param threaded through recursion, never read; delete.
4. Standardize model_config on ConfigDict (two styles live: dict-literal vs ConfigDict — pick ConfigDict, mechanical).
5. TQ-03 follow-through: a random-order run once surfaced a MUTATION-PROBE line in real naming.py (checked-in source verified CLEAN — leftover from an interrupted source-mutating guard test). AUDIT every source-mutating guard/verification test for finally-restore discipline; add a conftest session-end assertion that git-tracked src/ is unmodified after the suite (the cheap permanent alarm).
6. CON-04 quote-style on 'configurable' — verify ruff format (now enforced) already normalized it; if residue remains, fix.
Gates y5ux.
notes:
Item 1 (describe_type render bugs): TDD'd 6 tests in tests/test_renderers.py (TestDescribeTypeRenderCorrectness). Fix (a) recursive models: pass-1 now tracks the ancestor path and records back-edges in a 'recursive' set that is force-hoisted regardless of hoist policy, so the bare back-edge reference always has a 'type Name = {...}' declaration. Fix (b) tuple: added a dedicated tuple arm in _render_type that renders all positional members ([A, B, ...]); variadic tuple[X, ...] and bare tuple still fall through to single-element [X].
Item 2 (__main__.py --setup 4x re-import): cmd_check imports the setup module ONCE and threads the module object into _load_config/_load_template_resolver/_load_known_template_vars/_load_compile_kwargs (signatures changed to take setup_mod). Updated test_cli.py TestLoadConfig callers.
Item 3 (verify.py): deleted vestigial has_llm_ref param from _walk + its call-site arg (never read). grep confirms zero references remain.
Item 4 (ConfigDict): converted 3 dict-literal model_config sites to ConfigDict(...) — forward.py, node.py, construct.py — adding 'from pydantic import ConfigDict' where missing. All 14 model_config sites in src now use ConfigDict. mypy clean.
Item 5 (TQ-03): audited all source-mutating guard/verification tests (test_guards_*, test_verify, etc.) — every mutation-probe writes to tmp_path; NONE mutate real src (checked-in source clean, confirmed). Added session-scoped autouse conftest fixture _src_tree_unmodified_by_suite: hashes (git diff + git status --porcelain) of src/neograph at session START, re-checks at END, fails on delta. Delta-based (snapshot vs snapshot, not vs HEAD) so it tolerates the legitimate uncommitted batch. Proven to detect a mutation and stay green after restore. Degrades to no-op if git unavailable.
Item 6 (CON-04): no-op confirmed — all single-quoted 'configurable' occurrences are inside comments/docstrings/error-hint strings (ruff format never rewrites those); real code uses StateKeys constants.

title: Checkpoint schema validation — refuse resume on incompatible state instead of silent pydantic coercion
description:
## What

When a construct's @node output types change between runs (field
renames, new Pydantic fields, wrapper type swaps), LangGraph's
checkpointer silently coerces old-format state into the new models.
Pydantic fills in defaults for missing fields and ignores extras.
The next `run(graph, input=..., config=config_with_checkpointer)`
reads the coerced-but-broken state as "complete" and returns
`duration_s=0.0, total_cost=0` — no crash, no warning, no work done.

From the user's perspective: pipeline "succeeded" but produced nothing.
The persisted artifacts are from the previous run (pre-schema-change).
Impact analysis, downstream consumers, and observability all report
success on ghost state.

## Concrete repro from piarch

piarch landed three UC pipeline refactors (piarch-0dzjq / piarch-mbpxq /
piarch-szb6u) that changed:
- `ExtensionStep`: `step_label: str` → `step_number: int + letter: str + sub_step: int` with derived `label` property
- `UCOverview` → `UCOverviewValidated` wrapper with `errors: list[str]`
- `MainSuccessScenario` → `MainSuccessScenarioValidated` wrapper
- `ExtensionConditions` → `ExtensionConditionsValidated` wrapper
- `StepCompleteness.step_description` field removed

Running the same BR-UC-001 checkpoint after these changes:

```
23:46:00 rehearse_uc-develop_start  nodes=32
/Users/konst/projects/piarch-neo4j-driver/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pydantic/main.py:464:
  UserWarning: Pydantic serializer warnings:
  PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue(Expected `ExtensionStep` - serialized
    value may not be as expected [field_name='flow_steps',
    input_value={'step_label': 'a.1', 'ac...l check in MSS step 2.'},
    input_type=dict])
  ... (repeated for each pre-existing extension step)
23:46:00 graph_stats  amend_node=0 create_node=0 disk_ms=0.0 search_calls=0
23:46:00 rehearse_uc-develop_complete  cost_by_role={} duration_s=0.0 total_cost=0
23:46:03 rehearse.node_complete  amended=0 created=0 duration_s=11.2 status=success
```

The pipeline "completed" in 0 seconds with 32 nodes theoretically
executed and zero LLM calls. Pydantic emitted a UserWarning
(non-fatal) for each old-shape dict it couldn't coerce cleanly.
Status: `success`. That is a lie.

## Expected behavior

On checkpoint read during `run(..., config=config_with_checkpointer)`:

1. For each node in the resumed state, compare the checkpoint's stored
   output type (or a fingerprint of its schema) against the current
   `node.outputs` type annotation.
2. If they disagree — field added/removed, type changed, wrapper class
   renamed — raise `CheckpointSchemaError` with a list of mismatched
   nodes and a hint: "construct topology changed since checkpoint;
   either invalidate `<path/to/db>` or migrate."
3. Do NOT attempt to coerce and proceed. Do NOT fall through to
   pydantic silent-coercion. A schema mismatch is a programmer-caused
   incompatibility; silent resume is strictly worse than a clear error.

## Why it matters

The current silent behavior caused:
- 60+ minutes of LLM work silently bypassed (the new nodes never ran;
  the pipeline returned pre-change state as if it had done work)
- Misleading `status: success` in the rehearsal report
- `amended=0, created=0` — obvious in hindsight, but easy to miss
  when looking at a "pass" line
- No way to distinguish "legitimate resume, nothing to do" from
  "broken state, nothing CAN be done"

Legitimate fast resume (all nodes already complete, valid schema) is
still fine — this proposal does NOT break that case. It only adds a
schema-fingerprint check before declaring resume valid.

## Implementation sketch

A checkpoint entry already carries the pickled output value. We can
fingerprint the type at write time and verify at read time:

```python
# write path (already runs)
def _serialize_node_output(output: Any) -> bytes:
    type_fp = _fingerprint(type(output))  # e.g., class name + field-name/type tuple
    payload = pickle.dumps(output)
    return pickle.dumps({"fp": type_fp, "payload": payload})

# read path (new)
def _deserialize_node_output(raw: bytes, expected_type: type) -> Any:
    wrapper = pickle.loads(raw)
    current_fp = _fingerprint(expected_type)
    if wrapper["fp"] != current_fp:
        raise CheckpointSchemaError(
            node=...,
            checkpoint_fp=wrapper["fp"],
            current_fp=current_fp,
            hint="construct topology changed; invalidate checkpoint or migrate",
        )
    return pickle.loads(wrapper["payload"])
```

Fingerprint can be `(class_qualname, tuple((f.name, str(f.annotation))
for f in model_fields))` — stable across runs, changes when the model
shape changes.

Alternative: piggyback on Pydantic's own `model_validate(..., strict=True)`
and elevate the `PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue` warnings to
errors. Less robust (misses non-Pydantic outputs, misses class renames
when fields are identical) but much simpler.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: run a construct twice, second run after changing
a field name in one output model. Assert the second run raises
`CheckpointSchemaError` mentioning the changed node.

**Integration**: same setup, but the change is "rename class,
identical fields" — assert the error fires (classes are not
structurally equal by design).

**Integration**: identical construct, second run with no changes.
Assert the run proceeds normally (no false positives, no performance
regression on happy path).

**E2E**: piarch's UC pipeline — intentionally change a downstream
node's output, run against an existing checkpoint. Assert a clear
error instead of silent 0-second "success."

## Acceptance

- Schema fingerprint stored in checkpoint alongside pickled payload
- On resume, fingerprint compared against current node output type
- Mismatch raises `CheckpointSchemaError` naming the nodes + field
  deltas + migration hint
- Happy-path resume unaffected (no perf regression)
- Pydantic `UserWarning` coercion path is explicitly guarded against
- Integration + E2E tests covering: rename, add field, remove field,
  wrapper-type swap, identical-rerun (negative)
design:
## Design

### New error type (errors.py)
CheckpointSchemaError(NeographError) — raised when checkpoint schema mismatches current graph

### State fingerprint field (state.py)
Add neo_schema_fingerprint: str = "" to compile_state_model output.
Computed from sorted [(field_name, str(field_type)) for non-neo_ fields].

### Compile-time fingerprint (compiler.py)
After compile_state_model, compute fingerprint. Store on compiled graph:
  compiled._neo_schema_fingerprint = _compute_schema_fingerprint(state_model)

### Initial state injection (runner.py)
When starting fresh (no checkpoint), inject fingerprint into initial state:
  input["neo_schema_fingerprint"] = graph._neo_schema_fingerprint

### Resume verification (runner.py)
Before invoke(None), read checkpoint, extract neo_schema_fingerprint,
compare with graph._neo_schema_fingerprint. If different, raise CheckpointSchemaError
with field diffs.

### _compute_schema_fingerprint helper
Takes state_model, returns sha256 hex digest of sorted field specs.
Excludes neo_* framework fields (they change with modifier config, not schema).

Risk: LOW for the detection path. The only tricky part is initial state injection.
notes:
## Research

Core invariant: A checkpoint resume must never proceed when the state schema has changed since the checkpoint was written. Silent coercion is strictly worse than a clear error.

### Resume flow
1. runner.py:147 — _has_existing_checkpoint detects saved state
2. runner.py:148 — graph.invoke(None, config) resumes from checkpoint
3. LangGraph deserializes state via msgpack, constructs channels, wraps in Pydantic state model
4. NO schema validation anywhere in this path

### LangGraph has NO built-in schema versioning
- Checkpoint.v tracks wire format version (currently 4), not app schema
- channels_from_checkpoint simply assigns stored values to current channels
- Missing channels get MISSING, extra channels silently ignored

### Fingerprint design
Compute at compile time from state_model.model_fields:
  fingerprint = hash of [(field_name, canonical_type_str) for non-framework fields]
Store as state field: neo_schema_fingerprint: str (set on first write via initial state)
Verify at run() time before invoke(None): compare checkpoint fingerprint vs current graph fingerprint

### Interception points
- compiler.py:173 — compute fingerprint after state_model is built
- state.py — add neo_schema_fingerprint field to compiled state
- runner.py:147-148 and 161-162 — verify before resume
close_reason: Checkpoint schema fingerprinting: compute at compile, store in state, verify before resume. Raises CheckpointSchemaError on mismatch.

title: Portal: first-class dynamic handoff + runtime flow-definition (Command(goto), spec-driven, validated-at-dispatch)
description:
## What
A FIRST-CLASS dynamic-handoff / runtime-routing construct: a node decides at RUNTIME which peer (from a declared set) takes over next, lowering to LangGraph's Command(goto=...) (and Send for dynamic fan-out) rather than a statically-known conditional edge. This is genuine dynamic multi-agent workflow (the OpenAI-Swarm / CrewAI-hierarchical handoff pattern), currently NOT expressible in neograph's IR.

## Why (first-class, not an import hack)
neograph's IR today is STATIC-TOPOLOGY: edges inferred from typed params; if->add_conditional_edges (arms known at compile/re-trace time); Loop->static back-edge; Each->Send over a statically-declared collection. None expresses "a node returns which peer to route to next from a runtime-decided set." LangGraph HAS this (Command(goto)/Send) and neograph targets LangGraph, so there is NO runtime barrier — the gap is purely a missing IR primitive. Maintainer decision 2026-07-13: build it regardless of Agent Spec; dynamic workflows are a real capability neograph wants.

DOWNSTREAM BENEFIT (not the driver): Agent Spec's Swarm (dynamic decentralized handoff; first_agent + relationships) becomes a FAITHFUL import target once this exists. The swcy1 ratification chose reject-on-import for Swarm precisely because the only path today is a static fake (mis-reconstructs peer-to-peer as topological order). This construct changes that from 'reject forever' to 'reject until the combinator lands, then faithful import via Command(goto)'. Re-scope the Agent Spec Swarm decision accordingly once this ships. RemoteAgent/A2A is a SEPARATE (client-initiated call-node) concern, not this.

## The genuinely-new-IR caveat (layer discipline)
AGENTS.md: adding new IR capability is the SANCTIONED exception to 'no new IR primitives' — do it DELIBERATELY and document it (like _BranchNode for ForwardConstruct). This is that case. It touches modifiers.py / compiler.py / state.py / _wiring.py (the compiler must emit Command(goto)-based routing) — a real IR + compiler change, maximum blast radius. NOT a DX-layer sugar.

## Design spike FIRST (this ticket = the spike)
Open questions to settle before any code, with independent architect review:
1. SURFACE: what does the author write? A `Handoff`/`Router` modifier (`node | Handoff(peers=[...], route='cond')`)? A `self.handoff(peers, route)` ForwardConstruct builder? A dynamic-edge construct? Pin against the three-API-surface parity rule (declarative / @node / programmatic).
2. RUNTIME CONTRACT: how does a node signal its next hop? Return a routing value the compiler maps to Command(goto)? A typed HandoffDecision output? How does this interact with the state bus (the chosen peer reads what)?
3. TERMINATION / cycles: dynamic handoff can loop forever — max-hops budget? cycle detection? (parallels Loop.max_iterations / Tool budget).
4. VALIDATION: the whole neograph thesis is compile-time 'if it compiles it runs'. A runtime-routed graph is inherently less statically checkable — what CAN we validate (peers exist, types compatible across every possible hop, route condition registered) and what becomes a runtime guarantee? This is the crux: how much of the static-safety pitch survives dynamic routing.
5. LOWERING: exact Command(goto)/Send emission in compiler.py; how it composes with existing modifiers (can a handoff peer be an Oracle/agent node?); checkpoint/interrupt interaction.
6. Fan-out variant: is Send-based dynamic fan-out (runtime-decided N) part of this or separate?

## Deliverable (spike)
docs/design/dynamic-handoff-<date>.md: the surface decision, runtime contract, validation-vs-runtime boundary, lowering sketch, termination story, three-surface plan, and the Swarm-import re-scope. Independent architect review gate BEFORE implementation is greenlit.

## Priority / sequencing
Post-0.7. Parallel to the Agent Spec interop epic (2ev48) but NOT blocking it — the import/type-layer/export children proceed without this; only the Swarm-import faithfulness depends on it. Maintainer sequencing 2026-07-13: Agent Spec comes earlier than the TS port; this dynamic-workflow capability is first-class regardless.
notes:
SCOPE EXPANSION + NAMING (maintainer, 2026-07-13):

1. NAMING: this gets a NEOGRAPH-NATIVE term, not 'Swarm' borrowed from Agent Spec. Matrix-themed to match the Oracle (merge-judge) / Operator (HITL) precedent. Pending maintainer pick — candidates: Keymaker (creates a path/door to ANY destination incl. runtime-defined ones — best fit for spec-driven mode), Switch (Matrix crew member + routing pun — best for peer-routing mode), Trainman (transit router between realms). 'Swarm' acceptable as fallback.

2. TWO MODES OF ONE CONSTRUCT:
   (a) PEER ROUTING: a node picks its successor at runtime from a KNOWN declared peer set -> Command(goto). The classic Swarm handoff / faithful Swarm-import target.
   (b) DYNAMIC FLOW DEFINITION (the powerful one): a node emits AT RUNTIME the SPEC for the next flow (an Agent Spec Flow OR a neograph Spec), which neograph VALIDATES -> COMPILES -> dispatches. 'I want to dynamically define the next flow -- here we go, here is the spec.' This FUSES: dynamic handoff + runtime graph construction (already a first-class use case) + from_agent_spec/load_spec.

3. COUPLING TO AGENT SPEC (revises the 'largely parallel' note): mode (b) USES from_agent_spec (neograph-01i0g) / load_spec at RUNTIME as the flow-definition seam. So from_agent_spec is not just 'load a saved file' -- it becomes the runtime dynamic-flow mechanism. The peer-routing mode (a) stays independent; the spec-driven mode (b) depends on 01i0g (import). Agent Spec import gains a second, load-bearing consumer.

4. VALIDATION CRUX RESOLVED (supersedes the earlier 'how much static safety survives' worry): a runtime-supplied flow can't be statically checked, but it IS validated at DISPATCH -- the existing validator/lint runs on the emitted spec BEFORE it executes. This is the 'validation as safety rail for MACHINE-authored graphs' thesis realized. The pitch becomes: 'if it dispatches, it was validated' -- machine-authored or hand-written, every flow passes the same gate before running. The spike must pin: what runs at dispatch (full compile+validate vs a fast subset), failure mode on an invalid emitted spec (reject-and-route-to-error vs raise), and the max-hops/recursion budget for self-extending flows.

Spike deliverable updated accordingly: cover BOTH modes, the from_agent_spec runtime coupling, and the dispatch-time validation contract.
NAME PINNED (maintainer, 2026-07-13): the construct is KEYMAKER (Matrix-native, beside Oracle/Operator). Rationale: the Keymaker makes a key to ANY door, including destinations not pre-wired — captures both modes, especially the spec-driven one ('here is the door to the next flow; here is the key'). Surface sketch: node | Keymaker(peers=[...]) for known-peer routing; node | Keymaker(route='decide') for the emit-a-spec-at-runtime mode. The spike settles the exact kwargs, the routing/flow-emission return contract, and the dispatch-time validation gate.
SPIKE DELIVERED + v1 IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-14, epic neograph-t1f7z):
- Spike deliverable: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md (decision-complete design), docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md (4-way research), independent architect review (GO-WITH-CORRECTIONS), docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md (D1-D13 + design-doc judgment-call register + ratchet register + run summary).
- v1 of BOTH modes implemented (T1-T8): mode (a) peer-routing mesh (Command(goto)+destinations=, hop budget, checkpoint semantics, three-surface parity, @node peers= sugar, example 28, concepts/keymaker.mdx); mode (b) runtime dispatch (load_spec+compile gate, rejection-before-execution, example 29, docs).
- All consolidation gates green (pytest 3268 passed, mypy clean, ruff clean, website 13 tests + 46-page build, 12/12 keyless examples).
- Deferred v2/fast-follow work filed: neograph-a37vk, -nnds9, -do0d9, -fefar, -airpr, -4pr04, -2aw5c, -5x43u; D3 morning decision neograph-7t7tf.
- LEFT OPEN for maintainer's morning ratification (D3 lowering dissent + ratchet growths — see decision log run summary).
RENAMED 2026-07-14 (neograph-1t0zh): Keymaker -> Portal across the shipped surface (class Portal, @node(portal=[...]), Portal(to=[...])). Bodies of this epic and the deferred children keep historical 'Keymaker' references as planning text; the shipped API is Portal. Pinned by tests/test_guards_portal_naming.py.
CORRECTION (2026-07-15): Portal mode (b) dispatches the NATIVE neograph Spec (load_spec dict, modifier-aware) — NOT Agent Spec. Portal does NOT depend on Agent Spec import; the earlier coupling note is superseded. Agent Spec ingestion by Portal is an OPTIONAL interop path (see the convergence bead), never a blocker.
RE-CORRECTION (2026-07-15, supersedes the 07-15 CORRECTION above): per the unification, Portal mode (b)'s runtime format IS the neograph-flavored Agent Spec (= export/import format), NOT a bespoke native load_spec dict. mode (b) dispatch rides from_agent_spec (01i0g); the v1 load_spec path is removed (0la8v). So Portal mode (b) DOES depend on the flavored import — cleanly, through the one shared machine format. Human-authoring neograph Spec is unaffected (separate concern).

Independently smoke-verified. Deferred v2 tail (self.handoff, named meshes, mode-b safety knobs, Portal+Operator) moved to neograph-qtfof.
