title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.5
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.5` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.5/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.5
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.5)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.5 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.5 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.5/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.5 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances

   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash

```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

  regressed.

title: PROC-2: structural guard meta-pattern — regex slip + naming canonicity
description:
## Architectural invariant

Every structural guard in `tests/test_guards_*.py` has positive AND negative AND regex-slip meta-tests. Helpers across `src/neograph/` have at most ONE canonical name; near-duplicate names (Levenshtein ≤ 2, or substring) for different functions fail a structural test. Both invariants are enforced structurally; the documentation is the test.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

Read:
- All current structural guards in `tests/test_guards_*.py` — list which have positive meta-tests, negative meta-tests, and regex-slip meta-tests (the third is the gap surfaced by MED-06 in the synthesis).
- The synthesis `MED-06`: `_neo_isolated_input` slips the `^neo_` regex of the StateKeys centralization guard. Same class: any regex-based guard whose author didn't think about the `_neo_*` edge case.
- The synthesis `CON-01`: `_isinstance_safe` vs `_is_instance_safe` — dual-named, grep-hostile. Living in `di.py:91` and aliased in `factory.py:57` for legacy reasons.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern 1: "regex-based structural guard without a regex-slip meta-test."
- Scan: `grep -l "re\.compile\|re\.search\|re\.match" tests/test_guards_*.py`
- For each match, identify the regex AND determine whether a "should match but doesn't" meta-test exists.

Disease pattern 2: "near-duplicate helper names across src/neograph/."
- Scan: write a one-off script that enumerates all top-level `def _name(...)` in `src/neograph/*.py`, computes pairwise Levenshtein on the names, flags pairs with distance ≤ 2 OR one is a substring of the other.
- Manual review of the flagged pairs (some may be intentional, e.g., `_get` vs `_get_required`).

Disposition table per disease pattern.

## Phase 2 — Target design

1. **Meta-test discipline for regex guards** — add a `TestRegexGuardsHaveSlipMetaTests` structural test in `tests/test_guards_meta.py` (new file). For every regex used in a guard, REQUIRE the same module to include at least one "would-be-missed" test case proving the regex catches edge cases.

2. **Naming canonicity guard** — add `TestNoNearDuplicateHelperNames` in `tests/test_guards_meta.py`. Computes pairwise name similarity across `src/neograph/`. Flags Levenshtein ≤ 2 OR substring pairs. Allowlist for intentional pairs (e.g., `get` / `get_required` / `get_counter`).

3. **Fix existing failures**:
   - Rename one of `_isinstance_safe` / `_is_instance_safe` to canonical form; delete the alias.
   - Fix the `^neo_` regex in StateKeys centralization guard to anchor `^_?neo_` (or rewrite as AST-based — see TQ-03 in synthesis).
   - Add the regex-slip meta-test for that guard.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + GRASP rigorously. Iterate until:
- New meta-tests cover EVERY regex-based guard in `tests/test_guards_*.py`.
- The naming-canonicity guard scans all of `src/neograph/` and has its own positive + negative meta-tests.
- Both failure modes from the synthesis (MED-06, CON-01) are structurally impossible going forward.
- The Levenshtein scan + allowlist is checked in as part of the test suite.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO scoping the meta-test discipline to "guards we noticed today." It scans ALL existing guards.
- NO ad-hoc allowlist entries for the naming-canonicity guard without a written reason.
- NO replacing the existing `^neo_` regex without adding the slip meta-test that would have caught the original bug.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

Re-run both scans. Every regex guard has its slip meta-test. Every near-duplicate name pair is either resolved or allowlisted with a reason. The structural guards added by this ticket are themselves covered by positive + negative meta-tests (the guards guard themselves).

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer:
1. Is the meta-test discipline genuinely automatable, or did we just write "rules" without enforcement?
2. Is the Levenshtein threshold (≤ 2) right? Too strict (false positives) or too loose (`_isinstance_safe`/`_is_instance_safe` distance is 1 — would catch it)?
3. Is there a way a future contributor can add a regex guard WITHOUT a slip meta-test and have CI pass?

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- `tests/test_guards_meta.py` exists with both new structural tests
- Levenshtein scan run + allowlist documented + `_isinstance_safe`/`_is_instance_safe` consolidated
- StateKeys regex either fixed to `^_?neo_` OR converted to AST (per TQ-03)
- Slip meta-test added for StateKeys guard
- Independent reviewer verdict ELEGANT ≥85

## Core Invariant
Every regex in a tests/test_guards_*.py guard module is a NAMED constant carrying its own regex-slip meta-test (that invokes the scanner and asserts); every helper name across src/neograph/ (defs AND import aliases) is canonical -- Levenshtein<=2 (min-len>=4) near-duplicates for distinct functions are eliminated or allowlisted-with-reason; every framework magic-string key (state-bus AND config) is a named constant. All three disciplines are enforced by structural tests in tests/test_guards_meta.py so the documentation IS the test.

## Implementation Plan (refined per architect review)

### Step 1 -- Consolidate _isinstance_safe (CON-01)
- Delete dead alias factory.py:57 (from neograph.di import _isinstance_safe as _is_instance_safe  # noqa: F401).
- _input_shape.py:12 import _isinstance_safe directly (no 'as'); update :49,:144 call sites.

### Step 2 -- Centralize framework magic-string keys
- _state_keys.py: add ISOLATED_INPUT = '_neo_isolated_input' (keep literal value; no behavior change). node.py:414 -> state[StateKeys.ISOLATED_INPUT].
- config key _neo_input: add a named constant (StateKeys.CONFIG_INPUT = '_neo_input' OR a ConfigKeys sibling). runner.py:310,320 -> use constant. (Architect+user: pull into THIS ticket, anti-band-aid.)

### Step 3 -- Harden TestNeoStateKeysCentralized (MED-06), receiver-agnostic
- Layer A (unchanged): flag ALL ^neo_ string literals anywhere (no false positives; bare neo_ never a legit attr).
- Layer B (new): flag any ^_?neo_ string literal used as (i) a Subscript-slice constant X[lit], OR (ii) first call-arg to .get/.pop/.setdefault -- RECEIVER-AGNOSTIC (no Name(id='state') constraint; survives aliasing). Does NOT flag getattr/Attribute/__slots__ list elements. DOES flag configurable['_neo_input'] by design (-> caught by Step 2 centralization, so passes after fix).
- Slip test: prove state['_neo_synthetic']=x AND d.get('_neo_x') are caught; getattr(o,'_neo_attr') and __slots__=('_neo_x',) are NOT.

### Step 4 -- Require NAMED regex constants in guard modules

For every named regex constant, require a slip method named test_slip_<const>* (case-insensitive, underscores normalized) in the same module whose body (a) calls the module scanner helper and (b) has >=1 assert. Self-coverage: the meta module's own regex constant gets its own slip test. Own positive+negative meta-tests (inject a fake module missing a slip test -> flagged; with one -> passes).
- TestNoNearDuplicateHelperNames: pool top-level def names + ImportFrom aliases across src/neograph/*.py; lev<=2, both>=4 chars. ALLOWLIST (record lev in each): (_get_param_res,_set_param_res,lev1)=getter/setter symmetry; (_render_dict_value,_render_list_value,lev2)=parallel type renderers; (_render_input,render_input,lev1)=private/public underscore convention. Own positive+negative meta-tests.

### Step 6 -- Retrofit per-regex slip tests
- any_audit.py (_ARBITRARY_TYPES_RE), sidecar_imports.py (4 tool config REs -> name them if inline), ir_compiler.py (TICKET_ID_RE), llm_runtime.py (now MIGRATE: _NORMALIZE_FIELD_RE + _COUNTER_GET + _COUNTER_GET_DEFAULT each need a test_slip_<const>), function_local_imports.py (StateKeys PATTERN). consistency.py exempt (no regex). Scan ALL -- anti-band-aid.

### Step 7 -- gates
make quality green; in-loop codebase-elegance scan; independent Opus review ELEGANT>=85.

## TDD order (write-test atom)
Add the three meta/guard tests FIRST and confirm RED:
- TestNoNearDuplicateHelperNames fails (isinstance alias present).
- TestRegexGuardsHaveSlipMetaTests fails (inline regexes + missing per-regex slip tests).
- StateKeys slip test fails (Layer B not implemented).
Then implement Steps 1-6 until GREEN.

title: lint: validate template placeholders against runtime input dict keys (including sub-construct remapping)
description:
## What

Extend `neograph check` / `lint()` to verify that every `{placeholder}` in a
node's prompt template is satisfiable by the keys that `render_input()` will
actually produce at runtime. Currently lint checks DI parameter resolution
(FromInput/FromConfig bindings) but not the template→data contract.

Specifically: when a node lives inside a sub-construct, its input arrives under
the key `neo_subgraph_input` (hardcoded in factory.py:578), not under the
original parameter name declared in the @node function signature. A template
referencing `{load_uc_composite}` compiles and lints clean but crashes at
runtime because the dict has `{neo_subgraph_input}` instead.

## Why

piarch-neo4j-driver renamed 4 UC templates from `{uc_context}` to
`{load_uc_composite}` to match the @node parameter name — the "placeholder =
param name" invariant. All 1305 tests passed. At runtime, the pipeline
crashed: `KeyError: 'load_uc_composite'` because inside the research-internal
sub-construct, neograph delivers the input as `neo_subgraph_input`. This is
a class of bug that static tests and current lint cannot catch — only the
runtime dispatch path knows the actual key names.

## Expectations after delivery

- `lint()` returns a new issue type (e.g. `template_placeholder_unresolvable`)
  when a template placeholder cannot be satisfied by the node's input dict keys.
- For sub-construct nodes: lint knows that the sub-construct input arrives as
  `neo_subgraph_input` and flags templates that reference the outer parameter
  name instead.
- For top-level nodes: lint verifies placeholder names match the dict keys
  from fan-in resolution (parameter names).
- `neograph check` reports these alongside existing DI issues.
- Bridge-supplied standard vars (node_id, project_root, json_schema, etc.)
  are configurable as "known extras" so they don't false-positive.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/lint/test_template_placeholder_lint.py` —
(a) Construct with a top-level node whose template references `{param_a}` and
    the node has `param_a` in its signature → no issue.
(b) Same but template references `{nonexistent}` → lint returns
    `template_placeholder_unresolvable` issue.
(c) Sub-construct node whose template references `{original_param}` instead
    of `{neo_subgraph_input}` → lint returns issue with message mentioning
    sub-construct remapping.
(d) Template referencing a known extra (node_id) → no issue.

**E2E**: Run `neograph check` on piarch's `uc_derivation.py` with `--setup`
providing real config. Assert zero template-placeholder issues after the
piarch templates are fixed.

## Acceptance

- `lint()` checks template placeholders against runtime input dict keys
- Sub-construct `neo_subgraph_input` remapping is accounted for
- `neograph check` surfaces placeholder mismatches alongside DI issues
- Known bridge-supplied vars configurable to avoid false positives
- Existing DI lint behavior unchanged
design:
## Architecture

### Core invariant
lint must predict the exact input_data dict keys a node will receive at runtime, and validate template placeholders against those keys.

### New lint check: _check_template_placeholders

Added to _walk after existing DI binding checks. Only fires for LLM-mode nodes (mode != "scripted") that have a prompt.

#### Step 1: Predict runtime input keys

For each LLM node, compute what keys input_data will have at runtime:
- If node.inputs is a dict: keys are the dict keys (but port params remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" need detection)
- If node.inputs is a single type: no dict keys (isinstance scan — no validation possible)
- If node.inputs is None: no inputs

Detection of sub-construct port remapping:
- Walk needs to track whether we are inside a sub-construct (pass parent_construct to _walk)
- If inside a sub-construct with input= declared, and a node.inputs key matches the sub-construct input type, that key will be remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" at runtime

#### Step 2: Extract template placeholders

For inline prompts (contains space or ${): extract all ${var} using _VAR_RE. First segment of each var path is the expected key.

For template-ref prompts: we cannot extract placeholders from opaque template references. Skip template content validation. Instead, expose predicted_input_keys on the LintIssue so consumer-level lint can validate.

#### Step 3: Validate

For each extracted placeholder first-segment:
- If it matches a predicted input key: OK
- If it matches a known extra (node_id, project_root): OK (these are in state, accessible via config)
- If it matches nothing: emit LintIssue with kind="template_placeholder_unresolvable"

For sub-construct port remapping: if a placeholder references the original param name (before remapping), emit a specific LintIssue with kind="template_placeholder_remapped" explaining that the key is neo_subgraph_input at runtime.

### LintIssue extension

Add new kinds: "template_placeholder_unresolvable", "template_placeholder_remapped"
These use required=True (they will crash at runtime).

### Known extras (configurable)

Default set: {"node_id", "project_root", "human_feedback"}
Lint accepts known_template_vars: set[str] parameter for consumer-supplied extras.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| src/neograph/lint.py | Add _check_template_placeholders, _predict_input_keys, _extract_inline_placeholders. Extend _walk with parent_construct tracking. Add known_template_vars param to lint(). |
| src/neograph/__main__.py | Pass known_template_vars from config if provided |
| tests/test_validation.py | New test class TestTemplatePlaceholderLint |

### Risk: LOW
- Existing DI lint completely unchanged
- New check only fires for LLM-mode nodes with prompts
- No production code paths modified (lint is read-only analysis)
notes:
## Research Findings

Core invariant: lint must predict the exact input_data dict keys a node will receive at runtime, and validate template placeholders against those keys.

### Two template systems
1. Inline prompts (${var}): resolved by neograph _substitute_vars. Lintable — we know the template text and the input keys.
2. Template-ref prompts ("rw/summarize"): resolved by consumer prompt_compiler. Template text is opaque to neograph — cant lint the template content. BUT we can lint the input_data keys.

### Input dict key sources (from _extract_input in factory.py)
- FAN_IN_DICT: keys are upstream node field names (from node.inputs dict keys)
- SINGLE_TYPE: no keys (isinstance scan, no dict)
- EACH_ITEM: single value from neo_each_item
- Sub-construct port: original param remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" in _construct_builder.py:541

### The piarch bug pattern
Consumer prompt_compiler does template.format(**data). Template has {load_uc_composite} but data has {neo_subgraph_input}. KeyError at runtime.

### What lint can check
1. For inline prompts: extract ${var} and ${var.field} placeholders, validate first segment is in input dict keys
2. For all LLM nodes: compute predicted input_data keys and report if neo_subgraph_input remapping occurred
3. For template-ref prompts: expose predicted keys so consumer lint/checks can validate

### Known extras (always available)
In state: node_id, project_root, human_feedback
In config: everything from run(input={...})
Consumer prompt_compiler also gets: config, node_name, output_model, llm_config, output_schema, context
close_reason: 26 tests (21 deterministic + 5 Hypothesis). Covers all input shapes, sub-construct remapping, @node path, fan-in, dotted access, known extras, edge cases.

title: neograph check CLI command
description:
Add a CLI entry point that loads a Python module, discovers all Construct objects, runs compile() + lint() on each, and reports errors. Zero-execution validation for CI/CD.

## Usage
```bash
neograph check my_pipeline.py
neograph check my_package.pipelines
neograph check examples/lead-outreach/pipeline.py --config '{"node_id": "test"}'
```

## What it does
1. Import the module
2. Find all top-level Construct instances (or objects returned by construct_from_module/construct_from_functions)
3. Run compile() on each — catches CompileError (tool registration, LLM config, output_strategy, type mismatches)
4. Run lint(construct, config) on each — catches DI binding issues
5. Print results: pass/fail per construct, list of issues
6. Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail

## Implementation
- src/neograph/__main__.py (so `python -m neograph check` works)
- pyproject.toml: add `[project.scripts] neograph = "neograph.__main__:main"`
- Use argparse, keep it minimal
- Inspired by `dagster definitions validate`

## Note
lint() and compile() already exist — this is just the CLI wrapper that discovers constructs and calls them.
notes:
## Config handling for lint

JSON --config only works for serializable values. Real configs have Python objects (DB connections, rate limiters, resource handlers).

Two modes:
1. **--setup module.py**: imports a Python module that exports get_check_config() -> dict. Passes real objects to lint(). For power users / full validation.
2. **--types '{"resource_handler": "piarch.resources.ResourceHandler"}'**: type-only map. lint() checks DI params are satisfiable by type, no real objects needed. Default for CI.

lint() itself should support both:
- lint(construct, config={...}) — real values (existing)
- lint(construct, type_map={...}) — type-only check (new)

The type_map approach is better for CI: no side effects, no setup code, no secrets. Just 'these keys will exist with these types at runtime.'

title: Portal mode (b) runtime format = neograph-flavored Agent Spec (re-point emit+dispatch onto from_agent_spec)
description:
Portal mode (b)'s runtime dispatch format IS the neograph-flavored Agent Spec — the SAME single machine format that export (i3zsh) emits and import (01i0g) consumes (Agent Spec envelope + x-neograph reconstruction metadata that is inert to external consumers but rebuilds the exact Oracle/Each/Loop/Portal modifiers).

INVARIANT preserved: the human-authoring neograph Spec (_spec_schema.py, one-line modifier slots) is unaffected — that is the authoring DX, orthogonal to this machine/runtime format.

Update the ONE existing demo/fixture surface that emits native neograph-Spec dicts for mode (b) so they emit Agent-Spec-flavored dicts instead: `examples/29_portal_dynamic_flow.py` (`DispatchDecision.spec: dict` content), `tests/test_portal_dispatch.py`, `tests/modifiers/test_portal.py`, `tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/portal_dispatch_minimal.py`. Before closing: resolve the NEEDS-USER-INPUT flag in Findings (whether mode-(b) itself needs its own `neograph/portal_dispatch_spec`-style export marker, symmetric to `oracle_spec`/`each_spec`/`loop_spec`/`operator_spec`, or whether -- because the dispatched sub-flow is built at runtime rather than exported as part of a static Construct -- there is genuinely nothing to mark). title: Cross-linking depth: dotted Type.member refs link to the exact field anchor, not just the type section
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a dotted `Type.member` reference in prose links to that MEMBER's anchor inside the type's rendered reference section (a per-field id), not merely to the type's section heading — and the member anchor is manifest-derived + slug-stable, so it never dangles.

WHY: Stage B already VALIDATES dotted `Type.member` refs against the manifest (HARD tier: a missing member fails the Astro build), but it AUTOLINKS them to the TYPE's anchor (`#node-model`), dropping the reader at the top of the section rather than at the field. Once kec0k renders per-symbol field TABLES, each field row is a natural link target. This closes the 'cross-link to methods/members' half of the maintainer's goal (the RAMP mechanism links Message.field to the field, not just the message).

DEPENDS ON kec0k: the field tables + their stable per-field anchors must exist to link to. This ticket has two halves:
1. GENERATION (kec0k-adjacent): kec0k's field-table rows must emit a stable, manifest-derived per-field anchor (e.g. id='node-model-outputs' or slug('Node.outputs')). Settle the anchor scheme so it (a) cannot collide with a symbol anchor and (b) is reproducible by the plugin from manifest field data alone. If kec0k does not already emit field anchors, that emission is part of THIS ticket.
2. RESOLUTION (plugin): teach remark-api.mjs to resolve a validated `Type.member` ref to the field anchor when the type is fielded and the member is a field; fall back to the type anchor (current behavior) when there is no field-level anchor (e.g. a method/callable member with no row). Never emit a link to a non-existent field anchor (dead-anchor-proof, same discipline as the symbol path).

ANTI-BAND-AID: the member anchor must be COMPUTED from the manifest field name, not hand-authored per ref. A prose ref and the rendered field row derive the SAME anchor from the SAME manifest field, so they cannot drift.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A prose `Node.outputs` (and `Tool.name`, `ToolInteraction.typed_result`, etc.) emits a resolving <a href=...#node-model-outputs> in website/dist/, landing on the field row.
- The field anchor is manifest-derived and slug-stable (github-slugger of the rendered row == the plugin-computed target).
- Mutation-proven: renaming a manifest field (regen) moves BOTH the row anchor and the link target in lockstep; a ref to a removed field still fails the build (existing HARD-tier behavior preserved).
- Members with no field row (callables/methods) gracefully fall back to the type anchor — no dead links.

NOT 0.6.0-gating. The most advanced cross-linking step; do it AFTER symbol-level linking (kec0k) and the coverage capstone (wqzel) prove out.
design:
## Core Invariant
A dotted `Type.member` prose ref and the rendered field row it links to derive the SAME anchor -- `{type_anchor}-{field_name}` -- from the SAME manifest field, so the link can never dangle: the plugin emits a field anchor ONLY when the type's heading is present on the page, and render_reference_sections() emits the field row's <span id> for every manifest field, keeping emission and resolution in manifest-driven lockstep (the byte-for-byte freshness guard enforces it).

## Implementation Plan
1. GENERATION -- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py: change _reference_field_table(fields) -> _reference_field_table(fields, anchor); append a self-closing `<span id="{anchor}-{f['name']}" />` to each row's Field cell (`| \`{name}\`<span id="{anchor}-{name}" /> | ... |`). render_reference_sections() (:544) passes entry['anchor'] as the second arg. Field names are lowercase snake_case identifiers so `{anchor}-{name}` is github-slugger-stable with no member slugging.
2. GENERATION -- regenerate the api.mdx GEN:reference-sections region by hand-pasting the new render_reference_sections() output between the sentinels (no injector script; main() only writes JSON). This is the LOCKSTEP move with step 1.
3. RESOLUTION -- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:143-147: when `fields.some(f => f.name === member)` AND `headings.has(typeAnchor)`, emit `url: ${REF_PAGE}#${typeAnchor}-${member}` (was `#${typeAnchor}`). Preserve: the headings.has(typeAnchor) gate (dead-anchor proof), the resolved-but-undocumented early-return (line 149), and the non-field-member build-fail (line 153, HARD-tier preserved). Members with no field row keep falling back to the type anchor path -- but for a fielded owner every validated member IS a field, so the type-anchor fallback is the graceful default for the never-a-field case.
4. GUARD (TDD, write first) -- add to tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py: (a) every rendered field row emits a <span id="{anchor}-{field}"> and no field anchor collides with any symbol anchor; (b) every field name is a lowercase identifier (fails loud if a future uppercase field breaks slug==name). Update the freshness guard expectation by regenerating (step 2).
5. PLUGIN TEST -- website/plugins/remark-api.test.mjs: tighten test (a) to assert the EXACT field anchor '#lintissue-kind' (not just includes('#lintissue')); add a mutation-style test that a field member resolves to {type}-{field} and a non-field member still throws (HARD-tier preserved). Run `npm test` in website/.
6. VERIFY -- npm run build in website/ (HARD-tier validation runs here); grep dist/reference/api/index.html for id="node-model-outputs" and confirm a prose Node.outputs emits <a href=...#node-model-outputs>. Run uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py.

## Anti-band-aid
The member anchor is COMPUTED (`{anchor}-{name}`) on BOTH the render side and the plugin side from the same manifest field name -- never hand-authored per ref. Renaming a manifest field regenerates the row's <span id> and the plugin recomputes the target in the same breath; a ref to a removed field still hits the existing HARD-tier build-fail. No per-ref anchor table, no drift seam.
notes: ## Findings (research neograph-41t30.2) ### Field-anchor scheme DECISION: `f"{type_anchor}-{field_name}"` via explicit self-closing - kec0k's field-table rows emit PLAIN markdown cells (`| \`name\` | type | req | default |`) with NO id today. Verified in dist/reference/api/index.html: only headings carry ids (blobresult, node-model, node-function); field rows have none. So per-field anchors do NOT exist yet -> emitting them is part of THIS ticket (GENERATION half). - Anchor value = `{type_anchor}-{field_name}` (e.g. Node model anchor node-model + outputs -> node-model-outputs; matches the acceptance example exactly). type_anchor = the symbol's manifest `anchor` (already collision-free + kind-namespaced by _disambiguate_anchors). - SLUG-STABILITY PROVEN: every field name across BOTH manifests (core + mcp) is a lowercase snake_case identifier (verified: 0 non-snake fields). slug() lowercases + strips specials + collapses whitespace; underscores survive. So slug(field_name)==field_name and github-slugger of the rendered id == the plugin-computed `{anchor}-{member}` with NO slugging needed on the member. This is the 'github-slugger of the rendered row == plugin-computed target' acceptance clause. - COLLISION-SAFETY: (a) vs symbol anchors -- symbol anchors are unique+slug-stable; no symbol name slugs to `{type_anchor}-{field}`. (b) cross field-anchor -- field names are Python identifiers (never contain '-', only '_'), and type anchors are unique, so `{typeA}-{fieldX}` can't equal `{typeB}-{fieldY}`. Recommend a guard test asserting no field anchor collides with any symbol anchor + that all field names are lowercase identifiers (fails loud if a future PascalCase/uppercase field appears, which would break the raw-name==slug assumption). - EMISSION MECHANISM: append a self-closing `` to the Field cell of each row. No existing /HTML-in-table precedent in src/content/docs, and no guard forbids HTML in the GEN region, so it is byte-for-byte safe. Astro MDX (.mdx) parses inline JSX inside GFM table cells -> renders uri, a valid scroll target. title: DSML recovery is json_mode/text exclusive — structured strategy has no DSML handling
description:
## Context

**Real correctness bug, not refactoring.** When the LLM emits DSML markup (a tool-call-like XML format) instead of clean tool calls, neograph has recovery code that detects and re-parses it. The recovery is gated to `output_strategy="json_mode"` or `"text"` — when `output_strategy="structured"` (the default for most LLMs), DSML markup is silently dropped or causes errors.

This bug pre-dates the architectural sprint and survived the Wave D / Wave E refactors verbatim. Confirmed at `_tool_loop.py:354` (the gate) and `_llm_dispatch.py:20-43` (the `structured` path with no DSML handling).

**Bonus silent variant**: when LangChain's `with_structured_output(..., include_raw=True).invoke()` returns `{"parsed": None, "raw": <AIMessage with DSML>, "parsing_error": ...}` rather than raising, `_call_structured` unpacks `result = raw_result["parsed"]` and returns `None` to the caller as if it were a valid model. Not covered by current pinning test.

**Current state is pinned by a passing test**: `tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py::test_structured_path_has_no_dsml_recovery_when_provider_returns_dsml` asserts `structured_calls == 2` + bubbles `TypeError`. This test must be INVERTED as part of the fix.

## Source of truth

- **Research analysis**: `docs/design/dsml-recovery-fix-2026-05-20.md` (full bug confirmation, root-cause git archaeology, 3 options evaluation, test plan)
- **Architecture spec**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` — no specific § for DSML recovery (this is a correctness bug, not an architectural commitment). §3 (Retry concerns) mentions DSML-rendered feedback as the BAML-based output-quality retry path.
- **Original DSML recovery commit**: `727d1c9` (the git archaeology in the research doc shows this was where the json_mode-only gate was added)

## Decisions locked

- **Option B — strategy-agnostic recovery via shared helper**. Extract `_attempt_dsml_recovery(response, output_model, ...) -> ParsedModel | None` helper in `_llm_retry.py`. Wire into BOTH `_tool_loop.py` (pre-dispatch peek when ReAct loop final message contains DSML markup) and `_call_structured` (`_llm_dispatch.py`) on `TypeError` OR `parsed=None + raw containing DSML`.
- Detection is content-based (DSML regex on response text); strategy-orthogonal. The strategy controls invocation, not response detection.
- **Add `strategy` field to log payload** uniformly across recovery sites — operators can monitor recovery rate per strategy.
- **DSML regex consolidation**: single private helper in `_llm_retry.py` (currently duplicated at `_tool_loop.py:362` and `_llm_retry.py:163`).

## Scope (strict)

- **EDIT**:
  - `src/neograph/_llm_retry.py` (extract helper; consolidate regex)
  - `src/neograph/_tool_loop.py` (replace inline DSML block with shared-helper call; remove strategy gate; add strategy= to log)
  - `src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py` (`_call_structured`: catch TypeError → shared helper; handle parsed=None + raw containing DSML → shared helper)
  - `tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py` (invert pinning test; add ~4 new tests)
- **DO NOT TOUCH**:
  - DSML emission code (this is recovery only)
  - DSML test cluster other than the inversion (already audited as KEEP in 5fqg)

## Implementation plan

### Phase A — Extract shared helper (~1.5h)

In `src/neograph/_llm_retry.py`:

```python
import re

# Single source of truth for DSML pattern
_DSML_PATTERN = re.compile(r"...")  # consolidate from the two existing sites

def _attempt_dsml_recovery(
    response_text: str,
    output_model: type[BaseModel],
    *,
    log_ctx: dict,
) -> BaseModel | None:
    """Detect DSML markup in LLM response and attempt re-parse.

    Strategy-orthogonal: detection is content-based. Returns parsed model
    if recovery succeeds, None if no DSML detected or parse fails.

    log_ctx must include `strategy=` for uniform observability.
    """
    if not _DSML_PATTERN.search(response_text):
        return None

    log.warning("trailing_tool_call_markup", **log_ctx, recovered=False)
    parsed = ...  # extract + parse logic (consolidate from existing sites)
    if parsed is not None:
        log.info("trailing_tool_call_markup", **log_ctx, recovered=True)
    return parsed
```

Run existing `_invoke_json_with_retry` tests to confirm no regression.

### Phase B — Wire `_tool_loop.py` (~1h)

In `src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:354` area:

- Remove the `if strategy in ("json_mode", "text"):` gate
- Replace inline DSML detect-and-retry block with a single call:
  ```python
  recovered = _attempt_dsml_recovery(
      response_text=final_message.content,
      output_model=output_model,
      log_ctx={"strategy": strategy, ...other ctx},
  )
  if recovered is not None:
      return recovered, interactions
  ```
- The structured strategy now also goes through this path post-ReAct loop

### Phase C — Wire `_call_structured` (~1.5h)

In `src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py:20-43` (`_call_structured`):

- Wrap the `with_structured_output(...).invoke(...)` in try/except `TypeError`
- On TypeError: call shared helper with the response text from the LangChain compat retry path; if recovery succeeds, return it
- After successful `invoke`: check if `result["parsed"] is None` AND `result["raw"]` contains content matching DSML pattern; if both, call shared helper

title: §2: Migrate factory functions to closure-capture kwargs from compile()
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2 (compile() reads inputs from kwargs).

**Problem**: factory functions (`make_node_fn`, `make_subgraph_fn`, `make_oracle_redirect_fn`, etc. in `factory.py` and `_oracle.py`) currently read the runtime callables (`llm_factory`, `prompt_compiler`, `cost_callback`) from module-level globals in `_llm.py`. After the globals are dropped, these functions need the values passed in.

**Fix**: each factory function gains explicit parameters for the runtime callables it uses. The values flow from `compile()` kwargs into the factory function and are closed over in the returned node-function closure.

```python
def make_node_fn(
    node: Node,
    *,
    llm_factory: LlmFactory | None,
    prompt_compiler: PromptCompiler | None,
    cost_callback: CostCallback | None,
    # ... other compile-time inputs
) -> Callable:
    def node_fn(state, config):
        # uses the captured kwargs directly, no module reads
        ...
    return node_fn
```

`compile()` threads its kwargs into each factory-function call as it walks the construct.

**Acceptance**: no factory function reads from `_llm.py` module scope. Each takes its dependencies as explicit parameters.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestFactoryFunctionsTakeKwargs` (new) + `tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py::test_factory_closures_capture_compile_kwargs` (new behavioral test)
**Test type**: structural-guard + behavioral-integration
**What it exercises**: (a) `inspect.signature` each `make_*` function in `factory.py` and `_oracle.py`; assert presence of `llm_factory`, `prompt_compiler`, `cost_callback` keyword-only parameters (or whichever subset each factory needs); assert NO `from neograph._llm import _llm_factory|_prompt_compiler|_global_renderer|_cost_callback` line exists in `factory.py` or `_oracle.py` (AST scan). (b) Behavioral: build a fake `LlmFactory` F1, call `make_node_fn(node, llm_factory=F1, ...)` to get a closure; invoke the closure; assert F1 (and not module global) was used.
**Expected initial state**: failing — factory functions currently read from module scope.
**Persistence**: both stay in suite.

Order: write the failing guard + behavioral test FIRST → run them → must fail → refactor factory functions to accept kwargs + thread through compile() → run again → must pass.
close_reason: Factory functions accept runtime as closure-captured parameter. AST guards confirm factory files don't import the removed _llm globals, don't reference _get_global_renderer, and don't reach into the compat slot. Behavioral test confirms make_node_fn(node, runtime=R) closure uses R's factory. The bulk of threading was done in ticket 1 (lyvi) — this ticket adds 3 new structural guards + 1 behavioral test to lock in the pattern.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for w74k.3.1
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show w74k.3.1` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/w74k.3.1/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" w74k.3.1
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (w74k.3.1)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/w74k.3.1/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add w74k.3.1 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sweep verification for w74k.3.1
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on w74k.3.1
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" w74k.3.1`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (w74k.3.1)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add w74k.3.1 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: KEYMAKER T3: hop budget + checkpoint semantics
description:
INVARIANT: the budget is enforced BEFORE the goto is emitted; every hop is one checkpointed superstep; the counter persists across resume. Per design sections 3.4/6/7: shared per-mesh counter neo_handoff_hops_<entry_field> as plain (int, 0), read-modify-write in the keymaker wrapper (Loop's _state_write.py:133-139 pattern), checked in the wrapper before emitting; on_exhaust='error' raises ExecutionError naming the entry (Loop parity, no new exception class); 'exit' routes to the exit node with the last payload on the bus (deliberate rename vs Loop's 'last', design section 3.4). runner.py: raise the recursion floor by each mesh's max_hops (_ensure_agent_recursion_limit, runner.py:51). Keymaker+Operator is illegal (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO), so checkpoint tests use an Operator AFTER the mesh exit. FILES: factory.py/_state_write.py, runner.py, tests/test_checkpoint_keymaker.py (real file-backed sqlite saver per test conventions: hops-as-supersteps history count, counter persistence across resume, Operator-after-exit interrupt+resume, sync+async), budget error/exit tests in test_keymaker.py. ACCEPTANCE: budget error and exit paths tested; checkpoint suite green sync+async.

Design doc (decision-complete, cite it): docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md. Decision log: docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md. Research grounding: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md. Epic: neograph-t1f7z (feature bead neograph-07inf). Execute via /dev-practices:execute discipline: TDD (failing test first), quality gates (uv run --extra dev pytest on touched suites, mypy, ruff) before commit; commit per task, no push until consolidation task.
design:
## Core Invariant
The hop budget is enforced (counter read-modify-write + max_hops check) INSIDE the keymaker wrapper BEFORE the Command(goto) is emitted, using the ENTRY member's max_hops/on_exhaust and a single shared entry-keyed counter, so every hop remains exactly one checkpointed superstep and the counter persists verbatim across resume — never a new exception class, never a router, never a state-schema change.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Thread the entry's budget into every member's wrapper.** In _wiring.py:_add_keymaker_mesh (:735 entry=members[0]), extract entry.modifier_set.keymaker.max_hops / .on_exhaust / entry.name and pass them into make_keymaker_fn for EVERY member (:748). Do NOT read the per-member keymaker for the budget — non-entry members carry defaults. (Reuse the existing loop over members; add 3 params to the call.)
2. **Add the counter RMW + budget check at the factory.py:160-163 seam.** Thread `state` into _to_command (keymaker_wrapper already holds it at :166-170). Compute `count_field = StateKeys.handoff_hops(entry_field)`; `current = adapt_state(state).get_counter(count_field)` (copy _state_write.py:137-143). Fork on the entry budget exactly like _wiring.py:559-567: if exhausted and on_exhaust=='error' -> ExecutionError.build('handoff exceeded max_hops', node=entry_name, expected=..., found=...) (SAME class as Loop); if 'exit' -> Command(goto=exit_name, update={**update, count_field:n, channel_key:payload}); else emit the goto with update also carrying count_field:current+1. TDD the off-by-one boundary FIRST.
3. **Raise the recursion floor per mesh** in runner.py:_ensure_agent_recursion_limit (:51-87). Add a mesh term: for each contiguous Keymaker mesh (predicate: classify_modifiers(n)[0]==ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER, as state.py:250), += entry.max_hops. Sum alongside the existing agent_cost; only raise the floor.
4. **Budget error/exit tests in tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py** — copy the RouteHop/_build_mesh scaffold (:232-373); add a member that never routes to HANDOFF_END so it exhausts. Assert 'error' raises ExecutionError naming the entry; 'exit' leaves via the exit node with the last payload on the bus and downstream runs.
5. **New tests/test_checkpoint_keymaker.py** — copy the file-backed sqlite exemplar (test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py:229-283): sync SqliteSaver + async AsyncSqliteSaver via tmp_path, same thread_id. Assert (a) hops-as-supersteps: len(get_state_history) == hop count; (b) counter persists across a resume on the same thread; (c) Operator-AFTER-mesh-exit interrupt+resume (copy test_checkpoint_sqlite_async.py:201-260; Operator on a mesh MEMBER is illegal per D4, so place it after the pass-through exit node). Sync + async.
6. **Gates**: uv run --extra dev pytest on tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py + tests/test_checkpoint_keymaker.py (+ the existing keymaker/checkpoint suites), mypy, ruff. TDD (failing test first) per bead. Commit per task; no push until consolidation. No changes to modifiers.py/state.py/_state_keys.py needed (max_hops already declared, counter field already built, StateKeys already present).
notes:
## Findings (T3: hop budget + checkpoint semantics)

REUSE-FIRST: every mechanism T3 needs already exists as a Loop analog or a pre-seeded seam. No new primitives, no new exception class.

- **The T3 seam is a literal commented block**: factory.py:160-163 inside make_keymaker_fn's `_to_command`. The Command(goto) + channel-write + target-check are already live (T2); only the counter RMW + max_hops check go here, BEFORE line 163's `goto = ...`. Design §3.4/§6/§7 all verified against source.
- **Loop RMW counter exemplar** (the pattern to copy): _state_write.py:137-143 — reads `state.get_counter(count_field)` (bootstrap absent/None->0), writes `current+1` into the update dict. StateKeys.loop_count is the sibling of StateKeys.handoff_hops.
- **Counter read plumbing already exists**: StateBus.get_counter (_state_bus.py:69-70 dict / :91-92 model) + adapt_state (_state_bus.py:98). The keymaker_wrapper (factory.py:166-170) already holds `state`; `_to_command` currently takes only `update` — thread `state` in so it can call `adapt_state(state).get_counter(count_field)`. Read the SHARED counter from incoming state, not from update.
- **Hop-counter state field is ALREADY declared** (T1/T2, runtime-inert): state.py:257 `fields[StateKeys.handoff_hops(entry_field)] = (int, 0)`, keyed off the mesh entry (state.py:250-253). neo_-prefixed -> excluded from schema fingerprint (design §7; existing rule state.py:410-419). Nothing to add in state.py for T3.
- **StateKeys.handoff_hops**: _state_keys.py:130-136 (`neo_handoff_hops_{field}`), sibling of loop_count (:125-127). No change needed — the fragment guard (G2) already covers it.
- **Loop exhaust exemplar** (the on_exhaust fork to mirror): _wiring.py:559-567 in _make_loop_router — `if count >= loop.max_iterations: if on_exhaust=='error': raise ExecutionError.build(...); return exit_name`. Keymaker's fork lives in the FACTORY wrapper (not a router — the mesh has no router), but the shape and ExecutionError.build(expected=/found=/node=) call are identical. Same ExecutionError class — NO new exception type.
- **Recursion floor**: runner.py:51-87 _ensure_agent_recursion_limit. Currently sums only agent/act cycle costs (iter_nodes at :72, `node.mode in ('agent','act')`). T3 adds a mesh term: for each mesh, +entry.max_hops supersteps (a K-hop mesh consumes K supersteps). Detect meshes via classify_modifiers==ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER (same predicate state.py:250 uses). Only RAISES the floor; keep user-supplied higher limit.
- **BUDGET IS ENTRY-ONLY, wrapper is per-member (KEY SUBTLETY)**: make_keymaker_fn (factory.py:105) receives the MEMBER's own keymaker; non-entry members default max_hops=10/on_exhaust='error'. The budget must use the ENTRY's max_hops/on_exhaust. _add_keymaker_mesh (_wiring.py:735 `entry=members[0]`) is where to source them and thread `entry.modifier_set.keymaker.max_hops`/`.on_exhaust` (+ entry.name for the error) into make_keymaker_fn for EVERY member. Do NOT read the member's own keymaker for the budget.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/factory.py:105-173 — make_keymaker_fn / _to_command; the T3 seam is the comment at :160-163. Thread `state` into _to_command; add count_field RMW + max_hops check + on_exhaust fork before `goto=`.
- src/neograph/_state_write.py:137-143 — Loop counter RMW exemplar (copy the get_counter/+1 shape).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:714-769 — _add_keymaker_mesh; `entry=members[0]` (:735); pass entry's budget params + entry.name to make_keymaker_fn in the member loop (:748).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:559-567 — Loop on_exhaust fork (error->raise / exit->exit_name) to mirror in the wrapper.
- src/neograph/runner.py:51-87 — _ensure_agent_recursion_limit; add per-mesh +max_hops term.
- src/neograph/state.py:250-258 — hop-counter + channel fields already declared (no T3 change).
- src/neograph/_state_bus.py:69-92,98 — get_counter + adapt_state (the read path).
- tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py:229-283 — file-backed sqlite exemplar: `db=str(tmp_path/'x.db')`; sync `with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(db) as saver` + `compile(..., checkpointer=saver, **build_test_compile_kwargs())`; async `async with AsyncSqliteSaver.from_conn_string(db)` + neograph.arun. Same thread_id across runs. COPY THIS for test_checkpoint_keymaker.py.
- tests/test_checkpoint_sqlite_async.py:72-97,201-260 — interrupt+resume exemplar (Operator interrupt_when -> `__interrupt__` in result -> re-run on same thread to resume). Use for the Operator-AFTER-mesh-exit interrupt+resume case (D4: Operator on a mesh member is illegal; place it AFTER the exit node).
- tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py:232-373 — T2 runtime-routing scaffold: RouteHop payload (plain-str `goto` + `hops:int`), _build_mesh via Node.scripted + register_scripted. COPY this for the budget error/exit tests (add a member that never routes to HANDOFF_END so it exhausts).
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md §3.4/§6/§7 — decision-complete spec. keymaker-decision-log D4 (Operator combo illegal), D10 (read-side channel threading) — both verified in source.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **Off-by-one (pin with a TDD test)**: Loop increments in _build_state_update then the router checks `count >= max_iterations`. Keymaker does BOTH increment and check in one wrapper. Decide: check `current >= max_hops` (before incr) vs `current+1 >= max_hops` (after incr). Match design's 'max_hops=6 -> 6 hops allowed' intent; write the boundary test first (a mesh that runs exactly max_hops then must exhaust) and let it pin the semantics. Counter starts 0; each member increments the SHARED entry-keyed counter.
- **'exit' writes counter too**: the on_exhaust='exit' branch returns Command(goto=exit_name, update={**update, count_field:n, channel_key:payload}) — no raise, last payload stays on the bus (design §3.4 deliberate rename vs Loop's 'last').
- **Shared counter across members**: because all members key the counter by entry_field, the RMW must read incoming `state` (not the local update dict) so hops accumulate across DIFFERENT members' wrappers, not per-member.
- **Recursion floor interaction**: a mesh with agent/act members is already illegal (D-MEMBER-MODES), so the mesh term and the agent term never overlap on the same node — but a construct can have BOTH a mesh and separate agent nodes; sum both terms.
- **Checkpoint fingerprint**: neo_handoff_hops_* is neo_-prefixed -> already excluded from fingerprint (state.py:410-419); no upgrade-invalidation risk. Verify hops-as-supersteps by counting graph.get_state_history entries (one checkpoint/superstep).
- No doc/code contradictions found. D4 and D10 both hold in source.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-0umvg)

Pattern: hand-rolled hop/loop counter access (f-string field-name join OR raw state.get/getattr for a counter) instead of the canonical StateKeys.handoff_hops(field) + adapt_state(state).get_counter(field) helpers; and hand-rolled on_exhaust fork instead of the Loop ExecutionError.build shape.
Scan classification: SYNTACTIC (regex-able) -> single-executor scan, no fan-out.
Scan commands (reproducible, re-run verbatim in sweep-verify):
  A: grep -rnE 'f"[^"]*neo_(handoff_hops|loop_count)_' src/neograph/
  B: grep -rnE '\.get\(\s*[^)]*hops|getattr\([^)]*hops' src/neograph/
  C: grep -rn handoff_hops src/neograph/
  D: grep -rn get_counter src/neograph/
Total instances found: 2 f-string joins (both canonical definitions), 0 bypass sites.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _state_keys.py:127 | f"neo_loop_count_{field_name}" | ALLOWLIST | canonical DEFINITION inside StateKeys.loop_count -- this IS the helper, not a bypass |
| 2 | _state_keys.py:136 | f"neo_handoff_hops_{field_name}" | ALLOWLIST | canonical DEFINITION inside StateKeys.handoff_hops -- this IS the helper |
| 3 | _state_write.py:142,195 | state.get_counter(count_field) | ALLOWLIST | already canonical read (Loop RMW exemplar T3 copies) |
| 4 | _wiring.py:558 | bus.get_counter(count_field) | ALLOWLIST | already canonical read (loop_router) |
| 5 | _subconstruct.py:178 | bus.get_counter(count_field) | ALLOWLIST | already canonical read |
| 6 | _wiring.py:560-567 | on_exhaust=="error" -> ExecutionError.build(...) | ALLOWLIST | canonical exhaust fork; T3 mirrors this exact shape in the factory wrapper (no new exception class) |

Conclusion: disease is NOT spread. Every counter access in the tree already routes through StateKeys.* + get_counter; the on_exhaust fork already uses ExecutionError.build. T3 introduces NEW code at the factory.py:157-163 seam and MUST follow these existing canonical forms (StateKeys.handoff_hops for the field, adapt_state(state).get_counter for the read, ExecutionError.build mirroring _wiring.py:560-567). No MIGRATE rows, no DEFER rows. 0 follow-up tickets required.
## Architect Review (neograph-qxh8y.4)

Verified against source: factory.py:145-169 (_to_command seam + wrappers hold state), _wiring.py:735-761 (_add_keymaker_mesh entry=members[0], per-member loop), _state_write.py:137-143 (Loop RMW exemplar), _wiring.py:555-567 (Loop on_exhaust fork), runner.py:51-87 (_ensure_agent_recursion_limit), state.py:250-258 (counter/channel fields declared), construct.py:58 (iter_nodes), _wiring.py:696-711 (_contiguous_keymaker_mesh). All cited lines accurate.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Recursion-floor step (plan step 3) is under-specified against the tool it names AND has an early-return trap. (a) iter_nodes (construct.py:58) LEAF-FLATTENS and discards level/contiguity, so it cannot identify a mesh ENTRY nor group a contiguous run -- a per-mesh 'entry.max_hops' sum is not directly expressible via the classify predicate over iter_nodes as written. (b) The existing guard 'if agent_cost == 0: return config' (runner.py:77) fires BEFORE the floor is applied; a mesh-only construct (no agent/act nodes) would take that early return and NEVER raise the floor -> a large-max_hops mesh hits LangGraph's default ceiling before the budget-exhaust fork fires (GraphRecursionError). Suggestion: reconcile the zero-guard to a combined total (agent_cost + mesh_cost) BEFORE the early return; and either (i) reuse a level-ordered walk like _contiguous_keymaker_mesh over construct.nodes (recursing sub-constructs) to add entry.max_hops ONCE per mesh, or (ii) explicitly adopt a per-member iter_nodes sum as a documented SAFE OVER-approximation (floor only raises; the entry member itself carries the real max_hops so the sum is always >= the true requirement). Do NOT hand-roll a per-mesh sum that re-derives the entry from a non-entry member (defaults max_hops=10) -- that under-counts when entry.max_hops>10.

- [LOW] Finding: The hops-as-supersteps checkpoint assertion 'len(get_state_history) == hop count' (plan step 5a) is almost certainly an off-by-constant: get_state_history also includes the initial input checkpoint, the pass-through __handoff_exit_ node, and any downstream (Operator-after-exit) nodes. Suggestion: assert 'hops + fixed overhead' or count history growth between two marker nodes; let the TDD run pin the real constant rather than raw hop count.

- [LOW] Finding: Off-by-one boundary is adequately de-risked (step 2 + risk note: TDD-first, matched to design intent 'max_hops=N -> N hops allowed'), but the plan does not state whether the ENTRY member's own execution counts as hop 1 or whether hop 1 is the first inter-member handoff. Suggestion: the boundary test should assert the exact meaning of the counter increment (who increments first) against design section 3.4, and cover the 'exit' path hop count too, not just 'error'.

Confirmed SOUND (survived attack): entry-only budget threaded as make_keymaker_fn closure params sourced from entry=members[0] (consistent with T2 closure-capture threading; not literally D10's normalizer-stamp but the appropriate analog); counter read from incoming state not the local update dict (correct for cross-member accumulation -- update never carries the counter, so a from-update read would always bootstrap 0 and break accumulation); count_field '(int,0)' plain field = last-write-wins overwrite, correct for per-superstep accumulate; on_exhaust='exit' writes count_field + channel_key:payload (last payload survives); on_exhaust='error' reuses ExecutionError.build, no new class (Loop parity); neo_-prefix excludes counter from schema fingerprint (no resume-invalidation); D4 Operator-after-exit placement correct; each hop is one Command(goto) = one checkpointed superstep.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Refinement (post-review, team-lead adjudicated) — neograph-qxh8y.12

RECURSION FLOOR (MEDIUM resolution, binding):
- In _ensure_agent_recursion_limit (runner.py:51-87): compute mesh_cost = sum of entry.max_hops over every Keymaker mesh, AND agent_cost as today. Reconcile the zero-guard (runner.py:77) to `if agent_cost == 0 and mesh_cost == 0: return config` so a mesh-ONLY construct still raises the floor. Combined required = agent_cost + mesh_cost (+ existing base). Floor only RAISES (max(user_limit, required)); never lowers a user-supplied higher limit.
- Mesh detection: sum max_hops over nodes whose keymaker slot DECLARES max_hops (entry-only per T1 — non-entry members do not set it). Walk that reaches entry nodes (recurse sub-constructs). title: Self-loop param resolution by type in @node decorator
description:
## Problem
@node requires parameter names to match upstream node names. Self-loop nodes naturally name params after the concept ('draft'), not the upstream ('seed'). When loop_when is set and a param doesn't match upstream by name, the decorator should resolve by type.

## Fix
In decorators.py _build_construct_from_decorated (~line 1137), before raising ConstructError for unmatched params, add loop-aware fallback:

1. New helper _resolve_loop_self_param(node, param_name, decorated, sub_by_field):
   - Get param type from node.inputs[param_name]
   - Find all upstreams producing compatible type (via effective_producer_type + _types_compatible)
   - If exactly 1 match: return that upstream field_name
   - If multiple matches: raise ConstructError with disambiguation message
   - If 0 matches: return None (fall through to existing error)

2. In the adjacency loop, when pname not in decorated and node has Loop modifier:
   - Call _resolve_loop_self_param
   - If resolved, add to adjacency and continue

3. In inputs cleanup section (~line 1209): rewrite the inputs dict key from original param name to resolved upstream name (e.g. 'draft' -> 'seed') so _extract_input can find it in state on first iteration.

4. Track the param rename mapping and pass it through to _register_node_scripted so the scripted shim maps args correctly.

## Import needed
from neograph._construct_validation import effective_producer_type, _types_compatible
(Check if _types_compatible is private — may need to make it importable or duplicate the check)

## Files
- src/neograph/decorators.py

## Verification
- test_self_loop_respects_max_iterations passes (param 'draft' resolves to 'seed' by type)
- test_self_loop_raises_on_exhaust_error passes (same fix)
- test_self_loop_exits_when_condition_met still passes (uses named param 'seed', unaffected)
- New test: ambiguous type match raises ConstructError
- Existing tests: uv run pytest -q passes
design:
## Architecture Decision
Add _resolve_loop_self_param helper to decorators.py. When @node has loop_when and a param doesn't match upstream by name, find exactly one upstream of matching type. Ambiguous → ConstructError. Rewrite inputs dict key to resolved upstream name. Track param rename for scripted shim registration.

Follows the fan_out_params pattern (classify params that don't match upstream, then handle in inputs cleanup).

No changes to _extract_input needed — the Loop path reads from own field on re-entry, and the renamed key ensures first-iteration reads from the correct upstream.
notes:
## Findings
- The @node decorator requires param names to match upstream node names (decorators.py:1137-1158)
- Self-loop nodes name params after the concept ('draft') not the upstream ('seed')
- The adjacency loop at line 1137 raises ConstructError for unmatched params
- effective_producer_type in _construct_validation.py returns the state-bus type for a producer
- _types_compatible in _construct_validation.py checks type compatibility (handles generics, subclass, list/dict compat)

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/decorators.py:1110-1170 — adjacency building loop
- src/neograph/decorators.py:1209-1235 — inputs cleanup section
- src/neograph/decorators.py:1237-1248 — scripted shim registration
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:30-59 — effective_producer_type
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:435-469 — _types_compatible

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Multiple upstreams of same type → must error, not silently pick one
- inputs dict key rewrite needed so _extract_input finds the upstream by name on first iteration
- Scripted shim registration must handle the renamed param (original name in fn signature, resolved name in inputs dict)

## Core Invariant
Every @node parameter resolves to exactly one upstream by name or unambiguously by type — no silent guessing when multiple candidates exist.

## Pattern Match
The fan_out_params dict (line 1063-1076) is the closest pattern: params that don't match upstream names are classified as fan-out receivers. The loop self-reference follows the same structure — classify, then rewrite inputs.
## Regression Tests
- test_self_loop_respects_max_iterations: FAILED (ConstructError: param 'draft' doesn't match)
- test_self_loop_raises_on_exhaust_error: FAILED (same reason)
- test_raises_when_loop_param_ambiguous_type_match: FAILED (no resolver yet, hits generic error)
All fail for the right reason — the _resolve_loop_self_param helper doesn't exist yet.
## Implementation
- Added _resolve_loop_self_param helper: finds exactly one upstream of matching type, errors on ambiguity
- Integrated into adjacency loop with loop_param_renames tracking
- Inputs dict key rewrite: 'draft' → 'seed' in inputs cleanup
- Scripted shim: added loop_renames map so shim reads correct key from input_data
- Quality: 428 passed (+4 from baseline), 2 failed (both need test rewrite for new API)

title: Error-hierarchy rule + re-parent ResourceExpiredError/NonIdempotentReplayError under ExecutionError + di.py raise-style migration + parentage guard (review PAT-01)
description:
From the 2026-07-07 pre-release review (synthesis: .claude/code-review/070726_prerelease_arc/synthesis.md, HIGH-01 live-verified). THE PATTERN: error types are parented ad hoc per ticket — PromptVarMissing subclasses ExecutionError while ResourceExpiredError and NonIdempotentReplayError (equally runtime failures raised during node execution) subclass bare NeographError, so a consumer's except ExecutionError around run() silently misses expiry/replay failures. This ships as public API at 0.6.0 — fix before release.

SCOPE: (1) write THE RULE into errors.py module docstring: failures raised during graph execution subclass ExecutionError; assembly-time -> ConstructError; configuration/setup -> ConfigurationError; compile -> CompileError. (2) Re-parent ResourceExpiredError + NonIdempotentReplayError under ExecutionError (0.x no-compat rule — no shims). (3) Decide-and-document the two PRE-EXISTING direct children: StateMissingError (runtime read miss -> likely re-parent) and CheckpointSchemaError (resume-time schema decision — arguably ConfigurationError-adjacent; the ticket owner decides WITH the rule, then documents the rationale in the class docstring either way). (4) CON-02: migrate di.py's legacy raw _ExecutionError(...) raises to the 4-field .build(hint=) style — one style, whole module. (5) GUARD: a parentage test pinning category->parent for every public error type, so the next new error cannot re-drift (table-driven; new types must be added to the table or the guard fails). (6) Website/API docs: the error-hierarchy section reflects the rule. TDD: an except-ExecutionError-catches-expiry E2E first (red today).
close_reason: Wrote THE RULE (parentage by lifecycle phase) into errors.py docstring; re-parented ResourceExpiredError, NonIdempotentReplayError, StateMissingError, NodeOutputError under ExecutionError and CheckpointSchemaError under ConfigurationError (documented rationale in each docstring); migrated di.py's 5 legacy raw _ExecutionError raises to .build(hint=) style; added tests/test_error_hierarchy.py (E2E except-ExecutionError + table-driven parentage guard w/ completeness check); updated website api.mdx error-hierarchy section. title: [EPIC] Portal x Agent Spec: safe dynamic routing + round-trip-faithful interop
description:
Umbrella coordinating the Portal primitive (epic neograph-07inf) and Agent Spec interop (epic neograph-2ev48). Two tracks, sequenced so the round-trip fidelity contract is defined once.

INVARIANT (Portal): dynamic routing targets a region's declared ENTRY PORT, never its interior — a class of LangGraph deadlocks/runaway loops stays unrepresentable. Grounded in the port-taxonomy design doc.

Export owns the round-trip fidelity contract — you cannot write a faithful reader before deciding what the writer emits. to_agent_spec emits x-neograph reconstruction metadata so a neograph-produced spec re-imports losslessly (same Oracle/Each/Loop/Portal primitives that compile to LangGraph); from_agent_spec READS that metadata (primitive-level fallback for external specs); the round-trip test is the proof. Tradeoff: export is the harder direction (Oracle->ParallelFlow lowering is the flagship gap), so this front-loads difficulty — accepted for contract cleanliness.
