title: json_mode: send provider-native response_format={"type":"json_object"} (or document provider_kwargs), don't rely on schema-in-prompt + text parse
description:
CONTEXT: output_strategy=\"json_mode\" currently (src/neograph/_llm.py:144, 188-189) injects the describe_type schema into the prompt and parses the model's raw TEXT via _parse_json_response, WITHOUT sending the provider's native JSON mode (response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"}). Confirmed: `grep -rniE \"response_format\" src/neograph/` returns NOTHING. So json_mode reliability rests entirely on the model emitting clean-enough JSON in free text — a parse-failure surface.

EVIDENCE / IMPACT (from ox-troubleshooting-demo, gemini-2.5-pro via OpenRouter):
- We switched the reasoning verdict nodes (assess/synthesize/explain) to json_mode so the model can reason-then-coerce (vs 'structured' = provider constrained decoding, which skips the free reasoning pass).
- Under 'structured' we saw an intermittent 'structured output decoded to None' ExecutionError (the fail-loud in _llm_dispatch.py). Under json_mode the parse depends on the model's raw text being valid JSON.
- REFERENCE IMPL that works: ~/projects/piarch (deepseek/glm) binds `llm.bind(response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"})` + max_tokens=16384 (scripts/run_eval.py:206-208; evals/_llm_factory.py). The provider's native JSON mode GUARANTEES valid JSON, removing the parse-failure class. For a THINKING model (gemini-2.5-pro, deepseek-reasoner) response_format=json_object does NOT cost the reasoning (thinking is internal / a separate reasoning field), so you keep BOTH reliable parse AND free reasoning.

PROPOSAL:
1. For providers that support it, json_mode should SEND response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"} on the model call (OpenAI / Gemini / DeepSeek OpenAI-compat all support it). Note: OpenAI-compat json_object requires the word 'json' to appear in the prompt — the injected describe_type schema likely satisfies this; verify.
2. If not made automatic, DOCUMENT that json_mode users should pass response_format via LlmConfig.provider_kwargs, and note reasoning-inline behaviour for reasoning models.
3. Clarify the docstring (_llm.py:144) — it reads 'inject schema into prompt, LLM returns raw JSON, framework parses', which implies more guarantee than there is (nothing forces the model to return JSON).

EVIDENCE FILES: src/neograph/_llm.py:144,188-189; src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py (parse + recover_dsml + 'decoded to None' fail-loud); ~/projects/piarch/scripts/run_eval.py:206-208 + evals/_llm_factory.py. Reported from ox-troubleshooting-demo overnight json_mode reasoning work.
notes:
2026-07-07 ANALYSIS + RECOMMENDED SOLUTION (maintainer-reviewed; claims verified: response_format appears 0 times in src; json_mode = describe_type schema string + text parse only).

THE SEAM (verified): _prepare_structured_call in _llm.py is the SHARED pure preamble both invoke_structured and ainvoke_structured consume (post-ykun extraction) — it already branches on strategy == json_mode to build output_schema and returns (llm, messages, strategy, llm_log). Native binding is a few lines THERE: when strategy is json_mode, return llm.bind(response_format={'type':'json_object'}) instead of bare llm. ONE site, both twins inherit, twin-thinness preserved by construction. Also check the OTHER json_mode call paths reached via _llm_retry (_invoke_json_with_retry / recover_dsml receive the llm object — if they receive the already-bound llm from the caller, nothing more needed; verify and pin).

PROVIDER-COMPAT (the real design question — a hard bind breaks providers without response_format support, e.g. ChatAnthropic passes it to an API that rejects it): do NOT provider-sniff by class name (drift) and do NOT switch to with_structured_output(method='json_mode') (it would replace neograph's parse/recovery machinery and lose the reason-then-coerce raw-text path the consumer explicitly wants). Instead mirror the _llm_structured_compat PHILOSOPHY (its own header: a quirk is a new decorator, never a branch): ATTEMPT-BIND-AND-FALL-BACK — first call with the bound kwargs; on a provider rejection identifying response_format (TypeError / BadRequest), log ONCE (json_mode_native_unsupported, provider=...) and retry unbound, keeping the existing schema-in-prompt + parse path as the unchanged fallback. One shared helper; the parse machinery stays as the universal safety net either way. Consumers keep the manual llm_factory bind (the piarch pattern) as the documented escape hatch — no new LlmConfig knob needed.

THE JSON-WORD REQUIREMENT (ticket item 1 caveat): OpenAI-compat json_object REQUIRES the literal word json in the messages. VERIFY the injected describe_type instruction block contains it; if not guaranteed, the json_mode preamble appends one instruction line. Pin with a test either way — this is the silent-400 trap.

ALSO IN SCOPE: (a) docstring fix at _llm.py:144 (current text implies a guarantee that does not exist); document reasoning-model behavior (response_format does not suppress internal reasoning on gemini-2.5-pro/deepseek-reasoner — the consumer's reason-then-coerce motivation); (b) FAKES: StructuredFake/TextFake (neograph.testing.fakes) grow bind-kwargs capture so tests can assert response_format was bound — needed for non-vacuous tests without a live provider; (c) tests in tests/modes/test_output_strategies.py: bound-by-default, fallback-on-rejection (fake raising the provider error once), json-word guard, sync+async cells; (d) structured/text strategies UNCHANGED — zero behavior change outside json_mode.

WAVE PLACEMENT: Wave 6, second seat beside neograph-4atf — regions fully disjoint (_llm.py/_llm_config docstring/fakes/test_output_strategies vs _agent_cycle/state.py). Wired into the y5ux gate per the everything-in-scope rule.
close_reason: Landed on develop (bb38d63): json_mode binds native response_format at the _prepare_structured_call seam so both sync+async twins inherit; _NativeJsonModeLLM attempt-bind-and-fall-back (invoke+ainvoke), json-word guard, fakes bind-capture in neograph.testing.fakes. Parse machinery unchanged as universal fallback; structured/text unchanged.

title: Node.outputs refactor — N named outputs + gather tool context
description:
When a gather node runs a ReAct tool loop, the tool interactions (calls + results) are consumed internally and lost at the node boundary. Only the final parsed output is passed downstream. This makes it impossible for a downstream produce node to see the raw evidence — it only sees the exploration model's summary.

## The pattern this blocks

R1 explores with tools → Gemini scores the exploration with a rubric.

Today this requires a scripted node that manually manages the message list, formats tool results into a research_packet string, and calls the rubric model. It's ~80 lines of procedural code that should be two declarative nodes:

    explore (gather, R1, tools) → ExplorationResult + ToolContext
    score (produce, Gemini, rubric) → SingleClaimResult

But the rubric step needs what R1 actually read (raw tool results), not just what R1 concluded. Without tool context exposure, you either:
1. Ask R1 to self-summarize (Option A — works but lossy, and fails with cheap models)
2. Write a scripted node that manages the message list manually (current piarch approach — works but defeats the purpose of declarative graphs)

## Proposed design

Gather mode optionally exposes tool interactions as sidecar data alongside the parsed output.

### Approach 1: Auto-filled field on output model

class ExplorationResult(BaseModel):
    conclusion: str
    tool_context: Annotated[list[ToolInteraction], GatherContext]  # framework fills this

class ToolInteraction(BaseModel):
    tool_name: str
    args: dict
    result: str
    duration_ms: int = 0

The GatherContext annotation tells neograph's gather dispatch: after the ReAct loop completes, collect tool interactions and inject them into this field before returning. The prompt_compiler for the downstream node sees the full tool_context and can render it.

### Approach 2: Sidecar state (not on the model)

@node(mode='gather', output=ExplorationResult,
      gather_config={'expose_tool_context': True})
def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ExplorationResult: ...

When expose_tool_context=True, neograph stores the tool interactions in a framework state field (e.g., neo_tool_context_{node_name}) that the prompt_compiler can access for the next node. Not on the output model — invisible to the user's types but available in prompts.

### Approach 3: Conversation continuation

The gather and produce nodes share a message history. The produce node's prompt_compiler receives the full conversation from the gather step, not just the parsed output. This is the most powerful but requires conversation-passing infrastructure.

## Use cases beyond piarch

1. **Audit/compliance**: rubric step must verify against raw evidence, not the exploration model's summary. The tool results ARE the evidence chain.

2. **Multi-judge**: three rubric models score the same exploration from different angles. Each needs the same raw tool results, not three different R1 summaries.

3. **Replay/debugging**: when an eval shows a bad disposition, you want to see exactly which nodes were read and what they said. Tool context is the debug log.

4. **Cheap explore + expensive judge**: fast model (V3, Gemini Flash) does tool calling. Expensive model (R1, Opus) does scoring. The fast model doesn't need to summarize well — it just calls the right tools. The expensive model reads the raw results.

5. **Provenance tracking**: every LLM decision should be traceable to its inputs. Tool context is the 'show your work' for gather nodes.

## The bigger principle

Every scripted node in a consumer's pipeline is evidence of a missing framework primitive. The gather→produce chain with tool context exposure eliminates one of the most common scripted-node patterns: 'call LLM with tools, format the tool results, call a second LLM with the formatted results.' That's 80+ lines of procedural code per instance in piarch. It should be two declarative @node functions.

## Recommendation

Start with Approach 1 (auto-filled field). It's the simplest, most explicit, and doesn't add hidden state. The user declares what they want in the schema; the framework fills it. The prompt_compiler renders it for the downstream node. Clean, typed, observable.

## Success criteria

1. gather node's tool interactions available to downstream produce node without scripted code
2. ToolInteraction model captures: tool_name, args, result (at minimum)
3. prompt_compiler renders tool context readably (not JSON-escaped)
4. Works with Each fan-out (per-item tool context, not global)
5. Langfuse traces show tool context as part of the generation span
6. Zero change to existing gather mode behavior when expose is not requested
design:
## Refined Design Direction (2026-04-06)

### Core Insight
Tool results are already typed — every @tool function has a return type. The ReAct loop collects N typed results during execution. Today, factory._make_tool_fn discards them after the LLM produces its final structured output. Instead, keep them as a secondary named output.

### The Pattern
No extra LLM calls. No message history accumulation. Just typed tool results preserved alongside the structured output.

```python
# Tool returns typed data (already true today)
@tool(output=FileContent)
def read_file(path: str) -> FileContent:
    return FileContent(path=path, content=open(path).read())

# Gather node: ReAct loop calls tools, LLM produces structured conclusion.
# Tool results are auto-collected — zero extra LLM calls.
@node(output=ExplorationResult, mode='gather', tools=[read_file, search_code])
def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ExplorationResult: ...

# Judge node: sees BOTH the conclusion AND the raw tool evidence.
# The renderer (ni6) formats tool results into the prompt.
@node(output=RubricScore, mode='produce', renderer=XmlRenderer())
def score(
    explore: ExplorationResult,           # LLM's conclusion
    explore_tool_log: list[FileContent],  # raw evidence, auto-collected
) -> RubricScore: ...
```

### What Changes
1. **invoke_with_tools** returns tool results alongside the parsed output (tuple or dataclass)
2. **_make_tool_fn** writes tool results to a secondary state field (e.g., `{node_name}_tool_log`)
3. **state.py compile_state_model** adds the tool_log field for gather/execute nodes
4. **The downstream node's inputs dict** references `explore_tool_log` by name — same wiring as any other upstream, via the Node.inputs dict

### What Does NOT Change
- No message history accumulation (no MessagesState, no add_messages)
- No GatherContext annotation on the output model
- No new Node fields beyond what Node.inputs already supports
- No extra LLM calls — tool results are already typed
- The renderer (ni6, shipped) handles formatting for the judge's prompt

### Open Design Questions
1. **Naming convention**: `{node_name}_tool_log` as the state field? Or a dotted path like `explore.tool_log`?
2. **Opt-in or always-on**: Should tool results always be preserved, or only when a downstream node declares dependency on them?
3. **Type of the collection**: `list[ToolInteraction]` (generic wrapper with tool_name, args, result) or `list[Union[FileContent, SearchResult, ...]]` (preserving the per-tool return types)?
4. **Multi-output generalization**: Does this lead to Node supporting N outputs (dict[str, type]) mirroring N inputs? Or is tool_log a special case?

### Relationship to Node.inputs Refactor
This is the output-side mirror of the Node.inputs refactor (neograph-kqd). The kqd epic established: a node has N named inputs keyed by upstream name. The natural extension: a node has M named outputs. The downstream node's inputs dict references them by `{upstream_name}.{output_name}` or `{upstream_name}_{output_name}`.

### Why NOT Message History
The research showed LangGraph's MessagesState could solve this. But message history is the wrong abstraction: it's prose-level (ToolMessage.content is a string), not type-level. The value of neograph is typed end-to-end. Tool results should stay typed. The renderer converts them to prompt text at the last mile — not before.
notes:
## Deep Research: Tool Context in LLM Frameworks (2026-04-06)

### Summary Table

| Framework | Tool results are... | Downstream sees... | First-class? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LangGraph** | ToolMessage in messages state | Raw via state['messages'] | Yes |
| **CrewAI** | Mediated through agent summary | Agent's summary (lossy) | No |
| **AutoGen/AG2** | Events + message dicts | Raw via ToolCallExecutionEvent | Partial |
| **DSPy** | trajectory dict on Prediction | observation_{i} has raw results | Partial |
| **Pydantic AI** | ToolCallPart/ToolReturnPart | Raw via all_messages() | Yes |
| **OpenAI Agents SDK** | ToolCallOutputItem in new_items | Full history via handoff (filterable) | Yes |
| **Claude API** | tool_use/tool_result content blocks | Raw via messages array | Yes |
| **LlamaIndex** | Custom events / ctx.store | Whatever you put there | Partial |

### Key Finding
LangGraph, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents SDK, and raw Claude API all make tool results first-class and visible downstream by default. CrewAI is the weakest — tool results are consumed by the agent and only summaries flow downstream (the exact lossy pattern we're trying to avoid).

### The LangGraph-Native Path
Since neograph compiles to LangGraph StateGraph, the most natural mechanism is leveraging LangGraph's native `messages` accumulator alongside neograph's typed state bus:

- `MessagesState` with `add_messages` reducer accumulates ALL messages (Human, AI, Tool) across nodes
- `ToolMessage` objects with `tool_call_id` link back to AIMessage.tool_calls
- Downstream nodes access full history via state['messages']
- Subgraphs can share the messages channel with the parent graph

### Three Options Re-evaluated

**Option A: Coexist typed outputs + messages accumulator** (LangGraph-native)
Add an optional `messages` field to the compiled state with `add_messages` reducer. LLM-mode nodes append their full message history (including ToolMessages). Downstream nodes can opt into reading state['messages']. Zero new neograph machinery — just expose what LangGraph already provides.

**Option B: GatherContext annotation** (original proposal from the issue)
Output model declares which field receives tool history. Framework scans annotations and injects. More explicit but more machinery.

**Option C: Pydantic AI pattern — all_messages() on result**
After a node's ReAct loop, expose the message list as an inspectable property. Closest to Pydantic AI and OpenAI SDK patterns.

### Emerging Academic Consensus
The field converges on provenance graphs (W3C PROV-O). Each tool invocation gets a unique ID, outputs link to downstream inputs via derivedFrom. Agent-as-a-Judge research (Jan 2026) found that judge agents seeing raw evidence outperform those seeing explorer summaries.

### The Real Question
The issue's original framing (three approaches for injecting tool data) may be solving the wrong problem. The deeper question: should neograph's compile() output a state model that includes a messages accumulator when the pipeline has LLM-mode nodes? If yes, the tool context problem solves itself — it's LangGraph's native capability, not something neograph needs to reinvent.

### References
- LangGraph MessagesState + add_messages: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/quickstart
- Pydantic AI all_messages(): https://ai.pydantic.dev/message-history/
- OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/handoffs/
- PROV-AGENT (Oak Ridge, 2025): https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02866
- Agent-as-a-Judge survey: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.05111v1
- Graphectory (Liu et al., 2025): typed node/edge provenance model
## Design Decision: Demand-Driven Collection (2026-04-06)

Tool results are collected ONLY when a downstream node declares dependency on them via its inputs dict. If no consumer references the tool log, the ReAct loop runs exactly as today — results consumed internally, nothing extra in state.

This means:
- compile_state_model checks whether any node in the graph references a tool_log field. If not, no field is added to the state model.
- _make_tool_fn checks at compile time whether the tool_log state field exists. If not, it skips collection entirely — zero overhead.
- The downstream node's inputs dict IS the opt-in signal. No flags, no config, no annotations.

This is consistent with neograph's existing pattern: the graph topology drives what gets computed. Unused outputs don't exist in state (nodes without downstream consumers still run but their state fields are minimal). Extending this to tool results is natural.
## Design Decision: Renderer Pipeline for Tool Results (2026-04-06)

Tool results flowing to a downstream node go through the SAME rendering pipeline as any other input:

1. `describe_type(ToolReturnType)` (shipped in neograph-7as) produces the schema header with field descriptions from Field(description=...) annotations
2. `XmlRenderer` / `DelimitedRenderer` (shipped in neograph-ni6) renders each tool result instance
3. The downstream node's prompt_compiler receives pre-rendered tool results alongside pre-rendered upstream outputs — no special-casing

This means: the tool's return type (a Pydantic model with Field descriptions) IS the rendering contract. The framework applies describe_type for the schema + the active renderer for each instance. The judge sees structured, annotated evidence — not JSON dumps, not raw strings.

No new rendering machinery needed. The existing renderer dispatch (node > construct > global) applies uniformly to all inputs including tool results. The tool author controls rendering quality by writing good Field(description=...) annotations on their return type.
## Design Decision: N Named Outputs (2026-04-06)

Node.outputs becomes dict[str, type] — the mirror of Node.inputs.

A gather node produces:
```python
@node(
    outputs={'result': ExplorationResult, 'tool_log': list[ToolInteraction]},
    mode='gather', tools=[read_file],
)
def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ExplorationResult: ...
```

A downstream node consumes any subset:
```python
# Consume both
@node(output=RubricScore)
def score(explore_result: ExplorationResult, explore_tool_log: list[ToolInteraction]) -> RubricScore: ...

# Consume only tool results (valid — judge doesn't need explorer's conclusion)
@node(output=EvidenceAudit)
def audit(explore_tool_log: list[ToolInteraction]) -> EvidenceAudit: ...

# Consume only the main output (current behavior, backward compat)
@node(output=Report)
def report(explore: ExplorationResult) -> Report: ...
```

### Naming convention
State fields: `{node_name}_{output_name}` (e.g., explore_result, explore_tool_log).
Backward compat: when outputs is a single type (not a dict), the state field is `{node_name}` as today.

### Scope
This is a second refactor epic (Node.outputs), mirroring Node.inputs (neograph-kqd). Same pattern:
1. Node.output → Node.outputs: dict[str, type] (rename + shape change)
2. State model compiler emits one field per output key
3. Validator checks downstream inputs against upstream outputs by name
4. Factory writes each output to its named state field
5. @node decorator infers outputs from return annotation or explicit kwarg
6. Backward compat: single-type output stays as shorthand

### This IS neograph-1bp now
The gather tool context feature is a USE CASE of N named outputs, not a separate feature. Filing the outputs refactor as the implementation path for neograph-1bp.

title: Auto-rewind on a NON-COERCIBLE field-type change raises raw pydantic ValidationError before rewind (found during TQ-01 E2E)
description:
Surfaced by the neograph-oitm auto-rewind E2E. When a checkpointed pipeline is recompiled with an INCOMPATIBLE (non-coercible) output field-type change (e.g. int->str) and resumed on the same thread_id with auto_resume=True, the resume does NOT produce a clean CheckpointSchemaError. Instead a raw pydantic ValidationError is raised INSIDE the get_state_history() walk in _auto_resume_from_divergence, BEFORE the rewind decision runs: LangGraph materializes every historical snapshot into the CURRENT state schema, and the old tip's score=int fails str validation. Coercible changes (int->float) work correctly and are proven by the landed E2E.

Impact: the durability/auto-rewind pitch implies schema evolution on resume works generally; today only COERCIBLE evolution is clean. The 0.6.0 release notes must NOT claim arbitrary schema evolution on resume until this is handled (relates to neograph-y5ux release-notes framing and the neograph-oitm marketing precondition).

Disposition to design: detect the schema divergence and raise CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) BEFORE walking get_state_history into the new schema (or wrap the history materialization so a per-snapshot validation failure is translated into the invalidated-node signal rather than bubbling raw). Add an E2E cell (sync+async) mirroring TQ-01 for the non-coercible case asserting the clean error. Discovered-from neograph-oitm.
close_reason: Non-coercible field-type change (int->str) on checkpoint resume now raises a clean CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) before any node re-executes, instead of a raw pydantic ValidationError bubbling from the get_state_history re-materialization. Added _raise_incompatible_schema translator single-sited between sync/async rewind twins; wrapped both history walks. TDD: added sync+async non-coercible E2E cells (real file-backed Sqlite/AsyncSqlite savers) to tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py, verified red then green. Coercible int->float path unregressed.

title: @node: test coverage for produce/gather/execute modes (LLM dispatch path)
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness).

## Problem

All six tests in `TestNodeDecorator` use `mode='scripted'`. The @node decorator's LLM-mode path (produce/gather/execute) is completely untested. Whether it actually works end-to-end — whether the LLM dispatch in `factory.py` correctly sees the `input`/`output`/`prompt`/`model` values set by the decorator — is theoretical.

This is a major gap because the Dagster-style example in the research report and the beads brief for neograph-dur BOTH showcase LLM-mode @node usage:

    @node(mode='produce', output=Claims, prompt='rw/decompose', model='reason')
    def decompose(topic: RawText) -> Claims: ...

If this path is broken, the @node decorator's marquee use case (inferred topology for LLM pipelines) doesn't exist yet.

## What to test

### Produce mode

`test_node_decorator_produce_mode_end_to_end`: Two `@node(mode='produce', ...)` functions chained via parameter names, configured with a fake LLM via `configure_fake_llm(lambda tier: StructuredFake(...))`. Run via `construct_from_module` + `compile` + `run`. Assert the expected structured outputs flow through.

`test_node_decorator_produce_mode_fan_in`: Fan-in pattern with 3 upstream produce nodes feeding a fourth produce node. Verify the fourth's `.input` is inferred correctly and the LLM receives the expected upstream value (the first parameter's value, per the current decorator's single-input contract).

### Gather mode

`test_node_decorator_gather_mode_with_tool`: A `@node(mode='gather', tools=[@tool-decorated fn], ...)` that uses the ReAct loop. Mirror `TestToolDecorator::test_tool_decorator_auto_registers`. Verify the tool is called and the final output is produced.

### Execute mode

`test_node_decorator_execute_mode_with_mutation_tool`: A `@node(mode='execute', tools=[...])` that calls a mutation tool. Mirror `TestExecuteMode::test_execute_with_tools`.

### Mixed mode pipeline

`test_node_decorator_mixed_scripted_and_produce`: A pipeline that combines a scripted @node (e.g., data fetch) with a produce @node (LLM processing). Verify end-to-end correctness. This proves both dispatches coexist under `construct_from_module`.

### Existing test class patterns to mirror

- `TestProducePipeline` / similar — structured output fakes
- `TestGatherMode::test_gather_react_loop` — ReAct fake pattern
- `TestExecuteMode::test_execute_with_tools` — mutation tool pattern
- `TestToolDecorator` — @tool integration

## Acceptance criteria

- All five new tests pass.
- Each test uses a fake LLM (no real API calls) via `configure_fake_llm` from `tests/fakes.py`.
- Tests live in `TestNodeDecorator` class alongside the existing six scripted tests.
- Full suite stays green.
- If any test reveals a bug in the current decorator → LLM dispatch path, file a follow-up issue and fix as part of this task (it's exactly what this coverage is meant to surface).

## Files to read

- `src/neograph/decorators.py:145-154` — how Node is constructed with mode/prompt/model/tools
- `src/neograph/factory.py` — `_make_produce_wrapper`, `_make_gather_wrapper`, `_make_execute_wrapper`
- `tests/fakes.py` — `StructuredFake`, `TextFake`, `ReActFake`, `FakeTool`
- `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py::TestMiniRWPipeline::test_mixed_mode_pipeline` — mixed-mode pattern
- `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py::TestToolDecorator::test_tool_decorator_auto_registers` — tool integration

## Dependencies

Should probably land AFTER neograph-q54 (mode footgun fix) because the mode-inference logic affects how these tests instantiate the decorator. Not a hard block — the tests can pass `mode='produce'` explicitly and work without the inference fix.
close_reason: See prior close reasons. Force-closing because the subtask→epic dependency direction was set backwards at creation (subtask depends on epic instead of epic depends on subtask); cleanup will correct the direction across all epic subtasks in a single pass after this commit.

title: EPIC 1: Unify IR finalization via neograph._ir_normalize
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this epic)

For every Node in a constructed Construct, the value of every IR field (fan_out_param, oracle_gen_type, scripted_fn, and any future inferred field) is identical regardless of which API surface built it. This invariant is enforced STRUCTURALLY by a single normalization site, not by parallel inference in two assembly paths plus structural guards policing drift.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register — every updates[field] = ... write, the condition under which it fires, and the inferences it performs.
2. construct.py::Construct._normalize_fan_out_params + _normalize_oracle_gen_type — the retroactive-replay logic added by vgc1 + aqau.
3. loader.py::_apply_modifiers + _build_construct — what the YAML loader does NOT do.
4. _construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs — the parallel fan-out detection logic at validator time.
5. tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField — the guard policing the drift.
6. tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection — the guard policing runtime band-aid recurrence.

Output: a classification table in bead notes:
- Which inferences are TRULY @node-specific (requires Python function with annotations)?
- Which inferences are IR-level (must produce identical IR regardless of surface)?
- Which inferences appear in BOTH _cleanup_inputs_and_register AND Construct._normalize_*?

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ docs/design/architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md AND the design field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- New neograph._ir_normalize module exposes ONE entry point normalize_ir(construct) that all three assembly paths call exactly once.
- Each IR-level inference is a separate IrNormalizer Protocol implementation with applies_to + apply methods. Normalizers are REGISTERED, not enumerated.
- _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register no longer writes updates[<IR-level-field>]. The @node-specific work stays.
- Construct._normalize_fan_out_params and _normalize_oracle_gen_type are DELETED. Construct.__init__ calls normalize_ir(self) once.
- The structural guard TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField is REPLACED by a stronger invariant: a test that checks normalize_ir is the ONLY writer of IR-level fields post-construction.
- The validator no longer needs parallel fan-out detection — fan_out_param is set by the time validation runs.

If the proposed diff adds another _normalize_<field> method to Construct, STOP. The iteration is incomplete.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO branching-over-polymorphism (N normalizers must be N Protocol implementations, not one function with N if/elif branches).
- NO dict-over-types (Protocol registry stays typed; use list[IrNormalizer] not dict[str, Callable]).
- NO new structural guards to police things that should be impossible by construction. If a new guard is proposed, ask: what abstraction would make this guard structurally redundant?
- Acceptance is NET-NEGATIVE complexity: lines deleted (from _construct_builder, construct.py, structural guards) must exceed lines added (in _ir_normalize).

## Phase 5 — Independent review (correctness AND elegance)

After implementation, spawn a feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with model: opus. The prompt must demand evaluation of:

1. CORRECTNESS — does the unification preserve every behavior of the three pre-fix paths?
2. ELEGANCE — does the solution apply the codebase's exemplary pattern (Protocol + registered implementations + boundary normalization, same as StateBus/normalize_outputs/fakes)?
3. NET COMPLEXITY — count lines added vs deleted across all touched files. Must be negative.
4. INVARIANT — is there a code path where IR can be inconsistent across surfaces? Try to construct one.
5. NO NEW HYDRA — can the next normalizer be added in 10 LOC in one file, or does it touch three places?

Reviewer must explicitly verdict ELEGANT or NOT, confidence ≥85. If NOT ELEGANT, reopen the ticket.

## Tickets subsumed by this epic

- aqau (already shipped — refactor into the new structure)
- vgc1 fan_out_param normalization (already shipped — refactor)
- fbk5 (aqau hardening: normalizer dispatch list) — fully subsumed
- gup9 (ghost state-model fields) — subsumed
- 3zai (split _construct_builder.py) — partially subsumed

## Acceptance

- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py: Protocol + ≥2 registered normalizers + normalize_ir entry point
- Construct.__init__ delegates to normalize_ir; two _normalize_* methods deleted
- _construct_builder.py stops writing IR-level updates
- One structural guard deleted/replaced
- All existing tests pass
- Net diff: lines deleted > lines added across touched files
- Independent reviewer (opus) verdicts ELEGANT with confidence ≥85, written to bead notes
- bd close after reviewer ELEGANT verdict, not after make quality green
design:
## Target design (from architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md, Epic 1)

### Pattern

Protocol + registered implementations + boundary normalization. This is the SAME pattern the codebase has already perfected for StateBus + _DictStateBus/_ModelStateBus, for normalize_outputs/normalize_inputs, and for the test fakes layer. We are applying that pattern to IR-level field inference.

### Module shape

```python
# src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py

from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class IrNormalizer(Protocol):
    """Infers a single IR field on a Node post-construction.

    Stateless. Idempotent. Called exactly once per Construct.__init__
    regardless of which API surface built the Construct.
    """
    def applies_to(self, node: Node) -> bool: ...
    def apply(self, node: Node, peer_field_names: set[str]) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


# Registered implementations (one per IR-level field):

class _FanOutParamNormalizer:
    def applies_to(self, node): ...   # has Each, dict-form inputs, fan_out_param is None
    def apply(self, node, peers): ...  # returns {"fan_out_param": <inferred>} or {}


class _OracleGenTypeNormalizer:
    def applies_to(self, node): ...   # has Oracle.merge_fn, oracle_gen_type is None
    def apply(self, node, peers): ...  # returns {"oracle_gen_type": <inferred>} or {}


_NORMALIZERS: list[IrNormalizer] = [
    _FanOutParamNormalizer(),
    _OracleGenTypeNormalizer(),
]


def normalize_ir(construct: Construct) -> None:
    """The single IR-level normalization entry point.

    Walks construct.nodes once, applies every registered normalizer, writes
    updates via model_copy. Idempotent: normalizers that find a field already
    set return {} and are no-ops.
    """
    peer_field_names = {field_name_for(it.name) for it in construct.nodes if ...}
    for i, item in enumerate(construct.nodes):
        if not isinstance(item, Node):
            continue
        updates: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for normalizer in _NORMALIZERS:
            if normalizer.applies_to(item):
                updates.update(normalizer.apply(item, peer_field_names))
        if updates:
            construct.nodes[i] = item.model_copy(update=updates)
```

### Call-site changes

1. `src/neograph/construct.py::Construct.__init__` — replace the two `self._normalize_*` calls with one `normalize_ir(self)` call. Delete both methods. Remove the `infer_oracle_gen_type` import.

2. `src/neograph/_construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register` — Phase 3 (deferred oracle_gen_type inference at line 577-583) DELETED. The fan_out_param assignment at line 565 can either stay (defensive, idempotent with the normalizer) or delete (cleaner). Recommend delete for elegance — normalize_ir owns IR-level fields exclusively.

3. `src/neograph/loader.py` — no change needed. YAML loader builds a Construct, Construct.__init__ now calls normalize_ir automatically.

4. `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField` — REPLACE with a stronger guard: AST-scan _construct_builder.py for any `updates[<IR-LEVEL-FIELD>] = ...` write, fail if any present. The IR-level field list is `{"fan_out_param", "oracle_gen_type"}` today. The new guard enforces: IR-level writes happen ONLY in _ir_normalize.

### Why Protocol not ABC

Protocol enables structural typing and runtime checking. New normalizers can be defined in any module (including downstream consumer code) without inheriting from a base class. Aligns with the StateBus Protocol pattern already in the codebase.

### Why list[IrNormalizer] not dict[str, Callable]

The list preserves the typed Protocol contract (`IrNormalizer` is a type, `Callable` is not). Future maintainers cannot accidentally insert a bare function and lose the `applies_to`/`apply` contract.

### Why one applies_to + one apply method (not just apply returning Optional)

Separating predicate from mutation is the GRASP Pure Fabrication principle — each method does one thing, both can be tested independently, the call site reads naturally.

### Rejected alternatives

- "Inline all inferences in normalize_ir as if/elif branches" — branching-over-polymorphism, the explicit anti-pattern.
- "Pydantic model_validator(mode='after') on Node" — would need to access peer producer set, which isn't available to Node in isolation; creates a circular import with merge_fn registry. Construct.__init__ is the natural place because peers are known there.
- "Push inference to Modifiable.__or__ at pipe time" — registry not always populated at pipe time for programmatic code. Rejected for the same reason as in aqau analysis.

### Net complexity expected

Add: ~80 LOC for _ir_normalize.py (Protocol + 2 normalizers + entry point).
Delete:
- ~30 LOC across two _normalize_* methods in construct.py
- ~10 LOC oracle_gen_type inference in _construct_builder.py Phase 3
- ~50 LOC TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField (replaced by ~25 LOC stronger guard)
- Net: -10 to -20 LOC

The win is structural (single source of truth), not line count. The structural-guard delta is what matters.
notes:
## Phase 1 — Code Archaeology (research atom neograph-i2rc.2, 2026-06-02)

### 1. _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register (lines 518-593)
Single-pass loop over decorated @node dict. Three phases accumulate `updates`:
- **Phase 1 (inputs + fan_out_param), lines 543-565**: strips DI params, rewrites port/loop keys → `updates['inputs']`. Line 564-565: `if skip: updates['fan_out_param'] = next(iter(skip))` where `skip = fan_out_params.get(field)` (precomputed by _detect_fan_out_params at line 627).
- **Phase 2 (scripted_fn), lines 567-575**: `_register_node_scripted` → `updates['scripted_fn']`. TRULY @node-specific (needs the function sidecar).
- **Phase 3 (oracle_gen_type), lines 577-583**: `infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn)` → `updates['oracle_gen_type']` when gen_type differs from outputs. DUPLICATES construct.py logic exactly.

### 2. construct.py::Construct.__init__ + _normalize_* (lines 156-218)
`__init__` calls `_normalize_fan_out_params()` then `_normalize_oracle_gen_type()` BEFORE `_validate_node_chain(self)`.
- **_normalize_fan_out_params (163-195)**: for each Node with Each + dict-form inputs + fan_out_param unset, computes peer_field_names, finds the single `unknown` input key (not a peer, not self) → `model_copy(update={'fan_out_param': unknown[0]})`. Only fires when len(unknown)==1.
- **_normalize_oracle_gen_type (197-218)**: for each Node with oracle.merge_fn + oracle_gen_type unset, `infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn)` → model_copy. IDENTICAL inference to _construct_builder Phase 3.

### 3. loader.py::_apply_modifiers (244-275) + _build_construct (121-151)
Loader builds `Node | Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator` then wraps in `Construct(...)`. Sets NEITHER fan_out_param NOR oracle_gen_type — relies entirely on Construct.__init__ normalization. This is the proof the normalization MUST live in Construct.__init__ to serve the YAML surface.

### 4. _construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs (587-655)
Lines 611-629: PARALLEL fan-out detection. `fan_out_key = item.fan_out_param`; `_each_skip_used = (fan_out_key is not None)`. If fan_out_param unset BUT `has_each`, the FIRST unmatched input key is skipped as the fan-out receiver (band-aid for programmatic Each before normalization ran). After normalize_ir sets fan_out_param pre-validation, the `has_each and not _each_skip_used` fallback becomes dead for the single-receiver case.

### 5/6. Structural guards (test_structural_guards.py)
- **TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection (4129)**: AST-asserts _extract_fan_in_dict has no state.keys() scan. Polices runtime band-aid recurrence. KEEP (orthogonal — runtime layer).
- **TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField (4168)**: AST-scans _construct_builder for `updates[<field>]` writes; requires each to be in PASSTHROUGH_FIELDS={inputs,scripted_fn} or NORMALIZED_FIELDS={fan_out_param,oracle_gen_type}. This is the drift-policing guard to REPLACE with the stronger 'normalize_ir is sole writer' invariant.

### Classification table
| Inference | TRULY @node-specific? | IR-level (surface-invariant)? | In BOTH builder + construct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| inputs (strip DI / rewrite ports) | YES (needs fn signature + DI bindings) | no | no (builder only) |
| scripted_fn | YES (needs the sidecar fn) | no | no (builder only) |
| **fan_out_param** | no | **YES** | builder Phase1(565) + construct._normalize_fan_out_params |
| **oracle_gen_type** | no | **YES** | builder Phase3(581) + construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type (IDENTICAL code) |

→ The two IR-level inferences (fan_out_param, oracle_gen_type) are EXACTLY the targets for _ir_normalize. inputs+scripted_fn stay in _construct_builder (@node-specific).

### Note on builder vs construct fan_out_param sourcing
Builder derives fan_out_param from `_detect_fan_out_params` (signature analysis: param with no producer + Each). Construct derives it from the 'single unknown input key' heuristic. Both must yield the SAME value. Normalizer must reproduce the construct.py heuristic (it's surface-agnostic; works on the assembled Construct). The @node path will ALSO converge because by the time Construct.__init__ runs, the @node builder has already set fan_out_param — normalizer is idempotent (skips when already set). RISK to verify in implementation: builder currently sets fan_out_param via model_copy at line 565; if we DELETE that (recommended in design), the normalizer must reproduce it for @node Each nodes too. Must test all three surfaces (parity rule).
## Architect Review (fresh-context architect, 2026-06-02)

Reviewed against Core Invariant, source files (construct.py 114-218, _construct_builder.py 293-319/518-593, _construct_validation.py 587-655, loader.py 244-275, _sidecar.py 79, test_obligation_r1r2.py 240-314, structural guards 4129-4269).

- [LOW] Invariant alignment: The decomposition is correct. Phase-1 classification (fan_out_param + oracle_gen_type are the only IR-level surface-invariant inferences; inputs/scripted_fn are @node-specific) matches the source exactly. Moving the two to a single normalize_ir(construct) called from Construct.__init__ is the right structural fix. loader.py confirms the YAML surface sets NEITHER field and relies on Construct.__init__, so the single site genuinely serves all three surfaces. Pattern (Protocol + registered list[IrNormalizer] + boundary normalization) matches the codebase's StateBus/normalize_outputs exemplar. Granularity (one applies_to + one apply per field) is right.

- [HIGH] Approach soundness / derivation divergence: The design proposes DELETING the fan_out_param write at builder:565 and letting _FanOutParamNormalizer reproduce it. THE TWO DERIVATIONS ARE NOT EQUIVALENT.
  - @node (_detect_fan_out_params, builder:318): derives from FUNCTION SIGNATURE param names — {p for p in pnames if p not in decorated and p not in di_params and p not in _ports}. Returns a SET; builder:565 does next(iter(skip)) — picks ARBITRARILY if 2+.
  - construct.py heuristic (_normalize_fan_out_params:187): derives from the INPUTS DICT keys (ni.by_name), excludes peers+self, fires ONLY when len(unknown)==1.
  These differ on the multi-unknown case. test_obligation_r1r2.py:271 (two_unmatched_is_error) proves the construct heuristic intentionally does NOT pick when 2+ unmatched (validator errors). The @node path with next(iter(skip)) would have PICKED one and succeeded. So for an @node Each node with 2+ non-peer/non-DI/non-port params, deleting :565 changes behavior: today @node picks arbitrarily; post-delete the normalizer no-ops (len!=1) and the validator path decides. This is a real behavioral delta, not idempotent.
  Suggestion: Either (a) KEEP builder:565 (the design lists this as an allowed option — 'stay, defensive, idempotent'); the normalizer's applies_to no-ops because @node already set the field, so there is no double-write and no drift — OR (b) before deleting :565, prove via a three-surface test that no @node Each fixture produces a 2+ -element skip set (the DI/port stripping likely reduces it to 1 in practice, but that must be ASSERTED, not assumed). Recommend (a) for safety + (b) as the test that justifies eventually doing (a)-with-delete. Do NOT delete :565 on the bare claim of idempotency — the derivations are not the same function, only coincidentally equal in the single-key case.

- [MEDIUM] Validator parallel detection (611-629) removal: The design says 'validator no longer needs parallel fan-out detection.' After normalize_ir runs pre-validation, the single-receiver programmatic case gets fan_out_param set, so the has_each and not _each_skip_used fallback IS dead FOR len(unknown)==1. BUT it is NOT dead for: (1) 2+ unknown keys (normalizer no-ops, fan_out_param stays None, has_each fallback still skips exactly one then errors on the second — this is the behavior test:271 and test:287 lock in); (2) 0 unknown keys; (3) the fan_out_param-set + extra-key double-fire BUG that test:287 documents (match='mystery'). If you remove 611-629 in THIS epic you will change/break those three tested behaviors. Suggestion: DO NOT remove the validator fallback in this epic. Scope this epic to unifying the WRITE site (normalize_ir as sole writer). The validator's defensive skip is a separate concern (the 287 double-fire is a known bug with its own ticket surface). Leave 611-629 as-is; note in the epic that it becomes partially-dead-but-defensive. Removing it is a follow-up that must first resolve the test:287 double-fire semantics.

- [LOW] Pattern compliance / circular import: construct.py already imports infer_oracle_gen_type from _sidecar and field_name_for/normalize_inputs. _ir_normalize.py will need Node (node.py), normalize_inputs (_normalize), field_name_for (naming), infer_oracle_gen_type (_sidecar). construct.py imports node.py already (line 34), so construct.py -> _ir_normalize -> node.py is fine (node.py must not import _ir_normalize or construct — verify it doesn't). _sidecar import should MOVE from construct.py into _ir_normalize.py (construct.py no longer calls it directly). No cycle: _ir_normalize -> {node, _normalize, naming, _sidecar}; none of those import _ir_normalize. construct.py -> _ir_normalize is the only new edge. Confirm node.py has no import-time dependency on construct.py (it defines fan_out_param at node.py:169 as a plain field, so it should be clean).

- [LOW] oracle_gen_type coverage after deletion: Tracing — @node oracle node: builder Phase-3 (578-583) sets it today; if deleted, normalize_ir's _OracleGenTypeNormalizer must catch it. Its applies_to (oracle.merge_fn present AND oracle_gen_type is None) fires for the @node case identically because builder Phase-3 and construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type are BYTE-IDENTICAL inference (infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn), gen_type is not None and is not outputs). Unlike fan_out_param, there is NO derivation divergence here — both call the same _sidecar function. SAFE to delete builder Phase-3 AND construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type and let the normalizer own it. This is the clean half of the epic.

- [MEDIUM] Net-negative complexity claim (-10 to -20 LOC): Optimistic. Protocol + 2 normalizer classes (each with applies_to + apply + docstrings) + registry + normalize_ir walker is realistically ~90-110 LOC, not 80. Deletions: ~30 (two construct methods) + ~7 (builder Phase-3) + guard replacement (~50 deleted, ~25-40 added). If builder:565 STAYS (recommended), you delete ~7 fewer lines. Net could be slightly POSITIVE. Recommend: drop the hard 'net diff must be negative' acceptance gate OR scope it to 'net structural-guard + duplicated-inference LOC negative' rather than total LOC. The win is single-source-of-truth, which the epic itself acknowledges ('the win is structural, not line count'). The acceptance criterion contradicts the design's own caveat — fix the criterion.

- [MEDIUM] Replacement guard 'normalize_ir is the ONLY writer of IR-level fields post-construction': AST-checkable but the proposed framing (scan _construct_builder for updates[<IR-field>]) is too narrow — it only polices ONE file. A node.fan_out_param = / object.__setattr__(n, 'fan_out_param', ...) anywhere else evades it (test:307 already uses object.__setattr__). Concrete suggestion: guard scans ALL of src/neograph/*.py (excluding _ir_normalize.py) for (a) Assign/AnnAssign targets of form <x>.fan_out_param / <x>.oracle_gen_type, (b) model_copy(update={...}) calls whose dict literal contains those keys, (c) object.__setattr__(_, 'fan_out_param'|'oracle_gen_type', _). Allowlist only _ir_normalize.py and node.py field declarations. This is AST-checkable and not brittle if you match attribute NAME on the IR-level field set, not exact call shape. Keep the existing TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection guard (orthogonal — runtime layer, not write-site).

- [LOW] Idempotency: Confirmed correct. @node path sets fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type BEFORE Construct.__init__ runs (in _cleanup_inputs_and_register, before the Construct(...) call at builder:639). Both normalizers' applies_to gate on 'field is None', so they no-op on already-set @node IR. Idempotency holds REGARDLESS of whether :565 is kept — that is exactly why keeping :565 is safe.

- [LOW] Alternative not fully weighed: The design rejects model_validator(mode='after') on Node (needs peers — correct rejection). But it does not consider making normalize_ir a model_validator(mode='after') on CONSTRUCT, where peers ARE available. title: merge_prompt: pass upstream context alongside variant list
description:
## What

merge_prompt path in _oracle.py:200 calls invoke_structured(input_data=primary) where primary is list[OutputType] — the bare variant list. The merge prompt template can only reference the variants, not the upstream data that produced them. Templates like \${prepare_enrichment.site.name} resolve to empty string because _substitute_vars receives a list, not a dict with named upstreams.

## Why

divemesh hit this building a content writing pipeline: the Oracle merge judge needs to see both the N draft variants AND the upstream enrichment context (site name, tone, keywords) to make a quality decision. Without upstream access, the merge prompt is blind to context — it can only compare variants against each other, not against the brief.

piarch works around this with @merge_fn that calls piarch_llm_call() directly, building the prompt with full access to variants + upstream state. This works but is boilerplate that the framework should handle.

## Design

In make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py), read upstream inputs from state alongside the variant list:

```python
def merge_fn(state, config):
    results = getattr(state, collector_field, [])
    primary, secondaries = _unwrap_oracle_results(...)
    
    # Build dict with variants + upstream context
    input_data = {"variants": primary}
    if hasattr(node, "inputs") and isinstance(node.inputs, dict):
        for key in node.inputs:
            upstream_val = getattr(state, field_name_for(key), None)
            if upstream_val is not None:
                input_data[key] = upstream_val
    
    merged = invoke_structured(
        input_data=input_data,  # dict, not bare list
        ...
    )
```

The merge prompt then references both:
  ${variants} — the N drafts (rendered as BAML list)
  ${prepare_enrichment.site.name} — upstream context via dotted access

## Migration

Breaking change: existing merge_prompts that assume input_data is a list will get a dict instead. Guard with deprecation:
- If merge_prompt template contains ${variants} -> new dict path
- If merge_prompt template has no ${variants} reference -> wrap as {"variants": list} AND log deprecation warning suggesting migration to the new format

## Verification

Integration: Oracle with merge_prompt that references both ${variants} and ${upstream.field}. Assert the merge prompt receives both.
Integration: Existing merge_prompt with no upstream references. Assert backward compat (variants still accessible).
Integration: @merge_fn path unaffected (receives raw list as before).

## Acceptance

- merge_prompt input_data is dict with "variants" key + upstream node outputs
- Template ${variants} accesses the variant list
- Template ${upstream.field} accesses upstream data via dotted access
- render_for_prompt and field flattening apply to upstream values
- @merge_fn path unchanged (still receives raw list)
- Backward-compatible with deprecation warning for bare-list templates
design:
## Core Invariant
merge_prompt receives the same input_data shape as any LLM node — a dict of named entries — so upstream context and variants are both addressable by name in the template.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add node_inputs param to make_oracle_merge_fn
2. In merge closure: build dict {variants: primary, **upstream_from_state}
3. Thread node_inputs at 3 call sites (compiler.py:440, compiler.py:351, _wiring.py:251)
4. No fallback — always dict form

title: First-class production auth: OAuth 2.1 / client-credentials / JWT token_provider helpers
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a production consumer gets refresh/expiry-handling OAuth identity for an HttpServer by passing a battery helper to token_provider=, not by hand-rolling httpx.Auth.

WHY: token_provider returns a bare bearer string today; OAuth 2.1 / client-credentials / on-behalf-of / JWT flows exist ONLY as hand-rolled httpx.Auth in example 23 appendix. The MCP SDK ships the httpx.Auth providers (OAuthClientProvider / ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider / PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider) — wrap them so consumers get token refresh + expiry for free.

SCOPE: battery helper(s) (e.g. oauth_token_provider(...)) producing a token_provider/httpx.Auth wired into HttpServer bearer path, minting + refreshing per-run identity from config. Cover client-credentials at minimum; document on-behalf-of / JWT.

ANTI-BAND-AID: reuse the SDK httpx.Auth providers — do NOT re-implement OAuth token exchange/refresh. neograph carries identity from config to the transport; it never parses or stores the token (stays out of state/checkpoint/fingerprint, per the existing invariant).

ACCEPTANCE: an HttpServer against a demo OAuth-guarded endpoint authenticates via the helper; token refresh on expiry works without a reconnect; the token never appears in state/checkpoint; docs cover the three flows. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
A production consumer gets refresh/expiry-handling OAuth identity by attaching an SDK-built httpx.Auth to the transport (HttpServer.auth -> the adapter connection dict), and neograph_mcp only CARRIES that Auth from config to the adapter -- it never parses, stores, or refreshes the token itself (the token stays out of state/checkpoint/fingerprint).

## Implementation Plan
1. EXTEND HttpServer, not a new seam: add `auth: httpx.Auth | None = None` to the frozen dataclass (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:76-82). httpx is already transitive under the mcp extra.
2. WIRE the single choke point: in `_connection` (_client.py:88-101) add `if isinstance(spec, HttpServer) and spec.auth is not None: conn['auth'] = spec.auth`. This lights up all three surfaces (tool factories, resource fetcher, mcp_session) for free -- do NOT touch the surfaces individually. Precedence: if both `auth` and a bearer `token` are present, the httpx.Auth wins (an Auth manages its own Authorization header); document that token_provider is for stdio/static-bearer, auth for OAuth flows.
3. SHIP thin battery constructors that WRAP the SDK providers (reuse, never re-implement token exchange/refresh). Suggested surface in src/neograph_mcp (new _auth.py or in _client.py), exported via __init__.__all__:
   - `client_credentials_auth(server_url, client_id, client_secret, *, scopes=None, auth_method='client_secret_basic') -> httpx.Auth` -> wraps ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider with a fresh in-memory TokenStorage. (Covers the mandated client-credentials case.)
   - `private_key_jwt_auth(...)` / `oauth_client_provider(...)` -> wrap PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider / OAuthClientProvider (document on-behalf-of / interactive OAuth 2.1; can be thinner/doc-first).
   Each helper reads its client_id/secret from run config where per-run identity is needed, or takes them directly for static app identity. Prefer names ending in `_auth` returning httpx.Auth over the bead's misleading `oauth_token_provider` (see NEEDS USER INPUT in notes).
4. PROVIDE a minimal in-memory TokenStorage (implements mcp.client.auth.TokenStorage: get/set tokens + client_info) created per helper call, never persisted -- this is the structural guarantee the token never reaches state.
5. FUNCTION-LOCAL imports for mcp.client.auth.* and jwt-dependent providers (keep module import light; keep the fail-loud extra check in __init__ authoritative).
6. ## Findings (dp-researcher, neograph-5jrd0.34)

REUSE TARGET (do not re-implement OAuth): the mcp SDK 1.28.x ships the httpx.Auth providers already installed under the `mcp` extra:
- `mcp.client.auth.OAuthClientProvider` (interactive OAuth 2.1 / auth-code+PKCE)
- `mcp.client.auth.extensions.client_credentials.ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider(server_url, storage, client_id, client_secret, token_endpoint_auth_method='client_secret_basic'|'client_secret_post', scopes=None)`
- `...client_credentials.PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider(server_url, storage, client_id, assertion_provider)`
- `...client_credentials.RFC7523OAuthClientProvider`, `JWTParameters`, `SignedJWTParameters`, `static_assertion_provider`
All subclass `httpx.Auth` (MRO: Provider -> OAuthClientProvider -> httpx.Auth). They mint AND refresh tokens internally via the httpx auth_flow (401 -> refresh -> retry in the SAME httpx client, i.e. WITHOUT a reconnect). pyjwt 2.13 is present transitively (client_credentials does `import jwt`).

THE SINGLE WIRING CHOKE POINT: `_connection(spec, token)` in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88-101 builds the langchain-mcp-adapters connection dict for EVERY surface. All three consumer surfaces route through `_client_for` -> `_connection`:
- tool factories: _client.py:276 (_make_tool_factory)
- resource fetcher/replayer: _client.py:495 / :505
- mcp_session: _session.py:235
The adapter's `StreamableHttpConnection` TypedDict (langchain-mcp-adapters 0.3.0) ALREADY accepts an `auth` key (verified: keys include 'auth'). So threading an httpx.Auth requires touching ONE builder, not the three surfaces.

CURRENT (string) vs NEW (httpx.Auth) identity paths:
- CURRENT: `token_provider` (TokenProvider = Callable[..., str|Awaitable[str]], _client.py:55) returns a BARE bearer string, resolved once per superstep (_resolve_token, _client.py:114) and stamped into `headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'` (_client.py:96-97). A fresh client is built each superstep, so a token change here IS a reconnect. This path stays for stdio (tool-arg identity) and simple static bearers. NOT deprecated.
- NEW: an httpx.Auth lives IN the transport's httpx client and refreshes per-request. This is the ONLY path that satisfies the acceptance 'refresh on expiry without a reconnect'.

GUARD BOUNDARY (favorable): tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py scans `src/neograph` ONLY. The battery lives in `src/neograph_mcp`, which is ALLOWED to `import mcp` / httpx / hold client lifecycle. New helper code belongs in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py (or a new src/neograph_mcp/_auth.py), exported via src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py __all__ (the facade is the public contract per AGENTS.md naming policy).

TokenStorage: `mcp.client.auth.TokenStorage` is a Protocol (get_tokens/set_tokens/get_client_info/set_client_info). The SDK ships NO in-memory impl -> the battery must provide a tiny in-memory TokenStorage (per-run, never persisted; keeps the token out of neograph state/checkpoint by construction).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:76-82 -- `HttpServer` frozen dataclass (url, headers). Add `auth: httpx.Auth | None = None` here; it is the natural home for transport identity.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88-101 -- `_connection`: the single builder. Add `if spec.auth is not None: conn['auth'] = spec.auth`. Covers all three surfaces at once.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:104-111 -- `_client_for`: unchanged; already the shared client constructor.
- src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-61 -- facade; add the new helper(s) + HttpServer stays exported. Public iff in __all__.
- examples/23_mcp_client_selective_binding.py:453-488 -- APPENDIX B: the hand-rolled PerRunBearer httpx.Auth this task graduates; explicitly names the three SDK providers to wrap. This is the spec-in-prose.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:594-653 (TestHttpServerSmoke) + _demo_http_server fixture (:137-156) + _demo_http_server_spec (:166-169) -- the EXEMPLAR http-integration test to copy for an OAuth test class.
- pyproject.toml:43-47 -- the `mcp` extra (mcp>=1.28,<2, langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.3). pyjwt already transitive; confirm no new pin needed for PrivateKeyJWT before adding one.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the bead Core Invariant says the consumer wires OAuth 'by passing a battery helper to token_provider='. But `token_provider` returns a STRING resolved once per superstep, and a per-superstep client rebuild IS a reconnect -- so it structurally CANNOT satisfy the acceptance 'refresh on expiry WITHOUT a reconnect'. The httpx.Auth must live in the transport (HttpServer.auth / connection['auth']). Recommended resolution: add `HttpServer(auth=httpx.Auth)` and treat 'token_provider=' in the invariant as loose shorthand for 'the neograph identity seam'. Confirm the API shape (new HttpServer.auth field) before implementing. Corollary: the suggested name `oauth_token_provider` is misleading (it returns an httpx.Auth, not a token string) -- prefer `oauth_client_credentials(...) -> httpx.Auth` (or an `oauth_auth` family).
- Acceptance requires a 'demo OAuth-guarded endpoint'. The current examples/_mcp_demo_server.py is plain FastMCP that only ECHOES the Authorization header (bearer_identity) -- it runs NO OAuth token endpoint and enforces nothing. The SDK providers do RFC-8414 metadata discovery + a token-endpoint round-trip + 401-triggered refresh, so a faithful test needs a minimal OAuth token server (short-lived token + one 401 to prove refresh-without-reconnect). This is the largest lift; a Starlette token-endpoint fixture (mirroring _demo_http_server) is the likely shape. Scope the demo-server work explicitly.
- Token-never-in-state invariant holds by construction ONLY if the in-memory TokenStorage is created per-run inside the consumer factory and never written to config that enters state. Add a test asserting the token/secret never appears in checkpoint/state/fingerprint (mirrors existing 'token never enters state' pins).
- Three-surface note: this is a neograph_mcp battery, NOT a core IR change, so the @node/declarative/programmatic three-surface parity rule does not apply; the parity that DOES apply is the three neograph_mcp surfaces (tool factories, resource fetcher, mcp_session) -- all covered free by wiring `_connection`.
- client_credentials extension imports `jwt` (pyjwt) at module top; a bare `import` of the helper without pyjwt would fail. Gate the client_credentials import function-locally and keep pyjwt pinned in the mcp extra if PrivateKeyJWT/RFC7523 helpers are shipped.

Pattern: per-surface auth/header wiring instead of the single _connection choke point.
Scan command: grep -rn 'def _connection|conn\[|headers|Authorization|auth' src/neograph_mcp/_client.py
Total instances found: auth-header construction is ALREADY single-sited at _connection (:88-100); _client_for (:111) routes all 3 surfaces through it.

No MIGRATE — the centralization the ticket wants already exists; 27h3s extends it in place. BLOCKED pending token_provider= vs HttpServer.auth transport decision (NEEDS_USER_INPUT).
## Architect Review (neograph-5jrd0.36)

Gate hard-check PASS: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. - [HIGH] Finding: The flagged token_provider= vs HttpServer.auth contradiction is REAL and CORRECTLY framed. token_provider is typed Callable[...,str|Awaitable[str]] returning a bare bearer string, resolved ONCE per superstep before the client is built and stamped into a header (_client.py:96-97,122). Refresh-on-expiry-without-reconnect structurally requires the httpx.Auth object to live inside the persistent httpx client and intercept 401s via auth_flow -- a string returned by token_provider cannot do this. The ticket Core Invariant literally says "pass a battery helper to token_provider=", which is structurally unsatisfiable for the stated acceptance. Suggestion: This is a genuine HIGH because the resolution (a) adds a new PUBLIC field auth to the frozen public HttpServer dataclass and (b) rewrites the ticket-author-stated Core Invariant. The design already picked the correct approach (HttpServer.auth) and step 8 gates on it -- user should CONFIRM the API shape (new HttpServer.auth transport field + reframed invariant + renaming the misleading oauth_token_provider to an *_auth family returning httpx.Auth) before landing. Not open-ended; a confirm-this-shape gate.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Undefined precedence when both seams are set. token_provider (a param to mcp_tool_factories/mcp_tool_factory) and HttpServer.auth are INDEPENDENT seams both feeding _connection(spec, token). A consumer can set HttpServer(auth=...) AND pass token_provider=... -> _connection would set BOTH conn["headers"]["Authorization"] (from token) AND conn["auth"]. Design step 2 merely ASSERTS "httpx.Auth wins" relying on undocumented httpx header-vs-auth precedence, not enforced in the wiring. Suggestion: enforce mutual exclusivity (raise a clear error if a bearer token and spec.auth both resolve for the same HttpServer), or at minimum skip stamping headers["Authorization"] when spec.auth is set, so precedence is code-guaranteed rather than httpx-behavior-dependent. Add a test pinning the chosen precedence.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Demo OAuth-server fixture is underspecified in plan step 6 vs the risks note. Step 6 says "minimal OAuth token endpoint fixture (mirroring _demo_http_server)", but the SDK ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider does RFC-8414 metadata discovery (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) BEFORE the token round-trip. A naive copy of _demo_http_server (which only echoes the Authorization header, enforces nothing) will fail at discovery, not at the token endpoint. Suggestion: the fixture must serve BOTH the discovery document AND the token endpoint (+ a one-shot 401 to force refresh). This is the largest lift; scope it as discovery-endpoint + token-endpoint, and verify whether the provider also needs client_info from TokenStorage.get_client_info for the client-credentials path.

- [LOW] Finding: Reuse posture is sound -- plan correctly wraps SDK providers rather than re-implementing OAuth, extends the existing single choke point in place (disposition table has no MIGRATE, correctly), and lives in src/neograph_mcp (outside the src/neograph guard scope). No net-new primitive that duplicates an existing one. With future annotations in _client.py, auth: httpx.Auth | None annotation needs no runtime httpx import; the isinstance(spec, HttpServer) guard in step 2 needs no httpx import either.

Overall: NEEDS_USER_INPUT
## Triage (neograph-5jrd0.37): NEEDS_USER_INPUT — blocked for maintainer. 1 HIGH: token_provider= (bare string) cannot do refresh-without-reconnect; needs httpx.Auth on HttpServer.auth (design already picked this) — but it adds a public field + reframes the ticket invariant. Awaiting shape sign-off.
## MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-07-10): APPROVE HttpServer.auth + reframed invariant. Add auth: httpx.Auth | None to the frozen HttpServer dataclass; wire at the single _connection choke point (lights all 3 surfaces); ship SDK-wrapping helpers (client_credentials_auth, ...). Precedence: auth wins over bearer token when both set. token_provider stays for stdio/static-bearer. Core invariant reframed: production OAuth identity attaches via HttpServer.auth (transport httpx.Auth), NOT token_provider=; neograph only CARRIES the Auth (never parses/stores/refreshes).
## Pre-implementation verification (orchestrator, 2026-07-10)
