title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-2plcl
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-2plcl` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-2plcl/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-2plcl
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-2plcl)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2plcl --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2plcl --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-2plcl/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-2plcl codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-2plcl/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for cnxlx
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show cnxlx` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/cnxlx/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" cnxlx
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (cnxlx)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update cnxlx --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update cnxlx --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/cnxlx/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add cnxlx codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/cnxlx/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just

findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/uixi1/`:

description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on uixi1
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" uixi1`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (uixi1)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash
   bd update uixi1 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add uixi1 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for uagu7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show uagu7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/uagu7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" uagu7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (uagu7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update uagu7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update uagu7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/uagu7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add uagu7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/uagu7/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or

   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update 32qtx --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add 32qtx sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: to_agent_spec's Swarm export must be the EXACT structural inverse of loader.py's Swarm import (_reconstruct_swarm_mesh), using the same pyagentspec types the import path expects.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (member lowering type): each mesh member lowers to a pyagentspec Agent object (via _make_agent, _agent_spec.py:213), NOT a Flow LlmNode -- Swarm.first_agent/relationships require AgenticComponent/Agent per pyagentspec/swarm.py:105-107 and agent.py:23, and the import mirror (_reconstruct_swarm_mesh, loader.py:538-548) already treats each member as an Agent via _node_from_spec_agent. model_to_agent_spec_properties is still reused for the member payload Properties, but wrapped in an Agent, not an LlmNode.

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (guard-test lockstep): add a new _MARK_PORTAL_SPEC = 'neograph/portal_spec' module constant in _agent_spec.py alongside the existing _MARK_* constants; in the SAME change, extend tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py's _EXPECTED_MARKER_VALUES frozenset and its exact-wire-value pinned-assertion list to include the new marker -- the guard fails otherwise (it bans inline marker literals outside a _MARK_... constant and pins exact wire values).

Everything else (Swarm-vs-Flow top-level return-type special-case, mesh-member-collection reuse from _validation_portal.py, Swarm.handoff defaulting to HandoffMode.OPTIONAL, relationships built from each member's Portal.to list) stays as originally researched.
notes:
NOTE (2026-07-15): 'the emitted Spec' here is the neograph-flavored Agent Spec (the one machine format). A Portal mesh must be expressible in it via x-neograph metadata — part of the format/metadata contract defined by i3zsh.
## Findings
- CLARIFY per 5x43u's own 2026-07-15 NOTE: 'the emitted Spec' is NOT `src/neograph/_spec_schema.py`/loader.py's human-authoring YAML `Spec` (that stays authoring-DX-only, orthogonal). The ONE machine/runtime format is the Agent-Spec-flavored export (pyagentspec `Flow`/`Swarm` + `neograph/`-prefixed `metadata` markers), defined by `to_agent_spec()`/`from_agent_spec()` (neograph-i3zsh/01i0g, both closed). So 'extend the Spec schema + loader' in this task's raw description is STALE wording inherited from before the i3zsh UNIFICATION note landed — the real surface to extend is `src/neograph/_agent_spec.py` (export) with its already-existing sibling in `src/neograph/loader.py` (import), NOT `_spec_schema.py`/NodeSpec/ConstructSpec.
- **The import direction ALREADY EXISTS and is the exact template to mirror**: `loader.py`'s `from_agent_spec()` already imports a top-level pyagentspec `Swarm` (`pyagentspec.swarm.Swarm`, AgenticComponent, NOT a Flow node) onto a native Portal peer mesh via `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` (loader.py:522), `_swarm_agents_ordered` (loader.py:472, first_agent -> entry, then relationship order, dedup by identity), and `_synthesize_swarm_payload` (loader.py:491, builds a uniform `{goto: str, ...folded fields}` payload model via `create_model`). It builds `Node(inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload) | Portal(to=peers)` per agent and lets `_ir_normalize.py` (sole writer) derive `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel`; the assembled mesh is re-validated by the SAME `_check_portal_mesh` a hand-written mesh gets. It emits a `warnings.warn` (best-effort, structural downgrade disclosed, never silent).
- **The gap this task closes is the EXPORT direction (the missing mirror-image half)**: `_agent_spec.py`'s `_reject_unrepresentable_fields` (line 134) currently raises `ConfigurationError` for ANY node with `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` set, citing '(symmetric to the ratified Swarm import-reject...)' — but that citation is now WRONG/stale: the Swarm side is an ACCEPT (best-effort import), not a reject. Task 5x43u = replace that reject with a lowering: detect a Portal mode-(a) peer mesh at the current construct level and emit a pyagentspec `Swarm` (top-level `AgenticComponent`, symmetric to `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh`) instead of raising.
- **Mesh identification helper to REUSE, don't reinvent**: `_validation_portal.py`'s mesh-collection logic (lines 59-65: `[n for n in construct.nodes if n.modifier_set.portal is not None and not n.modifier_set.portal.is_dispatch]`) is the canonical way to find mesh members at one construct level; entry = first member in construct.nodes order (contiguity + entry-first already enforced by `_check_portal_mesh`, lines 120-132). `_check_portal_mesh` has ALREADY run by the time `to_agent_spec()` walks a validated `Construct`, so the exporter can trust contiguity/uniform-payload/entry-first invariants without re-deriving them — just re-use the same member-collection expression (or factor it into a shared helper if duplicated 3x).
- **Payload/routing shape**: mesh members share one payload type (`_declared_output(entry)`, checked by `_check_portal_mesh`) carrying the Portal `route` field (default `'goto'`) — this is what `_synthesize_swarm_payload`'s import-side reconstruction re-derives; export is the direct inverse: take each Portal member's declared output Property list (via the ALREADY-REUSED `model_to_agent_spec_properties`, same as every other node) and each member's `Portal.to` list becomes `Swarm.relationships` `(this_agent, dst_agent)` tuples; entry member -> `Swarm.first_agent`.
- **v1 D-MEMBER-MODES constraint carries into export too**: mesh members are `scripted`/`think`/`raw` only in v1 (`agent`/`act` rejected at assembly per `dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md` D-MEMBER-MODES) — so the export path never needs to handle a Portal member that is ALSO an agent/act composite; it only needs think/scripted/raw -> pyagentspec Agent/Tool-ish per-agent lowering (mirrors how `_node_from_spec_agent`/`_reconstruct_agent_node` do the inverse for plain agent/act nodes, but Portal members are simpler, think-mode-only in v1).
- **Round-trip markers precedent to copy**: every other modifier (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator) stamps a `neograph/<modifier>_spec` metadata marker (per-group, Layer A) on export so `from_agent_spec` can losslessly reconstruct beyond the primitive-level Swarm shape (e.g. `max_hops`/`on_exhaust`, which `_synthesize_swarm_payload`'s import currently has NO way to recover — best-effort/lossy on that axis today). Task 5x43u should stamp an equivalent `neograph/portal_spec` (or similarly named) marker on the exported `Swarm` (mirrors `OracleSpec`/`EachSpec`/`LoopSpec`/`OperatorSpec` pattern in `_spec_schema.py`, though those are for the OTHER human-authoring format — the marker payload shape here is a plain dict, not a `_spec_schema.py` model) carrying `max_hops`/`on_exhaust`/`route` so `from_agent_spec`'s Swarm-import path can eventually read it back losslessly (currently it can't — that upgrade is optional/stretch for THIS task, but at minimum the marker should be written so the information is not lost, i.e. round-trip-ready even if the reader isn't upgraded yet).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:134-141 (`_reject_unrepresentable_fields`) -- the CURRENT reject to replace with a Swarm-lowering branch; also see module docstring lines 20-26 (needs updating once Portal is no longer purely rejected).
- src/neograph/loader.py:472-560 (`_swarm_agents_ordered`, `_synthesize_swarm_payload`, `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh`) -- the EXISTING import-direction mirror to copy/invert; `from_agent_spec` dispatches on `type(flow).__name__ == 'Swarm'` at the top-level entry (line ~590), so `to_agent_spec` must symmetrically detect 'this Construct's top-level nodes contain a Portal mesh' and return a `Swarm` object instead of (or alongside) a `Flow`.
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40-215 (`_check_portal_mesh`) -- the assembly-time validator that ALREADY enforces contiguity/entry-first/uniform-payload/reachability/entry-only-knobs; `to_agent_spec` can rely on these invariants already holding for any `Construct` reaching export (line 59-65 member-collection expression to reuse).
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:599-650 (`Portal` class, mode-a fields `to`/`route`/`max_hops`/`on_exhaust`) -- the fields to lower/marker-stamp.
- src/neograph/node.py:207-220 (`handoff_param`/`handoff_channel`) -- single-writer fields (`_ir_normalize.py`), read-only signal the exporter checks (do not attempt to derive/set these in the exporter).
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:398 (`model_to_agent_spec_properties`) -- reuse for Portal member payload Property conversion, same as every other node (no new type walker).
- pyagentspec/swarm.py (installed at .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pyagentspec/swarm.py) -- `Swarm(AgenticComponent)` with `first_agent`/`relationships: list[tuple[Agent,Agent]]`/`handoff_mode: HandoffMode` fields (confirmed against real installed pyagentspec 26.1.x, not paraphrased).
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md ss1 (D-SCOPE, D-MEMBER-MODES, D-DICT-OUTPUTS judgment calls), s2.1 (Portal modifier field reference), s3 (mesh runtime contract) -- authoritative for what mode (a) actually guarantees at assembly.
- docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md -- cited by the raw task description; historical decision log for the Keymaker->Portal rename and v1 scope cuts (D-SCOPE explicitly deferred 'Keymaker-in-spec schema' -- this task is that deferred item, now re-scoped by the 07-15 NOTE to mean the Agent-Spec machine format, not the human-authoring Spec).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NEEDS USER INPUT: none outstanding — the 2026-07-15 NOTE on 5x43u already resolved the surface-of-truth ambiguity (Agent Spec, not `_spec_schema.py`) authoritatively; flagging here only so the implementer does not silently revert to the stale 'extend NodeSpec/loader.py Spec-YAML schema' reading of the raw task title.
- Dict-form Portal outputs are rejected at assembly (D-DICT-OUTPUTS) so the exporter never needs to handle a dict-form mesh payload — only single-type.
- v1 members are think/scripted/raw only (D-MEMBER-MODES) — do not build agent/act-composite lowering for mesh members in this task; that is out of scope (would need separate research if ever lifted).
- `max_hops`/`on_exhaust` (entry-only knobs) have NO native `Swarm` field — must ride in a `neograph/portal_spec` (or equivalently named) metadata marker on the `Swarm` object itself (Swarm IS a `Component` subtype per pyagentspec, so `.metadata` exists — confirm this before implementing, mirrors the Layer A per-group marker pattern already proven to survive `to_dict`/`from_dict` for Flow/Node per i3zsh's step-1 smoke test; the SAME smoke-test pattern should be re-run/extended for `Swarm.metadata` specifically before trusting it, since i3zsh's proof only covered Flow/Node/disaggregated-Tool, not Swarm).
- A Construct can mix a Portal mesh at the top level with ordinary Flow nodes alongside it (mesh nodes are just some of `construct.nodes`) — `to_agent_spec`'s current single-`Flow`-return shape may need to become a Flow containing a reference/embed to the Swarm, or the top-level return type may need reconsidering (a Swarm is NOT a Flow node) — this structural question (does a mixed mesh+Flow construct export as one Flow with an embedded Swarm-as-node, or does a Portal mesh require the WHOLE top-level construct to export as a bare Swarm) is not yet resolved by any existing code and should be the FIRST implementation question to pin (mirrors how `from_agent_spec` special-cases 'Swarm is a top-level AgenticComponent, not a Flow node' at the very top of the function, sidestepping the question entirely on import -- export may need the same top-level special-case, OR may need a genuinely new lowering shape for the mixed case).
## Codebase Disease Scan (5x43u)
Pattern: Portal peer/dispatch mode discrimination must go through Portal.is_dispatch (never an inline route=='decide' check) -- verify no call site duplicates this logic before adding the new Swarm-export branch.
Scan command: `grep -rn "is_dispatch" src/neograph/*.py`
Total instances found: 14 across _construct_validation.py, _validation_portal.py, compiler.py, _wiring.py, modifiers.py, state.py

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-14 | _construct_validation.py:249, _validation_portal.py:64, compiler.py:256, _wiring.py:722, modifiers.py (definition+comment+2 uses), state.py (_is_dispatch wrapper + 3 uses) | all read via .is_dispatch property or a thin _is_dispatch(n) wrapper | ALLOWLIST | all consistent -- single source of truth already respected everywhere; confirms the MIGRATE target is isolated to _agent_spec.py's _reject_unrepresentable_fields (the one reject site to replace with a Swarm-lowering branch, per design) |

No inline 'route == decide' duplication found anywhere. Scope confirmed as scoped in the design field.
## Architect Review
- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 3's reuse prescription is type-wrong. It tells the implementer to lower each mesh member via 'the SAME per-node lowering used for plain think-mode nodes' — but think-mode `_lower_node` returns `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.LlmNode` (a Flow NODE), while `Swarm.first_agent`/`relationships` are typed `AgenticComponent`/`List[Tuple[AgenticComponent, AgenticComponent]]` (confirmed in installed pyagentspec/swarm.py:105-107; `Agent(AgenticComponent)` in agent.py:23). Putting an LlmNode into first_agent/relationships fails pydantic validation. The import mirror confirms the correct shape: `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` (loader.py:538-548) treats each Swarm member as an `Agent` via `_node_from_spec_agent`, so the EXPORT inverse must build `Agent` objects (reuse/adapt `_make_agent`, _agent_spec.py:213), NOT the LlmNode think path. Suggestion: lower each mesh member to a pyagentspec `Agent` (via _make_agent), keeping `model_to_agent_spec_properties` only for the member payload Properties; correct step 3's 'reuse think-mode LlmNode lowering' wording to 'reuse the Agent lowering (_make_agent)'.
- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 4 (stamp `neograph/portal_spec` marker) omits the guard-test update. `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py` pins the marker contract with a hardcoded `_EXPECTED_MARKER_VALUES` frozenset (line ~49) + an exact-wire-value assertion list (test_marker_constants_pin_the_exact_wire_values), and bans inline marker string literals outside a `_MARK_... = "neograph/..."` constant assignment. Adding the marker therefore requires: (a) a new `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC = "neograph/portal_spec"` module constant in _agent_spec.py, and (b) extending `_EXPECTED_MARKER_VALUES` + the pinned-value list in the guard test, or that guard fails. Suggestion: name the guard-test edits explicitly in the write-test atom (guard-first, in lockstep with the constant).
- [LOW] Finding: Plan does not specify the `Swarm.handoff` mode to emit. Swarm requires non-empty `relationships` (raises on empty, swarm.py:150) and defaults `handoff=HandoffMode.OPTIONAL`; a Command(goto) peer mesh is semantically closer to a full conversation handoff than OPTIONAL send_message, and the field is lossy-on-import today (`_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` ignores it). Default is acceptable for v1, but state the choice explicitly. The empty-relationships raise is unreachable for a valid 2+ member mesh (`_check_portal_mesh` reachability guarantees each member has peers) — confirm rather than assume.

Survives attack (honest positives): `.metadata` DOES exist on Swarm via `Component` (component.py:173), so the risk-list 'confirm .metadata exists' is satisfiable. Step 2's interception BEFORE the per-item `_reject_unrepresentable_fields` loop is correct. Step 1 correctly identifies the Swarm-vs-Flow return-type question as first-to-pin (`to_agent_spec -> Flow` today, _agent_spec.py:586) with a sound v1 answer (bare top-level Swarm; ConfigurationError on mixed mesh+Flow). The is_dispatch disposition scan is accurate — no inline route=='decide' duplication exists.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestPortalMeshExportsToSwarm::test_portal_peer_mesh_lowers_to_swarm (+ sibling test_mixed_mesh_and_plain_flow_node_is_rejected)
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step). Confirmed: ConfigurationError('node triage has modifier combination PORTAL — no Agent Spec lowering yet') raised from _agent_spec.py's _lower_construct_item fallback (line ~578), NOT an import/collection error.
- Tests expected behavior: to_agent_spec() must lower a Portal mode-(a) peer mesh (Node.scripted(...) | Portal(to=[...])) to a top-level pyagentspec Swarm whose first_agent/relationships are real Agent objects (named '{node.name}-agent', via _make_agent) matching the mesh's entry + Portal.to edges, with max_hops/on_exhaust/route stamped on a neograph/portal_spec metadata marker; a Construct mixing a Portal mesh with an ordinary Flow node must raise ConfigurationError rather than silently exporting a partial shape.
## Implementation Notes
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py: added _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm() + top-level mesh detection in to_agent_spec() (before the existing per-item Flow-lowering loop). Detects Portal peer-mode mesh members via item.modifier_set.portal is not None and not is_dispatch; if ALL nodes are mesh members, exports a top-level pyagentspec Swarm; if SOME (mixed mesh+plain), raises ConfigurationError (fail-loud, no partial export).
- Each member lowers via the EXISTING _make_agent() helper (agent/act mode's Agent+ServerTool builder) -- reused unchanged, not reinvented. inputs/outputs passed as [] (not the member's payload Properties): pyagentspec's Agent ties inputs/outputs to {{placeholder}} names in system_prompt, and mesh members have no prompt template, so passing payload Properties unconditionally raised 'did not expect any properties' -- discovered via the actual pydantic validator, not assumed.
- Added _MARK_PORTAL_SPEC = 'neograph/portal_spec' constant + extended tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py's _EXPECTED_MARKER_VALUES (guard-test lockstep, per architect review finding #2).
- Entry-only knobs (max_hops/on_exhaust/route) ride the neograph/portal_spec marker on Swarm.metadata, since Swarm has no native field for any of them.
- Kept the original _reject_unrepresentable_fields's handoff_param/handoff_channel reject in place as a safety net for pathological cases that never reach the new top-level mesh detection (legitimate mesh members never fall through to it, since to_agent_spec's new mesh branch intercepts them before the per-item loop).
- Full tests/*agent_spec* suite (93 tests) passes. ruff/mypy clean.
## Sweep Verification (5x43u)

Re-scan command (same as Phase 1b): `grep -rn "is_dispatch" src/neograph/*.py`
Pre-fix instances: 14 | Post-fix instances: 15 (+1: my own new code)

| 1-14 | _construct_validation.py, _validation_portal.py, compiler.py, _wiring.py, modifiers.py, state.py | ALLOWLIST (all consistent, read via .is_dispatch property) | unchanged | YES |
| new | _agent_spec.py:660 (to_agent_spec's new mesh-detection: 'not item.modifier_set.portal.is_dispatch') | N/A (didn't exist at Phase 1b) | NEW, uses the SAME .is_dispatch property convention as every other site -- no inline route=='decide' duplication introduced | YES -- consistent with the established pattern, not a new disease instance |

Guard requirement: N/A -- Phase 1b's disposition table was all-ALLOWLIST for the is_dispatch pattern specifically (the real MIGRATE target was the separate handoff_param/handoff_channel reject in _reject_unrepresentable_fields, which this task's fix bypasses via new top-level mesh detection in to_agent_spec, rather than editing the reject itself in place -- confirmed: grep for the reject text still finds it unchanged, now unreachable for legitimate top-level meshes). title: Backfill: unit tests for normalize_outputs / normalize_inputs in _normalize.py (mqr3 follow-up)
description:
**Context**: neograph-mqr3 created `src/neograph/_normalize.py` (104 lines, NormalizedOutputs/NormalizedInputs dataclasses + `normalize_outputs()` / `normalize_inputs()` functions) and replaced 18 isinstance call sites with normalized access. Closed without unit tests on the new public API. The existing test suites passing only proves nothing broke — not that the normalizer correctly discriminates every form of the `type | dict[str, type] | None` trichotomy. A buggy normalizer would silently corrupt three-surface output/input mapping.

**Source**: docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §8; predecessor neograph-mqr3.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_normalize.py` (new)

**Test class**: `TestNormalizeOutputs` + `TestNormalizeInputs`

**Test type**: unit

**What it exercises**: each branch of the `type | dict[str, type] | None` trichotomy for both `normalize_outputs` and `normalize_inputs`. Direct table-driven tests on the dataclass fields returned.

**Cases for `TestNormalizeOutputs`**:
1. `outputs=SingleType` → `primary=SingleType`, `primary_key` is the expected default (read the module to determine: probably `None` or a specific sentinel), `secondary={}`, `is_dict_form=False`, `is_none=False`
2. `outputs=None` → `is_none=True`, `primary=None`, `secondary={}`
3. `outputs={"a": A, "b": B, "c": C}` → `primary=A`, `primary_key="a"`, `secondary={"b": B, "c": C}`, `is_dict_form=True` (first dict key is primary per the existing _resolve_primary_output convention)
4. `outputs={"only": Only}` → `primary=Only`, `primary_key="only"`, `secondary={}`, `is_dict_form=True`
5. Edge: `outputs={}` empty dict — document expected behavior (probably should raise or treat as None; check what mqr3 implemented)
6. `all_keys` field correctness for each case above

**Cases for `TestNormalizeInputs`**:
1. `inputs=None` → `is_none=True`, `by_name={}`, `single_type=None`
2. `inputs=SingleType` → `single_type=SingleType`, `by_name={}`, `is_dict_form=False`
3. `inputs={"x": X, "y": Y}` → `by_name={"x": X, "y": Y}`, `single_type=None`, `is_dict_form=True`
4. Edge: `inputs={}` empty dict — document expected behavior

**Expected initial state**: write tests FIRST against current `_normalize.py`. Most should pass (mqr3 implemented something reasonable). If ANY fail, the normalizer has a bug and 18 production call sites are reading it. File a P1 bug per failure.

**Persistence**: tests stay in suite permanently.

## Acceptance

- `tests/test_normalize.py` exists with at least 8 test cases (5 outputs + 3 inputs, plus edges)
- All tests pass against current `_normalize.py` (or P1 bugs filed for failures)
- `make quality` shows the new tests run as part of the suite
close_reason: 17 unit tests added in tests/test_normalize.py covering normalize_outputs (10 cases: single type, None, multi-key dict, single-key dict, empty-dict-raises-IndexError, all_keys ordering, all_keys empty for single+None forms, frozen, secondary-copy-independence) and normalize_inputs (7 cases: None, single type, dict, empty dict, by_name ordering, by_name-copy-independence, frozen). All 17 pass against mqr3's normalizer — verified, no bugs filed.

title: Oracle merge_prompt silently drops caller's llm_config (structured vs json_mode conflation)
description:
## What

`Oracle(merge_prompt=...)` triggers an LLM merge call via `_wiring._merge_one_group → invoke_structured(...)`. The call passes `model_tier`, `prompt_template`, `input_data`, `output_model`, `config`, but NOT `llm_config`. As a result the merge call ignores the caller's explicit `output_strategy` preference (set via `@node(llm_config=...)` or `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config=...)`) and falls back to `invoke_structured`'s default strategy (`"structured"`).

This silently flips the transport path from NeoGraph-native JSON parsing to LangChain's `with_structured_output()`, changing both correctness behavior (fence stripping vs. none) and failure modes (framework-side retries with error feedback vs. provider-side structured output enforcement).

## Current code (src/neograph/_wiring.py, _merge_one_group)

```python
if oracle.merge_prompt:
    from neograph._llm import invoke_structured

    if oracle.merge_pre_process is not None:
        input_data = oracle.merge_pre_process(variants)
    else:
        input_data = variants[0] if variants else None

    used_fallback = False
    try:
        merged = invoke_structured(
            model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
            prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
            input_data=input_data,
            output_model=output_model,
            config=config,
            # llm_config NOT passed — loses caller's explicit choice
        )
    ...
```

## Evidence — piarch rehearsal UC-fix1 traces

Across 26 LLM calls in the rehearsal on `BR-UC-001`:
- 23 calls used `strategy=json_mode` (correct — explicitly set via `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"})` on the sub-constructs)
- 3 calls used `strategy=structured` (wrong — the 3 Oracle merge_prompt paths: `uc/merge-internal-research`, `uc/merge-si-stakeholders`, `uc/merge-extensions`)

All 3 structured-strategy calls are Oracle merges. Generators inside the same sub-construct run `json_mode` as declared; the Oracle merge silently switches strategy.

Concrete failure that surfaced: `uc/merge-external-research` merge call — DeepSeek R1 returned fenced JSON (```json\n{...}\n```). Under `json_mode` NeoGraph's `_parse_json_response → _extract_json` strips markdown fences and succeeds. Under the silent `structured` fallback, LangChain passes the raw fenced text to `model.model_validate_json()` which fails with:

```
pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ExternalResearch
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
  input_value='```json\\n{\\n  "comparable_systems": ...  "sources": []\\n}\\n```'
```

The caller (piarch) had explicitly opted into json_mode via `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"}) | Oracle(merge_prompt=...)`, but the merge call silently ignored that choice.

## Why

Likely an oversight: when `_merge_one_group` was built, the invoke_structured signature grew an llm_config parameter later, and the existing merge path wasn't updated to thread it through.

Note: `structured` and `json_mode` are semantically different and both legitimate. This bug is NOT about picking a better default — it's about honoring the caller's explicit configuration. Flipping the default to `json_mode` would silently change semantics for callers who explicitly wanted LangChain's provider-native structured output path.

## Fix

Propagate the enclosing Node's (or Construct's) `llm_config` to the merge `invoke_structured` call. Two cases to cover:

### Case 1: @node-level Oracle (`@node(ensemble_n=3, merge_prompt=..., llm_config=...)`)

The Oracle is synthesized from the @node decorator. `_merge_one_group` receives the Node. Thread `node.llm_config`:

```python
merged = invoke_structured(
    model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
    prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
    input_data=input_data,
    output_model=output_model,
    config=config,
    llm_config=node.llm_config,  # NEW
)
```

### Case 2: construct-level Oracle (`construct_from_functions(..., llm_config=X) | Oracle(merge_prompt=...)`)

The Oracle wraps a Construct, not a single Node. The construct's `llm_config` needs to reach `_merge_one_group`. Options:

- **(a)** Store `construct.llm_config` on the synthesized barrier/merge Node at compile time, so `node.llm_config` is populated correctly for both cases.
- **(b)** Add a `merge_llm_config` field to `Oracle` itself for explicit override; if unset, fall back to the enclosing construct's llm_config.

Prefer (a) — it makes the merge call inherit the caller's explicit choice with zero extra wiring on the consumer side.

### Optional addition

For cases where the merge should use a DIFFERENT strategy than the generators (rare but legitimate — e.g. generators use `structured` with provider function calling, merge uses `json_mode` for tolerant parsing), add an explicit `Oracle(merge_llm_config=...)` override. Don't require it; default to inheriting.

## Acceptance

- `_merge_one_group`'s `invoke_structured` call receives `llm_config` derived from the enclosing Node or Construct.
- For @node-level Oracle: `node.llm_config` flows through.
- For construct-level Oracle: `construct.llm_config` is accessible at merge time (option (a) — stored on the compiled merge node).
- Unit test: Oracle(merge_prompt=...) on a Node/Construct with `llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"}` — assert the merge call is invoked with that strategy. Inspect via monkeypatching `invoke_structured` or reading the structlog `strategy` field.
- Regression test: existing tests still pass (no change to default behavior when `llm_config` is unset — merge still uses `invoke_structured`'s default, which is `strategy="structured"`).
- Integration check (downstream validation in piarch): after fix, piarch rehearsal trace on `BR-UC-001` shows zero LLM calls with `strategy=structured` (all inherit `json_mode` from piarch's explicit `llm_config` declarations).

## Context

Surfaced during piarch's `piarch-rhsu0` epic where multiple Oracle merge_prompt paths were newly introduced. The piarch side was already doing the right thing (declaring `output_strategy: json_mode` on sub-constructs), but NeoGraph's Oracle dispatch was dropping the config. Tracked downstream in piarch as `piarch-7j1he` (derive-business-rules prompt-framework mismatch) — that bug and this one surfaced in the same rehearsal.
design:
## Root Cause
make_oracle_merge_fn and _merge_one_group both call invoke_structured without llm_config. The enclosing node's llm_config is available at compile time but not threaded through.

## Fix Approach
1. Add llm_config param to make_oracle_merge_fn, close over it in the merge closure
2. Pass node.llm_config at all 3 call sites (compiler.py:443, compiler.py:354, _wiring.py:251)
3. In _merge_one_group (EachxOracle), read node.llm_config directly
4. Pass llm_config to invoke_structured in both _oracle.py and _wiring.py

2. _wiring.py:_merge_one_group (EachxOracle fused path) — same
Both need the same fix. No other invoke_structured call sites miss llm_config.

Overall: ALL_LOW
