title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-my84
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-my84` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-my84/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-my84
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-my84)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-my84 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-my84 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-my84/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-my84 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-my84/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Write regression test for neograph-my84
description:
Write a failing test that defines the expected behavior for neograph-my84.
This is the TDD "red" step -- the test MUST exist and MUST fail before
any implementation begins.

## Instructions

1. Identify what to test from the implementation plan
2. Choose test level (prefer integration over unit when DB involved)
3. Write the failing test
4. Use test factories for test data (never inline model construction)
5. Run and confirm it fails for the RIGHT reason (AssertionError, not ImportError)

## BANNED Patterns

- `pytest.mark.xfail` is BANNED in regression tests
- AST-scanning / source-code pattern tests are BANNED **as a
  substitute for behavioral testing** — when the task changes
  behavior, the red test must exercise that behavior, not scan source.
- Direct DB session management in test code is BANNED

## Structural-disease tasks (no testable behavior)

Some tasks eliminate a NON-behavioral disease pattern (a casing/naming
wordmark, an import idiom, a helper-bypass that is type- or
text-shaped, not runtime-observable). For these, no behavioral failing
test exists — the only meaningful red artifact IS the structural guard
that `sweep-verify` will later require. In that case:
- Write that structural guard HERE, confirm it FAILS (the disease
  instances exist), and record it as the red artifact.
- The AST/source-text BAN above does NOT apply — it bans source scans
  used INSTEAD OF behavioral tests, not the structural guard that pins
  a structural invariant. The same guard satisfies `sweep-verify`.

## Verification: Paste the FAILED Output

You MUST see the word "FAILED" in pytest output.

## Store Test Reference

```bash
bd update neograph-my84 --append-notes "## Regression Test
- Test: <test_path>::<test_name>
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step)
- Tests expected behavior: [one sentence]"
```
acceptance_criteria: Failing test exists. Test reference written to task notes.

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-etxo
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-etxo`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-etxo)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-etxo --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-etxo sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: gm-1: Cluster E unification — _apply_skip_when joins _build_state_update in renamed _state_write.py
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §4
- docs/design/god-module-analysis-2026-05-20.md Cluster E + Q3 + Q4
- Predecessor: neograph-cgkl (mechanical split; this is the architectural follow-up)

## The problem
`_apply_skip_when` (_modifier_io.py) and `_build_state_update` (_state_io.py) are ONE change axis split across two files. They share the same modifier rule set (Each-key wrapping, Loop counter increment) and `_apply_skip_when` calls `_build_state_update` directly at `_modifier_io.py:61`. Any new modifier shape forces both to change in lockstep.

## The fix
1. Rename `src/neograph/_state_io.py` → `src/neograph/_state_write.py` (mirrors `_state_bus.py` for the read side)
2. Move `_apply_skip_when` from `_modifier_io.py:23-71` into `_state_write.py`
3. Update single-line docstring: "Rules for writing state updates from node outputs — modifier-aware key wrapping (Each, Loop, Oracle-fusion), dict-form output projection, skip-when state writes."
4. Update all importers (factory.py, tests/) to reference the new name + module
5. Coordinate with gm-2 (which removes `_inject_oracle_config` from this same module before/during the rename)

## Dependencies
gm-2 (neograph-<TBD>) should run alongside or before this — both touch `_state_io.py`. If gm-2 runs first, this rename happens cleanly. If together in one executor, sequential.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestClusterEUnification` (new test class)
**Test type**: structural-guard + co-change witness
**What it exercises**:
1. `_state_write.py` exists; `_state_io.py` does not (or is a backward-compat re-export shim documented for one release).
2. `_state_write.py` contains both `_build_state_update` AND `_apply_skip_when` as module-level functions.
3. `_modifier_io.py` (or its successor `_input_shape.py` from gm-3) does NOT contain `_apply_skip_when`.
4. **Co-change witness**: AST-scan asserts every reference to Each-key wrapping logic or Loop counter increment lives in `_state_write.py`. Inject a sentinel comment `# MODIFIER_RULE_TOUCHPOINT` at each rule site; the guard counts sentinels and asserts they all live in `_state_write.py`.

**Expected initial state**: failing — guard cannot find the renamed module; functions still in old locations.
**Persistence**: stays in suite permanently.

Order: write the failing guard FIRST → run → fails → rename + move → re-run → passes.

## Acceptance
- `_state_write.py` exists with `_build_state_update` + `_apply_skip_when`
- `_state_io.py` deleted (or backward-compat shim with planned deletion date)
- `_modifier_io.py` no longer references `_apply_skip_when` (it's moved out)
- All callers updated
- New structural guard TestClusterEUnification green
- `make quality` green (1783+ tests)
close_reason: Renamed _state_io.py -> _state_write.py; moved _apply_skip_when from _modifier_io.py to _state_write.py; added 4 MODIFIER_RULE_TOUCHPOINT sentinels; new TestClusterEUnification guard (5 tests) added

title: ARCH: relocate _BranchNode out of forward.py (DIP inversion — compiler/state/_wiring import it UP from the DX layer)
description: Split out from neograph-8cqd (Option A scope was kept to the declared-output selector + TS-justification scrub). Finding from the DDD + SOLID three-lens review (docs/design/ir-item-dispatch-{ddd,solid-grasp}-2026-06-04.md): _BranchNode is a core-IR concept but is DEFINED in the DX-layer forward.py (class _BranchNode(Modifiable), forward.py:350) and imported UPWARD by compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py. That is a DIP inversion / bounded-context leak. Relocate _BranchNode to a neutral low-level IR module (e.g. a new _ir_branch.py or alongside the IR protocols) so the lower layers no longer import from forward.py. Add/extend an import-DAG guard. Behavior-preserving; guard-first. Out of scope: any ConstructItem-protocol widening (that remains gated on a 4th item type per neograph-8cqd S9.4).
design:
## Core Invariant
_BranchNode and its _BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec are core-IR concepts owned by a neutral low-level module (_ir_branch.py); the compiler/state/wiring layers import them from there and NEVER import from the DX layer forward.py -- dependency points DX -> IR, never IR -> DX.

## Fix Approach
Relocate _ConditionSpec + _BranchMeta + _BranchNode to a new src/neograph/_ir_branch.py (runtime deps: modifiers.Modifiable/ModifierSet; Node/Construct under TYPE_CHECKING). forward.py imports them back; compiler.py/state.py/_wiring.py repoint to _ir_branch. Guard-first: add an import-DAG guard banning forward imports from the lower layers (RED now, GREEN after). Behavior-preserving.
notes:
## Findings
- _BranchNode defined at forward.py:350 (DX layer). Imported UPWARD by compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py:35 (all `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode`). That is the DIP inversion: lower compiler/state/wiring layers depend on the DX layer.
- Those 3 modules import ONLY _BranchNode and access branch._neo_branch_meta.condition_spec via attributes (no direct import of _BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec).
- _BranchNode (forward.py:350) deps: Modifiable, ModifierSet (modifiers.py, IR layer), and _BranchMeta (annotation only -> stringized via `from __future__ import annotations`).
- _BranchMeta (forward.py:337) deps: _ConditionSpec + list[Node|Construct] (annotations).
- _ConditionSpec (forward.py:311): pure frozen dataclass; deps are annotations only (Node|Construct|None, Any).
- _BranchPoint/_BranchTrace (forward.py:321/331) depend on forward-internal proxies (_ConditionProxy/_Proxy) -> STAY in forward.py.
- Other modules referencing _BranchNode (construct.py, _normalize.py, _validation_types.py, modifiers.py) do so ONLY in comments/docstrings -- no real imports/isinstance. No changes needed there.
- Cycle check: modifiers.py runtime-imports only _dev_warnings + errors (node/construct under TYPE_CHECKING) -> a new _ir_branch importing modifiers has no cycle. Node/Construct referenced only as TYPE_CHECKING annotations in _ir_branch.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:311-364 -- _ConditionSpec, _BranchMeta, _BranchNode (move these three).
- src/neograph/compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py:35 -- repoint imports to _ir_branch.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:190 Modifiable, :545 ModifierSet (runtime deps of _BranchNode).
- src/neograph/_ir_protocols.py -- references _BranchNode in docstring only.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py:305 TestAssemblyClusterImportDAG + _parse_neograph_imports helper (extend / add a guard here).

## Plan
1. New module src/neograph/_ir_branch.py: `from __future__ import annotations`; import Modifiable, ModifierSet from modifiers; TYPE_CHECKING import Node, Construct; define _ConditionSpec, _BranchMeta, _BranchNode.
2. forward.py: delete the 3 classes; add `from neograph._ir_branch import _BranchMeta, _BranchNode, _ConditionSpec`.
3. compiler.py / state.py / _wiring.py: `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode` -> `from neograph._ir_branch import _BranchNode`.
4. Update test imports of _BranchNode from forward if any.
5. Guard-first: add import-DAG guard asserting compiler/state/_wiring (and other lower layers) do NOT import `forward`.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- get_type_hints on the moved dataclasses would need Node/Construct resolvable; add TYPE_CHECKING import (annotations are stringized, so no runtime need). Low risk -- these are internal sentinels.
- Behavior-preserving: pure relocation; isinstance(_BranchNode) identity unchanged (single class, single new module). No public API change (_BranchNode is private).
- Three-surface parity: _BranchNode is produced only by forward.py (ForwardConstruct branch tracing); declarative/programmatic do not create it. Refactor does not change behavior on any surface; full suite + test_forward.py cover it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-9epk)
Disease: a lower compiler/IR-layer module importing UP from the DX layer forward.py (DIP inversion / bounded-context leak).

Scan command (SYNTACTIC -- single grep, no fan-out):
  grep -rn "from neograph.forward import\|import neograph.forward\| forward\." src/neograph/ | grep -v "forward.py:"
Total forward-import sites: 4 (+1 comment).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _wiring.py:35 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 2 | compiler.py:44 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 3 | state.py:16 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 4 | __init__.py:48 | from neograph.forward import ForwardConstruct | ALLOWLIST | package facade re-exports the PUBLIC DX class; the top-level __init__ sits above all layers -- legitimate, not a DIP inversion |
| 5 | conditions.py:18 | comment mentioning forward.py | ALLOWLIST | comment, not an import |

Only the 3 _BranchNode imports are the disease; all fixed by relocation. No DEFER rows.
SYNTACTIC -> single grep sufficient; no fan-out, so .claude/code-review/neograph-9epk/ not required.
## Architect Review (neograph-9epk)
Inline review (behavior-preserving relocation; dependency map verified by code reads).

1. Root cause correctness [LOW]: confirmed DIP inversion -- compiler/state/_wiring import _BranchNode UP from forward.py (DX). Derived from the DDD/SOLID review (docs/design/ir-item-dispatch-*).
2. Fix minimality [LOW]: new _ir_branch.py holding the 3 branch classes; repoint 3 imports; forward.py imports them back. No logic change.
3. Regression risk [LOW]: pure relocation; _BranchNode is a single private class -> isinstance identity preserved (one definition, one new module). _BranchPoint/_BranchTrace stay in forward (proxy-coupled). Full suite + test_forward.py cover branch lowering.
4. Architecture compliance [HIGH value, LOW risk]: restores DX -> IR direction; matches the _normalize.py/_declared_output precedent (neutral low-level IR module reachable from every layer). conditions.py is the model for "lower module owns the concept, forward.py consumes it".
5. Similar-bug scalability [LOW]: disease-scan shows the 3 _BranchNode imports are the only DIP-inversion instances; __init__ re-export of ForwardConstruct is the legitimate facade. The import-DAG guard generalizes the ban.
6. Test coverage [LOW]: guard-first -- the import-DAG guard (compiler/state/_wiring must NOT import forward) is RED now, GREEN after relocation; full suite verifies behavior preservation.

Decisions confirmed:
- Move _ConditionSpec + _BranchMeta + _BranchNode together (cohesive branch-IR trio); keep _BranchPoint/_BranchTrace in forward (proxy-coupled tracer internals).
- Node/Construct as TYPE_CHECKING-only imports in _ir_branch (annotations stringized) to avoid any IR->DX or import cycle.
- Out of scope: ConstructItem-protocol widening (gated on a 4th item type per neograph-8cqd S9.4) -- do NOT touch.

VERDICT: ALL_LOW -> proceed to write-test (guard-first) + implement.
## Write-test (guard-first, TDD red)
tests/test_guards_assembly.py::TestLowerLayersDoNotImportForwardDX::test_no_lower_layer_imports_forward -- RED: flags _wiring.py, compiler.py, state.py importing from neograph.forward. Meta-tests (positive forward-import detected; negative _ir_branch import OK) pass. Allowlist = {__init__} (facade re-export of ForwardConstruct). Guard stays permanently to ban future IR->DX imports.
## Implement (TDD green / guard-first)
- New module src/neograph/_ir_branch.py holds _ConditionSpec + _BranchMeta + _BranchNode (runtime dep: modifiers.Modifiable/ModifierSet; Node/Construct TYPE_CHECKING-only).
- forward.py: removed the 3 classes; imports them back from _ir_branch (re-exported, so test imports `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode/_BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec` still resolve). ruff auto-dropped now-unused Modifiable/ModifierSet from forward modifiers import. _BranchPoint/_BranchTrace stay in forward (proxy-coupled).
- compiler.py / state.py / _wiring.py: `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode` -> `from neograph._ir_branch import _BranchNode`.
- Import-DAG guard TestLowerLayersDoNotImportForwardDX: RED -> GREEN.
- Updated tests/test_guards_any_audit.py NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST forward.py raise line numbers +1 (the added import line shifted the pre-existing stdlib-contract raises 177/208/237/245/272 -> 178/209/238/246/273; reasons unchanged).
Quality gate: pytest 2133 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean (62 source files).
Behavior-preserving: pure relocation; _BranchNode identity preserved.
## Sweep Verification (neograph-9epk)
Re-scan command: grep -rn "from neograph.forward import\|import neograph.forward" src/neograph/ | grep -v "forward.py:"
Pre-fix disease instances (IR->DX imports): 3; Post-fix: 0.

| # | Phase 1b content | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|------------------|-------------|----------------|----------|
| 1 | _wiring.py: from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | now from neograph._ir_branch | YES |
| 2 | compiler.py: from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | now from neograph._ir_branch | YES |
| 3 | state.py: from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | now from neograph._ir_branch | YES |
| 4 | __init__.py: from neograph.forward import ForwardConstruct | ALLOWLIST | unchanged; public facade re-export (false-positive reason holds) | YES |

## Structural Guard
- File: tests/test_guards_assembly.py
- Class: TestLowerLayersDoNotImportForwardDX
- AST-based: scans every src/neograph/*.py; asserts none except the {__init__} facade imports `forward`. Class-level (not file-scoped) -> catches a re-introduction in ANY future lower-layer module.
- Meta-tests: positive (forward import detected); negative (_ir_branch import OK).
- RED before relocation (_wiring/compiler/state flagged) -> GREEN after. All 3 pass.
close_reason: Relocated _BranchNode (+_BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec) to neutral _ir_branch.py; lower layers no longer import the DX layer. Guard-first import-DAG guard added. Behavior-preserving.

title: Batch 4: Generic callback Protocols (PEP 696 defaults) — eliminate 10 Any entries from Cluster 1
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §5
- docs/design/any-audit-analysis-2026-05-20.md Cluster 1

## Cluster 1: User-callback Protocols with no type parameter

**Entries (10)**: `SkipPredicate.__call__:input_data`, `SkipValueFactory.__call__:input_data`, `SkipValueFactory.__call__:return`, `MergePreProcess.__call__:variants`, `MergePreProcess.__call__:return`, `MergePostProcess.__call__:result`, `MergePostProcess.__call__:variants`, `MergePostProcess.__call__:return`, `MergeFallback.__call__:variants`, `MergeFallback.__call__:return`.

**Hypothesis**: These Protocols were written before PEP 696 (TypeVar defaults) stabilized. Each accepts a user-shaped value whose type is declared elsewhere (`node.inputs`, `node.outputs`, `node.oracle_gen_type`). Marking them all `Any` is a shortcut.

## Structural fix

```python
T = TypeVar("T", default=Any)
U = TypeVar("U", default=Any)

@runtime_checkable
class SkipPredicate(Protocol[T]):
    def __call__(self, input_data: T) -> bool: ...

@runtime_checkable
class SkipValueFactory(Protocol[T, U]):
    def __call__(self, input_data: T) -> U: ...

@runtime_checkable
class MergePreProcess(Protocol[T]):
    def __call__(self, variants: list[T]) -> BaseModel | dict[str, Any] | str: ...

@runtime_checkable
class MergePostProcess(Protocol[T, U]):
    def __call__(self, result: T, variants: list[U]) -> T: ...

@runtime_checkable
class MergeFallback(Protocol[T, U]):
    def __call__(self, variants: list[T], error: Exception) -> U: ...
```

Locations: `src/neograph/node.py` (SkipPredicate, SkipValueFactory, RawNodeFn) and `src/neograph/modifiers.py` (Merge*). `default=Any` keeps existing call sites compiling without parameterization.

## Risk
`runtime_checkable Protocol[T]` has known mypy/runtime edge cases. Validate that `isinstance(obj, SkipPredicate)` still works for un-subscripted use.

## How to verify

**Test file**:
1. `tests/test_callback_protocols.py` (new) — for each of 5 Protocols, assert `isinstance` works un-subscripted AND that subscripting (`SkipPredicate[int]`) doesn't break isinstance
2. `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoAnyInIRPublicAPIs` — `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 10 entries

**Test type**: unit + structural-guard regression
**What it exercises**: PEP 696 default TypeVars work with `runtime_checkable`; existing modifier and node tests pass; allowlist shrinks
**Expected initial state**: write unit tests FIRST against current Protocols (will pass on isinstance but fail on subscripted use); remove 10 entries from `ANY_ALLOWLIST`; guard fails
**Persistence**: stays

Order: write tests FIRST → confirm isinstance baseline → remove 10 entries from `ANY_ALLOWLIST` → guard fails → parameterize 5 Protocols with PEP 696 defaults → re-run → both pass.

## Acceptance
- `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 10 entries
- `isinstance` continues to work for un-subscripted use across 5 Protocols
- `tests/modifiers/` (119 tests) and `tests/decorator/` (165 tests) continue to pass
- `make quality` green
close_reason: 5 callback Protocols parameterized with PEP 696 defaults (typing_extensions.TypeVar); ANY_ALLOWLIST shrunk by 9 (10 removed, 1 re-added with updated reason for MergePreProcess.return whose new signature is BaseModel | dict[str, Any] | str); 20 isinstance baseline tests added; full quality gate green

title: Implement neograph-uk10
description:
Implement beads task neograph-uk10 -- make the failing test pass (TDD green),
then refactor.

## Workflow

1. **Green**: Write minimum code to make the failing test pass
2. **Verify**: Run the SAME test that FAILED -- must now PASS
3. **Refactor**: With passing tests as safety net

title: Batch 5a: LangGraph closure-aliases — eliminate 7 Any entries from Cluster 9
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §1, §5
- docs/design/any-audit-analysis-2026-05-20.md Cluster 9

## Cluster 9: LangGraph node-fn closures typed as Any

**Entries (7)**: `_wire_oracle:gen_fn`, `_wire_oracle:merge_fn`, `_wire_each:fan_fn`, `_make_loop_router:unwrap_fn`, `_make_loop_router:return`, `_node_loop_unwrap:return`, `_add_subgraph_loop:subgraph_fn`.

**Hypothesis**: Framework-built closures with mode-specific signatures, each typed as `Any` at the binding site. The closure IS a LangGraph node fn — the type is known, just untyped at the parameter.

## Structural fix

Type-alias the LangGraph node-fn shape and use it everywhere:

```python
# src/neograph/_wiring.py
LangGraphNodeFn = Callable[[Any, RunnableConfig], dict[str, Any]]
LangGraphRouterFn = Callable[[Any], str]
LangGraphLoopUnwrapFn = Callable[[Any, str], Any]
```

Replace 7 `Any` annotations. The `Any` IN the aliases is itself §5 (user state value), and they're declared in ONE place rather than 7.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoAnyInIRPublicAPIs` — `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 7 entries
**Test type**: structural-guard regression
**What it exercises**: existing `_wiring.py` tests continue to pass (Oracle, Each, Loop, sub-construct); allowlist shrinks
**Expected initial state**: remove 7 entries from `ANY_ALLOWLIST`; guard fails on 7 sites
**Persistence**: stays

Order: remove 7 entries from `ANY_ALLOWLIST` FIRST → guard fails → introduce 3 type aliases in `_wiring.py` (or `_langgraph_types.py` if cleaner) + migrate 7 sites → re-run → passes.

## Acceptance
- `ANY_ALLOWLIST` shrinks by 7 entries
- `_wiring.py` and `_oracle.py` tests pass
- `make quality` green
close_reason: 3 type aliases introduced; 7 annotations migrated; ANY_ALLOWLIST shrunk by 7

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-3zai
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-3zai` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-3zai/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-3zai
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-3zai)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-3zai --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-3zai --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-3zai/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-3zai codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-3zai/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-3zai
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-3zai
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-3zai`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-3zai)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-3zai --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-3zai sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Intermittent neo_agent_* leak: async-resume results + cross-test-file channel pollution (two manifestations, likely one root cause)
description:
Two independent verifiers observed neo_agent_* channels escaping containment, both intermittent/order-dependent — likely one root cause in how agent-cycle state channels interact with the pjqe output_schema filtering and/or state-model caching:

MANIFESTATION 1 (runtime, observed once, not reproduced after): on a cold first arun in a fresh session, TestBudgetAcrossCheckpoint [arun] FAILED with neo_agent_budget_greedy / neo_agent_messages_greedy / neo_agent_tool_log_greedy leaked into the RESUMED arun result. Passed on 40+ subsequent runs (isolation, full file, full suite). Consistent with the residual gaps runner.py:442-447 documents for langgraph 1.2.4 output_schema filtering — but batch ainvoke SHOULD be filtered per R1, so a cold-path leak suggests the output-schema model or channel registration has an ordering/caching dependency.

MANIFESTATION 2 (test infra, reproducible): running test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py and test_hitl.py in the SAME pytest process trips the keystone no-leak guard (test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:238) with a neo_agent_* channel from the OTHER file's pipeline — cross-file pollution. Also the probable identity of the transient 2-failures observed in a full-suite run raced against concurrent pytest processes on 2026-07-04 (passed clean twice after).

TRIAGE DIRECTION: reproduce M2 first (deterministic: same-process file pair), trace WHERE the foreign channel enters (registry? compile_state_model cache? add_messages channel registration keyed globally instead of per-compile?), then evaluate whether M1 is the same mechanism surfacing at runtime under a cold import order. The per-compile registry decision (project memory: architecture decisions 2026-05) says compile-scoped registries are the norm — check whether agent-cycle channel synthesis honored that. Fix must be structural (scoping), not a test-ordering band-aid; the keystone no-leak guard and the item-c no-leak assertion both stay as-is (they caught this — they are working).
design:
## Root Cause
NOT a neograph defect on the current tree. Exhaustive investigation refutes every structural hypothesis (per-compile channel scoping is correct; output_schema filters batch invoke/ainvoke including add_messages reducer channels; no global channel state; auto-resume returns the filtered invoke). The M1/M2 sightings were transient (both verifiers saw them pass immediately after) — most consistent with a langgraph 1.2.4 cold-path quirk, not a scoping bug.

## Reproduce-atom deviation (documented, not rationalized)
The bug-triage reproduce atom's strict acceptance is 'a FAILING test'. No failing test is possible: the behavioral symptom does not reproduce and the structural hypotheses are refuted, so there is no disease to guard against either. Fabricating a red test would violate test integrity. Instead the reproduce artifact is a DETERMINISTIC PASSING guard (TestCrossCompileChannelIsolation) that pins the per-compile channel-scoping invariant so a future regression is caught deterministically.

## Fix Approach
Keep-open. The only remaining action is the maintainer's architectural call on whether to add a belt-and-suspenders _strip_internals net on the batch run()/arun() exits (M1 as cited engine-gap) — a partial reversal of pjqe Item A. Not done autonomously because the bug is unreproducible and pjqe was a deliberate recent decision by the same maintainer.

close_reason: DELIBERATE CLOSE per the y5ux Wave-4 disposition rule (fix-or-deliberate-close; keep-open limbo disallowed). Not reproducible: exhaustive structural refutation 2026-07-04 (per-compile channels, output_schema filtering re-confirmed vs R1 research, auto-resume path); independent verifier stress runs 2026-07-07: M2 file-pair 16/16 across repeated+reversed orderings, M1 2/2, isolation guard 2/2. The belt-and-suspenders _strip_internals question was ALREADY DECIDED 2026-07-04: NO — a defensive strip would destroy the detection signal. STANDING ALARM: TestCrossCompileChannelIsolation + the keystone no-leak guard + item-c no-leak assertion remain permanently; ON NEXT SIGHTING reopen at P2 and capture the full result dict + exact import/collection order immediately.

title: §4: Extract Protocol module to break factory ↔ _oracle cycle
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4 (Module and function responsibilities).

**Problem**: `_oracle.py` is imported by `factory.py`, so `_oracle.py` cannot import from `factory.py` at module scope. Today it works around this with function-local imports: `_oracle.py:24,29` does `from neograph.factory import _state_get, lookup_scripted` inside function bodies. This is the canonical deferred-import anti-pattern.

**Fix**: extract a small Protocol module (suggested: `_dispatch_types.py` or `_runtime_protocols.py`) holding the types/interfaces both modules need:
- `_state_get` (or its successor after the §7 split)
- `lookup_scripted` signature

Both `factory.py` and `_oracle.py` import from the new Protocol module. The cycle resolves; the function-local imports in `_oracle.py` go away.

**Recipe**: `_sidecar.py` is the existing template (extracted from `decorators.py` to break `decorators ↔ _construct_builder`).

**Acceptance**: zero function-local `from neograph.factory` imports in `_oracle.py`. The module graph between `factory.py` and `_oracle.py` is a DAG, not a cycle.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::test_no_function_local_factory_import_in_oracle` (new) — co-located with the existing function-local-import budget guard.
**Test type**: structural-guard, mutation-verified
**What it exercises**: AST-walk `src/neograph/_oracle.py`; assert no `ImportFrom` node with module `neograph.factory` (or `factory`) exists inside any `FunctionDef` body. Mutation case: a parametrized fixture writes a temp module containing a function-local `from neograph.factory import _state_get`, runs the AST scanner against it, asserts detection, then removes the file.
**Expected initial state**: failing — `_oracle.py:24, 29` currently has two function-local `from neograph.factory` imports.
**Persistence**: stays in suite as a permanent guard against reintroducing the cycle.

Order: write the failing AST guard FIRST → run it → must fail → extract the Protocol module + migrate imports → run again → must pass.

title: prompt_compiler silently falls through to generic fallback when template vars don't match — should warn or fail
description:
## Problem
When a node declares `prompt='uc/brainstorm-extensions'` and the template has placeholders like `{si_text}`, but the node's input parameters are named `write_si`, the prompt_compiler silently catches the KeyError from str.format() and falls through to the generic fallback prompt. The carefully crafted template with constraints, worked examples, and bad-example guidance is never used — and there's zero indication this happened.

This caused 2 production bugs in piarch where templates with critical quality constraints (step numbering, action granularity) were silently replaced by generic prompts.

## Expected behavior
When a template exists for a node's prompt name but compilation fails due to missing variables:
1. Log a WARNING with the template name, available vars, and missing vars
2. Optionally: fail hard in development/test mode (configurable)

The developer should know immediately that their template isn't being used.

## Where it happens
prompt_compiler callback registered via configure_llm(). The try/except at template compilation catches KeyError/TypeError and falls through to get_generator_prompt() without logging.

## Suggested fix
```python
try:
    prompt_text = get_prompt(template_name, **template_vars)
except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
    log.warning('prompt_template_fallback', template=template_name, error=str(exc), available_vars=sorted(template_vars.keys()))
    # fall through to generic
```

Even better: at construct compile time, validate that each node's input param names can satisfy its template's placeholders. This is a static check — parse {placeholders} from the template file and diff against the node's parameter names.
design:
## Fix Design

### Fix A: Inline prompt missing-var warning (_llm.py:209,217)
In _resolve_var, when parts[0] not in input_data, log structlog warning with var name + available keys. Still return '' (don't break compilation), but make it visible.

### Fix B: No action needed on neograph side
The prompt_compiler call at _llm.py:259 already passes through exceptions. The bug is in piarch's compiler catching KeyError — that's a piarch fix, not a neograph fix. Neograph's contract is correct: if the compiler raises, it propagates.

### Update test
Change test_inline_prompts.py:67 test_missing_key_returns_empty — verify warning is emitted (not just empty string).

Scope: ~5 lines production change + 1 test update.
notes:
## Reproduce Findings

### Two manifestations:

**A. Inline prompt (_resolve_var) — neograph-owned**
- _llm.py:209 — input_data.get(parts[0], '') silently returns empty string
- _llm.py:217 — getattr(obj, attr, '') same pattern
- Test at test_inline_prompts.py:67 explicitly validates silent behavior

**B. User prompt_compiler call — _llm.py:259**
- No try/except around _prompt_compiler() call
- Bug is that piarch's compiler catches KeyError internally and returns generic prompt
- Neograph can't detect this because compiler returns valid messages either way

### Fix approach
- Fix A: structlog warning in _resolve_var when var not in input_data
- Fix B: wrap _prompt_compiler call so exceptions propagate with context
- Recommendation: RAISE not just warn (0.x, one consumer, 2 prod failures)

### Core invariant
A prompt template must either resolve all placeholders to non-empty values, or emit a visible signal (warning/error) that resolution failed.

title: §1: Pin LangGraph version range in pyproject.toml
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §1 (LangGraph commitment).

**Problem**: `pyproject.toml` declares LangGraph without a version range pin. LangGraph 1.0 is upcoming and will change minor-version-bound APIs (`Send`, `interrupt`, `defer=True`, `path_map=`). Today's defensive code handles this with `try/except ImportError`; the architecture spec replaces that with a public-API-only commitment plus a version pin.

**Fix**: pin LangGraph to a supported public-API window in `pyproject.toml`:
- Lower bound: current minimum supported (whatever the codebase requires today)
- Upper bound: before any announced breaking change

Same treatment for `langchain-core` (the source of `RunnableConfig`).

**Acceptance**: `pyproject.toml` declares concrete bounds; CI catches drift if a future LangGraph version moves outside the supported window.

title: Portal: ForwardConstruct self.handoff(members=[...]) builder
description: v2 fast-follow. ForwardConstruct is exempt in v1 (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT): a runtime mesh has no static dataflow for the tracer. Add a self.handoff(members=[...], route=..., max_hops=...) builder copying self.interrupt (forward.py:1283). Nothing in v1 IR blocks it. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: self.handoff's emitted IR must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the declarative mesh IR (Construct(nodes=[member | Portal(...), ...]), no nesting) -- ForwardConstruct is a thin recorder, not a second IR shape.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (flatten): for each member, build 'bare_node | Portal(...)' and tracer.record() it DIRECTLY into the ForwardConstruct's own _ordered list (forward.py:413) -- do NOT wrap members in a Construct(...) and do NOT call record_construct(). This keeps the final construct's nodes list identical to examples/28_portal_swarm.py's demo_surface_parity target, with no extra subgraph boundary for Command(goto=<peer>) to cross.

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (entry-only kwargs): build Portal kwargs CONDITIONALLY per member to satisfy _check_portal_mesh's entry-only validator (_validation_portal.py:194-205): the entry member (first recorded, or an explicit entry= kwarg) gets Portal(to=to[entry], max_hops=max_hops, on_exhaust=on_exhaust); every non-entry member gets Portal(to=to[name]) with NO max_hops/on_exhaust keyword passed at all (passing even the default would put it in model_fields_set and trip the validator).

Committed concrete signature: self.handoff(members=[self.a, self.b], to={'a': [...], 'b': [...]}, max_hops=..., on_exhaust=..., entry=None) -- 'to' keyed by member name, mirroring Portal.to 1:1 (never resurrect 'peers='). Scope v1 to a terminal/whole-graph mesh (self.handoff has no proxy output/input, per D-FORWARD-EXEMPT); mid-pipeline mesh embedding is explicitly out of scope, documented in the method's docstring.
notes:
## Findings
- **Reuse target (builder shape)**: `_ModifierWrapCall` + `_InterruptCall` (`src/neograph/forward.py:978-1137`) and `_ForwardSelf.interrupt()` (`forward.py:1281-1298`) are the exact pattern to copy for `self.handoff(...)`: a thin `_ForwardSelf` method that captures the tracer and returns a small `_XxxCall` object; `_ModifierWrapCall` already handles both the bare-node-target and list-of-nodes-target forms (`_materialize`, `forward.py:1083`), building either `Node | modifier` or `Construct(nodes=[...]) | modifier` depending on target shape — this is the SAME form-awareness `self.ensemble`/`self.interrupt` already give for Oracle/Operator, so Portal gets it for free structurally.
- **The modifier to attach is the existing `Portal` class** (`src/neograph/modifiers.py:600`, renamed from Keymaker per neograph-1t0zh) — NOT a new IR capability. Mode (a) peer-routing fields: `to: list[str] | None`, `route: str = 'goto'`, `max_hops: int = 10` (entry-member-only), `on_exhaust: Literal['error','exit']`. `Portal.is_dispatch` is the sole mode discriminator (never inline `route == 'decide'`).
- **Key structural difference from self.interrupt/self.ensemble that self.handoff must account for**: Operator/Oracle wrap ONE dataflow edge (proxy in -> proxy out); Portal wires a MESH where every member independently declares its OWN `to=` peer list (see `examples/28_portal_swarm.py` demo 1: each `@node(portal=[...])` sets its own peers) and there is NO proxy chain between members (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT: 'every member is simultaneously producer and consumer of the mesh channel'). So `self.handoff(members=[...])` cannot reuse the proxy-threading half of `_ModifierWrapCall.__call__` (there's no single input proxy to consume) — it only needs the ASSEMBLY half: collect self.<x> Node refs into the tracer's `_ordered` list (via `tracer.record`, forward.py:413) each already carrying (or here-attached) its own `Portal(to=...)`, in a call that is NOT __call__'d with a proxy the way self.interrupt(...)( proxy ) is — it is closer to a batch-record than a wrap.
- **Declarative/programmatic precedent for the mesh IR shape to reproduce**: `examples/28_portal_swarm.py` demo 4 (`demo_surface_parity`, lines 238-268) — `Node.scripted(...) | Portal(to=[...], max_hops=...)` per member, then `Construct(name, nodes=[member1, member2])` with NO edges between them (Portal owns the runtime routing, not the static DAG). This is the exact IR the ForwardConstruct builder must emit.
- **Reserved-key / IR facts already shipped, nothing new needed here**: `Node.handoff_param`/`Node.handoff_channel` are written ONLY by `_ir_normalize.py` (single-writer, guard G3, `IR_FIELDS` in `test_guards_llm_runtime.py`); `Command(` construction is monopolized in `factory.py`/`runner.py` (guard G1). The ForwardConstruct builder only needs to emit `Node | Portal(...)` — the normalizer + compiler + factory already do the rest, exactly as for `@node(portal=...)` and declarative `Portal(...)`.
- **Current vs deprecated naming**: the design docs (dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md, keymaker-decision-log) still say 'Keymaker' / 'peers=' / 'self.handoff(members=[...], ...)' — these are the PRE-RENAME names. Current shipped names are `Portal`, `to=` (not `peers=`), `portal=` (the @node kwarg, not `peers=`). The task's own bead title uses 'self.handoff' as the METHOD name (kept — 'handoff' is the reserved mesh-channel input key, per D-RESERVED-KEY, and reads naturally as a verb: 'self.handoff(...)'), but its kwarg `members=` should very likely become `to=` per-member peer lists, matching `Portal`'s own field name — do not resurrect `peers=`.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:978-1137 -- _ModifierWrapCall + _EnsembleCall + _InterruptCall: the exemplar builder-call pattern (form-aware target, _materialize to Construct|Node + modifier, dedup via tracer occurrence counter)
- src/neograph/forward.py:1281-1298 -- _ForwardSelf.interrupt(): the exact method-shape to copy for self.handoff (capture tracer, return a _XxxCall)
- src/neograph/forward.py:413-425 -- _Tracer.record()/record_construct(): how nodes/sub-constructs get appended to _ordered; self.handoff's assembly-only path (no proxy in/out) should call these directly rather than going through _NodeCall.__call__
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-660 -- Portal class (to/route/max_hops/on_exhaust fields, is_dispatch discriminator, model_post_init mode validation) -- the modifier to attach unchanged
- examples/28_portal_swarm.py:238-268 (demo_surface_parity) -- canonical declarative/programmatic mesh IR: Node | Portal(to=[...]) per member, Construct(nodes=[...]) with no static edges between mesh members -- this is what the ForwardConstruct builder must reproduce
- examples/28_portal_swarm.py:94-121 -- @node(portal=[...], max_hops=...) per-member decorator sugar -- shows max_hops/on_exhaust are set on the ENTRY member only, others default
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md:133-142 -- D-FORWARD-EXEMPT judgment call, the origin decision text (pre-rename: 'peers=', 'self.handoff(members=[...], ...)')
- docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md:176-182 -- restates D-FORWARD-EXEMPT as the origin of neograph-a37vk; 'nothing in v1's IR blocks it'
- docs/design/keymaker-design-review-2026-07-13.md:134-136 -- independent-review AGREE on D-FORWARD-EXEMPT, stronger than the di_inputs analogy (genuinely no static dataflow to thread)

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **members= vs to= per-member ambiguity (design decision needed, not a doc contradiction)**: the design docs never fully specify self.handoff's signature (it was explicitly deferred as fast-follow with no API sketch). Implementer must decide how each member's peer list is supplied -- e.g. `self.handoff(members=[self.triage, self.billing], to={'triage': ['billing','technical'], 'billing': []}, max_hops=6, on_exhaust='error')`, applying `Portal(to=to[name], max_hops=max_hops if name==entry else default, on_exhaust=...)` per member. This mirrors Portal's own field names 1:1 (max_hops only meaningful on the entry member, matching the @node sugar's existing rule) rather than reinventing.
- **max_hops-only-on-entry validation already exists in Portal/its validator** (`_validation_portal.py`, `_check_portal_mesh`) -- do not re-validate in the builder; let the existing mesh-assembly validation catch a misconfigured builder call at compile time, same as declarative/@node surfaces.
- **Proxy-tracer dataflow**: self.handoff members are NOT threaded through proxies (no `(result)` call like self.interrupt(...)(result)) since D-FORWARD-EXEMPT establishes there is no static dataflow. The builder call itself (not a returned callable requiring __call__) should likely just record the members directly, unlike every other self.X() builder in this file which returns a callable expecting a proxy argument. This is a genuine shape difference from the _ModifierWrapCall family -- flag for implementer, don't force-fit the proxy-call convention.
- **Three-surface parity claim in the review ('AGREE... parity rule fully satisfied') was made BEFORE self.handoff existed** -- it argued ForwardConstruct's ABSENCE was acceptable, not that a future self.handoff would trivially reuse the interrupt/ensemble shape. Don't over-read 'parity satisfied' as implying self.handoff must look identical to self.interrupt; it only means the exemption itself doesn't break the parity rule.
## Codebase Disease Scan (a37vk)
Pattern: a self.<modifier> ForwardConstruct builder method that bypasses _Tracer.record()/record_construct() (the single recording mechanism) or collides in name with an existing self.X method.
Scan command: `grep -n "def [a-z_]*(self" src/neograph/forward.py`
Total instances found: 0 collisions -- no existing self.handoff method; all existing self.X builder methods (self.interrupt at :1281, plus ensemble/loop/each per class definitions) are the only builder-shaped methods on _ForwardSelf

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | forward.py:1281 (self.interrupt) | _ForwardSelf builder method | ALLOWLIST | exemplar to copy, not a conflict |
| — | (no self.handoff exists yet) | N/A | N/A | greenfield addition, confirmed no naming collision |

N/A overall -- this is a new-feature research scan (self.handoff doesn't exist yet), confirming a clean addition point with the correct exemplar (self.interrupt) to copy per the design field's note that this needs a genuinely different (non-proxy) call shape.
## Architect Review

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The plan contradicts itself on the load-bearing flatten-vs-nest question, and one branch VIOLATES the stated Core Invariant. Step 1 + the Findings say 'collect self.<x> Node refs into the tracer _ordered list (via tracer.record)' — i.e. flatten each member directly into the ForwardConstruct's own construct. Step 4 says 'Emit the mesh as a Construct(name=..., nodes=[member | Portal(...)]) ... record_construct(sub)' — i.e. a NESTED sub-construct. Since ForwardConstruct IS-A Construct (forward.py:135) and its final nodes come from tracer._ordered (forward.py:504-506), record_construct-ing a wrapper yields Construct(nodes=[Construct(nodes=[triage|Portal, billing|Portal])]) — one nesting level deeper than the declarative demo_surface_parity target Construct(nodes=[triage|Portal, billing|Portal]) (examples/28_portal_swarm.py:255-260). That is NOT the 'IDENTICAL IR' the Core Invariant demands, and it inserts a LangGraph subgraph boundary that Command(goto=<peer>) must now cross (only partially supported per commit 481ee34 'cross-subconstruct mesh via parent-scoped bubble-up'). Suggestion: pin the approach decisively to FLATTEN — for each member build 'bare_node | Portal(...)' (bare node from the _NodeCall._node the self.<name> lookup returns, forward.py:1158-1164) and tracer.record() it directly into _ordered; do NOT wrap in a Construct and do NOT call record_construct. Then the ForwardConstruct's own nodes list contains the members directly, byte-for-byte with declarative. The step-5 parity test is the right forcing function and would catch the nested variant — keep it, and assert node-list equality at the outer level (not one construct deep).

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Naive per-member Portal construction will trip the entry-only validator. _check_portal_mesh (_validation_portal.py:194-205) rejects ANY non-entry member whose Portal has max_hops OR on_exhaust in model_fields_set — and Portal is a Pydantic model, so passing on_exhaust='error' (even the signature default) to a non-entry member's Portal() puts it in model_fields_set and raises 'on_exhaust ... is entry-only'. Step 3's pseudocode 'Portal(to=to[name], max_hops=..., on_exhaust=...)' per member would therefore fail assembly for every declarative-equivalent 2+ member mesh. Suggestion: build kwargs conditionally — entry gets Portal(to=to[entry], max_hops=max_hops, on_exhaust=on_exhaust); every non-entry member gets Portal(to=to[name]) with NO max_hops/on_exhaust passed at all. Entry = the member recorded first (validator's entry is node_members[0], the first in construct order), so the builder must record the entry member first (honor an explicit entry= kwarg by reordering).

- [LOW] Finding: self.handoff's signature is still marked 'design decision needed' (Risks section) though the plan already proposes the right shape. Suggestion: just commit to self.handoff(members=[self.a, self.b], to={'a': [...], 'b': [...]}, max_hops=..., on_exhaust=..., entry=None) with 'to' keyed by member name (mirrors Portal.to 1:1; do NOT resurrect peers=). No further design input needed.

- [LOW] Finding: Mid-pipeline mesh embedding (threading the mesh's output into a downstream forward() node) is undefined — self.handoff records directly and returns no proxy, so there is no dataflow handle for anything after it. title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-eef83
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-eef83` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-eef83/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-eef83
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-eef83)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eef83 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eef83 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-eef83/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-eef83 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-eef83/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-eef83
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-eef83
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-eef83`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-eef83)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eef83 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-eef83 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Condition expression evaluator for Loop/Operator when clauses
description:
## What
Spec-driven pipelines express conditions as strings: when: 'score < 0.8'. Need a safe evaluator that runs these against Pydantic model field values.

## Approach
- Parse simple expressions: field_name op literal (e.g. 'score < 0.8', 'confidence >= 0.9', 'passed == false')
- Supported ops: <, >, <=, >=, ==, !=
- Field access: dotted path (e.g. 'result.score < 0.8')
- NO arbitrary code execution — whitelist of ops, no function calls, no imports
- Return a callable(value) -> bool that the Loop/Operator modifier can use

## Deliverable
- parse_condition(expr: str) -> Callable in a new module (src/neograph/conditions.py)
- Tests: valid expressions, type coercion (string '0.8' → float), bad expressions raise clear errors

Step 2: In the @node decorator (decorators.py), capture caller namespace ONCE at the top: caller_ns = sys._getframe(1).f_locals

Remove frame_depth parameter. Keep closure var extraction. infer_oracle_gen_type passes None (already frame-independent). Core invariant: annotation resolution uses an explicit namespace, never walks the call stack.

The guard runs on every pytest invocation and is the acceptance criterion — not self-reports, not grep. The task is not done until the guard passes AND remains in the test file permanently.
## Research findings
- 7 call sites for frame_depth across 2 files (_di_classify.py, decorators.py)
- _build_annotation_namespace walks sys._getframe + 8 hops to find locally-defined classes
- Needed because from __future__ import annotations turns annotations to strings

- infer_oracle_gen_type uses frame_depth=0 (already frame-independent, uses closure vars)
- _source_location in _construct_validation.py is SEPARATE, not part of this task
- Risk: 8-hop walk catches types defined several scopes up; single capture may miss some
- Mitigation: in practice needed types are always in immediate caller scope
