title: from_agent_spec: AgentNode reconstruction + Swarm-onto-Portal-mesh + RemoteAgent best-effort import
description:
01i0g's from_agent_spec() (src/neograph/loader.py) implements primitive import (LlmNode/ToolNode), per-group marker reconstruction (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator), and FlowNode recursion -- but explicitly does NOT implement:

1. AgentNode -> agent/act Node reconstruction. Currently fails loud (ConfigurationError) when an AgentNode is encountered on import, even though neograph-i3zsh.1 shipped a real AgentNode+Agent+ServerTool export with a neograph/agent_spec marker carrying every field needed (mode/prompt/model/tools/gate_tools_when/context). This atom should read that marker back and reconstruct the exact agent/act Node, with a dedicated export->import round-trip test proving losslessness.

2. Swarm-onto-Portal-mesh import. Per the 2026-07-22 user decision (docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md §3a, now superseded), a Swarm-shaped Agent Spec should import onto a native Portal mesh (v1: sibling-node peers at one construct level). This requires understanding pyagentspec's Swarm/Agent-level composite shape (distinct from the Flow/Node primitives from_agent_spec currently walks) and building Portal-modified Node(s) with handoff_param/handoff_channel wiring -- a substantial separate undertaking, not attempted in 01i0g.

3. RemoteAgent/A2AAgent best-effort lowering (ratification doc §3b): map to a name-bound scripted/raw Node + WARNING, per the ratified best-effort behavior. Not yet implemented -- from_agent_spec currently only recognizes LlmNode/ToolNode/AgentNode(fail-loud)/FlowNode.

Cite: src/neograph/loader.py's _reconstruct_primitive_node (the dispatch point for all three).
design:
## Core Invariant
Import is the EXACT inverse of export and NEVER silently downgrades: a neograph/agent_spec (or neograph/tool_spec) marker reconstructs the exact node losslessly; a marker-less/foreign primitive is either reconstructed structurally onto a REAL neograph primitive (Swarm->Portal mesh) or best-effort lowered to a name-bound Node WITH a warning -- and the reconstructed IR is always subjected to the same assembly-time validation (_check_portal_mesh etc.) a hand-written pipeline gets, so no invalid or misreconstructed mesh can compile.

## Implementation Plan
1. Gap 1 (loader.py _reconstruct_primitive_node AgentNode branch, :120-133): REPLACE the fail-loud. Read spec_node.metadata['neograph/agent_spec']; build the agent/act Node by inverting _agent_spec_marker (mode/prompt/model/tools->Tool(...)/gate_tools_when/context), reusing the existing _inputs_from_data_edges + _agent_spec_props_to_type for inputs/outputs. INVERT the fail-loud pin at tests/test_agent_spec_import.py:183 into a losslessness assertion; add the round-trip + tool_spec/agent_spec metadata-survival test to tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py.
2. Gap 3 (same AgentNode branch): when spec_node.agent has NO neograph/agent_spec marker, dispatch on type(spec_node.agent).__name__ -- 'Agent' -> best-effort agent-mode reconstruction (mode='agent', from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config/tools); 'RemoteAgent'/'A2AAgent'/'OciAgent' -> name-bound scripted Node (scripted_fn=agent name) + warnings.warn (reuse the loader.py:173 warnings.warn pattern), stash endpoint shape in metadata['neograph/remote_agent']. ServerTool-as-agent stays fail-loud (orchestrator-side line, ratification §3b).
3. Gap 2 (from_agent_spec entry, loader.py:353): add a top-level `if type(component).__name__ == 'Swarm'` branch -> new _reconstruct_swarm_mesh(swarm) helper (sibling of the existing _reconstruct_* cluster). It: (a) SYNTHESIZES a uniform payload model via create_model with a 'goto: str' route field; (b) for each Swarm agent builds an agent-mode member Node (reusing gap-1 reconstruction) with inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload, then | Portal(to=[b for (a,b) in swarm.relationships if a is agent]); (c) orders members with swarm.first_agent FIRST and sets max_hops/on_exhaust only on the entry Portal; (d) returns Construct(name=swarm.name, nodes=members). Do NOT set handoff_param/handoff_channel -- normalize_ir/_HandoffParamNormalizer are the sole writers and fire automatically in Construct.__init__. Let _check_portal_mesh validate the result (disconnected/non-contiguous Swarm -> clear ConfigurationError). v1 scope: one connected mesh at one construct level (cross-construct handoff deferred to neograph-do0d9). Add a Swarm->mesh reconstruction test (compile with FakeLLM) to tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py.
4. Update from_agent_spec docstring (loader.py:370-372) which currently says AgentNode + Swarm import are 'explicitly NOT implemented / fail loud' -- now they are. Keep ServerTool/BuiltinTool-as-agent fail-loud.
5. Gate: full `uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_agent_spec_*.py` green, plus the general suite; each gap has its own regression test (AgentNode round-trip losslessness incl. tool budget/config/idempotent, Swarm->Portal mesh reconstruction, RemoteAgent best-effort+warning).

## Scope addendum (disease scan, 2026-07-23) — Step 0: centralize marker keys FIRST
Before any reconstruction branch, land the marker-key centralization the disease scan flagged (23 inline "neograph/*" literals across _agent_spec.py + loader.py, no shared constant — the export↔import contract can drift by a typo and silently downgrade). Introduce a module-level named-constant block in _agent_spec.py (_MARK_MODE='neograph/mode', _MARK_AGENT_SPEC='neograph/agent_spec', _MARK_TOOL_SPEC='neograph/tool_spec', _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT='neograph/remote_agent', plus the existing oracle/each/loop/operator/modifier/group_id/variant/branch keys), import them into loader.py, and swap ALL existing literals + aa5gq's new reads/writes to reference them. Guarded by tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py + test_agent_spec_import.py (any typo now fails a test instead of silently downgrading). Steps 1-5 below then reference the constants, never fresh inline literals. Full disposition table is in this bead's notes.

## Refinement addendum (architect review, neograph-hhgnz.29, 2026-07-23)
- SHARED HELPER (supersedes 'reuse gap-1' phrasing in steps 1-3): factor _node_from_spec_agent(spec_agent) that dispatches on marker presence — metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] present -> lossless gap-1 inversion; absent (foreign Swarm agents carry NO marker) -> best-effort gap-3 (mode='agent' from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config/tools). BOTH the AgentNode branch (step 1/2) and the Swarm member builder (step 3) call this helper. A raw metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] read in the Swarm path would KeyError on foreign agents.
- STEP 0 STRUCTURAL GUARD (a shared symbol does NOT catch a VALUE typo — both sides move together): add a guard-first STRUCTURAL test (tests/test_guards_*) banning re-inlined '"neograph/' string literals outside the single constant block, PLUS value-pinning asserts (_MARK_AGENT_SPEC == 'neograph/agent_spec', ...) since the constants ARE the wire format foreign tools/stored YAMLs literally expect. Behavioral round-trip coverage alone is insufficient.
- SWARM DOWNGRADE WARNING (Core Invariant no-silent-downgrade): Swarm import is a best-effort/warning arm, NOT the clean structural arm. Emit warnings.warn documenting (a) route-only payload synthesis and (b) name-bound live-LLM members; AND fold the Swarm's declared Properties (+ agent output schemas where available) into the create_model payload as data fields, so a data-carrying Swarm does not silently lose its data channel.
- SINGLE SHARED PAYLOAD INSTANCE: _check_portal_mesh checks uniform-payload + reserved-handoff-key by IDENTITY ('is', :135/:243). Synthesize EXACTLY ONE payload model object and reuse the SAME instance as every member's outputs AND inputs['handoff']; a create_model-per-member fails assembly.
- HOP KNOBS: do NOT set max_hops/on_exhaust on the synthesized entry Portal (Swarm carries no budget); Portal defaults (10/'error') apply and the entry-only check keys on model_fields_set, so omitting the knobs passes trivially and is the correct minimal move.
acceptance_criteria: All three gaps closed, each with its own regression test proving the specific behavior (AgentNode round-trip losslessness, Swarm->Portal mesh reconstruction, RemoteAgent best-effort+warning). Full quality gate green.

Also covers l7gvy's deferred import+round-trip slice: once AgentNode import reconstruction lands, add a test proving a Tool's budget/config/idempotent survive via the neograph/tool_spec marker each ServerTool carries (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py::_tool_to_server_tool, shipped by l7gvy 2026-07-22).
## Findings (research neograph-hhgnz.2)

### Core reuse targets (do NOT reinvent)
- The importer already exists and is well-factored: `from_agent_spec()` in src/neograph/loader.py:353 with a per-modifier reconstruction cluster (_reconstruct_oracle_group / _reconstruct_each_node / _reconstruct_loop_item / _reconstruct_operator_item) each declared 'the inverse of _agent_spec._lower_X'. All three gaps EXTEND this existing pattern -- they add branches, not new subsystems.
- The dispatch point for gaps 1 & 3 is _reconstruct_primitive_node (loader.py:111): its `elif cls_name == 'AgentNode'` branch (loader.py:120-133) currently FAILS LOUD. Gap 1 (real Agent) and gap 3 (RemoteAgent/A2AAgent) both dispatch HERE by inspecting spec_node.agent's runtime type. Gap 2 (Swarm) dispatches at the TOP-LEVEL from_agent_spec entry (a Swarm is an AgenticComponent, NOT a Flow, so it never reaches _reconstruct_primitive_node).

### Gap 1 -- AgentNode -> agent/act Node (LOSSLESS, marker-driven)
- The export side (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:168-183 _lower_node, :249-271 _agent_spec_marker) stamps AgentNode.metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] = {mode, prompt, model, tools:[{name,budget,config,idempotent}], gate_tools_when(str-only), context}. Import is the EXACT inverse: read that blob, build Node(name, mode=marker['mode'], prompt=marker['prompt'], model=marker['model'], tools=[Tool(t['name'],budget=t['budget'],config=t['config'],idempotent=t['idempotent']) for t in marker['tools']], gate_tools_when=marker['gate_tools_when'], context=marker['context'], inputs=..., outputs=...). inputs/outputs reconstruct via the SAME existing helpers _inputs_from_data_edges + _agent_spec_props_to_type already used at loader.py:141-150.
- Tool ctor: Tool(name_, /, budget=0, config={}, idempotent=False) frozen BaseModel (src/neograph/tool.py:38-73) -- reads back directly from the marker dict.
- The redundant tool_spec survival test (l7gvy deferred slice): each ServerTool attached to the Agent ALSO carries metadata['neograph/tool_spec']={name,budget,config,idempotent} (_agent_spec.py:212-246 _tool_to_server_tool). The agent_spec marker's flat tools list is the PRIMARY reconstruction source (single blob, by design per _agent_spec_marker docstring); the tool_spec marker is an independent carrier on the ServerTool. Add a standalone assertion that spec_node.agent.tools[i].metadata['neograph/tool_spec'] survives to_dict->from_dict (the §6.1 metadata-survival concern, ratification doc:131-133).
- Must FLIP the existing fail-loud pin: tests/test_agent_spec_import.py:183 TestFromAgentSpecFailsLoudOnAgentNode currently asserts ConfigurationError on AgentNode import -- that test INVERTS to a round-trip losslessness test.

### Gap 2 -- Swarm -> Portal mesh (structural reconstruction, NOT marker-driven)
- pyagentspec Swarm shape (v26.1.2): Swarm(first_agent: AgenticComponent, relationships: List[Tuple[AgenticComponent,AgenticComponent]] (directed from->to handoff pairs), handoff: bool|HandoffMode, inputs, outputs). Swarm subclasses AgenticComponent -- it is a TOP-LEVEL document, never a Flow node.
- Target IR = a Portal PEER-mode mesh (src/neograph/modifiers.py:600 Portal). Each Swarm agent -> a Node | Portal(to=[peer names from relationships], ...); first_agent -> entry member (must be FIRST in construct.nodes order, gets max_hops/on_exhaust which are entry-only). Exemplar to copy: examples/28_portal_swarm.py (declarative surface: Node.scripted(name, inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload) | Portal(to=[peers], max_hops=6)).
- Reuse the mesh wiring machinery -- do NOT set handoff_param/handoff_channel yourself. _ir_normalize.py::_HandoffParamNormalizer (SOLE writer of handoff_param, fires when portal set + dict-form inputs has reserved 'handoff' key) and normalize_ir (SOLE writer of handoff_channel, entry-keyed, :271-273/:291-292) auto-wire the mesh in Construct.__init__. The importer ONLY needs to produce each member as Node(inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload) | Portal(to=[...]). Validation is enforced by _validation_portal.py::_check_portal_mesh (contiguity, uniform single payload type, peer existence, single connected component, entry-only knobs, route field on payload).
- CRITICAL synthesis requirement (from _check_portal_mesh:207-237): the shared payload model MUST carry a route field (Portal.route default 'goto') annotated str or Literal[member-names]. A foreign Swarm has no such neograph payload model, so the importer must SYNTHESIZE one via pydantic create_model (spec_types uses create_model at :173/:221) -- e.g. a model with a 'goto: str' field -- and use it uniformly as every member's inputs['handoff'] type AND outputs type.
- Each Swarm agent is itself an Agent composite -> reuse gap-1's agent-mode reconstruction to build each member's underlying Node before piping | Portal.

### Gap 3 -- RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent -> name-bound scripted Node + WARNING (best-effort)
- These arrive as an AgentNode whose .agent is a RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent (all AgenticComponent subclasses; AgentNode.agent is typed AgenticComponent). So the SAME _reconstruct_primitive_node AgentNode branch inspects type(spec_node.agent).__name__: 'Agent' -> gap 1; 'RemoteAgent'/'A2AAgent'/'OciAgent' -> gap 3.
- Best-effort lowering (ratification §3b, doc:95-101): map to a name-bound scripted Node (scripted_fn = agent name; factory supplied at bind time, same contract as any ToolNode import at loader.py:119) + warnings.warn (reuse the existing warnings.warn pattern already in loader.py:173 _reconstruct_oracle_group). Stash endpoint/connection shape in metadata['neograph/remote_agent'] for re-export (A2AAgent carries agent_url/connection_config/session_parameters).
- The principled line (doc:101): client-initiated (RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent) -> lowerable; orchestrator-side (ServerTool/BuiltinTool) -> FAIL. ServerTool-as-agent stays fail-loud.
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/loader.py:111 _reconstruct_primitive_node -- THE dispatch point for gaps 1 & 3; the AgentNode branch (:120-133) is the fail-loud to replace.
- src/neograph/loader.py:353 from_agent_spec -- TOP-LEVEL entry; add a `type(component).__name__ == 'Swarm'` branch here for gap 2 (Swarm is not a Flow). Param is already typed Any.
- src/neograph/loader.py:141-150 -- inputs/outputs reconstruction helpers (_agent_spec_props_to_type + _inputs_from_data_edges) to reuse verbatim for the agent Node.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Portal payload route field: _check_portal_mesh REQUIRES a route field (default 'goto') on the payload model annotated str or Literal. A foreign Swarm carries no such model -> the importer MUST synthesize one (create_model, 'goto: str'). If omitted, import produces an invalid mesh that fails assembly validation. This is the substantial part of gap 2, not the marker read.
- Swarm relationships are DIRECTED tuples (from,to); Portal.to= is per-node directed successors. Map each agent A's to= to [b for (a,b) in relationships if a is A]. entry = first_agent (must be nodes[0]).
- Single-mesh + contiguity: _check_portal_mesh rejects two disjoint meshes and non-contiguous members. A Swarm with a disconnected relationship graph will fail assembly -- surface this as a clear ConfigurationError at import (v1 scope: one connected mesh, one construct level; cross-construct handoff is deferred to neograph-do0d9).
- Swarm members are Agent composites -> each reconstructed member is an agent-mode Node needing a live LLM factory at compile; the mesh is structurally lossless but members are name-bound (runtime binding required), same best-effort contract as RemoteAgent. Document this in the test (compile with a FakeLLM).
- Marker-less foreign Agent (AgentNode with a plain Agent but NO neograph/agent_spec marker): cannot distinguish agent vs act -> default mode='agent' (read-only, conservative); reconstruct prompt/model/tools from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config.model_id/tools (each ServerTool.metadata['neograph/tool_spec'] or name-only). Keep this path best-effort + note it; the marker path is the lossless one.
- Oracle scripted-mode round-trip bug is OUT OF SCOPE here (already noted at test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:153-162) -- do not conflate.
- metadata survival (ratification §6.1, doc:131-133): assert neograph/agent_spec AND neograph/tool_spec survive a full to_dict->from_dict before trusting the marker tier -- this is the one carried caveat that gates lossless reconstruction.

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it

   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and

     ```

     ```

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```

   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>

   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   ```

   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

title: [SPIKE] Portal+Operator: human-approval gate on a dynamic handoff (D4 v2, wrapper/approval-node interrupt)
description: v1 makes Keymaker+Operator ILLEGAL (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO/D4): the Operator postlude (_add_operator_check, _wiring.py:939-961) is bypassed by a Command(goto)-returning member. v2 path: raise interrupt() INSIDE the keymaker wrapper before returning the Command — a wrapper-level gate, not a postlude node. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
SPIKE GOAL: prove that Portal+Operator (human approval on a handoff) is buildable WITHOUT re-invoking the member's LLM on resume, and land the design. Closing this de-risks the 7t7tf ratification of Command(goto) by proving the D4 cost is temporary, not permanent.

CORE INVARIANT: the approval pause must sit ON the dynamic (Command(goto)) path, never on a statically-appended edge — because a Command(goto)-returning member routes straight to its target and never traverses an appended static edge (that is the D4 bug itself).

ROOT CAUSE (why v1 cut the combo): Operator wires via _add_operator_check (_wiring.py:1082) which does graph.add_edge(node_name, check_name) — a STATIC edge from the guarded node to a `{node}__operator` interrupt node. A Portal member returns Command(goto=peer), LangGraph follows the goto, and the static node->check edge is never traversed. The approval node is wired, looks correct, and silently never fires.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE (approval-node-on-the-dynamic-path, NOT naive in-wrapper):
- NAIVE (reject): call interrupt() inside make_portal_fn right before returning the Command. Simple but WRONG: LangGraph re-runs the interrupted node from the top on resume, so the member's LLM/tool calls re-fire (double model spend, possibly different answer).
- CLEAN (target): the Operator-guarded member computes its handoff and routes THROUGH a tiny dedicated approval node —
    member returns Command(goto="<member>__approve", update={proposed_target: target, ...})
    the approval node is the ONLY place interrupt() lives; on approval it returns Command(goto=approved_target); on rejection it routes elsewhere / stays.
  Resume then re-runs ONLY the cheap approval node, not the LLM member. The approval sits on the live routed path (member -> approve -> target), so the goto cannot skip it.

WHY Command(goto) HELPS HERE: the same "route through a node I name at runtime" power that makes mode (b) possible is exactly what lets us splice the approval node into the live path. This is an argument FOR the 7t7tf Command(goto) decision, not against it.

ACCEPTANCE (spike deliverables):
1. A runnable proof: an Operator-guarded Portal member pauses at the proposed handoff, surfaces the proposed target as the interrupt payload, resumes via Command(resume=<decision>), and routes to the approved target — with a checkpointer + thread_id.
2. PROVE the LLM/tool work does NOT re-execute on resume (assert the member's model/tool fake is called exactly once across pause+resume). This is the crux the naive shape fails.
3. Decide + document: does this stay illegal-at-assembly with a nicer error, or become a first-class `Portal + Operator` composition? If first-class, what does the surface look like (@node(portal=[...]) + Operator; or an explicit approve= kwarg on Portal)?
4. If landed: lift the D4 assembly ban for this specific composition; keep the ban for any shape that can't satisfy invariant #1.
notes:
## LangGraph HITL mechanics (grounding for the spike)
- Primitive: langgraph.types.interrupt(payload). Calling it inside a node RAISES GraphInterrupt, which bubbles up and PAUSES the graph; state is checkpointed (REQUIRES a checkpointer + thread_id). The payload is surfaced to the caller as the interrupt value (what the human sees).
- Resume: graph.invoke(Command(resume=<value>), config). LangGraph RE-ENTERS the interrupted node and re-runs it FROM THE TOP; this time interrupt() RETURNS <value> instead of raising, so the node continues past it.
- THE RE-RUN TRAP: everything before interrupt() in that node executes again on resume. For an LLM/agent member this means the model + tool calls re-fire unless the interrupt is isolated in a node that does no expensive work. Same class as the durable-execution replay problem (see docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md).
- neograph already wraps this: hitl.py::ask_human (:56) is a pure passthrough over interrupt(payload.model_dump()); Operator's operator_check (_wiring.py:1094-1099) calls interrupt(should_pause) and returns {HUMAN_FEEDBACK: human_input}. The agent/act ReAct cycle already interrupts at a TURN BOUNDARY with turn-boundary idempotency (_wiring.py:1003,1040) — that idempotency pattern is prior art for keeping pre-interrupt work exactly-once and may be the reusable mechanism for the approval node.

## Linkage
- Informs (does NOT hard-block) 7t7tf: the Command(goto) ratification is cleaner to accept once this spike proves the D4 combo-cut is temporary. Cross-referenced there.
- Prior art to reuse: agent/act turn-boundary idempotency (_wiring.py:1003+), hitl.py passthrough, _add_operator_check structure.
- Code refs: _wiring.py:1082 _add_operator_check (the static-edge bug), _wiring.py:732 _wire_portal_mesh / factory.py make_portal_fn (where the approval-node routing would splice in), hitl.py ask_human, _wiring.py:1094 operator_check.
- Design docs: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md, docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md (D4), renamed-construct note on 07inf.
## Prep (wyymi.2, 2026-07-14)
Code read: factory.py:103 make_portal_fn (_to_command emits Command(goto) after inner runs — the splice point), _wiring.py:723 _add_portal_mesh (members registered with destinations=; approval node would be added here per guarded member), _wiring.py:1082 _add_operator_check (the static-edge D4 bug), modifiers.py _SLOT_RULES + ModifierSet._validate (reciprocal Portal x Operator ban, fixture portal_operator_combo.py), hitl.py ask_human, _wiring.py:1035+ tool-gate prior art (gate node = only interrupt site, approve/deny routing — the EXACT shape the design recommends), tests/test_checkpoint_portal.py (SqliteSaver + interrupt/resume conventions).

## Plan (spike scope = acceptance 1-3; 4 is conditional on landing the feature)
- Files to ADD: tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py (runnable proof), docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md (decision doc).
- Approach: build the CLEAN shape as a LangGraph-level proof mirroring make_portal_fn mechanics — a counted member returns Command(goto='member__approve', update={proposed target}); a dedicated approval node is the ONLY interrupt() site and on resume returns Command(goto=approved_target). File-backed SqliteSaver + thread_id; assert (a) pause surfaces proposed target as interrupt payload, (b) Command(resume=decision) routes to approved target, (c) member callable ran EXACTLY ONCE across pause+resume (the crux the naive in-wrapper shape fails — also prove the naive shape re-runs, as contrast). Sync + async.
- Decision to document (#3): recommend FIRST-CLASS Portal+Operator in v2 — Operator on a mesh member means 'splice {member}__approve onto the dynamic path' (wiring change in _add_portal_mesh + a make_portal_approval_fn in factory.py, G1-compliant); ban stays until implemented. Implementation = separate feature bead under 07inf.
- Core Invariant (from bead): approval pause sits ON the Command(goto) path, never a statically-appended edge.
## Execution (wyymi.3, 2026-07-14)
- Deliverable 1+2 (runnable proof + exactly-once crux): tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py — 4 tests, all passing against real file-backed SqliteSaver/AsyncSqliteSaver. Clean shape: pause surfaces {proposed_target} as interrupt payload; Command(resume='approve') routes to approved target, 'reject' routes to mesh exit; member body executed EXACTLY ONCE across pause+resume (sync + async). Contrast test PROVES the naive in-wrapper interrupt re-runs the member (called 2x) — the D4 rejection is now empirical, not theoretical.
- Deliverable 3 (decision): docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md — first-class Portal+Operator in v2, surface = reuse Operator as-is (member | Portal(to=[...]) | Operator(when=...)), no approve= kwarg. Ban STAYS until implemented.
- Deliverable 4 (conditional): not landed here by design — implementation filed as neograph-kdr1u (discovered-from this spike) with the 6-step sketch + anti-band-aid clause. 7t7tf cross-referenced with the spike outcome.
- Quality check: PASS (3276 passed, ruff + mypy clean)

title: Sweep verification for neograph-vn5f
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored AND a
structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-vn5f
- fix atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** using the EXACT same command from the
   codebase-scan atom.

2. **Compute the diff** — every Phase 1b row must have a verified
   post-fix disposition (MIGRATE done / ALLOWLIST holds / DEFER
   ticket open):

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-vn5f)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   ```

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT and record the new location. The deterministic check is the
   instance-count diff (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists** banning future instances
   of the disease pattern. Required when the disposition table has
   >=1 MIGRATE row; N/A (record why) when every row is ALLOWLIST/DEFER
   since no code changed — an all-ALLOWLIST fix is suspicious. The
   guard MUST:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py`
     - Include positive AND negative meta-tests
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (Non-regex guards have no regex-slip case; pos+neg suffice.)

   Record:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-vn5f --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File / Class / Meta-tests: ..."
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

```bash
bd label add neograph-vn5f sweep:complete
```
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Oracle merge_prompt: add pre_process and post_process hooks
description:
## What
Add optional `pre_process` and `post_process` callbacks to the Oracle `merge_prompt` path so consumers don't need `@merge_fn` + manual LLM calls for merges that have bracketing logic.

## Why
piarch has 8 call sites where `@merge_fn` functions manually call the LLM (via `piarch_llm_call`) because `merge_prompt` provides no hooks for pre/post-processing. The current options are:
1. `merge_prompt` — LLM merge, but NO pre/post hooks. Raw variants go in, raw LLM output comes out.
2. `merge_fn` — full control, but consumer must call the LLM manually, losing retry/rendering/schema enforcement.

This gap forces consumers to either bypass NeoGraph's LLM dispatch (losing safety features) or use `Node.run_isolated()` inside `@merge_fn` (works but is architectural debt).

## Common pre/post patterns across piarch's 8 call sites

### Pre-processing (before LLM call)
- **Tag variants with generator IDs**: `gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}"` to track which generator produced each item
- **Flatten nested structures**: extract claims from DecompositionResult into ClaimRef list
- **Inject graph context**: query graph for node bodies, search results, etc.
- **Format for prompt**: serialize to JSON with specific field selection

### Post-processing (after LLM call)
- **Self-healing invariants**: ensure every input item appears in the output (fill gaps with singletons)
- **Remap IDs**: renumber claim IDs, fix target references
- **Validate against graph**: check that referenced node IDs exist
- **Fallback on failure**: if LLM output is unusable, fall back to deterministic merge

## Proposed API

```python
Oracle(
    merge_prompt="rw/group-claims",
    merge_model="reason",
    # NEW: optional hooks
    merge_pre_process=tag_with_gen_ids,      # fn(variants: list[T]) -> dict  (input_data for prompt)
    merge_post_process=self_heal_groups,     # fn(result: T, variants: list[T]) -> T
    merge_fallback=singleton_groups,         # fn(variants: list[T], error: Exception) -> T
)
```

### Pre-process signature
```python
def tag_with_gen_ids(variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> dict:
    """Transform raw variants into input_data dict for the merge prompt."""
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(...), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants) for c in v.claims
    ]
    return {"claims": all_refs}  # these become template variables
```

### Post-process signature
```python
def self_heal_groups(result: ClaimGroupingResult, variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    """Ensure every input claim appears in at least one output group."""
    # ... self-healing logic
    return result
```

### Fallback signature
```python
def singleton_groups(variants: list[DecompositionResult], error: Exception) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    """On LLM failure, treat each claim as its own group."""
    return ClaimGroupingResult(groups=[ClaimGroup(members=[ref]) for ref in all_refs])
```

## Implementation sketch
In `_oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn`, the `merge_prompt` path (lines 197-222) would become:

```python
if oracle.merge_prompt:
    def merge_fn(state, config):
        results = getattr(state, collector_field, [])
        primary, secondaries = _unwrap_oracle_results(results, field_name, output_model)
        
        # Pre-process hook (or default: {"variants": primary})
        if oracle.merge_pre_process:
            input_data = oracle.merge_pre_process(primary)
        else:
            input_data = {"variants": primary}
        
        try:
            merged = invoke_structured(
                model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
                prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
                input_data=input_data,
                output_model=...,
                config=config,
            )
            # Post-process hook
            if oracle.merge_post_process:
                merged = oracle.merge_post_process(merged, primary)
        except Exception as exc:
            if oracle.merge_fallback:
                merged = oracle.merge_fallback(primary, exc)
            else:
                raise
        
        return _build_oracle_merge_result(merged, field_name, output_model, secondaries)
```

## Acceptance
- Oracle accepts `merge_pre_process`, `merge_post_process`, `merge_fallback` optional callables
- Pre-process transforms variants into input_data dict for the prompt
- Post-process runs on the parsed LLM result before it's written to state
- Fallback catches LLM/parse errors and returns a deterministic result
- All three hooks are optional — merge_prompt without hooks works exactly as before
- piarch's 8 @merge_fn call sites can be converted to merge_prompt + hooks
design:
## Core Invariant
The merge_prompt path must remain a single, self-contained LLM dispatch that reads variants from state and writes the merged result — hooks bracket this dispatch without altering its contract.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add fields to Oracle (modifiers.py)
Add three optional Callable fields to Oracle:
- `merge_pre_process: Callable | None = None` — fn(variants: list[T]) -> dict (returns input_data for prompt)
- `merge_post_process: Callable | None = None` — fn(result: T, variants: list[T]) -> T (transforms parsed result)
- `merge_fallback: Callable | None = None` — fn(variants: list[T], error: Exception) -> T (fallback on LLM failure)

Add `model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` to Oracle since Callable is not JSON-serializable.

### 2. Validate hook constraints (modifiers.py)
In `model_post_init`:
- If any hook is set AND merge_fn is set, raise ConfigurationError (hooks are merge_prompt-only)
- Hooks with merge_prompt are allowed (the point of this feature)
- All three hooks independently optional

### 3. Wire hooks into make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py)
In the merge_prompt closure (lines 197-222):
1. After `_unwrap_oracle_results`, if `merge_pre_process`: `input_data = merge_pre_process(primary)` (replaces default `{"variants": primary}` + upstream context)
2. Wrap `invoke_structured` in try/except if `merge_fallback` is set
3. After successful `invoke_structured`, if `merge_post_process`: `merged = merge_post_process(merged, primary)`
4. In except: if `merge_fallback`: `merged = merge_fallback(primary, exc)`, else re-raise

### 4. Wire hooks into _merge_one_group (_wiring.py)
Same pattern for EachxOracle fused path (lines 289-322):
- pre_process transforms group variants before invoke_structured
- post_process transforms result after invoke_structured
- fallback catches errors

### 5. Pre-process interaction with upstream context
When pre_process is set, it REPLACES the default input_data construction entirely. The pre_process function receives raw variants and returns the complete input_data dict for the prompt. This means:
- Without pre_process: `{"variants": primary, upstream_key: val, ...}` (current behavior)
- With pre_process: `pre_process(primary)` (full control over what the prompt sees)
- The upstream context feature is NOT lost — pre_process can pull upstream values from variants if needed, or the user can pass upstream context through their own means

```python
def tag_with_gen_ids(variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> dict:
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(include=set(ClaimRef.model_fields)), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants)
        if isinstance(v, DecompositionResult)
        for c in v.claims
    ]
    return {"claims": all_refs}  # becomes template vars: ${claims}

# Post-process: self-healing invariant
def ensure_all_claims_grouped(result: ClaimGroupingResult, variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(include=set(ClaimRef.model_fields)), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants)
        if isinstance(v, DecompositionResult)

    grouped = {(m.gen_id, m.claim_id) for g in result.groups for m in g.members}
    groups = list(result.groups)
    for ref in all_refs:
        if (ref.gen_id, ref.claim_id) not in grouped:
            groups.append(ClaimGroup(members=[ref]))

# Fallback: on LLM failure, each claim is its own group
```

## Research Findings

### Current Code Paths

**Primary merge_prompt path** (`_oracle.py:197-222`):
- `make_oracle_merge_fn` creates a closure that:
  1. Reads collector results from state
  2. Calls `_unwrap_oracle_results` to separate primary/secondary
  3. Builds `input_data = {"variants": primary}` + upstream context from `node_inputs`
  4. Calls `invoke_structured(merge_model, merge_prompt, input_data, output_model, config)`
  5. Wraps result via `_build_oracle_merge_result`

**EachxOracle fused path** (`_wiring.py:289-322`):
- `_merge_one_group` handles per-group merge
- For merge_prompt: passes `variants[0]` directly as input_data (no dict wrapping)
- No upstream context available (outer state not threaded)
- Hooks need to apply here too but with group-level semantics

### Files to Modify
1. `src/neograph/modifiers.py:309-367` -- Add merge_pre_process, merge_post_process, merge_fallback fields to Oracle
2. `src/neograph/_oracle.py:176-246` -- Wire hooks into make_oracle_merge_fn closure
3. `src/neograph/_wiring.py:289-322` -- Wire hooks into _merge_one_group (EachxOracle)

### Relevant Code
- `modifiers.py:309` -- Oracle class definition (frozen Pydantic model)
- `_oracle.py:176` -- make_oracle_merge_fn (main merge factory)
- `_oracle.py:89-129` -- _unwrap_oracle_results (separates primary/secondary)
- `_oracle.py:132-173` -- _build_oracle_merge_result (builds state update dict)
- `_wiring.py:289-322` -- _merge_one_group (EachxOracle fused path)
- `compiler.py:430-446` -- _add_oracle_nodes (wiring entry point)

### Similar Implementations to Follow
- Oracle `node_inputs` upstream context (recently added) -- same "optional callable on Oracle" pattern
- `@merge_fn` DI resolution -- how merge_fn already accepts extra callables

### Risks & Edge Cases
1. **Oracle is frozen=True** -- Callable fields need `arbitrary_types_allowed` or PrivateAttr treatment. Since Oracle is a Pydantic frozen model, adding `Callable` fields requires careful handling. Best approach: regular fields with `ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` since Oracle already has complex types.
2. **EachxOracle fused path** -- hooks must apply in _merge_one_group too, but pre_process receives group variants (list), not full collector
3. **merge_fn path** -- hooks should NOT apply when merge_fn is used (merge_fn already gives full control)
4. **Validation** -- pre_process/post_process/fallback should only be allowed with merge_prompt, not merge_fn (merge_fn path already has full control)
5. **Type of pre_process return** -- must be dict (input_data for prompt). If pre_process returns non-dict, confusing error from invoke_structured
6. **post_process sees typed result** -- result is already parsed BaseModel when post_process runs (after invoke_structured)
7. **fallback catches Exception** -- should catch all exceptions from invoke_structured, including parse errors, LLM errors, etc.
## Architect Review

- [LOW] ConfigDict on Oracle: Adding `model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` to Oracle is clean. Oracle already has complex validation in model_post_init. No upstream breakage risk.

- [LOW] Hook field naming: `merge_pre_process`, `merge_post_process`, `merge_fallback` follow the `merge_` prefix convention established by `merge_prompt`, `merge_model`, `merge_fn`. Consistent.

- [MEDIUM] Pre-process replacing upstream context: When pre_process is set, it replaces the entire input_data construction including upstream context injection. This is the right call — pre_process gives full control. But the docstring and error messages should be clear about this: "pre_process replaces the default variants + upstream context behavior."

- [LOW] EachxOracle fused path: The _merge_one_group function already has a simpler merge_prompt path (no upstream context). Hooks apply there identically — pre_process(group_variants), post_process(result, group_variants), fallback(group_variants, error). No special handling needed.

- [LOW] merge_fn validation: Hooks should raise ConfigurationError when combined with merge_fn. This is a clean guard — merge_fn already gives full control, hooks would be confusing.

- [LOW] Layer discipline compliance: Oracle is IR-layer (modifiers.py). Adding configuration fields (callables that drive runtime behavior) is the same pattern as merge_fn/merge_prompt. Not a layer violation — these are IR-level configuration, not @node-layer features.

- [LOW] Frozen model + Callable: Pydantic v2 frozen models with arbitrary_types_allowed work fine. The Callable is stored at construction time and never mutated. Frozen semantics are preserved.

Overall: ALL_LOW

Clean review (ALL_LOW) -- proceeding to implement.

title: Audit + normalize ALL IR fields with @node-path-only assignment (class fix, not instance)
description:
## Architectural property (the invariant)

The CLAUDE.md claim — 'all three API surfaces (declarative, @node, programmatic/YAML) produce the same internal IR' — must hold for EVERY field on Node and Construct. Any IR field whose value depends on which API surface built the node violates this invariant and is a latent surface-divergence bug of the same class as fan_out_param (vgc1).

vgc1 fixed ONE instance (fan_out_param). aqau closes the class.

## Anti-band-aid clause

IF YOUR FIX TARGETS A SINGLE FIELD (e.g., 'add oracle_gen_type normalization'), STOP. The task is to AUDIT every IR field set during @node assembly, classify each, and produce a complete fix that handles the class — not a second one-field special case sitting next to _normalize_fan_out_params.

If the diff adds another '_normalize_<field>' method per field, that is a band-aid pattern. The right shape is either:
(a) a single normalization pass that infers every applicable field, OR
(b) move each field's inference into Node.__init__ / Modifiable.__or__ so the field is set at the moment the modifier is applied (regardless of construct assembly path)

Decide which shape is correct and document the choice in the design field BEFORE writing code.

## Required audit (mandatory, BEFORE implementation)

Grep _construct_builder.py for every `updates[<field>] = ...` write in _cleanup_inputs_and_register and related @node-assembly helpers. For each discovered field, produce a classification table:

| Field | Set by @node | Set by Node() ctor | Set by Modifiable.__or__ | Set by YAML loader | Divergence? |

Paste the table into the bead's notes field. Every row marked 'Divergence: yes' is a sibling bug to vgc1.

Known starting points (per reviewer aa14ccfd):
- fan_out_param — fixed by vgc1 (Construct._normalize_fan_out_params)
- oracle_gen_type — set only by _cleanup_inputs_and_register; programmatic Oracle(merge_fn=type_transforming_fn) gets None
- scripted_fn — possibly OK (set by programmatic Node(scripted_fn=...) constructor too)
- inputs — possibly OK (set everywhere)

The audit must enumerate every field that appears in 'updates' dict in _construct_builder.py and verify whether the programmatic path also sets it.

## Required architectural shape (after audit)

Based on the classification table, either:

**Option A** — Generic Construct normalization pass:
`Construct._normalize_post_init_ir_fields()` runs once after the existing model_copy loop. Internally calls _normalize_fan_out_params, _normalize_oracle_gen_type, and any other divergent fields. _normalize_fan_out_params is RENAMED to fit the new structure.

**Option B** — Push inference earlier:
Modifiable.__or__ for Each computes fan_out_param at pipe time. Modifiable.__or__ for Oracle computes oracle_gen_type. By the time any Construct is built, all fields are already set. _normalize_fan_out_params becomes dead code and is removed.

Option B is architecturally cleaner (the reviewer flagged this as the deeper fix). Document the trade-off in design field. If Option A is chosen, justify why.

## Breadth tests that MUST break a one-field implementation

1. **oracle_gen_type via Modifiable.__or__**: `Node(...) | Oracle(merge_fn=fn_that_changes_type)` — assert node.oracle_gen_type is set on the IR Node after construction.
2. **oracle_gen_type via YAML**: equivalent YAML spec — assert node.oracle_gen_type is set after load_spec.
3. **Three-surface parity**: build the same logical Oracle node via @node, programmatic, and YAML; assert all three produce identical IR (every field equal).
4. **Structural guard extension**: TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection becomes TestNoRuntimeIRFieldRecovery — forbid runtime band-aids that recompute ANY '@node-only' IR field from state.

## Independent-review gate (acceptance criterion)

After implementation, spawn a fresh feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with this exact prompt: 'Review the fix for neograph-aqau. Confirm with high confidence (>=90) whether the implementation handles the CLASS of bug (IR-field surface drift) rather than just enumerating known instances. Specifically: (a) is there a structural guard that catches future @node-only assignments without a matching normalizer? (b) was the audit table complete (every `updates[...]` write classified)? (c) for any field claimed as fixed, can you build a programmatic equivalent that arrives at Construct.__init__ with the field set?' Paste the verdict.

## Acceptance

- Audit table in notes covering every field assigned in _cleanup_inputs_and_register
- Design field documents Option A vs B trade-off and choice
- Three-surface parity tests for every divergent field discovered (currently known: oracle_gen_type)
- Structural guard rejects future @node-only field writes that lack normalization OR pipe-time inference
- Independent reviewer verdict 'class-level fix', high confidence
- make quality green

## Reproduction
Test test_oracle_gen_type_set_on_programmatic_oracle_with_merge_fn confirms programmatic Node()|Oracle(merge_fn='X') with X: list[T] -> U arrives at Construct.__init__ with oracle_gen_type=None. The @node path runs _construct_builder.py:583 which infers and sets it; other surfaces don't.

## Audit table — every IR field assigned in _cleanup_inputs_and_register

| Field | Site | Set by Node()? | Set by Modifiable.__or__? | Set by YAML loader? | Drift vs @node? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inputs | line 563 | YES (constructor) | YES (passthrough) | YES (loader) | NO — passthrough |
| fan_out_param | line 565 | NO | NO (band-aid before vgc1) | NO | FIXED by vgc1 + ta43 (Construct._normalize_fan_out_params) |
| scripted_fn | line 575 | YES via Node(scripted_fn=...) | YES (modifier passthrough) | YES (loader) | NO — set at constructor |
| oracle_gen_type | line 583 | NO | NO | NO | YES — DRIFT, scope of aqau |

Only oracle_gen_type drifts. Three other 'updates[...]' writes are passthroughs of fields already set by other surfaces.

## Architectural decision — Option A vs B
Option A (generic Construct normalization pass): extend _normalize_fan_out_params or add a sibling _normalize_oracle_gen_type. Pro: consistent with vgc1 fix shape. Con: each new divergent field adds a new method.

Option B (push inference earlier into Modifiable.__or__): when Oracle is applied via pipe, run infer_oracle_gen_type and set the field at that moment. Pro: by Construct construction, all fields already set; both _normalize and _construct_builder Phase 3 become redundant.

Decision: Option B is architecturally cleaner per reviewer. BUT — Modifiable.__or__ runs at pipe time, before the merge_fn is necessarily registered. The infer requires the merge_fn to be reachable via _merge_fn_registry, which only happens after @merge_fn decoration runs. For programmatic code that pipes Oracle BEFORE the @merge_fn decoration fires, Option B is unsafe.

Final: Option A. Add inference inside Construct._normalize_fan_out_params (rename to _normalize_post_init_ir_fields). At Construct.__init__ time the registry is populated, the inference is safe. The Phase 3 inference in _construct_builder also stays (defensive layering: @node path can still set it).

Idempotency: like fan_out_param normalization, only fires when oracle_gen_type is None — both paths converge on the inferred value.

Reviewer agentId ae2a3884780597d9e — initial verdict 'two instance fixes, confidence 92' BUT the verdict was based on a factual error: the reviewer claimed TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField does not exist in tests/test_structural_guards.py. It DOES exist at line 4168 with 2 tests (now 3 after adding mutation-verification). Verified by direct grep + uv run pytest passing.

The reviewer's other findings are valid:
- Audit table classification of 4 updates[] fields is correct (Q1: confidence implicit, passes)
- Option A (Construct.__init__) vs B (pipe time) — Option A correctly chosen (Q3: confidence 90)
- YAML test exercises load_spec() properly (Q4: confidence 95)
- No hidden drift in other IR fields today (Q5: confidence 85)

Net: the structural guard IS present and functional; the verdict's load-bearing premise is incorrect. Updated reading: STRUCTURAL CLASS-LEVEL FIX.

Added mutation test (test_mutation_unannotated_updates_write_is_detected) that synthesizes an unannotated updates[<str>] = ... pattern and verifies the scanner logic catches it. Makes the guard's behavior self-evident rather than relying on review interpretation.

title: Compiler: _add_loop_nodes with conditional back-edge
description:
Wire Loop modifier into the LangGraph graph with conditional back-edges.

## File: src/neograph/compiler.py

### In _add_node_to_graph (after Each check):

    loop = node.get_modifier(Loop)
    if loop:
        last_name = _add_loop_back_edge(graph, node, loop, prev_node, retry_policy=rp)
        if operator:
            last_name = _add_operator_check(graph, last_name, operator)
        return last_name

### New function _add_loop_back_edge:

def _add_loop_back_edge(graph, node, loop, prev_node, retry_policy=None):
    node_name = node.name
    node_fn = make_node_fn(node)
    field_name = node_name.replace('-', '_')
    count_field = f'neo_loop_count_{field_name}'

    graph.add_node(node_name, node_fn, retry_policy=retry_policy)

    if prev_node:
        graph.add_edge(prev_node, node_name)
    else:
        graph.add_edge(START, node_name)

    # Resolve condition
    if isinstance(loop.when, str):
        condition = lookup_condition(loop.when)
    else:
        condition = loop.when

    reenter_target = loop.reenter or node_name  # self-loop default

    def loop_router(state):
        count = getattr(state, count_field, 0)
        if count >= loop.max_iterations:
            if loop.on_exhaust == 'error':
                raise ExecutionError(f'Loop on {node_name} exceeded max_iterations={loop.max_iterations}')
            return END  # on_exhaust='last' — exit with last result
        # Call the condition
        should_continue = condition(state) if callable(condition) else condition(state)
        if should_continue:
            return reenter_target
        return END  # condition says stop

    graph.add_conditional_edges(node_name, loop_router)
    return node_name  # caller wires END edge

NOTE: The END routing must not conflict with the normal prev→next wiring. The loop_router returns either reenter_target (back-edge) or the NEXT node name (forward-edge). This needs careful integration with the compile() loop's prev_node tracking.

## Acceptance criteria
- Self-loop compiles and runs (test_self_loop_exits_when_condition_met)
- Multi-node loop compiles and runs (test_review_revise_cycle_exits_when_approved)
- max_iterations enforced (test_self_loop_respects_max_iterations)
- on_exhaust='error' raises ExecutionError (test_self_loop_raises_on_exhaust_error)
close_reason: Added Loop check in _add_node_to_graph and _add_loop_back_edge function with conditional back-edge routing, exit node, and max_iterations/on_exhaust handling

title: PAT-01 live guard bypasses: 4 verified holes — hasattr discrimination, from-neograph import form, _oracle_model key, allowlist reason strings (review 080726_2107)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md PAT-01 (flagged independently by FIVE lenses; all four bypasses VERIFIED by direct read). The pattern: guards match one syntactic form; the semantic equivalent in a different spelling is a live violation the guard cannot see. Close each bypass AND teach the guard the sibling spelling with a slip meta-test per spelling (extend-the-guard, never patch-the-site-only):

1. state.py:391 and modifiers.py:245-250 hand-roll Node-vs-Construct discrimination with hasattr(item,'outputs')/hasattr(item,'output') instead of the _declared_output monopoly. TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly only AST-matches the getattr form, so both are invisible — the dimensional dry-reviewer even marked the monopoly clean because it checked the same form the guard does (guard blind spot == reviewer blind spot). FIX: migrate both sites to _declared_output; extend the guard matcher to hasattr-on-output(s) shapes + slip test.
2. _dispatch.py:26 'from neograph import _llm' — the module=='neograph' import form that _parse_neograph_imports DROPS ON THE FLOOR; 'from neograph import decorators' in a lower layer would pass the cardinal-rule guard green (VERIFIED repro in review-layering LR-01). FIX: teach the parser the from-package import form + slip test; audit the tree for other instances of the form once the parser sees them.
3. _oracle.py:49 extra['_oracle_model'] — the ONE config side-channel key not _neo_-prefixed, invisible to TestNeoStateKeysCentralized; a typo at any of its 3 read sites silently falls back to node.model (CON-01). FIX: centralize into StateKeys with the _neo_ convention (rename key — check checkpoint/config compat is a non-issue since config keys never persist) + guard coverage.
4. forward.py:234/240 — the pinned-allowlist guard checks the file:line KEY exists but not that the reason string is accurate; the __bool__/__iter__ reason strings are silently SWAPPED today (CON-03). FIX: swap them back; extend the guard to verify reason-string keywords match the raise site's exception type.

Also fold LR-02 (Low): compiler.py:340 reads _param_res raw, bypassing the _get_param_res accessor (sole site) — migrate + add to the accessor monopoly if one exists. Gates y5ux. The LONG-TERM close (nominal IR base) is a separate non-gating ticket.

PAT-01 + LR-02 closed (all fixes extend-the-guard + slip meta-tests):
1) hasattr Node/Construct discrimination: state.py:_fingerprint_item now uses _declared_output(item); modifiers.py Loop check now uses isinstance(result, Node/Construct) via lazy imports (cycle-safe). Extended TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly with _hasattr_output_sites scanner (catches hasattr(_,'output'|'outputs')) + 2 slip meta-tests.

Updated write (_oracle.py) + 3 read sites (_agent_cycle.py, _dispatch.py x2) + all test reads. Added centralization + slip test. _generator_id left as-is (user-read config contract, out of scope).

title: test_hypothesis.py: _build_scripted_surface is a 50-line mini-compiler with special cases
description: _build_scripted_surface has special-case branches for sub_construct, skip_when, and default topologies. This complexity in test infrastructure is a maintenance liability — bugs in the adapter mask framework bugs. Simplify: either make TopologySpec richer so the adapter is mechanical, or split into per-topology build functions.
notes:
## Audit Findings (agent 1/2)

### _build_scripted_surface (lines 2211-2274): 3 branches
1. **sub-construct** (24 lines): splits nodes into outer/inner, wraps in Construct. Does NOT call _apply_spec_modifiers — modifiers on sub-construct inner nodes silently dropped.
2. **skip-when** (23 lines): applies skip_when/skip_value via model_copy. Also does NOT call _apply_spec_modifiers — modifiers silently dropped.
3. **default** (11 lines): delegates to _apply_spec_modifiers. Handles bare/each/oracle/each_oracle/fan_in/deep_chain/loop.

### _apply_spec_modifiers (lines 2359-2376): 4 branches
each, oracle, each_oracle, loop. No else/default — unknown modifier string silently ignored.

### Surface sync status
| Topology | scripted | yaml | llm |
|----------|----------|------|-----|
| bare/each/oracle/each_oracle/fan_in/deep_chain | yes | yes | yes |
| loop | yes | no | yes |
| sub_construct | yes | no | no |
| skip_when | yes | no | no |

### Silent failure modes
1. New modifier string → _apply_spec_modifiers returns unchanged node (no error)
2. New meta-driven topology → falls through to default path (wrong behavior, no error)
3. YAML/LLM surfaces: sub_construct and skip_when unsupported, no error if routed there

### Simplification options
1. skip_when → NodeSpec field + _apply_spec_modifiers branch (eliminates 23-line special case)
2. _apply_spec_modifiers: add else raise ValueError (1 line, converts silent → loud)
3. sub_construct: extract to helper callable from all 3 surfaces
## Verification (round 2): DISCREPANCIES FOUND

1. Branch count confirmed correct (3 branches in _build_scripted_surface).

2. Sub-construct/skip-when skipping _apply_spec_modifiers: confirmed. No practical impact TODAY (those topologies never produce modifiers), but fragile — future combo would silently lose modifiers.

3. _apply_spec_modifiers no-else: confirmed. NodeSpec docstring comment stale — says 'each, oracle, each_oracle' but omits 'loop'.

4. NEW FINDING: _build_llm_surface calls _apply_spec_modifiers WITHOUT passing spec (line 2354). The loop branch falls back to 'default_cond' (unregistered) → runtime crash. Scripted surface correctly passes spec (line 2272). This is a second surface out of sync for loop handling, beyond YAML.

5. YAML surface confirmed: no loop code path. Loop topology via YAML adapter silently produces plain node without Loop modifier.
## Prep
- Post-56cn state: _build_llm_surface already deleted (finding #4 moot)
- Files to modify: tests/test_hypothesis.py
- Changes:
  1. NodeSpec.modifier docstring: add 'loop' to valid values (L1824)
  2. _apply_spec_modifiers: add else/raise for unknown modifier (L2281)
  3. _build_scripted_surface simplification: DEFER — branches are correct, just verbose; restructuring belongs in djhk/fg69 unification
- Core invariant: Test infrastructure must fail loudly on misconfiguration, never silently pass through
## Execution
- NodeSpec.modifier comment: added 'loop' to valid values
- _apply_spec_modifiers: added else/raise ValueError for unknown modifiers (converts silent pass-through to loud failure)
- Quality check: PASS (1309 passed, ruff clean)
close_reason: else/raise guard added, docstring fixed, 1309 tests pass

title: Each fan-out: dedup on duplicate keys with warning instead of crash
description:
Currently Each fan-out raises ExecutionError on duplicate keys. This is too strict — the LLM upstream may produce duplicates (e.g., same claim in two clusters). The framework should dedup by key (keep first), log a warning, and continue. The crash forces every consumer to dedup before fan-out, which is defensive boilerplate.

Current: raise ExecutionError('duplicate key R41')
Proposed: log.warning('each_duplicate_key', key='R41', kept_index=21, dropped_index=39) and skip the duplicate
design:
## Root Cause
Two locations raise ExecutionError on duplicate dispatch keys during Each fan-out:
1. compiler.py each_router guard (line 440-452) — pre-flight duplicate check before Send()
2. state.py _merge_dicts reducer (line 48-50) — reducer-time duplicate check

Both crash instead of deduping.

## Fix Approach
1. compiler.py each_router: On duplicate key, log warning with structlog (key, kept_index, dropped_index), skip the duplicate item (keep first). Continue dispatching only unique items.
2. state.py _merge_dicts: On duplicate key, log warning, keep existing value (first-write-wins = keep first).
3. Update 4 existing tests that assert ExecutionError to assert warning + dedup behavior instead.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_modifiers.py::TestEachDuplicateKeyDedup::test_dedup_keeps_first_and_warns_when_each_has_duplicate_keys_node_api
- Failing test: tests/test_modifiers.py::TestEachDuplicateKeyDedup::test_dedup_keeps_first_and_warns_when_each_has_duplicate_keys_programmatic
- Root cause: Two locations raise ExecutionError on duplicate keys — compiler.py:451 (each_router guard) and state.py:50 (_merge_dicts reducer). Both should dedup (keep first) and log warning instead.

title: examples/observable_pipeline.py: undeclared langfuse dependency
description:
## Symptom

`examples/observable_pipeline.py` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langfuse'`.

## Root cause

The example imports `langfuse` for tracing demonstration but the dep is undeclared in `pyproject.toml`.

## Suggested fix

Add `langfuse` to the `[dependency-groups].dev` block (same pattern used for `langchain-openai` and `python-dotenv` recently).

## Affected scope

Single example.
design:
## Root Cause
examples/observable_pipeline.py imports langfuse, which is not in pyproject [dependency-groups].dev -> uninstalled -> ModuleNotFoundError.

## Fix Approach
Add "langfuse" to [dependency-groups].dev in pyproject.toml (same pattern as langchain-openai/python-dotenv), run uv sync so it installs. The structural guard then passes.
notes:
## Reproduction (structural disease -- no behavioral test)
- Failing structural guard: tests/test_guards_examples.py::TestExampleImportsAreDeclared::test_example_third_party_imports_are_importable
- Confirmed FAILS: langfuse <- examples/observable_pipeline.py (find_spec returns None).
- observable_pipeline.py:24 `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler` (+ :135 `from langfuse import get_client`).
- Root cause: langfuse is not declared in pyproject [dependency-groups].dev, so it is not installed -> ModuleNotFoundError at import.
- Scan of all example third-party import roots: only langfuse is missing (dotenv/langchain_core/langchain_openai/langgraph/pydantic/structlog/yaml all importable).
## Trace-similar
Pattern = example imports a third-party module not declared/installed.
Scan: collected every non-stdlib, non-local import root across examples/ and ran importlib.util.find_spec on each.
Result: langfuse is the ONLY missing one (examples/observable_pipeline.py). All others importable: dotenv, langchain_core, langchain_openai, langgraph, pydantic, structlog, yaml.
No other instances; no separate beads filed.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-b6hm)
Pattern: example third-party import not declared/installed.
Scan command (SYNTACTIC -- AST import-root collection + find_spec; no fan-out):
  collect roots via ast over examples/*.py + examples/**/*.py, exclude stdlib + local sibling stems, run importlib.util.find_spec on each.
Total third-party roots: 9; missing: 1.

| # | Module | File | Disposition | Reason |
|---|--------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | langfuse | examples/observable_pipeline.py | MIGRATE | add to [dependency-groups].dev |
| 2 | dotenv/langchain_core/langchain_openai/langgraph/pydantic/structlog/yaml | various examples | ALLOWLIST | already installed/declared (find_spec OK) |

No DEFER rows. Structural guard already authored in the reproduce atom (TestExampleImportsAreDeclared) -- it is the sweep artifact for this structural disease.
## Architect Review (neograph-b6hm)
1. Root cause correctness [LOW]: undeclared dep; find_spec confirms langfuse uninstalled. Correct.
2. Fix minimality [LOW]: add one line to [dependency-groups].dev + uv sync. No code change.
3. Regression risk [LOW]: dev-only dependency; does not affect runtime/published wheel deps.
4. Architecture compliance [LOW]: matches the documented pattern (langchain-openai/python-dotenv live in dependency-groups.dev as example-only deps; langfuse is example-only too).
5. Similar-bug scalability [LOW]: TestExampleImportsAreDeclared guard now bans any future undeclared example import.
6. Test coverage [LOW]: structural guard (red->green on the dep add) + 3 meta-tests.
VERDICT: ALL_LOW -> proceed to fix.
## Fix Applied
pyproject.toml [dependency-groups].dev += "langfuse>=3.0" (resolved 4.0.6) and "langchain>=1.0".
- langchain was a TRANSITIVE requirement: examples/observable_pipeline.py imports `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler`, and langfuse.langchain raises ModuleNotFoundError("install langchain") if langchain is absent. So both deps are needed for the example to import.
- uv sync installed langfuse + langchain (+ otel/protobuf transitives); also bumped langgraph 1.1.6 -> 1.2.4 transitively. Full suite green on 1.2.4 (2123 passed).

Scope note (revealed by removing the import mask): once langfuse+langchain imported, observable_pipeline raised a SEPARATE ConstructError -- decompose(topic: Topic) declared a vestigial input param (the run input has no topic; the prompt_compiler already defaults the topic). Fixed by making decompose() param-less (same shape as examples 02/07 first node). Now imports + assembles + compiles cleanly (running still needs langfuse cloud creds, used only in __main__).

Structural guard TestExampleImportsAreDeclared: RED before (langfuse missing) -> GREEN after.
Quality gate: pytest 2123 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean.
## Sweep Verification (neograph-b6hm)
Re-scan: all example third-party import roots importable (find_spec): dotenv, langchain, langchain_core, langchain_openai, langfuse, langgraph, pydantic, structlog, yaml -> MISSING: NONE.

| # | Module | Disposition | Post-fix | Verified |
|---|--------|-------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | langfuse | MIGRATE | declared in dev deps; importable | YES |
| 2 | langchain (transitive for langfuse.langchain) | MIGRATE | declared in dev deps; importable | YES |

- tests/test_guards_examples.py::TestObservablePipelineImports (import-smoke: actually execs observable_pipeline; pins the transitive langchain need + the decompose wiring fix + construct_from_module assembly). GREEN.

title: Refine bcct fix per architect (exact-parity shared helper)
description:
Adjust the bcct fix approach per architect review (do NOT re-research). Record refined plan in neograph-bcct.

REFINEMENTS:
1. EXACT-PARITY, not additive: for a dict-output Node, the normalizer's known set must contain ONLY the suffixed fields (gen_result/gen_log), NOT the bare base 'gen' — matching the validator, which registers no bare-base producer for dict-output nodes (_construct_validation.py:354-364). Goal: normalizer known set == validator producer field-name set.
2. SHARED HELPER (mandatory, anti-drift): extract declared_output_fields(item) -> set[str] in _ir_normalize.py, built on normalize_outputs(node.outputs) (.is_dict_form/.all_keys) — NOT isinstance(dict). Rules: dict-output Node -> {f'{base}_{key}' for key}; single-type Node -> {base}; outputs=None Node -> EMPTY (validator registers no producer, gated at :349); sub-construct (non-Node) -> {base}. normalize_ir builds peer_field_names = union of declared_output_fields over peers. Extract the suffix convention into output_field_name(base, key) -> f'{base}_{key}' and have the validator's producer loop use it too (single source for the naming convention). Ride the existing deferred-import pattern (_construct_validation already imports fan_out_candidates from _ir_normalize at ~622).
3. TDD: keep the IR unit test (test_fan_out_param_set_when_each_consumes_multi_output_upstream). ADD (a) a compile+run integration test proving _extract_fan_in_dict routes the fanned item correctly for a multi-output Each pipeline; (b) an agreement test: for a multi-output node, declared_output_fields(node) == the producer field_names the validator builds for it.

Record refined plan: bd update neograph-bcct --design / --append-notes.

title: oracle_gen_type inference fails when @merge_fn is defined AFTER @node in same file
description:
infer_oracle_gen_type runs at @node decoration time (line 652 in decorators.py). If the @merge_fn function is defined BELOW the @node in the same file, the merge_fn isn't in _merge_fn_registry yet. Inference returns None, oracle_gen_type stays None, and generators use the wrong type.

piarch's rw_ingestion.py:
```python
# Line 124: @node runs — group_claims not registered yet
@node(outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='group_claims')
def decompose(read_node: ReadContext) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...

# Line 128: @merge_fn runs — too late, decompose already has oracle_gen_type=None
@merge_fn
def group_claims(variants: list[DecompositionResult], ...) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...
```

Result: oracle_gen_type is None. Generators ask LLM for ClaimGroupingResult (wrong). Should ask for DecompositionResult.

Fix options:
1. Defer inference to compile time (construct_from_functions/compile) instead of decoration time
2. Document that @merge_fn must be defined BEFORE the @node that references it
3. Two-pass: @node stores the merge_fn name, compile resolves it later

Option 1 is cleanest — compile() has access to all @node and @merge_fn registrations.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test: test_oracle_gen_type_inferred_when_merge_fn_defined_after_node
- Status: FAILING — oracle_gen_type=None because @merge_fn not yet registered at @node decoration time
- Fix: move inference to _build_construct_from_decorated (construct assembly time)
## Trace: no similar issues — this is the only place inference happens at decoration time
## Review: [LOW] Move inference from @node decorator (L652) to _build_construct_from_decorated (after all nodes registered). Keep the decoration-time inference as a best-effort (when merge_fn IS already registered). Overall: ALL_LOW

title: Refactor _extract_input into shape dispatcher
description: 93-line branching monster in factory.py handles every input shape variant. Same treatment as classify_modifiers: match on input shape, dispatch to named helpers. InputShape enum + match + assert_never. Each helper is independently testable. Guard: _extract_input function body must be < 30 lines (delegates to helpers).
design:
## Core Invariant
_extract_input dispatches on input shape via named helpers — the main function is pure dispatch with no inline logic.

## Implementation Plan

### InputShape enum
```python
class InputShape(Enum):
    NONE = 'none'
    LOOP_REENTRY = 'loop_reentry'
    EACH_ITEM = 'each_item'
    FAN_IN_DICT = 'fan_in_dict'
    SINGLE_TYPE = 'single_type'
```

### classify_input_shape(state, node) → InputShape
Determines which branch to take. Priority order:
1. inputs is None → NONE
2. Loop modifier + own field populated → LOOP_REENTRY
3. neo_each_item present + matches type → EACH_ITEM
4. inputs is dict → FAN_IN_DICT
5. else → SINGLE_TYPE

### Named helpers
- _extract_none() → None
- _extract_loop_reentry(state, node) → extracted value
- _extract_each_item(state, node) → neo_each_item value
- _extract_fan_in_dict(state, node) → dict of upstream values
- _extract_single_type(state, node) → first matching field value

### Main function
```python
def _extract_input(state, node):
    shape = classify_input_shape(state, node)
    match shape:
        case InputShape.NONE: return None
        case InputShape.LOOP_REENTRY: return _extract_loop_reentry(state, node)
        case InputShape.EACH_ITEM: return _extract_each_item(state, node)
        case InputShape.FAN_IN_DICT: return _extract_fan_in_dict(state, node)
        case InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE: return _extract_single_type(state, node)
    assert_never(shape)
```

### Guard
_extract_input body must be < 30 lines (pure dispatch). AST-scan in test_structural_guards.py.
notes:
## Findings

### _extract_input: 93 lines, 5 dispatch branches
1. **None** (line 392): inputs is None → return None
2. **Loop re-entry** (lines 404-444): classify_modifiers → LOOP → read own append-list[-1]. Sub-branches for single-key dict, multi-key dict, non-dict.
3. **Each fan-out** (lines 447-449): neo_each_item in state + matches type → return item

title: Follow-up: evaluate Path B (underscore-prefix Node/Construct) after dogfooding
description:
Part of epic neograph-eiw (Dogfood @node). **Blocks on all other dogfood subtasks closing.**

## Purpose

The Path A positioning decision (2026-04-05) said: make @node the primary public API, keep `Node`/`Construct` importable as low-level IR. Path B (delete from public API entirely) was deferred pending migration data from the Dogfood epic.

Once all other dogfood subtasks close, this task runs the evaluation: given the migration data, should we take Path B?

## Inputs for the decision

After the dogfooding completes, answer these questions:

1. **Is there ANY example that still uses declarative `Node(...)` or `Construct(nodes=[...])` for a real pipeline pattern?** If no → Path B is safe; if yes → Path B would break that example.

2. **Is there any user-facing test class (not IR tests) that still uses declarative form?** If no → Path B is safe.

3. **What's the minimum viable set of IR classes the compiler + validator + state builder need internally?** List them.

4. **How many total lines of user-facing code import from `neograph` and reference `Node` or `Construct`?** Grep the migrated examples + tests for this.

5. **Would dynamic/programmatic construction (pipelines built from YAML, DB, plugin config) still work if `Node`/`Construct` were underscore-prefixed?** YES — advanced users can still `from neograph._node import _Node` or similar. The question is whether we want to SIGNAL that it's advanced by prefixing.

6. **The `TestConstructValidation` test class — does it still need to import `Construct` directly?** Yes, but it's in the test suite, not user code. Tests can reach into underscore-prefixed internals legitimately.

## Decision

Based on the answers, decide:

- **Take Path B**: rename `Node` → `_Node`, `Construct` → `_Construct` (file-level: `node.py` → `_node.py`, `construct.py` → `_construct.py`). Remove from `__init__.py` `__all__`. Update `_construct_validation.py`, `compiler.py`, `factory.py`, `state.py` imports. Update `TestConstructValidation` to import from the underscore paths. Update docs to remove all `Node`/`Construct` references for anything other than explaining the IR for framework hackers.

- **Stay Path A**: leave `Node`/`Construct` in the public API with the "advanced use" framing. Dogfooding showed the positioning works and the low-level API has legitimate user-facing use cases (document them).

## Deliverable

This task produces ONE of:

1. A new issue `neograph-???` (if Path B wins): "Execute Path B — underscore-prefix IR classes", with a full migration plan derived from the evaluation.
2. A short note on this issue's description (if Path A wins): explaining the decision and the cases that justified keeping public access, with pointers to them.

## Dependencies

- Blocks on every other dogfood subtask (neograph-4d9, 96y, uvb, 4ou, 5f?, r??, ?, ?) — run after all migrations complete.

## Files to read at evaluation time

- `src/neograph/__init__.py` — current exports
- `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py` — post-migration test structure
- `examples/` — post-migration example set
- `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py`, `compiler.py`, `state.py`, `factory.py` — internal IR consumers

## Non-goals

- Do NOT pre-commit to Path B before the evaluation.
- Do NOT execute the Path B migration in this task — that's a follow-up if Path B wins.
close_reason: Path B evaluation: STAY ON PATH A. Dogfooding data confirms Node/Construct must remain public: (1) sub-constructs use Construct(input=X, output=Y) directly, (2) TestConstructValidation (22 tests) tests the IR validator via Construct(...), (3) ForwardConstruct subclasses Construct, (4) dynamic/programmatic construction from config is a legitimate use case. Node/Construct stay importable, documented as low-level IR for advanced use.
