title: Codebase-wide disease scan for g2jg
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show g2jg` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/g2jg/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" g2jg
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (g2jg)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/g2jg/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add g2jg codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/g2jg/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for g2jg
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on g2jg
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" g2jg`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (g2jg)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add g2jg sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Each over-path navigation crashes on None/absent intermediate instead of routing to the existing empty_bypass
description:
Consumer-reported (ox-troubleshooting-demo cascade: hypothesize | Each(over='hypothesize.candidates') — intermittent ~11 percent whole-run loss when a structured decode flake yields None). REPRODUCED 2026-07-06 on develop with a minimal probe: scripted node declaring outputs=HypothesisSet returns None -> node_complete fires -> Each router crashes TypeError: NoneType object is not subscriptable.

THE BUG DEFEATS ITS OWN DESIGN: _wiring.py:66-69 — the comment above bus.get(root) explicitly anticipates 'a runtime-absent root surfaces as an empty/None collection below', and each_router (~:165) already has an empty_bypass path routing an empty collection downstream. But _collect_each_items navigates the dotted segments with getattr(obj, part) if hasattr else obj[part] and never guards obj is None — it crashes at :69 BEFORE returning the empty list that would trigger the bypass. The safety net exists; the navigation jumps over it. Latent sibling hole at :73 — list(obj) on a None root with zero segments raises the same way.

EXPECTED: a None/absent over source resolves to an empty collection -> each_router routes to empty_bypass -> downstream proceeds (fails-closed on 'no items'), exactly as the comment and bypass promise. No raw TypeError, and never a framework-internals stack trace that does not name the user's node or path.

FIX SHAPE (per existing design intent): break out of segment navigation when obj is None; treat missing mapping keys/attrs as None; return [] when the resolved obj is None. Guard :73 too. Emit a log.info (e.g. each_over_absent, fan_out=..., path=...) so an unexpected empty fan-out is diagnosable — silence would hide the Bug-2 class this often masks (see companion ticket for the None-output write-boundary question; the two are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives: this fix covers legitimately-absent upstream — untaken branch arm, skip_when — while the companion covers ran-and-violated-contract).

NOTE: _collect_each_items is the monopolized navigation rule shared by each_router AND flat_router (Each x Oracle fusion) — one fix covers both topologies; test both. TDD: minimal repro is a node declaring outputs=Foo returning None feeding | Each(over='node.items') — today TypeError, expected zero-item fan-out with the bypass taken. Also cover: absent root via untaken branch arm; dotted path where an INTERMEDIATE attr is None; consumer after the bypass still runs. Three-surface parity applies (map_over decorator form + programmatic Each).
close_reason: Guard _collect_each_items to fail-closed to [] on None/absent Each over-root (untaken branch/skip_when) or intermediate-None dotted attr, with each_over_absent log.info; each_router/flat_router now hit empty_bypass instead of crashing TypeError

title: §2: Per-compile @node shim lookup via construct walk
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2 (compile() reads inputs from kwargs).

**Problem**: `_registry.py` declares a process-global `Registry` singleton (`registry = Registry()` at line 52) that holds `@node`-decorated function shims. Two `compile()` calls in the same process share this registry, leading to test isolation issues and the `id()`-keyed shadowing bug (R4, `neograph-xdvt`).

**Fix**: `compile()` builds a fresh per-compile `dict` (no need for a `Registry` class wrapper) for `@node` scripted shims. The walk:

1. Traverse the construct's nodes
2. For each `@node`-decorated function (sidecar present), build a scripted shim via the existing `_register_node_scripted` logic
3. Insert the shim into the per-compile dict under a unique name (use `secrets.token_hex(8)` per `neograph-xdvt`, not `id(f)`)
4. The dispatch layer reads the shim from the per-compile dict (closed over in factory closures)

**Acceptance**:
- No `Registry` class or singleton remains
- Two `compile()` calls produce two independent shim dicts that cannot collide
- The `id(f)` keying from `decorators.py:151` is gone
- `tests/conftest.py` registry-cleanup fixture goes away (no longer needed)

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoGlobalRegistry` (new) + `tests/decorator/test_node_decorator.py::test_two_compiles_yield_independent_shim_dicts` (new behavioral test)
**Test type**: structural-guard + TDD-red-then-green
**What it exercises**: (a) AST-scan `src/neograph/_registry.py`; assert no module-level `registry = Registry()` instantiation remains; assert no `class Registry` definition remains (or it is reduced to a thin per-compile container). (b) Behavioral: decorate the SAME function name in two different test scopes, compile two different constructs, run both, assert no shim shadowing — each compile's dict has its own shim keyed by a fresh `secrets.token_hex` value. (c) Assert `tests/conftest.py` no longer declares the registry-cleanup fixture (grep).
**Expected initial state**: failing — module global `registry = Registry()` exists today and `id(f)` keying makes the two-compile test collide.
**Persistence**: both stay in suite.

Order: write failing tests FIRST → run → must fail → migrate to per-compile dict + secrets.token_hex keys → run again → must pass.
close_reason: Per-compile @node shim lookup. compile() walks the construct, collects each Node's _scripted_shim (PrivateAttr) into a fresh dict, threads it through factory closures. Two compile() calls produce two distinct _neo_scripted dicts. Singleton registry = Registry() removed from _registry.py; legacy register_*() helpers write into a separate _FALLBACK in _runtime_registry.py (will be removed in ticket 5). id(n) keying gone from _register_node_scripted.

title: fan_out_param divergence when an Each node consumes a multi-output upstream's per-key field
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this fix)

The set of "known field names" used by `_FanOutParamNormalizer.apply` (and any future normalizer that needs to recognize what counts as an upstream producer) is IDENTICAL to the set the validator's `_check_fan_in_inputs` computes from `producers`. Multi-output nodes contribute one field per output key (`{node}_result`, `{node}_tool_log`); single-output nodes contribute one field (`{node}`). One source of truth, applied in two places (normalizer + validator), via a shared helper that lives in the IR layer — not duplicated logic.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py::normalize_ir` (lines ~180-205) — how `peer_field_names` is built today (one entry per node name only).
2. `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py::fan_out_candidates` — how it uses `known_field_names` to identify the unique unknown key.
3. `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py::_validate_node_chain` — how the validator builds the FULL producer set, including per-output-key fields for multi-output nodes. Trace the code path that registers producers for dict-form `Node.outputs`.
4. `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs` — confirms it sees `gen_result` as a real producer field (not just `gen`).
5. `src/neograph/state.py` / `src/neograph/_normalize.py` — how `normalize_outputs` exposes `all_keys` / `primary_key` for dict-form outputs.
6. Existing test fixtures: search `tests/` for any case combining multi-output upstream (`outputs={"key1": T1, "key2": T2}`) AND a downstream `Each` consumer that takes one specific output key as a fan-in input. If none exists, that gap is itself a finding.

Output in bead notes: a side-by-side table of "what `peer_field_names` contains today" vs "what the validator's producer set contains" for a sample multi-output construct. The divergence row IS the bug.

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ the `design` field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- A SHARED helper computes "field names contributed by a Node IR" — handles both single-type outputs (returns `{field_name_for(node.name)}`) and dict-form outputs (returns `{f"{field_name_for(node.name)}_{key}" for key in output_keys}`). Single source of truth.
- The normalizer's `peer_field_names` is computed via this helper, NOT inlined.
- The validator's per-producer registration is ALSO via this helper (or otherwise verifiably consistent — a structural guard pins agreement).
- A behavioral test that EXERCISES the bug: build a Construct with a multi-output node `gen` (`outputs={"result": T1, "log": T2}`), a downstream Each node consuming `inputs={"gen_result": T1, "cluster": ClusterGroup}` over `gen.result`. Pre-fix: `fan_out_param` is None and runtime `_extract_fan_in_dict` raises. Post-fix: `fan_out_param = "cluster"` and the pipeline runs.
- A structural guard that pins agreement between normalizer's known-field computation and validator's producer-field computation (so a future change to multi-output semantics in one place breaks the other test loudly).

If the proposed diff special-cases the dict-form output path inside the normalizer (rather than via the shared helper that BOTH sides consume), STOP. That's a band-aid.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO branching-over-polymorphism (if a future output form is added, the shared helper grows ONE branch in ONE place, not three).
- NO inline `field_name_for(...)` enumeration that duplicates dict-form handling.
- NO patching just the normalizer to "see" the missing fields — fix the underlying duplication. The validator and normalizer must agree by sharing a function, not by parallel inline computation.
- Net acceptance is STRUCTURAL: the new shared helper lives in `_ir_normalize.py` (or a sibling module like `_ir_fields.py`) and BOTH the normalizer and the validator import it. Duplication is mechanically impossible.

## Phase 5 — Independent review (correctness AND elegance)

After implementation, spawn a feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with model: opus. Demand evaluation of:

1. CORRECTNESS — the multi-output + Each consumer pipeline COMPILES and RUNS. Existing single-output + Each cases unchanged. All 1925 existing tests pass.
2. ELEGANCE — is there ONE function/method that owns "what field names does this Node contribute?" Or is the rule still spread across normalizer + validator?
3. INVARIANT — try to construct a Node IR form where the normalizer's view of "known fields" and the validator's view would still diverge. If you can, the fix is incomplete.
4. NO NEW HYDRA — when a hypothetical THIRD output form is added (e.g., tagged-union outputs), how many places must change? Must be ONE.
5. PINNING — is there a structural test that fails loudly if a future change drifts the two views apart?

Reviewer must verdict ELEGANT or NOT, confidence ≥85. If NOT ELEGANT, reopen.

## Why this is P1 not P3

Filed initially as P3 because no real user has hit it (no fixture covers the case). Re-evaluated: the bug is a SILENT MISCOMPILE — the construct passes validation but fails at runtime with a confusing error. Multi-output Each consumers are a legitimate use case (the audit doc itself includes `tool_log` as a typical secondary output key). Shipping with this latent miscompile is the kind of debt a real user would file as P0 the moment they hit it. Fix now, before any user encounters it.

## Acceptance

- Shared helper exists: one function computes the field-name contribution of a Node IR
- Normalizer and validator both consume it (verified by structural guard)
- Behavioral test: multi-output upstream + Each consumer compiles AND runs end-to-end
- All existing tests pass (1925 baseline)
- Independent reviewer (opus) verdicts ELEGANT with confidence ≥85, written to bead notes
- bd close after reviewer ELEGANT verdict
design:
## Root Cause
normalize_ir's peer_field_names = {field_name_for(name)} (peer NODE names) is NARROWER than the validator's producer field-name set (per-output-key fields for dict-output nodes). An Each consumer fanning over a multi-output upstream's suffixed field (gen_result) sees it as an extra unknown candidate -> 2 candidates -> fan_out_param=None; validator (full producer set) sees 1 and tolerates -> construct validates with a wrong (None) IR -> runtime _extract_fan_in_dict cannot route the fanned item.

## Fix Approach (refined per architect — exact-parity shared helper)
1. _ir_normalize.py: add output_field_name(base, key) -> f'{base}_{key}' (the suffix convention) and declared_output_fields(item) -> set[str]:
   - dict-output Node: {output_field_name(base, k) for k in normalize_outputs(item.outputs).all_keys}
   - single-type Node: {base}
   - outputs=None Node: set()  (validator registers no producer)
   - non-Node (sub-construct): {base}
   built on normalize_outputs (NOT isinstance(dict)). base = field_name_for(item.name).
2. normalize_ir: peer_field_names = union of declared_output_fields(item) over construct.nodes. Exact parity with validator producer NAMES (no bare base for dict-output nodes).
3. _construct_validation.py producer loop (~357): key_field = output_field_name(field_name, output_key) — single source for the naming convention (anti-drift). Function-local import if needed (cycle already broken via the existing fan_out_candidates deferred import).
4. Tests: keep IR unit test; add (a) compile+run integration test for a multi-output Each pipeline (runtime routing), (b) agreement test declared_output_fields(node) == validator producer field_names for a multi-output node.

## Core Invariant
The set of field names the normalizer treats as 'known producers' is IDENTICAL to the validator's producer field-name set, derived from one shared output-field-naming helper.

## Reproduction (atom fsth.2)

- FAILED: assert None == 'item' (Construct ACCEPTED — validator tolerates — but consumer.fan_out_param is None).
- Root cause: _FanOutParamNormalizer derives candidates via fan_out_candidates(node, peer_field_names) where peer_field_names = {field_name_for(n.name)} — peer NODE names only. A multi-output upstream 'gen' (outputs {result, log}) produces FIELDS 'gen_result'/'gen_log', which are NOT in peer_field_names, so an Each consumer with inputs={'gen_result', 'item'} sees TWO candidates -> declines -> fan_out_param=None. The validator uses the full producer field set (incl. per-output-key names) so it sees ONE candidate and passes.
## Trace similar (atom fsth.3)
Searched for the same 'peer field set from node NAMES, blind to per-output-key fields' pattern. Result: ISOLATED to ONE site — normalize_ir's peer_field_names (_ir_normalize.py:192-193). 
- construct.py:137 is the llm_config/renderer propagation loop (no field-set logic).
- The CORRECT multi-output expansion already exists in _construct_validation.py:348-373 (producer loop): single-output -> field_name_for(name); dict-output -> f'{field_name}_{output_key}' per key. state.py builds matching per-key state fields. Both the validator and state model already handle multi-output; only the normalizer lagged.
- No systemic spread. Fix mirrors the validator's f'{field_name}_{output_key}' naming when expanding peer output fields. No other call site needs changing.
## Architect Review (pragmatic, 2026-06-02)

DECISION: exact-parity via SHARED helper. NOT additive. Shared helper = YES (mandatory, not optional).

- [LOW] Q1 additive-safety: additive (keep bare base + suffixed) is SAFE in isolation — adding names can only REMOVE candidates, never miss a legit receiver. The only 'missed receiver' counter-case requires the user to name the fan-out receiver identically to a real producer field (e.g. receiver param 'gen_result' while node 'gen' has output key 'result'), which is a pre-existing name collision the construct was already broken by. Not introduced by the fix.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q3 additive vs exact-parity: choose EXACT PARITY (drop the bare 'gen' for dict-output nodes). RATIONALE: the validator does NOT register a bare-base producer for dict-output nodes (validation:354-364 takes the dict branch, skips the else at 365). The bead invariant demands the two sets be IDENTICAL. Additive leaves the normalizer's set a strict SUPERSET of the validator's -> technically violates the invariant and could let the structural guard pass while the views differ. Parity is correct.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q2 edge cases — the prompt's additive snippet has TWO real defects vs the validator:
  1. outputs=None Node: validator registers NO producer (gated 'output_type is not None' at val:349). Additive snippet keeps the base -> INVERSE divergence (normalizer sees a field the validator doesn't). Exact-parity helper must return EMPTY set for None-output nodes.
  2. Sub-construct (not Node): validator registers ONE producer at field_name_for(name) via .output (singular). Helper must return {field_name_for(name)} for sub-constructs (base only). The 'isinstance(item, Node)' guard handles this only if the None-output gate is also respected.
  3. Each-wrapped multi-output upstream: validator wraps per-key TYPES in dict[str,X] but field NAMES unchanged. Helper is name-only/type-independent -> no impact. Correct.

- [LOW] Q4 site + shared helper: CORRECT site, but hand-mirroring f'{base}_{key}' is the band-aid the bead forbids. MANDATORY shared helper. Place it in _ir_normalize.py (or sibling _ir_fields.py). PRECEDENT: _construct_validation already deferred-imports fan_out_candidates FROM _ir_normalize (val:622-624) specifically to break the _construct_validation->_ir_normalize->_sidecar cycle. The new helper rides the SAME deferred-import pattern — proven, low-risk. Helper MUST be built on normalize_outputs(node.outputs) (.all_keys / .is_dict_form), the existing leaf primitive in _normalize.py — do NOT re-roll isinstance(outputs, dict). The validator's producer loop (val:346-376) should then derive its field NAMES from the same helper so name-convention drift is mechanically impossible.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q5 TDD: IR-level assertion (fan_out_param=='item') is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. The bug's severity claim is a SILENT MISCOMPILE failing at runtime in _extract_fan_in_dict. Need BOTH: (a) IR unit test pinning the inference, (b) compile+run integration test proving the runtime fan-in path consumes fan_out_param for the multi-output case, (c) structural guard pinning normalizer<->validator field-name agreement (bead already requires this).

Decision: EXACT-PARITY (not additive); SHARED HELPER = YES, built on normalize_outputs, deferred-imported by validator per existing fan_out_candidates precedent; helper must reproduce validator's None-output and sub-construct gating exactly.
Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (fix approach is right in spirit but the prompt's literal additive snippet diverges from the validator on None-output + sub-construct + bare-base; tighten to exact-parity shared helper).

NEEDS_REFINEMENT — autonomously resolvable. Architect gave precise direction (exact-parity shared helper + None/sub-construct gating + integration & agreement tests). Refine atom neograph-b994 created; fix proceeds after.
## Fix (atom fsth.6)
- naming.py: added output_field_name(base, key) -> f'{base}_{key}' — single source of the per-output-key naming convention.
- _ir_normalize.py: added declared_output_fields(item: ConstructItem) -> set[str] (built on normalize_outputs; dict->per-key fields, single->base, None->empty, sub-construct->base). normalize_ir's peer_field_names is now the union of declared_output_fields over all nodes — EXACT parity with the validator's producer field-name set.

- Tests: IR repro (test_fan_out_param_set_when_each_consumes_multi_output_upstream) now PASSES; added TestDeclaredOutputFields (dict/single/None/hyphen parity) + TestFanOutMultiOutputRuntime (compile+run proving _extract_fan_in_dict routes the fanned item end-to-end).
- Quality: PASS (1931 passed, lint + mypy clean). No regressions.

- example 04 (each fanout) runs clean end-to-end.

title: merge_fn exceptions should surface at compile time or fail loud at runtime
description:
## Problem
A merge_fn that throws an exception during execution is silently caught by the consumer (piarch's group_claims), causing the entire Oracle merge to fall back to no-op behavior (singleton groups). The pipeline runs to completion producing garbage results — 3x too many claims, 3x the LLM cost — with zero errors in the log.

The root cause in this case was an AttributeError inside piarch_llm_call (ModelRole.FAST doesn't exist). But any exception in the merge_fn is equally dangerous.

## What NeoGraph should do

1. **At compile time**: validate that merge_fn can be called with the expected signature. If the merge_fn references external symbols, at minimum verify the function is importable without errors.

2. **At runtime**: if the merge_fn throws, NeoGraph should NOT silently continue. It should either:
   a. Re-raise the exception (let RetryPolicy handle it), OR
   b. Log the exception at ERROR level with full traceback and mark the node as failed

Currently: NeoGraph calls the merge_fn and returns whatever it returns. The silent fallback is in the consumer's code (piarch's except Exception: fallback). But NeoGraph could provide a safer pattern — e.g., merge_fn results are validated against the output type, and type mismatches are flagged.

## Impact
An unnoticed AttributeError caused every pipeline run to produce 62 singleton groups instead of ~20 merged groups. This tripled the downstream workload (62 explore+score calls instead of ~20), costing 3x in LLM tokens and time, with no indication anything was wrong.
design:
## Root Cause
make_oracle_merge_fn (factory.py:651-700) calls the merge function and passes the result to _build_oracle_merge_result without validating the return type. A merge_fn that returns the wrong type silently writes garbage to state.

## Fix Approach
In make_oracle_merge_fn, after calling the merge function, validate the result:
- isinstance check against output_model (or the primary type for dict-form outputs)
- If wrong type: raise ExecutionError with clear message naming the merge_fn, expected type, and actual type

This is a one-line addition in each of the three merge_fn paths (merge_prompt, @merge_fn metadata, scripted merge).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test 1 (merge_fn raises): PASSES — neograph already propagates the exception. The silent failure was in the consumer (piarch's except Exception fallback), not neograph.
- Test 2 (merge_fn returns wrong type): FAILS — neograph silently accepts a string where Claims was expected. No type validation on merge_fn result.
- Failing test: tests/test_modifiers.py::TestOracleMergeFnErrors::test_wrong_return_type_raises_when_merge_fn_returns_bad_type
- Root cause: make_oracle_merge_fn in factory.py does not validate the merge result against output_model.
## Trace Similar
Pattern: unvalidated function results written to state.
1. make_oracle_merge_fn: merge result not validated against output_model (THE BUG)
2. _build_oracle_merge_result: blindly accepts whatever merged value it gets
3. make_subgraph_fn: output extraction uses isinstance check (line 780) — this one IS validated
4. Scripted node wrappers: result from raw_fn written directly to state — no type check

The merge_fn case is the highest-risk because the merge is user code that can silently return wrong types. Scripted nodes are also user code but the type mismatch is more likely to cause downstream errors (next node gets wrong input). The subgraph path is already safe.
## Architect Review
Core invariant: merge_fn results must be validated against the declared output type before being written to state.
Approach: ALL_LOW — add isinstance check in _build_oracle_merge_result, raise ExecutionError on mismatch.
Risk: None — single function, clear fix.

title: arch: Pydantic schema for YAML/JSON spec loader (parse-don't-validate for user pipeline specs)
description:
Child of ianf. The spec loader at src/neograph/loader.py accepts YAML/JSON user input and walks it as untyped dicts. Typos in spec files fail late with cryptic errors; no schema for users to discover valid keys.

## Current state

```
loader.py:35  project: str | dict[str, Any] | None = None
loader.py:65  def _parse_input(source: str | dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]
loader.py:90  def _validate_spec(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None
loader.py:107 def _build_construct(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> Construct
loader.py:147 def _build_node(node_spec: dict[str, Any]) -> Node
loader.py:232 def _apply_modifiers(item: Any, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> Any
```

Each builder does its own `.get(key, default)` + manual shape validation.

## Biggest user-UX impact of any ianf child

Consumer pipelines are often defined in YAML for non-Python stakeholders (analysts, ops). A typo like `output_stratgy: json_mode` currently produces a silent default. With a Pydantic schema:

- Typos rejected at load time with 'unknown field X; did you mean Y?'
- Required fields flagged at load time, not at first run
- JSON Schema auto-generated for IDE / documentation
- Schema versioning becomes possible ('spec_version: 2' gates allowed fields)

## Design

```python
# src/neograph/_spec_schema.py (new)
class SpecModifier(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    type: Literal['oracle', 'each', 'operator', 'loop']
    # ... per-modifier fields

class SpecNode(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    mode: Literal['think', 'agent', 'act', 'scripted', 'raw']
    inputs: str | dict[str, str] | None = None
    outputs: str | dict[str, str] | None = None
    prompt: str | None = None
    model: str | None = None
    llm_config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)  # or LlmConfig after pej0 lands
    tools: list[SpecTool] = Field(default_factory=list)
    modifiers: list[SpecModifier] = Field(default_factory=list)
    # ...

class SpecConstruct(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    input: str | None = None
    output: str | None = None
    nodes: list[SpecNode | SpecConstruct]  # self-referential for sub-constructs
    llm_config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Spec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    version: Literal['1'] = '1'  # future-proofing
    types: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)  # Pydantic model definitions
    construct: SpecConstruct
```

Loader becomes:

```python
def load(source: str | dict | Path) -> Construct:
    raw = _parse_input(source)
    spec = Spec.model_validate(raw)  # rejects typos, missing fields, wrong types
    return _build_construct(spec.construct)  # typed walker
```

## Benefits

- Spec typos rejected at load time with field-path error
- Every builder reads `spec_node.name` (typed attr) instead of `spec.get('name')`
- JSON Schema exports cleanly for documentation (`Spec.model_json_schema()`)
- Spec versioning gates future-breaking changes
- Users discover valid fields via schema or via Pydantic error messages

## Breaking change surface

Users with correct specs unchanged. Users with typos in spec files newly fail at load time -- **this is a latent bug surfacing**. Users using undocumented spec fields (e.g., someone added a field the loader doesn't read) fail with 'extra_forbidden'; migration is to either declare the field in the schema or remove it.

Needs a migration grace period if consumers (piarch) have unknown fields in their specs. Options: publish the schema first, let consumers audit, then land `extra='forbid'` in a following release.

## Tests

- `test_typoed_field_raises_at_load` -- spec with `output_stratgy: json_mode` raises ValidationError with clear path
- `test_missing_required_field_raises_at_load` -- spec without `name` raises
- `test_valid_spec_loads_successfully` -- golden-path smoke
- `test_sub_construct_self_reference_valid` -- SpecConstruct.nodes contains SpecConstruct
- `test_json_schema_roundtrip` -- Spec.model_json_schema() produces valid schema; a serialized spec re-validates

## Effort

~2-3 days. Need to model the entire spec surface (Node, Construct, Modifier, Tool), thread SpecX types through the _build_* walkers, and coordinate the breaking change with piarch.

## Follow-on wins

- JSON Schema ships with the package; can publish at neograph.pro/schema.json for IDE integration
- `neograph check --spec path.yaml` becomes a standalone command (schema validation without needing Python types loaded)
- Spec diffing across versions becomes structured

## Dependencies

Child of ianf. Cleanest to land AFTER pej0 (so llm_config in specs can type to LlmConfig directly).

## Core Invariant

User pipeline specs (YAML/JSON) are parsed into typed Pydantic Spec models with extra='forbid' at load time, so typos and unknown fields surface as ValidationError with field-path context BEFORE any _build_* walker runs; the existing flat-list + string-ref structure is preserved (sub-constructs reference top-level node names, no recursive nesting); LlmConfig and other typed IR types are nested directly into the spec models so post-pej0 typed-config benefits flow into specs.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Red tests (TDD)

Add new test class TestSpecPydanticSchema in tests/test_spec_loader.py (or new tests/test_spec_pydantic.py if count grows):

1. test_typoed_top_level_field_raises -- spec with 'pipline' (typo of 'pipeline') raises ValidationError with field path
2. test_typoed_node_field_raises -- node spec with 'outpus' raises ValidationError pointing to the node name + bad field
3. test_typoed_modifier_field_raises -- oracle spec with 'merge_promp' raises
4. test_extra_field_in_oracle_block_raises -- oracle with unknown 'foo: bar' raises
5. test_missing_required_node_name_raises -- node spec without 'name' raises
6. test_unknown_loop_field_raises -- loop spec with 'when_expr' instead of 'when' raises
7. test_tools_field_now_consumed -- node spec with tools=['search'] produces Node(tools=[Tool('search')])
8. test_llm_config_typo_in_spec_raises -- llm_config={'max_retires': 5} raises (post-pej0 already does this; verify path)
9. test_valid_spec_loads_clean -- golden path; the existing test_spec_loader.py specs all stay green
10. test_spec_pydantic_class_exposes_json_schema -- Spec.model_json_schema() produces a dict with 'type': 'object'
11. test_construct_nodes_must_be_strings -- ConstructSpec(nodes=[NodeSpec(...)]) raises (recursive form rejected)
12. test_unknown_field_at_root_raises -- spec with 'foo: bar' at root raises

### Phase 2: Define Pydantic schema in src/neograph/_spec_schema.py

```python
from typing import Any, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
from neograph._llm_config import LlmConfig

# Modifier specs (Oracle merge_pre_process etc Callables NOT addressable from YAML)

class OracleSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    n: int | None = None
    models: list[str] | None = None
    merge_fn: str | None = None
    merge_prompt: str | None = None
    merge_model: str = 'reason'

class EachSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    over: str
    key: str

class LoopSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    when: str
    max_iterations: int = 10
    on_exhaust: Literal['error', 'last'] = 'error'

class OperatorSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    when: str

class NodeSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    mode: Literal['think', 'agent', 'act', 'scripted', 'raw'] = 'scripted'
    inputs: str | dict[str, str] | None = None
    outputs: str
    prompt: str | None = None
    model: str | None = None
    scripted_fn: str | None = None
    context: list[str] | None = None
    llm_config: LlmConfig = Field(default_factory=LlmConfig)
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    oracle: OracleSpec | None = None
    each: EachSpec | None = None
    loop: LoopSpec | None = None
    operator: OperatorSpec | None = None

class ConstructSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    input: str
    output: str
    nodes: list[str]  # string references to top-level NodeSpec.name (NOT recursive)
    oracle: OracleSpec | None = None
    each: EachSpec | None = None
    loop: LoopSpec | None = None
    operator: OperatorSpec | None = None

class PipelineRef(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    nodes: list[str]

class Spec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    description: str = ''
    types: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    nodes: list[NodeSpec] = Field(default_factory=list)
    constructs: list[ConstructSpec] = Field(default_factory=list)
    pipeline: PipelineRef
```

### Phase 3: Rewire loader.py to use Spec

1. _validate_spec becomes:
   ```python
   def _validate_spec(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Spec:
       try:
           return Spec.model_validate(raw)
       except ValidationError as exc:
           raise ConfigurationError.build('invalid spec', hint=str(exc)) from exc
   ```

2. load_spec pipeline:
   ```python
   raw = _parse_input(source)
   spec = _validate_spec(raw)
   if project: load_project_types(project, raw.get('types', {}))
   else: load_project_types(None, raw.get('types', {}))
   return _build_construct(spec)
   ```

3. _build_construct, _build_node, _build_sub_construct, _apply_modifiers signatures change from dict[str, Any] to Spec / NodeSpec / ConstructSpec / OracleSpec etc. Each .get() becomes attribute access.

4. _parse_llm_config becomes redundant -- llm_config is already typed in NodeSpec. Delete or simplify.

5. tools field: in _build_node, after constructing the Node, look up each tool name and pass to Node.tools=[Tool(name) for name in node_spec.tools]. CLOSES THE SILENT-DROP BUG.

6. Drop jsonschema dependency from _validate_spec. Document removal in changelog.

### Phase 4: Tests must stay green

- All ~80 tests in test_spec_loader.py must pass.
- test_spec_schema.py tests against the hand-written JSON schema -- decide whether to:
  (a) Keep hand-written schema and update it to match Pydantic shape, OR
  (b) Auto-generate from Spec.model_json_schema() in a one-time script.
  Decision: (a) -- keep hand-written for now to avoid scope creep; tighten it to match Pydantic semantics. Auto-generation is a follow-up.
- test_spec_types.py untouched.

### Phase 5: Quality gate

make quality:
- 1688 + ~12 new tests = ~1700 minimum green
- Ruff clean, Mypy clean

### Phase 6: Implement tools field

In _build_node, after constructing the Node, resolve each tool name. The tools list is already in NodeSpec via tools: list[str]. Convert via Tool(name=name). Add a test that asserts agent-mode node with tools=['search'] reaches Node.tools.

### Acceptance gates

- TestSpecPydanticSchema: 12 red tests turn green
- All 1688 existing tests stay green
- _parse_llm_config simplified or removed
- tools field consumed (closes silent-drop bug)
- Spec / NodeSpec / ConstructSpec / OracleSpec / EachSpec / LoopSpec / OperatorSpec / PipelineRef live in src/neograph/_spec_schema.py
- jsonschema dependency removed (or made truly optional with no warning emission)
- mypy clean
- ruff clean

### Out of scope

- Auto-generated JSON schema from model_json_schema() (separate follow-up)
- Recursive sub-construct nesting (format change, not in bha9)
- CLI integration (neograph check pipeline.yaml is a future enhancement)
- Loop.history support (unrelated)
- Oracle merge hooks via spec (callables can't be serialized)
notes:
## Findings (research atom e51n.2)

### Loader public surface

- load_spec(source, project=None) -> Construct (loader.py:35-58)
- Pipeline: _parse_input -> _validate_spec (jsonschema-based) -> optional load_project_types -> _build_construct
- _build_construct (loader.py:109-146) builds nodes + sub-constructs flat lists, then orders per spec.pipeline.nodes
- _build_node (loader.py:161-192) -- already calls _parse_llm_config which uses LlmConfig (post-pej0)
- _build_sub_construct (loader.py:195-243) -- resolves input/output, wires per-node inputs
- _apply_modifiers (loader.py:246-280) -- oracle/each/loop/operator
- _parse_llm_config (loader.py:149-158) -- already typed (post-pej0)

### Spec dict shape (every .get() call)

**Root spec**:
- spec.get('nodes', []) -- node defs
- spec.get('constructs', []) -- sub-construct defs
- spec['pipeline']['nodes'] -- required, ordered references
- spec['name'] -- required
- spec.get('description', '')

**Node spec** (12 fields):
- name (required), mode (default 'scripted'), outputs (required)
- inputs, prompt, model, scripted_fn, context (all optional, None default)
- llm_config (already typed via _parse_llm_config)
- tools -- IGNORED BY LOADER even though JSON schema accepts it (real bug)

**Construct spec**:
- name, input, output, nodes (all required)

**Modifier specs**:
- Oracle: optional n, models, merge_fn, merge_prompt, merge_model
- Each: required over, key
- Loop: required when (parsed via parse_condition), optional max_iterations=10, on_exhaust='error'
- Operator: required when (registered name, NOT parsed)

### IMPORTANT structural reality (contradicts task design)

The task description proposes `SpecConstruct.nodes: list[SpecNode | SpecConstruct]` (recursive nesting). REALITY:
- Spec.nodes: list[NodeSpec] (top-level, FLAT)
- Spec.constructs: list[ConstructSpec] (top-level, FLAT)
- ConstructSpec.nodes: list[str] (string references back to top-level nodes)
- Spec.pipeline.nodes: list[str] (string references)

Sub-constructs share the global node pool BY REFERENCE, not by containment. Recursive nesting is a FORMAT CHANGE, not a schema migration. Stick with the current flat-with-string-refs structure for bha9.

### Existing _validate_spec

- loader.py:92-103. Best-effort jsonschema.validate against schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json.
- Skips silently if schema file missing or jsonschema not installed (warns).
- All real validation happens at _build_* phases (KeyError, ConfigurationError, ValidationError for llm_config).

### JSON Schemas (hand-written today)

- src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json (213 lines)
- src/neograph/schemas/project.neograph.schema.json (119 lines)
- No model_json_schema() exporter exists anywhere in src/
- Hand-written schema is more permissive than the post-pej0 LlmConfig (additionalProperties: true on llm_config block)

### Documentation gaps to close

- tools field on Node spec: docs advertise it (spec-format.mdx:53,67-68,180-181), JSON schema accepts it, _build_node IGNORES it. extra='forbid' on Pydantic schema either fixes (implement tools) or fails loudly. RECOMMENDATION: implement tools resolution as part of bha9.
- Loop.history: IR supports, JSON schema does not, loader does not.
- Oracle merge hooks (merge_pre_process etc): Callables, deliberately not addressable from YAML.

### Existing tests

- tests/test_spec_loader.py (1054 lines, 16 test classes, ~80 tests). Comprehensive coverage of: minimal/full pipelines, oracle, each, loop, sub-constructs, YAML/JSON, size limits, error paths, immutability, multi-node sub-constructs.
- tests/test_spec_schema.py (348 lines). Tests JSON schema validation directly.
- tests/test_spec_types.py (333 lines). Type registry.
- NO test for typo-rejection (e.g., 'outpus' instead of 'outputs') -- the bug class bha9 closes.
- NO YAML/JSON spec fixtures on disk -- all specs are inline dicts.

### piarch impact (zero direct evidence in repo)

- No piarch/ directory in this repo.
- Only signal: website docs at website/src/content/docs/concepts/spec-format.mdx.
- A typo-rejection regression for piarch would be: any spec with a typoed field newly raises ValidationError at load. Acceptable per project's '0.x breaking changes are fine' policy.

### CLI

- src/neograph/__main__.py is module-not-spec oriented (neograph check <module>, neograph test-scaffold <module>).
- No CLI entry point currently consumes specs. bha9 doesn't change this; future enhancement (neograph check pipeline.yaml) would benefit.

### Risks / Edge cases

1. **JSON schema drift after Pydantic-ization**. The hand-written schema must either be regenerated from Spec.model_json_schema() or kept in sync. Cleanest: replace _validate_spec's jsonschema delegation entirely with Spec.model_validate(spec); auto-generate the JSON schema via a build script for non-Python consumers.

2. **Recursive nesting is NOT current shape**. Stick with flat lists + string references. Schema models:
   - Spec(name, description, types, pipeline: PipelineRef, nodes: list[NodeSpec], constructs: list[ConstructSpec])
   - PipelineRef(nodes: list[str])
   - NodeSpec(name, mode, inputs, outputs, prompt, model, scripted_fn, context, llm_config: LlmConfig, tools: list[str], oracle: OracleSpec | None, each: EachSpec | None, loop: LoopSpec | None, operator: OperatorSpec | None)
   - ConstructSpec(name, input, output, nodes: list[str], oracle/each/loop/operator)
   - OracleSpec, EachSpec, LoopSpec, OperatorSpec (one per modifier with their fields)

3. **Tool field implementation**. Either implement (read tools from node spec, pass to Node()) or extra='forbid' surfaces the gap. Implement is the right call -- the docs already advertise it.

4. **llm_config inside spec**. Already a LlmConfig at runtime (_parse_llm_config). In schema: type as LlmConfig directly. Pydantic handles dict coercion.

5. **inputs/outputs as type names (strings) vs resolved types**. Loader resolves via lookup_type at _build_* time. Schema field type: `str | dict[str, str] | None` (string-form name + dict-form for fan-in). Resolution stays at the build phase.

6. **Deprecation**: jsonschema dependency becomes optional/removable. Pydantic owns validation entirely.

7. **JSON Schema export**. Add a build script (e.g., scripts/regen_schema.py) that runs Spec.model_json_schema() and writes schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json, OR embed the schema in CI/pre-commit. Out of scope for bha9 unless the task explicitly requires keeping the JSON file alive. The task doesn't require it -- mention as follow-up.

### Three-surface coverage check

Spec loader is a SINGLE-SURFACE feature -- there's no @node / declarative / programmatic split. It's the YAML/JSON entry point only. Three-surface rule does not apply.

def _resolve_tool(t: str | ToolSpec) -> Tool:
    if isinstance(t, str):
        spec = ToolSpec(name=t)
    else:

    if spec.name not in registry.tool_factory:
        raise ConfigurationError.build(
            f"unknown tool {spec.name!r}",
            hint="register the tool factory via register_tool_factory()",
        )
    return Tool(name=spec.name, budget=spec.budget, config=spec.config)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-e9zse.2
description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-e9zse.2` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-e9zse.2/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.2
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-e9zse.2)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.2 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.2 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-e9zse.2/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.2 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-e9zse.2/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-e9zse.2
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-e9zse.2
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.2`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-e9zse.2)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.2 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.2 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-e9zse.1
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-e9zse.1
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.1`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-e9zse.1)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.1 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.1 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Audit and fix 13 bare except Exception handlers across src/
description:
## Problem
13 bare `except Exception` handlers across src/neograph/*.py. These suppress real errors, making debugging impossible when things go wrong silently.

## Inventory (13 sites)

### Category 1: get_type_hints fallbacks (6 sites) — NARROW the exception
These catch failures from `typing.get_type_hints()` which can raise NameError, AttributeError, TypeError, or RecursionError on malformed annotations. Should catch `(NameError, AttributeError, TypeError)` instead of bare Exception.
- _construct_validation.py:580
- _di_classify.py:155
- _sidecar.py:116
- decorators.py:404
- decorators.py:465
- decorators.py:658

### Category 2: Best-effort diagnostics (3 sites) — ADD structlog.warning
These are genuinely best-effort (frame walk, graph visualization, dev-mode print). The except Exception is acceptable but should log the swallowed error via structlog.warning so it's visible in debug mode.
- _construct_validation.py:759 (_source_location frame walk)
- compiler.py:265 (describe_graph)
- compiler.py:274 (_print_dag_summary)

### Category 3: Genuinely wrong (3 sites) — FIX
- _llm.py:82 — cost callback inner: except Exception: pass — should catch specific exceptions or at minimum log
- _llm.py:84 — cost callback outer: except Exception: pass — same
- _sidecar.py:103 — lookup_scripted: silently returns None instead of propagating ConfigurationError

### Category 4: Correct (1 site) — NO CHANGE
- _llm.py:368 — except Exception as exc: raise ExecutionError(...) — wraps and re-raises, correct pattern

## Fix
1. Category 1: Replace `except Exception` with `except (NameError, AttributeError, TypeError)`
2. Category 2: Add `log.warning('swallowed_error', exc=str(e))` inside the handler
3. Category 3: Fix the actual logic — cost callback should catch specific exceptions, lookup_scripted should propagate
4. Add structural guard test: no bare `except Exception: pass` in src/
