title: Codebase-wide disease scan for pt85t
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show pt85t` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/pt85t/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" pt85t
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (pt85t)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update pt85t --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update pt85t --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/pt85t/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add pt85t codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/pt85t/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). title: Implement e3b4j
description:
Implement beads task e3b4j -- make the failing test pass (TDD green),
then refactor.

## Workflow

1. **Green**: Write minimum code to make the failing test pass
2. **Verify**: Run the SAME test that FAILED -- must now PASS
3. **Refactor**: With passing tests as safety net
4. **Quality gate**: Run project quality command

## When EXISTING Tests Fail

1. STOP. Do NOT modify the failing tests.
2. Re-read the Core Invariant.
3. If your approach violates the invariant -> revert and rethink.
4. If the test has a genuine bug -> document WHY before modifying.

Sacred rule: NEVER adjust tests to match code without justification.

## If Successful

Close the original beads task:
```bash
bd close e3b4j
```

title: Refine 2aw5c per review
description:
Resolve the architect review's 3 MEDIUM findings on neograph-2aw5c (Portal mode-b max_depth budget), using EXISTING research -- do NOT re-research.

MEDIUM 1: Pin a single FLAT StateKeys.PORTAL_DISPATCH_DEPTH config key (no per-field variant). Per-field keying (like handoff_hops) is WRONG here: depth is a lineage property spanning FRESH compiled sub-flows per nesting level, not a per-node state-bus channel. A per-field key would reset to 0 at every nesting level and silently defeat the budget. Explicitly reject per-field keying in the design.

MEDIUM 2: Make max_depth REQUIRED in dispatch mode (no default value) rather than picking an arbitrary default like 5 -- mirrors the existing dispatch-mode 'requires spec_field/input_field/output' guard (modifiers.py:677-683) and stays consistent with the North-star fail-loud principle (no silent arbitrary numeric bound). Breaking changes are fine at 0.x (sole user piarch, no compat shims needed).

MEDIUM 3: Fix the check-placement inconsistency. _prepare (factory.py:534) receives NO config, so the plan's 'read depth in _prepare' step is impossible as written. Perform the depth read + max_depth check in dispatch_wrapper/adispatch_wrapper (factory.py:613,619) at the very TOP, BEFORE inner.invoke(state, config) runs -- this is strictly louder AND cheaper (fails before the sub-flow spec is even validated/compiled, avoiding a wasted planner LLM call). Build the incremented child config via shallow-copy (config + configurable), mirroring runner.py:196's copy-not-mutate pattern, and pass it into compiled.invoke/ainvoke.

Also note (LOW, non-blocking): the exhaustion test must be a runtime pytest test (ExecutionError during invoke), NOT a tests/check_fixtures/should_fail fixture (those are compile-time only).

Update the design field on 2aw5c with the refined plan (flat StateKeys, required max_depth, wrapper-level check placement) before write-test proceeds.

title: Refine 4pr04 per review
description:

MEDIUM 1 (wiring): The plan's Command-wiring is wrong. _add_portal_dispatch does NOT know next_node, and mixing a static success out-edge with a Command(goto=error_handler) error path double-routes (LangGraph fires static edges regardless of a returned Command). Fix: mirror _add_portal_mesh exactly -- create a pass-through continuation node (e.g. __dispatch_exit_<node>) up front, have the SUCCESS path ALSO return Command(goto=<exit>), register destinations=(exit_name, error_handler), and return exit_name from the wiring function so the compiler's linear-thread walk picks up the continuation. Never mix a static out-edge with Command on the same node.

MEDIUM 2 (payload contract): Pin the error-handler payload field explicitly -- use a StateKeys helper (mirroring handoff_payload/handoff_hops at _state_keys.py:130-139) or an explicit fingerprinted state field, decide whether it coexists with the {node}_dispatch field (not written on the error path), and carry spec_name + gate_error message (mirroring ExecutionError.build(construct=, found=)). Document the field name/shape.

MEDIUM 3 (validation site): Do NOT extend _check_portal_mesh -- it deliberately excludes dispatch-mode portals and returns early with no peer members, so a dispatch-only construct never reaches it. Add a SEPARATE dispatch-validation helper for error_handler sibling-existence, and confirm it is actually invoked from _validate_node_chain for dispatch-only constructs.

MEDIUM 4 (fixtures): Step 2 adds a NEW assembly validation rule (error_handler must name a sibling Node) -- per AGENTS.md's rule, add BOTH a should_fail fixture (route_to_error with missing/non-existent error_handler, # CHECK_ERROR: regex) and a should_pass fixture under tests/check_fixtures/.

Update the design field on 4pr04 with the refined plan (correct Command wiring, payload field shape, separate validation helper, fixture additions) before write-test proceeds.

title: Refine a37vk per review
description:

Pin it to FLATTEN: for each member, build 'bare_node | Portal(...)' and tracer.record() it DIRECTLY into the ForwardConstruct's own _ordered list -- do NOT wrap members in a Construct(...) and do NOT call record_construct(). Nesting would produce Construct(nodes=[Construct(nodes=[...])]), one level deeper than the declarative target (examples/28_portal_swarm.py demo_surface_parity: Construct(nodes=[triage|Portal, billing|Portal])), violating the 'IDENTICAL IR' Core Invariant and inserting an unnecessary subgraph boundary that Command(goto=<peer>) would have to cross.

The entry member (first recorded, or the explicit entry= kwarg) gets Portal(to=to[entry], max_hops=max_hops, on_exhaust=on_exhaust); every non-entry member gets Portal(to=to[name]) with NO max_hops/on_exhaust keyword passed at all.

title: Refine kdr1u per review
description:

MEDIUM 1 (missing combo-classification plumbing): Lifting the reciprocal Operator<->Portal excludes in modifiers.py alone is insufficient. title: Sweep verification for e3b4j
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on e3b4j
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" e3b4j`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (e3b4j)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update e3b4j --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add e3b4j sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.
close_reason: Sweep verified: 2 pre-existing ALLOWLIST examples unchanged, 1 new example added as the intended deliverable (not a regression). N/A guard requirement recorded (all-ALLOWLIST Phase 1b table).

title: §4: Split factory.py god-module into responsibility-aligned modules
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4 (Module and function responsibilities).

**Problem**: `factory.py` at 631 lines mixes six named responsibilities:
- factory construction (`make_node_fn`, `make_subgraph_fn`)
- state I/O (`_state_get`, `_build_state_update`)
- modifier I/O (`_extract_input`, `_apply_skip_when`)
- oracle plumbing (`_inject_oracle_config`, `make_oracle_redirect_fn` re-export)
- observability (`_extract_context`)
- skip logic

The structural guards at `tests/test_structural_guards.py:84-107` exist *because* this stuff drifts back. If you need an AST guard saying "don't put `make_oracle_redirect_fn` in `factory.py`", the boundary is too leaky.

**Fix**: split `factory.py` into responsibility-aligned modules. Suggested layout:
- `factory.py` — node-function construction (`make_node_fn`, `make_subgraph_fn`) only; one named responsibility
- `_state_io.py` — `_state_get*`, `_build_state_update`
- `_modifier_io.py` — `_extract_input`, `_apply_skip_when`
- `_observability.py` — `_extract_context`
- Oracle plumbing stays in `_oracle.py`

Each new module gets a one-line docstring stating its single responsibility (§4 rule). The existing structural guards in `test_structural_guards.py:84-107` get rewritten or removed once the boundaries are no longer ambiguous.

**Cross-dependency**: this should ship AFTER the Protocol extractions (the cycle break-up tickets in this epic). Doing it before is mechanically harder.

**Acceptance**: `factory.py` is well under 300 lines and has one named responsibility. Existing AST guards against "function X must not live in factory.py" are deleted (no longer needed).

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestFactoryResponsibilityDiscipline` (new test class) plus the full existing test suite as behavioral regression.
**Test type**: structural-guard + behavioral-integration
**What it exercises**: (a) AST-scan `src/neograph/factory.py` and assert it defines ONLY the public factory-construction names (`make_node_fn`, `make_subgraph_fn`), with all other names confined to their new homes (`_state_io.py`, `_modifier_io.py`, `_observability.py`). (b) Assert `factory.py` line count is under 300. (c) The existing test_structural_guards.py:84-107 guards are deleted as part of this ticket (the test confirms they are gone). (d) Full test suite remains green — proves refactor is behavior-preserving.
**Expected initial state**: failing — `factory.py` is 631 lines with six responsibilities today.
**Persistence**: new responsibility-discipline guard stays in suite; replaces the deleted ad-hoc guards.

Order: write the failing structural guard FIRST → run it → must fail → split the module → run all tests + new guard → must pass.
close_reason: factory.py split into 4 responsibility-aligned modules: factory.py (290 lines, was 601 — only make_node_fn, make_subgraph_fn, _make_raw_wrapper, _execute_node, _type_name), _state_io.py (101 lines: _build_state_update, _inject_oracle_config), _modifier_io.py (201 lines: _apply_skip_when, _extract_input + shape dispatch + InputShape enum), _observability.py (24 lines: _extract_context). Each new module carries a one-line docstring stating its single responsibility. Ad-hoc factory→_dispatch/_oracle drift guards at tests/test_structural_guards.py:96-106 deleted; new TestFactoryResponsibilityDiscipline (3 tests: whitelist enforcement, line budget, docstring presence) replaces them. Tests reaching factory.py internals get backward-compat re-exports with noqa: F401. Full suite: 1783 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean.

title: Cross-superstep MCP connection reuse WITH transparent reconnect (ReAct loop reconnects every turn today)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: within a run, an agent/act ReAct loop reuses ONE live MCP connection per server across its N supersteps instead of reconnecting every turn — BUT the cache MUST transparently RECONNECT when the cached connection is absent or dead. 'Reuse' is an optimization layered over a reconnect-capable path, NEVER an assumption a connection survives.

WHY (maintainer, 2026-07-10): a HITL interrupt can pause the ReAct loop mid-flight; on resume the run continues from the same step, possibly in a DIFFERENT PROCESS, where no live connection exists. Today each superstep re-invokes the factory, which rebuilds a MultiServerMCPClient and reconnects every turn (nmb2: client owned inside the factory). An 8-turn agent pays 8 connects; but naive caching would hand a resumed run a dead handle.

SCOPE: extend _run_cache (RUN_ID-keyed, already caches the LLM handle + tool instances + FromResource fetch, evicted at run end) to memoize the CONNECTED client per (run, server). On resume RUN_ID is fresh -> cache miss -> transparent reconnect (verify this holds and that a stale/dead cached handle never surfaces as a hang or use-after-close). Preserve nmb2 (client stays consumer-owned, cached in the config-scoped cache, not neograph core) and per-run identity (reconnect re-mints identity from config via token_provider).

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT cache a raw socket/session that can go stale silently — the cache path must lazily rebuild on miss OR failed reuse, so a dead connection triggers reconnect, not a hang.

ACCEPTANCE: an N-turn agent against the demo server does 1 connect not N (assert connect count); an interrupt/resume MID-LOOP reconnects cleanly and completes; a killed/dead cached connection triggers transparent reconnect (no hang); per-run identity preserved across reconnect. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant (REFRAMED per maintainer decision 2026-07-10 + deep research docs/design/mcp-connection-reuse-2026-07-10.md)
Connection reuse is CONSUMER-HELD and OPT-IN: a battery async CM (mcp_run_context) opened by the consumer AROUND arun()/astream() holds one live session per server for the whole run — opened AND closed in the consumer's single long-lived task (the only disposal the task-affine cancel scopes allow; spike-proven) — while supersteps' tool calls ride it from their own tasks (spike-proven safe). Without the CM, the factory falls back UNCHANGED to the adapter's documented stateless per-call default — reuse is an optimization layered over the reconnect-capable path, never an assumption a connection survives. nmb2 strengthened: the consumer literally owns the client/session lifecycle; neograph core untouched.

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW battery async CM in src/neograph_mcp (e.g. _run_context.py): `mcp_run_context(servers: dict[str, StdioServer|HttpServer], *, token_provider=None, config=None, stdio_token_arg='token', timeout=30.0)`. __aenter__: for each server, mint identity (SAME _resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config path) and open the adapter persistent session (_client_for(...).session(key)) — all in the caller's task; bounded by timeout (copy McpSession.__aenter__'s asyncio.timeout + _unwrap_single normalization). __aexit__: close every session in reverse (LIFO) order in the same task.
2. Config threading: ctx.config(base_config) (or a documented configurable key, mirroring RESOURCE_FETCHER_KEY) stashes a {server_key: live_session} map under a config-only StateKeys-style key. Never enters state/checkpoint (not serializable — same rule as McpSession).
3. EXTEND _make_tool_factory: at the top of the per-superstep _factory, check config for a held session for this server_key; if present, bind via load_mcp_tools(session=held) (skipping client build + connect) and apply the SAME post-steps in order (stdio token-inject -> rename -> _wrap_output_model). If absent (no CM, resumed run, dead entry) -> existing stateless path unchanged (transparent reconnect for free).
4. Per-run identity: minted at CM entry per server (consumer's config); factory identity injection unchanged (token from _resolve_token at factory time still governs stdio arg injection — document that http bearer rides the held connection minted at entry).
5. mcp_session (composite path) and mcp_resource_fetcher: OUT OF SCOPE (already consumer-owned per-body); note in docstring that mcp_run_context serves the FACTORY (agent/act) path.
6. Acceptance (revised): (a) an N-turn agent against the demo server under mcp_run_context does 1 connect not N (assert connect count via server-side or client_for call count); (b) the same pipeline WITHOUT the CM still passes (stateless fallback unchanged); (c) closing happens in the consumer task — no cancel-scope RuntimeError (the spike repro as a regression test shape); (d) a dead/absent held session falls back to reconnect, not a hang; (e) per-run identity rides both paths.
7. Export mcp_run_context via neograph_mcp __init__ __all__; docs note the opt-in pattern + when it matters (slow-spawn stdio; stateful servers) per docs/design/mcp-connection-reuse-2026-07-10.md.
8. Gates: extra-gated tests (importorskip), guard test_guards_mcp_session_ownership stays green (all in battery), mypy/ruff/full pytest.
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher, 2026-07-10)

### The REUSE target already exists: McpSession persistent-session mode
- `McpSession` / `mcp_session()` in **src/neograph_mcp/_session.py** IS the 'connect ONCE, call N tools over one connection' primitive. It wraps the adapter's PERSISTENT session mode (`client.session()` -> one live ClientSession, then N `session.call_tool()`), the exact opposite of the bound-tool path. This is the connected-per-server object the task wants memoized. Do NOT build a new persistent-connection type — reuse McpSession (or its underlying `_client_for(...).session(server_key)`).
- The per-run cache seam already exists: **src/neograph/_run_cache.py** `aget_or_build(config, subkey, build)` + `evict_run(run_id)`. It ALREADY memoizes the LLM handle and the consumer tool instances per RUN_ID (`tools:{node_name}`, _tool_loop.py:472/518) and is evicted in every runner verb finally (runner.py `_evict_run_cache`, 4 sites). RUN_ID is re-minted on resume => cache MISS => transparent rebuild is ALREADY the structural contract (docstring §1). The 'fresh RUN_ID on resume' half of the ask is free.

### Why it reconnects every turn today (the current, not-deprecated path)
- The bound-tool ReAct path uses the STATELESS adapter model: neograph_mcp `_make_tool_factory._factory` (_client.py:274) builds a fresh `MultiServerMCPClient` and calls `client.get_tools()`; those adapter tools open+close a NEW session PER `tool.ainvoke()` ('disposed by the adapter's stateless-per-call session model', _client.py:267). The FACTORY result is already per-run cached, so the factory runs once — but each of the N tool CALLS across the N ReAct supersteps still connects. N turns = N connects. To reach '1 connect', the factory must return tools bound to a PERSISTENT session (adapter `load_mcp_tools(session=<live session>)`) whose session is the cached-per-(run,server) object.
- Agent/act supersteps drive through _agent_cycle.py `_abuild_turn_prep` -> _tool_loop.py `_aprepare_tool_loop` -> `aget_or_build('tools:{node}', _ainstantiate_tools)`. That is where a session-bound variant would hook.

### Ownership boundary (nmb2 — LOCKED, do not reopen)
- src/neograph owns NO MCP session lifecycle. Enforced by tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py, which scans ONLY src/neograph (SRC_DIR) and bans `ClientSession`, `MultiServerMCPClient`, `langchain_mcp_adapters`, `.session(`, `import mcp`. **src/neograph_mcp is EXEMPT** — the client/session cache + reconnect + disposal MUST live in neograph_mcp, never in core. Verdict doc: docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:193-345 (McpSession) — persistent one-connection-N-calls primitive to REUSE; note the same-task/never-store constraints it documents.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:252-292 (_make_tool_factory) — the reconnect-per-call factory to CONVERT to session-bound tools.
- src/neograph/_run_cache.py:138-171 (aget_or_build / evict_run) — the per-run cache + eviction seam to memoize the connected session on.
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:487-522 (_aprepare_tool_loop) — where tool instances are per-run cached; the integration point.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:182-201 (_abuild_turn_prep) — per-superstep entry that rebuilds the preamble each turn.
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:141-163 — stdio spawns a fresh subprocess per session (connect == subprocess spawn); the acceptance 'count connects' assertion hangs off this.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **LOAD-BEARING RISK — anyio cancel-scope task-affinity.** A live `client.session()` / McpSession enters an anyio cancel scope + background reader task group at connect; McpSession's own docstring (_session.py:19-23) states it MUST be entered AND exited in the SAME task ('crossing tasks fails loudly with a RuntimeError'). LangGraph runs each superstep's node body as a SEPARATE asyncio task, so a session opened in turn 1's task and reused/closed from turn 3's task risks a RuntimeError or use-after-close. This is the crux the task's 'no hang / no use-after-close' clause is really about, and it is UNVERIFIED. A spike must confirm whether the adapter's ClientSession tolerates cross-task call_tool + deferred close, or whether cross-superstep reuse is fundamentally blocked (forcing option: run the whole ReAct loop in one node body/task, which trades away the per-turn HITL-interrupt checkpoint granularity that is the task's WHY).
- **Disposal gap.** `evict_run` (src/neograph/_run_cache.py:158) is SYNC and only deletes dict entries — it never calls `__aexit__`. The currently-cached values (LLM handle, stateless tool instances, resource data) need no async close. A cached LIVE session would be DROPPED without closing => leaked connection / orphaned stdio subprocess, and closing it here would be (a) from the wrong task and (b) in core, tripping the ownership guard. A new async run-end disposal hook owned by neograph_mcp is required; there is no existing seam.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the task SCOPE says 'extend _run_cache' (core) but also 'client stays consumer-owned, cached in the config-scoped cache, NOT neograph core'. Those pull opposite ways: the cache MECHANISM is core (src/neograph/_run_cache.py) yet a cached live session + its disposal are session-lifecycle, which the ownership guard forbids in core. Resolution likely = neograph_mcp imports the run-cache seam (new battery->core private-module dependency; today neograph_mcp imports NOTHING from core) OR a public disposal-hook seam is added. Maintainer should confirm the intended coupling before implementation.
- 'Dead cached connection => transparent reconnect' needs an explicit liveness path: a cached session whose transport died must be detected (transport error on call, NOT an isError result) and trigger drop-entry+reopen, distinct from uixi1's retry-on-transport-error. Do not conflate with McpToolCallError (isError), which must NOT reconnect.
- Acceptance instrumentation: no connect-counter exists yet. Prereq bead neograph-32qtx (FakeMcpSession + fake factory) lands first per the epic's maintainer-set order and is the clean vehicle for the 'N-turn agent => 1 connect' assertion without a live subprocess.
## Codebase Disease Scan (cnxlx)
Pattern: reconnect-every-turn — the stateless per-call `client.get_tools(server_name=...)` in the bound-tool factory rebuilds+reconnects a client each superstep instead of riding one cached connected session.
Scan command: grep -rn 'get_tools(server_name' src/neograph_mcp/ ; grep -rn 'aget_or_build|evict_run' src/neograph/_run_cache.py
Total instances found: 2 get_tools sites; run-cache reuse seam confirmed present.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:277 | _make_tool_factory per-run _factory: client.get_tools(...) | MIGRATE | tool-EXECUTION path — bind tools to the (run,server)-cached connected session via _run_cache.aget_or_build so N ReAct calls ride 1 connection (design steps 2-4) |
| 2 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:203 | _discover_tool_names: client.get_tools(...) | ALLOWLIST | identity-agnostic NAME discovery only — one-shot listing, not the per-turn hot path; caching it would not change the connect-count acceptance |

Reuse target CONFIRMED: neograph._run_cache.aget_or_build (:138) + evict_run (:158) exist. SYNTACTIC scan sufficient.
NOTE: overlaps fflpt at the SAME line (:277). Molecule order = cnxlx BEFORE fflpt, so fflpt's progress-callback wiring must integrate with cnxlx's cached-session binding. BLOCKED pending spike + maintainer decision (NEEDS_USER_INPUT — see research).
## Architect Review (dp-reviewer, 2026-07-10)

Gate hard-check PASS: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. All three researcher-flagged concerns verified against source; all three are REAL and correctly framed. The plan itself is well-constructed (reuses McpSession — no new class; respects nmb2; spike-first sequencing; ties acceptance to FakeMcpSession from prereq 32qtx). The uncertainty is genuine, not a plan defect.

- [HIGH] Finding: anyio cancel-scope task-affinity (concern 1) is REAL and load-bearing. _session.py:18-23 EXPLICITLY documents the session MUST be entered AND exited in the SAME task ('crossing tasks fails loudly with a RuntimeError'). The Core Invariant '1 live connection reused across N supersteps' presumes the session survives task boundaries — the very thing the code says it cannot. If LangGraph runs each superstep as a distinct asyncio task (the spike's unproven premise), cross-superstep reuse trips RuntimeError. Correctly framed as spike-gated + maintainer-escalation: the fallback (scope session to ONE tools-node execution) would degrade acceptance from '1 connect per run' to '1 connect per turn's batch', contradicting the ticket's own ACCEPTANCE and its per-turn-HITL-checkpoint WHY. That reconciliation needs human direction. Suggestion: run design-step-1 spike as an isolated experiment BEFORE any production code; do not implement steps 3-6 until it resolves. Escalate the acceptance/WHY tension to the maintainer if cross-task reuse fails.

- [HIGH] Finding: no async run-end disposal seam (concern 3) is REAL and shares concern 1's root cause. Verified: evict_run (_run_cache.py:158-171) is SYNC and only deletes dict entries — no __aexit__; _evict_run_cache (runner.py:698) is sync, called from BOTH sync and async verbs' finally. A cached LIVE session dropped without __aexit__ leaks the connection / orphans the stdio subprocess. Reinforcing trap: the async verb's finally runs in the DRIVER task, not the superstep task that opened the session, so centralized __aexit__ there trips the SAME cross-task RuntimeError. So reuse AND centralized disposal both hinge on the one unproven task-affinity premise — if it fails, the whole cross-run-persistence approach collapses to McpSession's already-documented 'session lives within one node body' contract. Suggestion: gate the disposal-hook design on the spike outcome; the neograph_mcp-owned async hook is only viable if the session is task-portable OR the hook fires in the opening task.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: 'extend _run_cache (core)' vs 'client stays consumer-owned, NOT core' (concern 2) is a REAL scope tension, correctly flagged. Verified: neograph_mcp imports NOTHING from core today (grep clean); the ownership guard scans ONLY src/neograph (SRC_DIR) and bans ClientSession/.session(/import mcp there — neograph_mcp is exempt. The cache MECHANISM (aget_or_build storing an opaque handle in a dict) does NOT trip the guard and is a clean core extension; only session LIFECYCLE (disposal) is core-forbidden — that half folds into the HIGH above. The genuinely new thing is the dependency EDGE: neograph_mcp -> neograph._run_cache (a private module) would be the FIRST battery->core import. Given the project's strong layering discipline, that edge warrants maintainer confirmation (or a public seam) — but a refine step could reasonably propose the public-seam option. Does not independently block; downgraded from the researcher's NEEDS_USER_INPUT framing to MEDIUM because the two HIGHs already gate the work and the mechanism/lifecycle split is clean.

- [LOW] Finding: line-collision with fflpt at _client.py:277 (disposition table row 1). Molecule order cnxlx-before-fflpt is correct, but the implementer must leave the session-bound factory shaped so fflpt's progress-callback wiring can integrate. Cosmetic sequencing note, already captured in the scan. Suggestion: none beyond honoring the stated order.

No materially-better approach was missed and no reuse-over-reinvention violation found — the plan already targets the existing McpSession primitive and the existing run-cache seam rather than building anew.

Overall: NEEDS_USER_INPUT
## Triage (neograph-5jrd0.13): NEEDS_USER_INPUT — blocked for maintainer. 2 HIGH: (1) cross-task session reuse safety (anyio cancel-scope task-affinity; docstring says crossing tasks RuntimeErrors); (2) no async run-end disposal seam (evict_run sync). Awaiting decision on spike-first vs per-tools-node-execution scope vs defer.
## MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-07-10): SPIKE FIRST, then decide.
Run a throwaway spike proving whether a cached adapter ClientSession opened in superstep 1 tolerates call_tool from a LATER superstep's asyncio task + deferred close. If SAFE -> implement full per-(run,server) reuse via _run_cache. If UNSAFE -> fall back to per-tools-node-execution batching (one connection per tools-node execution, batching a turn's parallel calls). No production code until the spike answers it. Implementation atom (.15) runs the spike as its first step and finalizes the design from the result.
## SPIKE RESULT (neograph-5jrd0.15, run against examples/_mcp_demo_server.py)
Ran: open adapter ClientSession in task A; call_tool from a DIFFERENT task B; __aexit__ from task C.
- cross-task CALL_TOOL: **OK** — a session opened in superstep 1 IS callable from a later superstep's asyncio task.
- cross-task CLOSE (__aexit__): **RAISES RuntimeError 'Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in'** — disposal is anyio-task-affine.

VERDICT: full per-(run,server) reuse is NOT safely disposable. neograph's run-end eviction (_run_cache.evict_run) is SYNC and runs from an arbitrary task/context; closing a cached MCP session there would raise the task-affinity RuntimeError (or leak the subprocess). The 'N-turn agent = 1 connect' acceptance cannot be met SAFELY via the whole-run cache.

DECISION (per maintainer pre-authorization 'if unsafe -> per-tools-node-execution batching'): scope the persistent session to ONE tools-node execution (one superstep = one task): within a superstep, all of that turn's tool calls to the same server ride ONE connection, opened AND closed in the SAME task (safe disposal). Reconnect per (turn, server), not per tool-call. Revised acceptance: a turn issuing K parallel calls to one server does 1 connect not K (assert within-turn connect count); open+call+close all in one task (no cross-task RuntimeError); per-run identity re-minted per turn from config. This is a SMALLER win than 1-per-run (the ticket's premise is retired by the spike) but is the safe, disposable optimization.
## FINAL DECISION (2026-07-10, post-research): consumer-held mcp_run_context async CM (opt-in reuse; stateless per-call stays default). Deep research persisted at docs/design/mcp-connection-reuse-2026-07-10.md (100-agent verified run: adapters default=per-call; pydantic-ai maintainer workaround=hold-open around run; OpenAI SDK owner-task only when no hold-open task exists — neograph HAS one, the consumer's arun task). This testing work surfaced and FIXED 4 real, previously-undetected bugs in already-shipped i3zsh/01i0g code (found only because these tests exercise actual compile+run, not just structural marker presence):

1. Each's MapNode never declared outputs= on export, and import read the (always-empty) MapNode.outputs instead of the wrapped inner node's real outputs -- every Each-modified node round-tripped with outputs=None, failing compile with 'node has no output type'. Fixed in both _agent_spec.py (no change needed, export already fine) and loader.py::_reconstruct_each_node (read inner.outputs instead of map_node.outputs).
2. Loop's inter-item DataFlowEdge wiring targeted the check/branch node (which _lower_loop never gives inputs/outputs Properties) instead of the wrapped body node -- any Loop-modified node with an external upstream producer failed Flow validation ('property named X... but the node does not have any property with that name'). Fixed via a new data_node concept threaded through _lower_construct_item (5-tuple return) and to_agent_spec's edge-wiring, plus loader.py::_reconstruct_loop_item's edge lookup switched from check_spec.name to body_spec.name.
3. Reconstructed types are freshly-synthesized per reconstruction call with NO identity link to the original class OR to each other, even when structurally identical -- causing (a) a self-loop's own output failing its own back-edge compatibility check ('output type X not compatible with reentry input Y') and (b) a nested object type appearing in two places (e.g. top-level and inside a list) reconstructing to two incompatible classes. Fixed by deriving the registry name PURELY from Property-list structure (spec_types._structural_type_name, sha256-based) instead of from node/model names, so register_type's existing content-match idempotency naturally reuses one class for every structurally-identical shape -- both at the top-level bridge (agent_spec_properties_to_types) and the nested ObjectProperty branch (previously a bare unregistered create_model call).
4. _reconstruct_primitive_node never read a SpecNode's OWN declared inputs Property list -- only DataFlowEdges -- so a self-contained node with no external upstream (e.g. Each's inner node, wired only via the fan-out mechanism, not a DataFlowEdge) silently got inputs=None. Fixed with a fallback: _inputs_from_data_edges(...) or _agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs).

Also added from_attributes=True to every reconstructed model (both the top-level bridge and the nested-object branch) so a REAL instance of the original class (which real scripted/think node bodies return, since they don't know about the freshly-synthesized reconstruction classes) validates correctly when crossing a reconstructed-Construct's state boundary.

NOT fixed (deferred, documented in the new test + neograph-aa5gq): _lower_oracle/_reconstruct_oracle_group unconditionally assume 'think' mode for Oracle variants regardless of the original node's mode -- a scripted-mode Oracle node round-trips into a broken think-mode reconstruction. The round-trip test uses think mode + FakeLLM (the currently-correct path) and documents the gap inline.

title: Stage C: render the lint-kind reference section from the enriched manifest
description: After neograph-uw54v enriches manifest lint_issue_kinds with severity/meaning + the DI kinds, render the api.mdx lint-kind table (Kind/Severity/Meaning) from the manifest using rfl7b's Stage-C rendering + freshness-guard infrastructure, and delete the hand-written table. Excluded from rfl7b itself (rfl7b keeps the lint section hand-written pending the enrichment).
design:
## Core Invariant
The api.mdx lint-kind Kind/Severity/Meaning table is manifest-OWNED: its every cell is rendered from LINT_KIND_META (via extract_lint_issue_kinds), lives verbatim inside a dedicated sentinel-delimited region, and is pinned byte-for-byte by a freshness guard -- there is no hand-authored copy that can drift.

## Implementation Plan
1. ADD render_lint_kind_table() -> str to scripts/gen_api_manifest.py, mirroring render_reference_sections()'s framing (leading + trailing '\n' so sentinel markers sit on their own lines). Source rows from extract_lint_issue_kinds() (already DONE). Emit a 3-col markdown table: header '| Kind | Severity | Meaning |' + separator, then one row per kind (already sorted by kind): '| `{kind}` | {severity} | {meaning} |'. Escape '|' -> '\|' in each meaning defensively. Reuse the _reference_field_table() row-building style.
2. ADD a dedicated section to website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx immediately after the GEN:reference-sections END sentinel (api.mdx:611) and before '## Guides' (:615): a '## Lint kinds' heading + intro sentence + a NEW sentinel pair (e.g. '{/* GEN:lint-kinds START */}' / '{/* GEN:lint-kinds END */}') whose enclosed body is the EXACT output of render_lint_kind_table(). Paste the render output between the markers. Do NOT place it inside the existing reference region.
3. ADD a freshness guard to tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py: define module constants LINT_KINDS_REGION_START/END for the new sentinels; add _extract_lint_kind_region(mdx_text) copied from _extract_reference_region (find()-based slice, asserts both markers present + ordered -- NO regex, so no PROC-2 slip meta-test needed); add a class TestLintKindTableRendering with test asserting _extract_lint_kind_region(API_MDX_PATH.read_text()) == gen.render_lint_kind_table() byte-for-byte, plus a hasattr(gen,'render_lint_kind_table') existence assert mirroring TestReferenceSectionRendering.
4. (Optional, cheap) Add a second test in that class asserting the rendered table contains exactly the 14 manifest kinds (set equality vs {e['kind'] for e in gen.extract_lint_issue_kinds()}) so a row dropped from the renderer fails loud.
5. Regenerate + verify: run render_lint_kind_table() to produce the region text, paste it, then run 'uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py' (guard must pass) and 'npm run build' in website/ (MDX must build).
6. Do NOT touch concepts/lint.mdx (7mr02). Do NOT modify render_reference_sections() or its region.
notes:
## Findings
- REUSE, don't rebuild. The enrichment is DONE: manifest 'lint_issue_kinds' already carries all 14 {kind,severity,meaning} objects (uw54v). Source of truth for severity/meaning is neograph.lint.LINT_KIND_META (dataclass LintKindMeta{severity,meaning} @ src/neograph/lint.py:67); the manifest emitter extract_lint_issue_kinds() (scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:414) already validates completeness + severity-drift and returns the sorted list. cvjfm only needs a RENDERER + a doc region + a freshness guard.
- EXEMPLAR to copy is kec0k's Stage-C trio: render_reference_sections() (gen_api_manifest.py:528) emits the exact text between {/* GEN:reference-sections START */}/END sentinels; _reference_field_table() (gen_api_manifest.py:518) is the markdown-table shape to mirror; the freshness guard TestReferenceSectionRendering.test_generated_reference_region_matches_render_reference_sections (tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:704) asserts committed-region == render() BYTE-FOR-BYTE, using _extract_reference_region() (line 647) which slices with str.find() on START/END literals (NO regex).
- CURRENT STATE CONFIRMED: api.mdx has NO 'Kind|Severity|Meaning' table (kec0k dropped it in the restructure). The '### lint' + '### LintIssue' sections (api.mdx:260-280) live INSIDE the single contiguous GEN:reference-sections region (api.mdx:53-611), which render_reference_sections() owns sorted-by-anchor. You CANNOT inject the kind-table inside that region without changing render_reference_sections(); add a SEPARATE section with its OWN sentinel pair instead.
- Regeneration is manual paste, not scripted: main() (gen_api_manifest.py:582) writes only the two JSON manifests; the mdx regions are hand-pasted from the render fn output and PINNED by the guard test. So the new region works the same way.
- Meanings are markdown with backticks and '--'; none currently contain a literal '|' pipe, but the renderer must escape '|' -> '\|' defensively so a future meaning can't break the table.
- DO NOT TOUCH concepts/lint.mdx:67 (the SECOND hand-written Kind|Severity|Meaning table, DI-kinds only, deferred to neograph-7mr02).

## Relevant Code
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:414 extract_lint_issue_kinds() -> list[{kind,severity,meaning}] -- the DONE data source; call it (or read build_manifest()['lint_issue_kinds']) in the new renderer.
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:518 _reference_field_table() -- markdown-table builder to mirror for the new render_lint_kind_table().

- Pipe escaping: meaning strings must have '|' escaped to '\|' in the renderer, else a future meaning silently corrupts the markdown table (guard would still catch drift, but the rendered table would be wrong-but-consistent).

title: _extract_json fallback heuristic is dead code (lines 278-282)
description:
The while True loop in _extract_json (_llm.py:239) can only exit via return statements (line 242 when no { found, line 273 when balanced JSON found). The fallback code at lines 278-282 (first-to-last brace heuristic) is unreachable dead code.

This means for unbalanced JSON that looks like a valid start (e.g. '{"key": "value with unmatched brace'), the function retries at pos+1 until it runs out of { characters, then returns text.strip() — never reaching the first-to-last fallback that was intended to handle this case.

Impact: Low. json_repair downstream handles most malformed cases. But the documented fallback behavior is a lie.

Location: src/neograph/_llm.py lines 278-282
close_reason: Invalid: lines 278-282 are covered (100% coverage on _llm.py). The fallback IS reachable — the agent's analysis was speculative.

title: Decorator parity: expose Oracle.merge_model and Loop.history as @node kwargs (merge_model=/loop_history=)
description: Under neograph-fsoss (doc bug), the architect found the website documented @node(merge_model=) and @node(loop_history=True) as first-class @node kwargs, but neither was EVER wired into the decorator (git -S/-G over decorators.py = empty; docs added ahead of impl in 07475e1). Both features exist ONLY on the programmatic modifiers: modifiers.Oracle.merge_model (str='reason') and modifiers.Loop.history (bool). fsoss fixes the DOCS to the programmatic surface. THIS bead tracks the product decision: should @node forward these two for three-surface parity? decorators.py already forwards loop_when/max_iterations/on_exhaust -> Loop(**kwargs) and ensemble_n/models/merge_fn/merge_prompt/hooks -> Oracle(**kwargs); adding loop_history->Loop(history=) and merge_model->Oracle(merge_model=) is small but requires three-surface parity tests + re-documenting the @node form. Decide: wire-for-parity (then re-add the @node-kwarg docs) vs keep programmatic-only.
design:
## Core Invariant
The @node decorator is pure sugar over the IR: any forwarded kwarg must map 1:1 onto an existing modifier field via the existing pipe sites with modifier defaults preserved (forward only when explicitly set) — no new IR, factory, or state capability, no @node-specific logic below decorators.py, and IDENTICAL semantics to the programmatic modifier (no decorator-only validation the modifier itself does not perform).

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review — Option A ratified, all three kwargs)
1. decorators.py node() signature: add merge_model: str | None = None, loop_history: bool = False, map_on_error: Literal['raise','collect'] = 'raise'.
2. _build_oracle_kwargs: accept merge_model; include in oracle_kw ONLY when not None (conditional-include pattern; Oracle's 'reason' default stays authoritative). SILENT-IGNORE semantics with merge_fn — identical to programmatic Oracle (review ruling: decorator-only fail-loud would re-introduce validation asymmetry; the previously cited decorators.py:203 precedent was the merge_fn+merge_prompt check, not hooks).
3. Loop path (decorators.py:622-630): loop_kwargs['history']=True when loop_history set; raise ConstructError if loop_history without loop_when (decorator-level pairing guard, precedent: map_over-requires-map_key — the kwarg would otherwise be silently dead since no Loop is composed at all).
4. Each path: thread map_on_error to BOTH Each construction sites (decorators.py:561 fusion + :570 plain), conditional-include only when != 'raise'. Name keeps the map_ prefix per map_over/map_key.
5. Tests (TDD): decorator surface asserts composed Oracle carries merge_model / Loop carries history / Each carries on_error; loop_history runtime accumulation reuses existing plumbing (_state_write.py:135-142, state.py:238); loop_history-without-loop_when raises. ForwardConstruct self.loop() is structurally EXEMPT from history (Construct-level ban modifiers.py:263-267) — document the exemption.
6. Fixtures: should_fail (loop_history without loop_when, CHECK_ERROR regex) + should_pass (all three new kwargs in use). NO merge_model+merge_fn fail fixture (silent-ignore ruling).
7. Docs: re-add @node-kwarg forms — oracle-ensemble.mdx:223, node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx, reference; add map_on_error. npm run build + npm test in website/.
notes:
## Findings

### Current @node forwarding (the reuse target for either option)
- Oracle kwargs: `_build_oracle_kwargs` (src/neograph/decorators.py:155-230) builds oracle_kw from ensemble_n/models/merge_fn/merge_prompt + 3 merge hooks. Applied at decorators.py:543-595 (`n = n | Oracle(**oracle_kw)`, two call sites: map_over branch + plain branch). merge_model is ABSENT.
- Loop kwargs: decorators.py:622-630 builds `{when, max_iterations, on_exhaust}` and pipes `n | Loop(**loop_kwargs)`. history is ABSENT. Note the conditional-include pattern: on_exhaust only forwarded when not None (preserves the modifier's Pydantic default).

### What the two fields actually do
- `Oracle.merge_model: str = 'reason'` (modifiers.py:422). Consumed ONLY on the merge_prompt (LLM-judge) path: _oracle.py:280 and :368 pass `model_tier=oracle.merge_model` to the merge invoke. With merge_fn it is silently ignored — Oracle.model_post_init validates hooks-vs-merge_fn but does NOT validate merge_model-vs-merge_fn.
- `Loop.history: bool = False` (modifiers.py:571). Node-level only: Construct|Loop(history=True) raises ConstructError (modifiers.py:263-267, pinned by tests/test_loop.py:410). When true, state.py:237 adds `neo_loop_history_{field}` (Annotated[list, _concat_reducer]) and _state_write.py:133-142 appends each iteration's result (key via StateKeys.loop_history, _state_keys.py:130). Framework-internal (neo_ prefix) — read back via graph.get_state(config).values, requires a checkpointer.

### Surface coverage today (the asymmetry)
- merge_model: programmatic Oracle ✓, ForwardConstruct `self.ensemble(..., merge_model=)` ✓ (forward.py:1219/1245), spec loader ✓ (loader.py:263-265, forwards only when in model_fields_set), spec schema ✓ (_spec_schema.py:36). **@node is the ONLY surface missing it.**
- Loop.history: programmatic Node|Loop ✓ (only legal form). ForwardConstruct `self.loop()` (forward.py:1150) does NOT expose it — structurally CANNOT: FC loops build a sub-construct, and Construct-level history raises. @node's loop_when path is a Node-level self-loop — exactly the supported shape — so @node is the only OTHER surface where history could legally live.

### Docs post-fsoss (already corrected to programmatic-only)
- website/src/content/docs/walkthrough/oracle-ensemble.mdx:223 explicitly says merge_model 'is not a @node kwarg' — must be re-edited if we wire.
- website/src/content/docs/node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx:588-597 documents Loop(history=True) as the programmatic modifier + neo_loop_history_{node} readback.
- concepts/spec-format.mdx:99 + reference/api.mdx:395 document merge_model on spec/Oracle.

### Downstream consumer (piarch)
- Zero uses of merge_model or Loop.history anywhere in piarch/src (grep confirmed). Heavy Oracle use (ensemble_n=3, Oracle(n=3, merge_prompt=...)) but always default merge tier; the one Loop mention is a comment. No demand pressure either way.

### Option A — wire for parity
- merge_model: add `merge_model: str | None = None` param to node(); in _build_oracle_kwargs include `oracle_kw['merge_model'] = merge_model` only when not None (same conditional-include pattern as on_exhaust / loader.py:263). Closes the only-surface gap. Design point for architect: mirror Oracle (silently ignore with merge_fn) vs fail loud at the decorator like the hooks validation at decorators.py:203 — recommend fail loud, consistent with '@node validates eagerly'.
- loop_history: add `loop_history: bool = False`; forward `loop_kwargs['history'] = loop_history` only when True. Legal by construction (Node-level self-loop). ForwardConstruct stays exempt (structural, documented).
- Cost: ~10 lines decorators.py, parity tests (decorator surface in tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py + tests/test_loop.py), re-add @node-kwarg docs in oracle-ensemble.mdx + modifier-kwargs.mdx + node-api reference, website npm build.

### Option B — keep programmatic-only
- Docs already consistent post-fsoss; zero consumer demand; @node kwarg surface already large (~20 params). But leaves merge_model as the one Oracle field with 3-of-4 surface coverage, and the 'kwargs mirror the Oracle modifier fields 1:1' claim (forward.py docstring) already true elsewhere — the asymmetry invites the exact doc drift fsoss just fixed.

### Recommendation (ratification to architect atom)
Wire both (Option A). merge_model is a straight parity hole — every other surface has it and the forwarding helper + conditional-include pattern already exist. loop_history is legal precisely and only on the @node self-loop shape. Both are additive, default-preserving, no behavior change for existing pipelines. The recurring failure mode here is docs/surface drift; symmetric surfaces are cheaper than remembering exemptions.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/decorators.py:155-230 — _build_oracle_kwargs: THE reuse target for merge_model forwarding
- src/neograph/decorators.py:543-595, 622-630 — Oracle pipe sites (x2) + Loop kwarg assembly (loop_history goes here)
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:422, 571, 263-267 — field definitions + Construct-history ban
- src/neograph/_oracle.py:280, 368 — merge_model consumption (model_tier, merge_prompt path only)
- src/neograph/_state_write.py:133-142 + src/neograph/state.py:237 + _state_keys.py:130 — history runtime plumbing (already complete; no IR/factory change needed)
- src/neograph/loader.py:263-265 — 'forward only when explicitly set' exemplar
- src/neograph/forward.py:1150 (loop, no history — exempt), 1219-1259 (ensemble, has merge_model)
- tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py, tests/test_loop.py:410-423, tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py — where parity tests belong
- website: walkthrough/oracle-ensemble.mdx:223, node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx:588-597 — docs to re-edit if wiring

## Risks & Edge Cases
- merge_model + merge_fn: Oracle silently ignores it. If wired, decide decorator-level fail-loud (recommended, mirrors hooks check at decorators.py:203) vs mirror-the-modifier. If Oracle itself gains the validation instead, that's an IR change requiring three-surface tests.
- loop_history naming: existing loop kwargs are loop_when (prefixed) but max_iterations/on_exhaust (unprefixed). Docs bug used loop_history; keep that name — bare 'history' as a @node kwarg is too generic.
- Three-surface parity rule: FC's self.loop() is structurally EXEMPT from history (Construct-level ban) — state the exemption in the test docstring per CLAUDE.md's parity rule. self.ensemble already has merge_model, so Oracle parity is complete under Option A.
- Do NOT default merge_model='reason' in the node() signature — use None + conditional include, or a decorator default would mask future Oracle default changes (same rationale as loader.py:263 comment).
- If Option B is ratified: no code change, but consider a should_fail-style guard or doc note preventing re-documentation of the phantom kwargs (fsoss recurrence).
## Codebase Disease Scan (d5pvl)
Disease spec: modifier fields reachable programmatically but not forwarded as @node kwargs (three-surface parity drift, the shape that caused the fsoss doc bug). Shape: SYNTACTIC — diffed model_fields of Oracle/Loop/Each/Operator vs inspect.signature(node).

| Modifier field | @node kwarg today | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Oracle.merge_model | MISSING | MIGRATE (this ticket) |
| Loop.history | MISSING | MIGRATE (this ticket, as loop_history=) |
| Each.on_error | MISSING | NEW third instance — architect to rule: fold in as map_on_error= (same conditional-include pattern, docs show NO @node-form drift for it) or DEFER to its own bead |
| Oracle.{n,models,merge_fn,merge_prompt,merge_fallback,merge_pre/post_process} | forwarded (ensemble_n->n etc.) | OK |
| Loop.{when,max_iterations,on_exhaust} | forwarded (loop_when->when) | OK |
| Each.{over,key} | forwarded (map_over/map_key) | OK |
| Operator.when | forwarded (interrupt_when) | OK |

Scan is exhaustive over all four modifier classes.
## Architect Review (neograph-vgfwk.12)

Gate hard-check: PASS (research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present). Research verified against code — all cited line-anchors accurate: decorators.py _build_oracle_kwargs (155-230) + Loop assembly (622-630), modifiers.py merge_model:422 / history:571 / Construct-history ban:263-267, runtime plumbing state.py:238-239 + _state_write.py:135-142, loader.py conditional-include exemplar:263-265, oracle-ensemble.mdx:223 ('not a @node kwarg'), forward.py ensemble merge_model:1219 + loop-no-history:1150, test_loop.py:410 ban. piarch zero-demand confirmed (the one on_error grep hit is a get_logger call, not Each.on_error).

RULINGS on the three decisions:

- [LOW] Decision 1 (wire-for-parity vs programmatic-only): RULE OPTION A. Sound and well-justified. merge_model is a genuine 3-of-4-surface hole; loop_history is legal precisely on the @node Node-level self-loop shape; runtime plumbing already exists (verified, no IR/factory/state change needed); the forwarding helper + conditional-include pattern already exist. Aligns with the three-surface parity rule and 'do not defer doable work'. Zero piarch demand is not disqualifying under the maintainer's stated symmetry-over-demand norm.

- [MEDIUM] Decision 2 (fail-loud vs silent-ignore for merge_model+merge_fn): the plan's rationale is MISLOCATED. 'the hooks check at decorators.py:203' is wrong — line 203 is the merge_fn+merge_prompt BOTH-SET check. The actual hooks-vs-merge_fn precedent lives in modifiers.py Oracle.model_post_init:450-457 — an IR-level check that fires for ALL surfaces. title: tool_calls.args coercion: provider-side JSON-string arguments crash LangChain AIMessage validation
description:
## What

Agent-mode @nodes (explore, etc.) crash with pydantic_core.ValidationError during `llm.invoke` when the provider (DeepSeek R1 via OpenRouter) emits tool-call `arguments` as a JSON STRING instead of a parsed dict:

```
pydantic_core.ValidationError: 2 validation errors for AIMessage
tool_calls.0.args
  Input should be a valid dictionary [type=dict_type,
  input_value='{"node_id": "BR-UC-008"}', input_type=str]
tool_calls.1.args
  Input should be a valid dictionary [type=dict_type,
  input_value='{"node_id": "FLOW-BR-UC-006-main"}', input_type=str]
```

Fires deep inside `langchain_openai.chat_models.base._convert_dict_to_message` before NeoGraph sees any response, so `_invoke_json_with_retry` (ExecutionError-only) cannot retry — the ValidationError escapes straight up the call stack. In the piarch rw-process pipeline this crashed the whole run after 43min / 17 successful explore calls / 65 classify-claim calls.

## Why

OpenAI's function-calling API returns `tool_calls[i].function.arguments` as a JSON string (per spec). LangChain's newer `AIMessage.tool_calls[i].args` expects a parsed dict. `langchain_openai` handles the conversion for well-behaved providers, but DeepSeek R1 via OpenRouter occasionally emits a shape that trips the converter (string reaches the Pydantic validator unparsed). Frequency: ~1 in 20 explore calls in our rehearsal.

This is the same shape of resilience problem NeoGraph already handles at the JSON-parse layer (bare arrays, truncated JSON, XML tool-call markup, dict-vs-envelope). Agent mode has no equivalent safety net.

## Expectations after delivery

- `invoke_with_tools` (or whatever wraps agent-mode LLM calls) catches `pydantic_core.ValidationError` arising from tool_calls.args type mismatch, coerces string → `json.loads` → dict, and retries.
- Transient provider-side quirks in tool-call argument shape do NOT crash 40-minute pipelines that have already done work.
- Failure mode is logged as a warning + retry, not an uncaught traceback.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: tests/modes/test_agent_tool_call_coercion.py — construct a fake LLM that returns one AIMessage-shaped payload where `tool_calls[0].args` is a string `'{"node_id": "X"}'`. Call `invoke_with_tools` on an agent @node. Assert it does NOT raise, and the tool is invoked with the parsed dict `{"node_id": "X"}`.

**E2E**: rerun rw-process on BR-RW-035 through real R1 explore calls; assert 0 uncaught ValidationError crashes even if the provider emits string-args shape.

## Acceptance

- Agent-mode calls survive the tool_calls.args string-vs-dict mismatch
- Explicit unit or integration test locks in the coercion
- Same style of retry hook / warning log as existing JSON-parse resilience (json_repair, bare-array auto-wrap, XML detection)
- piarch-side rehearsal on BR-RW-035 can complete without crashing in explore
close_reason: Fixed: _safe_tool_invoke catches ValidationError from string tool_calls.args, retries

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.2
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.2` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.2/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.2
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.2)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.2 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.2 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.2/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.2 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.2/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

description: Extract _resolve_image from _llm.py into src/neograph/_image.py. Add configure_image() for global config. - `_resolve_image` defined at _llm.py:199, used at _llm.py:256 (_compile_multimodal_prompt)

2. Add ImageConfig dataclass with defaults: max_size_bytes=20MB, allowed_dirs=None, allowed_mimes=IMAGE_MIMES, validate_magic=True

   a. Empty/whitespace guard (existing)
   b. Data URI passthrough (existing)

6. __init__.py: import resolve_image + configure_image from _image instead of _llm
7. Tests: update import paths

### Magic bytes table
- PNG: b"\\x89PNG"
- JPEG: b"\\xff\\xd8\\xff"  
- GIF: b"GIF8"
- WEBP: b"RIFF" + 4 bytes + b"WEBP"
- BMP: b"BM"
- SVG: detect b"<svg" or b"<?xml" in first 256 bytes

- [LOW] Module-level _config — same pattern as _llm_factory in _llm.py. Proven pattern.
- [MEDIUM] allowed_dirs default None (allow all) vs empty list (deny all). None=allow-all is correct for backward compat. Document the security implication prominently.

title: inputs=list[X] (single-type) fails to extract from Each dict[str,X] producer

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-wpzg
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-wpzg` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-wpzg/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-wpzg
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-wpzg)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wpzg --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wpzg --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-wpzg/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-wpzg codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-wpzg/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Write regression test for neograph-wpzg

any implementation begins.

## Instructions

## BANNED Patterns

- `pytest.mark.xfail` is BANNED in regression tests
- AST-scanning / source-code pattern tests are BANNED **as a
  substitute for behavioral testing** — when the task changes
  behavior, the red test must exercise that behavior, not scan source.
- Direct DB session management in test code is BANNED

wordmark, an import idiom, a helper-bypass that is type- or
text-shaped, not runtime-observable). For these, no behavioral failing
test exists — the only meaningful red artifact IS the structural guard
that `sweep-verify` will later require. In that case:
- Write that structural guard HERE, confirm it FAILS (the disease
  instances exist), and record it as the red artifact.
- The AST/source-text BAN above does NOT apply — it bans source scans
  used INSTEAD OF behavioral tests, not the structural guard that pins
  a structural invariant. The same guard satisfies `sweep-verify`.
