title: Sweep verification for neograph-wpzg
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-wpzg
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-wpzg`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-wpzg)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wpzg --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-wpzg sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: forward: ForwardConstruct base class + class-attribute node discovery
description:
Introduce `ForwardConstruct`, a subclass of `neograph.construct.Construct` whose nodes are discovered from class attributes instead of being passed as `nodes=[...]`. No tracing yet — this subtask only lands the class-attribute discovery scaffolding so subsequent subtasks can plug tracing into it.

## Context

- Parent epic: `neograph-pub` — `Construct.forward()` subclass mode for branching logic.
- Design spike: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` (chosen strategy: Symbolic Proxy). Read this first.
- Reference prototype: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/spike.py` — shows the discovery + shim pattern this subtask productionizes.

## Files

- NEW `src/neograph/forward.py` — module housing `ForwardConstruct`, the `Proxy` class, the tracer, and the `_ForwardSelf` shim. Keep tracing infrastructure scoped to this one module.
- `src/neograph/__init__.py` — re-export `ForwardConstruct` at the top level.
- `tests/test_forward_construct_discovery.py` — new test file (do NOT modify existing tests).

## Signatures

```python
# src/neograph/forward.py
class ForwardConstruct(Construct):
    def __init__(self, name_: str | None = None, /, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        # 1. Discover Node class attrs via _discover_node_attrs()
        # 2. For this subtask ONLY: pass the discovered nodes in declaration order
        #    directly as the nodes list. (Tracing happens in the next subtask.)
        # 3. Call super().__init__(name_, nodes=discovered, **kwargs)
        ...

    @classmethod
    def _discover_node_attrs(cls) -> dict[str, Node]:
        """Walk cls.__mro__ in reverse; return attr_name -> Node for every
        class attribute that isinstance(v, Node). Subclass attrs shadow base.
        """
        ...

    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "ForwardConstruct subclasses must override forward()"
        )
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `class Foo(ForwardConstruct)` with two class-level `Node.scripted(...)` attrs instantiates and `foo.nodes` returns the two Nodes in class-declaration order.
2. Declaration order is preserved across Python versions (rely on `__dict__` insertion order, documented since 3.7).
3. Inheritance works: a subclass that adds a new Node attribute gets parent + new. Overriding an attribute name replaces the parent's.
4. Instantiating `ForwardConstruct` directly (no subclass) raises a clear error — "subclass ForwardConstruct and declare node attributes".
5. `_validate_node_chain` still runs on the discovered list (inherited from `Construct.__init__`), so a bad chain raises `ConstructError`.
6. New test file covers: basic discovery, inheritance/override, direct instantiation error, validation still fires, declaration order.

## Out of scope

- Running `forward()` at all. Discovery only. The next subtask (forward-tracer) adds the actual trace.
- Any behavior that depends on the order being call-order rather than declaration-order — that distinction only matters once tracing lands.
- Touching `compiler.py` or `state.py`. The nodes list is already in the shape they consume.
close_reason: Straight-line ForwardConstruct MVP complete. di0: base class with node discovery via __mro__ walk + Pydantic ignored_types fix. 3us: symbolic proxy tracer (_Proxy + _Tracer + _ForwardSelf + _NodeCall) wired into ForwardConstruct.__init__. vxv: zero compiler changes — tracer output is a plain nodes list that compile()/state-builder/factory consume unchanged. 10 new tests across 3 classes. 169/169 passing.

## Prep
### Analysis after reading the full file (3460 lines)

The two strategy systems serve DIFFERENT purposes:
- Old system (L115-L998): Strategies produce (Construct, meta) tuples. Tests exercise specific topology axes (dict outputs, sub+Each, nested subs, @node path, DI, skip_when, operators, error patterns). These are NOT redundant with the new system.

3. oracle_pipeline → oracle_topology (both produce Oracle ensemble)
4. loop_pipeline → loop_topology (both produce Loop iteration)

- TestPerComboInvariants (5 tests, per-strategy) — subsumed by framework promise tests
- TestEachKeyCompleteness (2 tests) — subsumed by TestEachFansOutToEveryItem
- TestLoopTermination (2 tests) — subsumed by TestLoopTerminatesAndAccumulates
- TestDescribeGraph (2 tests, bare/each only) — borderline, uses describe_graph() which no new test exercises

### NOT redundant — must keep:
All old strategies from L459-L998 and their test classes (L648-L1793). These exercise unique axes:
- dict_output_pipeline → TestDictFormOutputs (dict-form outputs)
- sub_construct_pipeline → TestSubConstructs (sub isolation)
- mixed_modifier_pipeline → TestMixedModifiers (Each→collector→Oracle in one Construct)
- each_empty_collection → TestEachEmptyCollection (empty Each regression)
- di_pipeline → TestDIPositive (DI params)
- skip_when_pipeline → TestSkipWhen (conditional execution)
- node_decorator_pipeline → TestNodeDecoratorPath (@node code path)
- sub_construct_with_each → TestSubConstructWithEach
- nested_sub_construct → TestNestedSubConstructs
- fan_in_pipeline → TestFanIn (N→1 fan-in)
- each_with_dict_outputs → TestEachWithDictOutputs
- node_decorator_with_di → TestNodeDecoratorWithDI
- Inline tests: TestNodeDecoratorMapOver, TestNodeDecoratorEnsemble, TestListConsumerOfEach, TestMultipleSubConstructs, TestSubConstructWithOracle, TestSubConstructWithLoop, TestTypeSubclassCompat, TestOperatorCombo, TestContextParam, TestRunIsolated, TestCreativeHumanErrors, TestInvalidTopologyErrors, TestDIErrorMessages, TestDIPreFlight

### Approach
1. Delete 5 redundant old strategies + any_pipeline
2. Delete 4 redundant test classes (13 test methods total)
3. Keep TestDescribeGraph (moves to use bare_topology/each_topology instead)
4. Keep all other old strategies and test classes — they test unique axes

Core invariant: Every deleted test must be verifiably subsumed by a kept test. No coverage loss.

title: PROC-3: multi-agent codebase scan as in-loop ticket gate
description:
## Architectural invariant

Architecturally-significant tickets gain a fast multi-agent codebase-wide review as a phase-gate INSIDE the ticket, not just as a periodic full audit. The seven-reviewer scan that was previously a `/dev-practices:code-review` session now has a callable form scoped to a single disease pattern, runnable in 2-3 minutes from inside a ticket's review atom.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

Read:
- `/Users/konst/projects/pi-agentic-coding/plugins/dev-practices/skills/code-review/` — the existing skill
- `.claude/code-review/020626_2218/` — the report shape from the Jun-2026 review
- The current `feature-dev:code-reviewer` agent definition — what it can do today

The current code-review skill spawns 5 review agents in parallel (testing, dry, consistency, layering, python-practices) plus 2 optional (architecture, security). Each writes a separate Markdown report. The synthesis is post-hoc.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern: "architectural tickets that close without a codebase-wide elegance review." Scan:
- Recently-closed P1 architectural tickets (last 30 days): `bd list --status=closed --priority=1`
- For each, did the close note reference a multi-agent scan?
- Most probably did NOT. Count them.

Disposition table per ticket (this is a process-correctness scan, not a code-pattern scan).

## Phase 2 — Target design

Define a `codebase-elegance-scan` callable form:

1. **Scope** — takes a one-line "disease pattern spec" (the same spec produced by the molecule's `codebase-scan` atom). Example: "raw `getattr(state, ...)` instead of `bus.get/get_required` in routing modules."

2. **Agents to spawn (in parallel, single message)**:
   - `review-dry` — does this disease appear elsewhere (DRY violations)?
   - `review-consistency` — is this the only naming/regex form?
   - `review-layering` — does the fix cross layer boundaries it shouldn't?
   - Optional: `feature-dev:code-reviewer` (opus model) for the elegance question.

3. **Output** — each writes to `.claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/`. The synthesizer (the ticket's executor) reads all, produces a one-page verdict for the bead notes.

4. **Time budget** — ≤ 5 minutes per scan. (The Jun-2026 review was 7 agents over the whole codebase and took ~3 minutes per agent. A single-disease scan is faster.)

5. **Integration with the molecule** — the `review` atom in `task-execute.yaml` / `bug-triage.yaml` SHOULD invoke this scan. Phase 6 of the per-ticket discipline ("independent codebase-wide elegance review") becomes mechanical.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + GRASP. Iterate until:
- The callable form is documented in the dev-practices skill (probably as a new sub-skill `code-review-targeted` or as an option in the existing one)
- The molecule formulas reference it from the `review` atom
- A probe ticket exercises the in-loop scan end-to-end
- The scan produces actionable output (a disposition table for the disease pattern, NOT a 41-finding catalog)

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO defining the discipline without making it callable. "Reviewers should run a scan" is aspirational; "the molecule spawns the scan as part of the review atom" is structural.
- NO collapsing the targeted scan with the full audit — they serve different purposes (the targeted scan is fast and disease-specific; the full audit is periodic and exhaustive).

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

Re-scan the recently-closed P1 ticket list. The discipline for NEW tickets includes the in-loop scan. (Old tickets are not retroactively fixed — that's what ARCH-1..4 do.)

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer:
1. Is the callable scan actually faster than a full multi-agent run? Time it.
2. Does the disposition table format integrate cleanly with the molecule's existing bead-notes conventions?
3. Can a future ticket SKIP the in-loop scan? If yes, the discipline isn't structural — fix that.

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- `code-review-targeted` callable exists (skill / sub-skill / documented invocation)
- task-execute and bug-triage `review` atoms invoke it (YAML updated in agentic-toolkit)
- Probe ticket exercises in-loop scan; output in `.claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/`
- Independent reviewer verdict ELEGANT ≥85
design:
## Core Invariant
Architecturally-significant tickets gain a fast, single-disease multi-agent codebase scan as a STRUCTURAL phase-gate inside the ticket -- delivered as a --targeted MODE of the existing code-review skill (NOT a duplicate skill) -- that fans out disease-scoped lenses, writes to .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/, and produces a one-page disposition table the codebase-scan:complete gate REQUIRES to exist; the full periodic audit stays a separate mode.

## Implementation Plan (deliverable in agentic-toolkit; commit + PUSH)

### Step 1 -- review-disease-scan agent (the missing primitive)
New agents/review-disease-scan.md (dev-practices plugin). Read-only. Input contract (via spawn prompt): a one-line DISEASE-PATTERN SPEC + a LENS in {dedup, consistency, layering}. Behavior:
- WHOLE-TREE scope (explicitly NO git-diff/Changed-Function anchor -- unlike the dimensional review-* agents).
- Find every instance of THE ONE pattern through its lens (dedup=semantic duplicate logic; consistency=naming/form drift, dominant-usage; layering=does the pattern cross a layer boundary).
- Output ONLY disposition rows: | # | file:line | Form | Disposition (MIGRATE/ALLOWLIST/DEFER) | Reason |. NO Critical/High/Med/Low severity catalog.
- Write to the assigned output file.

### Step 2 -- code-review --targeted MODE (no new skill)
Edit skills/code-review/SKILL.md: keep args '[scope]'; add a Targeted Mode section. Invocation: /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<disease-spec>" [ticket-id].
- Output dir .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ (ticket-id arg; fallback DDMMYY_HHMM).
- Spawn IN ONE MESSAGE: review-disease-scan x3 (lens=dedup/consistency/layering) -> <dir>/disease-<lens>.md; + optional opus feature-dev:code-reviewer (elegance question) for architectural tickets -> <dir>/elegance.md.
- Executor synthesizes a ONE-PAGE disposition table (merge the 3 lens rows, dedup by file:line+Form) appended to bead notes -- NOT a multi-section synthesis.md.
- Time budget <=5 min (3+1 agents, single disease) -- contrast documented vs the full mode (5-7 agents, whole-codebase, periodic).
- SEMANTIC-vs-SYNTACTIC boundary documented: targeted fan-out is the prescribed method for SEMANTIC diseases (logic duplicated under different names); for purely syntactic patterns (getattr(state), magic-string keys, dual-name alias) a single executor grep in the codebase-scan atom suffices -- don't fan out for those.

### Step 3 -- Wire into molecule formulas (REPLACE manual, don't augment)
task-execute.yaml + bug-triage.yaml codebase-scan atom: replace the 'executor greps by hand' narrative with 'produce the disposition table by invoking /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<spec>" <ticket-id> (semantic diseases) or a single grep (syntactic)'. Gate label/acceptance otherwise unchanged. sweep-verify re-scan step (step 1 'Re-run the scan') re-invokes the same mode.

### Step 4 -- Structural un-skippability
Amend the codebase-scan atom acceptance: codebase-scan:complete REQUIRES .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ to exist AND contain the disposition table. Reuses the existing label-gate hard-check (downstream review atom greps the label). Now the gate can't be earned without the scan having run + written output.

### Step 5 -- Static wiring guard (toolkit repo)
A check (test or the plugin's validation) asserting: (a) skills/code-review/SKILL.md documents the --targeted mode + arg contract; (b) agents/review-disease-scan.md exists; (c) both formula codebase-scan atoms contain the literal 'code-review --targeted'. Proves wired, not just markdown.

### Step 6 -- Probe ticket end-to-end
File a probe bead; run code-review --targeted on a real SEMANTIC disease spec (e.g. 'merge/redirect logic re-derived inline instead of via the single oracle merge helper' OR reuse a PROC-2 semantic pattern); confirm .claude/code-review/<probe-id>/ output + 1-page table; time it (<5 min, faster than the full run).

### Step 7 -- gates
make quality (neograph side unaffected); independent Opus review (faster-than-full? disposition integrates with bead-notes? can a ticket SKIP it? -> artifact gate must make NO). ELEGANT>=85. Then commit + push BOTH repos.

## Acceptance mapping
- callable exists -> Steps 1-2 (--targeted mode + review-disease-scan agent)
- task-execute + bug-triage review/scan atoms invoke it -> Step 3
- probe exercises in-loop scan; output in .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ -> Step 6
- independent ELEGANT>=85 -> Step 7

## Verification (non-code deliverable)
RED artifact = the Step-5 wiring guard failing before the skill/agent/formula edits exist; GREEN after. Probe run = behavioral proof.

## Findings (PROC-3 research)

### Existing machinery
- Skill: pi-agentic-coding/plugins/dev-practices/skills/code-review/SKILL.md -- full multi-agent review.   - The 'review' atom (task-execute.yaml:222) is a single-agent ARCHITECT review of the design; the 'codebase-scan' atom (:122) produces a disposition table per disease pattern. PROC-3 wants the codebase-scan/review/sweep-verify to be able to invoke a FAST multi-agent targeted scan.

### Deliverable location
pi-agentic-coding (= github postindustria-tech/agentic-toolkit), a SEPARATE git repo. The skill + formula YAML edits commit THERE, not in neograph. neograph beads tracks the work; the probe-ticket output (.claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/) can live in either repo's .claude.

### Disposition-table convention (from PROC-2 codebase-scan atom -- the integration target)
Per disease pattern: 'Pattern: <one-line spec>', 'Scan command', 'Total instances: N', then a table | # | file:line | Form | Disposition (MIGRATE/ALLOWLIST/DEFER) | Reason |. The targeted scan must EMIT this shape (one page), NOT a 41-finding catalog.

### What 'callable' means (anti-band-aid clause: must be callable, not aspirational)
A new skill skills/code-review-targeted/SKILL.md that: takes a one-line disease-pattern spec (arg); spawns review-dry + review-consistency + review-layering in ONE message (parallel), each scoped to the SINGLE disease (not whole-codebase dimensions); optional opus elegance reviewer (feature-dev:code-reviewer or reviewer); each writes .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/<agent>.md; the invoking executor synthesizes a one-page disposition verdict into bead notes; time budget <=5 min. The molecule's codebase-scan / sweep-verify / review atoms reference it so Phase-6 'independent codebase-wide elegance review' becomes mechanical.

### Risks
- Scope creep: targeted scan must NOT collapse into the full audit (different purpose). Keep agent count small (3 + optional 1) and disease-scoped.
- Skippability (Phase-6 reviewer Q3): if the molecule atom only SUGGESTS the scan, it isn't structural. The formula text must make invocation the default path for architecturally-significant tickets, with the disposition table as the gate artifact.
- Determinism: PROC-2 already exercised this pattern manually (architect atom + Phase-6 reviewer). PROC-3 formalizes it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-djpi) -- PROCESS-correctness scan

Pattern: architecturally-significant P1 ticket closed WITHOUT an in-loop codebase-wide (multi-agent) elegance review as a phase-gate.
Scan command: bd list --status closed --priority 1 ; count tickets carrying codebase-scan:complete (the molecule's in-loop scan gate label).
Total closed P1: 50. With in-loop scan gate (codebase-scan:complete): 2 (neograph-0e9a PROC-2, neograph-ruqm PROC-1). Without: 48.

| # | Ticket(s) | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | neograph-0e9a (PROC-2), neograph-ruqm (PROC-1) | had codebase-scan + sweep-verify in-loop | COMPLIANT | the molecule discipline already ran; PROC-2 even ran the multi-agent architect+reviewer gate manually |
| 2 | 48 older P1s (n2li, ianf, y20i, ble3, 20xq, vgc1, aqau, pej0, rnjw, ...) | closed pre-discipline / with only reproduce: or research: labels; no multi-agent codebase-wide scan referenced in close notes | DEFER (forward-only) | Per PROC-3 Phase 5, OLD tickets are NOT retroactively fixed -- ARCH-1..4 (s0iz/aiiz/gf9g/v3xx) handle the specific remediations the Jun-2026 audit found. PROC-3 is the structural counter-measure for NEW tickets. |

Conclusion: 48/50 (96%) of closed P1 architectural tickets closed without an in-loop multi-agent elegance scan -- this is precisely the disease PROC-3 eliminates GOING FORWARD by making code-review-targeted a callable phase-gate the molecule invokes. No MIGRATE rows (process scan, not code migration). No new DEFER tickets needed -- ARCH-1..4 already track the retroactive code remediations.

Note: PROC-2 (just completed) is the proof the in-loop multi-agent gate works -- its architect-review atom + Phase-6 independent reviewer were exactly the targeted-scan pattern PROC-3 formalizes into a reusable skill.
## Architect Review (neograph-rlur.12)
Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (3 HIGH must-fix-before-build + a user-facing scope fork)

- [HIGH] Separate code-review-targeted skill DUPLICATES the full skill's scaffold (~80% shared: output-dir/TeamCreate/spawn/synthesis) -> self-refuting (the DRY disease the molecule's own scan exists to catch). Use a --targeted <spec> [ticket-id] MODE of the existing code-review skill (its args:'[scope]' already anticipates it). Acceptable middle: a thin alias skill that just invokes the mode.

- [LOW] existence/frontmatter guard proves existence not invocation; the artifact-existence gate is the real lever.

title: Portal: cross-subconstruct mesh via Command.PARENT
description: v1 restricts peers to sibling Nodes at one construct level (D-MESH-LEVEL); a peer across a sub-construct boundary is a ConstructError. v1 already lowers to Command(goto) precisely so this v2 cross-boundary mesh needs no re-lowering — add Command.PARENT routing + cross-boundary validation. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Core Invariant

A routing decision made inside an isolated sub-construct that names a parent-level Portal peer must reach that peer as a BOUNDARY-PORT handoff on the parent mesh -- never by the parent graph reaching into the sub-construct's interior, and never by the sub-construct's isolated invoke() mutating parent control flow directly. Command( construction stays inside the existing G1 monopoly (factory.py/runner.py only). See docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md for the full ratified doc -- this field is a summary pointer, not a duplicate; read the doc for the resolved Q1-Q7 checklist, the rejected alternatives, and the spike.

## STALE: the previous Implementation Plan below (8 steps, written 2026-07-14/16) is SUPERSEDED

It described the literal `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, ...)` mechanism, which was spiked and PROVEN DEAD (2026-07-15, see NOTES) -- do not follow steps 3/4 below, they describe a mechanism that does not work. Kept only for history; the CURRENT implementation plan is docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md §3.1 (What do0d9 actually builds -- the delta), which lists the 5 Node-typed sites to extend (post-independent-review corrections applied 2026-07-23):

1. `factory.py` -- new `make_portal_subgraph_fn` (sibling of `make_portal_fn`), wraps `make_subgraph_fn`'s sync/async twins, pipes the returned update through the EXISTING `_portal_route_to_command`. Sole new Command(-adjacent site; already inside the G1 monopoly.
2. `_validation_portal.py` -- relax the blanket `isinstance(member, Node)` rejection (`:86-95`) to admit a Construct member whose declared `.output` matches the mesh payload type. MUST also fix `member.outputs` (`:104`) to route through `_declared_output(member)` (Construct has no `.outputs` field) -- this will AttributeError otherwise. The reserved-`handoff`-key check (`:241-252`) operates on a Node-only-narrowed list and should stay Node-scoped by design (a Construct's boundary port is `.input`/`.output`, not a fan-in `inputs` dict).
3. `_ir_normalize.py` (guard G3, single-writer for `handoff_channel`) -- `:264` and `:280` both `isinstance(item, Node)`-gate and currently EXCLUDE a Construct mesh member; must be extended so a Portal-carrying Construct member is collected into `portal_members` and gets a `handoff_channel` key threaded to it (via the SAME `_add_subgraph` recursive-compile-kwarg channel as `checkpointer`/`runtime`/`scripted_lookup` -- not a new field on Construct).
4. `_wiring.py` -- `_contiguous_portal_mesh`'s collection loop and `_add_portal_mesh`'s `members: list[Node]` typing / `entry_label_map` (keyed off `member.mode`, which Construct lacks) both need a Construct-aware branch dispatching to `make_portal_subgraph_fn` instead of `make_portal_fn`.
5. Fixtures + example: should_pass/should_fail check-fixtures for a cross-boundary peer reference (valid + invalid target), and a runnable example mirroring 28/29's Portal showcase pattern.

Acceptance for closing do0d9: the design doc's mechanism implemented across all 5 sites above, PLUS a real end-to-end test proving an ACTUAL `Construct` object sitting inside a `Portal` member list routes correctly (the design doc's own spike used a plain `@node` wrapper hand-invoking the sub-construct, which does NOT exercise sites 2-4 above -- see design doc §8 finding 5). Three-surface parity per AGENTS.md; ForwardConstruct stays exempt (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT, inherited unchanged, until neograph-a37vk gives it a handoff builder).

---

### Original stale plan (superseded, kept for history only)

1. NEEDS USER INPUT FIRST (see notes' Risks section): disambiguate which cross-boundary shape(s) do0d9's acceptance criteria require -- (i) a peer INSIDE a sub-construct routing OUT via literal Command(graph=Command.PARENT, goto=<parent_peer>), (ii) a parent-level peer routing INTO a sub-construct's entry, and/or (iii) two sibling sub-Constructs at the SAME level acting as whole-Construct mesh members. [RESOLVED 2026-07-16: scoped to (i)/(iii) which the 2026-07-23 design doc shows collapse to one mechanism; (ii) stays out of scope, belongs to Mechanism 1.]
2. Spike literal Command.PARENT. [DONE 2026-07-15: DEAD, does not propagate through isolated invoke().]
3-4. [DEAD: described the literal Command.PARENT wrapper variant -- do not implement.]
5-8. [Superseded by the design doc's own §3.1/§4/§7 treatment of validation, guard G1, fixtures, and three-surface parity -- follow the doc, not this list.]
notes:
## Findings
- REUSE TARGET (v1 lowering to extend, not re-derive): Portal mesh lowering already produces `Command(goto=...)` at ONE construct level — `make_portal_fn` (src/neograph/factory.py:103-207) builds the wrapper, `_add_portal_mesh` (src/neograph/_wiring.py:723-789) wires `add_node(member.name, member_fn, destinations=...)` with a pass-through `__handoff_exit_<entry>` re-join node. D-MESH-LEVEL's ratified rationale ("Lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering", decision log table row) means do0d9 extends THIS wrapper/factory, not a new lowering mechanism.
- REUSE TARGET (mesh-assembly validation cluster): `_check_portal_mesh` in src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40-254 is the SINGLE place mesh rules live (per AGENTS.md's single-sited-validation-cluster discipline). The CURRENT v1 rule that do0d9 must relax/extend is the shape check at lines 86-95: `if not isinstance(member, Node): raise ConstructError(...'Portal mesh member is a Construct'..."mesh members must be sibling Nodes (D-MESH-LEVEL)")`. do0d9 turns this hard rejection into a validated cross-boundary case instead of ripping it out wholesale — v1's "same-level sibling Node" rule still holds for the SAME-LEVEL mesh; do0d9 adds the NEW case (a peer reference that crosses INTO or OUT OF a sub-construct boundary).
- REUSE TARGET (sub-construct boundary machinery): `_add_subgraph` (src/neograph/compiler.py:438-497) + `make_subgraph_fn` (src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:57-207) are the existing single-typed-entry/output boundary-port machinery (Construct.input/output, construct.py:113-123) that any cross-boundary addressing must hook into, per the ratified portal-addressability doc (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md) mechanism 1 (entry-label map) framing.
- CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE FINDING (the actual hard part of do0d9, not yet resolved by any doc): neograph's sub-construct compilation is NOT LangGraph's native subgraph-as-node nesting. `make_subgraph_fn`'s `subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node` (src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:182-199) call `sub_graph.invoke(sub_input, config=config)` — a plain, isolated, top-level Pregel invocation from inside a RunnableLambda that the PARENT adds as an ordinary node — NOT `parent_builder.add_node(name, compiled_child_graph_object)` (the native form LangGraph's own subgraph docs assume). LangGraph's `Command.PARENT` bubble-up mechanism (verified in installed langgraph 1.x: `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_retry.py:544-631`, `_io.py:56-59`) works by an inner node's Pregel task-loop catching `cmd.graph == Command.PARENT`, rewriting it to the checkpoint-namespace-derived parent segment (`_checkpoint_ns_for_parent_command(ns)`), and RE-RAISING as a bubble exception that the enclosing Pregel task loop (one level up) catches again, repeating until `cmd.graph` matches the CURRENT graph's own namespace. This bubble is namespace-string-driven (`config['configurable'][CONFIG_KEY_CHECKPOINT_NS]`), not object-identity driven, so it MAY already work through neograph's isolated-invoke wrapper (config is passed through unmodified at src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:150/188/198, and nothing in neograph catches/swallows an exception around the `sub_graph.invoke`/`ainvoke` call — grep confirmed zero `except` blocks there). But this has NEVER been exercised in this codebase (zero hits for `Command(graph=` / `graph=Command.PARENT` in tests/ or src/) and is genuinely uncertain without an empirical spike, because `sub_graph.invoke()` is its own fresh top-level Pregel run (own recursion_limit, own stream_mode) rather than a task dispatched BY the parent's own Pregel scheduler — whether LangGraph's `Pregel.invoke()` entry point respects and threads an INCOMING checkpoint_ns from config to continue the parent's namespace (vs. resetting to a fresh root namespace) is the crux unresolved question.
- Command construction monopoly: guard G1 (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`, tests/test_guards_assembly.py) restricts `Command(` construction to factory.py and runner.py ONLY — any new Command.PARENT emission must land in one of those two files, not _wiring.py or _subconstruct.py.
- The design doc (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md) explicitly scopes mechanism 1 (entry-label map) as WITHIN one compile() level, and calls out do0d9's Command.PARENT mechanism as the deliberately-separate cross-boundary case (see "A note on lowering substrate" + mechanism-1 section) — confirms do0d9 is not expected to reuse mechanism 1 verbatim, just to keep the two textually separate, which the doc already does.
- CURRENT vs DEPRECATED: no deprecated pattern here — this is a net-new capability layered onto the still-current v1 mesh machinery (Portal, formerly Keymaker; the rename is already complete, use Portal/handoff terminology throughout, never 'Keymaker' except when quoting the historic banner-preserved docs).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:86-95 -- the CURRENT hard `ConstructError` for a Construct mesh member (D-MESH-LEVEL v1 rule); do0d9 must extend this function (not inline elsewhere) to admit the validated cross-boundary case.
- src/neograph/factory.py:103-207 (`make_portal_fn`) -- the exemplar same-level `Command(goto=...)` lowering incl. fail-loud invalid-target (`ExecutionError`) and hop-budget accounting; the pattern any cross-boundary `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, goto=...)` wrapper should mirror for consistency (same channel-key/hop-count conventions).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:723-789 (`_add_portal_mesh`) + :697-720 (`_contiguous_portal_mesh`) -- mesh wiring/collection walk; a cross-boundary member would need either a new collection rule here or a parallel `_add_portal_mesh_cross_boundary`-style helper, kept in this file (compiler-layer, matches Command-construction-adjacent placement even though guard G1 restricts literal Command( to factory.py/runner.py).
- src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:182-199 -- `subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node`: the isolated `sub_graph.invoke()` call with NO exception handling around it; the mechanism whose Command.PARENT-bubble-compatibility is the open empirical question above.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:438-497 (`_add_subgraph`) -- sub-construct compile entry, fail-loud `sub.input is None` check; the existing boundary-port machinery to extend.
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:126-145 (`StateKeys.handoff_payload`/`handoff_hops`) -- reuse verbatim for any cross-boundary channel/counter naming; no new state-key scheme per AGENTS.md's `neo_`-prefix discipline.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`, guard G1) -- pins where `Command(` may be constructed; extend/verify against, don't bypass.
- docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md -- ratified Core Invariant doc (see notes above); cite verbatim, don't re-derive.
- docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md -- D-MESH-LEVEL entry (verbatim: "Peers = sibling Nodes at same construct level; sub-construct member / Command.PARENT cross-boundary = ConstructError. Lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering.") is the direct origin/justification for do0d9; do not re-derive.
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md:112-130,536-556,620-642,769-774 -- deepest existing research on Command.PARENT semantics + langgraph-swarm's `create_handoff_tool` precedent; read before designing the cross-boundary wrapper.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- The single biggest risk: do0d9 could be implemented as "just add graph=Command.PARENT to the wrapper" without first spiking whether neograph's isolated-invoke sub-construct architecture actually propagates LangGraph's checkpoint-namespace bubble-up correctly. If it does NOT propagate (e.g. `sub_graph.invoke()` resets checkpoint_ns to a fresh root), the mechanism will silently do nothing OR raise a LangGraph-internal error ("no parent graph") at runtime with no compile-time signal — a genuine SILENT SEAM the North-star invariant explicitly forbids. Recommend an isolated LangGraph-only (no neograph IR) spike FIRST: two nested `StateGraph`s where the child is invoked via a wrapping RunnableLambda exactly like `_subconstruct.py` does, one inner node returns `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, goto=<parent_peer>)`, and confirm empirically whether the parent-level goto fires. This determines whether do0d9 is (a) a straightforward wrapper extension, or (b) requires first migrating the relevant sub-constructs to LangGraph's native `add_node(name, compiled_child_graph)` nesting (a much bigger architectural change, likely needing its own decomposition/bead).
- Symmetric case ambiguity: "cross-subconstruct mesh" could mean (i) a peer INSIDE a sub-construct routing OUT to a parent-level peer (Command.PARENT literally as named), (ii) a parent-level peer routing INTO a sub-construct's entry (this is arguably mechanism-1's entry-label map territory, not Command.PARENT), or (iii) two sibling sub-constructs at the SAME parent level acting as whole-Construct mesh members (peer = a Construct, not a Node — currently rejected by the isinstance(member, Node) check). The bead title says "Portal: cross-subconstruct mesh via Command.PARENT" but the decision log's D-MESH-LEVEL phrasing ("sub-construct member... cross-boundary") is ambiguous between (i) and (iii). Needs disambiguation before implementation — likely (i) is the literal Command.PARENT case and (iii) is a separate, simpler "whole-Construct-as-mesh-member" extension that does NOT need Command.PARENT (it could lower to a same-level Command(goto=<subconstruct's field_name>) since sub-constructs already compile to ordinary nodes at the parent level via `_add_subgraph`). NEEDS USER INPUT: confirm which of (i)/(ii)/(iii) — or "all three" — do0d9's acceptance criteria actually require; the bead body's one-liner is a design pointer, not a spec.
- Async: `_subconstruct.py` has dual sync/async twins (`subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node`); any Command.PARENT-bubble compatibility must be verified on BOTH `sub_graph.invoke` and `sub_graph.ainvoke` paths (Phase-1 H2 invariant: async must propagate through every nesting level) — do not spike only the sync path.
- Checkpointer interaction: `_add_subgraph` threads `checkpointer=checkpointer` recursively into the child `compile()` call (compiler.py:474-482) — if a bubble-up path requires checkpoint_ns continuity, the presence/absence of a real checkpointer (vs None) on the child compile may change behavior; the spike should test both with and without a checkpointer.
- No existing test/example exercises `Command(graph=...)` or `Command.PARENT` anywhere in this repo (grep confirmed zero hits in tests/ and src/) — there is no prior art within neograph to copy; the langgraph-swarm precedent (external library) is the closest analog, cited in dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md:150.
SPIKE FINDING (2026-07-15): Command(graph=Command.PARENT) does NOT propagate through neograph's isolated sub_graph.invoke() sub-construct compilation. Standalone LangGraph-only spike, both handling strategies: (a) wrapper CATCHES the raised ParentCommand -> escape is swallowed, the static successor edge fires, the parent-level peer never runs (SILENT SEAM — North Star forbidden); (b) wrapper lets it PROPAGATE -> uncaught exception, outer Pregel does NOT interpret it as routing. Command.PARENT is a NATIVE subgraph-nesting feature; neograph deliberately uses isolated invoke for state hygiene, so the parent graph has no structural knowledge of the child. Zero Command(graph= usages existed in the repo — this path was never exercised.

D-MESH-LEVEL FALSIFIED: the v1 'lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering' forward-compat claim was based on an untested assumption. The lowering (Command(goto) vs path_map) was never the blocker; the propagation mechanism is.

RE-SCOPE (design-first): do0d9 is NOT literal Command.PARENT. Mechanism = neograph-native parent-scoped bubble-up — the sub-construct wrapper CATCHES the escape intent (explicit, not silent), reads its target, and writes it onto the parent mesh channel (StateKeys.handoff_payload) so the parent mesh routes on it via the normal Portal path. This preserves isolated-invoke state hygiene and is Mechanism 2 (mesh-transparent-exit, ozrct) extended across the boundary. REJECTED alternative: switch sub-construct compilation to native LangGraph subgraph-as-node nesting — trades the state-isolated boundary-port invariant for one feature. do0d9 now needs a design step (spike done -> design -> implement) before implementation; it must NOT proceed through disease-scan/review/implement as an impl task.
## Scope decision (2026-07-16, user-directed)
The literal Command.PARENT shape (i) is a PROVEN SILENT SEAM: spiked and confirmed it does not propagate through neograph's isolated sub_graph.invoke() wrapper -- catching it swallows the escape, letting crashes propagate uncaught. This falsifies D-MESH-LEVEL's 'lower to Command(goto) so v2 needs no re-lowering' bet. Recorded in docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md (Mechanism 1 section, 2026-07-15 correction) so the disproven mechanism does not propagate to whoever implements this next.

do0d9 is RE-SCOPED: a neograph-native parent-scoped bubble-up. The wrapper catches the escape intent and writes it onto the parent mesh channel (StateKeys.handoff_payload) for the parent mesh to route on -- NOT literal Command(graph=Command.PARENT,...). Shape (iii) (whole-Construct same-level mesh members) and shape (ii) (parent-peer routing into a sub-construct entry) are explicitly NOT this bead's scope -- (ii) belongs to the entry-label-map mechanism (mechanism 1 in the addressability doc).

do0d9 re-enters the design-first path (spike -> design -> implement, same as ozrct/a37vk), not the direct-implementation task-execute molecule. PULLED OUT of epic neograph-vihe7's task-execute run -- its remaining atoms (disease-scan/review/write-test/implement) are being closed as deferred, not executed against a guessed scope. i3zsh and nnds9 continue through neograph-vihe7 independently.
## Unblocked (2026-07-23)
Both dependencies closed: neograph-ozrct (addressability doc) and neograph-670qe (this task's own design+spike). Ready to implement against docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md -- see that doc's §3.1 for the 5 Node-typed sites the implementation must extend (post-review corrections applied), and §8 finding 5 for the still-unspiked Construct-as-mesh-member integration path that should be proven before closing this task.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-do0d9) — 2026-07-23

Pattern (one-line): Portal-mesh assembly/accounting code gates on `isinstance(member/item, Node)` and would break-or-silently-exclude a `Construct` mesh member (the do0d9 capability).
Disease shape: SYNTACTIC (enumerable via one grep + Portal-context classification; no multi-agent fan-out).

title: construct_from_functions: accept Construct items alongside @node items
description:
construct_from_functions rejects Construct instances with 'not decorated with @node'. This breaks the primary use case for sub-constructs: mixing @node functions with sub-construct pipelines in the same parent.

## The pattern that doesn't work

piarch has 15 @node functions + 1 sub-construct (verify_claim = explore→score) in the same pipeline. The @node functions reference the sub-construct output by parameter name:

    @node(outputs=ClusterMatchResult, mode='gather', ...)
    def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ...: ...

    @node(outputs=ClusterMatchResult, mode='produce', ...)
    def score(explore_result, explore_tool_log) -> ...: ...

    verify_claim = construct_from_functions('verify-claim', [explore, score],
                                            input=VerifyClaim, output=ClusterMatchResult)

    # Parent pipeline: 15 @node functions + 1 sub-construct
    @node(outputs=ConsolidatedDisposition)
    def deterministic_merge(verify_claim: dict[str, ClusterMatchResult], ...) -> ...: ...

    rw_ingestion = construct_from_functions('rw-ingestion', [
        ..., flatten_claims, verify_claim, deterministic_merge, ...
    ])

This fails at TWO points:

1. construct_from_functions line 862: 'argument is not decorated with @node (got Construct)' — rejects verify_claim
2. Even if you splice it in afterward, the @node validator rejects 'deterministic_merge' because parameter 'verify_claim' doesn't match any @node in the list

## What example 13 does differently

Example 13 avoids this by using Construct(nodes=[...]) with Node.scripted for the parent — NOT construct_from_functions with @node. This means the parent pipeline can't use @node's signature-based dependency inference. The workaround defeats the purpose of @node.

## What should work

construct_from_functions should accept both @node items AND Construct items. For Construct items:
- Name: construct.name (already available)
- Output type: construct.output (already declared)
- The validator should resolve @node params against BOTH peer @nodes AND peer Constructs
- Topology: Construct items are opaque — they produce their declared output type

Alternatively: provide construct_from_mixed('name', [@node_fns...], sub_constructs=[...]) if type heterogeneity in the list is a concern.

## Impact

This blocks the gather→produce sub-construct pattern (neograph-4a7 fix) from being usable in @node-based pipelines. Example 13 proves the sub-construct works, but only in the programmatic API — not in the primary @node API that the README leads with.
design:
## Core Invariant
_build_construct_from_decorated must produce the same node ordering and type relationships as a hand-built Construct(nodes=[...]) containing the same Nodes and sub-Constructs.

## Implementation Plan
1. construct_from_functions: accept both Node and Construct items. Separate into two lists. Validate: Nodes must have @node sidecar; Constructs must have output declared.
2. _build_construct_from_decorated: new param sub_constructs: list[Construct]. Register them in decorated dict (field_name -> Construct). They participate in adjacency (as producers) but skip all sidecar-dependent processing.
3. Adjacency: when pname matches a sub-construct field_name, wire the edge. No sidecar check needed.
4. Topo sort: sub-constructs participate like nodes. They get placed in ordered list.
5. Inputs cleanup + scripted shim: skip for Construct items (isinstance check).
6. Final Construct(): include all items (Nodes + Constructs) in topo-sorted order.

~40 lines of changes, all in decorators.py.

### How Construct items differ from Node items

- No inputs/outputs dict (Construct has input/output singular) — use construct.output for producer type
- No mode/fan_out_param/scripted_fn — skip modifier and shim processing

### Pattern from existing code
The Construct.__init__ in construct.py already handles mixed Node+Construct lists: 'nodes: list[Any]'. The compiler's _add_node_to_graph checks isinstance(item, Construct) vs isinstance(item, Node) and dispatches accordingly. So the LOWER LAYERS already handle mixed lists. The gap is purely in the decorator layer's adjacency builder.

### Risks

title: Wrong-driver checkpointer misuse (run+AsyncSqliteSaver / arun+SqliteSaver) fails silently
description: Surfaced in Phase 1e review (neograph-w74k.2.5). Passing an AsyncSqliteSaver to sync run() or a sync SqliteSaver to arun() is user error. _has_existing_checkpoint / _ahas_existing_checkpoint swallow AttributeError/TypeError/KeyError and return False -> a fresh run silently starts, IGNORING an existing checkpoint rather than erroring. TDD: 4 new tests in TestWrongDriverCheckpointerGuard (test_checkpoint_sqlite_async.py) — confirmed RED (InvalidStateError) then GREEN. title: Model compatibility test suite: schema round-trip across strategies and models
description:
Build a test harness that sends a moderately complex Pydantic schema (nested models, enums, lists, optional fields) through each output strategy (structured, json_mode, text) and verifies the round-trip.

Purpose:
- Catch model-specific parsing failures (R1 XML, thinking tags, markdown fences) BEFORE users hit them
- Verify renderer output (BAML/XML/JSON) produces parseable prompts for each model
- Document which models work with which strategies (compatibility matrix)

The schema should be complex enough to expose real issues:
- Nested BaseModel (e.g., Lead with Experience list)
- Enum fields
- Optional fields with defaults
- list[str] and dict fields

Test dimensions:
1. Rendering: how the schema appears in the prompt (describe_type, XmlRenderer, JsonRenderer)
2. Round-trip: schema → rendered prompt → LLM → parse response → validate against original schema
3. Strategies: structured, json_mode, text
4. Models: reason (Claude), fast (Gemini), creative (GPT-4o), and edge cases (R1, Qwen)

This replaces the whack-a-mole approach of discovering and patching parsing edge cases one model at a time.
notes:
## Scale
Target: every model on OpenRouter (100+ models). Run as a scheduled CI job, not just local tests. Results published as a compatibility matrix — which models work with which strategies (structured/json_mode/text) and which renderers (XML/JSON/delimited).

This becomes a feature of neograph itself: 'pick a model, we already know if it works with your pipeline configuration.'

## Implementation sketch
- One parametrized pytest test: @pytest.mark.parametrize over (model, strategy, renderer)
- Model list pulled from OpenRouter API or a maintained YAML
- Complex Pydantic schema as fixture (nested models, enums, optionals, lists)
- Results stored as JSON artifacts — CI publishes to a page on neograph.pro
- Failures are not test failures — they're compatibility data points. Mark as expected/known.

title: DI pre-flight validation in run()
description:
Before starting any node execution, scan all nodes in the compiled graph, collect their required DI params, and validate that all required keys are present in run(input=) and config.

This catches missing params at the gate instead of mid-pipeline. Especially valuable for long pipelines where a missing param on node 5 of 10 wastes the first 4 nodes' execution.

Implementation: in run() (or a new _preflight_di_check), walk the Construct's nodes, collect DIBindings where required=True, check config['configurable'] keys. Raise ExecutionError listing ALL missing params at once (not one at a time).

Files: src/neograph/factory.py or new src/neograph/_preflight.py
Depends on: required=True default (so there are required params to check)
Guard: test that run() with missing required params raises before any node starts (check that node_start log event never fires).
notes:
## Acceptance
- Write test: run() with missing required params raises ExecutionError before any node starts (node_start log never fires)
- Pre-flight scan collects ALL missing params and reports them in one error (not one at a time)
close_reason: Pre-flight DI check in run(): collects all missing required params before graph.invoke().

title: @node decorator: parameter-name dependency inference (Dagster-style)
description:
Source: Dagster @asset, LlamaIndex @step
Effort: Large
Breaks API: No (additive — legacy Node(...)/Construct(nodes=[...]) stays)

# Motivation

KILLER IDEA #1. The function signature IS the dependency graph. No list, no order, no add_edge.

Current NeoGraph:
    decompose = Node('decompose', mode='produce', output=Claims, ...)
    classify  = Node('classify',  mode='produce', input=Claims, output=Classified, ...)
    pipeline  = Construct('rw', nodes=[decompose, classify])

Dagster-style (proposed):
    @node(mode='produce', output=Claims)
    def decompose(topic: str) -> Claims: ...

    @node(mode='produce', output=Classified)
    def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...
    # parameter name 'decompose' matches upstream node 'decompose' → auto-wires

    pipeline = construct_from_module(my_pipeline_module)

Wins:
- No nodes=[...] list, topology inferred from signatures
- Refactor-safe: rename function → downstream parameter is a NameError surface
- Fan-in is free: def report(claims: Claims, scored: Scored, verified: Verified)
- IDE jump-to-definition works on parameter names
- Zero string coupling for topology

Source: .claude/research/dx_research_040426.md #1

---

# Template: how @tool works (mirror this exactly)

Read `src/neograph/tool.py` lines 89-133 fully before writing a line of code. `@node` must follow the same shape:

1. Accepts both `@node` and `@node(...)` forms (see tool.py:130-132 — the `if fn is not None: return decorator(fn)` trick).
2. Inside the inner `decorator(f)`, does a *function-local* import of the factory to dodge the circular import:
       from neograph.factory import register_scripted   # cf. tool.py:116 'register_tool_factory'
3. Returns a `Node` *instance* (NOT the wrapped function). The instance is what downstream code references. The original function is stashed on the instance so the factory can execute it.
4. Auto-registers any side-effect needed for execution (for @tool it's `register_tool_factory`; for @node it's `register_scripted` when mode='scripted').

Sample shape for @node (pseudocode — not for copy-paste, implementer decides final form):

    def node(
        fn: Callable | None = None,
        *,
        mode: Literal["produce", "gather", "execute", "scripted"] = "produce",
        input: Any = None,
        output: Any = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        prompt: str | None = None,
        llm_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        tools: list[Tool] | None = None,
        name: str | None = None,
    ) -> Any:
        def decorator(f: Callable) -> Node:
            from neograph.factory import register_scripted

            node_name = (name or f.__name__).replace("_", "-")
            inferred_input  = input  if input  is not None else _infer_input_from_hints(f)
            inferred_output = output if output is not None else _infer_output_from_hints(f)

            n = Node(
                name=node_name,
                mode=mode,
                input=inferred_input,
                output=inferred_output,
                model=model,
                prompt=prompt,
                llm_config=llm_config or {},
                tools=tools or [],
                scripted_fn=(f.__name__ if mode == "scripted" else None),
            )
            if mode == "scripted":
                register_scripted(f.__name__, f)
            # Stash the original fn + declared param order for construct_from_module
            n.__neo_fn__ = f                           # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            n.__neo_param_names__ = tuple(             # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                p.name for p in inspect.signature(f).parameters.values()
            )
            return n

        if fn is not None:
            return decorator(fn)
        return decorator

Note: stashing `__neo_fn__` / `__neo_param_names__` requires `Node` to tolerate attribute setting. `Node` is a pydantic BaseModel with `model_config = {"arbitrary_types_allowed": True}` (node.py:67). Pydantic v2 BaseModel blocks arbitrary attr-setting by default — implementer must either (a) add `model_config["extra"] = "allow"` locally for decorator use, (b) use a sidecar `WeakValueDictionary[id(node)] -> fn` in decorators.py, or (c) add explicit (but private) fields on Node. The sidecar approach is recommended because it keeps Node's schema clean.

---

# Node class surface (src/neograph/node.py)

Full list of Node fields `@node` must map from decorated function + decorator kwargs:

| Node field      | Source                                                                        |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`          | `name` kwarg if given, else `fn.__name__.replace("_", "-")`                   |
| `mode`          | `mode` kwarg (default `'produce'`)                                            |
| `input`         | `input` kwarg if given, else inferred from the first-non-upstream param's annotation (see precedence below) |
| `output`        | `output` kwarg if given, else `fn.__return_annotation__`                      |
| `model`         | `model` kwarg                                                                 |
| `prompt`        | `prompt` kwarg                                                                |
| `llm_config`    | `llm_config` kwarg (default `{}`)                                             |
| `tools`         | `tools` kwarg (default `[]`)                                                  |
| `scripted_fn`   | `fn.__name__` iff `mode == 'scripted'`; else None                             |
| `raw_fn`        | NOT set by @node — raw_node() already covers that path                        |
| `modifiers`     | NOT set — modifiers applied post-hoc via `| Oracle(...)` etc.                 |

Constructor: `Node(name_=..., **kwargs)` — accepts name positionally or as kwarg (node.py:69-73).

The name->state-field transform `node.name.replace("-", "_")` is the canonical rule (see node.py:147, state.py:65/115, factory.py:107, _construct_validation.py:60). Node names are hyphenated; Python identifiers are underscore-separated. @node MUST use this rule in both directions:
- Function name `make_clusters` → node name `make-clusters`
- Downstream parameter name `make_clusters` → matches node `make-clusters`

---

# Construct assembly (src/neograph/construct.py + _construct_validation.py)

`Construct(nodes=[...])` today:
1. Pydantic model with `name`, `description`, `nodes: list[Node|Construct]`, `input`, `output`, `modifiers`.
2. `__init__` accepts name positionally, then calls `_validate_node_chain(self)` AFTER pydantic validation (construct.py:72-79).
3. `_validate_node_chain` walks nodes in list order, accumulating `(field_name, output_type, label)` producers. For each node with declared input, checks upstream produces a compatible type. Uses `name.replace("-", "_")` for field naming (_construct_validation.py:60).

`construct_from_module(mod)` must:
1. Walk `mod.__dict__` (or `vars(mod)`) collecting every value that `isinstance(x, Node)` AND has the `__neo_fn__` sidecar (so it only picks up @node-built nodes, not plain `Node(...)` instances that happen to be module-level — leave those alone).
2. For each such node, read its stashed `__neo_param_names__` to learn its upstream dependencies (by parameter name).
3. Build name-to-node map keyed by `node.name.replace("-", "_")` (the state-field form, which matches the parameter name).
4. Topologically sort: node N depends on every node whose state-field-name appears in N's param list. Raise `ConstructError` on cycles or unknown params.
5. Raise `ConstructError` if any parameter name does not match a node in the module (v1 rule: no scalar params, all params must be upstream nodes — see decisions below).
6. Hand the sorted list to `Construct(name=mod.__name__.split('.')[-1], nodes=sorted_list)`. From that point on, Construct's own `_validate_node_chain` runs the existing type-compatibility walker, so the IR is IDENTICAL to hand-written Constructs. No new validation path.

Return value: a `Construct` instance — same class, same compile()/run() pipeline.

Default construct name: last segment of `mod.__name__` (e.g. `my_app.pipelines.rw_ingest` → `'rw_ingest'`). Allow override via `construct_from_module(mod, name='...')`.

---

# RESOLVED OPEN QUESTIONS (these are decisions, not debate)

## 1. Parameter-name -> node-name mapping

RULE: `param_name == node.name.replace("-", "_")`.

- Function written as `def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...` binds to node `'decompose'`.
- Function written as `def report(make_clusters: Clusters) -> Report: ...` binds to node `'make-clusters'`.
- `@node` itself derives node name from `fn.__name__.replace("_", "-")`, so a function `def make_clusters(...)` becomes node `'make-clusters'` whose downstream parameters spell it `make_clusters`. Symmetric.
- Explicit `@node(name="custom-label")` kwarg overrides function name; downstream params then use `custom_label` to reference it.

Justification: matches existing state-field convention everywhere in the codebase.

## 2. Where does @node + construct_from_module live?

FILE: new `src/neograph/decorators.py` — does not exist yet, creating it is clean.

Rationale:
- @tool lives in `tool.py` next to `Tool` — the decorator + data class co-location pattern.
- @node is different: the Node class is large and declarative; adding the decorator there would clutter it and create more circular-import surface (decorator needs to `register_scripted` from factory, which already imports Node). A dedicated `decorators.py` keeps `node.py` declarative-only.
- `construct_from_module` belongs next to `@node` because it's the second half of the same feature — it only makes sense with decorated functions as input.
- Alternative considered (rejected): extend `construct.py`. Rejected because `construct.py` should stay focused on the Construct class + its validation entry point.

Export from `neograph/__init__.py`:
    from neograph.decorators import node, construct_from_module
    __all__ += ["node", "construct_from_module"]

## 3. Type-hint-based `input` / `output` inference

PRECEDENCE (strict): explicit decorator kwarg wins; annotation is the fallback.

    @node(mode='produce', output=Classified)              # output explicit
    def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...     # input inferred from param annotation

    @node(mode='produce')
    def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...     # BOTH inferred

    @node(mode='produce', input=SomeOtherThing, output=Classified)
    def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...     # kwargs override annotations entirely

Inference rules:
- `output` fallback = the function's return annotation. If none → `output=None` (Construct will fail at assembly if a state-writing mode needs it).
- `input` fallback = the annotation of the FIRST parameter whose name matches an upstream node. (For multi-param fan-in, the per-node `.input` field only tracks a single type today — matches the existing Node contract. The other params still drive topology; they just don't feed `_extract_input`.) If the function has no parameters, `input=None`.
- When the kwarg is provided, annotations are ignored entirely (not cross-checked). Simpler rule, fewer surprises.

## 4. Fan-out interaction with Each / .map()

DECISION: OUT OF SCOPE for v1.

@node v1 handles 1:1 dependencies only. A parameter annotated `list[ClusterGroup]` whose upstream produces `Clusters` with `groups: list[ClusterGroup]` will NOT auto-generate `Each(over='clusters.groups', ...)`. The developer must still apply `.map(...)` or wrap the node with `Each(...)` manually AFTER decoration.

Rationale: auto-fan-out requires deciding a `key=` expression, which has no safe default. Deferring to v2 keeps v1 small and obvious.

## 5. Positional vs keyword-only params

DECISION: accept positional (match Dagster).

`def classify(decompose: Claims) -> Classified: ...` — `decompose` is a normal positional param. `@node` uses `inspect.signature(fn).parameters` in declaration order; positional, keyword-only, and positional-or-keyword all count the same. `**kwargs` and `*args` are rejected with `ConstructError` at decoration time (no sensible mapping).

## 6. Non-node function parameters (scalars, run-input kwargs)

DECISION: v1 rejects them.

    @node(mode='produce', output=Report)
    def report(claims: Claims, tenant_id: str) -> Report: ...
    # ConstructError: parameter 'tenant_id' in node 'report' does not match any
    # @node in module 'my_pipeline'. All parameters must name upstream nodes.

Error is raised by `construct_from_module(mod)`, not by `@node` itself (because at @node time we don't yet know which other nodes exist in the module).

Scalar / run-input params are a v2 feature. Workaround for v1: put the scalar in a seed scripted node.

---

# Acceptance criteria

Done when ALL of the following hold:

1. `src/neograph/decorators.py` exists and exports:
   - `node` — decorator implementing sections above (explicit-kwargs path + annotation-fallback path, both `@node` and `@node(...)` call shapes).
   - `construct_from_module(mod, name: str | None = None) -> Construct` — topologically sorts the module's @node-built nodes and hands off to `Construct(...)`.
2. `src/neograph/__init__.py` exports `node` and `construct_from_module`; both are appended to `__all__`.
3. New test class `TestNodeDecorator` in `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py` (add it immediately after `TestToolDecorator`, around line 2167). Required tests:
   - `test_node_decorator_basic_chain` — a 2-node scripted chain built with @node + construct_from_module compiles, runs, and produces the expected output.
   - `test_node_decorator_fan_in_three_upstreams` — `def report(a: A, b: B, c: C)` wires correctly; topological order puts `a`, `b`, `c` before `report`.
   - `test_node_decorator_explicit_kwargs_override_annotations` — `@node(output=X)` wins over `-> Y` return annotation.
   - `test_node_decorator_unknown_param_raises` — param name not matching any @node in module raises `ConstructError` with a clear message.
   - `test_node_decorator_topological_ordering` — given a shuffled module-level declaration order, `construct_from_module` still emits nodes in DAG order.
   - `test_node_decorator_name_underscore_to_hyphen` — function `def make_clusters(...)` becomes node `'make-clusters'`; downstream param spelled `make_clusters` resolves correctly.
4. `examples/01b_scripted_pipeline_decorator.py` exists: it is `examples/01_scripted_pipeline.py` rewritten with `@node(mode='scripted', ...)` + `construct_from_module(sys.modules[__name__])`, producing identical output.
5. `pytest` full suite + the new tests pass. No existing test modified (additive only).
6. No changes to `src/neograph/node.py`, `src/neograph/construct.py`, or `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py`. The decorator must work entirely through the existing public constructors. (Exception: if the sidecar-attribute approach from the Node section requires adding `extra='allow'` to Node's `model_config`, that single-line change is permitted, but the WeakValueDictionary approach is preferred to keep node.py untouched.)

---

# Files to read before starting (in this order)

1. `src/neograph/tool.py` lines 89-133 — the `@tool` decorator. This is the template. Understand the two-form invocation trick, the function-local import for circular avoidance, and the "return a spec instance, not the wrapped function" shape.

2. `src/neograph/node.py` (entire file, ~176 lines) — the `Node` class fields, the `Node.__init__(name_, /, **kwargs)` signature, and `Node.scripted(...)` classmethod. Also note `raw_node` at the bottom — it's a different decorator (wraps a LangGraph-style `(state, config)` function) and must not be conflated with `@node`.

3. `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py` lines 38-67 — `_validate_node_chain`. This is the existing producer-labeling logic @construct_from_module will feed into. Pay attention to line 60: `field_name = name.replace("-", "_")` is the state-field naming rule that matches parameter names.

4. `src/neograph/construct.py` (entire file, ~82 lines) — shows that `Construct(nodes=[...])` already does all validation. `construct_from_module` is purely a sort-and-forward shim.

5. `src/neograph/factory.py` lines 38-68 — `register_scripted`, `register_condition`, `register_tool_factory`. `@node(mode='scripted', ...)` must call `register_scripted(fn.__name__, fn)` so the scripted wrapper in factory.py:124 can find the function by name.

6. `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py::TestToolDecorator` at line 2094 — the test-class template. Use the same style: one test verifying the decorator returns the right spec type, additional tests verifying it works end-to-end through `Construct` + `compile` + `run`. Imports (`configure_fake_llm`, `Claims`, etc.) are already at the top of the file.

7. `examples/01_scripted_pipeline.py` (entire file, ~82 lines) — the canonical example. The decorator-port lives next to it as `01b_scripted_pipeline_decorator.py`; same schemas, same scripted functions, same output, but the pipeline is built from @node-decorated functions + `construct_from_module`.

---

# Non-goals (explicit out-of-scope for v1)

- Fan-out auto-generation from `list[T]` annotations (see Decision #4).
- Scalar / run-input parameters (see Decision #6).
- Class-based module walking (`construct_from_module(SomeClass)`). v1 walks module objects only.
- Replacing or deprecating the legacy `Node(...) + Construct(nodes=[...])` API. Both coexist forever.
- Changes to the compile() / run() / runner layer. @node is purely an ergonomic front-end; the IR is unchanged.

Node.py untouched (sidecar pattern via id-keyed dict + weakref.finalize). Scripted @node functions route through raw_fn to support fan-in nodes with N upstream parameters — small deviation from the brief, verified by test_node_decorator_fan_in_three_upstreams. 111/111 passing (103 prior + 2 ebe + 6 dur).

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-c265k
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-c265k` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-c265k/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-c265k
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-c265k)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-c265k --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-c265k --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-c265k/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-c265k codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-c265k/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

       committed values BEFORE committing.

**RM2 -- Phase B's import bookkeeping is internally inconsistent, and it poisons Phase D's
acceptance signal.** Step 4 introduces `_raise_no_agent_spec_lowering(item, combo) -> NoReturn`,
but `NoReturn` is not currently imported (`_agent_spec.py:40` is
`from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, TypeGuard, cast`) and step 7 adds only `assert_never`.

`ModifierCombo` import is NOT dead, ruff F401 does NOT fire, and step 11's stated expectation
("`grep -rln ModifierCombo src/neograph/` collapses from 2 files to 1") is FALSE even when the
migration is entirely correct -- an acceptance signal that fails on a success. Resolve by:
pinning the helper's exact signature in the plan; adding `NoReturn` to the typing import; and
restating step 11's acceptance signal as **zero DISPATCH-CONTEXT `ModifierCombo` occurrences**
(the AST census -- the invariant the guard actually scans). A bare annotation reference is
invisible to `_combo_dispatch_sites` and is harmless.

**RM3 -- The gate command omits the extra that makes the proof run at all.** Step 14 gates on
`uv run --extra dev pytest`, but EVERY artifact proving zero-behaviour-change is
`pytest.importorskip("pyagentspec")`-gated -- `test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py:55`,

because pyagentspec happens to be present in the local `.venv`. On a clean sync the byte-snapshot,
the new T4 pin and the entire matrix SKIP, and the migration lands with its proof never executed.

pytest`, and recording the COLLECTED (not merely passed) count for the four agent-spec files
alongside the 3751 baseline, so a silent skip is visible as a count drop rather than a green run.

UNCONDITIONALLY check `.has_operator` and wrap with `_lower_operator`", and §1.7 prescribes a

ruling (BARE-only postlude here; Phase 7 owns the rest) is CORRECT and the reviewer endorses it --
