title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-tjpn4
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-tjpn4` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjpn4/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-tjpn4
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-tjpn4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjpn4 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjpn4 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjpn4/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-tjpn4 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjpn4/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in

title: Public neograph.testing fakes with a loop-compat guarantee (FakeLLM / install helper) (GH issue 5 addendum)
description:
From GitHub issue 5 addendum. CONSUMER BREAKAGE EVIDENCE: consumers fake the LLM at the llm_factory seam with hand-rolled AIMessage duck-types; the m6d3 agent-cycle refactor coerces messages through LangChain (_to_lc_messages -> add_messages), so every hand-rolled fake broke at once with NotImplementedError: Unsupported message type / MESSAGE_COERCION_FAILURE — with no version bump (editable path dep), looking like an env flake until traced.

THE FAKES ALREADY EXIST AND ARE BATTLE-HARDENED: tests/fakes.py ships StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, GuardFake, StubbornFake, FakeTool, _final_json_content, configure_fake_llm — they survived the f7nt/eoi8/m6d3 refactors because WE update them with every loop change. The consumers broke precisely because they cannot import them. SCOPE: promote the fake contract to a public, supported API: (1) namespace decision FIRST — src/neograph/testing.py is already occupied by the scaffold codegen (bd neograph-gfoq touched it); likely resolution: convert to a neograph/testing/ package (codegen + fakes submodules) or a new neograph.fakes module — decide with a one-line ADR note in the ticket; (2) export a canned FakeLLM(outputs: dict[node_name -> BaseModel|str]) guaranteed compatible with the agent cycle: real langchain_core AIMessage types, bind_tools/with_structured_output/bind surface, empty-tool_calls final-turn semantics, per-node routing INCLUDING the Oracle-merge node_name=='' case (all already implemented in tests/fakes.py — this is extraction+export, not new code); (3) install_fake_llm(monkeypatch, outputs) / pytest-fixture helper patching the llm_factory seam; (4) THE GUARANTEE: a compat test in neograph's own suite drives a public FakeLLM through an agent node end-to-end — any future loop refactor that breaks the public double breaks OUR suite first, not every consumer's; (5) docs page under testing.

ANTI-DUPLICATION: neograph's own tests migrate to import from the public location (or a structural guard pins that tests/fakes.py re-exports from it) — one implementation, two consumers. Optional stretch from the issue (recorded-real/VCR variant): file separately if wanted, NOT in scope. Reply-to-GH cross-link once maintainer approves commenting.
design:
## Core Invariant
There is EXACTLY ONE implementation of the fake LLM contract, and neograph's own test suite consumes it through the public location — so any future loop refactor that breaks the public double breaks OUR suite first, before it can silently break a consumer.

## Implementation Plan
1. NAMESPACE (ADR): convert src/neograph/testing.py -> package src/neograph/testing/: move the codegen verbatim to testing/scaffold.py; testing/__init__.py re-exports scaffold_tests (keeps __main__.py:214 working) and the new public testing API. No neograph.fakes top-level module.
2. EXTRACT, don't rewrite: move the canonical fake bodies (StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, TextFake, FakeTool, GuardFake, StubbornFake, GatedAsyncFake, event_loop_lag_watchdog, _final_json_content) from tests/fakes.py into src/neograph/testing/fakes.py, unchanged. Keep the wiring helpers (build_fake_llm_kwargs, configure_fake_llm alias, build_fake_runtime, drive_agent_via_cycle) — decide which are public vs test-only; at minimum build_fake_llm_kwargs is public.
3. ADD the one genuinely-new piece — a canned FakeLLM(outputs: dict[str, BaseModel|str]) router. It is a callable llm_factory: def __call__(self, tier, *, node_name='', **kw) -> per-node double. For each node_name it wraps a ReActFake configured with empty final tool_calls and final=lambda m: outputs[node_name] (BaseModel) or the string (TextFake/JSON final). MUST: declare node_name in its signature (so _get_llm does not strip it), tolerate node_name=='' (Oracle merge default/fallback), and inherit ReActFake's real-AIMessage + bind_tools + with_structured_output + empty-tool_calls-final-turn surface so think/agent/act/oracle all resolve.
4. ADD install_fake_llm(monkeypatch, outputs) + a pytest fixture. It builds a FakeLLM(outputs) and monkeypatch.setattr's _get_llm to return it at BOTH binding sites — neograph._llm._get_llm AND neograph._tool_loop._get_llm — since _tool_loop imported the symbol into its own namespace. (Consumers who own the compile() call can instead pass llm_factory=FakeLLM(outputs); install_fake_llm is for graphs compiled inside app code the test can't reach.)
5. THE GUARANTEE TEST (neograph's own suite, TDD): drive a public FakeLLM through an AGENT node end-to-end via compile()/run() — copy the tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py shape (or reuse drive_agent_via_cycle). Assert real langchain_core AIMessage types flow, bind_tools/with_structured_output are exercised, the empty-tool_calls final turn parses, per-node routing selects correctly, AND the Oracle-merge node_name=='' path resolves. This test is the tripwire.
6. ANTI-DUPLICATION: rewrite tests/fakes.py to RE-EXPORT everything from neograph.testing.fakes (thin shim) so the 124 'from tests.fakes import' sites keep working with zero churn. Add a structural guard that pins tests/fakes.py as a pure re-export of the public module (bans redefinition). Repoint test_guards_async_fakes.py FAKES_PATH to the public module (or assert the re-export). Add a guard: {modules importing _get_llm} == {sites install_fake_llm patches}.
7. DOCS: add a testing page under the docs 'testing' section documenting FakeLLM(outputs), install_fake_llm(monkeypatch, outputs)/fixture, the loop-compat guarantee, and the node_name routing incl. the '' Oracle-merge key. Update website if API surface page lists testing utilities. (VCR/recorded-real variant is OUT of scope — file separately if wanted.)
notes:
## Findings

### The reuse target (this is extraction+export, NOT new code)
- tests/fakes.py already ships the ENTIRE battle-hardened fake contract: StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, TextFake, FakeTool, GuardFake, StubbornFake, GatedAsyncFake, event_loop_lag_watchdog, _final_json_content, plus the wiring helpers build_fake_llm_kwargs / configure_fake_llm / build_fake_runtime / build_fake_tool_lookup / drive_agent_via_cycle. They survive every loop refactor because we edit them with each change. Consumers broke only because they cannot import them.
- ReActFake (tests/fakes.py:256) is the exemplar double for the loop-compat guarantee: it ALREADY implements the full agent-cycle surface — bind_tools()/abind_tools() (return self so counter persists), with_structured_output() (clone), invoke() that emits real langchain_core AIMessage, empty-tool_calls final-turn semantics (_final_message -> _final_json_content), and history-driven turn indexing (neograph-m6d3: counts prior tool-call turns in message history so it works whether the agent runs as one node body OR a cycle of supersteps). The public canned FakeLLM router should wrap ReActFake per node, not reinvent a double.

### The llm_factory seam (SINGLE resolution point, two import bindings)
- llm_factory is a compile() kwarg (compiler.py:65), captured into the frozen LlmRuntime bundle (_llm_runtime.py:55). It is NOT a module global — there is no default factory to patch.
- Resolution funnels through ONE function: _get_llm(runtime, tier, node_name=..., llm_config=...) in _llm.py:93. It calls runtime.llm_factory(tier, **kwargs) where kwargs are FILTERED to the params the factory declares (_llm.py:120-125 via LlmRuntime.llm_factory_params). So a router factory that declares node_name will receive it; a lambda tier: fake ignores it. This is exactly the per-node routing hook.
- BOTH LLM paths resolve via _get_llm: produce/think at _llm.py:191, and the agent/tool ReAct path at _tool_loop.py:312 (used by _agent_cycle prep). CRITICAL: _tool_loop.py:23 does 'from neograph._llm import _get_llm', binding the function into its own namespace — so monkeypatching neograph._llm._get_llm alone will NOT affect the agent path. install_fake_llm must patch _get_llm at BOTH binding sites (neograph._llm and neograph._tool_loop).

### Oracle-merge node_name=='' case
- _oracle.py:273 calls invoke_structured(runtime, model_tier=oracle.merge_model, ...) WITHOUT passing node_name, so _get_llm defaults node_name='' (_llm.py:96). A per-node routing FakeLLM must accept '' as the merge key (or provide a merge default), else Oracle pipelines KeyError.

### Current wiring pattern (the current way; nothing deprecated here)
- Post-ezqz: configure_llm() (module-state mutation) is GONE. Current way = pass llm_factory=/prompt_compiler= as compile() kwargs. build_fake_llm_kwargs(factory) returns that dict; tests splat compile(c, **build_fake_llm_kwargs(lambda tier: fake)). configure_fake_llm is now a back-compat alias returning the same dict (tests/fakes.py:792). Exemplar call sites: tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:163-167,324,385,473.

### Anti-duplication surface

- tests/fakes.py:48 _final_json_content — renders a final no-tool turn as parseable JSON (neograph-f7nt: agent parses final turn directly). Load-bearing for the empty-tool_calls final-turn guarantee.
- src/neograph/_llm.py:93-125 _get_llm — THE seam. node_name + llm_config are param-filtered before calling runtime.llm_factory(tier, **kwargs).
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:23,312 — second binding of _get_llm; the agent/ReAct resolution point. Must be patched too.

Only ONE internal importer: src/neograph/__main__.py:214 'from neograph.testing import scaffold_tests'. pyproject packages=['src/neograph']; converting testing.py->testing/ package is packaged automatically.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NAMESPACE ADR (one line): RECOMMEND converting src/neograph/testing.py -> a neograph/testing/ package (submodules scaffold.py [move codegen verbatim] + fakes.py [extracted fakes], __init__.py re-exports scaffold_tests for back-compat AND the public FakeLLM/install_fake_llm) rather than a separate neograph.fakes module — because the scaffold codegen already emits FakeLLM as the intended test double (testing.py:145-167) and the docs page lives 'under testing', so co-locating keeps one discoverable testing umbrella; only one internal importer (__main__.py:214) needs no change thanks to the __init__ re-export.

title: Four verified small correctness bugs: merge-hook error names wrong param; GraphBubbleUp swallowed in merge twins; sequential parallel tool calls; _notify_cost double-count (review 080726_2107)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md, all four VERIFIED:
1. _validation_modifiers.py:185 — the merge-hook check reads param_names[variants_idx] (index 1 for merge_post_process) but the raised message interpolates param_names[0], pointing the user at the RESULT param where it means the VARIANTS param. One-line fix (bind variants_name once) + a test asserting the message names the right param for merge_post_process.
2. _oracle.py:287/361 — the two merge_prompt twins swallow GraphBubbleUp into merge_fallback where make_each_redirect_fn (:619) correctly re-raises it before the broad except. VERIFIED asymmetry: with a user merge_fallback set, a HITL-interrupt/cancellation bubbling through the merge LLM call is treated as a merge failure. Low blast radius today, latent the moment a merge hook can bubble. Add the same except GraphBubbleUp: raise guard to both twins (shared helper per twin-thinness) + a test with a bubbling fake.
3. _agent_cycle.py:604 — parallel tool calls in ONE ReAct turn are awaited sequentially in atools_body: latency n_tools x RTT where ~max(RTT) is achievable. Fix ASYNC TWIN ONLY (sync body stays sequential — no threads): asyncio.gather the per-call coros, record results in the original tool_call order (ToolMessage/ToolInteraction ordering is part of the message-history contract — pin it), preserve budget-tracker correctness under concurrency (the tracker mutates shared state — guard with the established lock pattern or pre-reserve budget before gathering). Latency, not correctness — but it is the difference between a demo agent and a production one on multi-tool turns.
4. _llm.py:178 _notify_cost — callback-arity detection via except TypeError RE-INVOKES the callback if the user's body raises TypeError for a real reason -> double-counted cost. The codebase already has _accepted_params signature introspection — use it once instead of catching. Test: a callback whose body raises TypeError must not be invoked twice.
Gates y5ux.
notes:
Four correctness bugs, each TDD (failing test written first, verified RED, then fixed):
1) _validation_modifiers.py: bound variants_name=param_names[variants_idx] once; the merge-hook variant-type-mismatch message now names the VARIANTS param (index 1 for merge_post_process) instead of the hardcoded param_names[0] (the RESULT param). Test: test_post_process_variant_error_names_the_variants_param.
2) _oracle.py: extracted _merge_fallback_or_reraise() shared by both merge_prompt twins — re-raises GraphBubbleUp (HITL interrupt/Command/cancellation) BEFORE applying merge_fallback, mirroring make_each_redirect_fn. Both twins now call it. Tests: TestMergePromptBubbleUp (sync+async re-raise, + negative fallback-still-works).
3) _agent_cycle.py: atools_body (async twin ONLY) now asyncio.gathers per-call coros via _ainvoke_tool_timed. Budget PRE-RESERVED in tool_call order before gather (tracker.record_call moved out of _record_tool_result into new _build_tool_interaction; sync twin unchanged via _record_tool_result). Results assembled in ORIGINAL tool_call order. Tests: TestAsyncParallelToolCalls (concurrency via asyncio.Barrier deadlock proof = RED before fix; ordering pin; budget-under-concurrency pin; sync-unchanged pin).
4) _llm.py:_notify_cost: replaced try cb(**full) except TypeError: cb(**core) arity probe with _accepted_params() introspection ONCE + single invocation. A callback whose BODY raises TypeError is no longer re-invoked (was double-counting cost). Tests: test_notify_cost.py (body-TypeError-once = RED before fix, + reduced/full/kwargs signature dispatch).
Gates: mypy+ruff clean on all changed src; all new + touched tests green.
close_reason: 4 verified correctness bugs fixed TDD (wrong-param msg, GraphBubbleUp swallow, sequential parallel tools, cost double-count)

title: Rename node modes: produce→think, gather→agent, execute→act
description:
Rename three node mode strings to Matrix-inspired, self-explanatory names. Breaking change at 0.2.0.dev — one consumer (piarch), zero mode= declarations to update there.

## Mapping

|-----|-----|-----------|

title: ARCH: dedup comparison-operator->callable table (conditions._OPS vs forward._OP_MAP)
description:
Found by neograph-wpzg codebase disease scan. conditions.py:17 _OPS and forward.py:66 _OP_MAP are the same 6-entry table (<,<=,>,>=,==,!= -> operator.lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne), reordered but semantically identical. A new operator must be added in both. conditions.py owns the canonical table.

Fix: forward.py imports conditions._OPS (or a shared public OPERATORS constant). Note the layering implication: forward.py (DX layer) importing conditions.py — verify this does not create an undesirable dependency; if it does, promote the table to a neutral low-level module. Add a structural guard pinning single-table ownership. Out of scope for neograph-wpzg.
design:
## Core Invariant
The comparison-operator->callable table has exactly one definition (conditions.OPERATORS); every consumer imports it rather than re-declaring the mapping.

## Implementation Plan
1. conditions.py: rename canonical table to public OPERATORS (keep '_OPS = OPERATORS' internal alias so existing refs + test docstrings stay valid). 
2. forward.py: delete the _OP_MAP literal; add 'from neograph.conditions import OPERATORS'; change forward.py:298 to OPERATORS[self._op]. Keep 'import operator as op_module' (op_module.truth at :781 still needs it).
3. Structural guard (test_guards_helper_monopoly.py, new class): AST guard asserting the comparison-op dict literal (values operator.lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne) is defined in exactly ONE src module (conditions.py), plus forward.py imports OPERATORS from conditions. Positive + negative meta-tests.
4. make quality; baseline holds.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-97c6.18)
- conditions._OPS (conditions.py:17) and forward._OP_MAP (forward.py:66) are the SAME 6-entry comparison-operator table (<,<=,>,>=,==,!= -> operator.lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne), reordered, op_module is an alias for operator.
- conditions.py owns the canonical table (the safe-condition evaluator). It is a stdlib-only LEAF module (imports operator, re, collections.abc, typing — ZERO neograph imports). forward.py already imports construct/errors/modifiers/naming/node.
- Layering: forward.py (DX layer) -> conditions.py is a clean downward dependency to a leaf; NO import cycle (conditions imports no neograph module). No need to promote to a neutral module.
- _OP_MAP used only at forward.py:298 (op_fn = _OP_MAP[self._op]). _OPS used at conditions.py:125,128,131. NO external importers of either table.
- forward.py:781 uses op_module.truth and :53 'import operator as op_module' -> the operator import must STAY (truthy fallback), only the duplicate table is removed.
- tests/test_conditions.py references '_OPS' only in docstrings/comments (lines 297,305,307) — not as an imported symbol; safe to keep _OPS as an internal alias.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/conditions.py:17-24 (canonical), :125-131 (usage)
- src/neograph/forward.py:66-73 (duplicate), :298 (usage), :781 op_module.truth
- tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py — home for the single-table-ownership guard

Pattern: comparison-operator(<,<=,>,>=,==,!=)->callable(operator.lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne) dict table re-declared instead of importing the canonical conditions table.
Disease shape: SYNTACTIC -> single-executor scan, no fan-out.
Scan commands (reproducible):
  grep -rn ': operator\.\|: op_module\.' src/neograph/*.py
  grep -rln '\.lt\b\|\.le\b\|\.gt\b\|\.ge\b' src/neograph/*.py
Total tables found: 2 (both cited; no hidden third instance).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | conditions.py:17-24 (_OPS) | 6-entry op->callable | MIGRATE(home) | promote to public OPERATORS; canonical owner |
| 2 | forward.py:66-73 (_OP_MAP) | same 6-entry table (op_module alias) | MIGRATE | delete literal; import conditions.OPERATORS; :298 -> OPERATORS[self._op] |

No DEFER, no other ALLOWLIST instances. SYNTACTIC => no targeted-scan artifact dir required.

- [LOW] Invariant alignment: single canonical OPERATORS in conditions.py; forward imports it. Exactly satisfies the invariant.
- [LOW] Layering verified: conditions.py is a stdlib-only leaf (0 neograph imports) -> forward.py->conditions.py is a clean downward edge, no cycle. The assembly import-DAG guard (test_guards_assembly TestAssemblyImportDAG) governs only the {factory,_execute,_oracle,_state_write,_input_shape,_subconstruct} cluster; forward/conditions are out of scope and external edges are unenforced. No guard violated. Promoting to a 'neutral module' is unnecessary.
- [LOW] op_module retained: 'import operator as op_module' must stay (op_module.truth at forward.py:781). Only the duplicate _OP_MAP literal is removed.
- [LOW] Naming: public OPERATORS + internal '_OPS = OPERATORS' alias keeps conditions.py internal refs (and test_conditions.py docstrings mentioning _OPS) valid with minimal churn.
- [LOW] Guard: AST detection of the comparison-op dict literal (>=4 values being operator/op_module .lt/.le/.gt/.ge/.eq/.ne) must appear in exactly ONE module; plus assert forward imports OPERATORS. Positive+negative meta-tests.

Overall: ALL_LOW

title: Loop skip_when without skip_value — semantic ambiguity on re-entry
description: When skip_when fires with skip_value=None inside a Loop, the counter increments but no value is appended to the output list. Next iteration reads the PREVIOUS iteration's output (or upstream seed). The skip is effectively invisible to the data flow. Document this behavior or require skip_value when Loop is present.

title: Docs + example: Each+Oracle+Loop pipeline shown side-by-side with its Agent Spec Flow
description: Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s5, s10.8. Runnable example + website page. Show a compact neograph pipeline (Each + Oracle + Loop, a few @node/pipe lines) side-by-side with the flat Agent Spec Flow it lowers to (many nodes + explicit ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge). This is BOTH the fidelity spec AND the marketing asset: 'here are 3 lines; here is the 40-line Agent Spec they compile to -- same behavior, type-checked before it ran.' Update website/ (run npm run build) and add examples/ entry per CLAUDE.md example conventions. Blocked by the tests task.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: the shown Agent Spec text on the docs page must be EXACTLY what to_agent_spec() emits for the shown pipeline -- no hand-abridged JSON, no rhetorical line-count that doesn't match the real dump.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (fused vs three-panel): commit to THREE SEPARATE minimal panels (Each, Oracle, Loop), each directly adapted from the three already-proven pipelines in tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:87-195 (TestEachOracleLoopRoundTripPreservesBehavior). Do NOT attempt a single fused Each->Oracle->Loop construct -- it is unproven and risks assembly-validation errors with no existing test backing it. Adjust the page's marketing framing from '3 lines -> one 40-line Flow' to 'three compact modifiers, each collapsing N lines of hand-wired Agent Spec' (one comparison per modifier), consistent with the design doc's own per-modifier fidelity table (s5).

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (line-count accuracy): for each of the three panels, generate the Agent Spec side via to_agent_spec(pipeline).to_dict() (the confirmed current pattern, examples/29_portal_dynamic_flow.py:149) and compute the ACTUAL line count of the serialized dump (e.g. json.dumps(flow.to_dict(), indent=2).count(chr(10)) or similar) -- use that real number as the headline, never a guessed/rhetorical one. If a human-readable summary (not raw JSON) is shown instead of the raw dump, it must be mechanically derived from the live Flow object (e.g. a small script printing node names + edge count), never hand-abridged.

Oracle panel must use mode='think' + a keyless fake LLM (StructuredFake, matching test_agent_spec_export.py's own Oracle test) -- scripted-mode Oracle round-trip is known-broken and must not be used or silently glossed over; the doc page's fidelity notes must state this limitation explicitly (consistent with docs/design s6 lossy-callable-fields).

Everything else (example number 31, examples/30_hot_swap_agent_spec.py docstring convention, website/src/content/docs/runtime/agent-spec.mdx + astro.config.mjs sidebar entry, api-manifest symbols) stays as originally researched -- unchanged by this refinement.
notes:
## Findings

title: ForwardConstruct expressiveness parity: forward() must express every topology the declarative form can (identical IR)
description:
## Invariant (the whole point)
Every topology the declarative Construct form can express, ForwardConstruct.forward() must ALSO express — tracing to IDENTICAL IR. The forward.py docstring already promises this for straight-line pipelines (:15); this epic extends it to the full modifier/composition surface. Parity is BOUNDED BY declarative capability (ForwardConstruct need not exceed it — e.g. Each x Oracle fusion on sub-constructs is a documented declarative non-support and stays out of scope for both).

## Why we absolutely need to ship this
The imperative 'write the graph as Python control flow' DX is compelling but appears in ZERO apps (only demo example 15) — NOT because it's unwanted, but because its expressible topology set is a tiny subset (straight-line + per-node fan-out keyed 'label' + node-only loops + constant-comparison branches). Real agent pipelines need fan-out-inside-loop over sub-constructs, ensembles, HITL — none expressible today. The fix is PARITY, not new IR: the tracer is artificially stricter than the IR it already targets.

## Authoritative analysis
docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md — tracer mechanism (torch.fx symbolic proxy), the full capability x coverage x difficulty table, per-gap fix shapes with code sites, acceptance principle, anti-band-aid parity-matrix guard, phasing, effort, independent-review gate.

## The load-bearing fixes (PHASE 1 — ship first, ~2-3 days, zero IR/compiler changes, all in forward.py)
Both blockers are 'teach the tracer to emit what the IR already accepts', with self.loop() as the working blueprint:
1. self.each(body=[...], over=..., key=...) mirroring _LoopCall/self.loop() (:462-621): build Construct(input=,output=,nodes=body) | Each(over,key,on_error=), record_construct, return proxy. ~40 lines. Keep bare 'for x in proxy' as sugar for the trivial single-node/key='label' case. FIXES: custom key + fan-out over a SUB-CONSTRUCT (today :652 hardcodes key='label' and applies Each PER-NODE).
2. Relax self.loop() body validation (:491-498) to accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall/_EachCall results) alongside _NodeCall. Construct(nodes=...) already takes list[Node|Construct]; reuse _declared_output port inference (:519). FIXES: Loop over a sub-construct body (loop containing an Each fan-out) — the exact cascade shape.
3. Verify (mark with tests): fan-in multi-input node calls; multi-output dict nodes ({node}_{key} wiring through tracing).

## PHASE 2 (medium)
Oracle (ensemble_n+merge) is ENTIRELY ABSENT from forward() today (Oracle not even imported; no self.ensemble()). Operator/interrupt_when (HITL) not exposed. Add self.ensemble()/HITL tracing surfaces that build the EXISTING modifiers. Verify skip_when/skip_value survive tracing.

## PHASE 3 (hard — CLOSE or CAP)
Branch richness (re-trace is 2^N, constant-comparisons only, max 8 — :33-36) and try/except fallback (dead-code under symbolic tracing, :38-47). These do NOT block the unused-making topologies (the cascade 'branch' is an LLM output field, not graph control flow). Recommendation: keep as documented v1 limits with a LOUD escape to the declarative form rather than a fragile 2^N expansion. Decide during the epic.

## Acceptance — one verifiable principle
Traced IR == declarative IR, per topology class (graph-lint diff clean). Reference integration test = the cascade shape (intake -> triage -> Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key='id') }) -> explain): a ForwardConstruct expressing it must trace to the SAME IR the declarative ox cascade compiles.

## Anti-band-aid
Do NOT special-case the cascade. Deliverable is PARITY enforced by a PARITY TEST MATRIX: a corpus of declarative topologies, each with a forward() twin, asserted IR-identical. Permanent guard = a property test comparing traced IR to declarative IR across the corpus, so a new declarative capability lacking a forward() path FAILS LOUD (the parity ratchet). New tracer surfaces must build EXISTING IR, never ForwardConstruct-only IR.

## Independent-review gate
The DSL-surface design (bare-for sugar vs explicit self.each(); how loop/each compose+nest; keep the key='label' default?) is an API decision — fresh-context reviewer confirms BEFORE Phase 1. Review the parity matrix for coverage.

## Not 0.6.0-gating (0.6 shipped). Post-0.6, HIGH priority (maintainer: 'we absolutely need to ship this').
notes:
## PHASE 3 DECISION (2026-07-11): CAP, not close
Branch richness and try/except remain documented v1 limits with a LOUD declarative escape (per the design doc recommendation, executed by neograph-e9zse.7):
- Non-constant (proxy-vs-proxy) comparisons now raise ConstructError at trace time naming the limit + the declarative escape (previously traced silently and misbehaved at runtime).
- The _MAX_BRANCHES error hint now names the 2^N re-trace cost and the declarative escape.
- try/except stays docs-only (the except arm is unobservable under symbolic tracing — undetectable at trace time); module docstring + website branching page state the cap and the escape.
Rationale: these do NOT block the topologies that made ForwardConstruct unused (verified by the shipped parity corpus); a 2^N expansion would be fragile with low marginal value.
2026-07-11 POST-SHIP ADVERSARIAL VERIFY (fresh-context, worktree, 8 claims): 7 CONFIRMED via executed mutation probes — deep IR-equality helper catches Each key/on_error + Loop max_iterations divergence (3 valid-IR mutations each RED); cascade runs end-to-end (fan-out key mutation caught both integration + IR row); self.each==X|Each and each-in-loop IR-identical; ensemble/interrupt form-aware sharing _ModifierWrapCall, emit only existing Oracle/Operator IR; Phase-3 proxy-vs-proxy cap raises loud at trace time; no ForwardConstruct-only IR leaked. ONE REFUTED: the parity RATCHET is tautological (REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES derived from PARITY_CORPUS itself) — filed neograph-zrcln. Feature is correct; the forward-looking anti-drift guard is not yet real.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE. Phase 1: self.each() (a2834d6), loop-over-sub-construct + nesting (d208f55), verify tests (1209cef), parity matrix + ratchet (a78ef37). Phase 2: self.ensemble() (fbf9408), self.interrupt() (3dac12b). Phase 3: CAP decision executed (26346d6). Traced IR == declarative IR enforced by the parity corpus; PHASE2_PENDING empty; cascade reference topology expressible and running.

title: P1: self.each() tracing surface — fan-out over sub-construct with custom key
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 1, fix #1. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What
Add self.each(body=[...], over=..., key=..., on_error=...) to ForwardConstruct's _ForwardSelf in src/neograph/forward.py, mirroring the existing self.loop()/_LoopCall machinery (forward.py:462-621) as the blueprint:
- Build Construct(input=, output=, nodes=body) | Each(over=over, key=key, on_error=on_error)
- record_construct into the tracer, return an output proxy
- Reuse _declared_output port inference for input/output boundary types
- Keep the existing bare `for x in proxy` form as sugar for the trivial single-node / key="label" case (today forward.py:652 hardcodes key="label" and applies Each PER-NODE — that path stays as sugar; self.each() is the general form)

## Fixes
(a) custom Each key (not just "label"); (b) fan-out over a SUB-CONSTRUCT (multi-node body wrapped as one Each'd sub-construct); (c) on_error pass-through (e.g. 'collect').

## Core Invariant
New tracer surfaces must emit ONLY existing IR (Construct | Each) — identical to what the equivalent declarative form produces. Never ForwardConstruct-only IR. Zero changes to IR/compiler modules (node.py, construct.py, _construct_validation.py, compiler.py, factory.py, state.py, modifiers.py).

## Independent-review gate (from the epic — review atom must cover)
DSL-surface API decisions: bare-for sugar vs explicit self.each() builder; how self.loop()/self.each() compose and nest; whether key="label" default stays. The review atom is the fresh-context reviewer the epic requires BEFORE Phase 1 implementation.

## Acceptance
A forward() twin of declarative `Construct(input=X, output=Y, nodes=[a, b]) | Each(over=..., key="id")` traces to IDENTICAL IR (same nodes list, same modifier params, graph-diff clean). Tested via TDD: failing IR-equality test first.
design:
## Core Invariant
New tracer surfaces emit ONLY existing IR — self.each() must produce a node list byte-identical to the declarative `Construct(input=X, output=Y, nodes=[...]) | Each(over, key, on_error)` twin, with zero changes outside src/neograph/forward.py (no IR/compiler/validator edits).

## Confirmed API shape (review gate resolved 2026-07-11)
TWO-STEP, mirroring _LoopCall: `each_verify = self.each(body=[self.verify], key='id', on_error='raise')` returns a deferred _EachCall; `results = each_verify(items.claims)` (proxy) or `each_verify('seed.claims')` (raw string, Option C inference) builds the sub-construct, records it, returns the output proxy.

## Implementation Plan (TDD: failing IR-equality test first)
1. TEST FIRST (tests/test_forward.py, new class TestSelfEachTracing): build the declarative twin from tests/test_composition.py:3190-3229 (seed -> Construct(input=FanItem,...)|Each(over='seed.items', key='item_id')) and a ForwardConstruct using two-step self.each(); assert traced nodes list is IR-identical (names, node lists, input/output boundary ports, Each params incl. on_error). Verify it FAILS before implementing.
2. Extract the proxy->over-path computation inline in _Tracer.record_iteration (forward.py:377-385) into a module-level helper (field_name_for + _attr_chain_after_prefix); record_iteration calls it — zero behavior change.
3. Add _EachCall (sibling of _LoopCall, forward.py:462-567, copy-adapt):
   - __init__(tracer, body, key, on_error='raise'): validate body items are _NodeCall (same errors as _LoopCall:491-505), non-empty
   - __call__(over): _Proxy -> over_path via helper from step 2; str -> Option C root inference: reverse-resolve the root segment to a traced node (field_name_for inverse over tracer-recorded nodes), fail loud (ConstructError.build) at trace time if root unmatched
   - item_type inference: normalize_outputs(_declared_output(over_source)).primary, walk attr segments with _resolve_field_annotation, then _extract_list_element (neograph._validation_types); fail loud when uninferrable (mirror forward.py:524-528)
   - output_type = normalize_outputs(body_nodes[-1].outputs).primary
   - body copies via model_copy(update={'inputs': item_type}) ONLY when inputs is None (copy-not-mutate, neograph-2o9n)
   - deterministic name 'each-{body_slug}' with PER-KIND occurrence counter (generalize next_loop_occurrence so loop/each over the same slug do not share a counter)
   - build Construct(name, input=item_type, output=output_type, nodes=copies) | Each(over=over_path, key=key, on_error=on_error); tracer.record_construct(sub); return _Proxy(source_node=sub, name=f'out_of_{name}')
4. Add _ForwardSelf.each(body, key, on_error='raise') next to .loop() (forward.py:600-621) returning _EachCall.
5. Keep bare-for sugar untouched (_apply_loop_modifiers, forward.py:638-654, key='label' per-node) — test pins both forms coexist; note they are NOT IR-identical twins (per-node vs wrapped sub-construct) by design.
6. More tests: on_error='collect' pass-through; multi-node body; class-level Node non-mutation (mirror TestLoopCallDoesNotMutateClassNodes); error paths (empty body, non-_NodeCall body item, uninferrable item type, raw-string root unmatched); raw-string over happy path (Option C); re-trace determinism for loop+each over same body slug.
7. Gates: uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_forward.py tests/test_composition.py, then full suite + ruff + mypy.
notes:
## Findings (research, 2026-07-10)

REUSE TARGET (the blueprint, per design doc + confirmed in code): `_LoopCall` + `_ForwardSelf.loop()` in src/neograph/forward.py:462-621. self.each() is a copy-adapt of this machinery: an `_EachCall` that builds `Construct(input=item_type, output=..., nodes=body_copies) | Each(over=..., key=..., on_error=...)`, calls `tracer.record_construct(sub)` (forward.py:353), and returns `_Proxy(source_node=sub, name=f'out_of_{name}')`. Zero IR/compiler changes needed — the IR already accepts Construct|Each (exemplar below).

- Declarative twin ALREADY WORKS and is the parity oracle: tests/test_composition.py:3190-3229 (`TestEachOnErrorCollect._build_parent`) builds `Construct('eok4-sub', input=FanItem, output=RawText, nodes=[...]) | Each(over='eok4_seed.items', key='item_id', on_error=...)` inside a parent Construct. This is the exact shape self.each() must emit.
- Each modifier: src/neograph/modifiers.py:484-510 — fields `over: str` (dotted path), `key: str`, `on_error: Literal['raise','collect']='raise'`. Pass all three through verbatim.
- over-path from a proxy: the bare-for sugar already computes it — `_Tracer.record_iteration` forward.py:377-385 (`field_name_for(source.name)` + `_attr_chain_after_prefix`). Extract/reuse that computation (module-level helper) rather than duplicating it in _EachCall.
- Item-type inference (the sub's `input=` port): reuse `_resolve_field_annotation` + `_extract_list_element` from src/neograph/_validation_types.py:135,213 (leaf module, no import-cycle risk — forward.py already imports from _normalize the same way). Walk: `normalize_outputs(_declared_output(over_source)).primary` -> resolve each attr segment -> extract list element = item type. Assembly validation then re-checks it via `_check_each_path` (src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:188-240), so a wrong inference fails loud at Construct.__init__.
- Output type: `normalize_outputs(body_nodes[-1].outputs).primary` — identical to _LoopCall forward.py:517.
- Copy-not-mutate: _LoopCall model_copy's body nodes to set `inputs` without mutating class-level Nodes (forward.py:541-545, pinned by TestLoopCallDoesNotMutateClassNodes, neograph-2o9n). self.each() body copies must do the same with `inputs=item_type`.
- Deterministic naming: mirror `next_loop_occurrence` (forward.py:357-366) — name `each-{body_slug}` + occurrence suffix so branch re-trace passes produce identical names. NOTE: the existing counter dict is keyed by body_slug only; either key it by `(kind, slug)` or include the 'each'/'loop' prefix in the slug so a loop and an each over the same body don't share a counter.
- Bare `for x in proxy` sugar STAYS: `_apply_loop_modifiers` forward.py:638-654 applies Each PER-NODE with hardcoded key='label' (line 652). Do not change it; self.each() is the general form (custom key, multi-node body, on_error).
- Current vs old: no deprecated pattern in play — forward.py is actively maintained (recent monopoly refactors b7dd223/d9e9731 moved `_declared_output`/`normalize_outputs` into _normalize; USE those, not `getattr(item,'output',None)` — TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly bans the inline form).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:462-567 — _LoopCall: the exemplar to copy-adapt (validation, type inference, naming, record_construct, output proxy)
- src/neograph/forward.py:600-621 — _ForwardSelf.loop(): where the sibling `each()` method goes
- src/neograph/forward.py:73-88, 377-385 — _attr_chain_after_prefix + record_iteration over-path build: reuse for proxy->over-path
- src/neograph/forward.py:638-654 — bare-for sugar (key='label', per-node Each): keep as-is
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:484-510 — Each(over, key, on_error) signature
- src/neograph/_validation_types.py:135, 213 — _resolve_field_annotation / _extract_list_element for item-type inference
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:188-240 — _check_each_path: assembly-time safety net that re-validates the emitted over path
- tests/test_composition.py:3190-3229 — declarative Construct|Each twin, the IR-equality oracle
- tests/test_forward.py:225, 892-1030, 1396+ — output-identity test pattern, TestSelfLoopTracing, TestLoopCallDoesNotMutateClassNodes, direct-_LoopCall unit tests: the test templates to mirror for _EachCall
- tests/hypothesis/conftest.py — FanItem/FanCollection schemas already used by the declarative twin

## Data-flow trace (one concrete example)
forward(): `items_out = self.seed(x); results = self.each(body=[self.verify], over=items_out.items, key='item_id')` -> _EachCall computes over_path 'seed.items' (field_name_for + attr chain), infers item_type=FanItem (seed.outputs=FanCollection -> .items -> list[FanItem]), copies verify with inputs=FanItem, builds Construct('each-verify', input=FanItem, output=MatchResult, nodes=[copy]) | Each(over='seed.items', key='item_item_id'... key='item_id', on_error='raise'), record_construct, returns proxy(source=sub). Construct.__init__ -> _validate_node_chain -> _check_each_path confirms 'seed.items' lands on list[FanItem]. compile() -> _wiring._collect_each_items router + barrier. Downstream consumers see dict[str, MatchResult] via effective_producer_type.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- API-shape decision (flagged for the epic's independent-review gate, NOT resolved here): _LoopCall is two-step (`self.loop(...)(proxy)`); for each, `over=` already carries the input binding, so a one-step `self.each(body, over=proxy.attr, key=...)` returning the output proxy directly is more natural and is what the bead text implies ('return an output proxy'). Recommend one-step; reviewer confirms.
- `over` should accept BOTH a _Proxy (traced, primary) and a raw string (declarative-parity escape when the collection root isn't a traced proxy). String form skips inference only if item type can't be derived — then fail loud (mirror _LoopCall's 'input type could not be inferred' error, forward.py:524-528).
- self.each() recorded INSIDE a bare `for x in proxy` loop: record_construct does not tag _loop_body_nodes (only record() does), so the sub-construct will NOT get an extra Each wrap — correct, but add a test pinning it (or an explicit ConstructError if nesting-under-sugar is disallowed).
- Loop/each occurrence-counter collision on same body slug (see Findings) — key the counter per kind.
- multi-node body: intermediate body nodes' inputs must chain node-to-node inside the sub (first node gets item_type; later nodes' edges come from their own Node.inputs). Only default-fill `inputs` when None, exactly like _LoopCall.
- Composition with e9zse.2 (loop body accepting each results) is explicitly the NEXT ticket; do not widen _LoopCall validation in this one.
- No doc/code contradictions found; design doc matches code (line refs :652, :491-498, :519 all verified accurate).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-e9zse.1)

Pattern: proxy->over-path computation (field_name_for + _attr_chain_after_prefix) and traced-Each construction inlined per call-site instead of routed through one shared helper.
Scan command: grep -rn "Each(" src/neograph/ ; grep -rn "_attr_chain_after_prefix" src/neograph/ ; grep -n "field_name_for" src/neograph/forward.py
Total instances found: 5

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | forward.py:377-385 | inline over-path build in record_iteration | MIGRATE | extract module-level helper (plan step 2); _EachCall reuses it |
| 2 | forward.py:652 | Each(over, key='label') per-node sugar | ALLOWLIST | documented bare-for sugar, stays per design; will consume the extracted helper's over_path |
| 3 | forward.py:294 | _attr_chain_after_prefix call | ALLOWLIST | different concern (node-call input attr chain, not Each over-path); already uses shared low-level helper |
| 4 | modifiers.py:377 | map_over sugar builds Each | ALLOWLIST | declarative-side canonical sugar, not tracer logic |
| 5 | loader.py:269 | Each from YAML spec | ALLOWLIST | spec loader passes spec fields verbatim; distinct surface |

No DEFER rows. Scope unchanged — design already covers the single MIGRATE instance.
## Architect Review (fresh-context, neograph-bhsdk.4)

Gate hard-check: PASS (research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present). Line refs in research verified accurate against forward.py (_LoopCall :462-567, loop() :600-621, record_iteration over-path :377-385, bare-for sugar :638-654 key='label' :652), modifiers.py Each(over,key,on_error) :484-510, _validation_types.py _resolve_field_annotation :135 / _extract_list_element :213, and the declarative twin test_composition.py :3190-3229. Reuse-over-reinvention is correct: this is a genuine copy-adapt of existing machinery emitting only existing IR (Construct|Each), zero IR/compiler edits. Type-inference, copy-not-mutate, naming-counter, and record_construct-not-tagging-loop-body edge cases are all identified and code-accurate.

- [HIGH] Finding (mandated item (a)+(b) — one-step vs two-step AND compose/nest): The plan's recommended ONE-STEP self.each(body, over, key) returning an output proxy is in direct contradiction with sibling ticket neograph-e9zse.2. e9zse.2's design and its 'Depends on' both state '_EachCall must exist' and relax self.loop() body validation (:491-498) to 'accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall / _EachCall) alongside _NodeCall'. That mechanism requires _EachCall to be a DEFERRED, placeable-in-a-body-list object exactly like _LoopCall — i.e. self.each(...) must return an _EachCall instance you can drop into self.loop(body=[ self.each(...) ], ...), where the loop's __call__ lowers it into the loop's per-iteration sub-construct. A one-step each instead EAGERLY calls record_construct at top level and returns a _Proxy: there is no persistent _EachCall to nest, and eager top-level recording double-records the sub-construct when it should live INSIDE the loop body. Since the epic's ENTIRE justification is the cascade topology 'Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key="id") })' (each nested inside a loop), the each API shape is load-bearing for e9zse.2 and cannot be chosen in isolation. The leaf-only acceptance test for e9zse.1 would pass with one-step and mask the defect — the break only surfaces in e9zse.2. Suggestion: adopt the TWO-STEP _EachCall shape, mirroring _LoopCall — self.each(body=[...], key=..., on_error=...) returns _EachCall; its __call__(over_proxy) computes over_path + item_type and builds Construct(input=item_type, output=..., nodes=copies) | Each(over, key, on_error), record_construct, returns the output proxy. This makes each a deferrable body item so e9zse.2 nests it with zero rework, and keeps loop/each symmetric. Confirm this reversal of the plan's recommendation (the epic routed exactly this DSL decision to the review gate before Phase 1).

- [MEDIUM] Finding (raw-string 'over' escape is underspecified): The plan and risks say 'over' should accept a raw string (declarative-parity escape) and 'skips inference only if item type can't be derived — then fail loud'. But a raw-string over has NO traced source proxy, so the sub-construct's input= boundary port (the fanned item type) cannot be inferred at all — and an Each'd sub-construct REQUIRES input=item_type so each item lands on the port. 'Fail loud' would make the raw-string escape unusable. Suggestion: either (i) require an explicit item/port type argument when over is a raw string, or (ii) resolve the producer by matching split_each_path(over)'s root field back to a traced node (field_name_for inverse) and infer from there, or (iii) drop raw-string over from this ticket's scope. Pick one and specify it before implementing.

- [LOW] Finding (mandated item (c) — key='label' bare-for default): Keeping the bare 'for x in proxy' sugar with hardcoded key='label' as-is is fine and correctly ALLOWLISTed. Note for the parity matrix (e9zse.4): bare-for emits PER-NODE (node | Each) whereas self.each emits a wrapped (Construct | Each) sub-construct — so for a single-node body the two forms are NOT IR-identical by design. The matrix must treat them as distinct twins, not assert equivalence.

- [LOW] Finding (naming-counter generalization): Plan step 3 correctly calls for keying the occurrence counter per (kind, slug) so a loop and an each over the same body slug don't collide. title: P1: relax self.loop() body validation — accept sub-construct-producing body items
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 1, fix #2. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What
Relax self.loop() body validation in src/neograph/forward.py (:491-498) to accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall / _EachCall results from neograph-e9zse.1) alongside _NodeCall. Construct(nodes=...) already accepts list[Node | Construct], so the tracer is artificially stricter than the IR it targets.

- Reuse _declared_output port inference (forward.py:519) for input/output boundary types on MIXED bodies (nodes + modified sub-constructs). This is the only fiddly part: type inference when a body member is a modified sub-construct (e.g. an Each'd construct whose effective producer type is dict[str, X] — use effective_producer_type from _construct_validation, do NOT re-inline modifier rules).
- Enables free nesting: loop containing an Each fan-out (the cascade shape), each inside loop, loop inside loop.

## Core Invariant
Same as the epic: traced IR == declarative IR; emit only existing IR; zero IR/compiler changes. effective_producer_type is the single source of truth for modifier-aware type effects.

## Acceptance
A forward() twin of declarative `Loop(over=...)` applied to a Construct whose nodes include an Each'd sub-construct traces to IDENTICAL IR as the declarative form. The cascade shape (intake -> triage -> Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key='id') }) -> explain) becomes expressible. TDD: failing IR-equality test first.

## Depends on
neograph-e9zse.1 (shares the DSL composition design confirmed by its review gate; _EachCall must exist).

Relax _LoopCall.__call__ body validation (:509-516) to _NodeCall | _EachCall | _LoopCall; materialize members IN ORDER: _NodeCall -> node copy (inputs=input_type fill only when inputs is None, model_copy, unchanged); _EachCall -> _materialize with root resolution against (a) preceding materialized peers via field_name_for(name) and (b) StateKeys.SUBGRAPH_INPUT -> walk the loop's input_type; root type for peers = effective_producer_type(peer) imported via the _construct_validation facade (mirrors _check_each_path's matched.effective_type). NOTE a wording contradiction in this ticket's own description ('_LoopCall / _EachCall results') — the RESULT of calling either is a _Proxy, which cannot nest (calling records at top level via tracer.record_construct, forward.py:657/:577). The review-gate decision resolves it: deferred objects nest; call-results do not. Do not implement proxy-in-body.

title: P2: self.ensemble() tracing surface — Oracle (ensemble_n + merge) in forward()
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 2. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What
Oracle is ENTIRELY absent from forward() today (not even imported). Add a self.ensemble(...) tracing surface to src/neograph/forward.py that builds the EXISTING Oracle modifier (ensemble_n, merge_fn/merge_prompt/merge_model) applied to a node or sub-construct, following the self.loop()/self.each() blueprint: record into the tracer, return an output proxy.

Design the exact signature during research/review (e.g. self.ensemble(node_or_body, n=, merge_fn=) vs kwargs mirroring Oracle fields) — mirror Oracle's declarative fields 1:1; invent nothing new.

## Core Invariant
Emit only existing IR (X | Oracle(...)); traced IR == declarative IR; zero IR/compiler changes.

## Acceptance
forward() twin of declarative `node | Oracle(ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='combine')` (and Oracle-on-sub-construct if declaratively supported — check compiler.py:474-476 for the documented Each x Oracle fusion non-support, which stays OUT of scope) traces to IDENTICAL IR. Add corpus rows to the parity matrix (tests from neograph-e9zse.4). TDD: failing IR-equality test first.

## Depends on
neograph-e9zse.4 (extends the ratchet corpus).
design:
## Core Invariant
self.ensemble() emits ONLY existing IR — a bare 'Node | Oracle(...)' member or a 'Construct(input=,output=,nodes=[...]) | Oracle(...)' sub-construct, byte-for-byte the declarative twin — with zero changes to modifiers.py, the IR/validator, or the compiler.

## Implementation Plan (TDD)
1. RED — extend the parity harness first (tests/test_forward_parity.py): add _modifier_oracle_params(item) (n, models, merge_prompt, merge_model, merge_fn verbatim; merge_* hooks by identity) into assert_ir_identical for both Node and Construct arms; add two corpus rows with capability keys 'oracle_ensemble' (node form: decl 'Node.scripted(gen,...) | Oracle(n=3, merge_fn=par_merge)') and 'oracle_ensemble_sub_construct' (body form: decl 'Construct(input=,output=,nodes=[...]) | Oracle(...)'); register a par_merge scripted fn in _register_corpus_fns; remove 'oracle_ensemble' from PHASE2_PENDING. Both rows fail: _ForwardSelf has no ensemble().
2. GREEN — src/neograph/forward.py: import Oracle alongside Each/Loop; add _EnsembleCall modeled on _LoopCall/_EachCall (reuse, don't reinvent):
   - _ForwardSelf.ensemble(target, *, n=3, models=None, merge_prompt=None, merge_model='reason', merge_fn=None, merge_pre_process=None, merge_post_process=None, merge_fallback=None) -> _EnsembleCall. Kwargs mirror Oracle fields 1:1; build Oracle(...) directly and let Oracle.model_post_init/__or__ do all validation + dev warnings (no tracer re-validation).
   - Node form (target is a _NodeCall): __call__(...) records 'target._node | Oracle(...)' via tracer.record and returns a _Proxy sourced at the modified copy — the _NodeCall pattern with the pipe applied (__or__ already model_copies; sidecar PrivateAttrs survive, pinned by test_node_sidecar_contract).
   - Body form (target is a list): mirror _LoopCall.__call__/_materialize — validate body kinds fail-loud, infer input port from proxy source with _declared_primary_of_body_item fallback, copy-not-mutate inputs fill, output = last member's declared primary, deterministic name 'ensemble-{slug}' via tracer.next_occurrence('ensemble', slug), build Construct(input=,output=,nodes=members) | Oracle(...), tracer.record_construct, return proxy.
3. Nested-in-loop (bounded-by-declarative, cheap): add _EnsembleCall to _LoopCall._validate_body_kinds allowlist + give it _materialize_nested (copy _LoopCall's: input from preceding member's declared primary or outer port; never records); extend _declared_primary_of_body_item for _EnsembleCall. Each bodies stay node-only (pre-existing Phase-1 restriction for all deferred builders). Each x Oracle on the body form stays a CompileError exactly as declaratively (compiler.py:473) — do not special-case.
4. Behavior tests beyond IR equality (tests/test_forward.py or the parity file): failing-loud cases (empty body, non-node body member, no merge strategy — surfaced by Oracle's own error) + one end-to-end run of a traced node-form ensemble with a registered scripted merge_fn (pattern: tests/modifiers/test_modifier_edge_cases.py:37, fakes.build_test_compile_kwargs).
5. Gates: uv run --extra dev pytest (full), mypy, ruff. Docs: forward.py module docstring + website ForwardConstruct page mention self.ensemble() (AGENTS.md: update website when API surfaces change; then npm run build in website/).
notes:
## Findings (research, neograph-y0fhw.2)
- REUSE TARGET: the existing Oracle modifier (src/neograph/modifiers.py:380) applied via Modifiable.__or__ (modifiers.py:215, returns a model_copy — class attrs never mutated). Fields to mirror 1:1: n (int, default 3), models (list[str]|None), merge_prompt (str|None), merge_model (str, 'reason'), merge_fn (str|None, scripted-registry name), merge_pre_process/merge_post_process/merge_fallback (Callables). Oracle.model_post_init already validates 'exactly one of merge_prompt/merge_fn' — do NOT re-validate in the tracer.
- NOTE: the ticket text says 'ensemble_n' but Oracle's field is n=. 'ensemble_n' is the @node decorator kwarg (decorators.py:155 _build_oracle_kwargs maps ensemble_n -> Oracle n=). For self.ensemble(...) mirror Oracle 1:1 (n=) per the ticket's own 'invent nothing' rule; the surface name already says ensemble.
- Declarative supports BOTH targets, so forward() needs both: (a) Node | Oracle — compiled by compiler.py:562 _add_oracle_nodes; (b) Construct | Oracle (sub-construct ensemble) — compiler.py:481 ORACLE case (_wire_oracle over the subgraph fn), pinned in construct.py:99 docstring. Each x Oracle on a SUB-CONSTRUCT raises CompileError (compiler.py:473-479) — OUT of scope, matches declarative. Each x Oracle FUSION on a bare Node IS supported (compiler.py:549 _add_each_oracle_fused), so a node-form ensemble output composes with bare-for sugar without tracer work.
- Blueprint = the Phase-1 deferred builders in forward.py: _LoopCall (forward.py:494) and _EachCall (forward.py:674). Pattern: _ForwardSelf method returns a *Call object; __call__(input_proxy) infers the boundary port from the proxy source (fallback _declared_primary_of_body_item, forward.py:483), materializes existing IR, tracer.record_construct(sub), returns a _Proxy sourced at the sub. Deterministic naming: '{kind}-{body_slug}' + tracer.next_occurrence(kind, slug). Copy-not-mutate inputs fill via model_copy (neograph-2o9n). effective_producer_type is the modifier single-source-of-truth — Oracle leaves the producer type UNCHANGED (merge collapses back to output), so Oracle'd members pass _LoopCall's fanned-out-terminal check with no changes.
- Nesting (bounded-by-declarative): declaratively, node|Oracle and Construct|Oracle members are legal inside loop-body sub-constructs (compile recurses; validation walks them). _LoopCall._validate_body_kinds allowlists (_NodeCall,_EachCall,_LoopCall) + calls member._materialize_nested — extend with _EnsembleCall the same way. _EachCall bodies are node-only for ALL deferred builders (pre-existing Phase-1 restriction), so ensemble-in-each-body stays out, consistent.
- merge_fn semantics: string name resolved at compile via per-compile scripted lookup or @merge_fn registry (_oracle.py:381 _run_merge_fn, _oracle.py:412 _assert_merge_fn_registered compile-time check). Tests register via tests/fakes.register_scripted (see tests/modifiers/test_modifier_edge_cases.py:45 — Node.scripted | Oracle(n=1, merge_fn='deg_merge') is the exemplar).
- PARITY RATCHET: tests/test_forward_parity.py — 'oracle_ensemble' sits in PHASE2_PENDING (line 562); this ticket adds ParityRow(s) to PARITY_CORPUS and removes the key (test_phase2_pending_keys_do_not_overlap_required enforces the move). IMPORTANT GAP: assert_ir_identical (line 120) compares Each params + Loop when-identity but NOT Oracle — it must gain an Oracle comparison (n, models, merge_prompt, merge_model, merge_fn verbatim; hooks by identity) or the new rows would vacuously pass.
- Validation already in place downstream (nothing to add): fan-over-agent guard (_construct_validation.py:150 raise_if_unsupported_fan_over_agent — Oracle over self-contained agent auto-wrapped by compile pre-pass), merge-hook signature checks (_validation_modifiers.py:107), ModifierSet rejects Oracle+Loop and duplicate Oracle.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:494 _LoopCall / :674 _EachCall — the two-step deferred builder blueprint to copy (esp. _materialize vs _materialize_nested split, d208f55).
- src/neograph/forward.py:465 _NodeCall — record-and-return-proxy primitive; node-form ensemble is 'record node|Oracle instead of node'.
- src/neograph/forward.py:951-1011 _ForwardSelf.loop/.each — where self.ensemble() lands.
- src/neograph/forward.py:483 _declared_primary_of_body_item — extend for _EnsembleCall if nested-in-loop ships.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:380 Oracle; :215 Modifiable.__or__ (copy semantics).
- src/neograph/compiler.py:481 (Construct|Oracle), :562 (Node|Oracle), :473 (Each x Oracle on sub-construct = CompileError, out of scope).
- src/neograph/decorators.py:155 _build_oracle_kwargs — @node's Oracle-field mirroring precedent (ensemble_n naming).
- tests/test_forward_parity.py — PARITY_CORPUS/PHASE2_PENDING/assert_ir_identical (rows land here); tests/modifiers/test_modifier_edge_cases.py:45 — scripted-node Oracle exemplar; tests/fakes.py register_scripted + build_test_compile_kwargs.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Silent-pass risk: adding corpus rows WITHOUT extending assert_ir_identical to compare Oracle params would make the parity test green even if the tracer dropped the modifier. Extend the helper first (TDD).
- Node-form vs body-form are DIFFERENT IR (bare Node|Oracle vs Construct|Oracle). Wrapping a single node in a Construct is NOT the twin of node|Oracle — the surface must keep both shapes distinct.
- Body-form input inference: forward-input proxy has source_node None — reuse the _LoopCall fallback (_declared_primary_of_body_item on last body member) verbatim.
- Oracle(n=1) and uneven models distribution emit dev_warn in __or__ — free via reuse; don't duplicate warnings in the tracer.
- oracle_gen_type (node.py:236, merge_fn A->B type transform) is a Node field set by the @node layer, not by Oracle — out of tracer scope; class-attr Nodes carry it themselves.
- No doc/code contradictions found; no NEEDS USER INPUT items. (Minor: ticket text writes Oracle(ensemble_n=3,...) — that field name is wrong for the Oracle IR class; correct is n=.)
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-e9zse.5)

Pattern: (a) parity IR-equality helper comparing only a SUBSET of modifier params (Oracle absent -> vacuous-pass risk for new rows); (b) tracer surfaces building modifiers outside the shipped _LoopCall/_EachCall blueprint.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|

## Architect Review (neograph-y0fhw.4)

Gate: PASS — research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present on the bead.
Verified against code: Oracle fields (modifiers.py:395-403) mirror the proposed kwargs 1:1 (n=3, models, merge_prompt, merge_model='reason', merge_fn, merge_pre/post_process, merge_fallback); ticket-text 'ensemble_n' correctly rejected in favor of Oracle's n= (research caught this). Modifiable.__or__ (modifiers.py:215) is copy-not-mutate and emits the n==1/uneven-models dev_warns for free. compiler.py:473 (Each x Oracle sub-construct = CompileError, out of scope) and :562/:481 (Node|Oracle / Construct|Oracle both supported declaratively) confirmed. _LoopCall/_EachCall blueprint (forward.py:494/674) and the _materialize vs _materialize_nested split confirmed as the reuse target.

### Findings

- [LOW] Finding: Dual-target one-surface (node-ref vs list) is the RIGHT DX. It mirrors declarative Oracle, which applies to both a bare Node and a Construct, and the plan correctly keeps the two IR shapes distinct (bare Node|Oracle vs Construct|Oracle) per the research risk note. isinstance(_NodeCall) vs list dispatch is clean. Suggestion: ship as designed. Minor: ensemble uses a positional 'target' while loop/each use keyword 'body='; acceptable (node-ref is the common ensemble case and reads naturally positionally) but note the small surface-naming asymmetry.

- [LOW] Finding: Plan step 1 (extend assert_ir_identical with a _modifier_oracle_params comparison on BOTH the Node arm and the Construct arm BEFORE adding corpus rows) is sound and necessary — the current helper (test_forward_parity.py:112-168) compares Each+Loop only, so new oracle rows would vacuously pass. This is the correct anti-silent-pass ordering. Suggestion: proceed; ensure the Node arm (else-branch, ~line 155-168) gets the Oracle comparison too, not just the Construct arm — the node-form row lives there.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 3 (nested-in-loop) is under-specified/incoherent for the NODE-form ensemble. It says give _EnsembleCall a _materialize_nested that copies _LoopCall's — but _LoopCall._materialize_nested returns self._materialize(...), a Construct. That is correct ONLY for the body-form (Construct|Oracle). A NODE-form _EnsembleCall nested in a loop body must emit a BARE Node|Oracle member (declaratively legal: loop body = [review, gen | Oracle(...)]), not a wrapped Construct. _LoopCall._materialize (forward.py:594) only appends bare nodes for _NodeCall members and routes every other kind through _materialize_nested -> Construct + sets seen_construct=True; a node-form _EnsembleCall would therefore be silently wrapped into a sub-construct = NON-twin IR, directly violating the Core Invariant for that topology. Worse, no nested corpus row is planned to catch it, so it fails silently. Suggestion: pick one and state it explicitly — (a) make _EnsembleCall's nesting form-aware: node-form participates in _materialize's bare-member path (inputs-fill, seen_construct stays False, emits Node|Oracle), body-form returns Construct|Oracle; OR (b) explicitly scope nested node-form ensemble OUT of this ticket with a fail-loud guard AND a negative test, shipping only nested body-form. Either way add a nested-in-loop corpus row (node-form) that would catch the wrapping regression.

### Preserved-invariant check
Top-level node-form and body-form (the two REQUIRED acceptance rows) are fully and correctly specified across steps 1,2,4,5 — those preserve 'traced IR == declarative IR' with zero IR/compiler changes. The gap is confined to step 3's nested node-form.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Refinement (resolves review MEDIUM, 2026-07-11)
_EnsembleCall nesting is FORM-AWARE: _materialize_nested returns a bare 'node | Oracle(...)' member when the target is a node ref (a Construct wrap would be non-twin IR) and 'Construct(...) | Oracle(...)' when the target is a body list — mirroring exactly what each form emits at top level. A nested test pins the node-form-in-loop-body member as a Node (not Construct). LOWs accepted: kwargs mirror Oracle 1:1 (n=, not ensemble_n); merge hooks compared by identity in the parity helper.

  - TestNestedEnsembleFormAware::test_node_form_ensemble_in_loop_body_stays_a_bare_node_member — form-aware nesting: node-form ensemble in a self.loop body materializes as a bare Node|Oracle member (isinstance Node, NOT Construct)
  - TestNestedEnsembleFormAware::test_loop_with_node_form_ensemble_traces_ir_identical_to_declarative — full IR equality of the nested topology vs declarative loop twin
- Harness extended FIRST (anti-vacuous-pass, plan step 1): _modifier_oracle_params (n, models, merge_prompt, merge_model, merge_fn verbatim) + _assert_oracle_hooks_identical (merge_pre/post_process, merge_fallback by identity) wired into BOTH the Construct and Node arms of assert_ir_identical; par_merge registered in _register_corpus_fns; 'oracle_ensemble' removed from PHASE2_PENDING (now only 'operator_interrupt'); both new capability keys are required via PARITY_CORPUS.
- Status: FAILING (expected — TDD red). Observed: 4 failed, 14 passed; each new test fails with AttributeError: 'Twin' object has no attribute 'ensemble' (the tracing surface is absent from _ForwardSelf), pre-existing 14 rows green.

description:

title: invoke_with_tools double-counts tokens for json_mode/text strategy
description:
In _llm.py:invoke_with_tools (lines 707-731), when output_strategy is 'json_mode' or 'text', the final message's token usage is double-counted.

The json_mode/text path sets usage = getattr(last_msg, 'usage_metadata', None) where last_msg = messages[-1]. Then the message walk loop (lines 720-727) iterates ALL messages including messages[-1], summing their usage. Finally, lines 729-731 add 'usage' (from last_msg) AGAIN. This double-counts the final message's input_tokens and output_tokens.

The 'structured' strategy path does NOT have this bug because _call_structured makes a NEW LLM call (not in the messages list).

Repro: any agent/act mode node with llm_config={'output_strategy': 'text'} will report ~2x the actual token usage for the final ReAct message.

Fix: set usage=None after the json_mode/text parse since last_msg is already in the messages list.

title: _check_item_input dict bypass uses wrong check
description:
## Original report
Line 85 in _construct_validation.py does 'if isinstance(input_type, dict)' which checks if input_type IS a dict instance (always False for types). Should be 'if input_type is dict'. Currently Node.scripted(input=dict) fails validation even though the comment says 'dict / non-class input types defer to runtime isinstance-scanning'.

## Triage (2026-04-04)

**Reproduction confirmed**: `Node.scripted(input=dict)` followed by `Construct(nodes=[producer, consumer])` raises `ConstructError: Node 'b' in construct 'test' declares input=dict but no upstream produces a compatible value.`

**Runtime analysis** (factory.py:287-336):
- `_extract_input` supports THREE dict-shaped input specs:
  1. `input={"field": Type, ...}` — dict INSTANCE — multi-field extraction at factory.py:323
  2. `input=dict` — raw class — isinstance scan at factory.py:331, `_is_instance_safe(val, dict)` matches any dict-valued state field
  3. `input=dict[str, X]` — parameterized generic — `_is_instance_safe` uses `get_origin(dict[str, X]) → dict`, then `isinstance(val, dict)`
- All three are legitimate and work at runtime.

**Validator current behavior** (`_construct_validation.py:85`):
- `if isinstance(input_type, dict): return` — skips case 1 (instance) correctly
- Cases 2 and 3 fall through, hit the `isinstance(input_type, type)` guard (True for `dict`, True for `dict[str, X]`? — needs verification), then proceed to producer-matching where they (usually) fail.

**Root cause**: the validator's dict-bypass check only covers multi-field dict instances, not the other two shapes the runtime supports.

**Proposed fix** (small, in `_check_item_input` at _construct_validation.py:85):
```python
from typing import get_origin

# dict-shaped inputs of all three flavors defer to runtime isinstance
# scanning (factory.py:287-336):
#   - dict instance: multi-field extraction, e.g. input={"a": X, "b": Y}
#   - raw dict class: input=dict (isinstance match on any dict state field)
#   - parameterized generic: input=dict[str, X] (get_origin-based match)
if isinstance(input_type, dict):
    return
if input_type is dict or get_origin(input_type) is dict:
    return
```

**Coupling to neograph-8k3**: this fix is a prerequisite for the 8k3 fix. Once 8k3 stores Each-producers as `dict[str, output_type]`, downstream consumers will legitimately declare `input=dict[str, X]` or `input=dict` to consume them, and the validator must accept those shapes. Fix ebe first, then 8k3 can build on it.

**Priority kept at P2**: runtime works, it's a validator false-positive-reject. No data loss. 3-line fix.

**Acceptance**:
- `_check_item_input` accepts all three dict shapes as deferred-to-runtime
- New test `test_dict_class_input_deferred` — `Node.scripted(input=dict)` passes validation
- New test `test_dict_generic_input_deferred` — `Node.scripted(input=dict[str, X])` passes validation
- Existing `test_dict_input_skipped` (dict-instance case) still passes

**Files a fresh agent needs**:
- `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:80-100` (`_check_item_input` guards)
- `src/neograph/factory.py:287-336` (`_extract_input` + `_is_instance_safe` — runtime behavior this validator must match)
