title: merge_fn DI bindings invisible to lint()
description:
lint() walks Construct.nodes but never inspects Oracle merge_fn functions. DI bindings in @merge_fn (e.g., Annotated[SharedResources, FromConfig]) are completely invisible to static validation. Production code (piarch/rw_ingestion.py) uses this pattern in 5 merge functions.

Root cause: lint.py _walk() only calls _get_param_resolutions on Node instances, never on merge_fn registry entries.

Fix: Extend _walk() — when a Node has an Oracle modifier with merge_fn, look up the function via get_merge_fn_metadata(), extract its param_res, and validate DI bindings. Extract existing DI-check logic into a _check_di_bindings() helper to avoid duplication.

Fixture: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/di_merge_fn_missing_config.py
close_reason: Fixed: lint() now checks merge_fn DI bindings

title: Default output_strategy to json_mode (schema-in-prompt + auto-recovery) instead of structured
description:
Proposal: change the default LlmConfig.output_strategy from 'structured' to 'json_mode'.

WHY:
1. AGENT-MODE DOUBLE-GENERATION. With mode='agent' + output_strategy='structured', the ReAct loop first emits a free-form final answer to end the loop, THEN _call_structured makes a SEPARATE with_structured_output LLM call that re-generates the same object (_tool_loop.py:369-398: the 'structured' branch calls _call_structured; the 'json_mode'/'text' branch instead parses messages[-1] directly — no 2nd call). Observed in ox-troubleshooting-demo trace deal-4818-alice (77653beff70fc50a76649a5d5e427e77): GEN1 tool-call (8 tok) + GEN2 fenced JSON answer (232 tok) + GEN3 structured re-gen (227 tok, ~1.6s, ~$0.00094 ≈ 43% of the whole trace cost). The diagnosis is generated twice.
2. json_mode is functionally equivalent for the RESULT: inject schema into the prompt (already done via describe_type/BAML) -> llm.invoke -> parse -> auto-recovery with error feedback (_invoke_json_with_retry appends bad output + validation errors + full schema and retries). Same typed object, self-healing.
3. 'structured' requires a provider-compat shim (_llm_structured_compat.py) BECAUSE with_structured_output(include_raw=True) is polymorphic across providers (include_raw rejection, parsed=None, dict variants). json_mode is provider-uniform (plain invoke + parse), so defaulting to it removes reliance on that fragile surface.

TRADE-OFF (for maintainers to weigh): 'structured' uses provider-native CONSTRAINED DECODING — a stronger conformance guarantee for weaker models / providers that don't reliably emit valid JSON. json_mode relies on the model emitting parseable JSON (schema in prompt) + recovery. For capable models this is a win (cheaper, uniform, no double-gen); for weak models constrained decoding may be safer.

OPTIONS:
- (A) Flip the global default to json_mode; keep 'structured' as opt-in for constrained-decoding guarantees.
- (B) Narrower: keep 'structured' default for single-shot nodes, but in AGENT mode stop the redundant 2nd call — reuse/parse the ReAct final answer (i.e., agent mode effectively uses the json_mode tail). This kills the double-gen without changing conformance strategy for non-agent nodes.
Recommend deciding between (A) and (B); (B) is the minimal fix for the wasteful path, (A) is the broader simplification the reporter advocates.

Origin: ox-troubleshooting-demo; pairs with the tool-budget preamble (this repo, prior issue) as the efficiency/fewer-calls theme. Refs: _llm_config.py:36, _llm.py:142-145, _tool_loop.py:369-398, _llm_dispatch.py:_call_structured, _llm_retry.py:_invoke_json_with_retry, _llm_structured_compat.py.

title: loader.py path detection heuristic — len<=4096 and Path.exists()
description: loader.py:72-75 uses len(source) <= 4096 and Path(source).exists() to distinguish file paths from YAML strings. Short YAML that is also a valid file path would be misinterpreted.
design:
## Fix Design
1. Add newline pre-filter: '\n' not in source before Path.exists() check
2. Add test: YAML string not misidentified when same-named file exists
Scope: 1 production line change + 1 test
notes:
## Reproduce Findings

### Heuristic code (loader.py:65-87)
len(source) <= 4096 and Path(source).exists() and p.is_file()

### Exploitability: theoretical only
- Multi-line YAML (required for valid spec) contains newlines → won't match file paths
- Downstream schema validation (_validate_spec + _build_construct) catches misclassification
- Single-line YAML can never be a valid pipeline spec (needs name, nodes, pipeline keys)

### Severity: LOW
Not exploitable in realistic usage. Downstream validation is a safety net.

### Test coverage: ZERO tests for path-vs-string ambiguity

### Recommended fix: 1 line
Add newline check: if len(source) <= 4096 and '\n' not in source:
Plus a test confirming YAML string is never misidentified as path.

### Core invariant
_parse_input(s) must parse content strings as YAML/JSON and read file paths as files. The heuristic conflates these two intents.

title: Narrow except Exception in .map() to (TypeError, AttributeError)
description:
MED-08 from code review 040426_2207 (PP-02).

src/neograph/modifiers.py:94-102 wraps all exceptions from source(recorder) as TypeError('pure attribute-access chain'). Legitimate non-access failures (e.g. 'lambda s: 1/0' raises ZeroDivisionError, or a user helper raising ValueError) get mis-reported as 'not a pure attribute chain'.

title: Branch-arm sub-constructs compile with checkpointer=None while the main path threads the parent checkpointer
description:
Found by the three-layer audit (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md section 2.5.2). _wiring.py:576 and _wiring.py:585 both compile branch-arm sub-constructs with checkpointer=None; the main sub-construct path threads the parent checkpointer (compiler.py:213 passes checkpointer=checkpointer into _add_subgraph). By the codebase's own theory — the main path threads it because it is needed — a sub-construct inside a branch arm has no persistence: an Operator interrupt inside it may fail or lose state, and crash recovery would re-execute the whole arm rather than resume inside it.

CAVEAT that makes this failing-test-FIRST: LangGraph may propagate the parent checkpointer to invoked subgraphs via config at invoke time, in which case the two paths coincidentally behave identically and the fix is to make the code CONSISTENT (and document which form is authoritative) rather than behavioral. Either outcome is informative.

TDD: branch arm containing a sub-construct with an Operator; run with a real file-backed SqliteSaver; interrupt; resume; assert the arm CONTINUES from the interrupt rather than restarting. Write the test before touching either call site. If the test passes as-is, the deliverable becomes consistency + a pinning test, not a behavior change.
close_reason: BEHAVIORAL bug confirmed via TDD (not consistency-only): an Operator sub-construct inside a branch arm failed to COMPILE with 'Operator modifier requires a checkpointer' because _add_branch_to_graph compiled arm sub-constructs with checkpointer=None (also dropped conditions=), while the main path (_add_subgraph) threads both. Fix: threaded parent checkpointer + condition_lookup into _add_branch_to_graph and both arm-sub-construct _compile call sites in _wiring.py (compiler.py passes them in). Now compiles, interrupts mid-arm, and resumes from the interrupt (pre-interrupt node runs exactly once). Test: tests/test_branch_arm_checkpointer.py (3 tests, real file-backed SqliteSaver, true+false arm + main-path parity). Verified RED without fix / GREEN with. Added ANY_ALLOWLIST entry for checkpointer:Any. Full suite 2245 passed. Filed neograph-tdbb for the independent iter_nodes/branch-arm shim-collection gap discovered en route (blocks @node sub-constructs in branch arms).

title: aqau hardening: normalizer dispatch list + DRY cross-ref + relocation-proof guard
description:
P2 architectural hardening from independent review (agentId aad2fed1b9fc8c9bc, confidence 82). The class-level fix lands but the SHAPE risks future drift.

Three improvements:
1. Refactor per-field _normalize_<field> methods into a single dispatch list:
   _NORMALIZERS: list[Callable[[Construct], None]] = [_normalize_fan_out_params, _normalize_oracle_gen_type]
   Called from one place in __init__. Adding a third normalizer becomes a one-liner append rather than another method. Makes 'how many normalizers exist' immediately visible.
2. DRY between _construct_builder.py:583 (@node fast path) and Construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type (canonical) — add a comment at the builder site referencing the canonical normalizer location. A bug fix in one must propagate to the other; today nothing flags this dependency.
3. Structural guard at test_structural_guards.py:4168 is file-scoped to _construct_builder.py. If assembly logic migrates (TS port, refactor, file split), the guard silently stops enforcing. Add either: (a) a runtime invariant in Construct.__init__ that asserts every IR field is in PASSTHROUGH or NORMALIZED state at the end of normalization; (b) a comment in _construct_builder.py at the 'updates' dict declaration site naming the guard test so any refactor triggers a 'find references' hit.

Acceptance: normalizer list replaces individual methods (or justification for keeping); cross-ref comment exists; structural guard either has runtime invariant OR cross-ref comment in builder source.
close_reason: Subsumed by EPIC 1 (neograph-20xq). The aqau hardening (normalizer dispatch list + DRY cross-ref + relocation-proof guard) is fully covered by the IR-finalization unification epic, which deletes the two _normalize_* methods rather than refactor them into a list.

title: Portal: named meshes (>1 mesh per construct level)
description: v1 allows one mesh per construct level (D-SINGLE-MESH) because two disjoint meshes make the reserved 'handoff' input key ambiguous. Add named meshes so the reserved key can be disambiguated per mesh. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: a construct that validates must lower EXACTLY as validated -- grouping (which members belong to which named mesh) must be computed by exactly ONE shared helper, never three independently-inferred groupings across validator/normalizer/compiler that could silently diverge.

Resolution to MEDIUM (mandatory shared helper): the grouping helper is MANDATORY (not 'if practical') at all three consumer sites: _validation_portal.py (mesh validation), _ir_normalize.py (handoff_channel writer), and _wiring.py (mesh collector/compiler walk). Place it in an import-safe NEUTRAL module reachable by all three without an import cycle (verify against test_guards_assembly.py's import-DAG guard before picking a location -- modifiers.py next to the Portal class is the natural home since all three sites already import Portal-related symbols from there). The helper defines BOTH the group key (Portal.name, or a synthesized default) AND the None-handling rule (all name=None members belong to one default group) in exactly one place. Add a structural guard test (following this file's existing AST/grep-based guard conventions) pinning that grouping is computed ONLY via that helper -- not re-derived inline at any of the three sites.

Resolved (LOW): reserved-key disambiguation is grouping-based (not a handoff_<meshname> syntax change), per design doc S3.3 -- each node belongs to at most one mesh, so grouping alone disambiguates the reserved 'handoff' key. Add a model_post_init check rejecting name= on a dispatch-mode Portal (is_dispatch=True, not a mesh member) with a should_fail fixture.

Runtime test requirement: the multi-mesh test must explicitly assert non-interference of the two meshes' hop counters AND distinct exit-node names -- 'falls out for free' from the shared grouping is a claim to PROVE, not assume.
notes:
## Findings
- Current state: Portal enforces D-SINGLE-MESH — exactly ONE mesh (one connected component under the peer relation) per construct level. Enforced in `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py` (`_check_portal_mesh`), which today:
  - collects ALL Portal-modified (non-dispatch) siblings at a level into one `members` list (no grouping key),
  - requires them CONTIGUOUS in `Construct.nodes` (single `lo..hi` span, :121-130),
  - requires ONE connected component reachable from `members[0]` (entry) via the undirected peer relation (:169-192) — this is the literal D-SINGLE-MESH check; two disjoint components today raise "two disjoint Portal meshes at one construct level".
  - runs uniform-payload / route-field / reserved-key / entry-only-knob checks over that single `members` list.
- The reserved `handoff` inputs key ambiguity (the reason D-SINGLE-MESH exists) is concrete in the IR normalizer, NOT the validator: `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:257-273` collects ALL Portal members at a level into one `portal_members` list and computes ONE `handoff_channel = StateKeys.handoff_payload(field_name_for(portal_members[0].name))` — i.e. it blindly takes the FIRST Portal member across the whole level as "the" entry and stamps that single channel key onto every Portal member at the level. With two disjoint meshes this is actively wrong (members of the second mesh would get the first mesh's channel key), which is exactly why the validator forbids the scenario today rather than leaving it to silently misroute.
- Compiler-side mesh detection is ALSO single-mesh-shaped: `_contiguous_portal_mesh` (`src/neograph/_wiring.py:700-725`) walks forward from an entry while `classify_modifiers(item)[0] == ModifierCombo.PORTAL` (any Portal member, no name/group distinction) and stops only at a non-Portal item or a dispatch-mode Portal. Two named meshes placed back-to-back with NO plain node between them would currently be silently glommed into one `members` list by this collector — a second gap to close, not just the validator.
- State-key generation (`StateKeys.handoff_hops` / `StateKeys.handoff_payload`, `src/neograph/_state_keys.py:129-146`) is already keyed by an arbitrary `field_name: str` (currently always the mesh entry's producer field) — no format change needed for named meshes; it already supports parameterizing by whatever field the normalizer chooses to pass, so two distinct entries naturally get two distinct field names TODAY. The only thing missing is a GROUPING key (a mesh name) so the normalizer/validator/compiler agree on which Portal members belong to which mesh, instead of assuming one global group.
- `Portal` (`src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-670`) has NO `name=` field today. Confirmed via direct read — this task is fully unstarted, no partial work exists.
- Design doc explicitly scopes this as v2, deferred from KEYMAKER v1 T8 consolidation: `docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md` §3.1 (D-SINGLE-MESH judgment call, lines 166-172) and `docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md` line 235 ("D-SINGLE-MESH | One mesh per construct level ... Named meshes = v2 | SHIPPED | Ratify; named meshes filed").
- Most recent related Portal work (current-way precedent to copy the STYLE of, not the content): `docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md` (cross-subconstruct mesh via parent-scoped bubble-up, landed 2026-07-23, commit 481ee34) — shows the sanctioned pattern for extending `_validation_portal.py` / `_ir_normalize.py` / `_wiring.py` together as one coherent change, keeping the single-writer invariants (G1 Command monopoly, G2 StateKeys centralization, G3 handoff_param/handoff_channel sole-writer in `_ir_normalize.py`) intact rather than adding a second mechanism.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40-260 (`_check_portal_mesh`) -- the single mesh-assembly validator; the exemplar to EXTEND (group by mesh name, run existing per-group checks, add a NEW cross-group rule: peers must resolve within the SAME named group) rather than rewrite.
- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:239-295 (`normalize_ir`, the `portal_members` collection + single `handoff_channel` computation at :257-273) -- must become per-named-group (one `handoff_channel` per group, keyed off that group's own entry), still the sole writer of `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` (G3).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:700-725 (`_contiguous_portal_mesh`) -- compiler-side contiguous-run collector; must stop the run at a mesh-NAME boundary in addition to today's non-Portal/dispatch-mode stops, or two adjacent named meshes will be merged.
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:790+ (`_add_portal_mesh`) -- per-mesh lowering (Command(goto), destinations=, exit node); called once per detected mesh already (see compiler.py:243-277 walk) — should need only the entry-detection fix above, not new lowering logic, since it already lowers exactly the `members` list it's handed.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:243-277 -- the mesh-aware compile walk (dispatches `_add_portal_mesh` once per detected contiguous mesh via `meshed: set[int]` bookkeeping); already loops, so multiple meshes at a level should fall out for free ONCE `_contiguous_portal_mesh` correctly bounds each group.
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:129-146 (`StateKeys.handoff_hops`/`handoff_payload`) -- already parameterized by `field_name`; reuse as-is per named group's entry field, no signature change needed.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-670 (`Portal` class) -- add the new `name: str | None = None` field here (mirrors how `route`/`max_hops` etc. already live as plain fields); `None` should mean 'the level's single/default mesh' so existing single-mesh pipelines keep working with zero change (back-compat via a synthesized default group key, e.g. the level's first-seen Portal member's node name, or a fixed sentinel).
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md:153-260 (§3 runtime contract) -- the mesh/reserved-key/channel design section this task revises; the reserved-key rationale in §3.3 is the exact ambiguity this task resolves.
- docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md:130-140,235 -- D10 (channel-read-side, entry-keyed) and the D-SINGLE-MESH ledger row this task closes.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Reserved-key disambiguation is grouping-based, not naming-based: since a node belongs to at most ONE Portal group, the reserved `inputs={'handoff': T}` key does NOT need to change syntactically (no 'handoff_<meshname>' key) — the normalizer just needs to know WHICH group a member is in to stamp the right `handoff_channel`. Confirm this reading with the maintainer if the fefar bead intends a syntax change to the reserved key itself; the design doc's phrasing ("disambiguated per mesh") is consistent with grouping-based disambiguation, but double-check before implementing.
- Back-compat default group key: existing single-mesh pipelines set no `name=`; the implementation must synthesize a stable default group (e.g. all `name=None` Portal members at one level form the implicit default group) so current examples/tests (28_portal_swarm, test_keymaker.py-equivalent suites) do not need updating.
- Cross-group peer validation is a NEW rule not present today: a peer named in `to=[...]` that exists as a sibling but belongs to a DIFFERENT named mesh must be a `ConstructError" (today the validator only checks 'peer exists as a sibling' + 'peer is Portal-modified' + implicitly enforces same-mesh via the single-mesh-only connected-component check). Without this new explicit check, cross-mesh peer references would silently need a NEW single-component check PER group rather than a global one — an easy place to under-scope the fix.
- Contiguity semantics with multiple meshes: today ALL Portal members at a level must be one contiguous span. With named meshes, does each NAMED group need its own contiguous span (most natural, minimal extension of existing per-group checks), and can two different-named groups be interleaved / adjacent? `_contiguous_portal_mesh`'s compiler-side collector needs matching semantics — whatever the validator decides for contiguity-per-group, the compiler's walk-and-collect must agree exactly, or a validator-accepted construct could compile with the wrong grouping (silent seam — violates the North-star fail-loud invariant).
- `ModifierCombo`/`_SLOT_RULES` (modifiers.py) exclusions and the Command-monopoly guard (G1) / handoff_param-sole-writer guard (G3) are UNCHANGED by this task in shape (still one Portal class, still `_ir_normalize.py` as sole writer) — but the guard tests (`test_guards_llm_runtime.py` G3, `test_guards_assembly.py` G1) must be re-verified they don't hard-code a level-has-at-most-one-portal-group assumption.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: none identified — design doc + decision log are unambiguous that this is v2 scope, unstarted, and grouping-based (not a reserved-key syntax change). Flagging only the disambiguation-mechanism question above as worth a quick confirm, not a blocking contradiction.
## Codebase Disease Scan (fefar)
Pattern: handoff_channel computed/written anywhere other than _ir_normalize.py's single-writer site (would indicate the D-SINGLE-MESH assumption is baked into multiple places, not one).
Scan command: `grep -rn "handoff_channel" src/neograph/*.py`
Total instances found: 19 across _agent_spec.py, _ir_normalize.py, _input_shape.py, _param_classify.py, _subconstruct.py, decorators.py, factory.py, loader.py, node.py

| # | File | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | _ir_normalize.py:271-292 | the SOLE writer, computes one global handoff_channel per construct level | MIGRATE | this IS the exact site that must change to support named/multiple meshes (per research's cited reuse target) |
| 2 | node.py:221 | the IR field itself (handoff_channel: str \| None) | ALLOWLIST | field declaration, not a computation; may need to become per-mesh-name but the field itself is not the disease |
| 3 | _agent_spec.py, _input_shape.py, _param_classify.py, _subconstruct.py, decorators.py, factory.py, loader.py (13 remaining sites) | all READ node.handoff_channel (never compute/write it) | ALLOWLIST | correctly respect the single-writer invariant; confirms the disease is isolated to _ir_normalize.py's single-mesh computation, exactly as research found |

Confirms MIGRATE scope is exactly the one site research identified -- no other write site to fix.
## Architect Review

Verified every reuse target against source: _ir_normalize.py:271-273 (sole handoff_channel writer, entry = portal_members[0]), _validation_portal.py:59-192 (single member_positions list; contiguity via lo/hi span; ONE connected-component walk from node_members[0]; uniform-payload/route/reserved-key checks all over the one members list), _wiring.py:700-725 (_contiguous_portal_mesh stops only at non-Portal/dispatch), compiler.py:251-277 (grouping-agnostic walk, meshed set by id()), modifiers.py:600 (frozen field-based Portal, no name field today). Plan's claims are accurate; scope table correctly isolates the one MIGRATE site.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 4 hedges the single most invariant-critical element. The Core Invariant demands ONE grouping key shared IDENTICALLY by validator + normalizer + compiler collector ('never three independently-inferred groupings that could silently diverge'), yet step 4 says 'Reuse the SAME grouping helper from steps 2/3 IF PRACTICAL.' 'If practical' re-admits the exact silent-seam the task exists to close (North-star: a construct that validates must lower exactly as validated). Two sub-gaps: (a) the plan never specifies WHERE the shared helper lives, and the three consumer modules (_validation_portal.py, _ir_normalize.py, _wiring.py) sit in the assembly import DAG guarded by test_guards_assembly.py -- a poorly-placed helper risks an import cycle; (b) None-handling semantics (all name=None members = one default group) must be encoded in that one helper, not re-derived per site. Suggestion: make the shared grouping helper MANDATORY (not 'if practical') for all three sites, place it in an import-safe neutral module reachable by all three (e.g. modifiers.py next to Portal, or _state_keys.py), and have it define both the group key and the None->default-group rule in one place. Add a structural guard pinning that grouping is computed only via that helper.

- [LOW] Finding: Reserved-key disambiguation mechanism was flagged by the research as 'confirm with maintainer' (grouping-based vs a handoff_<meshname> syntax change). The design doc S3.3 ('disambiguated per mesh') plus the structural fact that a node belongs to at most ONE mesh make grouping-based the correct and only sensible reading -- a syntactic per-mesh key would be redundant since each member already carries exactly one handoff_channel. Suggestion: proceed with grouping-based (no reserved-key syntax change) and record that decision in the design-doc update (step 8) so the open confirm is closed in-writing rather than left ambiguous.

- [LOW] Finding: Plan adds Portal.name as a plain field but does not address name= on a dispatch-mode Portal (route='decide'), which is not a mesh member and would silently ignore name. Fail-loud discipline suggests rejecting name= in dispatch mode. Suggestion: add a model_post_init check (ConfigurationError) forbidding name= when is_dispatch, or explicitly document it as ignored; add a should_fail fixture.

- [LOW] Finding: Step 5 asserts _add_portal_mesh / compiler walk / StateKeys need no changes and says 'verify with tests.' This is sound (exit node __handoff_exit_<entry>, hop key StateKeys.handoff_hops(field), and destinations= all derive from the per-group members list, so distinct entries yield distinct names for free), but the verification is load-bearing for the invariant. Suggestion: make the multi-mesh runtime test (step 7) explicitly assert non-interference of the two meshes' hop counters AND distinct exit-node names, so 'falls out for free' is proven, not assumed.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_portal_named_mesh.py::TestNamedMeshesCoexistAtOneLevel::test_two_named_meshes_run_independently_with_distinct_hop_counters
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step). Fails today with ConstructError: "two disjoint Portal meshes at one construct level" because Portal has no name= field yet (silently dropped by pydantic's default extra="ignore"), so two name-grouped meshes at one level collapse into one flattened members list and trip the existing D-SINGLE-MESH connected-component check.
- Tests expected behavior: two Portal meshes with distinct name= values coexist at one construct level, assemble+compile+run independently with their OWN hop counters (StateKeys.handoff_hops keyed per mesh entry) and OWN Command(goto) exit nodes, proving non-interference (distinct max_hops budgets reach distinct terminal values, not a shared/merged counter).
- Companion test: TestNamedMeshesCoexistAtOneLevel::test_unnamed_two_meshes_still_rejected pins back-compat (PASSES today) -- two disjoint UNNAMED meshes (name=None default group) still raise ConstructError exactly as before fefar.
Implementation complete. Added Portal.name (str|None) field for named mesh groups; shared _group_portal_members(items) helper in modifiers.py is the SOLE grouping point (validator/_ir_normalize/_wiring/state.py all delegate — never re-derive inline). Fixed a state.py bug found during implementation: mesh field registration used portal_members[0] (single global entry) instead of per-group, which silently dropped hop-counter/payload-channel fields for every mesh beyond the first. Added structural guard TestPortalMeshGroupingMonopoly (tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py) pinning the single-helper invariant per architect review's MEDIUM finding. New regression test tests/test_portal_named_mesh.py (2 tests: independent hop counters across 2 named meshes at one level, and back-compat rejection of 2 unnamed meshes). Full quality gate green: 3458 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean.
close_reason: Portal named meshes (one mesh per level,name pair) implemented, tested, committed 640bca8. Full quality gate green.

title: Fix: _safe_tool_invoke must coerce, not retry
description:
At 85% string-args rate, retry fails 72% of the time. The fix must extract string args from the ValidationError, json.loads them, construct AIMessage via post-init mutation with coerced dict args. No retry needed — deterministic fix.

Current code: catch ValidationError → retry → fail again → empty AIMessage fallback
Correct code: catch ValidationError → extract tool_calls from error context → json.loads string args → construct AIMessage with dict args → continue tool loop

The key insight: Pydantic v2 ValidationError.errors() includes input_value for each failing field. We can extract the string args, parse them, and reconstruct.
design:
## Core Invariant
Agent-mode tool calls must survive provider quirks deterministically. No retry-based approaches — coerce at the data level.

## Implementation
_CoercingToolWrapper class wraps bound LLM, intercepts ValidationError, uses _generate() fallback.
notes:
## Reproduction
The existing StringArgsFake now uses always_fail=True (every invoke raises). The _CoercingToolWrapper catches ValidationError and uses _generate() fallback to get the response via additional_kwargs path, which handles string args correctly. Deterministic — no retry, works at any failure rate.

## Fix
_CoercingToolWrapper wraps bind_tools result. On ValidationError from invoke():
1. Checks if error is tool_calls.args dict_type mismatch
2. Falls back to _generate() which returns raw ChatResult
3. Coerces any remaining string args via json.loads on the message
4. Last resort: empty AIMessage (tool loop exits gracefully)

title: Surface MCP progress notifications for long-running tools into stream()/astream()
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a long-running MCP tool that emits MCP progress notifications surfaces that progress to the caller through neograph streaming verbs (stream()/astream()), instead of the run appearing frozen until the tool returns.

WHY: MCP defines progress notifications (progressToken + notifications/progress) for long-running tools. neograph tool loop is request/response; a 60s tool call is a black box to the caller. Streaming is already first-class (four verbs), so progress is a natural custom-stream channel.

SCOPE: wire the MCP adapter progress callback into a neograph stream channel (LangGraph custom stream_mode / StreamWriter). A tool call carrying a progressToken forwards each notification as a stream event tagged with node + tool + progress fraction/message. No-op when the caller is not streaming or the tool emits no progress.

ANTI-BAND-AID: progress is OBSERVABILITY, never control flow — a missing/last progress notification must not affect the tool result, budgets, or replay. Progress events must NOT enter state or the checkpoint (ephemeral, like log lines), so they never touch the schema fingerprint.

ACCEPTANCE: a demo long-running tool emitting progress surfaces N events through astream() IN ORDER; a non-streaming arun() of the same pipeline is unaffected; progress never enters state/checkpoint; the tool result is byte-identical with and without a progress consumer. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
MCP progress notifications are ephemeral OBSERVABILITY surfaced ONLY through the existing custom-stream seam (emit_progress) — they never enter state, checkpoint, schema fingerprint, tool result, or budgets, and are a silent no-op when the caller is not streaming.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review neograph-5jrd0.53)
1. REUSE emit_progress as the surfacing mechanism (do NOT invent a stream channel). In src/neograph_mcp, define typed event model `McpProgress(BaseModel)` {server: str, tool: str, progress: float, total: float | None, message: str | None}. The callback calls PUBLIC neograph.emit_progress(McpProgress(...)); the src/neograph MCP-free guard stays green (wiring lives in the battery).
2. **[REVISED — constructor path, smaller diff]** Thread a `callbacks: Callbacks | None = None` param (default None) through `_client_for(server_key, spec, token, *, callbacks=None)` (_client.py:104) into `MultiServerMCPClient(connections, callbacks=callbacks)`. In _make_tool_factory's per-run _factory, build `Callbacks(on_progress=_on_progress)` and pass it to _client_for, then KEEP the existing `client.get_tools(server_name=server_key)` call intact — get_tools() forwards self.callbacks into load_mcp_tools verbatim, so the returned tools are byte-identical and the post-steps (stdio token-inject -> rename model_copy -> _wrap_output_model) stay unchanged in order. Do NOT switch to load_mcp_tools(connection=). _discover_tool_names (:203) and mcp_resource_fetcher are unaffected (callbacks defaults None).
3. **[REVISED — no envelope hand-roll]** on_progress closure: `async def _on_progress(progress, total, message, context: CallbackContext)` -> emit_progress(McpProgress(server=context.server_name, tool=context.tool_name, progress=progress, total=total, message=message)). PREFER the bare emit_progress path (per-call session + receive-loop task are created inside the node ainvoke context, so asyncio copies node contextvars at task creation — get_stream_writer() should resolve). If the E2E proves contextvars DO reach the callback task, ship exactly this and DROP any fallback. If a fallback is genuinely required, EXTEND neograph.emit_progress with an optional injected-writer param (emit_progress(event, *, writer=None)) so envelope-construction + warn-once stay single-sited in progress.py — NEVER call writer(payload) / reconstruct the {neograph_event/event_type/data} envelope inside neograph_mcp (that would reopen the Pattern-A single-seam bypass the scan pins at 0).
4. Add an async long-running demo tool to examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (e.g. `slow_export(n, ctx)`) looping `await ctx.report_progress(i, n, f'step {i}')` with small sleeps, then a deterministic result. FastMCP auto-attaches progressToken when the client passes a progress callback.
5. Acceptance test in tests/test_mcp_battery.py (extra-gated): (a) agent node binds slow_export, drive via astream(stream_mode='custom'); assert exactly N McpProgress envelopes surface IN ORDER; (b) arun() (non-streaming) returns a byte-identical tool result, unaffected (warn-once tolerated); (c) assert no progress payload in final state or checkpoint AND assert the McpProgress envelope key is NOT neo_*-prefixed (pins the actual state-isolation mechanism, mirroring test_emit_progress.py).
6. Three-surface note: agent/act (tool-loop) behavior in the neograph_mcp battery, not an IR change — no @node/declarative/programmatic parity obligation; seam is emit_progress (already three-surface-safe). NOT 0.6.0-gating.

## Disease disposition update
:277 remains the single MIGRATE site but the change is now 'thread callbacks= through _client_for so get_tools carries the on_progress callback', NOT 'replace get_tools with load_mcp_tools'. :203 stays ALLOWLIST.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-5jrd0.26)

REUSE TARGET (surfacing side) — do NOT build a new stream channel. `emit_progress` already IS the sanctioned custom-stream seam:
- `src/neograph/progress.py` — `emit_progress(event: BaseModel)` wraps a typed event in the stable envelope {"neograph_event":"progress","event_type":<cls>,"data":model_dump} and writes to LangGraph `get_stream_writer()`. Public API (neograph/__init__.py:74,115). Handles warn-once when non-streaming; never raises; never enters state (envelope key is deliberately NOT neo_*-prefixed so runner._finalize_chunk passes it through untouched). This is the CURRENT pattern (q8ec); there is NO deprecated alternative.
- `StateKeys.STREAM_CUSTOM` (_state_keys.py:69, config-only key) — set by stream/astream when consuming stream_mode='custom'; lets emit_progress distinguish a live consumer from a non-streaming driver. Never enters state/fingerprint. Matches the ANTI-BAND-AID clause exactly (ephemeral, like log lines).
- runner.py:612 `_wants_custom`, :819 `_finalize_chunk` (custom chunks pass through untouched), astream at :1104.

REUSE TARGET (MCP callback side) — langchain-mcp-adapters already exposes a progress seam:
- mcp SDK `ClientSession.call_tool(name, args, read_timeout_seconds, progress_callback, *, meta)` — progress_callback is native; passing it auto-mints a progressToken. Verified on installed mcp 1.28.x.
- `langchain_mcp_adapters.callbacks.Callbacks(on_logging_message, on_progress, on_elicitation)` with `.to_mcp_format(context=CallbackContext(server_name, tool_name))`. `on_progress` signature: `async def on_progress(progress: float, total: float|None, message: str|None, context: CallbackContext)`. CallbackContext carries server_name + tool_name (the 'tool + progress fraction/message' tagging the scope wants).
- `load_mcp_tools(session=None, *, connection=<dict>, callbacks=Callbacks(...), server_name=..., tool_name_prefix=..., handle_tool_errors=...)` and `convert_mcp_tool_to_langchain_tool(..., callbacks=...)` BOTH accept callbacks and thread progress_callback into call_tool. CONSTRAINT: `MultiServerMCPClient.get_tools(server_name=)` does NOT accept callbacks — the current factory build path bypasses the seam.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:252 `_make_tool_factory` — the exemplar to EXTEND. Its inner `_factory(config, tool_config)` runs per-superstep INSIDE the node's async context; currently builds tools via `client.get_tools(server_name=server_key)` (line ~276) which cannot carry callbacks. This is where progress wiring must land (switch to load_mcp_tools(connection=_connection(...), callbacks=...) or convert per-tool). Identity injection (_inject_stdio_token :175), rename (model_copy), and _wrap_output_model (:207) all operate on the returned BaseTool AFTER — order preserved.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88 `_connection` — already builds the connection dict load_mcp_tools needs.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:459 `_ainvoke_tool_timed` — `await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args'], config=config)`: the async tool call site inside the ReAct cycle where progress notifications actually fire. Progress is async-only; the sync loop (_tool_loop.py invoke path / run()) cannot surface it (acceptable — acceptance is astream/arun).
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:217+ — plain FastMCP @mcp.tool server; has NO long-running progress tool yet. Add an async tool taking `ctx: Context` that calls `await ctx.report_progress(i, total, msg)` in a loop (e.g. slow_export). FastMCP Context.report_progress is the standard emit.
- tests/modes/test_emit_progress.py + tests/test_streaming.py — the emit/astream-custom test exemplars to copy the acceptance test shape from.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:172 `_build_agent_construct`, :193 `_react_fake`, :225 arun-through-battery — the extra-gated harness to add the acceptance test to.
- GUARD: tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py — src/neograph must stay MCP-free; ONLY src/neograph_mcp may import the adapter. So callback wiring lives in neograph_mcp and calls the PUBLIC neograph.emit_progress seam (neograph_mcp already depends on neograph).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- CONTEXTVAR PROPAGATION (primary risk): emit_progress uses get_stream_writer() which reads LangGraph contextvars set during the node superstep. The on_progress callback fires from the mcp ClientSession receive-loop task (anyio task group). asyncio copies contextvars at task-creation; the on-the-fly per-call session is created INSIDE call_tool during the node's ainvoke, so it SHOULD inherit the writer — but this must be proven by the E2E test. FALLBACK if the writer isn't visible from the callback task: capture get_stream_writer() (or a bound emit closure) once inside _factory (which is in node context) and close over it in on_progress, instead of calling get_stream_writer() from within the callback.
- Build-path switch: moving from client.get_tools() to load_mcp_tools(connection=..., callbacks=...) changes the per-call session model — verify token injection/rename/output_model wraps still compose (they act on the returned BaseTool, so composition order is unchanged).
- warn-once: under a non-streaming arun() the demo tool's progress will trip emit_progress's once-per-process UserWarning; benign and required-by-design (must not vanish silently), does not affect result — assert result byte-identical anyway.
- Ordering: emit_progress writes synchronously per notification as it arrives, so N events surface IN ORDER naturally.
- No doc/code contradiction found; progress.py + STREAM_CUSTOM is the documented, current seam (no NEEDS USER INPUT).
## Codebase Disease Scan (fflpt)

Two patterns checked:

### Pattern A: hand-rolled custom-stream channel bypassing emit_progress
Scan command: grep -rn 'emit_progress\|get_stream_writer\|STREAM_CUSTOM\|stream_mode.*custom' src/ | grep -v test
Total instances found: 0 bypasses. emit_progress (src/neograph/progress.py) is the SOLE sanctioned seam over get_stream_writer; STREAM_CUSTOM is a documented KEEP. Design step 1 correctly reuses it. No MIGRATE/DEFER — clean.

### Pattern B: callback-blind client.get_tools() dropping the MCP progress callback
Scan command: grep -rn 'client.get_tools\|\.get_tools()' src/
Total instances found: 2

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:277 | _make_tool_factory per-run _factory: `tools = await client.get_tools(...)` | MIGRATE | tool-EXECUTION path — must build via callback-carrying adapter seam (Callbacks(on_progress=...)) so progress surfaces; this is design step 2 |
| 2 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:203 | _discover_tool_names: `tools = await client.get_tools(...)` | ALLOWLIST | discovery/listing ONLY — enumerates tool NAMES, never executes a tool, so there are no progress notifications to surface; wiring a callback here would be dead code |

No DEFER rows. Scope confirmed = 1 MIGRATE site (matches design), 1 ALLOWLIST false positive. SYNTACTIC disease → single-executor grep sufficient; no multi-agent artifact required.
## Architect Review (neograph-5jrd0.28/.29)

Gate: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. PASS.

Verified against installed deps + source: emit_progress seam (progress.py) is the sole sanctioned custom-stream writer and never enters state/fingerprint (docstring + envelope key confirm); Callbacks/CallbackContext/on_progress signature (progress,total,message,context); load_mcp_tools(session,*,connection,callbacks,server_name,...); _make_tool_factory:252, _factory get_tools at :277 (MIGRATE) and _discover_tool_names get_tools at :203 (ALLOWLIST). Disposition table is accurate. Core Invariant is preserved (additive observability, no state/checkpoint/result/budget impact). No HIGH.

- [MEDIUM] Research conclusion is subtly WRONG and drove a more invasive plan than needed. The notes state "MultiServerMCPClient.get_tools does NOT accept callbacks — the current factory build path bypasses the seam", concluding step 2 must REPLACE client.get_tools() with load_mcp_tools(connection=_connection(...), callbacks=...). But MultiServerMCPClient.__init__ accepts callbacks=Callbacks(...) and get_tools() forwards self.callbacks into load_mcp_tools verbatim (confirmed by reading get_tools source in installed langchain-mcp-adapters). The get_tools METHOD lacks a callbacks kwarg; the CLIENT does not. Suggestion: prefer threading callbacks through the existing _client_for -> MultiServerMCPClient(connections, callbacks=Callbacks(on_progress=_on_progress)) and KEEP the client.get_tools(server_name=server_key) call intact. This is a strictly smaller diff, preserves the nmb2 client-ownership/session model verbatim, and ELIMINATES the plans own "build-path switch" risk item (token-injection/rename/output_model composition) because get_tools produces byte-identical tools. Add callbacks param to _client_for with default None so _discover_tool_names/resource fetcher are unaffected. Note: the single-server get_tools(server_name=key) branch awaits load_mcp_tools in the current context (no asyncio.create_task), so it does not disturb node contextvar propagation; the multi-server branch does wrap in create_task, but the battery never uses it.

- [MEDIUM] Contingent-fallback collides with the single-seam invariant the disease scan (Pattern A) protects. Step 3 fallback says "capture get_stream_writer() (or a bound emit) once inside _factory and close over it". If the E2E shows contextvars do not reach the on_progress task and the fallback captures the writer directly, calling writer(payload) hand-rolls the envelope in neograph_mcp — exactly the emit_progress bypass Pattern A reports as 0 instances and must stay 0. emit_progress acquires its writer internally via get_stream_writer(), so binding a writer cannot route back through the public seam as written. Suggestion: if the fallback is needed, EXTEND emit_progress with an optional injected-writer parameter (e.g. emit_progress(event, *, writer=None)) so the envelope construction + warn-once logic stay single-sited, rather than reconstructing the {neograph_event/event_type/data} envelope in the battery. Primary bare-emit_progress path is likely fine (per-call session + receive-loop task are created inside the node ainvoke context, so asyncio copies node contextvars at task creation) — this only bites if the E2E forces the fallback.

- [LOW] Step 2 passes _connection(spec, token) as load_mcp_tools connection= (only under the plans rewrite; moot if the constructor-path MEDIUM is adopted). StdioConnection is a total TypedDict (__required_keys__ = all 8 keys incl cwd/encoding/session_kwargs), while _connection emits a partial dict. Works at runtime (existing code already casts past this for MultiServerMCPClient) but keep the cast(Any, ...) if this path is used. The constructor path avoids the issue since _client_for already casts.

- [LOW] Add a brief assertion in the acceptance test that the McpProgress envelope key is NOT neo_*-prefixed (the mechanism that keeps it out of _finalize_chunk/state), not merely that state lacks a progress payload — pins the actual isolation mechanism, mirroring test_emit_progress.py.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Triage (neograph-5jrd0.28): NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> injected refine neograph-5jrd0.53 (2 MEDIUM: callbacks-via-constructor, no-envelope-handroll-in-fallback; 2 LOW); write-test (neograph-5jrd0.30) re-pointed to wait on it.
## Refine (neograph-5jrd0.53) applied: design step 2 -> constructor callbacks path (keep get_tools); step 3 -> bare emit_progress primary, optional emit_progress(writer=) if fallback needed (no battery envelope hand-roll); test asserts non-neo_* envelope key. No re-research.
## Regression Test (TDD red, neograph-5jrd0.30)
- Test: tests/test_mcp_battery.py::TestMcpProgressStreaming — 4 tests:
  - test_slow_export_progress_surfaces_in_order_via_astream_custom
  - test_arun_unaffected_and_tool_result_identical_with_and_without_consumer
  - test_progress_never_enters_state_or_checkpoint
  - test_tool_emitting_no_progress_is_a_noop

title: test_hypothesis.py: naming inconsistency — two parallel pipeline description systems
description: Some strategies produce TopologySpec, others produce (Construct, dict) tuples. _build_scripted_surface takes TopologySpec, make_node_fn takes Node. Tests use both systems interchangeably. Unify on one representation throughout.
notes:
## Audit Findings (round 1)

### Two parallel systems:
**System A**: 13 strategies → (Construct, dict) with meta keys terminal_field, terminal_type inside dict
**System B**: 10 strategies → TopologySpec with terminal_field, terminal_type as top-level fields

### 5 naming conflicts (parallel functions, different return types):
bare_pipeline/bare_topology, each_pipeline/each_topology, oracle_pipeline/oracle_topology, loop_pipeline/loop_topology, each_oracle_pipeline/each_oracle_topology, any_pipeline/any_topology_spec

### 4 type confusion points:
1. _build_scripted_surface accepts only TopologySpec — incompatible with System A output
2. _assert_invariants accepts only TopologySpec — System A meta dict has different shape
3. _apply_spec_modifiers accepts only NodeSpec — System A builds modifiers inline
4. _build_yaml_surface/_build_llm_surface accept only TopologySpec

### Structural incompatibility:
System A: terminal_field/terminal_type are keys in meta dict
System B: terminal_field/terminal_type are top-level TopologySpec fields, meta holds extras only

### Meta key divergence:
System A unique: result_field, log_field, fan_field, coll_field, oracle_field, expected_fan_keys, upstream_names
System B unique: is_sub_construct, sub_name, sub_input, sub_output, inner_names, depth, step_size, max_iters, loop_cond, must_exhaust, skip_threshold, input_score, fan_in_keys

No shared assertion helper can work on both systems without an adapter.
## Verification (round 2): DISCREPANCIES FOUND

1. Coverage gap wider than audit stated — System A has 7 strategies with no System B counterpart (dict_output, mixed_modifier, di, node_decorator, sub_construct_with_each, nested_sub_construct, each_with_dict_outputs, node_decorator_with_di). System B has 3 with no System A counterpart (deep_chain, loop_exhaustion, skip_when — though skip_when_pipeline exists in A).

2. Missed meta keys: System A uses 'outer_sub_field' as alternative to 'terminal_field' in nested_sub_construct (structurally incompatible). System B uses 'step_size' and 'input_score' not mentioned in audit.

3. Variable shadowing: local var 'spec' is a raw dict in TestYAMLSurfaceSharedNodeImmutability (L3260) and TestEachKeyParityAcrossSurfaces (L3455), but TopologySpec in @given tests. Same name, different types — readability trap.

4. any_topology_spec_with_loops (L2197) is DEAD CODE — defined, never referenced. Also has a latent bug: claims to include skip_when but doesn't (skip_when_topology and loop_exhaustion_topology both absent from it).
## Prep (post-djhk)
### What changed since original audit:
- 56cn: deleted _build_yaml_surface, _build_llm_surface, SURFACE_ADAPTERS, _assert_invariants, any_topology_spec_with_loops (5 of 7 naming conflicts gone)
- djhk: deleted 5 redundant old strategies (bare/each/oracle/loop/each_oracle_pipeline + any_pipeline), eliminating all naming conflicts between systems

### What remains of fg69's original scope:
1. Old-system strategies still produce (Construct, dict) tuples — but these are NOT redundant (test unique axes). Converting them to TopologySpec would require extending TopologySpec/NodeSpec to support dict-form outputs, DI params, sub-construct composition, nested subs, etc. That's feature work, not cleanup.
2. Variable shadowing (spec = raw dict vs spec = TopologySpec) — not actually confusing in context. Different test sections, different purposes. The raw dict IS a YAML spec, naming it 'spec' is correct.
3. Meta key divergence — natural consequence of different systems testing different things. The old system needs result_field/log_field for dict outputs; the new system needs is_sub_construct/sub_name for topology assembly. No shared assertion helper needs to bridge them.

### Conclusion: fg69 is effectively DONE.
The naming inconsistency was between the 5 parallel strategies (same topology, different return types) — those are now deleted. The remaining old strategies test unique axes and their (Construct, dict) return type is correct for their purpose (they build real Constructs, not TopologySpec descriptions). Forcing them into TopologySpec would be scope creep and lose the direct Construct construction testing.

### Recommendation: close fg69 as resolved by djhk+56cn.
## Execution
- No code changes needed. The naming inconsistency (parallel strategies with conflicting names) was resolved by:
  - neograph-56cn: deleted dead surface adapters and dead any_topology_spec_with_loops
  - neograph-djhk: deleted the 5 redundant old-system strategies + any_pipeline
- Remaining old strategies are NOT inconsistent — they test unique axes via (Construct, dict) tuples, which is the correct form for their purpose.
- Quality check: PASS (1296 passed)
close_reason: Resolved by neograph-56cn + neograph-djhk: naming conflicts eliminated, remaining old strategies serve unique purpose

title: Research pej0
description:
Execute research for beads task pej0. All findings go into the
bead itself -- NOT the filesystem.

## Instructions

1. **Read the task**: `bd show pej0`
2. **Spec check** (if task touches schemas/protocol):
   - Read relevant specs and schemas
   - Check required vs optional, type constraints
3. **Explore the codebase**:
   - Search for relevant code
   - Read files that will need modification
   - Check existing tests for the affected area
   - Find 2-3 similar implementations to follow as patterns
4. **Check documentation** (doc-first rule)
5. **Engineering checklist** -- answer concretely:
   - DRY: Does similar logic exist?
   - Library idioms: How do your frameworks solve this?
   - Data flow trace: Walk one concrete example through the full chain
   - Existing conventions: What pattern do similar implementations follow?
   - Test infrastructure: What fixtures/helpers exist?
6. **Identify architecture decisions**
7. **Extract the core invariant** -- State in ONE sentence the architectural
   principle that ALL changes for this task must preserve.

## Store Research in the Bead

```bash
bd update pej0 --append-notes "## Findings
- [key findings]

## Relevant Code
- path/to/file.py:line -- [description]

## Risks & Edge Cases
- [potential issues]"

bd update pej0 --design "## Core Invariant
[One sentence: the architectural principle every change must preserve]

## Implementation Plan
1. [first step]
2. [second step]"
```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after notes AND design are written:
```bash
bd label add pej0 research:complete
```
acceptance_criteria: Task has research:complete label. Notes contain Findings. Design contains Core Invariant + Implementation Plan.

title: Architect review of pej0
description:
Pragmatic architect review of the research findings for pej0.

## Precondition

Run `bd show pej0` and verify research:complete label is present.

## Review Criteria

1. **Invariant alignment**: Does EVERY step maintain the Core Invariant?
2. **Approach soundness**: Will the plan work?
3. **Risk coverage**: Are risks identified and covered?
4. **Pattern compliance**: Does the plan follow project architecture patterns?
5. **Specificity**: Is the plan specific enough to implement without guessing?
6. **Alternatives**: Was a better approach missed?

## Rate Each Finding

- **LOW**: Minor suggestion, cosmetic, nice-to-have
- **MEDIUM**: Real concern but agent can resolve autonomously
- **HIGH**: Fundamental issue -- user input required

## Write Review

```bash
bd update pej0 --append-notes "## Architect Review
- [RATING] Finding: [description]. Suggestion: [what to do]

Overall: [ALL_LOW | NEEDS_REFINEMENT | NEEDS_USER_INPUT]"
```
acceptance_criteria: Review written to task notes with rated findings and overall verdict.

title: Write regression test for pej0
description:
Write a failing test that defines the expected behavior for pej0.
This is the TDD "red" step -- the test MUST exist and MUST fail before
any implementation begins.

## Instructions

1. Identify what to test from the implementation plan
2. Choose test level (prefer integration over unit when DB involved)
3. Write the failing test
4. Use test factories for test data (never inline model construction)
5. Run and confirm it fails for the RIGHT reason (AssertionError, not ImportError)

## BANNED Patterns

- `pytest.mark.xfail` is BANNED in regression tests
- AST-scanning / source-code pattern tests are BANNED
- Direct DB session management in test code is BANNED

## Verification: Paste the FAILED Output

You MUST see the word "FAILED" in pytest output.

## Store Test Reference

```bash
bd update pej0 --append-notes "## Regression Test
- Test: <test_path>::<test_name>
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step)
- Tests expected behavior: [one sentence]"
```
acceptance_criteria: Failing test exists. Test reference written to task notes.

title: Implement pej0
description:
Implement beads task pej0 -- make the failing test pass (TDD green),
then refactor.

## Workflow

1. **Green**: Write minimum code to make the failing test pass
2. **Verify**: Run the SAME test that FAILED -- must now PASS
3. **Refactor**: With passing tests as safety net
4. **Quality gate**: Run project quality command

## When EXISTING Tests Fail

1. STOP. Do NOT modify the failing tests.
2. Re-read the Core Invariant.
3. If your approach violates the invariant -> revert and rethink.
4. If the test has a genuine bug -> document WHY before modifying.

Sacred rule: NEVER adjust tests to match code without justification.

## If Successful

Close the original beads task:
```bash
bd close pej0
```
acceptance_criteria: Quality command passes. Regression test passes. Original task closed.

title: Thread-safe registry via contextvars.ContextVar
description:
## Problem
_registry.py uses a module-level Registry singleton with dict stores. The session() context manager copies dicts for test isolation, but the singleton is shared across threads. If two threads compile pipelines simultaneously, registry.scripted[name] lookups could see partial registrations.

## Proposed fix
Use contextvars.ContextVar for the registry, similar to Starlette/FastAPI request-scoped state. Each async task gets its own registry view without snapshot overhead.

## Context
LangGraph itself is not thread-safe for graph construction, so this is only a real issue if someone compiles in parallel threads (unlikely in current usage). Low priority but correct for library quality.

## Source
Expert architectural review concern #8 (Low-Medium).
notes: ## Research: DEFER. Zero threading/async usage in codebase. Registry only written during compile(), read during execution. No multi-tenant pattern. Theoretical concern only.
close_reason: Deferred: no multi-threaded usage found, theoretical concern

title: Fix 5 drifted doc snippets caught by Stage D snippet testing (neograph-3my4x)
description:
Stage D (tests/test_docs_snippets.py) caught 5 doc snippets that are Stage-B-green (symbols resolve) but no longer run against the current API. Each is currently skip-marked '{/* test-skip: BROKEN doc snippet (API drift) ... */}' so the suite stays green; this bug tracks fixing the DOCS and removing the skip markers.

1. concepts/lint.mdx -- '@node(output=Result)' (singular) in multiple blocks; decorator only accepts 'outputs='. NOTE: the same wrong singular form appears in the project's own CLAUDE.md DI example (@node(output=Result)) -- systemic; fix both.
2. node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx L534 -- '@node(loop_history=True)'; loop_history is not a valid @node kwarg, but surrounding prose documents it as a feature. Determine if it was removed/never-wired and fix prose+snippet.
3. walkthrough/oracle-ensemble.mdx L214 -- '@node(merge_model="reason")'; merge_model is not a valid @node kwarg.
4. reference/api.mdx L14 -- 'from neograph import RenderedInput'; RenderedInput is NOT exported from neograph (internal dataclass). Fix the import example.
5. walkthrough/produce-and-gather.mdx L80 -- the doc's own FakeSearchTool.invoke() is called with a config= kwarg it does not accept (doc-local fake bug).

After fixing each, remove its skip marker so Stage D executes it. Also verify item 1's CLAUDE.md occurrence.
design:
## Root Cause
Five doc snippets drifted from the current API and were skip-masked to keep Stage D green. Each is an independent doc-local defect (wrong kwarg name / non-exported import / doc-local fake signature), not a single systemic API break.

## Fix Approach (doc-only, minimal per snippet)
1. lint.mdx: output= -> outputs= (all 3 occurrences for correctness; 2 are in skipped illustrative fragments). In the executable 'full lint workflow' block, build a self-contained 'pipeline' from summarize (e.g. construct_from_functions('lint-demo',[summarize]) or Construct) so the max_len from_config assertions hold; do NOT rely on the page-threaded 'flat' pipeline.
2. modifier-kwargs.mdx (loop_history): ARCHITECT DECISION REQUIRED. Option A (doc-only, in-scope): rewrite the executable snippet to use programmatic 'refine_node | Loop(history=True)' (or construct the Loop modifier), and reframe prose so loop_history is presented as a Loop-modifier feature, not a @node kwarg. Option B (out-of-nominal-scope but parity-correct, ~3 lines): add loop_history param to decorator and pass history= into the Loop(**loop_kwargs) build at decorators.py:629. Prefer whichever the architect blesses; default to A since the bead is scoped doc-only.
3. api.mdx: remove RenderedInput and build_rendered_input from the 'from neograph import (...)' example (internal, not exported); keep ExcludeFromOutput.
4. oracle-ensemble.mdx: drop merge_model="reason" from the @node(...) call (no such kwarg).
5. produce-and-gather.mdx: change FakeSearchTool.invoke(self, args) -> invoke(self, args, config=None) to match framework tool-invocation (_agent_cycle.py:637 payload.invoke(args, config=config)).

## Core Invariant
Every executed doc snippet must run against the CURRENT public neograph API using only exported symbols and real @node/Loop/Oracle kwargs — no skip-marker may hide a snippet that would fail against the shipped API. Fixes change DOCS (and doc-local fakes) to match the API, never the reverse (unless the architect elects Option B parity-wiring for loop_history).

description: P2. title: ForwardConstruct: Loop + branch composition fails (Construct.outputs vs .output)
description:
## Problem
When self.loop() produces a Construct that ends up in a branch arm (via the re-trace strategy), compile_state_model crashes with AttributeError because _add_output_field accesses .outputs (Node-only plural) but Construct has .output (singular).

## Reproduce
test_loop.py::TestForwardConstructLoop::test_loop_followed_by_branch_composes (currently xfail strict=True)

## Root cause
state.py _add_output_field and the branch arm node iteration in compile_state_model assume all items are Nodes. When self.loop() puts a Construct in the traced node list, the branch tracer can put it in _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes or false_arm_nodes. The state builder then calls item.outputs (plural) on it, which doesn't exist on Construct.

## Fix approach
In state.py branch arm iteration, check isinstance(arm_node, Construct) and use .output (singular) instead of .outputs (plural). Same pattern as the existing sub-construct handling.

## Verification
Remove the xfail marker from test_loop_followed_by_branch_composes, test must pass.
design:
## Fix
1. state.py: in branch arm loop, check isinstance(arm_node, Construct). If Construct, handle same as sub_constructs section (use .output singular, apply modifier-aware field creation).
2. compiler.py _add_branch_to_graph: check isinstance(node, Construct). If Construct, use _add_subgraph() path (compile sub-graph, make_subgraph_fn) instead of make_node_fn.

Core invariant: Branch arms can contain both Nodes and Constructs — the same dispatch logic used at top-level (isinstance checks) must apply inside branch arms.
notes:
## Trace similar
Two crash sites when Construct appears in branch arm:
1. state.py:80-81 — _add_output_field(arm_node) accesses .outputs (Node-only)
2. compiler.py:507-513 — make_node_fn(arm_node) expects Node, not Construct

Both need isinstance checks to dispatch to Construct handling.
close_reason: Construct.outputs crash fixed, sequential loops fixed, sub-construct input extraction fixed. 2 xfails remain for loop+branch (neograph-477t).

title: Compiler should register output model types with LangGraph msgpack allowlist
description: When compiling a construct with MemorySaver checkpointer, LangGraph warns about unregistered types during checkpoint deserialization (on resume after interrupt). The compiler knows all node output types at compile time — it should collect them and pass to LangGraph via allowed_msgpack_modules. Currently produces hundreds of 'Deserializing unregistered type' warnings on resume. Types to register: all node output Pydantic models, their nested types (enums, sub-models), and framework types (NodeType, NodeStatus, GuaranteeType etc.).
design:
## Root Cause
LangGraph's JsonPlusSerializer defaults to _allowed_msgpack_modules=True (warn-and-allow). neograph's compile() passes the checkpointer through unchanged. with_msgpack_allowlist() is a no-op when _allowed_msgpack_modules is True. Result: every user Pydantic type triggers a warning on checkpoint deserialization.

## Fix Approach
In compile() (compiler.py), after compile_state_model(), collect all output types from the state model. Build an allowlist of (module, classname) tuples. Create a new JsonPlusSerializer with the explicit allowlist and replace the checkpointer's serde before passing to graph.compile(). Use LangGraph's _collect_from_type or walk Pydantic fields manually.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py::TestMsgpackTypeRegistration::test_output_types_registered_when_compiled_with_checkpointer
- Root cause: compile() never modifies checkpointer's serde. _allowed_msgpack_modules stays True (warn-all mode).
## Trace Similar
Pattern: compile() passes checkpointer to graph.compile() but doesn't configure it.
Only one instance of this pattern: checkpointer.serde._allowed_msgpack_modules.
No other LangGraph serialization configuration gaps found in the codebase.
Sub-construct compilation (line 108) also threads the checkpointer but LangGraph handles sub-graph checkpoint scoping internally.
## Architect Review
Core invariant: compile() must configure all LangGraph internals that depend on type knowledge.
Approach: ALL_LOW — walk state model fields, collect (module, classname) tuples, create new JsonPlusSerializer.
Risk: Depends on LangGraph's _allowed_msgpack_modules private attr. Wrap in try/except to gracefully degrade if API changes.

title: Expose a public LAZY single-tool MCP factory with explicit tool_name + rename (no build-time discovery)
description:
## What
Add a public neograph_mcp helper — e.g. a singular `mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None) -> ToolFactory`, or a `lazy=True` + explicit `tools={server: [names]}` / `rename={key: name}` option on `mcp_tool_factories` — that returns a single async ToolFactory which (a) DEFERS the MCP connect into the async factory body (NO build-time `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names)`), and (b) renames the discovered (possibly gateway-namespaced) tool to an explicit `rename_to` name. The internal `_make_tool_factory` (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:198) ALREADY implements BOTH behaviours (a lazy `_factory` body that connects on await + a `rename_to` param); this is purely a public-API-exposure gap.

## Why
A consumer binding a gateway-federated tool into a neograph node with a fixed `Tool('<bare-name>')` binding needs BOTH the factory-dict key AND the bound `tool.name` to be the BARE name. IBM ContextForge re-exposes federated tools NAMESPACED as `<peer>-<tool>`, but `mcp_tool_factories` only offers `namespace=True` ('server::tool') or `namespace=False` (the discovered namespaced name) — NEITHER yields the bare name. Separately, `mcp_tool_factories` connects EAGERLY at build time via `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names)`, which fires a live gateway connect inside a consumer's OFFLINE factory-build path (agent-stark's `build_tool_factories` runs at compile for every run + directly in offline fast tests) and breaks the deterministic suite. Today consumers must reach into the private `_make_tool_factory` or hand-roll the MultiServerMCPClient plumbing — both duplicate what neograph owns (nmb2). Surfaced by agent-stark's stark-63q.54.4 MCP-gateway GATE, which is BLOCKED on this.

## Expectations after delivery
- A consumer can bind ONE gateway-federated MCP tool into a node whose `Tool(name)` binding is a fixed bare name, with the factory built offline (no network until run/superstep time).
- agent-stark stark-63q.54.4 unblocks: build_tool_factories swaps the perplexity_research entry to this public lazy+rename factory with zero build-time connect.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: constructing the factory performs ZERO network I/O (assert no connection attempted at build); the connect happens only on first `await factory(config, tool_config)`. Against a live/fake MCP server exposing `<peer>-perplexity_research`, the awaited tool has `.name == 'perplexity_research'` (the rename) and invokes correctly. nmb2: the client is owned inside the factory (existing session-ownership guard stays green).

## Acceptance
- Public API in `neograph_mcp.__all__` builds a single async ToolFactory for a known (server, tool_name) with NO build-time network I/O.
- Returned tool `.name == rename_to` when provided (renames a gateway-namespaced `<peer>-<tool>` back to bare).
- nmb2 session-ownership invariant preserved; covered by a test.
- (Reuses the already-implemented internal _make_tool_factory — should be a thin public wrapper.)
design:
## Core Invariant
The MultiServerMCPClient is created and OWNED strictly inside the returned async factory body (nmb2) AND no MCP network I/O happens until the first await -- the singular helper adds a public name over _make_tool_factory without moving one line of connect logic out of the deferred _factory body.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token') -> ToolFactory` in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py, immediately after `mcp_tool_factories` (near :259). Body is a THIN delegation: `return _make_tool_factory(server_key, spec, tool_name, rename_to, token_provider, stdio_token_arg)`. Do NOT call _run_sync / _discover_tool_names / get_tools -- the whole feature is that build-time is connect-free. Docstring: state the single-tool / gateway-federated use case, the zero-build-network guarantee, and that `rename_to` maps a discovered (possibly namespaced <peer>-<tool>) name back to the bare Tool(name) binding. Mirror the plural's docstring voice.
2. Export it: add `mcp_tool_factory` to the import block (src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-41) and to `__all__` (:43-49). __all__ is the public contract (AGENTS.md naming policy).
3. Add a demo tool to exercise the namespaced->bare rename faithfully: `@mcp.tool(name='crm-perplexity_research')` in examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (a bare read-only echo tool, ~5 lines, token-echoing like crm_search). Safe: E2E/battery tool-set assertions are subset/membership.
4. Tests in tests/test_mcp_battery.py, new methods under (or beside) `TestOneConsumerSmoke`, all `@requires_mcp`, run via `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py`:
   (a) construction is zero-network: `f = mcp_tool_factory('crm', _demo_stdio_server(), tool_name='crm-perplexity_research', rename_to='perplexity_research')`; assert `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(f)` with NO subprocess spawned (no get_tools at build). Optionally construct against an unreachable spec and assert it still returns without raising.
   (b) awaited tool renames + invokes: `tool = await f(config, None)`; assert `tool.name == 'perplexity_research'`; assert it invokes correctly against the real demo server (echoes acting_as / returns payload).
   (c) token injection BEFORE rename: pin the order -- a stdio token_provider still injects `stdio_token_arg` even though the tool is renamed (proves inject introspects the real pre-rename schema). Assert the echoed token arrives AND `tool.name == rename_to`.
   (d) nmb2 preserved: rely on the existing tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py guard (scans all of src/neograph_mcp) -- confirm it stays green; the client is born inside the delegated _factory, so preservation is by construction. No new guard needed.
5. Run gates: `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py` + mypy on the two touched src files. Full suite per landing-the-plane.
6. Follow-up (separate, not this atom): website single-tool/gateway subsection; unblock agent-stark stark-63q.54.4 (swap perplexity_research entry to this lazy+rename factory).
notes:
2026-07-09 SEAM ANALYSIS (session leader, claim verified against src/neograph_mcp/_client.py): confirmed pure exposure gap — _make_tool_factory:183 is already fully lazy (all I/O incl. get_tools + rename inside the async _factory body, lines 198-212) and already takes rename_to. The ONLY build-time connect is the plural builder's _run_sync(_discover_tool_names) at :243. DECIDED SHAPE: the singular public helper mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token') -> ToolFactory — a thin delegation to _make_tool_factory + __all__ export. NOT the lazy= flag on the plural: discovery is inherently a connect, so lazy=True would contradict mcp_tool_factories' own contract and require a parallel tools={} argument (a second function wearing a flag). Tests: (1) zero network at construction (count connect attempts; first await connects), (2) awaited tool .name == rename_to against the demo server's namespaced name + invokes correctly, (3) nmb2 session-ownership guard green (preserved by construction — client born inside the factory body), (4) stdio token injection applies through the singular path, (5) PIN the order: token injection BEFORE rename (:208 -> :210) so stdio_token_arg introspects the server's real declared args. Effort: small (wrapper + docstring + integration tests via the FastMCP demo server, --extra mcp-examples harness). Gates y5ux (wired). Website: add a short 'single-tool / gateway-federated' subsection to walkthrough/mcp-client.mdx + concepts/mcp-integration.mdx when it lands.
## Findings (research grounded 2026-07-09, dp-researcher against current source)

- CONFIRMED pure exposure gap. `_make_tool_factory` (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:183-214) is ALREADY fully lazy and ALREADY takes `rename_to`. Its returned inner `_factory` (198-212) performs ALL I/O on await: `_resolve_token`(199) -> `_client_for`(200) -> `get_tools`(201) -> tool lookup by name(202) -> stdio token inject(208-209) -> rename(210-211). Zero I/O runs at `_make_tool_factory` call time. Signature is positional: `(server_key, spec, tool_name, rename_to, token_provider, stdio_token_arg) -> ToolFactory`.
