title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-s7zt3.7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-s7zt3.7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-s7zt3.7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.7/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-s7zt3.7
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-s7zt3.7
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.7`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-s7zt3.7)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.7 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

description:
Prerequisite for the two MCP-featuring examples (neograph-qb7q, neograph-3m6g), per maintainer 2026-07-08: fakes would demo neograph, not MCP — spin up a real FastMCP server so the examples exercise the actual protocol end-to-end while staying offline/deterministic/keyless.

DELIVERABLES:
1. examples/_mcp_demo_server.py — a FastMCP server (the mcp SDK's FastMCP; verify API against the version langchain-mcp-adapters 0.3.x pins) with the demo domain both examples share: TOOLS crm_search (read-only, idempotent), kb_lookup (read-only), update_deal (mutating), get_deal (returns the deal AND resource_link content blocks pointing at activity-history + email-history resources — RESEARCH ITEM: verify the pinned SDK version supports returning ResourceLink content items from a tool; if not, return structured link dicts and lift accordingly, documenting the gap); RESOURCES mcp://crm/deals/{id}/activity + a TEMPLATED mcp://crm/deals/{id}/emails{?from,to} (RFC 6570 — the query-a-fraction beat); an EXPIRY knob (env var or a control tool) that invalidates the email-history URI once so example 24's self-healing beat gets a REAL -32002 from a real server; AUTH echo — the server reads the Authorization/bearer (or a token arg for stdio) and stamps it into tool results so example 23's per-operator beat is observable.
2. TRANSPORT: stdio — the examples spawn the server as a subprocess (StdioConnection(command=sys.executable, args=[.../_mcp_demo_server.py])) via MultiServerMCPClient. No ports, no network; CI-safe. Document the streamable-http variant in comments only.
3. DEPS: pyproject optional extra (e.g. mcp-examples = [langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.3, mcp>=1.28]) — NOT core deps (src/ has zero MCP imports; the no-session-ownership guard scans src/ only, examples are exempt like the langfuse example precedent). Add the extra to the dev group so CI installs it.

TEST HARNESS: pytest integration tests that RUN both examples end-to-end as subprocess-spawning E2Es (skipif the extra is missing, so the core suite stays dependency-light); wire into the examples guard conventions (test_guards_examples.py) and the no-key example list in AGENTS.md — these ARE no-key but need the extra; document that distinction.
5. Confirm the no-session-ownership guard stays green (server + client usage live entirely in examples/); confirm uv run --extra mcp-examples runs both.

notes:
2026-07-08 DELIVERED. Files: examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (server), tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py (harness), pyproject mcp-examples extra, test_guards_examples.py (optional-extra import exemption + non-vacuity meta), AGENTS.md docs.

VERIFIED SERVER CONTRACT (empirically, real stdio round-trip — for qb7q/3m6g/xdt2):
- Client wiring: MultiServerMCPClient({"crm": {"command": sys.executable, "args": [<_mcp_demo_server.py>], "transport": "stdio", "env": {"NEOGRAPH_MCP_DEMO_STATE": <path>}}}). Tools via client.get_tools(); resources via `async with client.session("crm") as s: s.read_resource(AnyUrl(...))`.
- Tools: crm_search/kb_lookup (read-only idempotent), update_deal (mutating), get_deal (returns TextContent(deal json) + 2 ResourceLink blocks), arm_email_expiry (control). All echo `token` arg -> result["acting_as"] (per-operator identity; stdio has no headers, token is an ARG).
- get_deal ResourceLinks surface CLIENT-SIDE as {'type':'file','url':...} content blocks (NOT 'resource_link') — that's how langchain-mcp-adapters maps them. Manifest lifting must read type=='file' url.
- Resources: mcp://crm/deals/{id}/activity ; email fraction mcp://crm/deals/{id}/emails?from=..&to=.. (real query string honored by a custom low-level read_resource handler).
- Expiry/-32002: arm_email_expiry() writes a one-shot marker (env-pinned path, shared across subprocess spawns); first emails read after arming raises real McpError code -32002, self-clears (next read succeeds) = the self-heal beat. MUST catch INSIDE `async with client.session()` — the session teardown wraps escaping exceptions in an ExceptionGroup.

TWO mcp 1.28.x SDK GAPS worked around (documented in server docstring): (1) FastMCP @mcp.resource can't express RFC-6570 query templates; (2) @tool/@resource wrappers swallow JSON-RPC codes -> a real -32002 needs a custom @mcp._mcp_server.read_resource() handler. Pin mcp>=1.28,<2 (2.0 renames FastMCP->MCPServer).

DEVIATION from ticket: extra is NOT added to the default dev group. Rationale: the ticket also requires skipif-so-core-stays-light; putting deps in the default dev group defeats the importorskip. Resolution: optional extra only; CI runs the MCP E2Es via an explicit `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp-examples pytest tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py` step. Core `uv run --extra dev pytest` skips the module cleanly (verified: 2702 passed/1 skip light; 2708/2 with extra).

GATES: full suite green both configs; ruff format+check clean; mypy clean on new files; no-session-ownership guard green (src/ untouched, zero MCP imports in src). Example-running coverage (test_mcp_example_runs_end_to_end auto-discovers examples/2?_mcp_*.py) is live but empty until qb7q/3m6g land.

title: izo1-C: Validator tightening — node.context fields must have producers
description:
## Context

Third of 4 subtasks under epic neograph-izo1. Independent of A and B; can run in parallel with B once A lands. (Doesn't strictly need A either, but izo1 is the umbrella.)

§7 says "silent-None reads of required fields are a bug." The live manifestation: a node declares `context=["typoed_field"]`, no upstream produces `typoed_field`, runtime reads silently as None, renders in LLM prompt as the literal string `"None"`. Today the validator doesn't catch this at compile time.

This subtask closes the door at compile time — typoed context fields fail loudly before runtime.

## Source of truth

- `docs/design/state-bus-required-getter-2026-05-20.md` Q2 (validator gap analysis) + Section 4 step 3 (Phase C)
- `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §7

## Scope

### EDIT
- `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py` — extend validator
- `tests/test_validation.py` — new test asserting the new compile-time check
- Existing fixtures or tests with `context=["bad_field"]` that were silently tolerated — fix them (Phase E for THIS subtask)

### DO NOT TOUCH
- `src/neograph/_state_bus.py` (izo1-A)
- Call-site migrations (izo1-B)
- Structural guard for .get() discipline (izo1-D)

## The fix

In `_construct_validation.py`'s node-validation walk:

For each `Node` with `context=[<field_names>]`, verify every field name in the list corresponds to a field name produced by some upstream node's `outputs` dict (or single output) in the same construct.

If a context field has NO producer:
- Raise `ConstructError` at compile time
- Error message: `[Construct 'X', Node 'Y'] context field '<name>' has no producer; declare it as an output of an upstream node or remove it from context`

## Implementation

### TDD red→green

1. Write the failing test FIRST in `tests/test_validation.py`:
```python
def test_context_field_with_no_producer_raises_at_compile(self):
    @node(outputs=Result)
    def consumer(input: Input) -> Result: ...
    # consumer.context = ["nonexistent_field"]  # or build programmatically
    construct = Construct(name="bad", nodes=[consumer])
    with pytest.raises(ConstructError, match="nonexistent_field"):
        compile(construct, llm_factory=..., prompt_compiler=...)
```

2. Run → RED (currently the typo is silently tolerated; runtime renders "None")

3. Extend `_construct_validation.py`:
   - Walk all nodes in the construct
   - For each node with non-empty `context`, collect upstream producers' output field names
   - Assert each context field name is in the producer set
   - Raise `ConstructError` with the node name + field name on miss

4. Run → GREEN

### Side effect

`_execute.py:46`'s live "None" rendering bug becomes IMPOSSIBLE at runtime once this validator change lands. Any pipeline that would have hit the bug now fails to compile with a clear error message.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_validation.py::TestContextFieldProducerValidation` (new class) — or extend existing class
**Test type**: TDD red→green + structural-validation
**What it exercises**: compile-time rejection of pipelines with typoed context fields; explicit error message
**Expected initial state**: failing — current validator doesn't check this
**Persistence**: stays in suite permanently as regression guard

Order: write failing test → confirm RED → extend validator → confirm GREEN. Also run full suite to surface any FIXTURES with typoed context that were silently tolerated (Phase E for this subtask — fix the fixtures, not the validator).

## Acceptance

- `_construct_validation.py` rejects pipelines where any node's `context=[...]` references a field with no upstream producer
- Error message names the construct, the node, and the bad field
- New test in `tests/test_validation.py` covers the rejection
- Any existing fixtures with typoed context are fixed
- `make quality 2>&1 | grep -E "passed|failed|error"` green

## Effort

~2h. Validator extension + 1 test + fixture fix-out.

## Dependencies

Technically independent — can run in parallel with izo1-B. But izo1 epic blocks waiting for both.

## Out of scope

- StateBus.get_required (izo1-A)
- Runtime call-site migration (izo1-B)
- Structural guard for .get() discipline (izo1-D)
notes:
## Prep
- Existing validator at _construct_validation.py:296-306 already does the check for top-level constructs (skipped when construct.input is None — i.e., for sub-constructs).
- field_name_for() is a no-op for non-hyphenated names; comparison works for the common case.
- Real gaps to test: (a) top-level + non-hyphenated context with no producer → already raises; (b) sub-construct context → not validated (Q3 chose recommendation (b): leave best-effort, enforce at receiving #9 read in izo1-B); (c) hyphenated context names → comparison may break.
- Approach: write 3 TDD tests covering top-level rejection, hyphenated rejection, and assertion-message shape. If top-level case already passes (validator catches), that's GREEN-on-first-write and that's fine — the test is the regression guard. The actual functional gap stays unenforced per Q3(b).

title: ARCH-3: helper-monopoly sweeps (HIGH-05/06/10, MED-06) — output_field_name + .primary + naming canonicity + StateKeys
description:
## Architectural invariant

Every canonical helper in `src/neograph/` has a MONOPOLY: the helper is the ONLY way to express its concern. Hand-rolled equivalents are structurally banned. The codebase's existing pattern (the StateBus / normalize_outputs / output_field_name triad) is enforced at every relevant site, not just the motivating one. Helpers with similar concerns have ONE canonical name; near-duplicate aliases (Levenshtein ≤ 2) are renamed to one OR allowlisted with a documented reason.

## Source findings

Synthesis `.claude/code-review/020626_2218/synthesis.md`:
- **HIGH-05** — `output_field_name(base, key)` exists but 2 callers use it, 7 inline `f"{x}_{key}"` joins bypass it. Sites in `state.py`, `_state_write.py:65`, `_wiring.py:289`.
- **HIGH-06** — `normalize_outputs(x).primary` exists but 5 sites hand-roll `next(iter(x.values()))` in `_construct_validation.py:157, 204, 209` and `_oracle.py:180, 273`.
- **HIGH-10** — Dual-named helper `_isinstance_safe` (def at `di.py:91`) vs `_is_instance_safe` (alias at `factory.py:57`, used in `_input_shape.py:12`). Grep-hostile.
- **CON-01 / MED-06** — Framework state keys `node_id`, `project_root`, `human_feedback`, `_neo_isolated_input` (`node.py:414`) scattered as raw literals across 4 modules; `StateKeys` regex `^neo_` MISSES `_neo_isolated_input` due to the leading underscore.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (per molecule)

For each of the 5 disease patterns above, read the helper definition AND the bypassing sites AND the existing structural guards. Document which guards exist and which gaps let the bypasses through.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan (per molecule)

Run ALL FIVE scans (or condensed equivalents):

1. `grep -nE 'f["\047][^"\047]*\{[^}]*\}_\{[^}]*\}["\047]' src/neograph/` — output-field f-string joins
2. `grep -rn 'next(iter([^)]*\.values()))' src/neograph/` — hand-rolled .primary
3. `git grep -nE '_(is)?_?instance_safe'` — dual-named helper
4. `grep -rn '"node_id"\|"project_root"\|"human_feedback"\|"_neo_' src/neograph/` — framework literals
5. AST scan for `StateKeys.<name>` vs raw literal in source

Disposition table per pattern.

## Phase 2 — Target design

For each pattern, the fix shape:

1. **output_field_name sweep** — every MIGRATE row converted to `output_field_name(base, key)`. Structural guard: AST-scan disallowing `f"{base}_{key}"` patterns where `key` looks like an output-key variable.

2. **normalize_outputs().primary sweep** — every MIGRATE row converted. Structural guard: AST-scan disallowing `next(iter(<expr>.values()))` where `<expr>` is a known outputs container.

3. **_isinstance_safe consolidation** — pick one name (`_is_instance_safe` reads better but `_isinstance_safe` is the definition; the synthesis recommends the definition wins). Delete the alias. PROC-2's naming-canonicity guard catches future regressions.

4. **StateKeys centralization** — add `StateKeys.NODE_ID`, `StateKeys.PROJECT_ROOT`, `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK`, `StateKeys.NEO_ISOLATED_INPUT`. Migrate raw literals. Fix the existing guard's regex from `^neo_` to `^_?neo_` (or rewrite AST-based per TQ-03).

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY. Iterate until:
- Every MIGRATE row in every disposition table is fixed
- Each helper has a structural guard banning the hand-rolled equivalent
- `_isinstance_safe`/`_is_instance_safe` resolves to one canonical name
- StateKeys regex is fixed AND a slip meta-test (the `_neo_isolated_input` case) exists in the guard

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO leaving HIGH-06 sites that "look different" (e.g., `next(iter(x.values()))` where `x` is named something else) — if the semantic is "get the first/primary output value," use `.primary`.
- NO adding `output_field_name` callers without removing inline duplicates already in the file.
- NO leaving the alias `_is_instance_safe = _isinstance_safe` with a comment "for backward compat" — at 0.x there is no backward compat to preserve.
- NO `StateKeys` migration that adds new constants without deleting the raw literals that motivated them.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification (per molecule)

Re-run all 5 scans. Zero hits in src/ (modulo allowlisted false positives with documented reasons). Each structural guard has positive + negative + regex-slip meta-tests.

## Phase 6 — Independent review (per molecule)

Opus reviewer:
1. Are there OTHER helpers with similar bypass risk that this ticket didn't address? (Run the helper-monopoly pattern more broadly.)
2. Is the `_isinstance_safe` rename actually the right canonical name? (Naming bikeshed is fine here — the codebase will use this name forever.)
3. Did the `StateKeys` migration miss any literals? Run the scan once more from the reviewer's side.

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- HIGH-05, HIGH-06, HIGH-10, MED-06 all resolved
- 4 new structural guards (one per pattern) with full meta-test discipline
- One canonical name for `_isinstance_safe` family
- `StateKeys` regex fixed; `_neo_isolated_input` slip case captured as meta-test
- `make quality` green
- Independent reviewer verdict ELEGANT ≥85

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-6h08l
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-6h08l` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-6h08l/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-6h08l
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-6h08l)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-6h08l --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-6h08l --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-6h08l/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-6h08l codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-6h08l/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-6h08l
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-6h08l
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-6h08l`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-6h08l)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-6h08l --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-6h08l sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: ARCH-DECOMP-1: split _construct_validation.py (1005L) by validation concern
description:
## Architectural invariant

`src/neograph/_construct_validation.py` (currently 1005 LOC, the synthesis's "hardest code in the repo, and it's correct") is decomposed by validation concern into ≥3 focused modules. Each module owns ONE validation rule family. No module exceeds ~400 LOC. The split preserves every existing rule behaviorally — this is reshape, not rewrite.

## Why this is filed (and why it's P3)

The Jun-2026 multi-agent review explicitly praised this file's CORRECTNESS while flagging its size as a smell. Post-ARCH-SWEEP, the codebase is structurally coherent; the only remaining "is it too big?" anxieties (per a Jun-2026 maintainer audit) point at three files of which this is the largest. NOT a release blocker — the file works and is well-tested. But the decomposition is the cheapest plausible 1000→400 LOC win on the whole project.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

Read `_construct_validation.py` in full. Inventory every top-level function + class. Categorize each as belonging to ONE of:

- **Type compatibility** (`_types_compatible`, `_unwrap_optional`, PEP-604 helpers, `_MISSING` sentinel, ForwardRef resolution)
- **Fan-in validation** (`_check_fan_in_inputs`, `_check_item_input`, producer registry walk)
- **Fan-out / Each path resolution** (Each path navigation, list-element compatibility, dotted-path walk)
- **Context validation** (the recursive `_validate_node_chain` + `ambient_producers` + sub-construct depth)
- **Loop self-edge** (`validate_loop_self_edge`, output/input back-edge compat)
- **Merge hooks** (`_validate_merge_hooks` — Oracle hook arity/type checks)
- **Naming / field-name helpers** (small utilities)

Some functions cross categories — note which. Output the inventory as a table in bead notes.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern: "Validation rule helpers OUTSIDE `_construct_validation.py` that duplicate or shadow rules that should live in it." Scan for any validation logic in `node.py`, `modifiers.py`, `construct.py`, `_ir_normalize.py`, `_construct_builder.py`. Disposition table per the molecule.

This is also the input to deciding split boundaries — if e.g. modifier validation is already cross-referenced from `modifiers.py`, the split should preserve the seam.

## Phase 2 — Target design

Propose the new module layout. Strawman (validate during architect review):

- `src/neograph/_validation/__init__.py` (re-exports for `construct.py`'s single import call site)
- `src/neograph/_validation/_types.py` — type compatibility primitives
- `src/neograph/_validation/_fan_in.py` — fan-in producer registration + match
- `src/neograph/_validation/_fan_out.py` — Each path resolution + list-element checks
- `src/neograph/_validation/_context.py` — recursive walk + ambient_producers
- `src/neograph/_validation/_loop.py` — loop self-edge
- `src/neograph/_validation/_merge_hooks.py` — Oracle hook validation
- `src/neograph/_validation/_walker.py` — the top-level `_validate_node_chain` orchestrator (the only thing `construct.py` calls)

Single import boundary: `construct.py` imports `from neograph._validation import _validate_node_chain, ConstructError`. Internal module relationships private to the package.

Test files split in lockstep — `tests/test_validation.py` (currently slimmed-down post-`e8jg`) becomes the orchestrator-level test; per-rule tests already live in `test_fanin_validation.py`, `test_context_validation.py`, `test_construct_validation_merge_hooks.py` from the earlier split. Confirm no new test files needed.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID rigorously. Iterate until ALL of:

- No new module exceeds 400 LOC.
- Every function lives in exactly ONE module (no duplication across the split).
- `construct.py` has exactly ONE import line from the new package.
- Existing per-rule tests need at most their import line updated.
- The walker (top-level `_validate_node_chain`) is < 100 LOC — it's an orchestrator, not a rule-carrier.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO copying a function into a new module and leaving the original "for compat." Move = delete from old + add to new.
- NO `from neograph._validation._foo import *` star-imports in the `__init__.py`. List exports explicitly.
- NO module that ends up < 100 LOC — that's over-splitting. Merge sibling concerns if a candidate module is too thin.
- The validation BEHAVIOR must not change. Any test diff outside import updates is a red flag.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

- Re-run the Phase 1 inventory against the new layout. Every function from the original 1005-LOC file is in exactly one new module.
- `wc -l src/neograph/_validation/*.py` → all ≤ 400.
- `grep -rn "from neograph._validation" src/neograph/` → only `construct.py` appears outside the package itself.
- Run the full test suite — zero behavioral diffs.
- Add structural guard `TestValidationPackageBoundary`: AST-scan asserting `_validate_node_chain` and `ConstructError` are the only public names exported from `neograph._validation`.

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer evaluates:
1. Is the split boundary architecturally honest, or did the executor draw lines just to hit the LOC target?
2. Did the test suite catch every behavioral edge during the move?
3. Is the package `__init__.py` minimal (single import seam) or did it accumulate convenience re-exports?
4. Would the next contributor adding a new validation rule know which sub-module to put it in?

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- `_construct_validation.py` deleted; replaced by `neograph._validation` package (≥3 modules, none >400 LOC)
- `construct.py` imports unchanged in semantics (one line)
- All existing tests pass; test-file imports updated only as needed
- Structural guard pins the package boundary
- Independent reviewer ELEGANT ≥85
design:
## Core Invariant
Validation BEHAVIOR is byte-identical to the 1005-LOC original — every rule fires on exactly the same inputs producing the same ConstructError messages and locations; only file boundaries and the import seam change (reshape, not rewrite).

## Target module layout (4 files: 3 new sub-modules + slimmed orchestrator)
Flat peer modules per the neograph-3zai precedent (NO sub-package). Dependency DAG leaf -> root (architect-verified acyclic):

1. _validation_types.py (~220 LOC) — LEAF. _types_compatible, _extract_list_element, _resolve_field_annotation, _MISSING, _fmt_type, _source_location; shared vocab Producer / ProducerMap / NodeItem / _is_construct_like; effective_producer_type. Imports ConstructError/NeographError from neograph.errors DIRECTLY (never from _construct_validation). No intra-cluster deps.
2. _validation_inputs.py (~350 LOC) — consumer input satisfaction: _check_item_input (dispatcher) + _check_fan_in_inputs + _check_each_path (Each fan-out) + _build_no_producer_error + _suggest_hint. Imports _validation_types. fan_out_candidates stays FUNCTION-LOCAL (real cycle via _ir_normalize->_sidecar->_di_classify->_construct_validation).
3. _validation_modifiers.py (~210 LOC) — modifier-triggered rules: validate_loop_self_edge + validate_loop_construct + _validate_merge_hooks. Imports _validation_types + modifiers.
4. _construct_validation.py (slimmed ~180 LOC) — ORCHESTRATOR: _validate_node_chain + ValidationMode (KEEP HERE — cv.ValidationMode guard at test_guards_assembly.py:1340) + explicit (non-star) RE-EXPORT block: ConstructError, _validate_node_chain, _types_compatible, effective_producer_type, validate_loop_self_edge, validate_loop_construct, ValidationMode, Producer, ProducerMap. get_merge_fn_metadata stays FUNCTION-LOCAL in the orchestrator.

Boundary rationale (architect-accepted, honest): _validation_inputs is one concern (single dispatcher routes fan-in vs Each). _validation_modifiers groups by trigger axis (fired from |/Oracle) — mildly grab-bag but serviceable; the ticket anti-thin-module clause (standalone fan_out ~105 / loop ~90 breach the 100-LOC floor) forces the merge. 4 files, not the strawman 7.

## Implementation Plan
1. (write-test atom) Author structural guard TestValidationModuleBoundary in test_guards_assembly.py: (a) line-cap (all cluster files <=400) + symbol-location table (each func in its target module, absent from orchestrator), (b) SEAM: only _construct_validation.py is imported by files OUTSIDE the cluster {_construct_validation, _validation_types, _validation_inputs, _validation_modifiers}; intra-cluster imports allowed, (c) no `from neograph._construct_validation import *` and no `import *` within cluster. Include negative meta-tests like TestConstructBuilderSplit. VERIFY IT FAILS pre-refactor (modules do not exist yet).
2. Create _validation_types.py; move type primitives + shared vocab + effective_producer_type + _source_location. Import ConstructError from neograph.errors.
3. Create _validation_inputs.py; move fan-in + Each-path + error builder + hint. Keep fan_out_candidates function-local.
4. Create _validation_modifiers.py; move loop self-edge + loop construct + merge hooks.

title: skip_when + Each: skip_value result not wrapped in Each dict key
description:
When a node has both skip_when= and map_over= (Each), the skip_value result is returned as a bare model instead of being wrapped in the {dispatch_key: value} dict that Each expects.

The state reducer (_merge_dicts) calls new.items() on the bare Pydantic model → AttributeError.

## Concrete case

```python
@node(
    outputs=RawClaim,
    model='fast',
    prompt='rw/canonicalize-claim',
    map_over='flatten_groups',
    map_key='group_id',
    skip_when=lambda group: len(group.members) == 1,
    skip_value=lambda group: RawClaim(r_id=group.group_id, statement=group.members[0].statement, source_section=''),
)
def canonicalize(group: IndexedClaimGroup) -> RawClaim: ...
```

Multi-member groups go through the LLM and get wrapped correctly: {"G000": RawClaim(...)}.
Singleton groups hit skip_when, return the bare RawClaim from skip_value.
The reducer merges dicts from multi-member + bare models from singletons → crash.

## Error

```
File neograph/state.py:40, in _merge_dicts
    for key, val in new.items():
AttributeError: 'RawClaim' object has no attribute 'items'
```

## Expected

skip_value results should be wrapped in {dispatch_key: value} the same way normal Each results are. The dispatch key comes from the Each item's key field (group.group_id in this case).
notes:
## Reproduction confirmed
- Test: test_skip_value_wrapped_in_each_key_when_skip_fires
- Error: TypeError: 'MatchResult' object is not a mapping (in _merge_dicts)
- Root cause: _apply_skip_when (factory.py:114) returns {field_name: bare_result} — misses the Each {dispatch_key: value} wrapping that _build_state_update does at L194-196
- Fix: _apply_skip_when must call _build_state_update instead of building the dict directly, OR inline the Each wrapping logic

Not strictly an oversight. The `config:` parameter in `lint.py` represents the user-supplied config-shape dict for DI binding lookup -- specifically the inner `configurable` mapping, not the full RunnableConfig with `thread_id` / `callbacks` siblings. Two valid stances:

**Stance A (housekeeping)**: type as RunnableConfig anyway; lint reads `config['configurable'][binding.name]` style which is a valid RunnableConfig subscript pattern.

**Stance B (current)**: leave as `dict[str, Any]`; lint is testing whether DI bindings resolve, the inner shape is what matters, and over-typing here would obscure that lint is checking the user's CONFIG payload rather than LangGraph's runtime config.

## Recommended action

Audit each call site:
- `lint.py:46` -- `lint(construct, *, config: dict[str, Any] | None = None, ...)` -- public signature, callers pass through `config['configurable']` essentially. If this should accept a full RunnableConfig that contains `configurable=...`, change accordingly. Otherwise leave with a docstring clarifying the contract.
- `lint.py:116, 150` -- internal helpers; follow whatever 46 settles on.

## Effort

~1 hour. Decision + edit + test.

## Why P4

Zero user-facing impact. Internal type-surface consistency only. Could close as 'accepted as-is' if Stance B is preferred -- in that case, document the rationale in the ticket close-reason and add a docstring note on the lint() signature explaining why it's not RunnableConfig.

## Out of scope

Promoting `config` to a typed `LintConfig` Pydantic model -- if the lint surface ever grows more knobs, that becomes its own LlmConfig-pattern ticket.

title: Unify forward.py _discover_node_attrs onto _classify_member (third member-collection site)
description: ForwardConstruct._discover_node_attrs (src/neograph/forward.py:157-170) is a third isinstance(Node)-only collection site with the same Construct-blind shape as the neograph-xv9ay disease. Deferred from the xv9ay disease scan because it is NOT a silent drop today: a Construct class attribute fails LOUD at class-definition time (Pydantic non-annotated-attribute error, verified 2026-07-10), and final membership is fixed by forward() tracing, not the attr walk. Once _classify_member exists in _construct_builder.py (xv9ay fix), evaluate whether ForwardConstruct attr discovery should adopt it — which would amount to sub-construct support in ForwardConstruct class bodies (a feature decision, not a bug). Scan artifacts: .claude/code-review/xv9ay/.
design:
## Core Invariant (reworded per review)
ForwardConstruct pipeline membership is fixed by forward() tracing, never by the class-attr walk — _discover_node_attrs is a name->Node lookup table feeding the tracer, deliberately EXEMPT from _classify_member; the exemption is safe only while a non-Node pipeline object in a class body fails LOUD (PydanticUserError via ignored_types=(Node,)) instead of silently dropping.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED: Option B — exempt-by-design, ratified by review verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT)
1. Pin the loud failure with a behavioral test in tests/test_forward.py: a ForwardConstruct subclass with a Construct class attribute raises PydanticUserError at class-definition time. This is a guard-existing-behavior test (passes immediately — sanctioned refactor shape); it turns the exemption into a contract: if ignored_types ever widens without membership work, this test fails.
2. Docstring the exemption in _discover_node_attrs (forward.py) with a cross-ref to _member_select.py: attr-set -> trace contract; sub-pipelines enter a forward() trace via self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble(), not class attrs.
3. Record the exemption in TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly's docstring (tests/test_guards_assembly.py) so future disease scans stop re-flagging forward.py:192.
4. No behavior change, no new feature, no website docs change.
Option A (full adoption) intentionally rejected: the disease (silent drop) does not exist here; adoption would ship an unrequested edge-case-heavy public feature redundant with self.each()/self.loop() with zero demand evidence.
notes:
## Findings
- PRECONDITION SATISFIED: _classify_member EXISTS. It lives in src/neograph/_member_select.py:39 (not _construct_builder.py as the bead text says -- it was EXTRACTED from _construct_builder.py per the module docstring; _construct_builder.py:33 now imports _bucket_members from it). No sequencing blocker.
- The reuse target is _member_select.py: _classify_member (THE single membership predicate, returns _MemberKind: DECORATED_NODE / PLAIN_NODE / SUB_CONSTRUCT / ARTIFACT-when-output-is-None) + _bucket_members (THE sole skip/warn/raise policy site, parameterized source='module'|'list'). Guard TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly (tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1715) bans isinstance(x, Node/Construct) classification outside _classify_member -- but its scan scope is ONLY _construct_builder.py + _member_select.py; forward.py is currently outside the guard.
- Current third site: ForwardConstruct._discover_node_attrs (src/neograph/forward.py:182-194) -- reverse-MRO walk collecting isinstance(attr, Node) only. NOT a silent drop today, RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-11 by live repro: a Construct class attribute raises PydanticUserError 'A non-annotated attribute was detected' at class-DEFINITION time, because model_config ignored_types=(Node,) (forward.py:147) covers only Node.
- KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: adopting _classify_member in _discover_node_attrs is meaningful ONLY together with extending ignored_types to include Construct. Without that, Pydantic raises before discovery ever runs, so the SUB_CONSTRUCT/ARTIFACT branches would be unreachable dead code -- pure cosmetic churn. Therefore adoption == the feature 'sub-construct support in ForwardConstruct class bodies', exactly as the bead frames it (feature decision, not bug).
- The downstream chain ALREADY supports Construct members: _Tracer._ordered is list[Node | Construct]; _Tracer.record_construct exists (forward.py:392, used by self.loop()/self.each() deferred builders since e9zse wave, commits a2834d6/d208f55); _Proxy._neo_source is typed Node | Construct | None; _trace_forward returns list[Node | Construct]; Construct.__init__ validation + compiler.py three-way dispatch already handle sub-constructs from the trace. The ONLY gaps are (a) Pydantic class-body acceptance, (b) discovery predicate, (c) _ForwardSelf.__getattr__/_NodeCall which today wrap only Node and call tracer.record (dedup + loop-tagging) not record_construct (no dedup, no loop-tag).
- xv9ay scan artifacts (.claude/code-review/xv9ay/disease-consistency.md Instance 3, disease-dedup.md site 3) explicitly deferred this site with: 'Flag it so the xv9ay fix consciously decides whether ForwardConstruct joins the unified member predicate or stays exempt-by-design; do not fold it into the same change blind. No repro written (no evidence forward sub-construct-as-attr is a supported/used shape).'
- Current vs deprecated: nothing deprecated here; the e9zse self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble() surfaces (June commits) are the CURRENT way sub-pipelines enter a forward() trace. Class-attr sub-constructs would be a second entry path for the same capability -- the feature-decision question is whether that redundancy is worth the symmetry with construct_from_module (which now collects sub-constructs post-xv9ay).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_member_select.py:39 (_classify_member) and :64 (_bucket_members) -- the monopoly predicate + policy site to REUSE; module docstring pins the layer (assembly/DX, same as _construct_builder; do NOT push into IR).
- src/neograph/forward.py:147 -- ignored_types=(Node,) model_config; the loud-fail gate that must widen to (Node, Construct) if the feature ships.
- src/neograph/forward.py:182-194 -- _discover_node_attrs, the site to migrate.
- src/neograph/forward.py:1127-1133 -- _ForwardSelf.__getattr__ returns _NodeCall(node_attrs[name], tracer); needs Construct awareness if feature ships.
- src/neograph/forward.py:382-394 -- _Tracer.record (dedup via _seen + loop-body Each-tagging) vs record_construct (neither); must be reconciled for repeat calls / bare-for loop bodies over a class-attr sub-construct.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1715 -- TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly; extend its scanned-paths set to forward.py as the guard-first step.
- tests/test_forward.py (~67 tests) -- where new behavior tests go; tests/check_fixtures/should_fail + should_pass -- every new validation rule needs fixtures per AGENTS.md.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Decision risk (for architect atom vgfwk.4): adopt-as-feature vs exempt-by-design-with-documentation. Both are defensible; the epic title says 'forward.py unify' which leans adopt, but the bead itself says feature decision. Researcher recommendation below in design.
- ignored_types with a BaseModel subclass: Pydantic's ignored_types is documented for arbitrary classes; verify it accepts a BaseModel subclass value (Construct) without schema side effects -- smoke-test in the regression atom before building on it.
- ARTIFACT policy: with ignored_types widened, a Construct(output=None) class attr no longer fails loud via Pydantic -- _classify_member's ARTIFACT branch becomes the loud gate. A class body is a promise (like source='list'), so policy should raise, but the policy must live in _member_select (the sole policy site), not inline in forward.py -- add a class-body source kind or a small policy helper there, or the monopoly guard's spirit is violated.
- record_construct has no _seen dedup and no _loop_body_nodes tagging: calling the same sub-construct attr twice would duplicate membership; calling it inside a bare for-loop body would silently NOT Each-wrap. Either unify record/record_construct semantics or loudly reject sub-construct calls in loop bodies for v1.
- Proxy naming: out_of_{name} and _over_path_for_proxy use field_name_for(source_node.name); confirm a sub-construct's output surfaces in parent state under field_name_for(construct.name) so downstream proxy consumption wires correctly (composition tests in test_composition.py are the reference).
- Doc surface: website ForwardConstruct docs + AGENTS.md would need the new shape documented if the feature ships (verifiable-docs remark plugin will build-fail on bad refs; run npm test in website/).
## Codebase Disease Scan (gtzkd)
Disease spec: membership CLASSIFICATION of arbitrary objects into pipeline members via private isinstance ladders outside _member_select._classify_member (the xv9ay disease). Shape: SYNTACTIC re-verification — the June xv9ay ticket already ran the full 3-lens multi-agent scan (.claude/code-review/xv9ay/); this atom re-swept src/neograph/*.py for isinstance(x, Node/Construct).

| Site | Kind | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| forward.py:192 _discover_node_attrs | collection-time classification (attr walk) | THIS TICKET — the deferred xv9ay Instance 3 |
| __main__.py:55 _discover_constructs | CLI discovery of top-level Constructs in a user module — collects whole pipelines, not members | EXEMPT (different question: 'is this a pipeline', not 'is this a member') |
| all other ~45 hits (validator/compiler/state/lint/verify/construct walkers) | dispatch over ALREADY-collected construct.nodes members — the sanctioned irreducible sum-type match (cf. AGENTS.md compiler exception) | EXEMPT |

Post-fix expectation: zero collection-time ladders outside _member_select; guard TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly scan scope extended to forward.py enforces it.
## Architect Review (vgfwk.4, independent)

Research verified against code: guard scan scope = BUILDER+SELECT only (forward.py out of scope, confirmed test_guards_assembly.py:1715+); tracer record() has _seen dedup + loop-body tagging while record_construct() has NEITHER (forward.py:382-394); _discover_node_attrs is isinstance(Node)-only (182-194); ignored_types=(Node,) (147); _classify_member lives in _member_select.py:39 (research correctly re-sourced it). Live repro CONFIRMS the load-bearing 'fails loud today' claim: a Construct instance as a non-annotated ForwardConstruct class attr raises PydanticUserError 'A non-annotated attribute was detected' at class-def time, and widening ignored_types to (Node, Construct) is the necessary gate — so adoption == the feature, exactly as framed.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: REJECT Option A as the default. The motivating disease (silent sub-construct DROP) does NOT exist at this site — it fails loud today (repro'd). So the correctness pressure behind xv9ay is absent here; the only pull toward A is code-symmetry. A ships a NET-NEW public API surface (class-attr sub-constructs in forward bodies) that is REDUNDANT with the CURRENT sanctioned entry path self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble() (e9zse wave) — reuse-over-reinvention cuts against a second way to do the same thing. No demand: the xv9ay scan itself recorded 'no evidence forward sub-construct-as-attr is a supported/used shape', and sole-downstream piarch has no cited need. Cost is NOT a small delta — the plan's own risks list 5+ genuine edge cases (record/record_construct reconciliation for dedup + loop-body tagging, _NodeCall/_ForwardSelf Construct-awareness, UNDEFINED bare-for-loop-over-subconstruct semantics, proxy out_of_{name} naming confirmation, ARTIFACT policy routing). Suggestion: adopt Option B (exempt-by-design: keep isinstance(Node), docstring cross-ref to _member_select, pin the loud failure, note the exemption in the guard). If piarch later needs class-attr sub-constructs, revisit A then — non-blocking.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: the Core Invariant conflates TWO different questions and, as written, forecloses Option B (makes B a self-inflicted invariant violation). _discover_node_attrs is a PRE-DECLARATION name->Node lookup feeding the proxy/tracer machinery; FINAL membership is fixed by the TRACE (_Tracer._ordered), NOT the attr walk — the bead's own notes say 'final membership is fixed by forward() tracing, not the attr walk.' Forcing that lookup to delegate to _classify_member ('the membership predicate') is a category error. Suggestion: reword the invariant so attr-discovery-for-tracing is explicitly distinct from member-classification, carving out the documented forward.py exemption — otherwise the invariant and the two-option framing contradict each other.

- [LOW] Finding: gate label 'codebase-scan:complete' is ABSENT on gtzkd (only 'research:complete' present), so the atom's hard-check fails — but the '## Codebase Disease Scan' disposition table IS present and vgfwk.3 is CLOSED, so the scan was substantively done; this is a bookkeeping miss, not a bypass. Suggestion: apply the missing label.

- [LOW] Finding: Option B step 2 pins on PydanticUserError, which is version-fragile (message/type can drift across Pydantic upgrades). Suggestion: assert on a stable message substring / behavior rather than the exact exception path; and in B step 3 document in the guard WHY forward.py is deliberately outside the scan scope (attr-discovery != membership).

- [LOW] Finding: bead DESCRIPTION/DESIGN text still says _classify_member lives in _construct_builder.py; it was extracted to _member_select.py (research corrected this). Suggestion: propagate the correction into the refined plan so the implementer targets the right module.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Triage
Review verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> refined autonomously per formula routing: plan switched to Option B, Core Invariant reworded (attr-walk is a tracing lookup, not membership classification). No user input needed — the bead itself framed this as 'evaluate whether'; the evaluation's answer is exempt-by-design.
## Regression Test (vgfwk.6)
- Test: tests/test_forward.py::TestConstructClassAttrFailsLoud::test_class_definition_raises_when_construct_declared_as_class_attr
- Status: PASSING (guard-existing-behavior pinning test per refined Option B plan — sanctioned refactor shape, not TDD red)

- Full tests/test_forward.py: 95 passed (no collateral damage).
## Implementation (Option B shipped)
- forward.py _discover_node_attrs docstring: exemption documented with cross-ref to _member_select + the pinning test.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly docstring: exemption recorded so scans stop re-flagging forward.py.

Re-scan: same grep as disease-scan atom. forward.py:203 remains BY DESIGN — it is now the documented, contract-pinned exemption (disposition changed from 'THIS TICKET' to 'ALLOWLIST/exempt-by-design' per the ratified Option B). title: Eliminate ghost state-model fields from post-construction context mutation
description: P2. Compile-time state model builds a field per node.context entry. If context is mutated after Construct() but before compile(), the state model includes fields with no producer (ghost fields). Surfaced during tzzi behavioral test where I deliberately exploited this to bypass the validator. Implication: production code path exists where state has fields untracked by any producer; introspection tools (schema fingerprint, checkpoint resume) treat these as real. Fix: freeze node.context at Construct.__init__ OR rebuild state model from current context at compile time only. Acceptance: post-construction context mutation either raises or is reflected consistently in state model + validator + producers.
close_reason: Subsumed by EPIC 1 (neograph-20xq). Assembly-path unification freezes the IR before the state model is built; ghost fields from post-init context mutation become structurally impossible.

## Core Invariant

description:

2. Replace each `Node(...) | Operator(when='condition_name')` with `@node(..., interrupt_when='condition_name')` OR `@node(..., interrupt_when=lambda state: ...)` depending on the test's existing form.

Use inline lambda form for examples (cleaner DX), keep pre-registered form for tests that specifically exercise `register_condition`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Full test suite stays green.

## Dependencies

- **neograph-6y3** — hard block.

title: loader.py mutates Node.inputs directly — violates immutable IR
description: loader.py:208-215 does node.inputs = input_type and node.inputs = inputs_dict. Comment says 'preserve immutability' but code directly assigns. Contradicts model_copy pattern in _construct_builder.py. If spec-driven pipeline reuses a Node across constructs, second sees mutated inputs. Fix: use model_copy.
design:
## Root Cause
_build_sub_construct(loader.py:204-216) does `node = all_nodes[field_ref]` then `node.inputs = input_type` — direct field mutation on the shared instance. Node is not frozen (model_config only has arbitrary_types_allowed), so the assignment succeeds and corrupts the shared object.

## Fix Approach
Replace lines 208 and 216 with model_copy:
- Line 208: `node = node.model_copy(update={'inputs': input_type})`
- Line 216: `node = node.model_copy(update={'inputs': inputs_dict})`
The local variable `node` is appended to `nodes` list on line 217, so the copy replaces the mutated original correctly.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_spec_loader.py::TestLoaderImmutability::test_sub_construct_does_not_mutate_shared_node
- Root cause: loader.py:208 and :216 directly assign node.inputs = ... on shared Node instances from all_nodes dict. If a Node is reused across constructs, second construct sees mutated inputs.
## Trace Similar
Pattern: direct field mutation on shared Node instances.

Found 6 sites total:
1. loader.py:208 — node.inputs = input_type [BUG, this ticket]
2. loader.py:216 — node.inputs = inputs_dict [BUG, this ticket]
3. construct.py:109 — item.llm_config = merged [BUG, neograph-bchn]
4. construct.py:119 — item.renderer = self.renderer [BUG, neograph-bchn]
5. decorators.py:503 — n.oracle_gen_type = gen_type [SAFE: fresh local Node]
6. decorators.py:586 — n.oracle_gen_type = gen_type [SAFE: fresh local Node]

Sites 1-4 mutate shared instances; sites 5-6 are safe (freshly constructed, pre-return). All 4 bugs are covered by gy9r and bchn tickets.
## Architect Review
Fix is mechanical: replace direct assignment with model_copy. No design decisions.
Core invariant: Node instances are immutable after construction.
Routing: ALL_LOW

title: Validator rejects list[T] consumer of Loop node — effective_producer_type missing Loop rule
description:
## Bug

effective_producer_type() in _construct_validation.py doesn't account for Loop modifier. Loop nodes produce list[T] via the append-list reducer, but effective_producer_type returns the raw output type T. This causes the validator to reject a downstream node that explicitly wants list[T] (all loop iterations), even though _extract_input would correctly find and pass the raw list at runtime.

## Root cause

effective_producer_type() only has rules for Each (→ dict[str, T]) and default (→ T). It's missing Loop (→ list[T]).

## Impact

False rejection at assembly time. A pipeline like:
  refine | Loop(...) → summarize(inputs=list[Draft])
fails validation with 'no upstream produces a compatible value' even though runtime would work.

## Reproduction

Node 'refine' with outputs=Draft | Loop modifier, then Node 'summarize' with inputs=list[Draft]. Construct raises ConstructError.

## Fix direction

Add Loop rule to effective_producer_type: if item has Loop modifier, return list[output_type]. Also add a should_pass fixture for this case.

## Note

This may be intentional — the docs say downstream consumers see 'the final value (unwrapped)'. If consuming the full iteration history is not a supported pattern, this should be documented rather than fixed.
close_reason: Won't fix: effective_producer_type correctly returns T (unwrapped). Consumers see the latest value, not the append-list. Use Loop(history=True) + neo_loop_history_* for full iteration history.

title: ARCH: consolidate type-display renderers — promote public type_display_name; _execute._type_name + _validation_types._fmt_type delegate
description:
Found by neograph-wpzg codebase disease scan (layering + consistency lenses). THREE drifting variants of 'render a TypeSpec to a display string': _execute.py:24 _type_name (dict-aware, runtime layer, private), _validation_types.py:206 _fmt_type (IR layer, private, repr fallback), testing.py:39-43 (inline, NOT dict-aware). The dict-aware one is module-private in the runtime layer, so the CLI codegen module and IR validator cannot reach it cleanly — duplication justified by privacy.

Fix: promote one public type_display_name(t: TypeSpecStatic)->str (dict-aware, _execute variant is the template) into describe_type.py (existing public type-rendering home) or naming.py; have _type_name and _fmt_type delegate. CAUTION: _fmt_type feeds ConstructError messages — verify no test asserts on changed wording, or preserve exact format.

NOTE: the testing.py site itself is fixed in neograph-wpzg (uses normalize_outputs(...).primary + the safe type|None name pattern). This ticket covers the cross-file 3-way consolidation only. Out of scope for neograph-wpzg.
design:
## Core Invariant
Rendering a TypeSpec to a display string has exactly one implementation (describe_type.type_display_name); all other sites delegate.

## Implementation Plan
1. describe_type.py: add public type_display_name(t: TypeSpecStatic) -> str (dict-aware _execute template; None->'None'; dict-instance->'{k: vname,...}'; else getattr(t,'__name__',str(t))). TYPE_CHECKING import of TypeSpecStatic (runtime leaf preserved). Re-export from neograph __init__.
2. _execute.py: _type_name(t) = None if t is None else type_display_name(t); import it.
3. _validation_types.py: _fmt_type(tp) = type_display_name(tp); import it.
4. decorators.py:486-487: out_name/ret_name = type_display_name(outputs)/type_display_name(ret_hint); import it.
5. _construct_validation.py:147,149: inline -> type_display_name(input_type) in the DeprecationWarning f-string.
6. Keep _type_name + _fmt_type defs (structural guards + signature contracts).
7. Structural guard (test_guards_helper_monopoly): type_display_name defined once in describe_type.py; the dict-render idiom and the getattr-__name__-str idiom do not recur outside describe_type (modulo delegators). Positive+negative meta-tests.
8. Unit test type_display_name (None/dict/class/generic-alias).
9. make quality; watch ConstructError + DeprecationWarning tests.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-97c6.42)
THREE type-display variants:
- _execute._type_name(t)->str|None: None->None; dict->'{k: vname, ...}'; else getattr(t,'__name__',str(t)). DICT-AWARE. (template per ticket)
- _validation_types._fmt_type(tp)->str: None->'None'; __name__; else repr(tp). NOT dict-aware; repr fallback. Feeds ConstructError messages (35+ call sites in _construct_validation/_validation_inputs/_validation_modifiers).
- testing.py:39-43: already fixed in wpzg (out of scope here).

Equivalence analysis (str vs repr fallback): for generic aliases / UnionType / typing.Optional, str(x)==repr(x) in CPython, AND most have/resolve __name__ first. The ONLY wording divergence is a real dict INSTANCE (dict-form Node.outputs) reaching _fmt_type: current repr('{...}') vs rendered '{k: v}'. Grep: NO test asserts a dict-repr in error messages; asserted wording is single-type (e.g. test_validation.py:69 'declares inputs=Claims') -> identical under type_display_name (via __name__). So consolidation preserves all asserted wording; only the untested dict-form case improves.

Home: describe_type.py (public type-rendering home; currently a ZERO-neograph-import leaf). node.py does NOT import describe_type -> safe. Will use TYPE_CHECKING import of TypeSpecStatic to keep describe_type a runtime leaf and satisfy the no-Any-in-public-API guard (annotation text = TypeSpecStatic, not Any).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/describe_type.py (home for public type_display_name; re-export from neograph __init__)
- src/neograph/_execute.py:24 (_type_name -> delegate)
- src/neograph/_validation_types.py:238 (_fmt_type -> delegate)
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py:847/1525 (structural guards expecting _type_name/_fmt_type defs to remain in their files)

## Risks & Edge Cases
- _type_name returns str|None (callers pass to structlog input_type=); keep that signature: _type_name = None if t is None else type_display_name(t).
- _fmt_type returns str with None->'None'; type_display_name must return 'None' for None to preserve it.
- Guards at test_guards_assembly expect 'def _type_name' in _execute.py and 'def _fmt_type' present -> keep both as thin delegators (do NOT delete).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-97c6.43)
Pattern: render a TypeSpec to a short display string (getattr(t,'__name__',str(t)) / repr fallback / dict '{k: v}'), hand-rolled across modules instead of one helper.
Disease shape: SEMANTIC, grep-decomposable (getattr __name__ idiom + hasattr __name__ inline). Single-executor scan.
Scan commands:
  grep -rn "getattr(.*'__name__'" src/neograph/*.py
  grep -rn '__name__ if hasattr\|hasattr(.*__name__)' src/neograph/*.py

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _execute.py:24 _type_name | dict-aware helper (str\|None) | MIGRATE(home->delegate) | thin wrapper: None if t is None else type_display_name(t) |
| 2 | _validation_types.py:238 _fmt_type | repr-fallback helper (str) | MIGRATE(home->delegate) | _fmt_type = type_display_name; single-type wording identical; dict-form improves (untested) |
| 3 | decorators.py:486-487 | getattr(outputs/ret_hint,'__name__',str(.)) | MIGRATE (UNCITED - scan caught) | single-type (dict excluded by guard at :478); -> type_display_name(...). Tests match message text not type field |
| 4 | _construct_validation.py:147,149 | input_type.__name__ if hasattr else input_type (DeprecationWarning f-string) | MIGRATE (UNCITED - scan caught) | single-type (dict excluded at :142); -> type_display_name(input_type); f-string str() makes fallback identical |
| 5 | testing.py:39-43 | inline non-dict-aware | ALLOWLIST | already fixed in neograph-wpzg (uses normalize_outputs(...).primary + safe name); not re-inlined |
| 6 | describe_type.py describe_type/describe_value | full TS-notation schema render | ALLOWLIST | different artifact (full schema, not short display name) |

No DEFER. SCOPE EXPANSION: +decorators.py +_construct_validation.py DeprecationWarning. SEMANTIC-but-grep-complete => no artifact dir.
Wording safety: tests asserting these messages (test_basics/test_edge_cases 'outputs=.*differs from return annotation'; test_validation 'declares inputs=Claims') match message text / single-type names -> unchanged under type_display_name.
## Architect Review (neograph-97c6.44)
- [LOW] Invariant: type_display_name is the sole renderer; _type_name/_fmt_type become 1-line delegators; decorators + DeprecationWarning sites call it. Holds.
- [LOW] Cycle-safe: describe_type.py has 0 runtime neograph imports (pure leaf). All 4 consumers (_execute, _validation_types, decorators, _construct_validation) importing from it form no cycle. _validation_types already imports external 'node'; describe_type is another external leaf, consistent with its docstring (intra-CLUSTER deps forbidden; external allowed). TYPE_CHECKING import of TypeSpecStatic keeps describe_type runtime-leaf and satisfies the no-Any public-API guard.
- [LOW] __init__ already re-exports describe_type/describe_value -> adding type_display_name is consistent (public type-rendering surface).
- [LOW] Wording: single-type contexts only at all migrated sites (dicts excluded by guards at decorators:478 / validation:142, or rendered identically). Tests match message text / single-type names -> unchanged. Dict-form _fmt_type case (untested) improves repr->render.
- [LOW] Signature contracts preserved: _type_name stays str|None (structlog callers); _fmt_type stays str (None->'None'). Guards at test_guards_assembly expect both defs present -> kept as delegators.

Overall: ALL_LOW
