title: Batch model_copy calls in _cleanup_inputs_and_register
description:
## Problem
_construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register can call model_copy up to 3 times per node (line 556: filtered inputs, line 570: scripted_fn, line 580: oracle_gen_type). For a 20-node pipeline that's 60+ Pydantic model copies with validation + deep copy of PrivateAttrs.

## Fix
Accumulate all updates into a single dict, then call model_copy once per node. The three loops already iterate list(decorated) independently — merge them or accumulate updates across all three.

## Source
Expert architectural review concern #5 (Medium). Verified: 3 model_copy calls at lines 556, 570, 580.

title: Test the fan_out_param two-site design + strengthen normalize_ir behavioral tests
description:
From code review of 185c322 (synthesis.md TQ-02 + DRY-02 + TQ-04). The refactor deliberately KEEPS two derivations of fan_out_param: the @node signature-based write (_construct_builder.py:568) and the inputs-dict heuristic normalizer (_ir_normalize.py:83-93). This two-site design is the most-debated decision in the change and its justification is currently UNTESTED.

## TQ-02 + DRY-02: prove the two-site design is necessary (one test)
The justification: the @node signature can resolve a fan-out receiver even when MULTIPLE input keys are unknown, whereas _FanOutParamNormalizer declines (len(unknown)==1). Today nothing pins this — test_normalize_ir_idempotent_on_fan_out_param uses a single-unknown node where both paths agree, so the builder write at :568 could be DELETED and every test would still pass while multi-param @node Each nodes silently lose fan-out resolution.
Add a test: a @node Each whose function has TWO non-decorated/non-DI/non-port params (so _detect_fan_out_params picks one but the normalizer sees two unknowns). Assert (a) the assembled fan_out_param IS set (builder wins), and (b) clearing it then calling normalize_ir leaves it None (normalizer correctly declines). This documents WHY :568 is kept and would catch a future deletion. Also (DRY-02) assert cross-surface AGREEMENT: where both signature and inputs-dict derivations fire (single-unknown), they pick the same key.

## TQ-04: strengthen the idempotency test
test_normalize_ir_idempotent_on_fan_out_param short-circuits in applies_to before reaching apply, so it verifies 'no-op when already set', not inference idempotency — it would pass even if apply were broken. Strengthen: clear the field, call normalize_ir TWICE, assert the value after pass 1 == after pass 2 (and equals the re-derived value). This exercises the real apply -> applies_to=False idempotency loop.

## Note (no action, just context)
The broader oracle_gen_type/fan_out_param cross-surface parity IS covered by pre-existing tests in tests/hypothesis/test_regression.py (programmatic + YAML load_spec) and test_composition.py (@node) — verified passing. This ticket is about the NEW two-site divergence + idempotency, not re-proving parity.

## Acceptance
- New divergence test fails if _construct_builder.py:568 is deleted.
- Idempotency test reaches apply on the second pass.
- All in tests/test_ir_normalize.py; make quality green.
notes:
## Prep — empirical investigation (CORRECTS the TQ-02 premise)
Probed @node Each fan_out_param derivation directly:
- Single-fan-out @node Each: builder sets fan_out_param='item'; the normalizer ALONE (clear + _FanOutParamNormalizer.apply) reproduces {'fan_out_param':'item'} identically.
- 2-unknown @node Each (def summ(prod, item, extra), map_over=prod): REJECTED by _check_fan_in_inputs ('inputs[extra] has no upstream'). NOT a constructible passing pipeline.

CONCLUSION: TQ-02's premise — 'builder resolves a multi-unknown @node Each that the normalizer declines' — describes an INVALID construct. For every VALID @node Each, normalize_ir reproduces the builder's fan_out_param (normalizer is idempotent + equivalent). So _construct_builder.py:568 is REDUNDANT-but-consistent (belt-and-suspenders), not strictly necessary. The original 'richer / handles 2+' justification does not hold for valid constructs because the 2+ case is validator-rejected regardless.

Therefore I will NOT write a test asserting 'deleting :568 breaks something' — that would encode a false premise. The honest, valuable tests:
1. AGREEMENT (the real DRY-02 gap): for a @node Each, the builder-set fan_out_param EQUALS the normalizer's independent re-derivation. Pins that the two derivations converge.
2. TQ-04: strengthen idempotency — clear -> normalize -> normalize, assert stable AND equals the re-derived value (exercises apply, not just the applies_to short-circuit).
3. EXECUTE-atom experiment: temporarily remove :568, run the @node fan-out suite, confirm green (proves redundancy), restore. Document result.

title: to_agent_spec: Each-modified node's non-fan-out context inputs don't route to MapNode's iterated_-prefixed inner properties
description:
Discovered while fixing neograph-qtfof.1 (dict-form Each fan-out receiver export bug).

When an Each-modified node has BOTH a fan-out receiver key AND a non-fan-out upstream context key in its dict-form inputs (e.g. inputs={'source': RawText, 'cluster': ClusterGroup} with fan_out_param='cluster'), to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop emits a DataFlowEdge targeting the MapNode with destination_input='source.text' -- but pyagentspec's MapNode infers its own input Properties from the inner sub-flow's StartNode, each PREFIXED with 'iterated_' (e.g. 'iterated_source.text'), per MapNode's own docstring. So any Each-modified node with additional context inputs beyond the fan-out item fails export with a pydantic ValidationError: 'DataFlowEdge ... does not have any property with that name'.

Repro (raises pydantic.ValidationError, not caught by qtfof.1's fix which only handles the fan-out-receiver-only case):

    @node(outputs=RawText)
    def source() -> RawText: ...

    @node(outputs=Clusters)
    def clusters() -> Clusters: ...

    @node(outputs=MatchResult, map_over='clusters.groups', map_key='label')
    def verify(source: RawText, cluster: ClusterGroup) -> MatchResult: ...

    pipeline = construct_from_functions('mixed', [source, clusters, verify])
    to_agent_spec(pipeline)  # raises pydantic ValidationError

FIX: to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop (and/or _lower_each) needs to route non-fan-out context-key DataFlowEdges with destination_input prefixed 'iterated_' when the destination is a MapNode (Each-modified), instead of the bare dict-form-prefixed title used for non-Each destinations.
notes: FIXED by neograph-sdfgz consolidated family-A pass. Repro (Each map_over + non-fan-out context input) now exports AND round-trips; pinned by tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py cell each-context. _lower_each declares StartNode inputs so MapNode infers iterated_ inputs; to_agent_spec routes context-input edges to iterated_{title} via input_targets.

title: FromResource DI marker: declarative MCP resource wiring — Annotated[Model, FromResource(uri)] fetches + validates at node entry (async DI twin)
description:
Consumer-requested (2026-07-06, maintainer confirms a real consumer wants declarative resource wiring). MCP resources are untyped at the protocol level (mime + bytes Blobs via langchain-mcp-adapters MultiServerMCPClient.get_resources, adapter 0.3.0, async-only, stateless-session model) — the typed-channel paradigm supplies the missing half: the node boundary is where blob becomes contract.

THE FEATURE: a new DI marker joining the FromInput/FromConfig family — parameter annotated Annotated[ContractDoc, FromResource('mcp://server/uri')] is fetched at node entry per execution, parsed, validated into the declared model, and injected. Downstream nodes consume a validated model; fan-in validation sees the declared type at assembly time.

PURITY-TEST JUSTIFICATION (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md): a resource READ is side-effect-free I/O, safe to replay on resume — legal inside node-entry resolution (unlike mutating calls). Fetch-per-execution also gives resume-in-fresh-process re-fetch for free (same property as tool factories / token provider — no caching, no invalidation machinery).

HARD CONSTRAINTS (all carry prior-decision weight):
1. NO SESSION OWNERSHIP (nmb2 verdict, docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md + the structural guard): the client/connections are CONSUMER-OWNED, supplied via config['configurable'] (a client instance or an async resource-fetcher callable), exactly like tool factories. neograph never creates/holds/disposes MCP sessions.
2. THE DI RESOLVER IS SYNC TODAY (_resolve_di_value in decorators/di layer): FromResource needs an ASYNC resolution twin — the same H2 gap-shape as tool factories (neograph-w74k.3.1), solved the same way: async DI path on arun(), FAIL LOUD with ConfigurationError on run() (khff pattern). Do NOT introspect-and-branch inside one path; the driver selects.
3. Three-surface parity + 6-cell coverage (IR-level change).

DESIGN DECISIONS for the research/architect atoms:
- URI shape: static string first; templated URIs (per-run interpolation from FromInput values, e.g. mcp://server/tickets/{ticket_id}) as an explicit scope decision — likely v2.
- Parse strategy by mime: application/json -> model_validate_json (v1 scope); text/* -> require an explicit parser callable in the marker or defer to a think-node recipe (schema-aligned LLM parse is the documented pattern for unstructured content — do NOT silently LLM-parse inside DI resolution, that is hidden cognition + cost).
- Error path: missing resource / fetch failure / validation failure -> typed error at node entry naming the param, uri, and node (fail-loud house style); decide retry semantics (probably none in v1 — the consumer wraps with Loop/skip_when if needed).
- Lint: FromResource param + run()-driven graph -> reuse/extend tool_requires_async_driver-style check; lint knows the marker so template/DI key prediction stays coherent (interacts with neograph-euyh's di_inputs work — coordinate key naming).
- Where resolution lives: the DI classifier (_classify_di_params) gains a binding kind; the shim resolution gains the async twin. Keep ONE resolver/classifier for @node and @merge_fn (existing monopoly rule).

INTERIM (document in the ticket + docs until this lands): the three working patterns today — fetch-ahead into run(input=), async scripted node body fetching + returning its declared type (purity-legal), resource-as-tool for agent-driven pulls.

SEQUENCING: NOT wired into the 0.6.0 gate (y5ux) — it is a new feature, not a known fix; maintainer decides whether it gates the release or lands in 0.6.x. Depends conceptually on nothing open; can run as its own molecule post-wave-3.
notes:
2026-07-06 DEEP-RESEARCH FINDINGS (docs/design/mcp-resources-patterns-2026-07-06.md — 19 claims survived 3-vote adversarial verification, 6 refuted). THE HEADLINE: the field has NO named pattern for reference-in-state + hydrate-later-across-pause (the one focused publication, Frees arXiv 2510.05968, states these patterns remain undocumented; the protocol community itself routed deferred results through task tokens with negotiated TTLs — SEP-1686 — after explicitly REJECTING a resource-based approach). Independent precedents converge on our design regardless: Google ADK mandates references-in-state + artifact store + deliberately-ephemeral always-re-fetch hydration; LangGraph designates checkpointed thread-scoped state (not Store) as the HITL-survival tier. neograph would be NAMING this pattern, not adopting one.

PROTOCOL FACTS THAT SHAPE v2 SCOPE: (1) resource_link is a first-class tool-result content type explicitly designed for deferred client fetch (MAY, not SHOULD — servers are permitted, not encouraged). (2) Tool-emitted links are NOT guaranteed to appear in resources/list — a later step CANNOT validate a link by enumeration; the only check is resources/read + handle error -32002. (3) The spec is SILENT on URI stability/TTL/expiry (only lastModified annotation exists); cross-checkpoint durability is 100 percent server-defined. NOTE: the 2026-07-28 protocol RC adds ttlMs/cacheScope to list/read results — the protocol is catching up to exactly this gap; design v2 so ttlMs slots in when servers ship it.

RESEARCH-BACKED v2 DESIGN (extends the v1 FromResource marker): (a) typed ResourceRef manifest in a CHECKPOINTED state channel — and each ref SHOULD CARRY THE PRODUCING TOOL CALL (tool name + args) so an expired link is re-derivable; (b) hydration default = app-curated DI-injected fetch (FromResource/manifest-driven), read_resource-as-tool as opt-in for model-controlled pulls; (c) re-fetch on every hydration (replay-safe read, matches ADK's deliberate ephemerality) with OPTIONAL under-size-threshold caching into state; (d) LAYERED EXPIRY HANDLING on hydration failure: try resources/read -> on -32002 replay the producing tool call from the ref -> fail loud with a typed error naming ref+node. Cite the report in the design atom.
2026-07-06 DESIGN REFINED AND RE-CUT (docs/design/hgpt-refined-design-2026-07-06.md — comparative mechanics vs ADK/OpenAI/Claude-SDK/LlamaIndex + code-grounded design). This ticket is now the UMBRELLA; execution happens in the children: neograph-2dtk (v1a resource_reader + read_blob), neograph-vx9a (v1b FromResource + async DI twin), neograph-4atf (v2a ResourceRef manifest + resource_link lift), neograph-a5nh (v2b hydration + layered expiry + templated URIs, gated on neograph-lhc6 tool-idempotency annotation). v1 = 2dtk+vx9a, shippable together, rides ENTIRELY on existing machinery (async-only StructuredTool -> existing lint/budget/typed_result paths; async DI twin -> the same ScriptedDispatch driver-select shape as w74k.3.1). PATTERN NAME for docs: Typed Resource Manifest with Ephemeral Hydration — the ref is typed and self-healing (typed kind+reader model vs the field's stringly file_id; producing_call travels with the ref, the only re-derivation a lifetime-free resource_link allows). STEAL from the field: ADK's ArtifactService/SessionService durability split + LoadArtifactsTool per-call ephemerality; LlamaIndex's hash-keyed re-derivation direction. SKIP: framework-owned artifact stores (no-session-ownership), integer auto-versions, idle-expiry containers. Top risks + mitigations recorded in the doc (replay idempotency gate; max_bytes fail-loud before prompt; lint on unproduced kinds).
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all four children closed (2dtk resource_reader, vx9a FromResource sync+async DI, 4atf ResourceRef manifest, a5nh hydration+layered expiry+templated URIs) and the documentation obligation delivered by neograph-06qv (verified: every documented surface matches src signatures exactly). The Typed Resource Manifest with Ephemeral Hydration pattern is shipped end to end per docs/design/hgpt-refined-design-2026-07-06.md.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-mrb2y
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-mrb2y` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-mrb2y/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-mrb2y
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |

   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>

   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-do0d9 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard

- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-aa5gq
description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-aa5gq/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-aa5gq
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-aa5gq)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-aa5gq --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-aa5gq --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-aa5gq/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-aa5gq codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-aa5gq
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-aa5gq
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-aa5gq`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-aa5gq)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-aa5gq --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-aa5gq sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: _run_cache hardening: per-key single-flight + run-end eviction + the two concurrency pins (review PAT-03)
description: From the 2026-07-07 pre-release review (PAT-03; python-practices PP-01 re-scoped + PP-02 verified at source). _run_cache is sound for today's two consumers but unhardened as a shared primitive: (1) NO PER-KEY SINGLE-FLIGHT — get_or_build/aget_or_build lock only the map; two concurrent misses on one key (fan-over-agent branches under arun) both build: double LLM-handle build (waste) / double resource fetch (cost; correctness edge for non-idempotent fetchers). Fix: per-key in-flight latch minted under the map lock — sync threading.Lock-per-key, async asyncio.Lock-per-key (loop-affine: key the async latch map per loop or store latches in the same (run_id, subkey) namespace; do NOT share an asyncio.Lock across loops). (2) NO RUN-END EVICTION — bounded LRU only, so loop-bound MCP/LLM handles linger past their run until LRU pressure. Fix: evict the run's keys in the runner verbs' finally (the same finalize seam observe= flush uses — one hook, all four verbs; _prepare knows the run_id it minted). (3) The two Wave-8 unpinned properties land HERE as tests (moved from yc38): parallel-arun cross-run isolation (two concurrent aruns sharing a caller config -> factory call count == 2, no cross-contamination; GatedAsyncFake parking) and expiry-vs-cache (replay -> fresh run_id -> cache miss -> refetch, pinned with a two-run test; document no-mid-run-expiry-recheck by design). Twin-thinness applies to the single-flight twins.
close_reason: _run_cache hardening: per-key single-flight (sync threading.Lock / loop-affine asyncio.Lock minted under the map lock), evict_run() wired into all four runner verbs' finally, latch/eviction/loop-affinity + two Wave-8 arun pins added. Public get_or_build/aget_or_build signatures unchanged.

title: §5: Audit NeographError discipline — public functions raise typed errors, not bare exceptions
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5 (Type and error discipline).

**Problem**: the codebase has a typed error model with a builder (`errors.py:NeographError.build`) and an AST structural guard (`test_structural_guards.py:31`, `TestErrorBuilderEnforcement`) preventing bare `raise` bypass. But coverage of public-function failure modes hasn't been audited end-to-end; some public functions may still raise `ValueError` / `TypeError` / `RuntimeError` directly.

**Fix**: walk every public function in `src/neograph/` (anything re-exported from `__init__.py` plus `Node.run_isolated`, `compile`, `run`, `lint`). For each raise statement reachable from a public entry:
- If it raises `NeographError` (via `.build()`): ✓
- If it raises a bare `ValueError` / `TypeError` / `RuntimeError`: convert to `NeographError` with the right subclass and message
- If a public function returns silent `None` for a required value: convert to `NeographError` per §7 / §9

**Acceptance**: a grep for bare `raise ValueError|TypeError|RuntimeError` inside public-function call graphs returns zero hits. The structural guard catches future regressions.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestPublicFunctionsRaiseNeographError` (new test class)
**Test type**: structural-guard, mutation-verified
**What it exercises**: AST-walk every public name re-exported from `src/neograph/__init__.py` plus `Node.run_isolated`, `compile`, `run`, `lint`; for each raise reachable from a public entry, assert the raised type is `NeographError` (or a subclass). Allowlist for narrowly-justified third-party raises (e.g., `TypeError` from Pydantic re-raise) is explicit. Mutation case: temp file with a public function raising bare `ValueError`, scanner detects, file removed.
**Expected initial state**: failing — bare `ValueError`/`TypeError`/`RuntimeError` raises currently exist somewhere in the public call graph.
**Persistence**: stays in suite as a permanent discipline guard.

Order: write the failing AST guard FIRST → run it → must fail listing every offender → convert each to `NeographError` via the builder → run again → must pass.
close_reason: Added TestPublicFunctionsRaiseNeographError structural guard. AST-walks all raise statements in src/neograph/*.py, requires each to use a NeographError subclass (or be a bare re-raise, or be in NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST with a documented stdlib-contract reason). Converted 2 sites (configure_image, load_spec size guard) to ConfigurationError; allowlisted 25 legitimate stdlib raises (Pydantic validator boundaries, grammar parser contracts, Python attribute/iterator/bool protocols, abstract-method NotImplementedError). Updated 4 tests to assert ConfigurationError. 1737 tests passing, ruff+mypy clean.

title: Prompt compilation: exported fail-loud primitives + DefaultPromptCompiler (GH issue 5, layers 1-2)
description:
From GitHub issue 5 (consumer evidence: piarch and agent-stark both hand-roll the prompt_compiler seam and DIVERGED on the safety property — piarch fail-loud RuntimeError on unfilled placeholder, agent-stark silent .replace() which shipped the literal string {domain} to a production LLM, caught only by live e2e). The framework currently leaves 'unfilled var -> crash vs silent' to each app to get wrong. This is quintessential Layer-2 node-internal DX per docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md — exactly where neograph value belongs.

SCOPE — Layer 1, exported primitives (composable): (a) render_inputs(input_data) -> dict[str,str] exposing the BAML input-to-var rendering already done internally (renderers.py build_rendered_input — expose, do not duplicate); (b) substitute(template, vars, *, strict=True, syntax='brace'|'dollar'|Callable) -> str — ONE substitution primitive; strict raises typed PromptVarMissing(var, available=[...]); must be BRACE-SAFE so an injected JSON schema's {} does not break substitution (the exact reason agent-stark fell back to .replace); (c) inject_schema(vars, output_model|output_schema, key='json_schema') riding describe_type. Layer 2: DefaultPromptCompiler(loader, *, strict=True, syntax='brace', system=None, schema_var='json_schema') so the 90-percent case is compile(construct, prompt_compiler=DefaultPromptCompiler(Path('prompts'))); override hooks load_template/build_vars/render_messages — override one method, keep the rest.

PRINCIPLES (from the issue, all match house style): fail-loud by default (strict=True — the {domain}-reaches-the-model class becomes impossible without explicit opt-out); composable not monolithic (a custom compiler is ~10 lines of primitive composition); engine-agnostic syntax (brace/dollar/pluggable). ANTI-DUPLICATION: the primitives must be THE internals, re-exported/extracted — not a parallel second rendering path (one substitution rule; _llm_render inline-prompt handling and the new substitute must share the placeholder-parsing core or a guard explains why not).

ACCEPTANCE: from neograph import DefaultPromptCompiler, substitute, render_inputs (names finalizable); DefaultPromptCompiler + a prompts/ dir renders with zero app compiler code; unfilled placeholder raises PromptVarMissing under strict; existing custom prompt_compiler consumers unaffected (opt-in, zero behavior change without it). Companion tickets: di_inputs-to-compiler (layer 3) and public test doubles are filed SEPARATELY — do not fold in. Reply-to-GH cross-link once maintainer approves commenting.
design:
## Core Invariant
There is ONE substitution rule and ONE input-rendering path in neograph: the exported prompt primitives must be the existing internals (renderers.build_rendered_input, the _llm_render placeholder scanner, describe_type) re-exported/extracted — never a second parallel rendering path — and they compose behind the unchanged compile(construct, prompt_compiler=...) seam so consumers with their own compiler see zero behavior change.

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW public module src/neograph/prompt.py (Layer-2 node-runtime helper, sibling to renderers.py/describe_type.py). Holds the four primitives + DefaultPromptCompiler. Keep it engine-free (no langgraph imports).
2. EXTRACT the placeholder scanner (currently _VAR_RE at _llm_render.py:29 + the single-pass re.sub body of _substitute_vars:110) into a shared location both prompt.py and _llm_render.py import. Add the brace regex r'\{([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)\}' alongside the existing dollar _VAR_RE. Refactor _llm_render._substitute_vars to call the shared single-pass apply with its own resolver (fail-soft, dotted+BAML) — proving one scanner, two policies. Do NOT change inline fail-soft behavior.
3. substitute(template, vars, *, strict=True, syntax='brace'|'dollar'|Callable) -> str: single-pass over the chosen scanner; per-match resolver looks up vars; on miss raise PromptVarMissing(var, available=sorted(vars)) when strict else leave token verbatim. Brace-safe by construction (single pass, token-only pattern).
4. render_inputs(input_data, *, renderer=None) -> dict[str,str]: thin wrapper over renderers.build_rendered_input(...).for_template_ref. Reuse, do not reimplement.
5. inject_schema(vars, output_model=None, *, output_schema=None, key='json_schema') -> dict: sets vars[key] = output_schema or describe_type(output_model). Ride describe_type; accept the precomputed output_schema string the seam already threads.
6. PromptVarMissing in errors.py subclassing ExecutionError (runtime substitution failure); structured attrs var:str, available:list[str]; message via NeographError.build with hint listing available keys.
7. DefaultPromptCompiler(loader, *, strict=True, syntax='brace', system=None, schema_var='json_schema') — callable satisfying the PromptCompiler Protocol (_llm_protocols.py:33). __call__(template, input_data, *, output_model=None, output_schema=None, **kw): (a) load_template(template) via loader (Path -> read {name}.md, or a callable), (b) build_vars(input_data) via render_inputs [+ inject_schema when output_model/output_schema present], (c) render_messages(template_text, vars) via substitute -> [{'role':'system',...}?, {'role':'user','content':...}]. Each of load_template/build_vars/render_messages is an override hook — override one, keep the rest (~10-line custom compiler).
8. Export from __init__.py __all__: DefaultPromptCompiler, substitute, render_inputs, inject_schema, PromptVarMissing (coordinate with yc38 which also edits __all__).
9. TESTS (three-surface not required — this is Layer-2, exempt; but cover): unit for substitute brace-safety (injected schema with literal {} renders intact), strict PromptVarMissing(var, available), dollar+brace+Callable syntaxes; render_inputs returns BAML-rendered dict matching build_rendered_input; inject_schema uses describe_type; end-to-end compile(construct, prompt_compiler=DefaultPromptCompiler(Path('prompts'))) renders with zero app compiler code; an existing custom prompt_compiler still works unchanged (opt-in proof). Add a should_pass check_fixtures entry for the DefaultPromptCompiler happy path.
10. GUARD: structural test asserting the placeholder regex(es) are defined once (shared) and that prompt.py has no langgraph import; if the scanner is only partly shared, a guard-comment must state why (resolution-fusion in _llm_render is intentionally not shared).
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher — atom 938w.2)

REUSE TARGETS (the primitives must BE these internals, re-exported/extracted — not a parallel path):
- render_inputs(input_data) -> dict[str,str]: WRAP renderers.build_rendered_input (renderers.py:278). The BAML input->var rendering already exists there; RenderedInput.for_template_ref (renderers.py:55) is exactly the merged rendered+flattened dict a template-ref compiler consumes. render_inputs = thin wrapper returning that dict view. DO NOT reimplement _render_single/_render_with_flattening.
- substitute(template, vars, *, strict, syntax): share the placeholder-parsing core with _llm_render.py. The dollar-brace regex _VAR_RE = re.compile(r'\$\{([^}]+)\}') at _llm_render.py:29 is the existing single-pass scanner and IS ALREADY BRACE-SAFE (only matches ${...}, leaves literal {} untouched). _substitute_vars (_llm_render.py:110) is the exemplar: re.sub with a per-match resolver fn = single-pass, never re-scans substituted text (this is THE brace-safety mechanism; str.format is not single-pass over a fixed token set, which is why agent-stark fell back to .replace).
- inject_schema(vars, output_model|output_schema, key='json_schema'): RIDE describe_type (describe_type.py:73). Signature already returns the TS-style schema string; inject_schema just sets vars[key]=describe_type(output_model) (or the precomputed output_schema string). The compiler ALREADY computes output_schema and threads it: render_prompt at _llm_render.py:261-262 does 'if strategy==json_mode: output_schema = describe_type(output_model)'.

CURRENT prompt_compiler SEAM (how it is wired today):
- compile(construct, ..., prompt_compiler=...) at compiler.py:60-116. Kwarg folded into LlmRuntime.build (compiler.py:107) -> frozen LlmRuntime (_llm_runtime.py:46). Callable signature is the PromptCompiler Protocol (_llm_protocols.py:33): __call__(template:str, input_data:Any, *args, **kwargs) -> list. Simple shape (template, input_data)->list; advanced accepts kwargs.
- Invocation site: _llm_render.py:_compile_prompt (line 151), branch at :200-213. It builds all_kwargs = {node_name, config, output_model, llm_config, output_schema, (context)} then FILTERS by runtime.prompt_compiler_params (introspected once at build via _accepted_params, _llm_runtime.py:29) — so a compiler that declares output_model=/output_schema= in its signature receives them; one that only takes (template, data, **kw) gets everything. This means DefaultPromptCompiler can pull output_model/output_schema straight from the seam — no new plumbing needed for layer 1-2.
- Inline-prompt fast path: _compile_prompt short-circuits BEFORE the prompt_compiler when _is_inline_prompt (space or ${ present, _llm_render.py:33). File-ref templates (e.g. 'rw/decompose') go to the user prompt_compiler. DefaultPromptCompiler is the file-ref handler.

EXISTING hand-rolled exemplar (the thing being productized): examples/_shared.py make_template_prompt_compiler — loads {dir}/{name}.md and string.Template.safe_substitute. Header explicitly says 'NOT public API, every production consumer writes their own' — hjwv makes that unnecessary. Note it uses ${var} (dollar) precisely to avoid crashing on literal {curly} in code samples — same brace-safety motivation.

OPT-IN / zero-behavior-change: DefaultPromptCompiler is just a callable passed as prompt_compiler=. Consumers who pass their own callable are untouched (the seam is unchanged). No default is wired into compile(); absence still raises ConfigurationError (_llm_render.py:200-204).
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/renderers.py:278 build_rendered_input + :55 RenderedInput.for_template_ref — REUSE for render_inputs (the internal BAML input->str rendering; do not duplicate _render_single/_render_with_flattening at :320/:357).
- src/neograph/_llm_render.py:29 _VAR_RE (dollar-brace scanner, brace-safe) + :110 _substitute_vars (single-pass re.sub exemplar) — the placeholder-parsing core substitute() must share.
- src/neograph/_llm_render.py:151 _compile_prompt + :200-213 — the seam call site; shows kwargs (output_model/output_schema/config) already delivered to compilers via param-filtering.
- src/neograph/_llm_runtime.py:29 _accepted_params + :84 prompt_compiler_params — signature introspection that routes output_model=/output_schema= to a declaring compiler.
- src/neograph/describe_type.py:73 describe_type — RIDE for inject_schema.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:60-116 compile() prompt_compiler kwarg -> LlmRuntime.build (the wiring; unchanged by this ticket).
- src/neograph/_llm_protocols.py:33 PromptCompiler Protocol — the callable contract DefaultPromptCompiler must satisfy (structurally, __call__).
- examples/_shared.py:26 make_template_prompt_compiler — the hand-rolled pattern being productized (load .md, safe_substitute); dollar syntax chosen for brace-safety.
- src/neograph/errors.py:24 NeographError.build / :96 ExecutionError — PromptVarMissing subclasses here.
- src/neograph/__init__.py:78 __all__ — where the new public names register.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- BRACE-SAFETY (the load-bearing test): for syntax='brace', use a single-pass regex like r'\{([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)\}' with a per-match resolver — NEVER str.format. Empty {} and JSON-schema fragments ({ "foo": ... } with space/quote after brace) must not match the token pattern, and single-pass re.sub never re-scans the injected schema value. Write a should_pass-style test: template with {json_schema} where the injected schema contains literal {} — must render intact. This is the exact agent-stark regression.
- STRICTNESS ASYMMETRY: existing inline ${var} handling is fail-SOFT (log.warning at _llm_render.py:62/76, returns ''). New substitute() default is strict=True (raise PromptVarMissing). Do NOT flip the inline path to strict — that changes documented behavior (would break existing inline-prompt tests/examples). Reuse the parsing core, not the strictness policy. A structural guard can pin 'both use the shared regex' and explain the policy split.
- SHARE-CORE vs SEMANTIC GAP: inline path FUSES resolution (dotted attr access + BAML describe_value via _resolve_var, _llm_render.py:43) with substitution; substitute() takes a pre-built vars: dict[str,str]. The shareable unit is the token SCANNER (the two compiled regexes + single-pass apply), not _resolve_var. _FETCHER_HINT = (
    "provide config['configurable']['{key}'] = "
    "an async 'fetch(uri) -> (content, mime)' callable"
)  # .format(key=RESOURCE_FETCHER_KEY) at the raise site

def _require_fetcher(config, *, subject: str, required: bool = True) -> Callable | None:
    """Read the consumer-owned resource fetcher from config; fail loud when
    absent (unless required=False -> returns None). subject names the consumer."""
    fetcher = _get_configurable(config, RESOURCE_FETCHER_KEY)

        raise _ConfigurationError.build(subject, hint=_FETCHER_HINT.format(key=RESOURCE_FETCHER_KEY))
    return fetcher

title: §4: Function-local-import structural guard + initial documented allowlist
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4 (Module and function responsibilities).

**Problem**: today's structural guard at `tests/test_structural_guards.py:953` enforces a numeric budget (currently ≤45 function-local `from neograph...` imports) without naming which ones are accepted. The spec rule: forbid in new code, paid-down allowlist for existing cycles, target zero, no new entries.

**Fix**: rewrite the structural guard to be an allowlist, not a budget:
1. Enumerate the current function-local `from neograph...` imports in `src/neograph/` (file + line)
2. Build an allowlist data structure in the test (or in a sibling config file) listing every accepted entry with a comment naming the cycle it breaks
3. The guard test fails if any function-local `from neograph...` import exists in `src/neograph/` that is NOT in the allowlist
4. Each cycle-break-up ticket in this epic removes its imports from the allowlist as it lands

**Initial seed**: the current 49 or so entries are the starting allowlist. The target is zero; the allowlist shrinks as cycles are broken (other tasks in this epic).

**Acceptance**: the guard is allowlist-based, not budget-based. Adding a new function-local `from neograph...` import fails CI unless the allowlist is updated AND the new entry has a justification comment.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestFunctionLocalImportAllowlist` (replaces the existing budget guard at line 953)
**Test type**: structural-guard, mutation-verified
**What it exercises**: AST-walk `src/neograph/**/*.py`; collect every `(file, lineno, imported_module)` tuple for function-local `from neograph...` imports; assert each tuple is present in an explicit `ALLOWED = {(file, module), ...}` set defined inside the test (or in a sibling YAML/TOML). Each allowlist entry has a justification comment. Mutation case: parametrized fixture writes a temp module with a function-local `from neograph._llm import X` that is NOT in the allowlist, scanner detects, file removed.
**Expected initial state**: failing if any new unlisted import sneaks in; passes today as a seed snapshot of ~49 entries. The old budget guard is removed in the same change.
**Persistence**: stays in suite permanently. Shrinks as cycle-break tickets land.

Order: write the allowlist-based guard FIRST seeded with current entries → run it → must pass against today's snapshot → other tickets in this epic shrink the allowlist over time.
close_reason: Replaced numeric budget guard at tests/test_structural_guards.py:947-968 with TestFunctionLocalImportAllowlist (3 tests: main scan, mutation-detect, module-level/TYPE_CHECKING ignore). Seeded FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST with 30 entries keyed on (file, module, frozenset_of_names) — each entry has a justification comment naming the cycle and the ticket that will retire it. Goal: shrink to zero. Full guard suite (67 tests) and full test suite (1780 tests) green.

title: Use json_repair for lenient LLM JSON parsing in _parse_json_response
description:
## Problem
_parse_json_response does json.loads → model_validate_json with no error recovery. LLM JSON output frequently has:
- Control characters (\u0000-\u001F) inside strings — from tool results with markdown content
- Truncated field names ('r' instead of 'r_id') 
- Trailing commas, missing quotes, incomplete objects
- Markdown code fences wrapping the JSON (handled by _extract_json, but fragile)

Each of these crashes the pipeline. RetryPolicy doesn't help because DeepSeek caches responses — identical prompt produces identical broken JSON.

## Suggested Fix
Use json_repair library (pip install json_repair) as a preprocessing step:

```python
def _parse_json_response(text, output_model):
    from json_repair import repair_json
    cleaned = _extract_json(text)
    repaired = repair_json(cleaned)  # fix structural JSON issues
    return output_model.model_validate_json(repaired)
```

json_repair handles: control characters, missing quotes, trailing commas, single quotes, incomplete objects, unescaped characters. It's a BNF-based parser that tries stdlib json first and falls back to repair.

For fuzzy field name matching (e.g. 'r' → 'r_id'), consider fuzzy-json-repair which uses RapidFuzz to match LLM field names to Pydantic schema fields.

## References
- json_repair: https://github.com/mangiucugna/json_repair (PyPI: json-repair)
- fuzzy-json-repair: https://medium.com/@msayef/when-llms-get-creative-with-field-names-automatic-json-typo-repair-b5b7b664315f
- Instructor library uses similar approach: https://python.useinstructor.com

## Impact
Would have prevented 3 pipeline crashes in the current session:
1. ClusterOutput parse failure (malformed JSON from R1)
2. ExplorationResult control character crash (markdown content in JSON strings)  
3. DecompositionResult 'r' instead of 'r_id' (truncated field name)
design:
## Root Cause
_parse_json_response calls model_validate_json which uses strict JSON parsing (serde_json). LLM output frequently contains control characters, trailing commas, single quotes, and unescaped newlines that strict parsing rejects.

## Fix Approach
1. Add json-repair as a dependency in pyproject.toml
2. In _parse_json_response, call repair_json() on the extracted text before passing to model_validate_json
3. json_repair tries stdlib json.loads first (fast path), falls back to BNF-based repair only when needed — no perf penalty for well-formed JSON
4. Single-line change in the parse function, zero API surface change
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py::TestParseJsonResponseLenientParsing (4 tests)
- Root cause: _parse_json_response passes raw LLM text through _extract_json (only strips fences) then model_validate_json which uses strict JSON parsing — no tolerance for control chars, trailing commas, single quotes, or unescaped newlines

title: Unify mcp_session/mcp_run_context stdio .call() onto per-call identity re-resolution — kill the last freeze fork
description:
## Invariant
Identity is per-call fresh on EVERY MCP surface and EVERY transport; a consumer PINS identity by returning a constant from token_provider (never by the framework freezing it). One semantic, no transport-dependent surprise.

## The defect (last freeze fork left by neograph-qslrx)
Within the SAME mcp_session.call() surface, identity handling forks by transport (src/neograph_mcp/_session.py):
- http (:220): auth = _http_identity(...) — per-request httpx.Auth (_TokenProviderAuth re-invokes token_provider every request). FRESH.
- stdio (:225/:227 mint at __aenter__ -> :312-316 .call() reads self._token): the bearer/identity is minted ONCE at session open and the frozen self._token is reused as the tool argument on every .call(). FROZEN.

So mcp_session.call() refreshes on http but freezes on stdio. mcp_run_context has the same stdio mint-once. This is the single remaining mint-once site the qslrx completeness audit found (adversarial verifier, 2026-07-11): 'the direct mcp_session/mcp_run_context stdio .call() path (self._token) mints once at __aenter__ and reuses per .call().' qslrx documented it as a scope-out (design items 8/9: 'stdio: unchanged; sessions rarely stdio'); THIS ticket rejects that scope-out.

## Why it is an inconsistency, not a principled second path (verified against code)
- NO technical barrier: self._token_provider AND self._config are already held on the session (_session.py:203/:206), so .call() can re-resolve per call — await _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) — instead of reading self._token. ~2 lines.
- The FACTORY path ALREADY does exactly this for stdio (_inject_stdio_token re-resolves per call). mcp_session is the ONLY stdio surface still minting once — out of step with its own sibling, not with any transport constraint.
- Not perf (token_provider is a cheap consumer callable); not connection semantics (the stdio token is an ARGUMENT, not a connection property — changing it per call is free).
- The design's stated justification ('sessions rarely stdio; per-call arg injection is the factory concern') is a FREQUENCY argument, not a correctness one — the same 'rare therefore harmless' reasoning that kept Loop.history (neograph-eef83) alive. An inconsistency where a surface refreshes on http but freezes on stdio is a latent footgun regardless of frequency: test on http (see refresh), ship on stdio (silent freeze).
- The only real argument for mint-once — 'pin the whole session to one principal' — is already achievable the consistent way: a token_provider returning a constant pins identity (exactly like the http side). The framework must not FORCE pinning by freezing.

## Fix (Option: unify onto per-call, mirrors the qslrx factory path)
mcp_session.call() and mcp_run_context .call() (stdio branch) re-resolve identity per call via _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) (or _resolve_token_no_config when config is None) instead of self._token minted at __aenter__. http stays on _http_identity (already per-request). Result: ONE semantic — identity per-call fresh on all surfaces/transports; constant provider pins.

## Guard-first / TDD (same shape qslrx used)
1. Write the FAILING stdio-session freshness test FIRST: a rotating/counter token_provider over a stdio mcp_session; make >=2 .call()s; assert the SECOND call carries the FRESH token (demo server echoes it under acting_as). RED on current HEAD (self._token frozen). Mirror mcp_run_context if it exposes a direct .call().
2. Implement per-call re-resolution until green.
3. Static-provider regression: a constant token_provider still sends the same value every .call().
4. Consider extending tests/test_guards_mcp_identity_freeze.py (or a sibling) to ban 'mint identity once at __aenter__ then reuse across .call()' if AST-expressible; otherwise the behavioral tests are the pin.

## Scope
- IN: mcp_session + mcp_run_context stdio direct .call() identity re-resolution; freshness + static-regression tests; docs note that identity is per-call on ALL surfaces now (kill the 'except stdio sessions' caveat in _session.py:218-219 / _run_context.py:88-90 docstrings + design doc items 8/9).
- OUT: http path (already per-request via qslrx); the agent-loop factory/stdio path (already per-call).

## Provenance
Follow-up to neograph-qslrx (fix f491db4). Surfaced by the qslrx adversarial verification (the lone documented scope-out) + maintainer challenge 2026-07-11: 'this means there are two paths instead of one — why keep two?' Design context: docs/design/mcp-identity-refresh-2026-07-11.md (items 8/9 are the scope-out this reverses).
design:
## Root Cause
McpSession stdio identity is minted once at __aenter__ (self._token) and reused as the tool argument on every .call(); http identity on the same surface is per-request (httpx.Auth re-invokes token_provider). Transport-dependent freeze = the last mint-once fork after neograph-qslrx.

## Fix Approach (minimal)
In McpSession.call(), stdio branch: replace the read of self._token with a per-call re-resolution — token = await _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) when self._config is not None else await _resolve_token_no_config(self._token_provider); inject when not None. Drop the __aenter__ mint (self._token) entirely. Gate the injection on self._token_provider is not None instead of self._token is not None. Update the docstrings in _session.py (class + call + module) to say identity is per-call fresh on ALL surfaces/transports; also update design doc items 8/9 caveat (docs/design/mcp-identity-refresh-2026-07-11.md). Static-provider regression: constant provider keeps sending the same value (already covered by test pattern 3; add stdio-session variant if cheap).
notes:

## Trace-similar (mint-once identity pattern scan, src/)
Scanned every _resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config/self._token site:

## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-hs3mr)

Pattern: identity minted ONCE (at __aenter__/build time) and stored for reuse across calls, instead of per-call re-resolution via _resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config.
Scan command: grep -rn 'token_provider(\|_resolve_token\|_resolve_token_no_config\|_resolve_token_sync' src/ examples/ --include='*.py' (syntactic — every minting path goes through these helpers or a direct token_provider() invocation)

|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _session.py:225/227 | mint at __aenter__ -> self._token reused in .call() | MIGRATE | the motivating bug — move resolution into .call() |
| 2 | testing.py:114/116 | FakeMcpSession same mint-at-__aenter__ | MIGRATE | fake must mirror the real session per-call semantics (anti-echo-chamber parity) |
| 3 | testing.py:233 | fake_mcp_tool_factory resolves at tool build, closure reuse in _run | MIGRATE | real factory path is per-call since qslrx; fake is out of step |
| 4 | _client.py:375 (_TokenProviderAuth async_auth_flow) | per-request | ALLOWLIST | already per-call fresh |
| 5 | _client.py:382 (sync_auth_flow) | per-request | ALLOWLIST | already per-call fresh |
| 6 | _client.py:469 (_inject_stdio_token._with_identity) | per tool call | ALLOWLIST | already per-call fresh (the qslrx fix itself) |
| 7 | _prompt.py:88 | per _fetch invocation | ALLOWLIST | resolved inside each fetch; only prompt TEXT is memoized, and a server prompt template is run-stable by contract |
| 8 | examples/23 + 26 token_provider defs | consumer-side providers | ALLOWLIST | consumers of the seam, not minting sites |

No DEFERs. mcp_run_context has no minting site at all (stdio identity rides the factory path).
## Architect Review (atom .5)

1. Root cause correctness — LOW. Confirmed by RED behavioral test; self._token minted at __aenter__ (:225/:227) and injected frozen at :312-316. http branch of the same surface already per-request. mcp_run_context verified to have NO minting site (no direct .call(); stdio rides the factory's per-call injector) — the ticket's 'mirror mcp_run_context' clause is satisfied by a docstring-accuracy check only.
2. Fix minimality — LOW. Delete the __aenter__ stdio mint + self._token attr; in .call() stdio branch gate on self._token_provider is not None, _ensure_listing, check _declares_arg FIRST, THEN resolve (await _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) / _resolve_token_no_config) and inject when not None. Resolving only after the declares-check avoids spurious provider invocations for tools that don't carry identity — consistent with _inject_stdio_token, which only wraps declared tools.
3. Regression risk — LOW. Static provider: same value every call (regression test pattern 3; add stdio-session static variant). Semantic change is the intended one: provider invoked per call, not once at entry; zero-call sessions now invoke the provider zero times (previously once) — no consumer contract depends on that.
   MEDIUM (must handle in-fix): FakeMcpSession + fake_mcp_tool_factory must migrate in lockstep or the anti-echo-chamber parity invariant breaks (fake would freeze while real refreshes). .calls[].identity becomes 'identity resolved for THIS call'. title: Release 0.2.0: merge to main, tag, update website
description:
Merge develop to main, tag v0.2.0, update website docs for all 0.2.0 features.

## 0.2.0 Changelog (86 commits)

### Breaking changes
- Annotated[T, FromInput] DI surface replaces FromInput[T]
- Node modes renamed: produce→think, gather→agent, execute→act

### New features
- Node.inputs: dict-form fan-in (multiple typed upstream producers)
- Node.outputs: dict-form multi-output (result + tool_log per key)
- @node sub-constructs: construct_from_functions(input=, output=) with port param resolution
- construct_from_functions accepts Construct items alongside @node
- Typed tool results: ToolInteraction.typed_result preserves Pydantic models
- BAML rendering: describe_type (schema) + describe_value (instances)
- Tool results rendered as BAML in ToolMessage (not str())
- context= for verbatim state injection into prompts
- context forwarded from parent state into sub-constructs
- Oracle generator type inference from merge_fn signature
- skip_when= conditional produce (bypass LLM call)
- Pluggable input rendering (XmlRenderer, DelimitedRenderer, JsonRenderer)
- json_mode output schema via describe_type
- render_prompt() inspector
- Error hierarchy: NeographError → ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError
- list[X] merge-after-fanout (consume Each results as list)

### Bug fixes
- Sub-construct forwards context fields from parent state
- skip_when + Each: wraps result in dispatch key dict
- Oracle generator type deferred to assembly time (file ordering)
- Oracle generators use merge_fn input type (not post-merge type)
- Multiple port params raise ConstructError (not silent overwrite)
- Dict-form outputs + Oracle concurrent write error
- Each fan-out key validation in programmatic API
- 21 code review findings addressed

### Stats
- 417 tests (up from ~180 at 0.1.0)
- 16 runnable examples (up from 12)
- 76 files changed, 14K insertions

2. Update version in pyproject.toml

title: to_agent_spec(): export Construct/IR -> Agent Spec Flow (lower modifiers)
description:
Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s5, s6, s7. Add to_agent_spec() as a FREE FUNCTION in a new src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, exposed via neograph/__init__.py __all__ (NOT a Construct method -- layer discipline). Walk IR via existing iter_nodes/iter_with_arms (construct.py).

LOWER modifiers to Agent Spec primitives (doc s5 helper-lowerings table):
- Each -> MapNode/ParallelMapNode wrapping an extracted sub-Flow + collection edges
- Oracle -> ParallelFlowNode of N single-LlmNode flows (N LlmConfigs) + merge LlmNode/ToolNode + fan-out/fan-in edges (flagship gap; there is NO Oracle node)
- Loop -> BranchingNode(when) + cyclic ControlFlowEdges + self DataFlowEdges
- Operator -> per gate-task decision
Emit explicit ControlFlowEdge + DataFlowEdge from the inferred DAG + inputs dicts.

REJECT-OR-PLACEHOLDER callable-valued fields (doc s6): raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value, Loop when-as-callable, Oracle merge hooks, renderer -- fail loud with a clear error OR emit a name/placeholder. Handle _BranchNode sentinels (-> BranchingNode) or reject. Blocked by gate + type-layer tasks.
design:
## Core Invariant
`to_agent_spec()` is a free function that LOWERS the existing neograph IR (walked via `iter_with_arms`, typed via the already-bridged `spec_types.model_to_agent_spec_properties`) into flat Agent Spec primitives -- exactly the same lowering neograph already performs when compiling to LangGraph (Oracle fan-out/barrier, Each router/Send/barrier, Loop back-edge, Operator's single check-node-with-in-node-interrupt) -- and it must NEVER retarget or replace the high-level neograph `Spec`/modifier-aware IR to do so; every irreversible flattening (Oracle's flagship gap, Each's `over`/`on_error`, Loop's `when`/`max_iterations`, Operator's coercion) must be preserved losslessly via `neograph/`-prefixed `metadata` markers so the export remains BOTH a faithful flat Agent Spec (portable, ignorable markers) AND a lossless neograph round-trip source -- and it must fail loud (never silently downgrade or truncate) on any construct it cannot lower (raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value, Loop.when-as-callable, Oracle merge hooks, renderer, unresolvable _BranchNode, Portal handoff_param/handoff_channel, gate_tools_when-as-callable).

## Implementation Plan
1. Step 0 gate (mirrors nkjv9's step-0 pattern): `uv sync --extra dev --extra agent-spec` and write/run the metadata round-trip survival smoke test against real `pyagentspec` FIRST (ratification §6 residual item) -- confirms `Component.metadata` survives `to_dict -> from_dict` including disaggregation before trusting the Layer A/B marker strategy for anything beyond primitive-level export.
2. Add `src/neograph/_agent_spec.py` (free function, NOT a Construct/Node method -- per CLAUDE.md layer discipline and design doc §7). Copy `spec_types._import_agent_spec_property_classes()`'s function-local-import-guard shape for `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.*` / `pyagentspec.flows.flow.Flow` / `pyagentspec.flows.edges.*` / `pyagentspec.property` -- keep `src/neograph` core Agent-Spec-free by default.
3. `to_agent_spec(construct: Construct) -> Flow`: walk `iter_with_arms(construct)` (`_ir_branch.py`) as the top-level traversal (NOT `construct.iter_nodes`, which over-flattens and loses the Construct/_BranchNode boundaries needed to lower into `FlowNode`/`BranchingNode`). For each item: `Construct` -> `FlowNode` (nested Flow, recurse); `_BranchNode` -> `BranchingNode` (genuine sum-type, DIRECT per ratification); `Node` -> dispatch on `mode` (`think`->`LlmNode`, `agent`/`act`->`AgentNode`+tools, `scripted`/`raw`->`ToolNode`/`ApiNode`).
4. For every `Node.inputs`/`Node.outputs` (handle all three `TypeSpec` shapes: `None`, single type, dict/multi-output), call the ALREADY-BUILT `spec_types.model_to_agent_spec_properties(model)` to get `Property` lists -- do not hand-roll a second type walker. Emit `DataFlowEdge`s from the inferred `Node.inputs` dict (source_output -> destination_input) and `ControlFlowEdge`s from `Construct.nodes` order -- both explicit-from-implicit per the ratified structural mapping table.
5. Modifier lowering (read `_wiring.py`'s actual runtime sections for each before implementing, not just the design doc paraphrase):
   - `Oracle` -> `ParallelFlowNode` of N single-`LlmNode` flows (one `LlmConfig` per `Oracle.models` entry, or N copies if `models` is None) + merge `LlmNode` (`merge_prompt`) or `ToolNode` (`merge_fn`, name-only) + fan-out `ControlFlowEdge`s + fan-in `DataFlowEdge`s. Stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="oracle"` + the full `OracleSpec` (incl. `models`, which has no primitive representation) + a `group_id` linking the N variant nodes + the merge node.
   - `Each` -> `MapNode`/`ParallelMapNode` wrapping an extracted sub-`Flow`; stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="each"` + `EachSpec` (over/key/on_error).
   - `Loop` -> `BranchingNode({continue: back-edge, done: next})` + cyclic `ControlFlowEdge` + self `DataFlowEdge`; stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="loop"` + `LoopSpec` (when/max_iterations/on_exhaust/history). Reject a callable `Loop.when` with a clear error (only registered-string conditions serialize) -- `Loop.when` IS typed `str | Callable` (modifiers.py:573), so this rejection branch is real and reachable.
   - `Operator` -> the FULLY PINNED composite (neograph-03djs): `BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH})` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH) -> InputMessageNode(outputs=[StringProperty(title='user_input')])` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH) -> reconverge`. MUST implement the boolean-to-string-key coercion (render `should_pause` to the literal mapping-key string before the DataFlowEdge) -- this is a required correctness step, not an optional nicety; add a dedicated test asserting the PAUSE_BRANCH edge (not DEFAULT_BRANCH) is taken for a truthy condition. Treat dynamic `interrupt(should_pause)` payload vs static `InputMessageNode.message` as a documented-lossy edge case in metadata, never silently coerced. **CORRECTION (refine, neograph-vihe7.28): `Operator.when` is typed `str`-only (modifiers.py:543 -- 'registered condition function name') -- it CANNOT hold a callable, so a 'reject callable Operator.when' branch is unreachable dead code.
