title: Portal+Operator first-class: lift D4 ban, splice approval node onto the dynamic path
description:
Implement the v2 shape proven by spike neograph-airpr: an Operator-guarded Portal member routes Command(goto='{member}__approve') and the approval node (the ONLY interrupt() site) emits Command(goto=approved_target) on resume — so the human-approval pause sits ON the dynamic path and the member's LLM/tool spend happens exactly once across pause+resume (proven: tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py). Full design + implementation sketch: docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md.

CORE INVARIANT: the approval pause must sit ON the Command(goto) path, never a statically-appended edge (the D4 bug).

SURFACE (decided in the spike, acceptance #3): reuse Operator as-is — member | Portal(to=[...]) | Operator(when=...). No approve= kwarg on Portal. Operator.when gates whether the approval node interrupts; falsy predicate passes through without pausing.

SCOPE (sketch §Implementation, 6 steps):
1. _wiring._add_portal_mesh: per Operator-guarded member add {member}__approve via a new factory.make_portal_approval_fn (G1: Command( stays confined to factory.py/runner.py); thread the approval name into make_portal_fn so _to_command emits goto={member}__approve for PEER routes (HANDOFF_END exit unguarded — Operator guards the handoff, leaving the mesh is not a handoff; revisit in TDD if wrong).
2. Hop budget: check stays in the member wrapper; approved hop costs exactly one; settle rejected-hop counting in TDD.
3. Lift ban: remove operator<->portal reciprocal excludes from _SLOT_RULES + the pairwise arm in ModifierSet._validate; keep all other Portal exclusions. Move check_fixtures/should_fail/portal_operator_combo.py to should_pass; add should_fail fixtures for still-illegal shapes.
4. _validation_portal mesh checks accept Operator on any member; when strings resolve via condition_lookup.
5. Tests: three-surface parity; real-sqlite interrupt+resume (test_checkpoint_portal.py conventions); port the exactly-once crux assertion to the real surface; spike tests stay as the mechanics pin.
6. Docs: website concepts/portal.mdx + hitl page; D4-lift addendum in the decision log.

ANTI-BAND-AID: the interrupt must live ONLY in the approval node — never in make_portal_fn's wrapper (the naive shape re-runs the member LLM on resume, proven failing in the spike test). Audit that no other Portal path grows an inline interrupt.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: the D4 fix (approval interrupt lives ONLY in the approval node, never in the member wrapper) must extend to every Portal member class the ban-lift makes reachable -- never wider than the approval splice actually implements.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (combo-classification plumbing): before touching lowering, add a PORTAL_OPERATOR ModifierCombo + a corresponding _COMBO_MAP entry (modifiers.py:90-101) so ModifierSet.combo (line 793, direct [] subscript) does not KeyError on a portal+operator ModifierSet. Teach BOTH mesh-detection predicates that hard-code '== ModifierCombo.PORTAL' (compiler.py:254 routing into _add_portal_mesh; _wiring.py:714 _contiguous_portal_mesh run-collection) to also treat PORTAL_OPERATOR as a mesh member -- otherwise an Operator-guarded member silently falls through to the static _add_operator_check edge wiring (compiler.py:562), reintroducing D4. Write the guard-first test (construct a portal+operator node across all three surfaces) BEFORE any lowering change -- it must KeyError pre-fix, proving the gap.

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (narrowed-scope ban lift): implement the approval splice for ATOMIC members first (per the spike's proven shape). Keep a NARROWED fail-loud ConfigurationError rejecting Operator on agent/act and sub-construct Portal members (one should_fail fixture each) until those member classes get their own approval splice -- never lift the ban wider than the implementation actually covers. This resolves the DESCRIPTION-step-4-vs-DESIGN-step-7 contradiction toward the narrowed, safe reading.

Ban-lift edit sites (LOW, enumerated correctly): 3 sites, not 2 -- modifiers.py:748 (Operator row in _SLOT_RULES), modifiers.py:757 (the reciprocal Portal row), and model_post_init's pairwise arm (~:819). Test BOTH pipe orders (node|Operator()|Portal() and node|Portal()|Operator()).

## Findings
- Full design + spike proof already exist and are current: docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md + tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py (203 lines, 4 tests, passing, raw-LangGraph mechanics pin). Read both in full — the design doc's 'Implementation sketch' section is the primary source; this research confirms it against HEAD (2026-07-23) since Portal has churned since 07-14 (cross-subconstruct mesh 481ee34, agent/act members 497b269, mode-b dispatch 68243c0).

Any new approval-splice logic must flow through this ONE function, not a second copy — it already does target-validation / hop-budget / mesh-channel-write for all three member classes.
- REUSE: `target_resolve` (the entry-label map, dict DX-name -> real LangGraph node name, built in `_wiring._add_portal_mesh` at src/neograph/_wiring.py:834) is exactly the mechanism to extend for the approval splice: today it maps agent/act peers to `{name}__agent`; the new approval node needs the SAME kind of indirection (Operator-guarded member's PEER destinations resolve through `{member}__approve` instead of resolving straight to the peer). title: Stage C: render per-symbol signature blocks + Pydantic field tables from manifest
description: Now UNBLOCKED by rfl7b's unique anchors. Render committed .mdx section(s) from api-manifest.json symbols[] (signature + fields[]) with bare-name headings for non-colliding symbols and kind-namespaced headings for the 4 disambiguated symbols (node (function)->node-function, Node (model)->node-model, tool/Tool likewise) so Starlight slug == manifest anchor. Add a pytest freshness guard (committed partial == regenerated) + single-heading-per-anchor assertion (exception symbols also live in exception_hierarchy[] — keep those out of per-symbol heading generation or dedupe). Incremental/section-level per the design; prose stays hand-written.
design:
## Design Decision (refine atom uqy66.54, user-approved 2026-07-10): ONE GENERATED REFERENCE BLOCK
Chosen over minimal-hybrid and scope-to-4-collisions. Rationale: wqzel requires EVERY non-exception manifest symbol (64) to have a slug==anchor heading; a single contiguous generated region gives the simplest freshness diff (one region, manifest order) and cleanest generation, and resolves the reviewer MEDIUM-1 (no 1:1 heading-to-symbol layout exists) by NOT preserving per-symbol prose interleaving.

## Implementation Plan (refined)
1. gen_api_manifest.py: add render_reference_sections() returning str that emits, for each NON-exception manifest symbol (exclude kind==exception; uorb4 owns the fenced error tree), in a STABLE order (sorted by anchor), a section:
   - heading '### <bare name>' for non-colliders; '### node (function)' / '### Node (model)' / '### tool (function)' / '### Tool (model)' for the 4 collisions (heading TEXT slugs to the manifest anchor, verified via github-slugger 2.0.0).
   - body: a fenced python code block with the signature (from symbols[].signature), fenced so the remark harvester skips it (no anchor from the signature).
   - field table: for the 14 fielded symbols, a Pydantic field table from symbols[].fields[].
   Reuse slug() verbatim; do NOT touch the remark plugin.
2. api.mdx RESTRUCTURE: add a '## Symbol Reference' section with ONE contiguous generated region delimited by sentinel comments (GEN:reference-sections START ... END). render_reference_sections() output goes verbatim between them. Move hand-written narrative/overview prose into separate adjacent hand-written sections OUTSIDE the region. Delete the 39 old signature-in-heading per-symbol sections + the shared ResourceRef/ProducingCall/BlobResult heading + the Oracle/Each/Operator/Loop bold-bullet field material that becomes generated.
3. FRESHNESS guard: extract the single contiguous region between the sentinels from committed api.mdx and assert == render_reference_sections() (byte diff, one region).
4. SINGLE-HEADING guard (MEDIUM-2 scoping): parse ALL headings (levels 1-6, fence-aware, mirroring remark-api.mjs:75-80); assert each NON-exception manifest anchor is emitted by EXACTLY ONE heading whose slug==anchor; IGNORE hand-written organizer headings with no manifest anchor (Symbol Reference, Modifiers, Facade verbs, Shared, etc.). Exclude exception anchors (uorb4 fenced tree).
5. Verify: cd website && npm run build && npm test; grep website/dist/ for the 4 collision ids (node-function/node-model/tool-function/tool-model) AND resolving anchor links from the node/Node/tool/Tool prose refs. Regenerate api-manifest.json if needed (should be unchanged).
6. Prose preservation: hand-written per-symbol explanatory prose that must survive moves into the adjacent narrative sections; do not silently drop substantive guidance (compile() kwargs table, DI bundling notes) — relocate it.
NOTE for write-test: the freshness (region==generated) guard's red artifact is a mutation-proof (edit the committed region so it diverges from render_reference_sections()) since the region is green once generated.
notes:
ACCEPTANCE ADDENDUM (2026-07-10, from Stage-C fresh-context verification): the current reference/api.mdx headings embed full signatures (e.g. '### `Node(name, *, mode, ...)`') which github-slugger maps to garbage ('nodename--mode-...') — that is EXACTLY why node/Node/tool/Tool prose refs stay inert today (verifier confirmed: 0 autolinks emitted for the 4 collision anchors; their ids ABSENT from dist/). This ticket MUST REPLACE those signature-embedded headings with the manifest-generated ones (heading TEXT = 'node (function)'/'Node (model)'/'tool (function)'/'Tool (model)' for the 4 collision symbols, bare name otherwise) and verify (a) no orphaned/duplicate anchors remain in the built page, and (b) the four collision-pair prose refs emit RESOLVING <a href=...#node-function> links in dist/. The signature belongs in the section BODY (a code block), not the heading. This is the 'current reference headers to address' the maintainer flagged; wqzel is the permanent guard that pins it.
## Findings (research neograph-uqy66.10)

REALITY vs rfl7b: rfl7b (CLOSED) delivered ONLY the manifest-side anchor scheme + guard update, NOT any .mdx rendering. There is NO rendering script, NO committed partial, and reference/api.mdx is STILL 100% hand-written with signature-in-heading (e.g. api.mdx:280 '### `Node(name, *, mode, outputs, ...)`', :46 '### `@node(...)`', :398 '### `compile(...)`'). So the phrase 'rfl7b Stage-C rendering infrastructure' is aspirational -- what actually exists TO REUSE is: (1) the manifest data (disambiguated anchors already committed), (2) slug() the anchor contract, (3) the freshness-guard PATTERN in test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestApiManifestFreshness, (4) the remark plugin which needs ZERO logic change. kec0k IS the rendering task.

REUSE TARGET 1 -- manifest data is complete & disambiguated (do NOT re-introspect). website/src/data/api-manifest.json symbols[] (74 entries) already carry name/kind/anchor/signature/fields[]. VERIFIED the 4 collision anchors are already correct: node->node-function, Node->node-model, tool->tool-function, Tool->tool-model (scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:310 _disambiguate_anchors + :299 _KIND_ANCHOR_TAG, two-pass Counter). All other 70 symbols keep bare slug(name). 14 symbols carry fields[] (Node, Construct, Oracle, Each, Loop, Operator, Tool, ToolInteraction, ResourceRef, ProducingCall, BlobResult, LintIssue, VerifyIssue, EachFailure).

REUSE TARGET 2 -- collision heading TEXT verified against real github-slugger 2.0.0: 'node (function)'->node-function, 'Node (model)'->node-model, 'tool (function)'->tool-function, 'Tool (model)'->tool-model. So heading text = 'name (kindword)' reproduces the manifest anchor EXACTLY. Non-colliding heading text = bare name.

REUSE TARGET 3 -- remark plugin needs NO change (website/plugins/remark-api.mjs). It keys autolinks by symbol NAME->anchor (line 161 SOFT tier, line 144 HARD tier), gated on headings.has(sym.anchor). Once api.mdx headings slug to the manifest anchors, node/Node/tool/Tool prose refs autolink automatically. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: remark-api harvests headings by reading the reference/api.mdx FILE TEXT directly (line 32 refPageFile, line 75 readFileSync split lines, with fence-tracking line 76). It does NOT read imported partials or the render AST. => generated headings MUST live INLINE in api.mdx; a separate imported .mdx partial would NOT be harvested (and rfl7b flagged imported-MDX-component headings also drop out of Starlight's right-sidebar TOC). Fenced code blocks are skipped by the harvester -- that is why the existing error-hierarchy ASCII tree (api.mdx:692-704, fenced) never emits anchors, and why exceptions currently have NO per-symbol headings.

REUSE TARGET 4 -- freshness-guard exemplar: tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestApiManifestFreshness (:98) diffs committed-file == regenerated with a drift message naming the regen command; :152 is the not-a-noop meta-test; :229 test_every_symbol_anchor_is_slug_of_its_name already pins anchor uniqueness+slug-stability. Copy this shape for the rendered-section freshness guard.

EXCEPTION OVERLAP (the dedupe hazard): 10 exception-kind symbols live in symbols[] (NeographError, ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError, NodeOutputError, NonIdempotentReplayError, PromptVarMissing, ResourceExpiredError, CheckpointSchemaError) AND in exception_hierarchy[] (11 entries -- adds StateMissingError which is not in __all__). uorb4 owns the error tree (rendered as a FENCED block, anchors intentionally not harvested). => EXCLUDE kind=='exception' from per-symbol heading generation, else you double-emit anchors already owned by the tree. Single-heading-per-anchor assertion must account for this.

## Relevant Code
- website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx -- the hand-written page to edit in place; ~40 signature-in-heading sections to replace. Keep prose bullets hand-written.
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:94 slug() -- anchor contract, reuse verbatim in the renderer. :266 anchor=slug(name); :310 _disambiguate_anchors; :490 build_manifest(); :512 _write_json canonical form.
- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:32,75-80 -- heading harvester (reads api.mdx text, fence-aware). :144/:161 the two autolink emitters gated on headings.has(anchor).
- website/plugins/remark-api.test.mjs -- node:test harness, runs against REAL manifest+api.mdx; case (i) already pins the node-function/node-model disambiguation. Run 'npm test' after any plugin-visible change.
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestApiManifestFreshness -- freshness-guard exemplar to copy.
- website/astro.config.mjs:11-12 remarkPlugins wiring; website/package.json build+test scripts.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- MECHANISM DECISION (the crux): because remark-api harvests headings from api.mdx's own file text AND Starlight builds TOC only from inline markdown headings, generated sections MUST be inline in api.mdx, not an imported partial. Recommend a Python renderer that OWNS a sentinel-delimited region of api.mdx; the freshness guard extracts that region and diffs against regeneration. A separate committed .mdx that is imported would break BOTH remark harvesting and TOC.
- PROSE INTERLEAVING: rfl7b's named failure mode is flattening hand-written narrative bullets (api.mdx:79-101 @node kwargs, etc.) that have NO manifest equivalent. The generator owns heading+signature-block+field-table; prose bullets must stay hand-written. Reconcile via per-symbol paired sentinels (generator regenerates only the heading+signature+table span, prose sits below) OR a manifest-external prose store keyed by anchor that the renderer interleaves. This granularity is the main design call.
- EXCEPTION dedupe (above) -- exclude kind=='exception' from heading gen; assert single-heading-per-anchor over the NON-exception set.
- SIGNATURE-in-body accuracy: several current inline signatures are hand-embellished (api.mdx:52-76 @node lists ~20 kwargs incl. renderer/context/skip_when/inputs NOT in the introspected signature; :404-415 compile). The manifest signature is the introspected str(inspect.signature). Switching to manifest signatures is the point (drift-catching) but will visibly change these blocks -- expected, not a regression.
- MISSING-kind guard: renderer must skip kind=='missing' (currently zero) without crashing.
- After edit: run 'npm run build' (HARD-tier + build), 'npm test' (plugin regression), and grep dist/reference/api/index.html for id="node-function"/"node-model"/"tool-function"/"tool-model" AND resolving <a href=...#node-function> from the collision-pair prose refs (the addendum's acceptance check).
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom uqy66.11)
Pattern: per-symbol reference headings that EMBED the full signature (e.g. '### `Node(name, *, mode, ...)`') -> github-slugger produces garbage slugs (e.g. 'nodename--mode-...') that never match the manifest anchor, so prose refs (esp. node/Node/tool/Tool) stay silently INERT (0 autolinks; ids absent from dist/). Fix = manifest-generated headings whose slug == manifest anchor.
Scan: grep '^### `' api.mdx (39 headings); correlate with api-manifest.json symbols[].
Scope: 74 manifest symbols total. Exclude 10 exception-kind (owned by uorb4's fenced tree). Generate headings for the remaining ~64: bare-name for non-colliders, kind-namespaced TEXT for the 4 collisions (node->'node (function)'->#node-function, Node->'Node (model)'->#node-model, tool->#tool-function, Tool->#tool-model), field tables for the 14 fielded (Pydantic) symbols. Signature moves to the section BODY (fenced code block).

| # | Locus | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | api.mdx 39 '### `Sig(...)`' headings | signature-in-heading -> garbage slug | MIGRATE | kec0k replaces with manifest-generated headings (sentinel-delimited inline region) |
| 2 | the 4 collision symbols (node/Node/tool/Tool) | 0 resolving autolinks today (verifier-confirmed) | MIGRATE (motivating defect) | kind-namespaced headings make slug==anchor -> prose refs resolve |
| 3 | 10 exception-kind symbols | live in exception_hierarchy[] | ALLOWLIST/EXCLUDE | uorb4 owns the fenced error tree; keep out of per-symbol heading gen to preserve single-heading-per-anchor |
Single scanned artifact (api.mdx); no other page hand-authors per-symbol reference sections. Guard (kec0k adds): freshness (committed region==regenerated) + single-heading-per-anchor; wqzel is the permanent coverage capstone.
## Architect Review

Independent adversarial review (atom uqy66.12). Verified against codebase: slug() contract (gen_api_manifest.py:94), _disambiguate_anchors (:310), remark harvester (remark-api.mjs:32,75-80), api.mdx headings, TestApiManifestFreshness (test_guards_api_manifest.py:98). Empirically ran github-slugger 2.0.0 on the 4 collision heading texts.

CONFIRMED SOUND (survives attack):
- INLINE sentinel region (not a partial) is CORRECT. Harvester reads api.mdx file text with fence-tracking (lines 75-80) and Starlight TOC only sees inline markdown; an imported partial would break both harvesting and TOC. Fenced code body is skipped by the harvester, so moving the signature into a fenced block correctly keeps it out of anchor generation.
- Collision heading TEXT slugs to the manifest anchors: empirically 'node (function)'->node-function, 'Node (model)'->node-model, 'tool (function)'->tool-function, 'Tool (model)'->tool-model; garbage confirmed for signature-in-heading ('Node(name, *, mode,...)'->nodename--mode-outputs-inputsnone).
- Excluding kind=='exception' is SUFFICIENT and CORRECT: exceptions render in a fenced (unharvested) tree, disambiguation already makes ALL anchors unique across the full symbol set, so no non-exception symbol double-emits from generation. No other symbol-kind overlap exists.
- Reuse discipline is good: slug() reused verbatim, TestApiManifestFreshness shape copied, remark plugin needs zero change. No reinvention.
- Acceptance IS verified in the plan (step 5 greps dist/ for the 4 collision ids AND resolving <a href=...#node-function> links).

FINDINGS:
- [MEDIUM] Finding: The plan frames the work as 'replace 39 signature-in-heading sections,' but iterates ALL ~64 non-exception symbols (step 1) — and the current layout is NOT 1:1 heading<->symbol. Oracle/Each/Operator/Loop (4 of the 14 fielded symbols) have NO '### ' heading today; they live as bold-bullet prose under '### Modifiers (pipe syntax)' (api.mdx:324-360). ResourceRef/ProducingCall/BlobResult share ONE heading (:213). To make slug==anchor and emit field tables for these, the generator must CREATE new per-symbol headings, splitting the grouped section and restructuring the Modifiers block. The 'per-symbol paired sentinels, prose stays below' model assumes a layout that doesn't exist. Suggestion: make an explicit decision on WHICH of the 64 get generated headings and HOW grouped/narrative sections (Modifiers, ResourceRef trio) are restructured while preserving hand-written prose — do not leave this to implementer guesswork.
- [MEDIUM] Finding: The single-heading-per-anchor guard (step 4b) as specified — 'parse every level-3 heading, slug it, assert each maps to exactly ONE manifest anchor' — will FALSE-FAIL on legitimate hand-written organizer headings that have no manifest anchor: 'Modifiers (pipe syntax)'->modifiers-pipe-syntax, 'Facade verbs'->facade-verbs, 'Shared', 'Runtime wiring (compile() dict kwargs)', 'Error Hierarchy'. Also the harvester matches '#{1,6}' (all levels), not level-3 only, so scoping the guard to level-3 can mis-scope. Suggestion: scope the assertion to the intersection of heading-slugs with manifest anchors — assert each NON-exception manifest anchor is emitted exactly once and ignore non-anchor prose headings; mirror the harvester's all-levels + fence-aware parse.
- [LOW] Finding: With per-symbol sentinels scattered through interleaved prose, the freshness byte-diff must locate ALL sentinel regions, concatenate in file order, and diff against render_reference_sections() which emits in manifest/__all__ order — a file-order != manifest-order mismatch breaks the diff, and a newly-added symbol with no sentinel region is silently uncovered (coverage is wqzel's, out of scope). The plan claims per-symbol sentinels 'keep the diff minimal' but they actually make the freshness diff harder than one contiguous generated region. Suggestion: document the ordering contract, or prefer a single contiguous generated region with hand-written prose kept in a separate adjacent section.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

title: 7nan completion: make_oracle_redirect_fn + required node_name + integration test
description:
## Architectural property (the invariant)

No framework closure that calls StateBus.get_required may source its node_label from raw_fn.__name__. The node label surfaced in StateMissingError must always be the user's declared Node.name (or sub-Construct.name), independent of which closure is firing or which API surface built the closure.

This is an invariant about the relationship between framework infrastructure and user-facing error messages: error labels must trace to user-declared identifiers, never to mangled framework names.

## Anti-band-aid clause

IF YOUR FIX ADDS YET ANOTHER 'node_name: str | None = None' KWARG TO YET ANOTHER CLOSURE FACTORY, STOP. The architectural fix is to (a) make node_name REQUIRED (not optional) on every closure factory that exposes such a parameter, AND (b) audit every closure factory in _oracle.py for the same pattern, AND (c) consider whether the right abstraction is a structured 'NodeContext' object passed once rather than a string threaded through every factory.

If the diff just adds kwargs with default=None, it is a band-aid. The default=None silently preserves the broken fallback for any caller — internal or external — that omits the kwarg.

## Required architectural shape

1. Audit ALL closure factories in src/neograph/_oracle.py (and any other module): make_oracle_redirect_fn, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn, make_each_redirect_fn, and any others that propagate raw_fn.__name__ or call StateBus.get_required.
2. For every factory that exposes a node_name parameter, make it REQUIRED (`node_name: str` with no default). Every call site must supply it.
3. For make_oracle_redirect_fn specifically: even though it doesn't call get_required TODAY, audit whether its propagation of raw_fn.__name__ (line 71) creates the same surface bug if/when get_required is added there. If yes, add node_name now; do not leave a latent gap.
4. Consider — and document the decision in design field — whether the right abstraction is a NodeContext dataclass containing (name, field_name, ...) passed once to each factory, rather than threading a bare string.

## Breadth/integration tests that MUST break a band-aid implementation

1. **End-to-end through compile()**: build a Node(name='my-hyphenated-node', ...) | Each(...) | Oracle(...), compile and run with a state lacking EACH_ITEM (use a synthetic injection or mock the dispatch payload). Assert the resulting StateMissingError contains 'my-hyphenated-node' (with hyphen).
2. **Plain Oracle (no Each)**: same Node + Oracle setup without Each. Cover the make_oracle_redirect_fn path.
3. **Mangled-name protection**: at least one test where node.name contains a hyphen and the field_name (mangled) is observably different from node.name; assert the error uses the un-mangled form.
4. **Missing-kwarg detection**: if node_name is required, calling the factory without it must raise TypeError at function definition consumption, not at runtime — verify via a mypy strict-mode check OR a unit test that confirms the call site provides it.

## Audit step (mandatory)

Before implementing: grep the codebase for `raw_fn.__name__` and `node_label=`. Classify every site as (correct / fixed-by-7nan / still broken / latent). Paste the table into the bead notes.

## Independent-review gate (acceptance criterion)

After implementation, spawn a fresh feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with this exact prompt: 'Review the fix for neograph-kg8l. Confirm with high confidence (>=90) whether this is a complete structural fix or another partial patch. Specifically: (a) is node_name required (not optional) on every closure factory exposing it? (b) was make_oracle_redirect_fn audited, and if get_required is ever added there, will it Just Work? (c) is there an integration test that goes through compile()+run() rather than constructing closures in isolation?' Paste the verdict.

## Out of scope

- LangGraph's __name__ requirement at factory.py:121 (separate concern; that __name__ remains the mangled form for LangGraph graph identity).

## Acceptance

- node_name is required (str, no default) on every redirect factory that exposes it
- make_oracle_redirect_fn either has node_name or has a justification in design field explaining why it's exempt
- 4+ tests including 1+ end-to-end integration test through compile()
- Audit table pasted in notes
- Independent reviewer verdict 'structural', high confidence
- make quality green

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-tjupj
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-tjupj` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjupj/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-tjupj
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-tjupj)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjupj --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjupj --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjupj/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-tjupj codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjupj/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-tjupj
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-tjupj`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-tjupj)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjupj --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-tjupj sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Sync run() + async scripted/raw body silently stores an un-awaited coroutine
description: Latent footgun surfaced during Phase 1b (neograph-w74k.2.2). ScriptedDispatch.execute (_dispatch.py:123, SYNC path) and raw_node_wrapper (factory.py:101) call the user body and return its result directly. If a user writes an 'async def' scripted/raw body but runs the graph via the SYNC driver run()/graph.invoke, self.fn returns a coroutine that flows UN-AWAITED into state — silent wrong behavior (a coroutine object where a model is expected). Phase 1b handles the ASYNC driver correctly (isawaitable-await); this is the sync-driver+async-body mismatch. DECISION NEEDED: reject an async body at compile-time when only sync run is used (hard — driver is chosen at call time, not compile time), OR warn/raise at runtime when ScriptedDispatch.execute sees isawaitable(result) under the sync path (cheap, fail-loud). Recommend: in the SYNC ScriptedDispatch.execute + raw_node_wrapper, if inspect.isawaitable(result): raise a NeographError('async body invoked under sync run(); use arun()'). Out of scope for 1b (async path); file for a later phase.
notes:
Fail-loud guard for async body under sync driver.

Fix (two SYNC call sites): after calling the user body, if inspect.isawaitable(result) -> raise ExecutionError (subclass of NeographError) instead of returning the coroutine into state.
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py ScriptedDispatch.execute (~L127): added isawaitable check + result.close() + raise. Imported ExecutionError.
- src/neograph/factory.py raw_node_wrapper in _make_raw_wrapper (~L102): same guard. Imported ExecutionError.
Async twins (ScriptedDispatch.aexecute, araw_node_wrapper) unchanged — they correctly isawaitable-await.

Error: ExecutionError.build('async node body invoked under sync run(); use arun()', node=<name>, hint='...Call arun(graph, ...) / graph.ainvoke instead of run() / graph.invoke.'). Message matches /arun/. Chose ExecutionError over bare NeographError as the most specific runtime subclass; pytest.raises(NeographError) still catches it. Also close() the rejected coroutine to suppress the 'never awaited' RuntimeWarning.

Tests (TDD red-first) in tests/test_async_dual_path.py::TestAsyncBodyUnderSyncRunFailsLoud:
- test_scripted_async_body_under_sync_run_raises (async @node scripted body via run() -> raises)
- test_raw_async_body_under_sync_run_raises (mode='raw' async body via run() -> raises)
- test_scripted_async_body_under_arun_still_works (positive regression via arun())
- test_raw_async_body_under_arun_still_works (positive regression via arun())
Verified red before fix (scripted silently returned coroutine; raw got opaque LangGraph InvalidUpdateError), green after.

Gates: ruff check src/ tests/ -> All checks passed. Full suite 2384 passed. Targeted async/scripted/raw/dispatch suites 40+483 passed. NOT closed, NOT committed per instructions.

design:
## Core Invariant
The same Keymaker mesh built via all three surfaces (@node sugar, declarative Node(...) | Keymaker, programmatic Node.scripted(...) | Keymaker) produces IDENTICAL IR and IDENTICAL runtime results; handoff_param AND handoff_channel converge in the normalizer (_ir_normalize.py) for all three surfaces — there are NO writes of either field in decorators.py or _construct_builder.py (the neograph-ts7 / fan_out_param single-writer lesson), pinned by guard G3.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; most write-side already exists from T1/T2/T3)

1. GUARD-FIRST — G3 (extend, do not rebuild): in tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py add 'handoff_channel' to `TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter.IR_FIELDS` (:974). `handoff_param` is already there. Update the class docstring/comment to name handoff_channel as the SECOND Keymaker IR field, sibling of the fan_out_param ownership rule (_construct_builder.py:172-177, neograph-k7bg). Run it — it must be GREEN because _ir_normalize.py is already the sole writer (verify by grep: no handoff_channel/handoff_param writes in decorators.py/_construct_builder.py). To honor guard-first for a NET-NEW surface, ALSO add a decorator parity assertion that FAILS before step 2 (the @node peers= path does not exist yet, so an @node mesh cannot be built) — that is the failing-first test that step 2 turns green.

2. @node sugar in src/neograph/decorators.py (mirror loop_when=, NOT a new mechanism):
   a. Add kwargs to node() signature (~:280): `peers: list[str] | None = None`, `max_hops: int | None = None`. WIDEN existing `on_exhaust` annotation to `Literal['error','last','exit'] | None`. `route: str | None = None` (peer-mode routing FIELD; NOT route='decide' — mode b has no sugar).
   b. Add a `_build_keymaker_kwargs` helper mirroring `_build_each_kwargs` (:240): conditionally include route/max_hops/on_exhaust ONLY when non-default so model_fields_set matches the pipe form (IR identity).
   c. Decoration-time conflict raises (mirror :378, ConstructError.build): peers=×map_over= and peers=×loop_when=. Also max_hops=/route= WITHOUT peers= => error (mirror map_key-requires-map_over :372-377). on_exhaust is shared — route it by trigger, do not error on it alone.
   d. Add a `if peers is not None:` block near the loop_when block (:661) building `n = n | Keymaker(**keymaker_kwargs)`, re-registering the sidecar and param_res exactly as the loop_when block does. The 'handoff' param flows through existing inputs inference (:550-559) with zero special-casing; the normalizer then stamps handoff_param + handoff_channel on Construct(...) init.
   e. Route the shared on_exhaust/max_iterations: when loop_when set => Loop (validate on_exhaust in {error,last}); when peers set => Keymaker (validate on_exhaust in {error,exit}).

3. Parity test suite (copy tests/test_fanin_validation.py:568-687 shape) — new tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py section OR a new tests/test_keymaker_parity.py. Three builder fns for one canonical 2-member mesh (triage<->billing, RouteHop payload, reserved 'handoff' param, max_hops=6 on entry): `_km_mesh_declarative` (Node(...) | Keymaker), `_km_mesh_programmatic` (Node.scripted(...) | Keymaker), `_km_mesh_decorator` (@node(peers=..., max_hops=...)). Assertions: (i) all assemble; (ii) per-member handoff_param == 'handoff' and handoff_channel == StateKeys.handoff_payload(field_name_for('triage')) IDENTICAL across surfaces (copy test_ir_normalize.py:399-428); (iii) IR equality of the Keymaker modifier (peers, max_hops, on_exhaust, route, model_fields_set); (iv) end-to-end runtime: compile + run all three, assert identical routing result (reuse the tests/test_checkpoint_keymaker.py register_scripted mesh helpers). Class docstring MUST document the ForwardConstruct v1 exemption (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT).

4. Decorator-conflict tests: peers=×map_over= raises, peers=×loop_when= raises, max_hops= without peers= raises, on_exhaust='exit' routed to Keymaker / 'last' to Loop. Put in tests/decorator/ or the modifier-legality half of test_keymaker.py.

5. Gates (per /dev-practices:execute): `uv run --extra dev pytest` on tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py, tests/test_fanin_validation.py (or new parity file), tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py, tests/test_ir_normalize.py, tests/decorator/, plus mypy (new @node kwargs — assert_never not affected) and ruff. Commit per task; no push until the consolidation task.

Anti-band-aid: the @node layer is SUGAR OVER THE IR (AGENTS.md layer discipline) — decorators.py must ONLY build+pipe the Keymaker modifier and let _ir_normalize infer handoff_param/handoff_channel. Do NOT write either field, and do NOT special-case the 'handoff' key in decorators. If you find yourself touching node.py / _construct_builder.py / _ir_normalize.py to make @node work, STOP — that is the layer violation G3 exists to catch.
notes:
## Findings (T4 research — dp-researcher)

MUCH IS ALREADY DONE by T1/T2/T3. T4 is a SMALL task: @node sugar in decorators.py + a parity test suite + widening ONE existing guard. The IR write-side already fully exists — do NOT rebuild it.

- REUSE (do not re-derive) — the normalizer is ALREADY the sole writer of BOTH handoff fields. `_HandoffParamNormalizer` (src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:152-174) writes `handoff_param='handoff'` keyed off the reserved 'handoff' inputs key; the same module (_ir_normalize.py:271-292) computes the entry-keyed `handoff_channel` once and stamps it on every Keymaker member. Registered in `_NORMALIZERS` (:232). All three surfaces carry the 'handoff' inputs key explicitly and converge here. NOTHING in decorators.py / _construct_builder.py writes either field today (verified by grep — zero hits in decorators.py).
- G3 IS 90% ALREADY IN PLACE: the single-writer guard `TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter` (tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:940-1084) ALREADY has `handoff_param` in `IR_FIELDS` (:974). GAP: `handoff_channel` is NOT in that frozenset. T4's G3 = ADD 'handoff_channel' to IR_FIELDS (:974) — this makes it the exact sibling of the fan_out_param rule the mandate names. That single addition is the guard-first failing test (write it first; it will pass immediately because _ir_normalize is already the sole writer — so ALSO write a temporary negative mutation check, or rely on the AST scanner which already scans all of src/). Confirm node.py declares both fields as class-body `Name` decls (node.py:204 fan_out_param, :212 handoff_param, :221 handoff_channel) — these are DECLARATIONS the scanner deliberately ignores (:1001-1005), so adding handoff_channel to IR_FIELDS will not false-positive on node.py.
- @node sugar DOES NOT EXIST YET: grep 'peers|keymaker|handoff' in decorators.py returns ZERO hits. This is the net-new surface T4 adds.
- The reserved 'handoff' param flows NATURALLY through existing @node signature inference: a param named `handoff` typed as the payload model lands in the inferred `inputs_dict` (decorators.py:550-559) as `{'handoff': PayloadModel}` with no special-casing. So @node sugar only needs to BUILD + PIPE the Keymaker modifier; the normalizer does the rest — IDENTICAL IR to the pipe form by construction.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/decorators.py:280 — `loop_when=`/`max_iterations=`/`on_exhaust=` kwargs (the EXEMPLAR to mirror). NOTE: `on_exhaust` ALREADY EXISTS as a Loop kwarg typed `Literal['error','last'] | None` (:282). Keymaker needs 'exit'. Widen the annotation to `Literal['error','last','exit'] | None` and route by trigger kwarg (peers= vs loop_when=).
- src/neograph/decorators.py:661-671 — the `loop_when` block that builds `Loop(**loop_kwargs)` and pipes `n = n | Loop(...)`. Copy this shape for a `peers is not None` block building `Keymaker(**keymaker_kwargs)`.
- src/neograph/decorators.py:378 — the map_over/loop_when conflict-raise pattern (`ConstructError.build` at decoration). Copy for peers=×map_over= and peers=×loop_when= conflicts.
- src/neograph/decorators.py:240-249 — `_build_each_kwargs` CONDITIONAL-include idiom (only add on_error when non-default). Mirror this in a `_build_keymaker_kwargs` so route='goto'/max_hops=10/on_exhaust='error' defaults are OMITTED unless the user passed them — keeps `model_fields_set` IDENTICAL to the pipe form (critical for true IR identity; Keymaker.model_post_init reads model_fields_set at modifiers.py:666).
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:595-673 — `Keymaker` class; peer-mode kwargs peers/route/max_hops/on_exhaust (:624-627).
- tests/test_fanin_validation.py:568-687 — THE three-surface parity template (`_fan_in_valid_declarative`/`_decorator`/`_programmatic` + `TestThreeSurfaceFanInParity` parametrized). Copy this exact shape for the Keymaker mesh; document the ForwardConstruct exemption in the class/test docstring.
- tests/test_ir_normalize.py:399-428 — `test_fan_out_param_identical_across_node_and_programmatic` — the pattern for asserting an inferred IR field is IDENTICAL across @node and pipe. Copy it to assert handoff_param AND handoff_channel are identical across all three Keymaker surfaces.
- tests/test_checkpoint_keymaker.py:45-74 — the canonical programmatic mesh (`Node.scripted('triage', fn=..., inputs={'handoff': RouteHop}, outputs=RouteHop) | Keymaker(peers=['billing'], max_hops=N)`). The @node equivalent: `@node(outputs=RouteHop, peers=['billing'], max_hops=N)` `def triage(handoff: RouteHop) -> RouteHop: ...`. These must produce identical IR + identical runtime results.
- tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py — existing modifier-legality tests; add the decorator-conflict tests near here or in the decorator test package (tests/decorator/).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- on_exhaust KWARG COLLISION (the one real design wrinkle): `on_exhaust` is shared between Loop ('error'/'last') and Keymaker ('error'/'exit'). CANNOT error on a bare on_exhaust= alone. Route by trigger: peers= present => feed to Keymaker (validate in {error,exit}); loop_when= present => feed to Loop (validate in {error,last}). Since peers=×loop_when= is already a hard conflict error, on_exhaust is never ambiguous. Same for max_iterations (Loop) vs max_hops (Keymaker, NEW kwarg).
- IDENTICAL-IR fragility: passing default kwargs explicitly (route='goto') changes `model_fields_set` vs the pipe form. Use conditional-include (mirror _build_each_kwargs) so IR equality holds field-set-wise, not just value-wise.
- Trigger discipline: mirror loop_when — PRESENCE of `peers=` (a list, incl. `peers=[]` for terminal specialists) builds the Keymaker. `peers=None` (default) => no Keymaker. Guard: route=/max_hops=/on_exhaust='exit' passed WITHOUT peers= should raise a decoration-time ConstructError (mirror map_key-requires-map_over at decorators.py:372-377) — EXCEPT on_exhaust which is shared, so only flag max_hops=/route= without peers=.
- Mode (b) route='decide' has NO @node sugar in v1 (design §2.2) — decorator's route= is the peer-mode routing FIELD only. If a user passes route='decide' via @node without peers=, it must NOT silently build a broken Keymaker; either reject or ignore (recommend: only build Keymaker when peers is not None, and reject route= without peers=).
- Keymaker+Operator combo is illegal (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO): @node `interrupt_when=` + `peers=` will produce Keymaker|Operator which the slot rules reject at ASSEMBLY. Decoration-time conflict for this pair is OPTIONAL (design scope only names map_over/loop_when); the assembly ConstructError already covers it. Note but do not over-build.
- ForwardConstruct EXEMPT in v1 (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT, reviewer AGREED 'stronger than the di_inputs analogy'): a runtime mesh has no static dataflow for the tracer to thread. Document the exemption in the parity-test docstring (AC requirement). Do NOT add self.handoff() — it is a filed fast-follow.
- NOT a contradiction, just a doc-table gap already adjudicated (D10): design §4.1 SCOPE table omits _input_shape.py but T2 already wired the read side; no T4 action.
- Three-surface parity rule (AGENTS.md) requires testing ALL THREE or explaining exemption — ForwardConstruct is the sanctioned exemption; the other three (declarative Node(...), programmatic pipe, @node) are all in-scope and must be asserted identical.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-kk262)

Pattern: an IR field (handoff_param / handoff_channel) WRITTEN outside src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py (single-writer violation — the fan_out_param / neograph-k7bg discipline). T4 is net-new @node sugar; the disease it must not introduce is a decorator-path write of either Keymaker IR field (the exact neograph-ts7 three-surface-parity bug shape, D5/H2).

Scan command: grep -rnE '(handoff_param|handoff_channel)\s*(=|:|\+=)' src/neograph/*.py | grep -v '_ir_normalize.py' | grep -vE 'handoff_(param|channel):\s*str'
Total instances found: 0 writes (2 non-write matches, both benign)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _ir_normalize.py:152-174,271-292 | writes handoff_param + handoff_channel | KEEP (canonical) | the sanctioned SOLE writer for all three surfaces |
| 2 | _input_shape.py:119 | node.handoff_param is not None and input_name == node.handoff_param | KEEP (read) | comparison / read of channel key on extract path (D10) — not a write |
| 3 | _validation_inputs.py:134 | comment mentioning handoff_param=None | KEEP (comment) | documentation, not code |
| 4 | node.py:212,221 | handoff_param: str \| None = None / handoff_channel | KEEP (declaration) | class-body field decls; guard scanner deliberately ignores bare-Name decls (test_guards_llm_runtime.py:1001-1005) |
| 5 | decorators.py | ZERO Keymaker/peers/handoff hits | N/A | net-new surface T4 adds; MUST NOT write either IR field (only build+pipe the Keymaker modifier) |

Conclusion: no existing single-writer violation. T4's obligation is to ADD the @node sugar WITHOUT introducing one; G3 (adding handoff_channel to IR_FIELDS) is the ratchet that pins it. Sweep-verify re-runs the scan command verbatim — must stay 0 writes after implementation.
## Architect Review (neograph-5984x.4, dp-reviewer, fresh context)

Verified against src: decorators.py (signature :280, loop_when block :661, conflict pattern :378, _build_each_kwargs :240, inputs inference :550-559), modifiers.py Keymaker :595-672 + Loop.on_exhaust :575-582, _ir_normalize.py :152-174/:271-294 (sole writer, dict-literal/subscript write forms), _validation_keymaker.py :186-197 (entry-only knob check), tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py :940-1084 (G3 scanner + allowlist).

- [LOW] Finding: on_exhaust collision resolution is SOUND. Since peers=x loop_when= is a hard conflict, on_exhaust is never ambiguous; the built modifier validates it fail-loud (Loop.model_post_init rejects 'exit' -> ConfigurationError; Keymaker Literal['error','exit'] rejects 'last'). Note: the Keymaker 'last' path surfaces a raw Pydantic ValidationError rather than neograph's ConstructError convention, and widening the decorator annotation to Literal['error','last','exit'] drops the static-checker catch for Loop's 'exit'. Suggestion (optional): route on_exhaust by trigger at decoration and raise a clean ConstructError for the mismatched value, mirroring :378 — correctness is already fail-loud, this is DX polish only.

- [LOW] Finding: IDENTICAL-IR via conditional-include _build_keymaker_kwargs DOES guarantee IR identity AND is load-bearing beyond cosmetics — _validation_keymaker.py:189 reads Keymaker.model_fields_set to enforce entry-only max_hops/on_exhaust. If the decorator passed defaults explicitly, the non-entry member (billing) would fail assembly while the pipe form passes. The plan's canonical mesh (max_hops=6 on entry triage, bare billing) exercises exactly this, and asserting model_fields_set equality catches a botched conditional-include as a red test. title: Design neograph-pipeline.schema.json
description:
## What
Design the JSON Schema that defines the pipeline spec format. This is the contract — both YAML and JSON specs validate against it.

## Schema must cover
- nodes: name, mode, model, prompt (inline string), outputs (type ref), tools (list of refs), oracle (models, merge), loop (when, max_iterations, on_exhaust)
- constructs: name, input, output, nodes (refs), loop, oracle, each
- pipeline: name, nodes (ordered list of node/construct refs)
- Variable substitution syntax: ${node}, ${node.field}, ${node.field.subfield}

## Approach
- Use JSON Schema draft 2020-12
- Reference project.neograph.schema.json for type/tool/model resolution
- Write as a .json file in src/neograph/schemas/
- Test with jsonschema library: valid specs pass, invalid specs fail with clear errors

## Deliverable
src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json + tests
design:
## Architecture
JSON Schema draft 2020-12 with $defs for reusable types (NodeSpec, ConstructSpec, ModifierSpec, VariableRef). Pipeline schema references project schema via type/tool/model name strings. File: src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json
notes:
## Findings
- Haystack uses flat YAML: components dict + connections list
- Promptflow uses node list with ${node.output} refs and typed inputs
- The neograph schema needs: nodes (name/mode/model/prompt/outputs/tools/modifiers), constructs (name/input/output/nodes/modifiers), pipeline (nodes list)
- Variable syntax: ${node} and ${node.field.subfield} — dotted access only
- Modifiers expressed as nested objects: loop: {when: expr, max_iterations: N}, oracle: {models: [...], merge_fn: name}
- JSON Schema draft 2020-12 with $ref for reusable definitions

## Relevant code
- src/neograph/node.py — Node fields (name, mode, model, prompt, outputs, inputs, tools, modifiers)
- src/neograph/modifiers.py — Oracle, Each, Loop, Operator field definitions
- src/neograph/construct.py — Construct fields (name, input, output, nodes, modifiers)

## Core Invariant
The JSON Schema is a 1:1 mapping of the existing Construct IR — every schema element has a direct counterpart in the Python IR.

## Source

```python
# src/neograph/_ir_protocols.py (new tiny module)
@runtime_checkable
class ConstructItem(Protocol):
    name: str
    modifier_set: ModifierSet
```

`Construct.nodes: list[ConstructItem]` (still uses `BeforeValidator` at runtime; the static annotation is precise). `classify_modifiers(item: ConstructItem)`.

title: Epic: Node.inputs refactor — first-class fan-in + list[X] for Each consumers
description:
## Problem

`Node.input: type | None` carries ONE type per node. This shapes the whole framework around single-upstream nodes and forces three warts for everything else:

1. **Declarative and programmatic APIs can't statically validate fan-in.** A user writing `Node(name='report', input=Claims, ...)` picks ONE upstream type to validate and reads the others from state by isinstance scan. The dict form `input={'claims': Claims, 'scores': Scores}` turns validation off entirely (validator's dict bypass). LLM-driven pipelines emitting JSON specs get zero fan-in type safety.

2. **Two validator walkers exist.** `_validate_node_chain` walks `node.input` (single type). `_validate_fan_in_types` walks function signatures (N annotations). The split is forced by `Node.input` carrying one value — not by any fundamental difference in what they want to check. They share only `effective_producer_type` as of the recent refactor (neograph-ayq / neograph-8k3 follow-up).

3. **`@node` scripted fan-in routes through `raw_fn`.** `factory._extract_input` can only return ONE value. Fan-in @node functions need N values. The workaround: `@node` sets `Node.raw_fn` with a custom adapter that reads each parameter by name. Side effect: scripted `@node` execution logs show `mode=raw` instead of `mode=scripted`. Documented in AGENTS.md as a deliberate deviation.

All three warts disappear if `Node.input` can carry multiple typed inputs keyed by upstream name.

## Proposal

Replace `Node.input: type | None` with `Node.inputs: dict[str, type]` — a mapping of upstream-name → expected-type. Each key names an upstream producer; each value is the consumer-side expected type for that edge.

### New user-facing shapes

**Declarative** — fan-in is first-class:
```python
report = Node(
    'report',
    inputs={
        'claims':   Claims,
        'scores':   Scores,
        'verified': VerifyResult,
    },
    output=Report,
)
```

**Programmatic / runtime (LLM-driven)** — same shape, JSON-friendly:
```python
{
    'name': 'report',
    'inputs': {
        'claims':   'Claims',
        'scores':   'Scores',
        'verified': 'VerifyResult',
    },
    'output': 'Report',
}
```

**`@node`** — user code unchanged; decorator internals simpler:
```python
@node(output=Report)
def report(claims: Claims, scores: Scores, verified: VerifyResult) -> Report: ...

# Under the hood: Node(inputs={'claims': Claims, 'scores': Scores, 'verified': VerifyResult}, output=Report)
# No separate sidecar of param annotations. No raw_fn adapter. Normal scripted wrapper handles the dict.
```

### `list[X]` for Each consumers (the merge-after-fanout case)

When the upstream has an Each modifier, its effective state-bus type is `dict[str, X]`. Today, a downstream consumer must annotate `dict[str, X]` and call `.values()` manually. This is ergonomically wrong for the common 'reduce over fan-out results' pattern.

New compatibility rule: `list[X]` consumer is compatible with a `dict[str, X]` producer (i.e., Each-modified upstream). Runtime extracts via `list(state.upstream_field.values())`.

**Full compatibility matrix against an Each-modified upstream producing Y per item:**

| Consumer annotation | Compatible? | Runtime extraction |
|---|---|---|
| `dict[str, Y]` (exact) | yes | pass-through |
| `dict` (unparameterized) | yes | pass-through |
| `list[Y]` — NEW | yes | `list(state.upstream.values())` |
| `Y` (raw element) | no + hint | — |
| `dict[str, Z]`, Z != Y | no | — |

The element-type check is 'upstream's raw .output matches list element type'. Since every fan-out item is produced by the same node with a single .output, there is no cross-item variance to validate.

**Ordering caveat**: `dict.values()` preserves insertion order, but in Each fan-out that order is 'whichever Send arrived at the barrier first', not the original `each.over` collection order. Users who need deterministic ordering should use `dict[str, Y]` and key explicitly. The `list[Y]` form is for order-independent reductions (counts, aggregates, parallel summaries).

## What gets better

- **Fan-in validation for all three API surfaces** — not just `@node`. LLM-driven pipelines get assembly-time type safety.
- **One validator walker, not two.** Both surfaces walk `(upstream_name, expected_type)` pairs from `node.inputs`. `_validate_fan_in_types` in decorators.py either disappears or shrinks to a thin 'build inputs dict from function signature, delegate to the main walker'.
- **`factory._extract_input` simplifies dramatically.** Today: three branches (None, dict-instance, single type + isinstance scan) + a separate `_attach_scripted_raw_fn` path. After: one loop — `{name: extract_for(name, type) for name, type in node.inputs.items()}`. Each entry reads its declared upstream field directly; no type sniffing.
- **`@node` drops the `raw_fn` workaround.** Scripted fan-in nodes run through the normal `_make_scripted_wrapper`. The `mode=raw` log-line quirk documented in AGENTS.md goes away.
- **Consistent merge pattern for Each fan-out.** `verify: list[VerifyResult]` just works.

## Breaking changes (acceptable at 0.2)

1. **`Node.input` → `Node.inputs`.** Every `Node(name='x', input=Y, ...)` in the codebase becomes `Node(name='x', inputs={'somename': Y}, ...)`. Zero-upstream nodes use `inputs={}` instead of `input=None`.

2. **`Node.scripted("x", fn="f", input=Y, output=Z)` signature changes.** Rename to `inputs=` for consistency; accept a single-key dict or a type (we sugar the type case by using the field name as the key).

3. **Runtime extraction semantics change.** The old 'isinstance-scan state for a matching type' behavior is GONE. Every input names its upstream explicitly via the dict key. Implicit matching is no longer a thing.

4. **`@node`'s `.input` attribute disappears.** Use `.inputs`. Anyone inspecting node metadata updates.

5. **The dict-instance `input={'a': A, 'b': B}` multi-field form becomes the native case.** No semantic change for existing users of that pattern — it just starts getting validated.

6. **Schema change.** The Pydantic schema for `Node` has `inputs: dict[str, type]` instead of `input: type | None`. No one serializes Node today, so impact is internal.

- Keeping `input=` as a compatibility shim. We are at 0.2.0.dev; no deprecation cycle.
- Changing `ForwardConstruct` — `self.node(arg)` is single-arg at the call site, unchanged.

7. `_attach_scripted_raw_fn` in `decorators.py` DELETED. Scripted `@node` functions run through `_make_scripted_wrapper` like any other scripted node.

   - Fan-in via declarative `Node(inputs={...})` + `Construct`
   - Fan-in via programmatic `Node(inputs={...}) | Oracle(...)`

   - `list[X]` consumer + Each-modified upstream — end-to-end compile+run, validates type and extracts list

   - `dict[str, X]` consumer + Each upstream still works (pass-through)

11. Docs updated: README, website parameters.mdx, reference/api.mdx, walkthrough pages that show fan-in. CHANGELOG 0.2.0.dev entry documents the breaking change.
12. Full test suite passes. Zero regressions in the existing 223 tests (modulo the ones that construct `Node(input=...)` — those get mechanically rewritten to `Node(inputs={...})`).

## Implementation order

This is too big for one task. Break into subtasks:

1. **node-inputs-field** — rename `Node.input` → `Node.inputs`, update schema, update every `Node(input=...)` construction site (mechanical rewrite). Suite should still pass after this step — same semantics, different field name.
2. **validator-inputs-aware** — teach `_validate_node_chain` to walk `node.inputs` dict and validate per-key. Add the `list[X]` ↔ `dict[str, X]` compatibility rule in `_types_compatible`.
3. **factory-inputs-aware** — rewrite `_extract_input` to read named fields from `node.inputs`. Runtime extraction now deterministic per key.
4. **node-decorator-inputs** — rewrite `@node` decoration to produce `Node(inputs=...)` with all typed upstream params. Delete `_validate_fan_in_types` and `_attach_scripted_raw_fn`. Scripted `@node` functions run through normal scripted wrapper.
5. **list-of-type-consumer** — add end-to-end support for `list[X]` consumers of Each-modified upstreams, including the runtime unwrap and the ordering-caveat documentation.
6. **docs-and-changelog** — update README, website, CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md.
7. **integration-tests** — TestNodeInputs class, LLM-driven spec test, mode=scripted verification for fan-in, end-to-end merge-after-fanout example.

Each subtask leaves the suite green before moving on.

## References

- The current `effective_producer_type` helper in `_construct_validation.py` stays as-is and is reused in the new walker.
- The existing `TestEffectiveProducerType` (6 tests) keeps its contract.
