title: No cost/token tracking hook in LLM dispatch
description: NeoGraph's _llm.py invoke_structured goes through ChatModel.invoke() but provides no hook for consumers to track token usage and costs. Piarch has a CostTracker that records per-call token counts, but there is no way to wire it into NeoGraph's LLM path. LangChain responses include token_usage in response_metadata, but NeoGraph discards this after parsing the structured output. Consumers need either: (1) A callback/hook mechanism (on_llm_complete) that receives the raw LangChain response with token counts, or (2) An on_node_complete event that includes token usage from the LLM call, or (3) Support for LangChain callbacks passed through config (config[callbacks] is already a LangChain convention). Option 3 is the most standard — LangChain supports config[callbacks] natively. NeoGraph just needs to pass them through to ChatModel.invoke().
design: Enrich _notify_cost to pass node_name, mode, duration_s, total_tokens. Backward compat: add kwargs to cost_callback, existing callbacks that only accept (tier, input_tokens, output_tokens) must still work. Use **kwargs dispatch or a typed CostEvent dataclass. Core invariant: existing cost_callback consumers must not break.
notes:
## Research findings
Already exists: configure_llm(cost_callback=...) + _notify_cost(tier, usage) called at end of both invoke_structured (line 491) and invoke_with_tools (line 780). 5 tests in TestCostCallback.

LangChain config['callbacks'] ALREADY flow through — documented in _llm.py docstring. Consumers can pass Langfuse/LangSmith handlers via run(config={'callbacks': [handler]}).

Gaps to fill:
1. _notify_cost doesn't pass node_name (available at call sites)
2. _notify_cost doesn't pass mode (think/agent/act)
3. _notify_cost doesn't pass duration_s
4. _notify_cost doesn't pass total_tokens
5. No per-iteration hook in ReAct loop

The feature is NOT 'add cost tracking' — it's 'enrich the existing cost_callback with node_name, mode, duration'.
close_reason: cost_callback enriched with node_name, mode, duration_s. Backward compatible.

title: Expose agent-callable mid-node HITL interrupt (ask_human tool)
description:
## What
A first-class way for an agentic (mode='agent'/ReAct) node's tool to raise a TYPED human-in-the-loop interrupt MID-LOOP and receive the structured resume value — i.e. surface LangGraph's interrupt() from inside a tool/node, not only via the boundary-level interrupt_when/Operator that neograph exposes today.

## Why
Consumer (agent-stark) needs a research agent to pause mid-ReAct and ask the operator a decision ('found that person A left the company — remove / add-and-research / ignore?') then continue with the answer. Today neograph only supports interrupts AFTER a node (interrupt_when -> Operator -> interrupt(payload) -> human_feedback). LangGraph itself supports interrupt() inside a node/tool; neograph should expose it so consumers don't reach around the framework.

## Expectations after delivery
- An agent node's tool can call something like ask_human(payload: BaseModel|dict) that raises a typed interrupt and returns the operator's structured answer to the tool.
- The payload/resume contract is typed (consumer supplies the model), matching the existing human_feedback dict shape.
- Documentation of the replay-idempotency contract: on resume the node re-executes from the top, so any tool side effects before the interrupt must be idempotent.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: a ReAct node whose single tool calls ask_human; run to the interrupt, assert the compiled graph pauses with the typed payload; resume with a structured answer; assert the tool receives it and the node completes.
- E2E: a two-tool research node that asks a mid-loop question, resumes, and produces its typed output — asserting no duplicate side effects across the interrupt (idempotency).

## Acceptance
- Public API to raise a typed interrupt from within an agent node's tool loop and receive the resume value.
- Boundary interrupt behavior unchanged; existing tests green.
- Docs cover the payload/resume typing and the replay-idempotency footgun.
- Discovered during agent-stark Layer-1 interaction-protocol design (ADR-0007); V1 uses boundary interrupts, this unblocks mid-research decisions in V2.
notes:
## Now Phase D of epic neograph-w74k (mid-loop HITL) — scoped Level A 2026-07-02
Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.4. Ships at LEVEL A (document the idempotency footgun; costly/mutating tool calls before ask_human re-execute on resume). Independent of async — interrupt/resume already works under run(); tool-exec site and dispatch have no broad except (GraphInterrupt propagates).
ADD Level A.5 lint (review M3): flag ask_human in an act-mode node (mutations) — and/or a mutating-tool call preceding ask_human in the same node. Converts 'document the footgun' into 'catch it', keyed on the existing agent(read-only)/act(mutation) mode distinction. Note: today's interrupt() lives in a dedicated micro-node (operator_check, no re-exec problem); ask_human deep in a fat agent node is categorically more dangerous.
Level B (true replay-safety) is DEFERRED — research delivered: docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md (step- vs node-granularity; Level B = checkpoint-keyed step-memo layer in the tool loop, built only when a real consumer needs it and Phase 1 has landed). Level A->B compat: Level B must preserve results for tools idempotent under Level A.
Coordinate _tool_loop.py edits with Phases 1/3.
RE-SCOPE 2026-07-03 (three-layer audit; MECHANISM REPLACED). Design source: docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md sections 2.4 and 3.3; concern-disposition table in the audit.

Was: HITL Level A (document idempotency) + A.5 lint. Is: AGENT-AS-SUBGRAPH — compile agent/act mode to an agent-node/tool-node subgraph (LangGraph create_react_agent shape) instead of the while-True loop inside one node body (_tool_loop.py sync 402-580, async 635-788).

THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION (make this first, everything follows): message history, budget/iteration counters (ToolBudgetTracker is in-memory today and would reset on per-turn checkpoints), and tool_log become SUBGRAPH STATE CHANNELS (add_messages-style accumulation). With that: the hard cluster (final parse + structured fallback chain + usage summation — all need full message history) becomes an ordinary parse node reading state; the guard/unbind dance becomes conditional edges; preambles become compile-time seed messages.

WHAT THIS BUYS SIMULTANEOUSLY: (a) per-turn checkpoints — Level-A interrupt at turn boundaries becomes correct BY CONSTRUCTION, idempotency documentation unnecessary at the boundary; (b) tool-gating HITL (approve BEFORE side effects — the promise human-in-the-loop.mdx line 6 already makes and the current architecture cannot deliver) via Operator on the tool node; (c) agent token streaming (the loop is supersteps, visible to astream); (d) honest budget enforcement at turn granularity; (e) @task-per-tool-call journaling (Temporal-lite per the replay research doc) becomes reachable later.

BLAST RADIUS (known, concentrated): about 50-70 internal-reaching tests rewrite — 49 direct invoke_with_tools calls in tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py, 16 observability-contract reaches, GuardFake/StubbornFake become edge-routing tests; roughly 360 lines of while-body + fallback tail in _tool_loop.py die; _prepare_tool_loop/_finish_tool_loop/_CoercingToolWrapper survive. Everything through run()/arun() and all examples survive (assert on final typed output).

The A.5 lint survives re-targeted: during migration it warns on agent/act + Operator without subgraph compile; retires when migration completes. DEPENDS on neograph-q8ec (streaming verbs expose the per-turn supersteps this creates). 6-cell coverage rule applies — this is an IR-level behavioral change.
DESIGN DECISION (2026-07-03, executor research pass) — agent-as-subgraph

LOAD-BEARING DECISION (settled): message history, tool_log, and budget/iteration
counters (ToolBudgetTracker state, loop_count, cumulative_input_tokens) become
STATE CHANNELS with accumulation reducers:
  - messages:  Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add_messages]   (LangGraph canonical)
  - tool_log:  Annotated[list[ToolInteraction], operator.add]
  - budget:    per-tool call counts + iteration + cumulative_input_tokens as
               additive/last-value reducer channels (ToolBudgetTracker is in-memory
               today; per-turn checkpoints would reset it, so it MUST live in a channel).
With history in state, the hard cluster (final parse + structured fallback chain +
usage summation, all of which need full message history) becomes an ordinary parse
node reading state["messages"]; the guard/unbind dance becomes conditional edges;
preambles (output-schema + tool-budget) become compile-time seed messages.

SUB-DECISION (recommended, needs review gate): INLINE-INTO-PARENT expansion, NOT
nested-subgraph-invoked-via-wrapper. Expand an agent/act node into parent nodes
{node}__agent, {node}__tools, {node}__parse with conditional edges (ReAct cycle +
guard routing), mirroring how _add_each_nodes/_add_oracle_nodes/_add_branch already
expand one IR node into several parent StateGraph nodes with reducer channels.
Rationale:
  1. Turns become REAL parent supersteps -> turn-boundary interrupt correct BY
     CONSTRUCTION (the ticket's core goal); no dependence on interrupt-propagation-
     through-an-invoked-child (the open §2.5.2 question) which nested would inherit.
  2. Tool-gating HITL = existing _add_operator_check attaches to the real {node}__tools
     node boundary directly.
  3. Agent token streaming: turns visible to astream natively (no subgraphs=True).
  4. Introduces NO new engine execution verbs (.invoke/.astream on a COMPILED graph):
     the inline nodes call the LLM via llm.invoke(messages) which §2.1 already
     classifies as Layer-2 node-internal cognition, NOT an engine verb. => ZERO
     interaction with neograph-521j's guard. (Nested route would need one
     sub_graph.invoke() and a §3.5 allowlist entry.)
  Cost: the message/tool_log/budget channels are namespaced parent-state fields
  ({node}__messages etc.) — honest state bloat, same pattern Each/Oracle already use.

CONCERN DISPOSITION (made concrete against current _tool_loop.py):
  - output-schema + tool-budget preambles (_prepare_tool_loop L250-265) -> compile-time seed messages
  - tool instantiation + _CoercingToolWrapper bind (L267-279)            -> compile-time (bind once)
  - LLM call (invoke L404 / ainvoke L655)                                -> {node}__agent body
  - tool dispatch (tool_fn.invoke L463 / ainvoke L709)                   -> {node}__tools body
  - no-tool-calls exit (L411)                                            -> conditional edge agent->parse
  - guard/unbind dance (_guard_fired, rebind, L511-536)                  -> conditional edges (force-final path)
  - tool_log / budget counters / iteration+token guards                 -> STATE CHANNELS (the decision)
  - final parse + fallback chain + usage sum (_finish_tool_loop + tail L538-598) -> {node}__parse reading state["messages"]

KEPT HELPERS (survive as node bodies / compile-time builders):
  _prepare_tool_loop, _finish_tool_loop, _CoercingToolWrapper,
  _render_tool_result_for_llm, string-args coercion helpers.
DIES: ~360 lines of while-True bodies + parse-fallback tails (sync+async).

BLAST RADIUS: ~50-70 internal-reaching tests rewrite (49 direct invoke_with_tools
calls in tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py; 16 observability-contract reaches;
GuardFake/StubbornFake become edge-routing tests). run()/arun() + all examples
survive (assert on final typed output). 6-cell coverage applies (IR-level change).

GUARD COORDINATION (neograph-521j): inline route introduces NO compiled-graph
engine verbs -> no allowlist entry needed. If review flips to nested, add a §3.5-style
allowlist entry for the wrapper-invoke.
DESIGN ADDENDUM (2026-07-03) — INLINE LOCKED + 3 BINDING CONDITIONS (architect review)

DECISION LOCKED: INLINE (Option A). Expand an agent/act node into parent nodes
{node}__agent / {node}__tools / {node}__parse + conditional edges, mirroring the four
healthy expanders (_add_each / _add_oracle / _add_branch / _add_loop_back_edge).
Deciding win: NO new ENGINE VERB (LLM stays llm.invoke(messages); zero neograph-521j
impact). NESTED rejected: it would stake the keystone on §2.5.2's OPEN interrupt-
propagation-through-invoked-child question, adjacent to three filed subconstruct
defects (no async twin, checkpointer=None branch-arm threading, layer inversion).

BINDING CONDITION 1 — it IS a new compiler mechanism; own it.
"No new engine verb" is true; "no new compiler work" is FALSE. Adding _add_agent_cycle
(the compiler's most complex expander): a 3-way router with loopback —
  {node}__agent --(tool_calls)--> {node}__tools --> back to {node}__agent
  {node}__agent --(no tool_calls)--> {node}__parse
  {node}__agent --(budget/iter exhausted)--> FORCED {node}__parse (or error)
§2.4's hard cluster (final parse + structured fallback needing full history) relocates
into {node}__parse reading state[messages]. THE BUDGET-EXHAUST -> FORCED-FINALIZE EDGE
is where a bug will hide. Required tests: three-surface parity + turn-boundary-interrupt
E2E (the keystone) + a DEDICATED budget-exhaust-forced-parse E2E. (Scoped into m6d3.2.)

BINDING CONDITION 2 — agent state channels MUST be neo_-prefixed.
The state-channel decision settled that messages/tool_log/counters become channels but
NOT their naming. Plain names ({node}__messages) would LEAK full message history +
counters into (a) the returned state dict (_strip_internals only strips neo_*,
runner.py:388/454/626) and (b) the schema fingerprint (compute_schema_fingerprint
excludes neo_*, state.py:327). BINDING: add a StateKeys.agent_messages(field) /
agent_tool_log(field) / agent_budget(field) family under the neo_ prefix, mirroring
oracle_collector (neo_oracle_{field}) EXACTLY. Add a no-leak assertion (no neo_-internal
agent channel in returned state) to the keystone/parse tests. (Scoped into m6d3.2;

design:
## Core Invariant
An agent/act node's ReAct turns are REAL parent supersteps ({node}__agent / {node}__tools /
{node}__parse) with all mutable loop state in neo_-prefixed channels — so every payoff
(tool-gating, streaming, honest budgets) must be delivered by acting on those real nodes
and channels, NEVER by reintroducing in-node loop logic or leaking non-neo_ state.

## ORCHESTRATOR DECISION (neograph-8unp.21 refine): execute COHESIVELY (a+b+c+d in one chain).
The research's SPLIT recommendation below is preserved for the maintainer's future reorganization,
but this execution keeps m6d3.4 whole — the chain's review/triage/write-test gates supply the
design scrutiny and TDD the split was protecting. Item (a)'s API (`gate_tools_when=`) was confirmed
by architect review to be a sound conventional default (mirrors the existing `skip_when` Node-field
pattern) — NO maintainer API decision required. Item (d) = doc-only. Two refinements folded in below
(steps 3 and 6), superseding the prior orchestrator commitments.

## Scoping Recommendation: SPLIT (research's original recommendation — see decision above)
The four sub-items have fundamentally different natures:
- (a) tool-gating = a NEW public feature: new API surface + new wiring in _add_agent_cycle
  + resume-payload typing + should_pass/should_fail fixtures + 6-cell parity + review gate.
- (b) streaming = TEST-ONLY assertion riding on existing stream/astream verbs + real nodes.
- (c) honest budgets = mostly a TEST (budget already checkpointed per-turn); optional mypy
  narrowing.
- (d) A.5 lint = a near no-op reconciliation (the migration-lint was never built).
Bundling (a) with the verification items would let (a)'s real API design get shortchanged
under a "payoffs" framing. RECOMMEND: split into
  m6d3.4a — tool-gating HITL (the real feature: API + wiring + fixtures + 6-cell).
  m6d3.4b — payoffs verification + lint reconciliation: (b) astream turn-visibility test,
            (c) turn-granularity budget E2E across a checkpoint (+ decide mypy narrowing),
            (d) confirm/keep ask_human_in_mutating_node lint, correct doc line 341-342.
Rationale: (a) alone touches production wiring and public API and carries the parent's
Binding-Condition-1 risk (the forced-parse/router edge); (b)(c)(d) are low-risk
verification/cleanup that pair cleanly and unblock rsd1 docs. If the user prefers finer
grain, (d) can be its own trivial ticket, but (b)+(c) should stay together (same keystone
harness). Either way (a) MUST be its own task.

## Implementation Plan
### Item (a) — tool-gating HITL [its own task]
1. Design the API FIRST (record before coding): how does a user declare "gate tools on
   this agent node"? Recommended: a @node kwarg (e.g. gate_tools_when=<condition>) that
   maps to an Operator-like condition carried on the Node, since the user cannot name the
   synthesized {node}__tools. Decide the resume-payload contract (boolean-approve like
   Operator, vs a typed value that can rewrite tool args) — pin the typing.
2. REUSE the interrupt() body from _add_operator_check (_wiring.py:773-795), do NOT invent a
   new interrupt path. Add a gate node inside _add_agent_cycle so the router's `tools` arm
   goes agent -> {node}__tools_gate -> {node}__tools; the gate calls interrupt(payload) when
   the condition fires and writes StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK on resume. (Fallback if a
   condition is not needed: pass interrupt_before=[names.tools] at graph.compile()
   compiler.py:275 — but prefer the conditional gate for parity with Operator.)
3. VALIDATOR RULE (refine .21, MEDIUM-2): the should_fail fixture needs a REAL assembly-time
   rule to fire against. Add a validator: gate_tools_when set on a NON-agent/act node raises
   ConstructError at assembly (it only makes sense where a {node}__tools node exists). Place it
   where node-config validation lives (_construct_validation.py or the decorator-layer assembly
   that already validates agent/act config). The should_fail fixture triggers THIS rule.
   Fixtures: should_pass (gate approves, tool runs once, on an agent node) + should_fail
   (gate_tools_when on a scripted/think node -> ConstructError). 6-cell parity (@node /
   declarative / programmatic) per the three-surface rule. Keystone-style E2E: gate pauses
   BEFORE the side-effecting tool; assert the tool did NOT run pre-approval (counter==0 at
   pause), runs exactly once after resume.

### Item (b) — agent token streaming [verification task]
4. Add an astream test (reuse tests/test_resume_stream.py harness): drive a 2-turn fake
   agent with stream_mode="updates"; assert distinct {node}__agent and {node}__tools
   superstep updates appear (turns are visible). Optionally assert stream_mode="messages"
   surfaces AI turns. No production change expected; if a gap surfaces, fix in runner.py
   verbs only (never in _agent_cycle bodies).

### Item (c) — honest budgets at turn granularity across a checkpoint [verification task]
5. Reuse tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:310 budget-exhaust exemplar + the
   MemorySaver interrupt/resume harness. Add a checkpoint/resume mid-cycle and assert
   budget (iteration count, per-tool calls in neo_agent_budget_{field}) does NOT reset and
   forced-finalize still fires honestly post-resume. Assert no neo_-internal agent channel
   leaks into the returned state (Binding Condition 2, reuse the keystone no-leak assertion
   at test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:231-241).
6. TWO BASELINE MYPY ERRORS (_agent_cycle.py:162, testing.py:65) — REFINE .21 (MEDIUM-1),
   supersedes the prior 'widen ToolBudgetTracker' plan which is a BAND-AID. Root cause: node.tools
   is typed list[Tool|BaseTool] but _normalize_raw_base_tools converts every BaseTool->Tool at Node
   construction (node.py:180-192), so at these seams the list is ALWAYS list[Tool] at runtime.
   Widening ToolBudgetTracker + getattr(tool,'budget',0) guard would create a DEAD branch and mask
   that normalization invariant. CORRECT FIX: keep ToolBudgetTracker typed list[Tool]; at the two
   seams use a localized cast(list[Tool], node.tools) — or add a `normalized_tools` property on Node
   returning list[Tool] and use it at both seams. Also fixes testing.py:65 (tool.budget then resolves
   on Tool). Clears both baseline mypy errors WITHOUT masking the invariant. (tool.py:60 read-only
   error is a separate frozen-model PrivateAttr issue, NOT in m6d3.4 scope — leave as baseline.)

### Item (d) — A.5 lint reconciliation [trivial]
7. Confirm (grep) no "agent/act + Operator without subgraph" lint exists — it never did.
   KEEP _check_ask_human_in_mutating_node (lint.py:273, kind="ask_human_in_mutating_node")
   unchanged — it is the p8wz safety net, unrelated to migration. Correct
   docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md:341-342 to state the transitional lint
   was unnecessary because the migration landed atomically. NEEDS USER INPUT: confirm this
   disposition (doc-correction only) vs actually building+retiring a pointless transitional
   lint — recommend doc-correction only.
notes:
## Findings (research pass, code-verified 2026-07-04)

### 1. Agent-as-subgraph structure (foundational — landed ddc9461/f81ff12)
An agent/act node expands INLINE-INTO-PARENT into THREE real parent StateGraph nodes
(the create_react_agent shape), mirroring _add_each/_add_oracle/_add_branch/_add_loop:
- Names come from `cycle_names(node_name)` — `_agent_cycle.py:76-81`:
  `{node}__agent`, `{node}__tools`, `{node}__parse`. YES, there is literally a
  `{node}__tools` node.
- Topology owner: `_add_agent_cycle` — `_wiring.py:728-770`. add_node for the three
  bodies at `_wiring.py:754-756` (**tools node added at `_wiring.py:755`**). 3-way
  conditional router `agent -> [tools, parse]` at `_wiring.py:764-766`; ReAct loopback
  `tools -> agent` edge at `_wiring.py:768`. Returns `names.parse` as the region's exit.
- Node bodies + router live in `make_agent_cycle_bodies` — `_agent_cycle.py:227-459`
  (sync+async agent/tools/parse + `router` at `_agent_cycle.py:289-299`). LLM call is
  `caller.invoke(messages)` (`_agent_cycle.py:261`) — Layer-2 cognition, NOT an engine verb.
- Compiler dispatch: `_add_node_to_graph` match, `compiler.py:525-528` — combo
  `BARE|OPERATOR` + `node.mode in ("agent","act")` -> `_add_agent_cycle`. Each/Oracle/Loop
  OVER an agent node is a deliberate CompileError (`compiler.py:194-221`, m6d3.6 tracks fix).
- State channels (neo_-prefixed, Binding Condition 2): `StateKeys.agent_messages/
  agent_tool_log/agent_budget` -> `neo_agent_messages_{field}` etc. (`_state_keys.py:97-116`).
  Written back every superstep: agent_body returns `{msgs_key, budget_key}`
  (`_agent_cycle.py:265`); tools_body returns `{msgs_key, tlog_key, budget_key}`
  (`_agent_cycle.py:368`). This is what makes turn-boundary interrupt correct by construction.

### 2. (a) TOOL-GATING — needs NEW WIRING + NEW API; reuses the interrupt() body pattern
- Today an Operator on an agent node is combo `OPERATOR` -> `_add_agent_cycle` (returns
  `names.parse`) THEN `_add_operator_check(graph, names.parse, ...)` at `compiler.py:543-544`.
  So the interrupt fires AFTER the whole cycle (node boundary, after parse) — this is the
  OLD "review finished output" behavior, NOT gating before tool side effects.
- To approve BEFORE side effects, the interrupt must fire before the `{node}__tools` BODY
  runs. Because `{node}__tools` is now a REAL superstep parent node (the migration payoff),
  this is finally structurally possible (impossible in the monolith).
- REUSE target: `_add_operator_check` body pattern — `_wiring.py:773-795`
  (`interrupt(should_pause)` + `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK`). Two candidate mechanisms:
  (i) Insert a gate node between the router and tools: route `agent -> {node}__tools_gate
      -> {node}__tools`, gate body calls `interrupt(payload)` when a condition fires.
      Reuses the interrupt/condition_fn/HUMAN_FEEDBACK pattern verbatim; NEW wiring in
      `_add_agent_cycle` (add gate node + reroute the router's `tools` arm through it).
  (ii) LangGraph-native `interrupt_before=[f"{node}__tools"]` at `graph.compile()`
      (`compiler.py:275`, currently no interrupt_before passed) — unconditional, no
      per-call payload/condition. Weaker.
- BLOCKER either way: the user cannot name the synthesized `{node}__tools`, so a NEW API
  surface is required (e.g. a `@node(gate_tools_when=...)` kwarg mapping to a condition, or
  extended Operator semantics). This is a genuine feature with a design decision + review
  gate + should_pass/should_fail fixtures + 6-cell parity — NOT a test-only item.

### 3. (b) STREAMING — almost certainly TEST-ONLY (no code change)
- `stream`/`astream` verbs already pass `stream_mode` straight through to
  `graph.stream/astream` — `runner.py:521-546` (sync), `runner.py:696-721` (async).
  `_finalize_chunk` (`runner.py:461-476`) strips neo_* only for values/updates.
- Because agent/tools/parse are now REAL parent nodes, each ReAct turn IS a superstep:
  visible via `stream_mode="updates"` (one update per `{node}__agent`/`{node}__tools`
  superstep) and LLM tokens via `stream_mode="messages"`. This "falls out" of the migration.
- REUSE test infra: `tests/test_resume_stream.py` (real `astream` + `interrupt` + saver,
  `stream_mode=["custom","updates"]`) and `tests/test_streaming.py`. Assert per-turn
  `{node}__agent`/`{node}__tools` updates appear via astream (drivable with fakes).

### 4. (c) BUDGET — checkpointed per-turn ALREADY; item is E2E TEST across a checkpoint
- Budget is the `neo_agent_budget_{field}` state channel (`StateKeys.agent_budget`,
  `_state_keys.py:112-116`): dict `{iteration, cumulative_input_tokens, calls,
  forced_final, t0}`, initialised by `_init_budget` (`_agent_cycle.py:136-143`), rewritten

title: Agent-cycle: raise LangGraph recursion_limit to cover max_iterations*2 supersteps
description: Latent gap introduced by the inline agent cycle (neograph-m6d3.2). ReAct turns are now LangGraph SUPERSTEPS ({node}__agent + {node}__tools per turn), whereas the monolith ran the whole loop inside ONE superstep. LangGraph's default recursion_limit is 25, so an agent that legitimately loops beyond ~12 turns hits GraphRecursionError BEFORE the max_iterations guard (default 20) can force-finalize — i.e. the graceful forced-final edge is unreachable at the default max_iterations. Fix: set config['recursion_limit'] at invoke time (runner _prepare/_aprepare) to >= max(agent max_iterations)*2 + slack across the construct's agent/act nodes (config prep, not an engine verb — no 521j interaction). Not hit by current tests/examples (few turns, or max_iterations=3), but bites a real long-running agent. TDD: an agent that loops max_iterations>12 turns must force-finalize gracefully, not raise GraphRecursionError.
close_reason: Folded into m6d3.2 per leader decision. Runner _prepare/_aprepare now raise recursion_limit to a floor = 25 + sum over agent/act nodes of (max_iterations*2+3), only when below the floor (never clobbers a larger user value). CORRECTED understanding: a FLAT top-level agent does NOT crash at default (LangGraph's top-level invoke default is higher than 25); the real crash is a NESTED agent (sub-construct), where LangGraph applies default recursion_limit=25 to the child invoke — example 13's shipped shape. The raised top-level limit propagates into the child invoke, fixing it. Proven by test_forced_finalize_reachable_for_nested_agent_at_default_recursion_limit (run+arun) which fails without the floor (GraphRecursionError at ~turn 12) and passes with it. Full suite 2339 passed.

title: forward: Python 'for' loop support via Proxy.__iter__
description:
Add Python `for` loop support to `ForwardConstruct.forward()` tracing. The primary target is fan-out over a collection produced upstream — i.e. the same thing `Each(over=...)` does today, but written as a plain Python loop.

## Context

- Depends on conditional branching (subtask 4) because some loop bodies will contain `if`.
- Design: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` — "How control flow maps" (for section).
- Existing: `src/neograph/modifiers.py` `Each` + `src/neograph/compiler.py` `_wire_each`. This subtask should reuse that infrastructure, not reinvent it.

## Files

- `src/neograph/forward.py` — add `Proxy.__iter__` interception and loop-body recording.
- `src/neograph/compiler.py` — lowering path from traced loop IR to `_wire_each` (or an equivalent that reuses it).
- `tests/test_forward_construct_loops.py` — new test file.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `for claim in classified.claims: self.verify(claim)` traces into an `Each`-equivalent fan-out over `classified.claims` with `verify` as the per-item body.
2. Compiled graph topology is identical to the declarative equivalent `verify | Each(over='classified.claims')`.
3. Loop body with multiple nodes (`for x in xs: y = self.a(x); self.b(y)`) fans out the entire sub-pipeline, producing the same topology as wrapping both in a sub-Construct with `Each`.
4. Static-bound iterables (`for i in range(3): ...`) unroll at trace time — the body is duplicated 3 times in the nodes list.
5. Iteration over a Proxy whose source type is not a list raises `TracerError` with a clear message ("for-loops over non-list proxies are unsupported").
6. A loop inside an `if` (combined with the previous subtask) works.

## Out of scope

- `while` loops (harder; no obvious mapping onto LangGraph primitives — defer to a design discussion).
- `break` / `continue` inside the loop body (raise `TracerError` for v1).
- Nested loops (raise `TracerError` for v1; the user can factor into a sub-construct).
close_reason: for-loop via __iter__ lowering to Each (m8n, 4 tests) + try/except v1 pragmatic documentation (xi0, 4 tests). 195/195 passing. neograph-pub epic complete — all 6 subtasks closed.

title: _validate_type_spec is a no-op — dead code pretending to validate
description: node.py:31-38 — PlainValidator wrapping _validate_type_spec that accepts everything and returns it unchanged. The function checks isinstance for None and dict but returns v in all cases. Remove or implement actual validation.
design:
## Root Cause
_validate_type_spec accepts everything. The isinstance checks for None and dict are present but all branches return v without rejecting invalid types.

## Fix Approach
Add actual validation: reject non-None, non-type, non-dict, non-generic-alias values with TypeError. Check dict values are types too.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: test_validation.py::TestTypeSpecValidation::test_string_rejected_as_inputs, test_int_rejected_as_outputs, test_list_of_strings_rejected
- Root cause: _validate_type_spec (node.py:31-38) returns v unconditionally — never raises on invalid input
## Trace Similar
- Only 1 PlainValidator in codebase (the broken one)
- Other validators (_validate_n, _validate_over, _validate_skip_callables) actually validate and raise
- No similar no-op pattern found
## Architect Review
- Risk: LOW. The fix adds validation to a no-op function. No behavior change for valid inputs.
- Edge cases: generic aliases (list[X], dict[str,X], Optional[X]) must pass — they're used legitimately. Use inspect.isclass + typing.get_origin for generics.
- Triage: ALL_LOW — proceed to fix.

title: hydrate_resource_ref re-derivation ignores ref.kind — multi-link producer heals to WRONG resource_link
description:
INVARIANT: on the hydration replay path, re-deriving an expired ResourceRef MUST resolve to the resource_link whose KIND matches ref.kind. Healing must never silently substitute a different-kind blob.

DEFECT (verified by seat-3m6g via two live-server probes, root cause confirmed by maintainer in src): di.py:222 re-derives the fresh uri via _first_resource_link_uri(replay_result), which returns the FIRST resource_link regardless of kind. When the producing_call is a multi-link tool (the real demo server's get_deal returns [text, activity-history link, email-history link] — activity FIRST), healing an email-history ref reads the ACTIVITY blob and silently parses it as EmailHistory -> emails=[] (wrong data, no error). Exposed by the real FastMCP demo server via example 24 (neograph-3m6g); the shipped mcp_resource_fetcher replayer returns get_deal's whole content, so first-link != ref.kind.

FIX (anti-band-aid, kind-aware re-derivation): extract a single shared _resource_link_kind(block) derivation (currently inlined at _agent_cycle.py:456 as ) so lift-side and replay-side use ONE derivation and cannot drift. Add _content_blocks helper resolving the resource_link uri whose derived-kind == ref.kind. di.py replay becomes: kind-matched link -> first link (back-compat) -> ref.uri. NO band-aid in the example/battery.

TDD: failing regression test FIRST (multi-link replay result + email-history ref must heal to the EMAIL uri, not activity), verify red, then fix, verify green. Test in tests/modes/test_resource_manifest.py (NOT test_di.py — reserved for the concurrent prompt-surface seat). Parity note in docstring: hydration is surface-agnostic (FromResource DI runs the same for all three surfaces) so one hydration-level regression suffices.

DISCOVERED-BY: neograph-3m6g example-24 verification. BLOCKS: 0.6.0 (y5ux) — a featured example must not showcase a path that silently returns wrong data.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-rwion
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-rwion` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-rwion/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-rwion
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-rwion)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-rwion --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-rwion --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-rwion/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-rwion codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Structured output retry should coerce simple types to nested objects before failing
description:
## Problem
When BAML schema specifies `offstage_stakeholders: list[SupportingActor]` where SupportingActor has `name: str, role: str`, and the LLM returns plain strings like `["Software Architect", "Developer"]`, the validation fails with 'Input should be an object'.

The retry sends the validation error back but the LLM (DeepSeek R1) fails again — the correction message is lost in a 165K prompt.

## Expected behavior
Before raising ValidationError, NeoGraph should attempt type coercion:
- String → single-field object: `"Foo"  →  {"name": "Foo", "role": "Foo"}`
- This is the same pattern as JSON repair but for type mismatches

Or at minimum: the retry prompt should be more directive — show the expected schema for the failing field, not just the validation error message.

## Context
This happens consistently with DeepSeek R1 on large prompts (>100K chars). The model simplifies nested objects to strings when the prompt is long. NeoGraph's JSON repair handles malformed JSON but not type-level mismatches.
design:
## Reverted: _try_coerce_types was wrong approach

### Why the hack was wrong
1. Not generic — only handles list[str] → list[BaseModel] with all-string fields
2. Wrong layer — type coercion policy inside a parse-or-fail function
3. Treats symptoms — should let the LLM fix its own output via better retry

### Correct architecture: structured retry with schema context

The structured output pipeline should be:

1. **Parse** — _parse_json_response stays clean, parse-or-fail. No coercion.
2. **Diagnose** — On ValidationError, classify the error:
   - 'Input should be an object' on list items → LLM simplified nested to flat
   - 'Field required' → LLM omitted a field
   - 'Input should be a valid string' → type confusion
3. **Retry with schema** — _build_retry_msg sends:
   - The full describe_type(output_model) schema
   - The specific failing field's expected shape
   - An explicit instruction: 'nested objects must have ALL required fields'
   - Example of correct format for the failing field
4. **No coercion** — if retries are exhausted, fail with clear error. Do not guess.

### Implementation plan
1. Improve _build_retry_msg to include describe_type(output_model) schema
2. Add per-field error context: for 'Input should be an object' errors, include the inner model's field list
3. Increase default max_retries from 1 to 2 for json_mode/text strategies (structured strategy doesn't need this)
4. Add a test that verifies the retry prompt includes schema information
5. Do NOT add type coercion — the LLM must produce correct output

### Why this is better
- Generic: works for any type mismatch, not just string→object
- Right layer: retry logic belongs in _invoke_json_with_retry, not _parse_json_response
- Debuggable: the LLM sees exactly what schema it should produce
- No silent mutations: the output is exactly what the LLM produced, or an error
notes:
## Reproduce Findings

### Bug location
_llm.py:357 — model_validate_json raises ValidationError when LLM returns strings where Pydantic expects nested objects.

### Root cause
_parse_json_response does JSON repair (malformed syntax) but NOT type coercion (correct syntax, wrong types). When DeepSeek R1 simplifies `[{name: 'Foo', role: 'Bar'}]` to `['Foo', 'Bar']`, the JSON is valid but the types are wrong.

### Fix approach (two-layer)
1. **Type coercion in _parse_json_response**: On ValidationError with 'Input should be an object', try coercing string list items to single-field objects by filling required fields with the string value. Re-validate.
2. **Better retry prompt in _build_retry_msg**: Include the expected field schema for failing fields, not just the error message.

### Core invariant
_parse_json_response must extract a valid output_model from LLM text. Coercion is best-effort — if it fails, the original ValidationError propagates unchanged.

title: Add multimodal/vision support for image prompts
description:
Neograph should support image inputs in prompts for VLM (Vision Language Model) calls. Currently prompts are text-only. The image pipeline needs to send base64 or file-path images alongside text to models like Gemini 2.5 Flash.

## Requirements

1. Image as a first-class prompt variable — e.g. ${image} in inline prompts, or an image field in the prompt template
2. The prompt compiler converts image paths/base64 into multimodal LangChain message content (text + image_url blocks)
3. Works with standard @node(mode='think') — no special mode needed
4. Support both file paths and raw base64 strings
5. From the user perspective, it's just a prompt + an image — same ergonomics as text-only nodes

## Use case

The DiveMesh image pipeline VLM curation sends candidate images to a vision model for quality/relevance scoring. Currently uses raw ChatOpenAI. Should use neograph instead for consistent LLM wiring, observability, and retry logic.

## Possible design

- Detect ${image:variable_name} or ${image} in prompt template
- Resolve to file path or base64 string from input data
- Build multimodal HumanMessage: [{type: text, text: ...}, {type: image_url, image_url: {url: data:image/...}}]
- Fall through existing invoke_structured path (json_mode / structured output)
design:
## Core Invariant
Text-only inline prompts must produce identical output — the multimodal path activates ONLY when ${image:...} placeholders are present.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add _IMAGE_RE regex and _resolve_image utility (_llm.py)
- `_IMAGE_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{image:([^}]+)\}")` — matches `${image:field_name}` or `${image:field.sub}`
- `_resolve_image(path_or_b64: str) -> str` — converts file path or base64 to `data:mime;base64,...` URI
- Handles: absolute/relative file paths, raw base64, pre-formed data URIs (pass-through)
- Uses mimetypes.guess_type for MIME detection, fallback to image/png

### 2. Add _compile_multimodal_prompt helper (_llm.py)
- Called by _compile_prompt when _IMAGE_RE.findall(template) is non-empty
- Splits template on _IMAGE_RE pattern boundaries → alternating text/image segments
- For each text segment: run _substitute_vars to resolve remaining ${var} placeholders → text content block
- For each image segment: _resolve_var to get the value, _resolve_image to convert → image_url content block
- Returns `[{"role": "user", "content": [block1, block2, ...]}]`

### 3. Modify _compile_prompt inline path (_llm.py:258-260)
- Before existing _substitute_vars call, check `_IMAGE_RE.search(template)`
- If found: delegate to _compile_multimodal_prompt
- If not: existing fast path unchanged

### 4. Guard render_prompt inspector (_llm.py ~line 1014)
- If content is a list (content blocks), format as "[multimodal: N blocks]" instead of treating as string

### 5. Tests (test_inline_prompts.py)
- Test: ${image:photo} with file path produces image_url content block
- Test: ${image:photo} with base64 string produces data URI
- Test: ${image:photo} with pre-formed data URI passes through
- Test: mixed text + image produces correct content block ordering
- Test: multiple images in one prompt
- Test: text-only prompt unchanged (regression guard)
- Test: ${image:obj.field} dotted path works

### Files to modify
1. `src/neograph/_llm.py` — _IMAGE_RE, _resolve_image, _compile_multimodal_prompt, _compile_prompt guard, render_prompt guard
2. `tests/test_inline_prompts.py` — new TestMultimodalPrompt class
acceptance_criteria:
1. Inline prompts with ${image} or ${image:field_name} produce multimodal LangChain messages
2. Supports file paths (read + base64 encode) and raw base64 strings
3. Works with json_mode and structured output strategies
4. Existing text-only prompts unaffected (backward compatible)
5. Tests for the new multimodal prompt compilation
6. DiveMesh image pipeline VLM curation successfully uses it
notes:
## Research Findings

### Code Paths Affected

1. **`_llm.py:258-260` (_compile_prompt inline path)** — currently returns `[{"role": "user", "content": string}]`. Must produce content blocks for image prompts.
2. **`_llm.py:241-243` (_substitute_vars)** — regex replacement produces flat string. Cannot interleave image content blocks. Need a new function that splits template into text/image segments and builds content blocks.
3. **`_llm.py:195` (_VAR_RE)** — matches `${anything}`. A new `_IMAGE_RE` regex needed for `${image:field_name}` pattern.
4. **`_llm.py:555-557` (retry path)** — retries add `{"content": raw_text}`. This is fine for multimodal — retries reference text, not images. No change needed.
5. **`_llm.py:574-607` (_call_structured)** — passes messages through to `llm.invoke()`. LangChain handles content blocks natively. No change needed.
6. **`renderers.py` (RenderedInput)** — image fields referenced via `${image:X}` bypass the rendering pipeline entirely. `_resolve_var` is called on the `image:X` path to get the value, but the value is NOT rendered as text — it is converted to a data URI and placed in an image_url content block. No rendering changes needed.
7. **`_dispatch.py:_render_input`** — inline prompts get `ri.raw` (raw Pydantic objects). Image data (file path or base64 string) is a string field on the model, so `_resolve_var` can access it via dotted path. No change needed.

### Key Insight: Text-Only Fast Path
The `_IMAGE_RE.findall(template)` check at the top of the inline path means zero overhead for text-only prompts. Only prompts containing `${image:...}` enter the multimodal compilation path.

### Relevant Code
- `_llm.py:185` — _is_inline_prompt
- `_llm.py:195` — _VAR_RE regex
- `_llm.py:198-238` — _resolve_var (dotted path resolution, BAML rendering for BaseModel)
- `_llm.py:241-243` — _substitute_vars (regex replace)
- `_llm.py:246-260` — _compile_prompt (inline path)
- `_llm.py:574-607` — _call_structured (passes messages through, no content inspection)
- `_dispatch.py:217-236` — _render_input (raw vs rendered decision)
- `tests/test_inline_prompts.py` — 29 existing tests

### Risks & Edge Cases
1. **Image in template-ref prompts** — Not supported. Template-ref delegates to consumer prompt_compiler. Consumer can build multimodal messages themselves.
2. **Image field in RenderedInput BAML rendering** — Not a problem since `${image:X}` is a separate namespace from `${X}`. The image field is never passed through describe_value.
3. **retry path with multimodal initial message** — Retries append string-content messages. LangChain handles mixed content types in conversation history.
4. **render_prompt inspector** — Assumes content is string. Will need a guard for content blocks (display "[multimodal]" or similar).
5. **File size** — Large images (>10MB base64) could produce very long data URIs. Consider a warning.
## Architect Review

- [LOW] _IMAGE_RE pattern: `\${image:([^}]+)}` is clean. The `image:` prefix clearly distinguishes from text vars. No collision risk with existing `${var}` or `${var.field}` patterns.

- [LOW] _resolve_image utility: File I/O is acceptable in the compile path — images are typically <5MB, read once. The `mimetypes.guess_type` approach is standard. Fallback to `image/png` is safe.

- [LOW] _compile_multimodal_prompt: Splitting on _IMAGE_RE boundaries and building content blocks is the right approach. `re.split` with a capturing group gives alternating text/image segments naturally.

- [LOW] render_prompt inspector guard: Displaying "[multimodal: N blocks]" for content block messages is clean. No functional impact — purely diagnostic.

- [MEDIUM] Template-ref prompts: The design explicitly does NOT handle images in template-ref prompts. This is correct for now — consumers can build multimodal messages in their prompt_compiler. But the DiveMesh consumer may need guidance. Suggest: export `resolve_image` as a public utility they can use.

- [LOW] Layer discipline: All changes are in `_llm.py` (prompt compilation layer). No IR, compiler, or factory changes. Correct.

Overall: ALL_LOW
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_inline_prompts.py::TestMultimodalPrompt (7 tests)
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step)
- Tests: content block generation, file path read, data URI passthrough, mixed text+image ordering, multiple images, text-only regression, dotted path
close_reason: Implemented: ${image:field} in inline prompts produces multimodal content blocks

title: arch: typed schema for Tool.config (per-tool user config carries same dict[str, Any] smell)
description:
Child of ianf. Same pattern as rnjw/pej0 but for the `Tool.config` field -- per-tool user-supplied config dict forwarded to the tool factory.

## Current state

```
src/neograph/tool.py:37     config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
```

Flows to tool factory callbacks as `factory(config, tool_config)` at `_tool_loop.py:200-202` and `factory.py` tool construction sites. Consumers read via `.get(key, default)` (same pattern as rnjw).

## The bug class this closes

Identical to rnjw:
- Typos in tool.config keys stay silent
- Defaults duplicated across tool factories
- No schema for users to discover valid keys
- Pydantic validation would reject wrong types at Node/Construct assembly instead of at first tool invocation

## Design considerations

Unlike LlmConfig, `Tool.config` is naturally HETEROGENEOUS across tools -- one tool's config is totally different from another's. A single LlmConfig-style Pydantic model won't work. Two options:

### Option A: Generic on the Tool definition

```python
class Tool(BaseModel, Generic[ConfigT], frozen=True):
    name: str
    description: str
    config: ConfigT
    budget: int | None = None
```

Users subclass Tool or use `Tool[MyToolConfig]` with a per-tool Pydantic model. Typed all the way down but requires per-tool boilerplate.

### Option B: Factory-declared schema

Each tool factory declares its config schema; the framework validates the dict against that schema at Tool() construction. Less ergonomic but no Tool subclassing.

### Option C: Accept the dynamic shape

Argument: tool.config is genuinely user-open. Users writing custom tools decide their own schema. The framework doesn't read tool.config directly -- it's pass-through. So the None-bypass bug class may not apply here (no framework-level .get() sites).

**Audit needed FIRST**: does ANY neograph code read `tool.config[key]` with defaults, or is it purely pass-through to user factories? If pass-through, Option C is correct and this ticket closes as 'not a real instance of the bug class'.

## Recommended first step

Before implementing: audit all `.config` accesses on Tool instances across src/neograph. If all reads are `factory(config, tool.config)` pass-through (user owns the schema), close this ticket as 'accepted as dynamic'. If neograph itself reads keys from tool.config, proceed with Option A or B.

## Effort

- Audit: 30 min
- Option A (if chosen): ~4 hours; ripples through factory.py, _tool_loop.py, all @tool decorator call sites
- Option B (if chosen): ~6 hours; needs a schema-registration mechanism

## Dependencies

Child of ianf. No blocking dependencies.
design:
## Core Invariant

Tool.config is a pure pass-through dict between the user (who constructs the Tool) and the user (who registers the tool factory). The framework reads zero keys from it; no schema can be enforced because none exists at the framework layer.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: AUDIT (this atom)

Audit complete. Result: zero framework-side reads. Pure pass-through.

### Phase 2: Close as 'accepted as dynamic'

The task description explicitly authorizes this outcome:
'If all reads are factory(config, tool.config) pass-through (user owns the schema), close this ticket as accepted as dynamic.'

No code change is correct here. Forcing Option A or B would add type ceremony without closing any bug class.

### Phase 3: Collapse remaining atoms

The molecular workflow has write-test / implement / commit atoms downstream. Since no code change is required, those atoms close as no-op with reasons documenting the audit conclusion.

### Acceptance gates

- mlxg closed with reason 'accepted as dynamic; audit confirms pure pass-through'
- v2ey.11/12/13 (write-test/implement/commit for mlxg) closed as no-op
- ianf parent epic notes (if accessible) updated to record the disposition
notes:
## Findings (research atom v2ey.8)

### Audit: `Tool.config` access surface in neograph framework

**Search 1: `tool_spec.config` / `tool.config` reads in src/**
```
src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:205:    tool_instances[tool_spec.name] = factory(config, tool_spec.config)
```
ONE site. Pure pass-through to the user-supplied tool factory.

**Search 2: `tool_config[key]` dict-key access in src/ AND tests/**
```
(zero matches)
```

**Search 3: `tool_config.get(...)` accessor pattern in src/ AND tests/**
```
(zero matches)
```

**Search 4: `Tool(...config=...)` constructor uses**
```
src/neograph/tool.py:32  (docstring example: read = Tool("read_artifact", budget=10, config={"max_chars": 6000}))
src/neograph/tool.py:148 (the @tool decorator's Tool() instantiation: Tool(tool_name, budget=budget, config=config or {}))
```
No tests pass `config=` to `Tool(...)` -- searched tests/ and found no such call.

### Conclusion

`Tool.config: dict[str, Any]` is consumed exclusively by the user's tool factory at `_tool_loop.py:205`:
```python
factory(config, tool_spec.config)
```
where `factory` is the user-registered factory closure (`register_tool_factory(name, fn)`). The framework reads zero keys from this dict.

The bug class that motivated rnjw / pej0 (silent typos, framework default drift, late validation, per-call validation cost) **does not apply** here because:
1. No framework `.get(key, default)` sites can drift -- there are none.
2. No typo silently bypasses a default -- the framework never reads keys.
3. The schema is genuinely per-tool / per-factory; there is no single Pydantic model that can validate all tool configs.

The task description anticipated this outcome:
> Recommended first step ... If all reads are factory(config, tool.config) pass-through (user owns the schema), close this ticket as 'accepted as dynamic'. If neograph itself reads keys from tool.config, proceed with Option A or B.

### Risks of forcing one of the typed options anyway

- **Option A (Generic on Tool)**: `class Tool(BaseModel, Generic[ConfigT])` -- forces every test, every `register_tool_factory`, every `Tool(...)` call site to either use `Tool[MyConfig]` or accept the bare default. Big ripple, no benefit because the framework still doesn't read keys.
- **Option B (factory-declared schema)**: requires a registration-time schema, ties tool registration to Pydantic models, and forces piarch + future consumers to model every tool's config as a `BaseModel`. Cost is real; benefit is zero because the framework still doesn't validate.
- **Option C (accept dynamic)**: matches the actual semantics. Documents the contract clearly. Costs nothing.

### Recommendation

Close mlxg as 'accepted as dynamic'. The framework boundary is `factory(config, tool_spec.config)` -- the user owns both ends of that wire. No neograph-side code change is correct here.

### Optional follow-up (out of scope for mlxg)

Document Tool.config explicitly as "pass-through dict; tool factory owns the schema". Add a one-line docstring nudge in tool.py:37 if not already there. (Current docstring example at line 32 already shows the intended use case.)

### Three-surface check (N/A)

Tool.config does not flow through the @node decorator / declarative / programmatic surfaces in any framework-mediated way -- it lives entirely on the Tool instance, which is constructed identically across all three surfaces. The pass-through to the factory is the same.

### Existing test coverage

- tests/test_validation.py:1174-1212 -- Tool budgets and registration assertions
- tests/modifiers/test_compositions.py:310-340 -- Tool with budget in compositions
- tests/test_composition.py / tests/modes/test_core_modes.py -- factory closures of shape `lambda config, tc: ...` -- the `tc` parameter is `tool_spec.config` and is never read inside.

No existing test mutates or reads tool.config keys; no new test would close a real bug class.
## Architect Review (atom v2ey.9)

- [LOW] Finding: audit search coverage. The grep set covered tool_spec.config, tool_config[, tool_config.get(, and Tool( constructor sites. Not searched: dynamic getattr / getitem patterns, **tool_config kwarg unpacking, or pickled-config consumers. Suggestion: one more grep for 'tool_config' in any context to catch unconventional reads.

- [LOW] Finding: piarch-side consumption is unmeasurable from this repo. The Tool factory contract is documented, but if piarch reads tool.config keys, a Pydantic model would still close that bug class downstream. Suggestion: out of scope for mlxg; piarch can adopt Option A on its own tools without framework changes.

- [LOW] Finding: docstring nudge mentioned as optional follow-up. Confirm it's actually optional (not required to close mlxg). Suggestion: optional. The line 32 example already conveys the contract.

Audit conclusion validated:
- Single framework call site at _tool_loop.py:205 is pure pass-through.
- Zero .get(key)/[key] reads in src/ AND tests/.
- The bug class (typo silent, default drift, late validation) does not apply because there are no framework reads to drift against.

Verdict: ALL_LOW. The task description explicitly authorizes 'close as accepted as dynamic' when audit confirms pass-through. No code change is correct here.

Overall: ALL_LOW (close-as-accepted)
## Triage Verdict (atom v2ey.10)
Verdict: ALL_LOW (close as 'accepted as dynamic')
- Audit confirmed by review.
- Task description authorizes this outcome explicitly.
- Closing mlxg + collapsing v2ey.11 (write-test), v2ey.12 (implement), v2ey.13 (commit) as no-op.
close_reason: accepted as dynamic. Audit (atom v2ey.8) and architect review (atom v2ey.9) confirmed Tool.config is consumed only at _tool_loop.py:205 as pure pass-through to the user-supplied factory(config, tool_spec.config); zero framework-side .get(key)/[key] reads in src/ or tests/. The bug class (silent typos, default drift, late validation) does not apply because there are no framework reads to drift against. No code change is correct here -- forcing Option A (Generic) or Option B (factory schema) would add type ceremony without closing any bug. The task description explicitly authorized this disposition: 'If all reads are factory(config, tool.config) pass-through (user owns the schema), close this ticket as accepted as dynamic.'

title: Rec5: Node.outputs polymorphism normalizer
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §8 (Polymorphic Node.outputs / Node.inputs).

**Problem**: `Node.outputs` is polymorphic (`type | dict[str, type] | None`) and `Node.inputs` is similarly polymorphic. There are 18+ `isinstance(node.outputs, dict)` / `isinstance(node.inputs, dict)` callsites across `src/neograph/`. Each one is a place where:
- mypy can't help (`TypeSpec` is statically `Any` via `PlainValidator`)
- A future fourth form would silently slip through
- The single-type / dict-form / `None` trichotomy has to be re-derived

**Existing partial fix**: `_dispatch.py:239` has `_resolve_primary_output(node)` which is the start of normalization but only used in one dispatch path.

**Fix**: introduce a normalizer helper (suggested: `NormalizedOutputs` dataclass with `primary`, `primary_key`, `secondary` fields). Centralize the discrimination into one helper, replace 18+ isinstance sites with normalized access. `node.outputs` itself stays polymorphic for the user-facing API — the framework-side only sees the normalized shape.

**Same approach for `node.inputs`**: dict-form vs single-type vs None.

**Acceptance**: zero `isinstance(node.outputs, dict)` or `isinstance(node.inputs, dict)` checks remain in `src/neograph/` outside the normalizer module. Structural guard test enforces this.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §8.
close_reason: Node.outputs/inputs polymorphism normalized via _normalize.py; 18 isinstance sites replaced across _dispatch/_construct_builder/factory/state/_wiring/lint/testing/loader; structural guard added

title: Runtime graph hot-swap: emit Agent Spec -> validate -> recompile -> durable resume
description:
Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s1a (motivating use case). Demonstrate + provide a thin API for the payoff: a running agent whose graph is re-emitted as Agent Spec at runtime, recompiled, and resumed durably.

TIER 1 (no recompile): known path-set -> one compiled superset graph; LLM/router picks path via Command(goto)/Send/conditional edges. Durable + streaming intact. Agent Spec serializes superset + routing.

TIER 2 (recompile + resume): novel shape -> from_agent_spec -> compile-time VALIDATE (fail before execution -- the safety rail for machine-authored graphs) -> recompile -> resume same thread_id. LEVERAGES EXISTING checkpoint auto-rewind (_auto_resume_from_divergence): changed schema fingerprint re-runs only invalidated nodes, reuses checkpointed state. Do NOT rebuild rewind -- compose it.

DELIVERABLES: thin hot-swap helper (recompile-from-new-Agent-Spec on same thread_id + resume), an example, and a test proving (a) emitted-graph validation rejects a bad spec BEFORE any node runs, (b) resume after topology change re-runs only changed nodes. Depends on from_agent_spec import (neograph-01i0g); pairs with docs/example child (neograph-e3b4j).
design:
## Core Invariant
Tier-2 hot-swap must COMPOSE the existing seam -- route the new topology through from_agent_spec -> Construct.__init__(_validate_node_chain) -> compile(same checkpointer) -> run(same thread_id, auto_resume=True) so that (1) a machine-authored spec is type-channel-validated and fails BEFORE any node executes, and (2) the already-wired _auto_resume_from_divergence re-runs only fingerprint-invalidated nodes -- NEVER re-implement rewind, fingerprinting, or validation inside the hot-swap helper.

## Implementation Plan
1. THIN HELPER (compose, don't build). Add a new advisory-underscore module src/neograph/_hot_swap.py exporting one public free function (e.g. hot_swap or resume_from_agent_spec), wired through neograph/__init__.__all__ (public contract per CLAUDE.md naming policy). Body is ~3 lines: construct = from_agent_spec(flow); graph = compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer, **runtime_kwargs); return run(graph, config=config, auto_resume=True). Thread llm_factory/prompt_compiler/renderer kwargs through for LLM-mode nodes; add an arun/astream twin for parity. NO rewind/validation logic inside -- it is pure orchestration over loader+compiler+runner. Chosen module home avoids the loader->compiler->runner import cycle that putting it in loader.py would create (mirrors how _agent_spec.py sits beside loader.py).
2. EXAMPLE. Clone examples/19_checkpoint_auto_resume.py's all-scripted @node + MemorySaver + same-thread_id shape into a new examples/NN_hot_swap_agent_spec.py, but source the v2 pipeline via to_agent_spec(construct_v2) -> Flow -> from_agent_spec(Flow) (the round-trip), then hand it to the helper. The 'topology change' must change a node OUTPUT TYPE (add a field, exactly like AnalysisV1->V2) so the schema fingerprint actually diverges and rewind fires. Docstring must state the scope bound: think/scripted(+modifier) only; agent/act-mesh hot-swap awaits aa5gq (AgentNode import). Register it in tests/test_example_*.py if that harness auto-discovers examples.
3. TEST -- two proofs (new tests/test_hot_swap_agent_spec.py; reuse tests/fakes.py build_test_compile_kwargs/register_scripted). (a) VALIDATION-BEFORE-EXECUTION: build a deliberately type-mismatched emitted Flow (or a Construct whose fan-in types clash), give each node a body that appends to a module-level sentinel list; assert from_agent_spec(...)/compile(...) raises ConstructError/ConfigurationError/CompileError AND the sentinel list is empty (no node ran). (b) SELECTIVE RE-RUN AFTER TOPOLOGY CHANGE: copy tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py's per-node execution-counter style -- run v1 to checkpoint, hot-swap to a v2 whose changed node has a new output type, resume same thread_id via the helper, assert EXACTLY the changed node + its transitive downstream re-ran while untouched upstream did not, and the final result reflects the v2 schema.
4. THREE-SURFACE / FAIL-LOUD parity (cheap add-ons): assert the helper inherits the existing fail-loud contracts unchanged -- a hot-swap that leaves no rewind point raises CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) (runner.py:346), and an AgentNode-bearing Flow fails loud on import today (honest bound documenting the aa5gq dependency). Do NOT add band-aids to paper over the AgentNode gap; fail loud is correct until aa5gq lands.
5. DOCS: cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s1a and docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md (Tier-2 compose note) in the module + example docstrings; update website if a public helper symbol is added (CLAUDE.md website rule).
## Scope addendum (disease scan, 2026-07-23) — cite the in-graph gate exemplar
Disease scan confirmed all four seams (rewind=runner.py, fingerprint=state.py, spec-load=loader.py::from_agent_spec, in-graph reuse=factory.py) are SINGLE-SITED — zero duplication, no migration debt; mrb2y is a pure thin compose. Refinement: deliverable (a) 'validation rejects BEFORE any node runs' has a direct in-graph EXEMPLAR at factory.py:440-490 (make_portal_dispatch_fn._prepare): from_agent_spec(flow) -> Construct(...) validation raises ConstructError/ConfigurationError/ValidationError at factory.py:479-490 BEFORE compiled.invoke. mrb2y's helper is the OUT-of-graph durable sibling of that path — compose the SAME from_agent_spec + Construct gate (do NOT wrap in ExecutionError; raise the gate error straight to the caller), then compile(checkpointer=...) + run(same thread_id, auto_resume=True). Cite factory.py:440-490 in the helper docstring as the in-graph analog so the two stay a single discipline, never a fork. No new instances of the disease may be introduced (no bespoke validator/loader/rewind inside _hot_swap.py).

## Refinement addendum (architect review, neograph-hhgnz.30, 2026-07-23)
- FAIL LOUD ON MISSING DURABILITY (was a silent seam): run(..., auto_resume=True) with checkpointer=None short-circuits (_verify_checkpoint_schema returns early, runner.py:289) and silently full-re-runs with zero reuse — contradicts the Tier-2 durable payoff. The helper MUST raise ConfigurationError when checkpointer is None OR thread_id is absent from config['configurable'] (durable resume is definitional; the checkpointer-less path is Tier-1, a different feature). Assert this in the test.
- DELIVERABLE (a) BAD-FLOW AUTHORING (revised — the 'type-mismatched Construct' is impossible; Construct.__init__ self-validates so it never constructs): author the mismatch at the Flow/spec-dict layer — hand-build via pyagentspec OR mutate a valid emitted Flow's node output type to clash with a downstream consumer's declared input — then assert from_agent_spec(...)'s internal Construct(...) raises, with a module-level sentinel list proving NO node body ran. (Existing tests build Flows only via to_agent_spec; a hand-built/mutated Flow is new territory for the suite.)
- PIN THE RAW GATE EXCEPTION TYPE: deliverable (a) asserts ConstructError/ConfigurationError directly (the out-of-graph helper raises straight), NOT an ExecutionError wrapper (contrast factory.py:484's in-graph wrap) — prevents drift toward in-graph wrapping.
- WEBSITE + API-MANIFEST ARE MANDATORY (a public symbol is added via __init__.__all__): add the website page/reference AND regenerate scripts/gen_api_manifest.py -> website/src/data/api-manifest.json, else the verifiable-docs remark plugin won't autolink the new symbol. Run npm run build in website/.
- ASYNC PARITY PROOF: the arun/astream twins need coverage — mirror test_checkpoint_auto_rewind's sync+async style for at least one of the two proofs (rewind has async twins, _averify_checkpoint_schema runner.py:1036).
- PUBLIC NAME: use resume_from_agent_spec (describes emit->validate->recompile->resume) rather than hot_swap.
notes:
POINTER (KEYMAKER mode (b) shipped, epic neograph-t1f7z, 2026-07-14): Keymaker mode (b) runtime dispatch (emit neograph Spec -> validate -> compile -> invoke) shipped CHECKPOINTER-LESS in v1 (D-SCOPE). Tier-2 durable recompile-resume (emit -> validate -> recompile -> DURABLE resume across a checkpointer) remains THIS bead's scope. Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md.
## Findings (researcher: neograph-hhgnz.10, 2026-07-23)

REUSE TARGET (the whole point): the Tier-2 durable hot-swap is a THIN COMPOSITION of three primitives that already exist and already validate/rewind. There is NOTHING new to build in the rewind or validation machinery -- only a ~3-line orchestration helper + an example + a test.

The compose chain (data-flow trace of one hot-swap):
- run 1: Construct -> compile(construct, checkpointer=cp) -> run(graph, config={thread_id:T}). Checkpoint stores channel_values + StateKeys.SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT (fp1) + per-node fingerprints (nfp1) (runner.py:607 injects fp; compiler.py:333-334 stashes both on the graph).
- hot-swap: to_agent_spec(new_construct)  ->  Flow  ->  from_agent_spec(Flow)  ->  Construct2.  **Construct2 VALIDATES type-channels at Construct.__init__ (construct.py:194 calls _validate_node_chain) -- i.e. BEFORE any node runs, before compile.** Then compile(Construct2, checkpointer=cp) -> graph2 with schema_fingerprint=fp2, node_fingerprints=nfp2 (compile() adds the second validation pass: Operator/condition/checkpointer guards + compile_state_model).
- run 2: run(graph2, config={thread_id:T}, auto_resume=True). The EXISTING _verify_checkpoint_schema (runner.py:278) fires unchanged: get_tuple -> stored fp1 != current fp2 -> _compute_invalidated_nodes diffs nfp -> _auto_resume_from_divergence (runner.py:298) walks get_state_history for the OLDEST snapshot whose .next intersects invalidated, rewinds checkpoint_id, invoke(None) re-runs ONLY invalidated + transitive descendants. Async twins exist (_averify_checkpoint_schema:1036, _aauto_resume_from_divergence:1054).

So: the 'durable half' of Tier 2 is 100% already wired into run()/arun(). A hot-swap that routes the new topology through from_agent_spec -> compile(same checkpointer) -> run(same thread_id) gets validation-before-execution AND selective re-run for FREE.

Current vs deprecated: this is the CURRENT way. Portal/Keymaker mode (b) (epic neograph-t1f7z, shipped 2026-07-14) is the CHECKPOINTER-LESS v1 (emit->validate->compile->invoke, no resume). It is NOT deprecated -- it is Tier-1 (data-driven routing in one compiled superset graph). Tier-2 durable recompile-resume is the remaining net-new scope of THIS bead and does not touch Portal.

from_agent_spec COMPLETENESS vs aa5gq: from_agent_spec (loader.py:353) is COMPLETE ENOUGH for Tier-2 for think/scripted/modifier pipelines -- it reconstructs LlmNode(think), ToolNode(scripted), FlowNode(sub-construct recursion), and Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator via per-group markers. It FAILS LOUD on AgentNode (agent/act mode) at loader.py:376 (_reconstruct_primitive_node) -- that reconstruction is aa5gq's scope, NOT landed. => mrb2y's example+test MUST scope to think/scripted(+modifier) pipelines (exactly what example 19 already uses: all-scripted @node). A hot-swap of an agent/act mesh is BLOCKED on aa5gq, but the core Tier-2 payoff is fully demonstrable now without it. This is a partial, non-blocking dependency.

Tier-1 status: 'Agent Spec serializes superset + routing' is largely already delivered by Portal (mode a, Command(goto)) + the to_agent_spec exporter. mrb2y's net-new deliverable is the Tier-2 thin helper + its example + its test; Tier-1 needs only a demonstration that the superset+routing serializes (round-trip already proven by tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py).
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/runner.py:278 _verify_checkpoint_schema / :298 _auto_resume_from_divergence / :397 _compute_invalidated_nodes / :222 _decide_checkpoint_schema -- the durable-rewind machinery to COMPOSE, not rebuild. run():923 and arun():1134 already call the verify twin with auto_resume default True. Async twins at :1036/:1054.
- src/neograph/runner.py:346 _raise_no_rewind_point / :369 _raise_incompatible_schema -- fail-loud contract already covers 'no rewind point' and 'non-coercible change'. Tier-2 inherits these for free.
- src/neograph/loader.py:353 from_agent_spec(flow) -> Construct -- import gate. loader.py:363 _reconstruct_primitive_node dispatches LlmNode/ToolNode/AgentNode(FAIL-LOUD, loader.py:376)/FlowNode. Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator reconstructed from per-group markers. THIS is the 'validate a machine-authored spec' entry: the returned Construct's __init__ runs _validate_node_chain.
- src/neograph/construct.py:194 Construct.__init__ -> _validate_node_chain(self) -- the type-channel validation that rejects a bad emitted spec BEFORE execution. This plus compile() is the 'fail before any node runs' rail.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:567 to_agent_spec(construct) -> Flow -- the emit side (optional extra [agent-spec]). Use to serialize the running graph / build the mutated Flow.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:66 compile(construct, checkpointer=...) -- recompile step; :333-334 stashes schema_fingerprint + node_fingerprints on the graph (the diff basis). :174-201 Operator/condition/checkpointer validation runs here (second gate).
- src/neograph/state.py compute_schema_fingerprint / compute_node_fingerprints (_type_signature depth-fold) -- the type-based fingerprints. KEY: a topology change only fires rewind when it changes a node's OUTPUT TYPE (or field types). A pure edge/routing change with identical types does NOT invalidate -> that is Tier-1 territory (routing in the superset), by design.
- src/neograph/_compiled.py:102 CompiledNeograph.checkpointer property -- confirms the graph carries the checkpointer run() reads.
- EXEMPLAR (example): examples/19_checkpoint_auto_resume.py -- all-scripted @node, MemorySaver, construct_from_functions, v1/v2 output-type change, same thread_id, auto_resume True default + False strict. The new hot-swap example is this, with the v2 pipeline arriving via to_agent_spec->from_agent_spec instead of being hand-written.
- EXEMPLAR (round-trip): tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:90+ -- to_agent_spec -> from_agent_spec -> compile(build_test_compile_kwargs()) -> run pattern; uses tests/fakes.py (build_fake_llm_kwargs/build_test_compile_kwargs/register_scripted).
- EXEMPLAR (rewind assertions): tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py -- per-node execution counters asserting EXACTLY changed node + transitive downstream re-ran, untouched upstream did not; fail-loud no-rewind-point + non-coercible cases. Copy its counter-based assertion style for deliverable (b).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- FINGERPRINT-vs-ROUTING: rewind fires only on a type/schema fingerprint DIFF. The example/test's 'topology change' MUST change an output TYPE (add/retype a field, like example 19's AnalysisV1->V2) or the fingerprint is identical and no rewind occurs. A same-type re-route is Tier-1, not Tier-2 -- document this boundary in the example so the payoff is not miscommunicated.
- AGENTNODE BLOCK: from_agent_spec raises ConfigurationError on AgentNode (loader.py:376). Scope mrb2y deliverables to think/scripted(+Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator) pipelines. Agent/act-mesh hot-swap depends on aa5gq (not landed). State this explicitly in the example docstring and note it in the test (a should_fail-style assertion that an AgentNode Flow currently fails loud on import is a fair, honest bound).
- ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY: to_agent_spec lowers modifiers; from_agent_spec rebuilds via markers. To keep the (b) proof crisp, prefer all-scripted nodes (example 19 shape) so the round-trip is structurally trivial and the fingerprint diff is unambiguous. Modifier round-trip is already proven by test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py; do not re-litigate it here.
- HELPER HOME / IMPORT CYCLE: the helper calls from_agent_spec(loader) + compile(compiler) + run(runner). Putting it in loader.py risks loader->compiler->runner cycles. Mirror _agent_spec.py: a new advisory-underscore module (e.g. _hot_swap.py) exposed via neograph/__init__.__all__ (the public contract per CLAUDE.md naming policy). Keep it THIN -- no new rewind/validation logic inside it.

OR compile(...) raises (ConstructError/ConfigurationError/CompileError) AND the sentinel list is empty. That is the 'fail before execution' guarantee made testable.
