## Core Invariant
Runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS, never region interiors (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md): an agent/act mesh member's Portal-visible identity is its single declared entry (`{member.name}__agent`) and single reconverging exit (`{member.name}__parse`), never the interior `{member.name}__tools`/loopback nodes — every Command(goto=...) that targets this member, from any peer OR from the mesh's own static entry edge, MUST resolve through the entry, and every Command(goto=...) this member emits MUST originate from the exit, keeping the class of broken states (a jump into a ReAct cycle's interior) permanently unrepresentable, exactly like Portal already guarantees for atomic members.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Extract, don't duplicate, the Command-emission logic.** In `src/neograph/factory.py`, lift `make_portal_fn`'s inline `_to_command` closure (lines ~168-204) into a standalone, reusable factory.py-local function (e.g. `_portal_route_to_command(update, state, *, payload_field, route_field, valid_targets, channel_key, count_field, max_hops, on_exhaust, exit_name, node_name, entry_name)`), called from both the existing atomic-member wrapper AND the new agent/act path below. This keeps 100% of the budget/target-validation/channel-write logic single-sourced. G1 (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`) already forces this to live in factory.py — do not move it to `_wiring.py`/`_agent_cycle.py`.

2. **New factory.py function wraps the ReAct cycle's parse-body callables.** Add `make_portal_agent_cycle_fn(node, portal, entry_field, exit_name, *, max_hops, on_exhaust, entry_name, runtime, tool_factory_lookup) -> dict` in factory.py that: imports `make_agent_cycle_bodies` from `neograph._agent_cycle` (module-level import is safe — no reverse dependency exists), calls it to get the agent/tools/parse sync+async pairs + router, and returns a dict shaped like `_add_agent_cycle`'s `parts` PLUS Command-wrapped parse callables (parse_sync/parse_async wrapped so their returned update dict is piped through `_portal_route_to_command` before being returned). The agent/tools nodes and the 3-way router are UNCHANGED (reused verbatim — Mechanism 2 only touches the exit node).

3. **Extend `_wiring.py`'s mesh wiring via ONE shared helper, not a copy.** In `_add_portal_mesh` (`_wiring.py:723-788`), branch per member on `member.mode in ('agent','act')`. **COMMITTED (refine, neograph-vihe7.29): do not copy `_add_agent_cycle`'s ~95 lines wholesale.** Factor the shared agent/tools/router/loopback wiring (identical between the non-mesh and mesh cases) into ONE internal helper parametrized by `(parse-body builder, destinations=)`, called by BOTH `_add_agent_cycle` (non-mesh, plain dict return) and the new mesh path (Command-wrapped parse body + `destinations=` set on the `{member}__parse` add_node call, per LangGraph's requirement that any Command-returning node declares `destinations=`, mirroring the atomic member's `graph.add_node(member.name, fn, destinations=...)`). Only the parse node's registration (Command-wrapped body vs plain dict) and the `destinations=` argument diverge — every other line (agent/tools node registration, gate_tools_when arm, 3-way router, tools->agent loopback) is identical between the two callers.

4. **Build the entry-label map (Mechanism 1) scoped to the mesh**, as a DX-peer-name -> LangGraph-entry-node-name dict, computed once before the per-member loop: atomic members map to themselves (`member.name -> member.name`), agent/act members map to their cycle entry (`member.name -> f'{member.name}__agent'`). Use this map for (a) every OTHER member's `destinations=` tuple and Command `goto=` target resolution, AND (b) **the mesh's own static entry edge** — `_add_portal_mesh`'s `prev -> entry.name` wiring (`_wiring.py:783-786`) MUST ALSO resolve through this same map when the ENTRY member itself is agent/act (its real LangGraph node is `{entry}__agent`, not `entry.name`); this is not a separate mechanism, it is the same map applied to the entry as well as every peer. The agent/act member's own registration name stays `{member.name}__agent` (LangGraph node identity), while its DX-facing name for routing purposes is `member.name`. Build this as a plain local dict for nnds9's scope (mesh-local, not a graph-wide compiled artifact like schema_fingerprint — that graph-wide generalization is left as a code-comment pointer for do0d9/a37vk to pick up, not built here, to avoid scope creep beyond 'unlock agent/act members').

5. **Relax (narrow, don't delete) the D-MEMBER-MODES rejection.** In `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py`'s `_check_portal_mesh` (lines 96-104), remove the blanket `member.mode in ('agent','act')` rejection. Every other existing rule in the same function (uniform payload via `_declared_output`, route-field type/Literal check, dict-outputs-forbidden, contiguity, peer existence, single-mesh-per-level, entry-only `max_hops`/`on_exhaust`, reserved `handoff`-key typing) already reads `Node.outputs`/`Node.modifier_set` mode-independently and needs NO changes — confirm this with a should_pass fixture mixing agent+scripted members before touching anything else (guard-first: write the fixture, watch it fail against the OLD rejection, then remove the rejection). **The should_pass fixture set must include BOTH shapes: (a) a scripted entry + agent/act peer (tests peer-resolution through the entry-label map) AND (b) an agent/act ENTRY + scripted peer (tests the static entry-edge resolution from step 4b) — testing only (a) structurally dodges the entry-is-agent case (refine, neograph-vihe7.29).**

6. **Runner recursion-limit floor — concrete formula (refine, neograph-vihe7.29).** `runner.py`'s `_ensure_agent_recursion_limit` currently sums one `agent_cost` per agent NODE (via `iter_nodes`) plus `max_hops` per mesh — this budgets K hop-supersteps but an agent/act mesh member re-entered K times via mesh hops actually costs up to `K * (max_iters * 2 + overhead)` supersteps (each hop re-runs the full agent<->tools loop before the parse node ever emits its Command). **Pin the floor as: for each agent/act mesh member, multiply that member's per-cycle agent_cost by the mesh's max_hops (instead of adding a flat max_hops count), and add this to the existing floor calculation.** This gives the implementer a concrete formula and lets the checkpoint test in step 7 assert the floor is sufficient rather than guessing.

7. **Tests, guard-first per AGENTS.md convention:**
   - **CORRECTED TARGET (refine, neograph-vihe7.29): retire `tests/test_portal_validation.py:249` `test_agent_member_rejected`** (a unit test pinning the OLD D-MEMBER-MODES rejection) — invert it to assert the agent/act member now succeeds, or delete it if superseded by the new should_pass fixture. (The plan previously named a nonexistent check-fixture path `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/portal_agent_member_rejected.py` — no such file exists; `test_agent_member_rejected` is the real pin to retire.)
   - New `should_pass/portal_agent_mesh_member.py` fixture(s): per step 5, BOTH the scripted-entry+agent-peer AND agent-entry+scripted-peer shapes.
   - `tests/test_portal_validation.py` (or wherever mesh runtime tests live): new runtime test proving an agent/act member routes correctly (Command(goto) lands on the peer's real entry node, not a nonexistent bare name), the exit node reconverges identically to an atomic member's exit, the static entry edge resolves correctly when the entry is agent/act, and `gate_tools_when` composes with mesh membership.
   - New checkpoint test extending the existing Portal checkpoint suite: an agent/act member's hop spans multiple supersteps but is still resumable; hop counter persists correctly (only incremented once per COMPLETED hop, at the parse/Command-emission point, not per ReAct turn); recursion floor from step 6 is sufficient for a multi-hop agent/act mesh run (does not hit LangGraph's recursion_limit before max_hops exhausts).
   - Structural guard: extend or add a guard asserting no new `Command(` construction site outside `factory.py`/`runner.py` (G1 already covers this — just confirm the new code lands there, no new allowlist entry needed).

8. **Docs:** update `docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md`'s D-MEMBER-MODES entry with a forward-pointer to this task's resolution (historical record stays; **must keep the literal string 'D-MEMBER-MODES' present, per tests/test_portal_addressability_doc.py:102 which asserts on it (refine, neograph-vihe7.29)** — mark it resolved/superseded the same way D-LOWERING-DISSENT was marked RATIFIED in portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md), and the website Portal docs page (`website/src/content/docs/concepts/portal.mdx`) to remove/update any 'agent/act members not supported' caveat if one exists.

## Refinement applied (neograph-vihe7.29, 2026-07-16)
Per architect review (neograph-vihe7.12, NEEDS_REFINEMENT): (1) step 4 now explicitly resolves the static mesh-entry edge through the entry-label map when the entry itself is agent/act, and step 5's fixture set now covers that case; (2) step 7 retargeted from a nonexistent check-fixture to the real pin test_agent_member_rejected, and step 8 now preserves the literal 'D-MEMBER-MODES' string per the doc-assertion test; (3) step 6 now states a concrete recursion-floor formula instead of flagging without specifying; (4) step 3 now commits up front to one shared wiring helper instead of copy-then-maybe-merge.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Entry-node identity mismatch: if the entry-label-map mechanism is skipped and a naive implementation uses member.name directly as the Command(goto=) target for an agent/act peer, LangGraph will raise (no node named '{member.name}' exists -- only '{member.name}__agent' does) or, worse, silently mis-route if a differently-named node happens to collide. This must fail loud at ASSEMBLY validation time if possible (unknown peer), not only at runtime.
- destinations= tuple correctness: graph.add_node(member.name, fn, destinations=tuple(portal.to or ())+(exit_name,)) in _add_portal_mesh currently assumes every destination string IS a real add_node name. For an agent/act peer this must become the peer's __agent entry name, else LangGraph's own destinations= compile-time validation will reject the mesh at graph-build time with a confusing 'no such destination' error instead of a clean neograph ConstructError.
- Hop-budget interaction with the ReAct loop: each hop through an agent/act member consumes potentially MANY tool-loop supersteps (agent<->tools loopback) before the parse node ever emits its Command -- so Portal's max_hops (mesh-level hop count) and the agent cycle's own tool-call budget/max_iterations are two DIFFERENT counters that must not be conflated. runner.py's _ensure_agent_recursion_limit (per dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md section 6) already needs to add max_hops to the recursion floor for atomic members -- for an agent/act member this floor must ALSO account for the ReAct cycle's own internal supersteps per hop, or a legitimate mesh run could hit LangGraph's recursion_limit before max_hops is exhausted. This interaction is not addressed by the existing design doc and should be flagged during implementation review.
- Checkpoint/superstep semantics: an atomic Portal hop is one checkpointed superstep (existing invariant, dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md section 7); an agent/act member's hop is now THREE+ supersteps (agent/tools loop N times, then parse-emits-Command). Any test/guard that assumes '1 hop = 1 checkpoint' for mesh members will need updating to be mode-aware, or explicitly scoped to atomic members only.
- Operator/gate_tools_when interplay: D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO already forbids Portal+Operator on the SAME node. gate_tools_when is a DIFFERENT (agent/act-only) HITL mechanism that inserts a gate node on the tools arm INSIDE the cycle. Since it does not touch the parse node (the mesh-Command-emission point), it should compose freely with an agent/act mesh member -- but this needs an explicit should_pass fixture/test since it is a new combination that never existed before nnds9.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: none identified -- portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md is authoritative and internally consistent with dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md's D-MEMBER-MODES fast-follow framing; no doc/code contradiction found. The only open judgment call is HOW granular the entry-label-map artifact should be (mesh-local dict vs graph-wide compiled artifact) -- the design doc recommends graph-wide reuse for do0d9/a37vk, which this plan follows, but this is a scoping choice for the implementer to confirm is in-budget for nnds9 alone vs. deferring the graph-wide generalization to do0d9.

title: Deprecate single-type inputs= in favor of dict-form only
description: The senior architect review's #1 recommendation. _extract_single_type does O(N) isinstance scan of all state fields — first match wins, ambiguous when two upstreams produce same type. Dict-form inputs={'name': Type} matches by name, no ambiguity. @node already infers dict-form from function signatures. Deprecation path: warn on single-type inputs for non-first nodes, then remove _extract_single_type and InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE entirely.
design:
## Architect Decision: NEEDS_REFINEMENT — split into phases

### Analysis
The auto-normalize approach (inputs=X → inputs={'_input': X} at construction time) DOESN'T WORK at Node construction time because the producing node name isn't known yet. It must happen at Construct assembly time after topology is resolved.

The correct approach:
1. In _validate_node_chain, when encountering single-type inputs, resolve the producing upstream by type and rewrite to dict-form inputs={'upstream_name': Type}
2. Remove InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE and _extract_single_type from factory.py
3. Update EACH_ITEM classification (isinstance check on single-type path)
4. Update 179 test occurrences, 15 examples, 17 website pages

### Problem: scope too large for one task
- Auto-normalize requires _validate_node_chain refactor
- 179 test + 15 example + 17 website changes = massive churn
- Risk is theoretical (no real bug from type ambiguity yet)
- Only downstream user (piarch) uses @node exclusively (already dict-form)

### Recommended phased approach
Phase 1 (this task, minimal): Add DeprecationWarning when single-type inputs used on non-first nodes. No behavioral change. Signals direction.
Phase 2 (future task): Auto-normalize in _validate_node_chain at assembly time.  
Phase 3 (future task): Remove _extract_single_type, update tests/examples.

### Triage: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
Rescope this task to Phase 1 only (deprecation warning). File Phase 2+3 as separate tasks.
notes:
## Research Findings

### InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE references
- factory.py: definition (403), classification fallback (428), extraction (495-508), dispatch (523-524)
- test_structural_guards.py: guard tests (613, 633, 640-641)

### _extract_single_type (factory.py:495-508)
O(N) isinstance scan of all state fields — first match wins. Fragile: depends on field insertion order, can match wrong value when multiple fields have compatible types.

### Blast radius: HIGH
- 179 test occurrences across 40 files
- 15 example occurrences across 8 files
- 17 website doc occurrences across 11 pages
- Programmatic API (Node(inputs=X)) depends on it — documented as primary for LLM-driven runtime construction
- ForwardConstruct loop body wiring (forward.py:582) produces single-type
- EACH_ITEM classification path only works with single-type

### Cannot simply delete
Programmatic API surface depends on it. CLAUDE.md: 'the programmatic form is not legacy — primary path for runtime-assembled pipelines.'

### Recommended approach: auto-normalize at construction time
Convert inputs=X → inputs={'_input': X} at Node.__init__/validator time. External API unchanged (Node(inputs=X) still works). Internally always dict-form. Eliminates InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE, _extract_single_type, and EACH_ITEM isinstance-scan.

### Core invariant
Three API surfaces produce different inputs shapes converging through single validator + single runtime extractor. Removing SINGLE_TYPE requires either (a) converting programmatic/FC to produce dict-form (inventing param names), or (b) auto-wrapping single-type into synthetic dict at construction time.

title: @node: Oracle ensemble kwargs (ensemble_n=, merge_fn=, merge_prompt=)
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness). Surfaced by the Path A Dogfood epic.

## Problem

The Oracle modifier (`src/neograph/modifiers.py:127-156`) provides N-way ensemble + judge-merge via `node | Oracle(n=3, merge_prompt='rw/merge')` or `node | Oracle(n=3, merge_fn='combine')`. There is no way to attach an Oracle modifier to a @node-decorated function. Users writing LLM pipelines with ensemble-judge patterns cannot use @node.

Repro:
    # Desired
    @node(mode='produce', output=Claims, prompt='rw/decompose', model='reason',
          ensemble_n=3, merge_prompt='rw/decompose-merge')
    def decompose(topic: RawText) -> Claims: ...

    # Today
    decompose = Node(name='decompose', mode='produce', output=Claims,
                    prompt='rw/decompose', model='reason') | Oracle(n=3, merge_prompt='rw/decompose-merge')
    # Can't combine with @node at all — the Oracle modifier would have to be
    # applied after decoration, and neograph-jyw shows that modifier composition
    # on decorated nodes is broken (sidecar doesn't carry).

## Proposed API

Add three kwargs to `@node`:
- `ensemble_n: int | None = None` — number of parallel generators
- `merge_fn: str | None = None` — registered scripted function name (alternative to merge_prompt)
- `merge_prompt: str | None = None` — LLM judge prompt (alternative to merge_fn)

Semantics:
- If any of the three is set, attach `Oracle(n=ensemble_n, merge_fn=merge_fn, merge_prompt=merge_prompt)` to the Node at decoration time (not at construct_from_module time — the modifier is node-local).
- Validation at decoration time:
  - `ensemble_n` set but neither merge_fn nor merge_prompt → raise ConstructError
  - Both merge_fn and merge_prompt set → raise ConstructError (matches existing Oracle.model_post_init)
  - `ensemble_n` < 2 → raise (ensemble of 1 is pointless)
  - merge_fn or merge_prompt set without ensemble_n → default ensemble_n to 3
- The resulting Node carries the Oracle modifier in its `modifiers` list, same as the declarative path.

## Implementation sketch

In `src/neograph/decorators.py`:

    from neograph.modifiers import Each, Oracle

    def node(
        fn=None,
        *,
        mode='produce',  # or after q54 lands: None (inferred)
        ...,
        ensemble_n: int | None = None,
        merge_fn: str | None = None,
        merge_prompt: str | None = None,
    ):
        ...
        def decorator(f):
            ...
            n = Node(...)
            _register_sidecar(n, f, param_names)

            # Attach Oracle modifier if any ensemble kwarg is set.
            if ensemble_n is not None or merge_fn is not None or merge_prompt is not None:
                if merge_fn is None and merge_prompt is None:
                    raise ConstructError(
                        f\"@node '{node_name}' sets ensemble_n={ensemble_n} but \"
                        f\"neither merge_fn nor merge_prompt. One is required.\"
                    )
                if merge_fn is not None and merge_prompt is not None:
                    raise ConstructError(
                        f\"@node '{node_name}' sets both merge_fn and merge_prompt. \"
                        f\"Choose exactly one.\"
                    )
                n_copies = ensemble_n if ensemble_n is not None else 3
                if n_copies < 2:
                    raise ConstructError(
                        f\"@node '{node_name}' ensemble_n must be >= 2, got {n_copies}.\"
                    )
                # Use `|` to append the modifier (returns a new Node via model_copy).
                # Must re-register the sidecar on the new instance — see neograph-jyw
                # (sidecar carryover on modifier composition). This subtask assumes
                # neograph-jyw has landed.
                n = n | Oracle(n=n_copies, merge_fn=merge_fn, merge_prompt=merge_prompt)
                _register_sidecar(n, f, param_names)

            return n

## Acceptance criteria

- New tests in `TestNodeDecorator`:
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_with_merge_fn`: `@node(mode='produce', ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='combine')` end-to-end with a FakeLLM and registered merge function; result matches N-way ensemble semantics.
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_with_merge_prompt`: same with `merge_prompt='judge/prompt'`.
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_default_n`: `@node(merge_fn='combine')` without `ensemble_n` defaults to `n=3`.
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_no_merge_raises`: `ensemble_n=3` without merge_fn or merge_prompt raises at decoration time.
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_both_merge_raises`: both merge_fn and merge_prompt raises.
  - `test_node_decorator_oracle_n_too_small_raises`: `ensemble_n=1` raises.
- Oracle modifier is attached to the Node's `modifiers` list — verifiable via `node.get_modifier(Oracle)`.
- Integration tests from TestOracle still pass unchanged (this adds an API surface, doesn't change semantics).
- Update `@node` docstring with an Oracle usage example.
- Full suite stays green.

## Dependencies

- Blocks on **neograph-jyw** (Each interop via sidecar carryover) — the same sidecar-on-modifier-copy mechanism is reused here for Oracle. Do not duplicate the fix.
- Blocks on **neograph-q54** (mode inference) — for the docstring example. Soft dep, not hard.

## Files to read

- `src/neograph/modifiers.py:127-156` — Oracle class, model_post_init validation
- `src/neograph/decorators.py` — current `@node` decorator
- `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py::TestOracle` — existing Oracle test patterns
- `tests/fakes.py::StructuredFake` — LLM fake for Oracle tests

## Non-goals

- Do NOT edit `src/neograph/modifiers.py` — Oracle class stays as-is.
- Do NOT support Oracle on non-produce modes (ensemble over tool-calling is a different feature).

title: observe= opt-in: auto-attach Langfuse CallbackHandler (merge, no-clobber, no-op without keys) + flush in finalize; wire-or-drop the aspirational extra (GH issue 4, option A)
description:
From GitHub issue 4. VERIFIED: pyproject.toml:35 declares the langfuse extra; grep -rni langfuse src/ returns ZERO hits — the extra installs a package and wires nothing (aspirational-extra false advertising). Consumers must hand-attach langfuse.langchain.CallbackHandler to config.callbacks and remember to flush.

SCOPE (this is prepare()/finalize() territory — thin-verb-compatible per docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md, it merges config BEFORE the engine verb and never wraps the engine): (1) observe='langfuse' (and observe=True auto-detect) accepted by run/arun/stream/astream — decide run-level vs compile-level (run-level is right: the handler is per-run/per-trace; document why); (2) semantics per the issue, all three non-negotiable: gate on env keys present (clean no-op when LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY absent — never crash offline/CI), MERGE into config.callbacks (never clobber user-supplied handlers), flush on completion — which for stream verbs means flush after the generator is exhausted (and on generator close/cancellation — coordinate with the 51tr cancellation semantics), i.e. a finalize concern, not an exit line in each verb; (3) import langfuse lazily inside the observe path only — the extra stays optional, core import graph unchanged (function-local import allowlist entry + guard); (4) EITHER this lands and the extra is real, OR if rejected the extra gets dropped from pyproject — the current state (extra with zero wiring) is the bug; (5) example: observable_pipeline.py loses its hand-rolled handler attachment in favor of observe=True (keep the manual form documented as the escape hatch); website observability page updated.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED from the same GH issue — option B (native OTEL spans for graph lifecycle): EMPIRICALLY REFUTED premise. Probe 2026-07-06 (scratchpad cb_span_probe.py): a plain BaseCallbackHandler in config.callbacks receives on_chain_start for LangGraph AND every node (chain events: LangGraph, step-a, node_wrapper, step-b, node_wrapper) — the engine already broadcasts the whole DAG through its own callback abstraction; Langfuse v4 is OTEL-native so callbacks ARE the OTEL path. Building parallel neograph OTEL spans = the reinventing-runtime disease (same verdict shape as nmb2). Span HYGIENE is the real residue — see companion ticket.
design:
## Core Invariant
observe= is a per-run config merge that happens in the pre-engine brain (_prepare/_aprepare) and a finalize-time flush in the verb's finally — it MERGES into config.callbacks (never clobbers), NO-OPs cleanly when LANGFUSE env keys are absent, and imports langfuse lazily inside the observe path only; it must NEVER wrap the engine verb, add a compile-level hook, or import langfuse at module level (three-layer thin-verb principle preserved).

## Implementation Plan
1. GUARD-FIRST (per repo memory): write the NEW structural guard RED first — "langfuse imported only function-locally inside runner.py observe helpers; never module-level anywhere in src/." Model on tests/test_guards_examples.py `_third_party_import_roots` (AST third-party root extraction) + test_guards_sidecar_imports.py::test_no_private_langgraph_imports (src/ glob AST-walk). This enforces non-negotiable (3) and is currently UNENFORCED (the existing function-local allowlist only scans `from neograph...`). Put it in test_guards_sidecar_imports.py.
2. Add pure helper `_merge_observe_callbacks(config, observe) -> RunnableConfig` in runner.py beside `_mark_stream_custom`: resolve observe (None/False -> return config unchanged; True or 'langfuse' -> langfuse; unknown str -> raise); gate on os.environ (LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY [+PUBLIC_KEY] present, else return config unchanged); function-local `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler`; build a FRESH config dict merging the handler into a FRESH callbacks list (`[*existing, handler]`), handling list/None (and BaseCallbackManager via add_handler or documented-unsupported). Copy `_mark_stream_custom`'s no-mutation discipline.

title: Each fan-in validation double-skip: fan_out_param + _each_skip_used both fire
description:
When a node has both fan_out_param set (from @node decorator) AND has_each=True, the _check_fan_in_inputs validator double-skips unmatched keys. fan_out_param skips the fan-out receiver at line 416, but _each_skip_used remains False, so line 422-424 allows ONE ADDITIONAL unmatched key to pass silently. A typo in inputs dict is never caught.

Repro:
  n = Node.scripted('consumer', fn='f', inputs={'claims': Alpha, 'item': Beta, 'mystery': Gamma}, outputs=Gamma)
  n = n | Each(over='claims', key='value')
  object.__setattr__(n, 'fan_out_param', 'item')
  producer = Node.scripted('claims', fn='f', outputs=Alpha)
  Construct('test', nodes=[producer, n])  # should raise ConstructError for 'mystery' but doesn't

Fix: initialize _each_skip_used = True when fan_out_key is not None (the fan-out receiver slot is already consumed by the explicit fan_out_param).

Location: src/neograph/_construct_validation.py line 414

title: RetryPolicy support for LLM nodes
description:
NeoGraph-compiled graphs have no retry on LLM failures. The classic LangGraph pipeline uses RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3) on all LLM-calling nodes, which handles:
- Malformed JSON from json_mode (R1 occasionally produces broken JSON)
- Pydantic validation errors (LLM output doesn't match schema)
- Transient API errors (429s, timeouts)

Without retry, a single malformed JSON response crashes the entire pipeline. With retry, the node silently retries and usually succeeds on the second attempt.

Options:
1. compile() accepts a retry_policy= that applies to all LLM nodes
2. @node(retry=3) per-node declaration
3. construct_from_functions(..., retry_policy=...) at construct level

The rate limiter already handles 429 retries at the HTTP level. This is about node-level retry for parse/validation failures.

title: Oracle: generators use node.outputs type for LLM schema, but merge_fn changes the type
description:
When a node has Oracle(merge_fn=...) and the merge_fn returns a DIFFERENT type than what each generator should produce, the framework uses node.outputs as the LLM schema for each generator. This is wrong — the generator should produce its own type, and the merge transforms it.

## Concrete case

```python
@node(outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, model='reason', prompt='rw/decompose',
      ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='group_claims')
def decompose(read_node: ReadContext) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...

@merge_fn
def group_claims(variants: list[DecompositionResult], ...) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    # Takes 3x DecompositionResult, groups equivalent claims, returns ClaimGroupingResult
    ...
```

What happens:
- outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, so each generator's LLM call uses ClaimGroupingResult.model_json_schema() as the json_mode schema
- The LLM is asked to produce ClaimGroupingResult (which has groups: list[ClaimGroup] with gen_id cross-references) — impossible for a single generator to produce
- The LLM produces something that doesn't parse → generators return None/empty → merge gets empty variants → pipeline produces nothing

What should happen:
- Each generator should produce DecompositionResult (inferred from merge_fn's first parameter type: list[DecompositionResult] → element type is DecompositionResult)
- The framework should use DecompositionResult.model_json_schema() for each generator's LLM call
- The merge_fn receives list[DecompositionResult], returns ClaimGroupingResult
- node.outputs should reflect the POST-MERGE type (ClaimGroupingResult) for downstream consumers

## The type flow

```
Generator LLM call → DecompositionResult (per-generator type, from merge_fn signature)
merge_fn(list[DecompositionResult]) → ClaimGroupingResult (post-merge type, = node.outputs)
downstream node consumes → ClaimGroupingResult (from node.outputs)
```

## How to infer the generator type

The merge_fn's first parameter is typed as list[DecompositionResult]. The element type IS the generator output type. The framework can inspect this at compile time:

```python
import inspect, typing
sig = inspect.signature(merge_fn)
first_param = list(sig.parameters.values())[0]
# first_param.annotation is list[DecompositionResult]
element_type = typing.get_args(first_param.annotation)[0]  # DecompositionResult
```

## Impact

This blocks any Oracle where the merge transforms the type — the most common real-world pattern. The workaround (making generators and merge return the same type) forces unnatural API design.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test: test_oracle_generator_uses_merge_input_type_not_node_outputs
- Status: FAILING (confirmed bug)
- Log shows 'output=PostMerge' for generator calls — should be PerVariant
- Pydantic validation error: 'Input should be PostMerge' when PerVariant is written to collector
- Root cause: _resolve_primary_output(node) returns node.outputs which is the POST-MERGE type
- Fix locations:
  1. factory.py: _resolve_primary_output or the produce wrapper needs to use the generator type, not node.outputs, when Oracle is active
  2. state.py: compile_state_model builds the collector as list[node.outputs] — should be list[generator_type]
  3. compiler.py: _add_oracle_nodes could store the inferred generator type on the node or pass it to the factory
  4. Inference: inspect merge_fn signature, get_args(first_param.annotation)[0] = element type
## Trace Similar
- The same issue applies to gather/execute modes (not just produce) — _make_tool_fn also uses _resolve_primary_output(node)
- The state model collector type in state.py:_add_output_field (line 169) is Annotated[list[output_type], _collect_oracle_results] where output_type = node.outputs — also wrong for type-transforming merge_fn

## Architect Review
- [MEDIUM] Where to store the generator type? Options:
  A. Node field (node.oracle_generator_type) — requires node.py change (IR layer)
  B. Infer at compile time from merge_fn signature — requires compiler to pass it down
  C. Infer at factory time from merge_fn registry lookup — runtime overhead each call
  PREFER B: infer once at compile time, store result for factory use. The compiler already resolves the merge_fn. Use a new field on Node: oracle_gen_type.
- [LOW] State model collector needs the generator type too (list[gen_type] not list[output_type])
- [LOW] The @node decorator with ensemble_n= should also infer and store the gen type

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM is a placement choice, B is clearly best)

No test runs a real pipeline against a real checkpointer, mutates an output schema, resumes on the same thread_id, and asserts exactly the invalidated nodes re-ran. If _verify_checkpoint_schema stopped calling _auto_resume_from_divergence, ALL THREE units still pass. Add the negative cell: auto_resume=False raises CheckpointSchemaError with the right invalidated_nodes. Also fold TQ-02 (Low): the check_fixtures CHECK_ERROR alternations are broad enough to match the wrong error in the right family — tighten the named fixtures' regexes while in the test area.

This test is also the marketing precondition: the release notes should lead with auto-rewind (agent-dev verdict) and may only do so with this proof landed. Gates y5ux.

title: Tool results in ToolMessage: use describe_type schema + renderer, not model_dump_json
description:
When a tool returns a Pydantic model, the ToolMessage content (what the agent LLM sees during the ReAct loop) should use describe_type for the schema header + the configured renderer for the instance — same as every other prompt input. Currently it uses model_dump_json which is raw JSON values with no field descriptions.

## File: src/neograph/_llm.py, lines ~367-380

### Current (just shipped in neograph-iura):
if isinstance(result, _BM):
    rendered = result.model_dump_json(indent=2)
...
messages.append(ToolMessage(content=rendered, ...))

### Should be:
if isinstance(result, _BM):
    from neograph.describe_type import describe_type
    schema_header = describe_type(type(result))
    # Use the node's renderer (or global) to render the instance
    instance_text = _render_tool_result(result, renderer)
    rendered = f'{schema_header}\n\n{instance_text}'
...
messages.append(ToolMessage(content=rendered, ...))

## What the LLM sees now (model_dump_json):
{
  "source_file": "auth.py",
  "line": 42,
  "snippet": "def authenticate(user, password): ...",
  "relevance": 0.95
}

## What it should see (describe_type + renderer):
Tool result schema:
{
  source_file: string  // Path to the source file
  line: int  // Line number
  snippet: string  // Code snippet at that line
  relevance: float  // Relevance score 0-1
}

<source_file>auth.py</source_file>
<line>42</line>
<snippet>def authenticate(user, password): ...</snippet>
<relevance>0.95</relevance>

## Why this matters
- describe_type includes Field(description=...) annotations — the LLM knows what each field MEANS
- The renderer (XML/delimited/JSON) is consistent with how all other inputs are rendered
- model_dump_json gives values without context — the LLM has to guess field semantics

## Implementation detail
invoke_with_tools needs access to the node's renderer. Currently it doesn't receive it. Two options:
A. Pass renderer as a parameter to invoke_with_tools
B. Use the global renderer via _get_global_renderer() inside invoke_with_tools

Option A is cleaner — the factory already has the node, passes renderer down.

## Scope
- Only the ToolMessage content changes (what the agent LLM sees)
- ToolInteraction.result gets the same rendered text (backward compat: still a string)
- ToolInteraction.typed_result stays the original model (unchanged)
- Downstream nodes receive typed_result — how THEY render it is their business

## Acceptance criteria
- ToolMessage.content includes describe_type schema header for Pydantic tool results
- ToolMessage.content uses the configured renderer for the instance
- Non-Pydantic tool returns (str, dict) unchanged — str() as before
- All existing tests pass
- New e2e test: verify ToolMessage content has schema header + rendered instance

title: KEYMAKER T2: mode (a) core lowering — mesh-aware compile walk + Command(goto) + destinations + exit/END
description:

design:
## Core Invariant
An out-of-set route value (target not in peers UNION {HANDOFF_END}) raises ExecutionError inside the member wrapper BEFORE emitting the goto — never LangGraph's silent drop (_algo.py:312); the mesh lowers to Command(goto)+add_node(destinations=) (D3, non-negotiable this task), and the compile walk collapses the contiguous mesh to a SINGLE _add_keymaker_mesh dispatch so no member is double-added.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first, GUARD-FIRST)
1. GUARD-FIRST — write G1 + G2 FAILING before any impl:
   - G1 Command-construction monopoly: AST-walk guard (copy TestErrorBuildBodyMonopoly, tests/test_guards_assembly.py:84) asserting  is constructed ONLY in src/neograph/factory.py and runner.py. Fails now (factory has no Command yet — fine; it fails once you add it elsewhere; write it to scan src/ and pin the two-file allowlist).
   - G2 handoff-key centralization: focused pin on top of TestNeoStateKeysCentralized (tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py:449) — every neo_handoff_* literal must originate in _state_keys.py via StateKeys.handoff_hops/handoff_payload; no inline f-string in factory/_wiring/compiler/_input_shape.
2. factory.py — add make_keymaker_fn(node, keymaker, mesh_ctx): build inner update dict via the EXISTING make_node_fn twins (do not duplicate dispatch); read the route field off the node output; compute target (route value; HANDOFF_END -> exit_name); target-check against peers UNION {HANDOFF_END} -> ExecutionError on miss; return Command(goto=target, update={**inner_update, StateKeys.handoff_payload(entry_field): payload}). Sync+async twins via RunnableLambda(fn, afunc=afn) (factory.py:56 pattern). Import Command from langgraph.types. Leave a clean seam for T3's hop-counter RMW (do NOT inline budget).
3. _input_shape.py — add a handoff_param branch in _extract_fan_in_dict (sibling of the fan_out_param branch at :108): when input_name == node.handoff_param, read StateKeys.handoff_payload(entry_field) from state. REQUIRED for end-to-end routing (see Risks scope-gap).
4. _wiring.py — add _add_keymaker_mesh(graph, members, entry, prev_node, ...): copy _add_loop_back_edge's exit-node scaffold (_wiring.py:625-682) — pass-through '__handoff_exit_<entry>' node, static prev->entry edge, returns exit_name. Per member: make_keymaker_fn + graph.add_node(name, fn, destinations=tuple(peers)+(exit_name,)). NO inter-member static edges, NO conditional router.
5. compiler.py — (a) make the walk (243-277) mesh-aware: index-based iteration; at a Keymaker entry, collect the contiguous member run, call _add_keymaker_mesh ONCE, skip the members, set prev_node=exit; (b) replace the node-dispatch placeholder arm (623-627) to delegate to the mesh path (or make the walk handle it before dispatch); (c) keep the subgraph KEYMAKER arm (515-518) as a reject (D-MESH-LEVEL), reword off 'lands in T2' only after grep-checking no test pins that string on the subgraph path. Preserve assert_never exhaustiveness.
6. Tests — runtime-routing half of tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py: E1-shaped mesh routes end-to-end with a GENUINE CYCLE (A->B->A->exit) via scripted members + register_scripted; unknown/out-of-set target -> ExecutionError asserted; a walk test proving each member node appears exactly once (no double-add). Flip TestLegalMeshAssembles + test_keymaker_compile_is_staged_to_t2 (test_keymaker_validation.py ~118-157) from raises(CompileError,'lands in T2') to compile+run success. Move check_fixtures/should_fail/keymaker_mesh_minimal.py back to should_pass/ (D7).
7. Gates (execute-molecule): scoped pytest (test_keymaker.py, test_keymaker_validation.py, test_check_fixtures.py, the two guard suites) + mypy (assert_never sites) + ruff before commit. Budget/checkpoint stays in T3; three-surface @node sugar stays in T4.
notes:
## Findings (T2 research — dp-researcher, T1 @ b6bd69e is committed)

REUSE-FIRST TARGETS (extend, do not rebuild):
- make_keymaker_fn WRAPS make_node_fn (factory.py:24). make_node_fn already returns a dual-path RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper) whose sync/async twins return the inner update dict via _execute_node/_aexecute_node. The keymaker wrapper builds those SAME inner update dicts, then returns Command(goto=target, update={**inner_update, hops_key: n+1, channel_key: payload}). Do NOT re-implement dispatch — call the existing wrappers and post-process. Mirror the factory.py:56 dual-path shape (RunnableLambda(fn, afunc=afn)).
- Command comes from langgraph.types (already imported at runner.py:22). G1 monopoly = factory.py + runner.py only; factory.py adds the import.
- _add_keymaker_mesh models on _add_loop_back_edge (_wiring.py:625-682): the EXACT exit-node pattern to copy — a pass-through exit node (Loop uses '__loop_exit_<name>', def loop_exit(state)->{} at :660; Keymaker uses '__handoff_exit_<entry>'), static edge prev->entry, and returns exit_name so the walk resumes forward normally. KEY DIFFERENCE from Loop: NO conditional-edge router and NO static inter-member edges — members carry destinations= and return Command(goto). add_node(name, fn, destinations=tuple(peers)+(exit_name,)) per member.
- ExecutionError.build (errors.py:175) is the SAME error class Loop uses for out-of-set/exhaustion (_wiring.py:550). Out-of-set target = ExecutionError, node=member.name. No new exception type.
- Mesh detection for the walk: state.py:250 already computes 'keymaker_members = [n for n in nodes_only if classify_modifiers(n)[0]==ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER]; entry=keymaker_members[0]'. The compiler walk needs the CONTIGUOUS run starting at the current item; classify_modifiers (modifiers.py:105) + get_modifier(Keymaker) (modifiers.py:290) read peers/route/max_hops off each member. entry_field = field_name_for(entry.name); channel key = StateKeys.handoff_payload(entry_field); hops key = StateKeys.handoff_hops(entry_field) — both ALREADY declared as state fields in state.py:257-258.

WHAT T1 LEFT AS PLACEHOLDER (exact replace targets):
- compiler.py:623-627 (node dispatch, ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER arm) raises CompileError('Keymaker lowering lands in T2'). REPLACE with mesh dispatch. Keep assert_never exhaustive.
- compiler.py:515-518 (subgraph dispatch KEYMAKER arm) — KEEP as a reject (D-MESH-LEVEL: Keymaker-on-Construct illegal in v1), but its message may be re-worded from 'lands in T2' to a proper ConstructError/CompileError since T2 is now landing. Assembly already rejects Construct members, so this arm is defense-in-depth.
- The compiler WALK LOOP (compiler.py:243-277) is per-item and calls _add_node_to_graph per Node. Review-M1 edit: when the current item is a Keymaker member (entry), detect the contiguous mesh run, call _add_keymaker_mesh ONCE, advance the loop index past all members, and set prev_node = mesh exit. A plain 'for item in construct.nodes' can't skip-ahead cleanly — convert to index-based iteration OR pre-collapse the mesh. Without the skip, non-entry members get double-added (once by the mesh helper, once by the walk).

TEST-STAGING TO FLIP (D7):
- tests/test_keymaker_validation.py TestLegalMeshAssembles (lines ~118-157): three parity tests + test_keymaker_compile_is_staged_to_t2 currently assert 'with pytest.raises(CompileError, match="lands in T2")'. T2 flips these to assert successful compile + end-to-end run.
- tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/keymaker_mesh_minimal.py (# CHECK_ERROR: lands in T2) MOVES back to should_pass/ once lowering compiles it (D7 explicitly assigns this move to T2).

CURRENT vs DEPRECATED: no deprecated pattern here — Command(goto) is the ADJUDICATED lowering (D3, D-LOWERING-DISSENT). Do NOT switch to router+path_map even though Loop uses it (_wiring.py:676) and the H3 reviewer preferred it — D3 pins Command(goto)+destinations= and the morning-review reversal is a separate decision (T8).
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/factory.py:24-91 — make_node_fn; the dual-path RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper) at :90 is the twin pattern make_keymaker_fn copies. Inner sync twin _execute_node(node,state,config,dispatch) returns dict; async _aexecute_node.

- src/neograph/state.py:250-258 — mesh entry detection + handoff_hops/handoff_payload field declarations already present; entry_field = field_name_for(entry.name).
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:130-146 — StateKeys.handoff_hops / handoff_payload (G2 must route ALL handoff keys through these).
- src/neograph/_input_shape.py:96-118 — _extract_fan_in_dict: the fan_out_param branch at :108 is the exact sibling for a NEW handoff_param branch (see Risks — REQUIRED for end-to-end).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- SCOPE GAP (surface loudly, NOT a doc contradiction but AC-forcing): design §4.1 SCOPE table lists factory.py/_wiring.py/compiler.py but OMITS _input_shape.py. However design §3.3 explicitly requires _extract_input (_input_shape.py:108) to read StateKeys.handoff_payload(entry_field) when input_name == node.handoff_param. T1 wired NOTHING that reads handoff_param at runtime (verified: zero hits in _input_shape/_state_write/factory/_wiring). A peer that consumes the reserved 'handoff' inputs key CANNOT receive the payload without this branch, so the AC 'E1-shaped mesh routes end-to-end with a genuine cycle' is UNMEETABLE without editing _input_shape.py. Treat _input_shape.py as in-scope for T2.
- Walk-skip correctness (M1): the double-add bug — enumerate members by contiguous position, skip ALL of them in the outer loop, thread prev_node=exit. Add a walk test asserting each member node name appears exactly once in graph.nodes.
- entry vs re-entry handoff key: state.py keys the channel/counter off the ENTRY field only (one mesh per level, D-SINGLE-MESH). make_keymaker_fn for EVERY member must read/write the SAME entry-keyed channel, not its own field_name. Pass entry_field into the mesh_ctx.
- destinations= must include the exit node AND all peers UNION {HANDOFF_END-mapping}. HANDOFF_END ('__end__') is a route VALUE that maps to the exit node (not a peer name); Command(goto=exit_name) when route value == HANDOFF_END. LangGraph gives compile-time validation from destinations= (research §2b) but the RUNTIME out-of-set check in the wrapper is the invariant that closes _algo.py:312 silent drop — keep BOTH.
- on_exhaust='exit' vs 'error' lands in T3 (budget); T2 target-check is the routing half. But the wrapper structure must leave a clean seam for the counter RMW T3 adds (don't inline budget logic that T3 must rip out).
- assert_never exhaustiveness: replacing the node arm must keep the match exhaustive; mypy will bite if the KEYMAKER case is removed rather than filled.
- Subgraph KEYMAKER arm message: if reworded away from 'lands in T2', check no test greps that exact string on the subgraph path (grep before edit).
## Disease scan (atom p7y2z.3)
Disease pattern eliminated: bypassing canonical helpers — inline Command() construction, inline neo_handoff_ key f-strings, or re-implementing node dispatch instead of wrapping make_node_fn.
- Command() construction: ONLY runner.py:763,1022 today. factory.py will add one → the G1 two-file allowlist {factory.py, runner.py} is exactly right; no stray Command elsewhere.
- neo_handoff_ literals: ZERO outside _state_keys.py (node.py:206 is a code comment, not a string literal — no guard flags it). handoff_hops/handoff_payload/handoff_param all route through StateKeys/normalizer already.
- Exit-node naming: Loop uses __loop_exit_<name>; Keymaker uses __handoff_exit_<entry> — no collision.
- CRITICAL SEMANTIC CATCH: HANDOFF_END='__end__' is byte-identical to LangGraph END. The wrapper MUST map route value HANDOFF_END → exit_name (__handoff_exit_<entry>); passing goto='__end__' would terminate the whole graph and skip post-mesh downstream nodes. Confirmed in plan step 2/4 (destinations includes exit_name; HANDOFF_END→exit_name).

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The read-side entry_field threading is under-specified and is the plan's weakest seam. Step 3 says _extract_fan_in_dict should read StateKeys.handoff_payload(entry_field), but that function is on the INNER make_node_fn path (called by _execute_node), receives only (state, node), and node.handoff_param is the bare literal 'handoff' (confirmed _ir_normalize.py:173) carrying NO entry-field. A non-entry member (e.g. billing in test_programmatic_pipe_surface_assembles, inputs={'handoff': Handoff}) has its own field_name != entry_field, so it CANNOT build neo_handoff_<entry_field> from  alone. mesh_ctx/entry_field is threaded only to the WRITE side (make_keymaker_fn wrapper), NOT to the READ side. Unlike fan_out (fixed key StateKeys.EACH_ITEM, no per-mesh parameter), the handoff channel key is parameterized by entry_field, so 'add a sibling branch to :108' understates the work. The AC (genuine cycle, peer receives payload) is unmeetable until this is resolved. Suggestion: specify the mechanism — store the resolved entry_field (or full channel key) on each member node at normalize/state-build time so _extract_input reads it self-contained from  (mirroring fan_out_param's self-containment), OR thread entry_field through make_node_fn -> _execute_node -> _extract_input. Pick one explicitly; do NOT fall back to scanning state for a neo_handoff_* field (breaks entry-keyed determinism).

- [LOW] Finding: The runner recursion-limit floor is unassigned. Design 4.1 mode-(a) table lists a runner.py change (_ensure_agent_recursion_limit :51 add each mesh's max_hops — K-hop mesh costs K supersteps). T2's plan touches runner.py only as the G1 Command allowlist file; T3 is 'hop budget + checkpoint'. The AC's small A->B->A->exit cycle is well under LangGraph's default 25 so T2's test passes without it, but a high-max_hops mesh would trip the ceiling before on_exhaust. Suggestion: explicitly assign this to T3 (budget-coupled) in the plan/notes so it does not fall through the T2/T3 crack.

- [LOW] Finding: Seam-for-T3 trap in the NOTES reuse-target example. The 'REUSE-FIRST TARGETS' note shows make_keymaker_fn returning update={**inner_update, hops_key: n+1, channel_key: payload} — i.e. WITH the hop counter — while plan step 2 correctly omits hops (payload only) and says 'do NOT inline budget'. An implementer copying the reuse example would inline exactly the RMW T3 must rip out. Suggestion: align the NOTES example to the payload-only step-2 form, or annotate it 'hops_key lands in T3'.

- [LOW] Finding: G1's 'write FAILING first' does not literally hold for a monopoly-allowlist guard. Scanning src/ with a {factory.py, runner.py} allowlist is GREEN on the happy path (Command only in runner.py today, allowlisted; factory.py's add is also allowlisted). It only goes red if Command appears in a non-allowlisted file. The bead text acknowledges this. Suggestion: implementer should not burn time forcing G1 red; treat it as a permanent allowlist pin, and rely on G2 (handoff-key centralization) as the genuinely-red-first guard.

- [LOW] Finding: Locating the payload object inside inner_update for the route-field read is unspecified. make_node_fn twins return a state-field->value dict, not the payload object; step 2 says 'read the route field off the node output' without naming the key. Derivable via field_name_for(node.name)/primary_output_field (single-type payload guaranteed by 3.1 rule 4), but worth stating so the implementer uses the canonical selector, not getattr guesswork.

Confirmed SOUND (survived attack): (1) _input_shape.py correctly treated in-scope — design 3.3 requires it and the AC forces it; the 4.1 SCOPE-table omission is a doc gap, not a contradiction. (2) HANDOFF_END->exit_name mapping correct on both write (goto) and destinations= sides; route-value domain (peers UNION HANDOFF_END) and goto domain (peers UNION exit_name) line up. (3) Walk M1 index-based skip + once-only dispatch + prev_node=exit + per-member-appears-once test correctly kills the double-add; contiguity guaranteed by assembly 3.1r2. (4) G1 allowlist {factory.py, runner.py} matches reality (Command only at runner.py:763,1022). (5) Subgraph-arm reword is safe — no test greps the subgraph found= string; all four staging tests pin the NODE-path message 'Keymaker lowering lands in T2'. (6) D7 fixture move (should_fail -> should_pass) + test-flip correctly scoped. (7) Command(goto)+destinations= held per D3 — plan does NOT drift to router+path_map. (8) assert_never exhaustiveness (incl. D9 sixth site _state_write.py:94) preserved.

Reviewer verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT. Single MEDIUM (read-side entry_field threading under-specified) + 4 LOWs. All confirmed-sound items (8) survive. Refinement applied inline by executor (no re-research needed) and recorded as decision D10 in docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md:

- LOW (payload object locator): use primary_output_field(field_name_for(node.name), node.outputs) to pull the payload from the inner update dict — canonical selector, not getattr guesswork.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.1
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.1` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.1/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.1
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.1)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.1 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.1 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.1/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.1 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.1/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Create di.py module with DIResolver and DIBinding
description:
Phase 2 of architecture-v2.md section 3 (DI Unification).

## What
Extract DI resolution into a dedicated module: src/neograph/di.py.

REVISED from review:
- DIKind enum: FROM_INPUT, FROM_CONFIG, FROM_INPUT_MODEL, FROM_CONFIG_MODEL, FROM_STATE, CONSTANT (6 values — NO UPSTREAM, that is _extract_input not DI)
- DIBinding dataclass: name, kind, inner_type, required, payload
- DIResolver class with resolve(binding, config, state=None) -> value
- DIResolver handles config-based resolution ONLY. Upstream resolution stays in _extract_input.
- FROM_STATE is merge_fn-only — resolved from graph state by param name. Handled by resolve() when state is provided.
- Loop unwrap (_unwrap_loop_value) applies to FROM_STATE values only (they come from state which may have append-lists).

## Where
New file: src/neograph/di.py. Extracted from decorators.py (_resolve_di_value, _classify_di_params).

## Design
See docs/design/architecture-v2.md section 3 (REVISED). Three resolution scopes:
1. DIResolver — config-based (from_input, from_config, bundled, constant)
2. Upstream — stays in _extract_input (NOT part of DIResolver)
3. from_state — merge_fn-only, DIResolver.resolve() with state param

The scripted shim in _register_node_scripted interleaves DI-resolved args with upstream-resolved args. DIResolver covers ONLY the DI part. The shim still handles port params, loop renames, and fan-out params itself.

## How

title: Harden engine-verb receiver heuristic vs naming evasion (PAT-02/LR-03, review 130726)
description:
INVARIANT: the three-layer engine-verb guard classifies .invoke/.ainvoke/.stream/.astream on a compile(...)-bound receiver as an engine call regardless of variable name (e.g. 'g = compile(...); g.invoke(...)' must be flagged in a compile-layer module).
ANTI-BAND-AID: write the evasion meta-test FIRST — synthetic source binding a compiled graph to an innocent name must be flagged — the meta-test is what pins the broadening; do not just tweak the heuristic.
Design: docs/design/code-review-remediation-2026-07-13.md section PAT-02 (ticket T2).
Steps: (1) In tests/test_guards_three_layer.py, add evasion meta-test. (2) Broaden _receiver_is_graphlike/_scan_engine_verbs with intra-module compile(...) provenance: collect names assigned from a Call to compile (ast.Assign), treat engine verbs on those names as engine calls (~15 lines AST; no cross-module dataflow needed — the disease is intra-module by definition). (3) Confirm EXPECTED_ENGINE_SURFACE exact-match still passes (it is the true backstop and currently holds; blind spot verified NOT exploited — caller/payload in _agent_cycle.py are bound chat models, Layer-2). (4) AUDIT: grep -rnE '= *compile\(' src/neograph/*.py cross-checked against invoke receivers shows no compile-and-invoke pair outside runner.py/_compiled.py/_subconstruct.py. Touches only tests/test_guards_three_layer.py.
design:
## Core Invariant
The three-layer engine-verb guard classifies .invoke/.ainvoke/.stream/.astream on a compile(...)-bound receiver as an engine call regardless of variable name — no compile-layer module may schedule engine execution and evade detection by naming the compiled graph something without 'graph'.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add evasion meta-test FIRST** (anti-band-aid clause — TDD for guard hardening):
   - In tests/test_guards_three_layer.py, add `TestEngineVerbsConfinedToEngineSurface` method:
     - Name: `test_meta_compile_bound_to_innocent_name_is_flagged`
     - Synthetic source: `"g = compile(pipeline)\ng.invoke(state, config=c)"` (or similar)
     - Assertion: `_scan_engine_verbs(source)` must contain `("invoke", "shared")`
   - This meta-test MUST FAIL on current implementation, proving the blind spot exists

2. **Broaden _receiver_is_graphlike with provenance tracking** (~15 lines AST):
   - Add helper before `_scan_engine_verbs`:
     - Function `_compile_assignments(source: str) -> set[str]`
     - Parse AST with `ast.parse(source)`
     - Walk `ast.Assign` nodes where `value` is `ast.Call` with func.name == "compile"
     - Return set of target names (the left-hand side identifiers)
   - Modify `_receiver_is_graphlike(expr)`:
     - First check existing token-based logic (keep for speed path)
     - If no 'graph' token, check if receiver is `ast.Name` whose id is in compile-assigned set
     - Requires passing the compile-names set through OR building a closure that captures it
   - Alternative: modify `_scan_engine_verbs` to collect compile-names once per module, then filter calls

3. **Verify EXPECTED_ENGINE_SURFACE still matches exactly**:
   - After broadening, run `TestEngineVerbsConfinedToEngineSurface::test_engine_surface_matches_expected_exactly`
   - Must pass unchanged — confirms real engine surface is stable, detector didn't drift

4. **Audit step** (verification that blind spot was not exploited):
   - Run `grep -rnE '= *compile\(' src/neograph/*.py` to list all compile(...) assignments
   - Cross-reference against `grep -rnE '\.(invoke|ainvoke|stream|astream)\(' src/neograph/*.py` receivers
   - Confirm no compile-and-invoke pair exists outside runner.py/_compiled.py/_subconstruct.py
   - caller/payload in _agent_cycle.py are LLM/tools (Layer-2), correctly exempt

**Touch scope**: Only tests/test_guards_three_layer.py — no production code changes.
notes:
## Findings
- **Blind spot confirmed**: `_receiver_is_graphlike` checks only for 'graph' token in receiver names (line 198-206). Evasion case `g = compile(...); g.invoke(...)` would NOT be flagged.
- **NOT currently exploited**: All actual engine verb receivers either contain 'graph' token OR are Layer-2 LLM/tool calls (correctly excluded). Verified by cross-referencing:
  - `grep -rnE '= *compile\(' src/neograph/*.py` finds 7 compile(...) assignments (all use 'graph'/'sub_graph' names)
  - `grep -rnE '\.(invoke|ainvoke|stream|astream)\(' src/neograph/*.py` finds only allowlisted modules plus two Layer-2 calls
- **Layer-2 exemptions verified**:

## Architect Review (dp-reviewer, neograph-i90dv.28)

Therefore the planned broadening adds NO new real-surface hits -> EXPECTED_ENGINE_SURFACE exact-match stays green by construction, not by luck. This is the load-bearing safety check and it passes.

title: Portal addressability: port-taxonomy design doc (route-to-entry-port; entry-map + mesh-transparent-exit) — Core Invariant for mesh extensions
description:
Write docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md — the Core Invariant for the Portal mesh extensions (nnds9 / do0d9 / a37vk). They implement AGAINST this one invariant, not as bespoke tasks (anti-band-aid).

CONTENT:
- Three-class addressability taxonomy: ATOMIC (scripted/think = 1 node, goto works) | PORT-BEARING REGION (sub-Construct, agent/act cycle = multi-node but single defined entry+reconverging exit -> addressable WITH machinery) | PORTLESS REGION (bare Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator inline = fork/join or interrupt-on-static-edge, NO single boundary port -> permanently NON-addressable by design; wrap in a sub-Construct to hand off to it).
- The invariant: runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS; modifiers are internal wiring, not ports. neograph already has the port concept — Construct.input/output (singular).
- The two mechanisms that unlock port-bearing regions: (1) a compile-time entry-label map (DX destination name -> LangGraph entry node), stashed on the graph like schema_fingerprint; (2) mesh-transparent exit (the region's last_name consults the mesh channel instead of falling to its static successor).
- Framing: reducibility-by-construction (structured goto — reach a region's entry, never its interior). Prior art: Harel statecharts / UML entry-point pseudostates + history, behavior-tree uniform tick interface, FBP/HDL/ADL ports, Temporal child workflows, OpenAI Swarm agent-granularity handoffs, LangGraph subgraph + Command.PARENT.
- Bound the claim: ports kill invalid-entry-by-construction; max_hops handles the residual nonterminating-legal-routing class.
design:
## Core Invariant
Runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS, never region interiors -- a Command(goto=...) target (or, pending D-LOWERING-DISSENT, a router+path_map equivalent) must always resolve to a construct's declared entry (Construct.input's compiled entry node, an entry-label-map destination, or a Portal peer name), so an "addressable region" is defined by having exactly one such entry AND one reconverging exit; modifiers (Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator) are internal wiring that never qualifies as a port, which is why bare fork/join/interrupt regions stay permanently non-addressable unless wrapped in a sub-Construct.

## Implementation Plan
1. Write `docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md` as a design doc, NOT new code -- this task (u7gy8.2) only produces the doc; nnds9/a37vk/do0d9 implement against it.
2. Structure the doc around the existing `Construct.input`/`Construct.output` port concept (`src/neograph/construct.py:113-123`) as the anchor -- state explicitly that PORT-BEARING REGION addressability is "give Construct.input's compiled entry node a stable, DX-facing label" and "make the region's exit consult the mesh channel instead of its static successor," not a new port primitive.
3. Present the three-class taxonomy with ONE worked example per class, reusing code already in the repo instead of inventing hypotheticals. Lead with symbol names (`make_portal_fn`, `_add_agent_cycle`, `_add_subgraph`) in doc prose; keep line numbers only as an as-of-2026-07-15 parenthetical, not the primary reference (design docs outlive line numbers):
   - ATOMIC: any scripted/think node under `Portal(to=[...])` -- cite `make_portal_fn` (`src/neograph/factory.py:103`, as of 2026-07-15) as the shipped mechanism.
   - PORT-BEARING REGION: (a) a sub-Construct compiled via `_add_subgraph` (`src/neograph/compiler.py:438`) -- single typed entry (`sub.input`) already enforced fail-loud; (b) the agent/act ReAct cycle (`_add_agent_cycle`, `src/neograph/_wiring.py:989`) -- single entry `{node}__agent`, reconverging exit via its conditional router. Name both as candidates the entry-label map + mesh-transparent-exit mechanisms unlock, motivating nnds9 (agent/act mesh members) and a37vk (self.handoff builder needs a stable name to target).
   - PORTLESS REGION: a bare `Each`/`Oracle`/`Loop`/`Operator` applied inline (not as a sub-Construct) -- no single entry/exit exists structurally (fan-out barrier or static post-edge), so it is permanently non-addressable; the doc's prescribed fix is "wrap it in a sub-Construct" (which then becomes PORT-BEARING via mechanism (a)), not a bespoke routing rule.
4. Specify mechanism 1 (entry-label map) as a compile-time artifact stashed on the compiled graph exactly like `schema_fingerprint`/`node_fingerprints` (`compiler.py` CompiledNeograph construction, near the `result = CompiledNeograph(...)` block) -- `dict[str, str]` DX-name -> LangGraph node name, computed once per compile() level (never crossing a sub-Construct boundary -- that crossing is explicitly do0d9's Command.PARENT mechanism, keep the two mechanisms textually separate so implementers don't conflate them).
5. Specify mechanism 2 (mesh-transparent exit) as extending the existing Portal exit pattern: a region's exit-node's successor-resolution step additionally checks the entry-keyed mesh channel (`StateKeys.handoff_payload(field_name)`, `src/neograph/_state_keys.py:130-139`) before falling through to its static next-node edge -- same channel/state-key convention Portal peer routing already uses, no new state-key scheme. NOTE: for a multi-node PORT-BEARING region (agent/act cycle, sub-Construct), which node is the 'exit node' (the parse node? the router's done-arm? the subgraph's opaque-node boundary?) is a per-region-class detail this taxonomy doc does NOT pin -- it is deferred to nnds9/do0d9, and the doc must say so explicitly rather than imply a single well-defined 'last_name' for all region classes.
6. Any `Command(goto=...)` emission the two mechanisms require must land in `factory.py` or `runner.py` only (guard G1, `TestCommandConstructionMonopoly` in `tests/test_guards_assembly.py`) -- state this explicitly as a constraint on nnds9/do0d9/a37vk implementers, not something this doc's own text needs to satisfy (it writes no code). HOWEVER: D-LOWERING-DISSENT (`docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md`) is explicitly ESCALATED/contested -- v1 kept `Command(goto)+destinations=` per the 07inf bead pin, but the reviewer (H3) preferred router+path_map, and the decision log's own morning action is "DECIDE: ratify Command(goto) or switch to router+path_map" (filed as a bead, unresolved as of this doc's writing). The doc MUST add a paragraph acknowledging D-LOWERING-DISSENT is contested and state that the entry-label-map + mesh-transparent-exit mechanisms are LOWERING-SUBSTRATE-AGNOSTIC: they name a destination; whether that destination is reached via `Command(goto)+destinations=` or a router+path_map is the separate, still-open D-LOWERING-DISSENT decision, not something this taxonomy doc settles. This keeps the taxonomy durable if v1's lowering substrate changes.
7. Any new mesh-assembly validation rule implied by the taxonomy (e.g. rejecting a Portal target that names a PORTLESS node) belongs in `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py`'s `_check_portal_mesh`, per the existing single-sited-validation-cluster discipline -- name this explicitly so a future implementer doesn't inline the check in the compiler or decorators.
8. Cite `docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md`'s D-MESH-LEVEL / D-MEMBER-MODES / D-FORWARD-EXEMPT entries verbatim as the origin and justification for nnds9/do0d9/a37vk -- do not re-derive rationale the decision log already recorded. ALSO cite D-LOWERING-DISSENT verbatim (per step 6 above) as the one contested entry the taxonomy's substrate-agnostic framing insulates against.
9. Include the "bound the claim" framing required by the task brief: ports make invalid-entry unrepresentable BY CONSTRUCTION (same class of guarantee as Portal's existing peer-target validation); `max_hops` (already shipped, `Portal.max_hops`/`on_exhaust`, `src/neograph/factory.py:146-199`) is what handles the residual nonterminating-but-legally-routed class -- these are two different guarantees and the doc must not conflate "addressable" with "terminating."

title: BUG: to_agent_spec fails on dict-form fan-in (@node's primary shape) — DataFlowEdge source_output uses node name not property
description:
to_agent_spec() cannot export the PRIMARY @node fan-in shape. A downstream node with a typed upstream param (`def summ(seed: A)`) compiles to `inputs={'seed': A}` (dict-form keyed by upstream node name) — the dominant shape @node produces. Exporting it raises a raw pydantic ValidationError, not a clean neograph error.

REPRO (fails):
    import neograph as n
    from pydantic import BaseModel
    class A(BaseModel): x: int
    class B(BaseModel): y: int
    seed = n.Node.scripted('seed', fn='f', outputs=A)
    summ = n.Node.scripted('summ', fn='g', inputs={'seed': A}, outputs=B)
    n.to_agent_spec(n.Construct('rt', nodes=[seed, summ]))
    # -> ValidationError: DataFlowEdge 'seed_to_summ' source_output 'seed' is not a property of source node 'seed'
The pipeline COMPILES in neograph (valid). A real @node two-node pipeline reproduces it identically.

ROOT CAUSE: src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:647 — the general fan-in DataFlowEdge sets `source_output=upstream_name` (the inputs-dict KEY = the upstream NODE name) instead of the source node's real exported output PROPERTY title. Contrast the correct paths: Oracle (line ~398) and Loop (line ~478) use `source_output=prop.title`. Single-type inputs (inputs=Model, not dict) go through a different path and export fine.

TEST COVERAGE GAP: the export/round-trip suites (test_agent_spec_export.py, csdcl round-trip) used `_producer`/`_consumer` helpers with SINGLE-TYPE inputs — never the dict-form (@node) shape — so they were green while the primary shape was broken.

FIX: wire the fan-in DataFlowEdge(s) to the source node's actual output property/properties (match how outputs are exported, per-field like the Oracle/Loop paths). If any dict-form case is genuinely unrepresentable, fail loud via ConfigurationError, never a raw pydantic error. ACCEPTANCE: add a dict-form-fan-in EXPORT test AND a dict-form round-trip test; a real @node two-node pipeline must export + round-trip.
design:
## Root Cause
_agent_spec.py's general fan-in DataFlowEdge builder (dict-form branch, ~line 636-647) confuses the inputs-dict KEY (upstream node name, e.g. 'seed') with the upstream node's exported output Property TITLE (e.g. field name 'x' for a single-type output, or 'seed.x' were dict-form outputs involved). It sets both source_output and destination_input to the bare upstream_name, which pyagentspec's DataFlowEdge validator rejects because no node exports a property literally named after another node.

## Fix Approach
Mirror the single-type-inputs path (lines ~658-673) and the Oracle/Loop precedent (prop.title): for each dict-form inputs entry (upstream_name -> expected_type), resolve the upstream node's real output properties via _properties_for(upstream.outputs) (or normalize_outputs), and emit one DataFlowEdge per shared field: source_output=<upstream's real output Property title>, destination_input=<this node's own input Property title for that key — 'key.field' per _properties_for's dict-form prefixing convention>. If the upstream node cannot be resolved to a real property (fail-loud), raise ConfigurationError instead of letting pydantic's raw ValidationError leak through.
notes:
## Reproduction

- Root cause: the dict-form fan-in branch in _agent_spec.py (~line 630-647) sets source_output=upstream_name (the inputs-dict KEY, which is the upstream NODE'S NAME), instead of the upstream node's actual output Property title(s). Contrast Oracle (line ~399) and Loop (line ~479), which correctly iterate _properties_for(...) and use prop.title.
## Similar Pattern Analysis (trace-similar)
Bug pattern category: constructing a pyagentspec DataFlowEdge with a raw dict/name KEY instead of a resolved output-Property TITLE.

Conclusion: this is an ISOLATED instance, not a repeated pattern. The other 3 call sites already follow the correct convention (resolve real output/input Property titles via _properties_for before building the edge); only the dict-form fan-in branch skipped that resolution and used the raw dict key. No other beads tasks filed -- no other instances found.
## Codebase Disease Scan (ozxqw)

Total DataFlowEdge construction sites found: 4 (all in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py; grep -rln confirms no other file constructs a DataFlowEdge)
