No DEFERs. Fix scope is exactly the one MIGRATE row (lines 644-649).
## Architect Review (ozxqw)

1. **Root cause correctness**: CONFIRMED LOW risk of being wrong. Verified live (`python -c ...` repro) that pydantic.ValidationError is raised exactly where the design says (_agent_spec.py:644, dict-form fan-in branch), and confirmed by grep that the OTHER 3 DataFlowEdge sites in the same file already use resolved `prop.title`/`shared_title` — this branch is the only one using the raw dict key.

2. **Fix minimality — LOW risk, with one refinement**: the design's fix approach (resolve per-field Property titles instead of the bare upstream_name) is minimal and localized to lines ~636-650. Refinement for the fix atom: destination_input must use the ALREADY-established dict-form prefixing convention `_properties_for` applies to the destination node's own declared inputs (`f'{key}.{p.title}'`, e.g. 'seed.x') — not a bare field title — because that is what the destination SpecNode's own `inputs=` property list actually contains (verified at _agent_spec.py:176-177, _properties_for lines 152-166). source_output should use the upstream node's real output Property titles, resolved via `_properties_for(upstream_item.outputs)` (mirroring the single-type fallback path at lines 658-679), for symmetry with how the producer side is already computed everywhere else in this file.

3. **Regression risk — LOW**: change is additive/corrective inside one existing loop body; does not touch node.py/construct.py/_construct_validation.py/factory.py/modifiers.py (layer discipline respected — this is agent-spec-interop-only, per CLAUDE.md's off-limits list for those modules). Existing single-type-inputs and Oracle/Loop DataFlowEdge tests are unaffected (different code branch).

4. **Architecture compliance — LOW**: stays within _agent_spec.py, matches the file's existing prop-title-resolution convention exactly (no new pattern introduced) — in fact it REMOVES the one place that deviated from that convention.

5. **Similar-bug scalability — MEDIUM finding (adjacent, in-scope per the bug's own acceptance)**: the sibling line `if source_node is None: continue` (line 640-642) silently DROPS a DataFlowEdge whenever `upstream_name` doesn't match any node's bare `.name` — which is exactly what happens for a dict-form-OUTPUT producer referenced downstream via the '{upstream}_{key}' naming convention (documented in CLAUDE.md's Node.outputs section). ozxqw's own acceptance text says: 'If any dict-form case is genuinely unrepresentable, fail loud via ConfigurationError, never a raw pydantic error' — a silent `continue` is the fail-SOFT failure mode that invariant exists to prevent. RECOMMENDATION: the fix atom should convert this `continue` to `raise ConfigurationError.build(...)` (cheap, ~3 lines, same file, no new test surface beyond one more should_fail-style case) rather than leaving a second silent seam right next to the one being fixed.

6. **Test coverage sufficiency — LOW**: the reproduce atom's new test (TestToAgentSpecExportsDictFormFanIn) pins the primary regression via property-membership assertion (not a brittle exact-name match), which is appropriately loose. The fix atom's acceptance additionally requires a round-trip test per ozxqw's own text — not yet written, tracked for the implement atom.

## VERDICT: ALL_LOW (with one MEDIUM finding folded into the fix's scope, not blocking)
Proceed to fix. Scope for the implement atom: (a) resolve source_output/destination_input via _properties_for as described in #2, (b) convert the silent continue at line 640-642 to ConfigurationError per #5, (c) add the export test (already done in reproduce) + a round-trip test per ozxqw's acceptance criteria.
## Fix Applied

title: Oracle merge barrier is single-path (no async twin) — LLM merge threadpooled under ainvoke
description:
Found by neograph-expi trace-similar (bug-triage neograph-wj8m.3). SAME disease as neograph-expi (single-path node-callable factory whose body invokes a blocking child), DIFFERENT instance — the Oracle merge barrier, not the sub-construct.

make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py:383-427) returns a single sync merge_fn closure — no async twin, not RunnableLambda(afunc=...). Its body calls _merge_variants -> invoke_structured (_oracle.py:276, a SYNC LLM call) when the Oracle uses an LLM merge (merge_prompt/merge_model). group_merge_barrier (_wiring.py:261, the Each x Oracle fused merge) has the same shape via _merge_one_group -> invoke_structured. Both are added via graph.add_node with no afunc.

Consequence: under graph.ainvoke the Oracle/Each-Oracle merge barrier is threadpooled and its LLM merge runs on the sync path — blocks the event loop, violates the Phase-1 H2 invariant (async is driver-selected and must propagate through every nesting level). NOTE: the Oracle GENERATOR redirects ARE dual-path (make_oracle_redirect_fn/_oracle.py:90, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn/:135, make_each_redirect_fn/:461) — Phase 1a did those but missed the merge barrier.

Out of scope for neograph-expi (that fix is the sub-construct twin only; fixing the merge here would violate 'fix the bug only'). Needs its own dual-path fix: async merge twin awaiting ainvoke_structured (verify an async structured-invoke exists) + return RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn); mirror in group_merge_barrier. TDD: thread-identity / gate-parking discriminator over graph.ainvoke of an Oracle-with-LLM-merge pipeline.
design:
## Root Cause
The Oracle GENERATOR redirects were made dual-path in Phase 1a (make_oracle_redirect_fn/_oracle.py:90, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn/:135, make_each_redirect_fn/:461), but the MERGE barriers were missed:
- make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py:383-427) returns a single sync merge_fn; body -> _merge_variants -> _run_merge_prompt -> invoke_structured (sync LLM, _oracle.py). Added via _wire_oracle -> graph.add_node(merge_name, merge_fn, defer=True) with no afunc.
- group_merge_barrier (_wiring.py:261) -> _merge_one_group -> _merge_variants -> same sync invoke_structured. Added via graph.add_node(barrier_name, group_merge_barrier, defer=True) with no afunc.
Under graph.ainvoke both are threadpooled; the LLM merge runs on the sync path, blocking the loop (Phase-1 H2 invariant: async is driver-selected and must propagate through every nesting level). The scripted merge_fn path (_run_merge_fn) is pure Python (no I/O) — harmless if threadpooled — but the merge_prompt (LLM) path is the defect.

## Fix Approach (dual-path, mirrors _oracle.py redirects + Phase 1c ainvoke_structured)
1. Add async merge twins that await the async LLM seam:
   - _amerge_variants(...) mirroring _merge_variants, branching to an async _arun_merge_prompt that awaits _llm.ainvoke_structured (already exists, _llm.py:231). The _run_merge_fn (scripted) branch has no I/O; its async twin can call the same sync helper (or a thin await-nothing wrapper) — keep ONE merge algorithm, only the LLM seam differs (parity with invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured sharing _prepare/_finish).
2. make_oracle_merge_fn returns RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn); amerge_fn awaits _amerge_variants. _wire_oracle passes the Runnable to graph.add_node (defer=True) unchanged.
3. group_merge_barrier: add async twin agroup_merge_barrier awaiting _amerge_one_group (async twin of _merge_one_group); wrap graph.add_node(barrier_name, RunnableLambda(group_merge_barrier, afunc=agroup_merge_barrier), defer=True).
4. Structural guard (sweep): pin make_oracle_merge_fn AND group_merge_barrier's factory to be dual-path (afunc present + drives ainvoke_structured), extending the neograph-expi GUARD C pattern.
NO band-aid: do not thread-offload; the merge must AWAIT the async seam so async selection propagates.
notes:
## Reproduction (neograph-45xo.2)
- Failing tests: tests/test_async_llm_tool.py::TestOracleMergeAsyncSeam (2 cells)
  - test_single_group_oracle_merge_parks_on_async_seam (make_oracle_merge_fn, programmatic Node.scripted | Oracle(merge_prompt))
  - test_each_oracle_group_merge_parks_on_async_seam (group_merge_barrier, Each×Oracle map_over+ensemble+merge_prompt)
- Discriminator: gate-parking (GatedAsyncFake, no sync .invoke). Generators are SCRIPTED so the ONLY LLM call is the merge. Async path -> ainvoke_structured -> fake.ainvoke parks (enter_count==1). Sync path (today) -> invoke_structured -> fake.invoke -> AttributeError, run never parks. RED verified: enter_count=0, task.done=True (failed with AttributeError 'GatedAsyncFake' object has no attribute 'invoke' at _llm_structured_compat.py:118).
- Driven at graph.ainvoke (arun() is Phase 1d, not yet implemented) — same harness as test_async_dual_path/test_async_llm_tool.

## Trace-similar (neograph-45xo.3)
Pattern category: single-path node closure whose body invokes a sync LLM seam (invoke_structured / invoke_with_tools) with no afunc twin — threadpooled under graph.ainvoke.

Exhaustive re-scan of sync LLM-seam call sites reachable from a graph node:

Reached by exactly TWO node closures: make_oracle_merge_fn (single-group) and group_merge_barrier -> _merge_one_group -> _merge_variants -> _run_merge_prompt (Each×Oracle). BOTH already in this ticket's scope.
- invoke_with_tools (sync tool loop) HAS its async twin ainvoke_with_tools (Phase 1c) and is dispatched via ToolDispatch.aexecute — tool/agent nodes are already dual-path.
- Generator redirects (make_oracle_redirect_fn/make_eachoracle_redirect_fn/make_each_redirect_fn) already dual-path (Phase 1a).

## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-45xo.4)

Pattern: node-callable closure added to a StateGraph that invokes a sync LLM seam (invoke_structured / invoke_with_tools) with no afunc twin — threadpooled under graph.ainvoke, LLM runs on the sync path.

| 1 | _oracle.py:410 make_oracle_merge_fn (return merge_fn @ :427) | single-path merge barrier -> invoke_structured | MIGRATE | THIS ticket. Return RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn) awaiting ainvoke_structured |
| 2 | _wiring.py:261 group_merge_barrier (add_node @ :301) | single-path Each×Oracle fused merge -> _merge_one_group -> invoke_structured | MIGRATE | THIS ticket. Wrap RunnableLambda(group_merge_barrier, afunc=agroup_merge_barrier) |
| 3 | _dispatch.py:170 ThinkDispatch.execute -> invoke_structured | sync half of a dual-path dispatch | ALLOWLIST | ThinkDispatch also defines aexecute (:186) -> ainvoke_structured; GUARD A pins it. Sync call only on the sync driver |

| 5-13 | make_node_fn / 3 oracle redirects / make_subgraph_fn / pure-dict wiring nodes / routers | dual-path or no-blocking-child | ALLOWLIST | already dual-path (Phase 1a + neograph-expi) or structural pass-throughs |

## Architect Review (neograph-45xo.5)

Verdict: ALL_LOW — fix approach correct, minimal, architecture-compliant, low risk. Proceed to fix. Notes below are guidance + one out-of-scope observation.

1. Root cause correctness — LOW (confirmed). Two RED cells prove via gate-parking (GatedAsyncFake, no sync .invoke) that both merge barriers run invoke_structured on the sync path under graph.ainvoke. Root cause = single sync merge closure, no afunc. Precisely located.

2. Fix minimality — LOW. Clean async-twin addition mirroring invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured (which already share _prepare/_finish and differ only at the seam):
   - _oracle.py: _arun_merge_prompt (awaits _llm.ainvoke_structured; shares input_data build + merge_fallback/merge_post_process hooks with _run_merge_prompt — factor a shared pre/post helper to prevent drift, do NOT duplicate the hook logic). _amerge_variants branches merge_prompt->_arun_merge_prompt vs merge_fn->_run_merge_fn (the scripted branch is pure Python, reused verbatim). make_oracle_merge_fn returns RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn).
   - _wiring.py: _amerge_one_group (awaits _amerge_variants — pure delegation, trivial twin), agroup_merge_barrier awaiting it per group; wrap add_node(barrier_name, RunnableLambda(group_merge_barrier, afunc=agroup_merge_barrier), defer=True).
   ONE merge algorithm preserved; only the LLM seam gains an await.

3. Regression risk — LOW/MEDIUM. Sync path byte-identical (run() untouched). Risks: (a) sync/async DRIFT in _run_merge_prompt hook logic — MITIGATE by sharing pre/post helpers; (b) defer=True with a RunnableLambda-wrapped barrier — verify LangGraph accepts a deferred Runnable node (the merge barrier uses defer=True; expi barriers did not, so this is the new bit — smoke-test at implement). Existing merge_prompt tests (test_oracle/test_compositions run() under sync) lock the sync path.

title: @node context= for verbatim state injection into prompts
description:
Nodes that consume pre-formatted context (graph catalog, domain briefing) need a way to declare state fields that get injected verbatim into the prompt — not BAML-rendered, not part of the typed input model.

Use case: piarch's explore node needs the graph catalog (incident-encoded, BFS-ordered) alongside its typed VerifyClaim input. The catalog is pre-computed by an upstream node and stored in state. It must not be re-rendered — the format is crafted for LLM consumption.

Proposed API:
  @node(
      mode='agent',
      prompt='match-verify/explore',
      context=['build_catalog'],  # state fields injected verbatim
      tools=[search, read],
  )
  def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ExplorationResult: ...

Template uses {context.build_catalog} placeholders. Framework looks up state fields by name, passes strings through as-is. Typed input still BAML-rendered via {input}.

Three rendering strategies unified:
- Typed input (VerifyClaim) → BAML (generic)
- Tool results (SearchResult) → renderer dispatch (custom or BAML)
- Context (catalog, briefing) → verbatim (this feature)
close_reason: context= field on Node + @node, factory extraction, prompt compiler injection. 416 tests.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-on6jt
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-on6jt` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-on6jt/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-on6jt
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-on6jt)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-on6jt --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-on6jt --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-on6jt/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-on6jt codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-on6jt/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: ask_human(): typed mid-loop HITL ask — pure Layer-2 sugar over langgraph interrupt() + A.5 safety lint
description:
The namesake deliverable of neograph-m6d3, correctly scoped now that the mechanism has shipped. The capability EXISTS: raw langgraph.types.interrupt() inside an agent tool works through neograph today with exactly-once pre-interrupt tool execution (tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py, both drivers). What is missing is ONLY the typed contract and its lint visibility. Design sources: docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md (purity test, Layer-2 definition); consumer-chair gap analysis 2026-07-03 (marginal value = typed resume validation + lint visibility + documented contract; capability contributes ZERO).

SCOPE IN (the whole ticket, ~4 files, ~250-350 LoC, no compiler/topology changes):
1. src/neograph/hitl.py — ask_human(payload: BaseModel, resume_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None). Body is a PASSTHROUGH: langgraph interrupt(payload.model_dump()) then resume_model.model_validate(returned) when resume_model given, else return the raw dict. Roughly 40-60 LoC including docstring. Export from neograph __init__.
2. Lint rule(s) in lint.py — the A.5 safety deliverable and the real prize: ask_human is a first-class marker the validator can SEE (raw interrupt inside an opaque tool callable is invisible to lint). New issue kinds: ask_human_in_mutating_node (ERROR or WARN: ask_human reachable from an act-mode node) and, if cheaply detectable, mutating-tool-precedes-ask ordering WARN (non-idempotent side effect before an interrupt in the same node can double-fire — the residual Level-B case; cite docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md).
3. Tests: integration (typed payload pause -> resume -> tool receives validated ResumeModel; malformed resume raises at the boundary with a clear error, not deep in tool code); E2E reusing the keystone two-tool idempotency pattern but through ask_human; lint fixtures (tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/ask_human_in_act_node.py + a should_pass twin).
4. Docs: human-in-the-loop.mdx gains the mid-loop section with ask_human as the blessed path AND an explicit note that raw langgraph interrupt() remains supported.

SCOPE OUT — THE ANTI-REBOOT CLAUSE (this is the acceptance gate): the helper must contain ZERO execution logic. No interrupt mechanics, no resume plumbing, no Command handling, no checkpoint interaction, no topology or state-channel changes. If the implementation finds itself touching compiler.py, _wiring.py, _agent_cycle.py, runner.py, or state.py (beyond lint.py), it is rebuilding what m6d3 + LangGraph already deliver — STOP and re-read the keystone test. Raw interrupt() must remain fully supported; the transparency IS the architecture, the sugar is optional safety. The pause/resume path must remain byte-identical to the raw path (assert same __interrupt__ surface).

Independent-review gate before closing. Parent capability ticket neograph-m6d3 closes only after this lands (it is the last open acceptance item besides the m6d3.4 payoffs).
design:
## Core Invariant
ask_human is a pure Layer-2 passthrough over langgraph.types.interrupt() — its pause/resume path stays byte-identical to the raw keystone path (same __interrupt__ surface, same raw resume dict) with typed validation as the ONLY added transform, and it carries ZERO execution logic (no interrupt mechanics beyond the passthrough call, no compiler/topology/state-channel/runner changes).

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review neograph-ra60.4/.12)

1. NEW src/neograph/hitl.py (~40-60 LoC): 'def ask_human(payload: BaseModel, resume_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None)'. Body = passthrough: 'from langgraph.types import interrupt' (same primitive as _wiring.py:16), 'returned = interrupt(payload.model_dump())', 'return resume_model.model_validate(returned) if resume_model is not None else returned'. When resume_model is None the raw dict is returned UNCHANGED (byte-identical raw parity — keystone asserts received == [answer.model_dump()]). Malformed resume surfaces pydantic ValidationError at THIS boundary (clear context, not deep in tool code). Docstring: optional sugar; raw interrupt() stays fully supported.

2. Export: 'from neograph.hitl import ask_human' in src/neograph/__init__.py + 'ask_human' in __all__ (mirror lint.py:49 / __all__ pattern).

3. Lint (the real prize) in src/neograph/lint.py — new _check_ask_human_in_mutating_node, cloned from _check_async_only_tools (:440) + reuse _resolve_tool_object (:478). Wire into _walk next to the :271 call.
   SEVERITY: WARN (required=False) — avoids false-positive blocking of legit ask_human-then-idempotent-mutate. Document the rule trusts the DECLARED node.mode (a mutating tool mislabeled mode='agent' escapes — accepted limitation).
   GATE: node.mode == 'act' only (act==mutations; agent==read-only). agent-mode ask_human is fine and must NOT fire.
   DETECTION (MEDIUM fix — must cover tool-shape variance or the rule ships green but no-ops): for each resolved tool object, collect callables from the FULL attribute set and scan each one's __code__.co_names for 'ask_human':
     - StructuredTool: .func, .coroutine
     - BaseTool subclass: ._run, ._arun (bound methods → use getattr(fn,'__func__',fn).__code__)
     - duck-typed class tool (keystone _AskTool shape, the shape the E2E reuses): .invoke, .ainvoke
   Helper _tool_references_ask_human(tool_obj) -> bool: iterate that attr set, getattr(fn,'__code__',None) or getattr(getattr(fn,'__func__',None),'__code__',None); 'ask_human' in code.co_names. Direct-reference heuristic only (misses alias imports / indirection) — document the limitation; ask_human's value IS being a named marker, alias-hiders opt out.
   Emit LintIssue(node_name=f"Node '{node.name}'", param=str(tool_name), kind='ask_human_in_mutating_node', required=False, message=...). Use param=str(tool_name) to dodge the :466 Any-vs-str mypy landmine.
   FIX-IN-PASSING (LOW, no-band-aid): coerce lint.py:466 to param=str(tool_name) too, clearing the pre-existing mypy error since the new code clones that exact getattr-or pattern.

4. Tests — put ALL lint assertions in tests/test_lint.py (current-way, matches async-only/loop rules at :415). DEVIATION FROM TICKET (justified): the ticket asked for check_fixtures/should_fail/ask_human_in_act_node.py + should_pass twin, but test_check_fixtures.py only catches import/compile RAISES and lint() never raises — a lint-only fixture cannot fire. Both research and independent review confirmed. So NO check_fixtures files; test_lint.py covers positive (act-node tool calling ask_human -> issue emitted) AND negative (agent-node tool calling ask_human -> NO issue) with the keystone .invoke shape.
   (a) Integration (new test module or test_di/test_inline area): typed payload pause -> resume -> tool receives validated resume_model INSTANCE; malformed resume raises ValidationError at the ask_human boundary.
   (b) E2E reusing keystone two-tool exactly-once pattern (test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:183-244) but routing the interrupt through ask_human; assert identical __interrupt__ surface vs raw path.
   (c) Lint tests in test_lint.py per above.

5. Docs: website/src/content/docs/walkthrough/human-in-the-loop.mdx — add mid-loop section (ask_human as blessed path), correct the now-false 'per-tool gating not supported' caution box, note raw langgraph interrupt() remains fully supported. Run 'npm run build' in website/.

6. ANTI-REBOOT guard: if impl edits compiler.py/_wiring.py/_agent_cycle.py/runner.py/state.py, STOP — rebuilding what m6d3+LangGraph deliver.

## Findings (research neograph-ra60.2)

REUSE CONFIRMED — the ANTI-REBOOT clause holds. Every mechanism ask_human needs already exists; the deliverable is a passthrough helper + lint visibility + docs. ZERO changes to compiler.py/_wiring.py/_agent_cycle.py/runner.py/state.py required.

1. The interrupt mechanism is langgraph.types.interrupt — already imported/used in-repo (src/neograph/_wiring.py:16, :788 for the Operator boundary node). ask_human is pure Layer-2 sugar: call interrupt(payload.model_dump()); if resume_model given, resume_model.model_validate(returned), else return the raw dict.

2. The byte-identical raw path is PROVEN by the keystone: tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:141-144 (_AskTool.invoke) does exactly 'answer = interrupt({...dict...}); ... return f"operator decided: {answer}"'. The resume surfaces as result['__interrupt__'][0].value (:196) and the resume value is delivered as the WHOLE Command(resume=) dict via run(..., resume=answer.model_dump()) (:206, :215). ask_human MUST produce the identical __interrupt__ surface: pass the plain dict to interrupt(), and interrupt() returns the raw resume dict. Do NOT wrap/transform the return except optional resume_model.model_validate. The keystone's assertions (same __interrupt__ payload, exactly-once pre-interrupt tool) are the parity bar to re-assert through ask_human.

3. Lint rule exemplar to COPY: _check_async_only_tools (src/neograph/lint.py:440-475) + _resolve_tool_object (:478-500). It already (a) gates on node.mode in ('agent','act') and node.tools, (b) resolves the concrete tool object from Tool._bound_tool or the registered factory, (c) emits LintIssue via the standard pattern. Copy this exact structure into a new _check_ask_human_in_mutating_node, gate on node.mode == 'act' (act == mutations; agent == read-only — mode is the detectable act/agent signal, already read at lint.py:455), wire it into _walk alongside the other checks (lint.py:264-271). Node modes are directly detectable at lint time via node.mode.

4. Detection of ask_human reachability from an act node: the tool callable is opaque, so introspect the resolved tool object's underlying func/coroutine __code__.co_names (and/or module globals) for a reference to 'ask_human'. This is the 'first-class marker the validator can SEE' — raw interrupt() is invisible, but a named ask_human import shows up in co_names. Cheap and static; heuristic (see Risks).

5. LintIssue emission pattern: LintIssue(node_name="Node '<name>'", param=<str>, kind=<str>, required=<bool>, message=<str>) — lint.py:464-475 is the template. New kinds: ask_human_in_mutating_node (required=True for ERROR semantics, or False for WARN — ticket leaves ERROR-or-WARN open) and optional mutating_tool_precedes_ask (WARN, required=False).

6. Export pattern: src/neograph/__init__.py imports each public symbol at module top (e.g. lint.py:49 'from neograph.lint import LintIssue, lint') and lists it in __all__ (:75+). Add 'from neograph.hitl import ask_human' + 'ask_human' in __all__.

7. lint.py:466 pre-existing mypy error: param=tool_name where tool_name is Any (getattr chain, :462) but LintIssue.param is typed str (lint.py:47). The new ask_human lint code MUST pass a str literal for param to avoid re-introducing it; optionally coerce str(tool_name) at :466 to fix in passing.

## Relevant Code
- tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:141-144 — the raw interrupt() tool body ask_human must stay byte-identical to.
- tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:190-217 — pause/resume drive + __interrupt__ surface + resume-dict delivery; the E2E pattern to reuse through ask_human (two-tool exactly-once idempotency at :201/:223).

- src/neograph/lint.py:440-500 — _check_async_only_tools + _resolve_tool_object: the exact structure to clone for the act-node reachability check.
- src/neograph/lint.py:219-271 — _walk: where to register the new check (mirror :271 _check_async_only_tools call).
- src/neograph/lint.py:43-52,464 — LintIssue dataclass + emission template; :466 mypy Any-vs-str landmine.
- tests/test_lint.py:415,434 — lint-rule tests assert via 'any(i.kind == ... for i in lint(...))'; the async-only + loop-condition rules live HERE, not in check_fixtures (lint never raises).
- src/neograph/__init__.py:49,75+ — public export + __all__ pattern.
- tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/bad_output_strategy.py + test_check_fixtures.py:59-80 — fixture convention: '# CHECK_ERROR: <regex>', harness asserts a RAISE on import/compile.
- website/src/content/docs/walkthrough/human-in-the-loop.mdx:1-14 — docs deliverable; the caution box currently claims per-tool gating is unsupported (now false).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- FIXTURE-HARNESS MISMATCH (address in impl): the ticket asks for tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/ask_human_in_act_node.py + should_pass twin, but test_check_fixtures.py asserts an exception raised on import OR compile — and lint() NEVER raises (lint.py:7). A lint-issue-only fixture will NOT fire in that harness. The established current-way for lint rules is test_lint.py (assert on i.kind, see :415). Either (a) put the lint assertions in test_lint.py (recommended, matches loop/async-only rules), or (b) make the check_fixture explicitly call lint() at module top-level and 'raise' if the issue is present so the harness catches it. Flag to implementer; do not silently drop the fixture.
- DETECTION IS HEURISTIC: co_names introspection catches 'ask_human' imported/called by name inside the tool func; it misses alias imports, indirection, or ask_human reached through a helper the tool calls. Ticket says 'if cheaply detectable' — scope the rule to the direct-reference case and document the limitation. This is acceptable because ask_human's whole value is being a NAMED marker; users who alias-hide it opt out of the safety net.
- BYTE-IDENTICAL RETURN: when resume_model is None, ask_human must return interrupt()'s raw dict UNCHANGED (keystone asserts received == [answer.model_dump()], :215). Any always-on wrapping breaks raw-path parity. resume_model.model_validate(returned) is the only transform, and malformed resume must raise at that boundary (ValidationError with clear context), not deep in tool code.
- mutating_tool_precedes_ask (optional WARN): the residual Level-B ordering case per docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md §5 — a non-idempotent side effect BEFORE an interrupt in the same node can double-fire on resume (LangGraph memoizes at node granularity; ReAct loop = many steps in one node). Cheap detection is hard (needs intra-tool ordering); ship only if trivially detectable, cite the doc, do NOT build the step-memoization engine (that IS Level B, explicitly deferred).
- DOC UPDATE (not a blocker, in scope): human-in-the-loop.mdx caution box (line ~10) states per-tool/mid-loop gating 'is not yet supported' — the keystone (agent-as-subgraph) makes mid-loop interrupt work now. The mid-loop section must present ask_human as the blessed path AND explicitly note raw langgraph interrupt() remains fully supported (transparency IS the architecture).
- THREE-SURFACE PARITY: ask_human is a runtime helper invoked inside tool bodies, not an IR change, so node.py/_construct_validation.py/factory.py/state.py are untouched and the three-surface rule does not bind the helper. The lint rule operates on Construct/Node.mode/tools (surface-agnostic, walks all three already). Note in tests but no per-surface duplication needed.

title: Each×Oracle fusion + dict-form outputs: state model creates wrong collector field
description:
## Bug

When a Node has Both Each and Oracle modifiers (Each×Oracle fusion) AND dict-form outputs, the state model creates the wrong collector field name. The compiler's _add_each_oracle_fused() writes to neo_eachoracle_{field_name}, but _add_output_field() in state.py takes the Oracle-only branch (line 232) which creates neo_oracle_{field_name} instead.

## Root cause

In state.py:_add_output_field (line 231-247), when node.outputs is a dict AND node.has_modifier(Oracle), it unconditionally takes the Oracle path. It does NOT check for Each×Oracle fusion. The Each×Oracle handling exists in _add_single_output_field (line 260), but that function is never reached for dict-form outputs when Oracle is present.

## Impact

Runtime crash: InvalidUpdateError from LangGraph because per-key fields (verify_result, verify_meta) are created as plain fields without reducers, but M×N concurrent generators all write to them simultaneously.

## Reproduction

Node with outputs={'result': Result, 'meta': Meta} | Each(over='seed.items', key='id') | Oracle(n=2, merge_fn='merge_fn')

Crashes at runtime with: InvalidUpdateError: At key 'verify_result': Can receive only one value per step.

## Fix direction

In _add_output_field, when node.outputs is dict AND node has BOTH Each and Oracle, route to the Each×Oracle fusion state creation (tagged collector + merge_dicts reducer per key), not the Oracle-only path. Also fix make_eachoracle_redirect_fn to handle per-key state fields.
close_reason: Fixed: state model + redirect + barrier handle dict-form fusion

title: @merge_fn silently overwrites same-named functions + still on the global-dict registry @node moved off (review 080726 PAT-02)
description: From the 2026-07-08 review (verified Medium; decorators.py:763). Two defects, one root: (1) SILENT OVERWRITE — registering a second @merge_fn with the same function name silently replaces the first in _merge_fn_registry; two modules defining merge helpers with a common name (merge/combine) corrupt each other's Oracles with zero signal. FIX: fail loud on duplicate registration (ConstructError/ConfigurationError naming both definition sites), unless identical function object (idempotent re-import must stay safe — module reloads re-register). (2) REGISTRY PATTERN DEBT: @merge_fn remains on the module-global name-keyed dict while @node moved to the PrivateAttr sidecar and the 2026-05 architecture decisions made PER-COMPILE registries the norm (scripted/conditions/tool_factories all flow per-compile). AGENTS.md currently BLESSES the name-keyed pattern for string-referenced decorators — the review challenges that; the ticket owner evaluates migrating merge_fn resolution to the per-compile registry shape (Oracle references by string name -> resolve via compile-time lookup like conditions) and either migrates or documents WHY name-keyed-global stays (updating AGENTS.md either way so doc and decision agree). TDD the overwrite fail-loud first — that half is unambiguous. Gates y5ux.
notes:
DECISION (neograph-pbya defect #2, registry-pattern debt): DOCUMENT why the name-keyed global registry STAYS for @merge_fn — do NOT migrate to a per-compile / PrivateAttr-sidecar shape.

RATIONALE:
- The reason @node could move to a PrivateAttr sidecar is that @node RETURNS the Node it decorates — decoration site and storage target are the SAME object. @merge_fn is structurally different: it decorates a standalone function, returns the bare function (decorators.py: 'return f'), and that function is referenced from a DIFFERENT object (Oracle) purely by STRING NAME (Oracle(merge_fn='combine')). There is no Node/Oracle instance in scope at decoration time to hang a sidecar on — the two are wired later, by name. A name->metadata mapping is therefore a structurally-required symbol table, not incidental global state.
- Migrating to per-compile would NOT remove the global. Metadata is produced at import/decoration time and consumed at compile time; compile() would still need SOME import-time global to look the name up from (or the Oracle would need to carry resolved metadata, which it cannot because the Oracle does not exist when @merge_fn runs). This mirrors conditions/tool_factories, which the 2026-05 per-compile architecture STILL seeds from the decoration-time _runtime_registry fallback bridge. So @merge_fn's global is consistent with the actual current state of conditions/tool_factories — @node is the outlier precisely because it can self-store.
- The review's real correctness defect was the SILENT OVERWRITE, which is fully closed by the fail-loud collision guard (below). The 'process-global' concern does not by itself cause corruption once collisions fail loud.

RECOMMENDATION for the AGENTS.md-blessing agent (85nb): AGENTS.md's 'Known open DX items' note blessing the name-keyed pattern for string-referenced decorators STANDS and is now stronger — the blessing should cite the structural reason (decoration site decoupled from reference site by a string name = symbol table) plus the new fail-loud guard. No migration recommended.

FIX SHIPPED (defect #1, silent overwrite):
- decorators.py: on @merge_fn registration, a same-name collision between two DIFFERENT definition sites now raises ConstructError.build(...) naming BOTH sites (module.qualname + file:lineno). Idempotency preserved via _same_def_site(): same object, same code object (def re-run in a loop / hypothesis example -> new fn object, shared code object), or same source site+qualname (module reload recompiles code object but keeps file/line/name). Genuine cross-module collisions differ in filename/qualname/lineno -> raise.
- Added _qualname_site() and _same_def_site() module-level helpers in decorators.py.

TESTS (tests/decorator/test_di.py::TestMergeFnDuplicateRegistration):
- test_raises_when_two_different_functions_share_a_name
- test_raises_on_bare_name_collision_via_function_name
- test_reregistering_same_function_object_is_idempotent
- test_reexecuting_same_def_statement_is_idempotent (pins the loop/hypothesis code-object path)
- test_different_names_do_not_collide
TDD: the two raise-tests were confirmed RED before the guard, GREEN after.
close_reason: @merge_fn duplicate registration now fails loud (ConstructError naming both def sites), idempotent for same def-site/module reloads. Registry-debt: decided KEEP name-keyed global (structural symbol-table, unlike @node sidecar) + documented. TDD, 5 new tests.

title: arch: promote LlmConfig from runtime view to IR type; close typo hole + move validation to construct time
description:
Follow-up to neograph-rnjw (d8f5d3d). The rnjw refactor introduced LlmConfig as a runtime VIEW over the raw dict. This ticket promotes it to be the IR TYPE carried by Node and Construct, which eliminates an entire class of bugs structurally rather than just fixing specific instances.

## Problem class (not just rnjw symptoms)

Untyped `dict[str, Any]` carried as config across many layers, each consumer defaulting independently. The rnjw refactor fixed the ONE instance where None bypassed a default. The class of bugs it leaves open:

1. **Typos stay silent.** `Node(llm_config={'max_retires': 5})` -- `extra='allow'` preserves the typo as an unknown key, typed `max_retries` takes its default, user wanted 5 and gets 1. No error at any layer.
2. **Validation is runtime-late.** Errors surface at first LLM invocation, after compile() has 'succeeded'. A misconfigured pipeline passes compile, runs for 30s producing useful state, then crashes on the first invoke. Worse: for silent typos (item 1), it never crashes -- just produces wrong results.
3. **Per-call validation cost.** Every invoke_structured / invoke_with_tools re-validates the same dict. Wasteful and timing-wrong.
4. **Merge blindness.** `construct.py:124` merges `{**parent, **child}` at dict level. LlmConfig never sees the merge until much later, so typed merge semantics are impossible.
5. **Duplicated defaults.** Even post-rnjw, defaults could drift if anyone adds a new consumer that reads `llm_config.get('foo', default_here)` instead of going through LlmConfig. The dict-level interface keeps inviting this mistake.

Generalizes beyond llm_config: any `dict[str, Any]` crossing a layer boundary in this codebase (`renderer: Any`, `prompt_compiler: Callable` signatures, etc.) is a latent instance of the same pattern. This ticket scopes only to llm_config; others can follow.

## Architectural principles

1. **Parse, don't validate** (Alexis King). Convert untyped input to a typed representation at the boundary; pass typed data through the system; the result type is the proof of validity.
2. **Make illegal states unrepresentable.** If `output_strategy: Literal['structured','json_mode','text']`, a wrong value literally cannot exist in the typed world. The bug 'wrong strategy reaches runtime' becomes not possible.
3. **Push validation upstream as far as possible.** runtime -> compile time -> construct time -> decoration time. Earlier = more bugs caught = cheaper to fix.

## Design

### 1. LlmConfig becomes the IR type

```python
from typing import Any, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

class LlmConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')  # typos fail loudly at construction

    # Known framework fields -- the ONLY place defaults live
    output_strategy: Literal['structured', 'json_mode', 'text'] = 'structured'
    max_retries: int = 1
    max_iterations: int = 20
    token_budget: int | None = None
    budget_exhausted_message: str | None = None

    # Explicit escape hatch for provider-specific knobs (temperature, max_tokens,
    # model_tier, ...). Separate namespace -- cannot accidentally shadow a
    # framework key with a provider key.
    provider_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

    def resolved_budget_exhausted_message(self, output_model_name: str) -> str:
        return self.budget_exhausted_message or (
            'Your previous response contained tool-call markup. '
            'All tool budgets are exhausted. Do NOT invoke any more tools. '
            f'Produce the final response as a {output_model_name} object. '
            'No markup, no tool calls. Output ONLY the structured response.'
        )

    def as_factory_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        '''Flat dict for the llm_factory callback. Framework keys take
        precedence over provider_kwargs on name collision (keeps framework
        semantics authoritative).'''
        return {**self.provider_kwargs, **self.model_dump(exclude={'provider_kwargs'})}

    def merged_with(self, child: 'LlmConfig') -> 'LlmConfig':
        '''Construct-level propagation: parent default + child overrides.
        Child wins on framework fields; provider_kwargs merge with child winning on collisions.'''
        return LlmConfig(
            output_strategy=child.output_strategy if 'output_strategy' in child.model_fields_set else self.output_strategy,
            max_retries=child.max_retries if 'max_retries' in child.model_fields_set else self.max_retries,
            max_iterations=child.max_iterations if 'max_iterations' in child.model_fields_set else self.max_iterations,
            token_budget=child.token_budget if 'token_budget' in child.model_fields_set else self.token_budget,
            budget_exhausted_message=child.budget_exhausted_message if 'budget_exhausted_message' in child.model_fields_set else self.budget_exhausted_message,
            provider_kwargs={**self.provider_kwargs, **child.provider_kwargs},
        )
```

## What this eliminates by construction

| Bug class | How it becomes impossible |
|---|---|
| None-bypass (rnjw) | No .get(key, default) anywhere. Field type either accepts None or rejects it. |
| Typos (max_retires) | extra='forbid' rejects at Node construction. |
| Duplicated defaults | Default lives on one field in one class. No call sites to drift. |
| Late validation | Node construction raises at author time, not at first run. |
| Per-invoke validation cost | Validation is once per Node, not once per LLM call. |
| Merge corruption | Construct propagation is LlmConfig.merged_with(), which understands the type. |
| Provider-knob confusion | provider_kwargs is a separate namespace. Cannot accidentally shadow a framework key. |
| Future-consumer drift | Adding a new field adds it in one place; consumers read by attribute; no new .get() sites. |

def merged_with(self, child: 'LlmConfig') -> 'LlmConfig':
    parent_dump = self.model_dump(exclude={'provider_kwargs'})
    child_overrides = child.model_dump(exclude_unset=True, exclude={'provider_kwargs'})
    return LlmConfig(

title: §4: Module structure — god-module splits + cycle break-up + function-local-import guard
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4 (Module and function responsibilities).

**Decision locked**: each module and each function owns one named responsibility. God-modules and god-functions are forbidden. Imports form a DAG; cycles are broken by extracting Protocol modules. Function-local `from neograph...` imports are forbidden in new code; the current allowlist (existing exceptions) is documented in code and paid down as cycles are broken.

**Current state to fix**:
- `factory.py` is 631 lines with 6 named responsibilities (factory construction, state I/O, modifier I/O, oracle plumbing, observability, skip logic)
- `_llm.py` is 901 lines mixing global-state singleton, Protocol definitions, `_call_structured` dispatch, JSON parsing/retry, `render_prompt`, `invoke_structured`
- 53 function-local `from neograph...` imports across `src/neograph/`
- Three named real cycles: `factory ↔ _oracle`, `decorators ↔ factory`, `_dispatch ↔ _llm`
- The `_sidecar.py` extraction is the template recipe — both god-module splits and cycle break-ups follow it

**Children** (filed as separate tasks depending on this epic):
1. Extract Protocol module to break `factory ↔ _oracle` cycle
2. Extract Protocol module to break `decorators ↔ factory` cycle
3. Extract Protocol module to break `_dispatch ↔ _llm` cycle
4. Split `factory.py` god-module into responsibility-aligned modules
5. Split `_llm.py` god-module into responsibility-aligned modules
6. Function-local-import structural guard + initial documented allowlist

**Ordering note**: Protocol extractions should ship before the god-module splits — the splits are mechanically cleaner once the cycles are broken.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §4.

Independent of §2 epic (`neograph-n2li`) but the §2 work will be easier after this lands.
close_reason: Final child neograph-8ne2 closed via Wave E: _llm.py split 829→192L into responsibility-aligned modules (_llm_dispatch, _llm_retry, _llm_render) per §4 change-axis clustering. Plus the architectural-rewrite followup (gm-1 through gm-5) addressed the cgkl mechanical-split shortcomings. §4 architectural commitment realized: every module has one named responsibility; imports form a DAG; function-local imports paid down to an explicit allowlist.

title: Retire hand-rolled engine-duplicating plumbing: neo_* strip tax and STREAM_CUSTOM flag (use the engine's own abstractions)
description:
The consumer-chair audit (2026-07-03) classified ~10 percent of the epic's code as category-4: re-implementation of signals/filters the engine already provides. Each instance exists because neograph hand-rolled a parallel mechanism instead of using a LangGraph abstraction. Design source: docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md.

THE INVARIANT (lead with this): when the engine offers an abstraction for a concern, neograph must use it; a hand-rolled parallel mechanism is a standing violation even when it works. The deliverable of this ticket is the DELETION of the hand-rolled mechanisms, not their improvement.

ITEM A — the neo_* strip tax (the root one). _strip_internals (now in _state_keys) and the stripping half of _finalize_chunk exist ONLY because framework keys (neo_schema_fingerprint, neo_node_fingerprints, neo_each_item, CONFIG_INPUT echo...) live in USER state channels and must be scrubbed at every exit (run/arun return, values-mode chunks, updates-mode chunks, sub-construct returns). LangGraph's OWN abstraction for this is schema separation: StateGraph(state_schema, input_schema=..., output_schema=...) — output filtering at the engine level. RESEARCH ATOM FIRST, these are the questions that decide feasibility: (1) does output_schema filter stream_mode=values chunks and updates chunks, or only invoke/ainvoke results? (2) do excluded-from-output channels still persist in checkpoints (fingerprints MUST persist — that is why they are in state)? (3) how does it interact with sub-construct isolated schemas and with get_state (auto-resume reads fingerprints back via channel_values)? If the engine filter covers the surfaces: declare output_schema excluding neo_* at compile time, then DELETE _strip_internals call sites and the stripping arm of _finalize_chunk (the helpers die or shrink to nothing; the four exit-point wraps in run/arun and the per-chunk strip disappear). If research shows a genuine engine gap (e.g. updates-mode not filtered), document the gap precisely in the ticket and keep ONLY the minimal residue, with a comment citing the gap.

ITEM B — STREAM_CUSTOM flag plumbing. progress.py's _custom_stream_active + the STREAM_CUSTOM config key set by the streaming verbs (_mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom in runner.py) re-implement a signal LangGraph already provides: get_stream_writer() returns a no-op writer when no custom-mode consumer is attached. Replace the flag plumbing with writer-presence detection for the warn-once; delete _mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom and the config key. Keep the warn-once behavior itself (that is Layer-2 value) — only the detection mechanism changes. Verify the no-op-writer semantics against the installed langgraph version first; if it cannot distinguish (e.g. returns a real writer under a non-custom stream), document and keep the flag with a citation.

ITEM C (minor, docs-only) — unconditional Operator adds nothing over raw interrupt_before; its value is the CONDITIONAL predicate form. One honest paragraph in the Operator docs saying so, steering users with static gate needs to interrupt_before via the facade.

ANTI-BAND-AID: no shims layered over the old mechanisms during migration — each item flips atomically behind its research answer. Audit step after A: grep for any remaining neo_-stripping logic outside the single residue site. Every existing pinning test (values/updates strip, custom/messages passthrough, prefix-strip invariant) must be RE-POINTED at the engine-level filter, not deleted — the behavioral contract (users never see neo_*) is unchanged; only its enforcement moves into the engine. Independent-review gate before closing.
design:
## Core Invariant
When the engine (LangGraph 1.2.4) offers a first-class abstraction for a concern, neograph must USE it by DECLARING at compile time (output_schema on StateGraph) rather than hand-wrapping the engine's runtime output — and any surviving hand-rolled residue must carry a written, cited engine-gap justification.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first, evidence-scoped)
1. DECLARE, don't wrap (Item A core). In compiler.py:241 pass output_schema to StateGraph. Reuse the fields compile_state_model (state.py:96) already built — do NOT recompute 'user fields'. Build a Pydantic submodel from the state model containing every field whose name does NOT start with StateKeys.FRAMEWORK_PREFIX ('neo_'). This exactly mirrors _strip_internals (prefix-based), so node_id/project_root/human_feedback still surface (invariant test test_invariants.py:535 depends on it). input_schema STAYS UNSET (R1: it hard-filters the fingerprints run() seeds via initial input). Do this at BOTH the top-level compile and the recursive sub-construct compile (compiler.py:417) — the child's output_schema = its non-neo_ fields (surfaces sub.output).
2. DELETE the 4 dead strips atomically behind step 1: runner.py:509, runner.py:682, _subconstruct.py:169, _subconstruct.py:178. No shim overlap. The _strip_internals import in _subconstruct.py can go once both its uses are gone.
3. KEEP the 2 stream arms (runner.py:443 values, :447 updates) — engine gap: stream_mode=values/updates chunks are NOT filtered by output_schema in 1.2.4 (R1). Add a comment on each arm citing docs/design/langgraph-output-schema-research-2026-07-03.md (R1). _strip_internals stays alive for these two only.
4. Item B (STREAM_CUSTOM) — DOCUMENTED KEEP, not deletion (R4). Add a citation comment at progress.py:110 and the STREAM_CUSTOM def (_state_keys.py:58-64): get_stream_writer() returns the PRIVATE langgraph.runtime._no_op_stream_writer (config.py:196 / runtime.py:206) with no public sentinel, so the config flag is the robust discriminator. Leave _mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom/_custom_stream_active in place.
5. Item C (docs) — one honest paragraph in website/src/content/docs/node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx: unconditional Operator adds nothing over raw interrupt_before; its value is the CONDITIONAL predicate form; steer static-gate users to interrupt_before via the facade. Run npm run build in website/.
6. Tests — RE-POINT (do not delete) the 4 dead-site pinning tests at the engine filter (contract unchanged, users still never see neo__): test_invariants.py:535, test_streaming.py:208, test_composition.py:532, test_composition.py:549, test_topologies.py:269. KEEP the _finalize_* stream-arm tests as-is. ADD: (a) a test that output_schema does NOT filter get_state()/channel_values (R2 auto-resume fingerprint read-back), (b) an arun batch-exit neo-free test symmetric to the sync one (guards the :682 deletion), (c) [refine .20] a sub-construct with TWO internal nodes producing the SAME output type asserting last-wins child return (guards multi-producer value-correctness).
7. Audit (anti-band-aid): after step 2, grep for any neo_-stripping logic outside the 2 stream arms + the single _strip_internals helper — must be zero. Independent-review gate before closing.

## Three-surface parity
Compile-layer change (state model -> output_schema) affects all three API surfaces identically; verify a run() through @node, declarative Node.scripted, and programmatic Node()|Modifier still yields neo_-free results (the composition + invariant tests already cover multiple surfaces).

## Refinement (neograph-8unp.20, 2026-07-03) — child output_schema reconciliation
AUTHORITATIVE: child output_schema = child state-model fields NOT starting with neo_ (SAME filter as top-level compile, step 1). This exactly mirrors today's _strip_internals(sub_graph.invoke(...)) then _scan_subgraph_output reverse-scan (last-wins across multiple same-type internal producers).
DO NOT declare child output_schema = 'exactly sub.output field' — that would collapse multi-producer channels and could change which value _scan_subgraph_output (_subconstruct.py:43, reverse-scan of ALL stripped values) returns. The research doc R3 verdict line has been corrected to match.
This is captured in step 1 (child = non-neo_ fields) and step 6(c) (multi-producer test).
notes:
2026-07-03 maintainer-approved framing for Item A (append verbatim into research/implement atoms):

THE KEYS STAY — THE STRIP DIES. The neo_* channels are NOT the disease. Group 1 (oracle gen_id/model, each_item, subgraph_input, loop counters/history, oracle collectors, agent-cycle messages/tool_log/budget) exists because one neograph definition compiles to MANY LangGraph nodes (Oracle = router + N generators + barrier; Each = router + workers + barrier; agent = agent/tools/parse cycle) and those synthesized nodes pass framework data between themselves through state channels — which is the engine's OWN mechanism for inter-node data. Group 2 (schema/node fingerprints) lives in state because checkpoints persist state — that is how versioning metadata durably attaches to a thread. Nobody removes or relocates the information.

The disease is that compile() never DECLARES which channels are framework-internal, so every exit surface is hand-wrapped: ~10 _strip_internals wrap sites (4 exits in run, 4 in arun, sub-construct return) + the stripping arm of _finalize_chunk per streamed chunk. That wrapping is the wrapper-owns-the-execution-path pattern this epic deleted everywhere else; the runner verbs cannot be thin while every one must remember to scrub.

INTERFERENCE vs USE (the distinction that makes this sound): interfering with the engine = intercepting/wrapping its RUNTIME behavior. Using the engine = DECLARING to it at compile time and letting it run untouched. StateGraph natively accepts input_schema / state_schema / output_schema; the engine itself filters invoke results down to output_schema — first-class mechanism for internal working channels (LangGraph's prebuilt agent hides its own step-tracking channels the same way). compile() already knows exactly which fields are user outputs (it built the state model) — declare output_schema = user fields, and enforcement moves from a runtime wrapper we own to a compile-time declaration the engine honors. Same user-visible contract; this is the same move as Operator being a compile-emitted boundary node rather than runtime interception.

RESEARCH QUESTIONS (empirical, against the installed langgraph — decide feasibility per surface):
R1. Does output_schema filter (a) invoke/ainvoke results, (b) stream_mode=values chunks, (c) stream_mode=updates chunks? Expectation: (a) yes, (b) verify, (c) probably NO (updates emits raw per-node writes — a synthesized barrier writing neo_oracle_* would appear). If (c) is unfiltered: a one-line residue survives for updates-mode chunks ONLY, commented as a cited engine gap — documented fallback, not a silent band-aid.
R2. Do channels excluded from output_schema still persist in checkpoints and surface via get_state channel_values? MUST be yes (auto-resume reads fingerprints back there; that path never goes through output filtering). Verify with a fingerprint round-trip.
R3. Sub-construct interaction: child isolated schema + parent type-scan read internal state directly — verify unaffected.
R4 (Item B): does get_stream_writer() return a detectable no-op when no custom-mode consumer is attached, distinguishing live-consumer from non-streaming driver for the warn-once? Verify against installed version; if indistinguishable, the STREAM_CUSTOM flag stays with a citation.

If research answers come back bad (e.g. values-mode chunks unfiltered), the strip STAYS and the outcome is a documented engine-gap justification where today there is an unexamined habit. Either way the mechanism ends up either the engine's, or ours WITH A WRITTEN REASON.
2026-07-03 RESEARCH COMPLETE — empirical, against langgraph 1.2.4. Full report: docs/design/langgraph-output-schema-research-2026-07-03.md. The ticket is RE-SCOPED by evidence:

R1: output_schema filters invoke/ainvoke ONLY; values/updates stream chunks (sync+async) are NOT filtered. CRITICAL: never declare input_schema — it is a hard input filter and silently drops the fingerprints run() seeds through the initial input; declare output_schema alone (keyword-only kwarg in 1.2.4).
R2: excluded channels persist in checkpoints AND get_state is unfiltered — auto-resume fingerprint read-back needs zero change.
R3: the sub-construct CHILD compile can declare output_schema (exactly sub.output field) — kills both strips in make_subgraph_fn.
R4: STREAM_CUSTOM CANNOT be replaced — get_stream_writer() never returns the public no-op sentinel in 1.2.4 (always a live closure); the only discriminator is a private freevars probe, more fragile than the flag. ITEM B RESOLVES AS DOCUMENTED KEEP, not deletion.
R5: managed values do not persist in checkpoints — do not fit fingerprints; output_schema is the right mechanism.

Reality correction: SIX strip sites, not ten (code already consolidated). IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE, final: (1) declare output_schema=user-fields at main compile + sub-construct child compile, input_schema stays unset; (2) DELETE 4 strips: runner.py:509 (run), runner.py:682 (arun), _subconstruct.py:169+:178; (3) KEEP 2 strips: _finalize_by_mode values arm (runner.py:443) + updates arm (:447), each commented citing the research doc (engine gap: streamed chunks unfiltered in 1.2.4); (4) Item B: keep STREAM_CUSTOM, add citation comment; (5) Item C unchanged (docs paragraph); (6) re-point existing pinning tests at the engine filter for the 4 dead sites (contract unchanged: users never see neo_*), keep stream-arm tests as-is; add a test that output_schema does NOT filter get_state (pins the auto-resume assumption against future langgraph upgrades).

title: Verifiable docs Stage B: remark plugin — validate + autolink symbol refs against the manifest (ports from RAMP)
description: Per docs/design/verifiable-docs-research-2026-07-09.md section 5 Stage B (~2-3 days). Port ~/projects/RAMP-Protocol/protocol/website/plugins/remark-proto.mjs swapping loadSchema() for api-manifest.json. Scan inline-code nodes across all .mdx pages. TIERED CONFIDENCE IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT AN OPTION (report section 4): dotted Type.member refs -> resolve or FAIL THE ASTRO BUILD when the type exists but the member doesn't; bare single tokens (compile, run — collide with English) -> autolink ONLY on exact manifest match, NEVER build-failing. Autolink resolved refs to reference/api#<anchor>; validate anchors by slugging the ACTUAL reference-page headings (RAMP-style) until Stage C makes anchors manifest-owned; self-cleaning ignore file (stale entries fail the build — the structural-guard discipline). Port RAMP's plugin unit tests (remark-proto.test.mjs pattern). Catches renamed/removed symbols + dead anchors across all 45 pages with zero page edits.
design:
## Core Invariant

A backticked symbol reference must never silently lie: a dotted `Type.member` reference to a known manifest type with declared fields must either resolve or fail the Astro build; a bare token must resolve-and-link or stay inert — never link to a dead anchor, never fail the build on a false positive. Tiered confidence is the contract: HIGH confidence (dotted member of a fielded type) is build-gating; LOW confidence (bare token, English-collision-prone) is best-effort.

## Implementation Plan

1. CREATE `website/plugins/remark-api.mjs` by porting RAMP's `remark-proto.mjs`, DROPPING the entire directive half (lines 119-149 + the four `*TableNodes`/`vocabParagraph` builders). Keep: the cached `setup()` pattern, the single `visit(tree, 'inlineCode')` autolink pass, the `unresolved` set + throw, the self-cleaning ignore check. Swap `loadSchema()` for reading BOTH `website/src/data/api-manifest.json` and `api-manifest-mcp.json` and concatenating their `symbols` arrays.

2. BUILD the symbol index as `symbols` = `Map<name, {anchor, kind, fields?}>` (name-keyed, unambiguous for the node/Node collision). BUILD `fieldedOwners` = `Set<name>` of symbols whose `fields` array is non-empty (the 14 HARD-tier owners). BUILD `headings` = `Set<slug>` by scanning `website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx` with a FRESH `new GithubSlugger()` and the same fence-aware heading regex RAMP uses (lines 38-44). Load + self-clean the ignore set from `website/api-symbols-ignore.json`.

3. DEFINE neograph tiers (the mandatory report-section-4 mapping):
   - `RE_DOTTED = /^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+\.[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` → HARD IFF the pre-dot token is in `fieldedOwners`. Member in `fields` → autolink if `headings.has(owner.anchor)`. Member missing AND not ignore-listed → add to `unresolved`. (RAMP's `RE_MSG_FIELD` analogue; owner gate is "has fields" not "proto kind".)
   - `RE_BARE_PASCAL = /^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+$/` and `RE_BARE_SNAKE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]+$/` → SOFT. Exact name in `symbols` AND `headings.has(anchor)` → autolink. Otherwise leave as plain inlineCode. NEVER throw.
   - Dotted ref whose owner is a manifest symbol WITHOUT fields (function/exception/class) → INERT (no validation possible, no false positive). Bare token not in symbols → INERT.

4. AUTOLINK target: `reference/api#${anchor}` (RAMP's `REF_PAGE` pattern). Copy the `parent.children[index] = { type: 'link', url, children: [node] }` + `[SKIP, index+1]` return.

5. THROW on non-empty `unresolved` with the RAMP error-message shape (name the symbols, point at the ignore file). This is the build-gate.

6. CREATE `website/api-symbols-ignore.json` with `{"_comment": "...", "ignore": []}` (start empty). Port RAMP's stale-entry check verbatim: a listed token that now resolves → throw.

7. WIRE into `website/astro.config.mjs`: add `markdown: { remarkPlugins: [remarkApi] }`. Import `remarkApi` from `./plugins/remark-api.mjs`. NO remark-directive (no directives).

8. ADD deps to `website/package.json`: `unist-util-visit` (^5), `github-slugger` (^2). NOT needed (proto-specific): mdast-util-from-markdown, micromark-extension-gfm-table, mdast-util-gfm-table, remark-directive. Add `"test": "node --test plugins/*.test.mjs"` to scripts.

9. CREATE `website/plugins/remark-api.test.mjs` porting `remark-proto.test.mjs` lines 14-54 (DROP the directive tests 56-89). Required cases: (a) resolved fielded-member autolinks; (b) unknown member of a fielded type THROWS; (c) dotted ref whose owner is a non-fielded symbol is left alone (no false positive); (d) bare exact-match token autolinks; (e) bare non-symbol token left inert; (f) resolved symbol with no heading is NOT linked (heading-gating); (g) ignore-listed ref does not throw; (h) STALE ignore entry (now resolves) THROWS. Use the same `run()`/`para()`/`has()` helpers.

10. VERIFY end-to-end: `cd website && npm test` (node:test green) then `npm run build` (Astro build green with the plugin wired). Confirm a deliberately-bad `Node.bogus_zzz` ref in a scratch page fails the build, then remove it.

### Out of scope (explicitly Stage C / Stage D)
- Generating reference sections from the manifest (Stage C closes the heading/anchor seam — makes anchors manifest-owned).
- Snippet execution testing (Stage D).
- Any change to the Python manifest generator or its freshness guard (Stage A, landed).
notes:
## Findings

### Reuse target (the exemplar to port, NOT re-derive)
- `~/projects/RAMP-Protocol/protocol/website/plugins/remark-proto.mjs` (187 lines) is the load-bearing port. It already implements: cached `setup()` building a symbol map + a heading set, a single `visit(tree, 'inlineCode')` autolink pass, tiered hard/soft confidence, the `unresolved`-set throw, and a self-cleaning ignore file. Port this shape; swap `loadSchema()` (proto descriptor) for `JSON.parse(readFileSync(api-manifest.json))`.
- `~/projects/RAMP-Protocol/protocol/website/plugins/remark-proto.test.mjs` is the test pattern to port: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, a `run(tree)` helper, `para(value)`/`directive(name,attrs)` mdast builders, and a `has(tree, pred)` predicate. No new test harness — node's built-in test runner.

### What NOT to port (the directive half — proto-specific, biggest simplification)
RAMP runs TWO halves in one pass: (1) directive expansion (`::proto-enum`/`::proto-message`/`::proto-service`/`::proto-vocab` → GFM tables via `fromMarkdown`+`gfmTable`), and (2) the inlineCode autolink. neograph has NO directive equivalent — reference content stays hand-written until Stage C. DROP the entire directive half plus `enumTableNodes`/`messageTableNodes`/`serviceTableNodes`/`vocabParagraph` and the `mdast-util-from-markdown`/`micromark-extension-gfm-table`/`mdast-util-gfm-table`/`remark-directive` deps. The neograph plugin is autolink+validate ONLY. This removes ~80 of RAMP's 187 lines and 4 deps.

### Tiered confidence — the MANDATORY design (report section 4), mapped to neograph
The manifest (Stage A, `website/src/data/api-manifest.json`) has 74 core symbols across kinds: function, class, pydantic_model, dataclass, exception, other. 14 symbols carry a declared `fields` array (the HARD-tier validation set): Node, Construct, Oracle, Each, Loop, Operator, Tool, LintIssue, BlobResult, ToolInteraction, ResourceRef, ProducingCall, VerifyIssue, EachFailure.

- HARD (build-failing): a dotted `Type.member` inline-code token where `Type` is a manifest symbol that HAS a `fields` array. Member in fields → autolink to `reference/api#<Type.anchor>` (when that anchor is a live heading). Member NOT in fields → THROW (collect into `unresolved`, fail build). This is RAMP's `Message.field` analogue — pure manifest validation, FULL coverage, NO heading dependency on the fail path. Regex: `/^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+\.[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`. RAMP's owner-kind gate (`owner.kind === 'message'|'service'|'enum'`) becomes "owner has a `fields` array" (i.e. kind is pydantic_model or dataclass). A dotted ref whose owner is a function/exception/class WITHOUT fields cannot be validated → leave inert (no false positive), mirroring RAMP's "Type.member whose type is not proto is left alone."

title: Loop + dict-form inputs: first iteration passes empty list instead of None for self-reference key
description:
## Bug

When a Node with Loop modifier has dict-form inputs (e.g. inputs={'refine': Draft, 'seed': Config}), the first iteration receives an empty list [] for the self-reference key instead of None.

## Root cause

In factory.py:_extract_input, the Loop re-entry check (line 506-545) only fires when own_val is a truthy list. On first iteration, own_val is [] (empty append-list from state initialization), which is falsy, so the check is skipped. Execution falls through to the fan-in dict path (line 556+), which reads the raw state field 'refine' and gets the empty list []. The unwrap check (line 566) doesn't fire because empty lists are falsy. So [] is passed to the user function as the value for the self-reference key.

## Impact

User code expecting Draft | None for the self-reference key on the first iteration gets [] instead. This causes AttributeError if the code tries input_data['refine'].text or similar attribute access. The user must add defensive checks for empty lists, which contradicts the typed contract.

## Reproduction

Node with inputs={'refine': Draft, 'seed': Config}, outputs=Draft, Loop modifier. On first iteration, input_data['refine'] is [] instead of None.

## Fix direction

In the fan-in dict path of _extract_input, when a Loop node reads its own append-list field and gets an empty list, it should return None for that key instead of the raw empty list. Add: if isinstance(value, list) and not value and node.has_modifier(Loop) and state_key == own_field: value = None
close_reason: Fixed: empty list [] treated as None on first iteration
