title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-0umvg
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-0umvg` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-0umvg/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-0umvg
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-0umvg)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-0umvg --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-0umvg --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-0umvg/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-0umvg codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

## What

`_render_tool_result_for_llm()` (in `_llm.py:605-622`) falls back to
`describe_value()` BAML notation when no renderer is configured, so tool
results are always rendered as BAML. `render_input()` (in `renderers.py:208-222`)
has no such fallback — when renderer is None it returns `input_data` unchanged,
leaving the consumer's `prompt_compiler` to render Pydantic models however it
wants. Result: tool results arrive at the LLM as BAML, prompt-placeholder
inputs arrive as raw Pydantic objects (or JSON via consumer hand-rolling).

Because `render_for_prompt()` on models is only invoked inside `_render_single`
(which is only reached when renderer is non-None), the model-level projection
hook is dead code unless a renderer is explicitly configured. This subtlety is
not documented; consumers add `render_for_prompt()` methods to models and they
silently never run.

## Direction

**BAML (`describe_value()`) is the canonical rendering.** XmlRenderer /
DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer are historical pluggability — the answer for
every real consumer is BAML because that is what tool results already use by
default, and mixing formats inside a single prompt is strictly worse than
uniform BAML.

### Dispatch (in precedence order, applied to every Pydantic input)

1. **`model.render_for_prompt()` wins if defined.** Consumer-authored
   projection has the highest priority. The returned value is used directly:
   - If it returns `str` → insert verbatim into the placeholder.
   - If it returns a `BaseModel` → BAML-render the returned model (honoring
     its own `exclude` fields and its own `render_for_prompt()` if any).
   The renderer configuration is IRRELEVANT for this path.
2. **Otherwise, BAML-render the original model** via `describe_value()`.
   This already honors `field_info.exclude` today (see `describe_type.py:403`).
   Consumer marks non-presentable fields with `Field(..., exclude=True)` on
   the source model and they disappear from the prompt automatically.

This is symmetric with how tool results already work — BAML by default, no
configuration required. `render_for_prompt()` stays and remains the escape
hatch for curated views (truncated snippets, renamed tags, computed fields).

### Remove the renderer-config gate

`configure_llm(renderer=...)` stops being required for ANY of the above. The
`Renderer` abstraction remains in the codebase for legacy XmlRenderer /
DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer opt-ins, but:

- Default config produces BAML everywhere, no opt-in needed.
- `render_for_prompt()` runs unconditionally.
- `Field(exclude=True)` is honored unconditionally via `describe_value()`.
- Consumers that opt into a non-BAML renderer trade away the default
  symmetry — their choice, their responsibility.

## Why this matters

A consumer using NeoGraph gets BAML for tool results "for free" and must
reinvent rendering for prompt inputs. Concretely, `piarch-neo4j-driver` has
`HydratedResearch.render_for_prompt() -> ResearchPresentation` (comment says
"NeoGraph BAML-renders the returned model") — which never executed, because
piarch never wired a renderer. The same project's `prompt_compiler`
accumulated ~60 lines of ad-hoc `model_dump()` / `model_dump_json()` / alias
logic to compensate, and that logic has been the source of multiple bugs
(most recent: `{uc_context}` placeholder never filled because the aliasing
table doesn't know about it; pipeline silently no-opped research phase for
8 days before a strict-mode refactor turned the failure loud).

The framework advertises `render_for_prompt()` in the dispatch hierarchy
("model.render_for_prompt() > node.renderer > construct.renderer > global >
None" in `node.py:119` / `construct.py:94`), but without an active renderer
the whole chain collapses to None and input data stays raw. Consumer
expectation (matching the tool-result path) is that default behavior is
BAML, with `render_for_prompt()` available as escape hatch when needed.

## Expectations after delivery

- Input-data and tool-result rendering produce BAML by default via
  `describe_value()`. One code path, one format.
- `render_for_prompt()` on a model ALWAYS runs when that model flows into
  a prompt placeholder, regardless of renderer configuration. Its return is
  either used verbatim (str) or BAML-rendered (BaseModel).
- `Field(..., exclude=True)` filters fields from BAML output unconditionally.
- `configure_llm(renderer=...)` becomes optional; consumers with no renderer
  set still get BAML for inputs.
- Existing consumers that already set `renderer=XmlRenderer(...)` continue to
  work identically (no behavior change when a renderer is explicitly set).

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_render_input_baml_default.py` — define
a Pydantic model with mixed field types and one `exclude=True` field; call
the input-rendering pipeline with NO renderer configured; assert the result
is a BAML string matching `describe_value(instance)` output and the excluded
field is absent.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_render_for_prompt_precedence.py` —
model defines `render_for_prompt()` returning (a) a string and (b) another
BaseModel in two parametrized cases; with NO renderer configured, assert the
projection IS invoked, strings pass through verbatim, and returned models
are BAML-rendered. Then ALSO assert the same behavior when an XmlRenderer
IS configured — render_for_prompt() still wins, regardless of renderer.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_parity_tool_and_input.py` — given
the same Pydantic instance, assert that its rendering as a tool result and
as a prompt input produce the same BAML output under default configuration.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_exclude_fields_honored.py` — model with
some `Field(exclude=True)` fields; assert BAML output via both the tool-result
path and the prompt-input path omits the excluded fields. Nested models
with exclude fields also covered.

**E2E**: `tests/e2e/test_dispatch_rendering_parity.py` — run a two-node
construct where node A's output is consumed by node B's prompt AND by a tool
call; assert both paths produce the same BAML string with default config
(no renderer explicitly set).

## Acceptance

- Default render path for prompt inputs is BAML via `describe_value()`,
  matching tool-result rendering.
- `render_for_prompt()` is called unconditionally (no renderer gate) and
  takes precedence over direct BAML rendering.
- `render_input(model, renderer=None)` returns a BAML string, not a raw
  model.
- `Field(..., exclude=True)` is honored on the BAML default path.
- Tool-result BAML and input BAML go through the same `describe_value()`
  function — no "two flavors of BAML."
- Consumer `piarch-neo4j-driver` can delete its hand-rolled `model_dump()` /
  `model_dump_json()` / alias logic from its `prompt_compiler` and rely on
  the framework; its existing `render_for_prompt()` on `HydratedResearch`
  becomes live without any other change.
- README and module-level docstring on `renderers.py` / `describe_type.py`
  document BAML as the canonical default and `render_for_prompt()` as the
  primary escape hatch. XmlRenderer / DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer are
  documented as legacy opt-ins.
design:
## Root Cause
render_input(input_data, renderer=None) returns input_data unchanged at line 216-217 of renderers.py. _render_single() is only called when renderer is not None. This means:
1. Pydantic models flow through as raw objects (no BAML)
2. render_for_prompt() is never checked
3. Tool results get BAML via describe_value() but prompt inputs don't

## Fix Approach
Minimal change in render_input() and _render_single():
- Remove the early return on renderer=None
- Make _render_single accept renderer=None
- When renderer is None: check render_for_prompt() first, then BAML via describe_value() for BaseModel/list[BaseModel], else pass through unchanged
- This matches the tool-result path exactly
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_renderers.py::TestRenderInputBAMLDefault (5 tests), ::TestRenderForPromptUnconditional (4 tests), ::TestToolInputRenderingParity (3 tests)
- 11 of 12 new tests FAIL — all demonstrate the asymmetry
- Root cause: render_input() line 216-217 short-circuits on renderer=None, returning raw Pydantic objects. _render_single() is never called without a renderer, so render_for_prompt() is dead code and describe_value() BAML fallback never fires.
## Trace Similar
Pattern: 'fallback path divergence' — renderer=None skips rendering entirely at 4 sites:
1. renderers.py:216 — render_input() early return (ROOT)
2. _dispatch.py:226 — _render_input() skips call when renderer=None (CALLER — fix by always calling render_input)
3. _llm.py:616 — tool result rendering (CORRECT — has describe_value fallback)
4. _llm.py:923 — render_prompt inspector (CALLER — same fix as #2)

Fix strategy: fix render_input() to handle renderer=None with BAML fallback, then callers 2 and 4 always call render_input regardless of renderer config.
## Architect Review
1. Root cause: CORRECT — render_input early-returns on renderer=None
2. Fix minimality: LOW risk — ~30 lines across 3 files (renderers.py, _dispatch.py, _llm.py)
3. Regression risk: LOW — only behavioral change is raw->BAML for unrendered models, which is the correct behavior
4. Architecture: GOOD — symmetric with tool-result path, uses shared describe_value
5. Test coverage: 12 tests covering all facets
Verdict: ALL_LOW — proceed to fix
close_reason: Fixed: render_input now BAML-renders Pydantic models by default, symmetric with tool-result rendering. render_for_prompt() fires unconditionally.

title: Oracle over an agent/act node with multiple upstream inputs OR dict-form outputs: bundle-port synthesis
description: Follow-on to neograph-qot6 (single-producer input-port synthesis, landed). qot6 auto-wraps Oracle-over-agent when the agent has ZERO or ONE upstream producer (single-type inputs, or a single-key dict-form fan-in) -- the value maps cleanly onto the single-value subgraph boundary (neo_subgraph_input). Two sub-cases stay fail-loud: (1) MULTIPLE distinct dict-form upstream producers -- the single-value boundary can't carry N values; needs a synthesized 'packer' node in the parent that bundles the N upstreams into one port model, plus an 'unpacker' inside the sub-construct (or a prompt-var mapping) so the agent still sees the original keys. (2) dict-form (multi-output) agent OUTPUTS -- the sub-construct has a single output boundary port. Both are genuinely ambiguous (prompt variable surface for the bundle) so were left fail-loud with precise ConstructErrors. See src/neograph/_fan_agent.py::_unsupported_reason and docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md.
notes: 2026-07-07 verification note for this seat (Wave 8): the shipped qot6 agent-fan tests assert merged-N (wiring) but NOT that each isolated cycle SAW the upstream value — the verifier's echo probe (scratchpad/probe_qot6.py pattern: prompt_compiler renders upstream into the message, echo fake reflects it, merge concatenates) proved value delivery manually. When this seat touches the fan tests, COMMIT that echo-style value-delivery assertion for the single-type, dict-form, and DI shapes so the property is pinned, not probe-only.
close_reason: Bundle-port synthesis. (1) Oracle over agent with MULTIPLE dict-form producers now supported via packer-port synthesis: wrap_fan_over_agents takes scripted_lookup; _expand_agent_node returns [packer, wrapped_sub] for multi-producer. Synthesized parent packer bundles N upstreams into a _NeoAgentPort_* model; inner per-key unpacker nodes re-expose the ORIGINAL producer names inside the sub-construct so the agent's dict-form fan-in + prompt-var surface is unchanged. Scoped to Oracle; Each/Loop multi-input stay fail-loud (precise error). (2) Dict-form multi-output agent OUTPUTS kept fail-loud by design (single output boundary + undefined N-way merge of secondary outputs would silently drop declared outputs) - sharpened message + should_fail fixture. Moved oracle_over_agent_multiple_inputs.py should_fail->should_pass; added oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py should_fail. WAVE-8 value-delivery pins committed: TestOracleOverAgentValueDelivery asserts each isolated cycle SAW its upstream value for single-type/dict-form/DI shapes (echo prompt-compiler+echo ReAct fake+concat merge); TestOracleOverAgentMultiInputBundle asserts BOTH bundled values reach each cycle. @node-surface multi-input parity test added. Design addendum in docs/design. Full suite: 2650 passed; ruff check clean.

title: Each over empty list deadlocks pipeline — should produce empty dict
description:
When a node with map_over receives an empty list from its upstream, the Each fan-out produces no output. Downstream nodes that depend on the Each node's output never fire, and the pipeline terminates silently.

Repro: 
1. Node A returns []
2. Node B has map_over='node_a', map_key='id'
3. Node C depends on node_b output
4. Pipeline stops after Node A — Node B produces nothing, Node C never runs.

Expected: Each over [] should produce {} (empty dict output), allowing downstream nodes to proceed. Same as map(f, []) = [] in any language.

Discovered in piarch rw-ingestion pipeline: find_duplicate_candidates returns 0 pairs → resolve_duplicate (Each) deadlocks → apply_dedup never runs → entire pipeline terminates after decompose phase.
design:
## Architecture Decision

Follow the __loop_exit_ pattern: compiler-generated bypass node for empty collections.

### Topology

Normal (N > 0):
  prev → each_router → [Send(fan, item) × N] → fan → barrier → next

Empty (N = 0):
  prev → each_router → [Send(__each_empty_{name}, state)] → __each_empty_ → barrier → next

### Implementation

All changes in compiler layer (_wire_each and _add_each_oracle_fused).

1. _wire_each: register __each_empty_{fan_name} node that writes {field_name: {}}.
   Wire: __each_empty_ → barrier (alongside existing fan → barrier).
   Router: when unique_items is empty, return [Send(empty_name, state_dict)].
   path_map: add empty_name alongside fan_name.

2. _add_each_oracle_fused: same pattern for M=0 case.
   When items collection is empty, Send to bypass node instead of M×N generators.

### Why this is correct

- Wiring decision (compiler layer), not execution logic (factory layer)
- Follows __loop_exit_ convention — compiler-generated nodes with __ prefix
- Zero value for Each is {} (empty dict) — map(f, []) = [] semantics
- Downstream list[X] consumers see list({}.values()) = [] — correct
- Checkpointing: state has field={}, resume works
- 2 call sites, same pattern, no shared helper yet (extract at 3)

### Core invariant

Each over an empty collection produces an empty dict result, not a pipeline deadlock. Downstream nodes always fire.
notes:
## Triage

Root cause: _wire_each in compiler.py line 811-813. When each_router gets an empty collection, it returns [] (empty Send list). LangGraph interprets this as 'no successors' → graph stops → downstream nodes never fire.

Location: src/neograph/compiler.py:783 each_router() inside _wire_each()

Fix approach: When unique_items is empty, return a Send to the barrier_name directly (with current state, no neo_each_item). The barrier already returns {} (pass-through). The Each field's state will be the default (None or empty dict from reducer), which is the correct 'empty result' semantics.

Alternative: Return [Send(barrier_name, state_dict)] to skip fan-out and go straight to barrier. Need to verify barrier_name is registered before the router fires (it is — added at line 825).

Risk: LOW — only changes behavior for empty collections (new code path). Non-empty collections unchanged.

Regression test: @node with Each over empty list, assert downstream node fires and receives empty dict.
## Verified fix approach

Pattern: add __each_empty_{name} bypass node that writes {field_name: {}} when collection is empty. Router returns [Send(bypass, state)] instead of []. Bypass → barrier edge added alongside fan → barrier.

Tested in pure LangGraph:
- Non-empty: unchanged behavior  
- Empty: downstream fires with results={} (empty dict, correct semantics)
- list[X] consumers see [] (list of empty dict values)

Backfire risks checked:
1. Each×Oracle fusion — same fix needed in _add_each_oracle_fused (M=0 case)
2. Each on Construct — uses _wire_each, fix applies automatically
3. List consumers — list({}.values()) = [], correct
4. Checkpointing — state has results={}, resume works
5. skip_when — fires after node, not at router level, N/A

Node name: __each_empty_{fan_name} (convention matches __loop_exit_)
## Trace similar
_add_each_oracle_fused (compiler.py:417 flat_router) has the same M=0 bug — returns empty sends when collection is empty. Same fix needed: __each_empty_ bypass node.

Also checked: _add_subgraph (Construct with Each) — goes through _wire_each, same fix applies automatically.
close_reason: Fixed: __each_empty_ bypass node handles empty collections. Downstream proceeds with {}.

title: gm-3: Lifecycle/factory split — create _execute.py, delete _observability.py, rename _modifier_io.py → _input_shape.py
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §4
- docs/design/god-module-analysis-2026-05-20.md Clusters B + D + G + Q1 + Q2 + Q5

## The problem
factory.py mixes 3 change axes: A (wrapper assembly = make_node_fn, _make_raw_wrapper), B (lifecycle orchestration = _execute_node), C (sub-construct = make_subgraph_fn — gm-4 handles this one).

`_execute_node` is in factory.py because it's the closure body called by make_node_fn's returned wrapper — that's a call-graph fact, not a change-axis fact. A change to lifecycle (new step, reorder, observability span) touches `_execute_node` and nothing in `make_node_fn`; vice versa.

`_observability.py` is a 24-line misnamed stub. `_extract_context` is prompt-context extraction (LLM context fields), not observability. Sole caller is `_execute_node`.

`_modifier_io.py` is misnamed — after gm-1 moves `_apply_skip_when` out, what remains is pure input-shape read-side: classify shape + extract typed input. Should be `_input_shape.py`.

## The fix
1. Create `src/neograph/_execute.py` with single responsibility: "Runs one node invocation through the standard preamble → dispatch → postamble lifecycle"
2. Move `_execute_node` from `factory.py:89-130` into `_execute.py`
3. Move `_type_name` from `factory.py:77-86` into `_execute.py` (private helper; `_make_raw_wrapper` keeps `from neograph._execute import _type_name`)
4. Move `_extract_context` from `_observability.py` into `_execute.py` as a private helper (sole caller is `_execute_node`)
5. Delete `src/neograph/_observability.py` (now empty)
6. Rename `src/neograph/_modifier_io.py` → `src/neograph/_input_shape.py` (one-line docstring: "Read-side: classifies a node's input shape against state and extracts the typed input")
7. Update all importers
8. factory.py:159 becomes `from neograph._execute import _execute_node`

## Dependencies
After gm-1 (rename `_state_io.py` and pull `_apply_skip_when` out of `_modifier_io.py`). Otherwise the rename to `_input_shape.py` would happen with `_apply_skip_when` still inside, which is wrong.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestLifecycleSeparation` + `TestInputShapeRename` + cohesion fan-out metric
**Test type**: structural-guard + cohesion metric
**What it exercises**:
1. `_execute.py` exists; defines `_execute_node`, `_type_name`, `_extract_context` (the latter two as private helpers)
2. `factory.py` no longer defines `_execute_node`, `_type_name`, or any context-extraction logic
3. `_observability.py` does NOT exist (or is a removed-stub marker for one release)
4. `_input_shape.py` exists; `_modifier_io.py` does not
5. `_input_shape.py` does NOT define `_apply_skip_when` (it was moved out via gm-1)
6. **Cohesion fan-out metric**: count external modules importing from each new module. `_execute.py` should be imported by factory.py (one importer) — the lifecycle driver has high fan-in by design. `_input_shape.py` imported only by `_execute.py` (single consumer means the abstraction is real).

**Expected initial state**: failing — modules don't exist; current factory.py contains the functions; `_observability.py` exists.
**Persistence**: stays.

Order: write all the failing structural assertions FIRST → run → fails → create modules + move code + delete stub + rename → re-run → passes.

## Acceptance
- `_execute.py` exists with `_execute_node` as public + `_type_name`, `_extract_context` private
- `_observability.py` deleted
- `_input_shape.py` exists with InputShape, _classify_input_shape, _extract_input, _extract_*; no `_apply_skip_when`
- factory.py contains ONLY make_node_fn, _make_raw_wrapper, make_subgraph_fn (gm-4 will extract the last)
- All callers updated
- `make quality` green
close_reason: Created _execute.py with _execute_node + _type_name + _extract_context; renamed _modifier_io.py -> _input_shape.py; deleted _observability.py; factory.py updated; TestLifecycleSeparation + TestInputShapeRename guards added (9 tests)

title: Dedupe _type_name helper across factory.py and construct.py
description:
HIGH-02 from code review 040426_2207. Flagged independently by 2 agents (dry + consistency).

Two definitions:
- src/neograph/factory.py:71 — _type_name(t: Any) -> str | None (returns None for None input)
- src/neograph/construct.py:282 — _type_name(tp: Any) -> str (returns literal 'None' for None input)

Same name, divergent return types and None handling. grep -n '^def _type_name' src/neograph/ returns both.

Lowest-friction fix: rename the construct.py version to _fmt_type. The two helpers serve different roles — factory uses None for log-field omission, construct uses 'None' for error rendering. Trying to merge them requires settling the None convention and risking behavioral changes in logging.

Alternative: promote a single canonical helper to a shared module (e.g. src/neograph/_types.py) with one agreed-upon None convention.

Source: .claude/code-review/040426_2207/synthesis.md HIGH-02
close_reason: Wave 1: HIGH-01 tightened fan-out assertion in TestEach::test_fanout_over_collection (line 319) and TestNodeMap::test_map_end_to_end_fanout (line 386) with set equality + per-key payload. HIGH-02 renamed construct.py's _type_name to _fmt_type (7 call sites); factory.py's _type_name stays. 99/99 passing.

fix is designed, so the fix addresses every instance — not just the

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design's Fix Approach.

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** (NOT just the file where the bug
   manifests). Choose the method by disease shape:

     `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" zrcln`
     then merge the per-lens rows into the disposition table below.
   - **SYNTACTIC** (one exact literal / regex-able form): a single
     grep / AST scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out.

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>
   ```

title: Sweep verification for zrcln
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored AND a
structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on zrcln
- fix atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** using the EXACT same command from the
   codebase-scan atom.

2. **Compute the diff** — every Phase 1b row must have a verified
   post-fix disposition (MIGRATE done / ALLOWLIST holds / DEFER
   ticket open):

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (zrcln)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   ```

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT and record the new location. The deterministic check is the
   instance-count diff (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists** banning future instances
   of the disease pattern. Required when the disposition table has
   >=1 MIGRATE row; N/A (record why) when every row is ALLOWLIST/DEFER
   since no code changed — an all-ALLOWLIST fix is suspicious. The
   guard MUST:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py`
     - Include positive AND negative meta-tests
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (Non-regex guards have no regex-slip case; pos+neg suffice.)

   Record:

   ```bash
   bd update zrcln --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File / Class / Meta-tests: ..."
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

```bash
bd label add zrcln sweep:complete
```
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-p8wz
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-p8wz` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-p8wz/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-p8wz
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-p8wz)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-p8wz --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-p8wz --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-p8wz/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-p8wz codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

design:
## Core Invariant (unchanged)
The api-manifest.json is the single source of truth: every generated reference section renders FROM the manifest (never re-introspects neograph), and every generated heading's Starlight slug MUST equal the manifest's anchor for that symbol -- so the manifest owns both ends of every cross-link.

## Implementation Plan v2 (maintainer decisions applied 2026-07-10)

DECISION 1 (anchor scheme) = KIND-NAMESPACE ANCHORS IN STAGE A. DECISION 2 (lint section) = ENRICH MANIFEST FIRST (precursor neograph-uw54v); lint section EXCLUDED from rfl7b, rendered later by neograph-cvjfm. DECISION 3 (error tree) = generate tree STRUCTURE from manifest, keep hand-authored annotations column.

1. ANCHOR DISAMBIGUATION (prerequisite for all per-symbol generation) -- in scripts/gen_api_manifest.py, kind-namespace the anchors for symbols whose bare-name slug collides. VERIFIED collisions: node(fn)/Node(class) AND tool(fn)/Tool(class) both slug to one anchor. Give each colliding symbol a distinct, deterministic anchor (e.g. append a kind suffix for the class or function member of a collision) so slug(heading) can equal it. Regenerate website/src/data/api-manifest.json.
2. RE-PIN the Stage-A snapshot/slug-contract guard (tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py L1) for the new anchor scheme -- this is a deliberate Stage-A contract change consumed by Stage B.
3. FIX remark-api.mjs's false premise (L64 'manifest Python slug is dedup-free (unique names)') -- names are unique, slugs were NOT; after step 1 they are unique again, so update the comment/logic to reflect the disambiguated scheme.
4. RENDER (Python codegen -> committed .mdx partial(s), mirroring Stage-A commit-artifact + freshness-guard):
   - Per-symbol signature blocks: heading text = disambiguated symbol name so Starlight slug == manifest anchor; signature in a fenced block under the heading (rustdoc layout). All 74 symbols now that anchors are unique.
   - Pydantic field tables (14 symbols) from manifest symbols[].fields.
   - Error-hierarchy TREE structure from exception_hierarchy[]; KEEP the hand-authored '(ValueError)' base annotations + curated em-dash descriptions as a hand-written column (DECISION 3) -- do not let manifest doc-first-line silently reword them.
   - EXCLUDE the lint-kind table (DECISION 2) -- stays hand-written until neograph-uw54v enriches the manifest; then neograph-cvjfm renders it.
5. FRESHNESS GUARD (pytest): committed partial matches regenerated output; assert single-heading-per-anchor (exception symbols appear in both symbols[] and exception_hierarchy[] -- keep the tree a fenced block so its anchors are not emitted twice, review LOW finding).
6. Sequence incrementally, prose stays hand-written (section-level generation).

## Out of scope (tracked)
- Lint-kind rendering -> neograph-cvjfm (after neograph-uw54v).
- Manifest lint enrichment -> neograph-uw54v.
notes:
## Findings

REUSE TARGET (do NOT re-introspect): the Stage A manifest is already the single source of truth for everything Stage C renders. scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:351 build_manifest() emits symbols[] (name, kind, anchor, signature, fields[], bases[], doc), exception_hierarchy[] (name, parent, anchor, doc), and lint_issue_kinds[]. Verified coverage in the committed website/src/data/api-manifest.json: 74 symbols (29 function / 18 class / 13 pydantic_model / 10 exception / 2 dataclass / 2 other), 14 symbols carry field tables, exception_hierarchy has 11 entries, lint_issue_kinds has 10. Every one of the four candidate generated sections (per-symbol signature blocks, Pydantic field tables, error-hierarchy tree, lint issue kinds) is ALREADY fully backed by manifest data. Stage C is a RENDERER over this JSON, not a new introspector.

REUSE the slug contract: scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:92 slug() is github-slugger-2.0.0-compatible and snapshot-pinned (JS-authoritative) by tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py (L1). Each manifest entry already carries anchor=slug(name). Stage C must render headings whose text is the bare symbol NAME so Starlight's own slugger reproduces exactly that anchor -- that IS 'manifest-owned anchors'.

CONFIRMED anchor-drift seam Stage C closes (measured, not assumed): current reference headings embed the signature, so their Starlight slug diverges from the manifest anchor. Node heading 'Node(name, *, mode, outputs, ...)' slugs to 'nodename--mode-outputs-...' but manifest anchor is 'node'; 'run(graph, *, ...) -> dict' slugs to 'rungraph--...' vs anchor 'run'; likewise lint/Oracle/Each. Only the few headings that already reduce to a bare token link today (@node(...) -> node, compile(...) -> compile, ToolInteraction -> toolinteraction) -- which is exactly the partial-SOFT-coverage seam remark-api.mjs:18-21 documents. Making the heading text = symbol name makes slug(heading)==manifest anchor for ALL symbols, so the Stage B SOFT tier (remark-api.mjs:153) fully autolinks and the HARD tier's owner-anchor target (remark-api.mjs:139) always exists.

MECHANISM -- three candidates from the design doc, weighed:
 (a) Python codegen emitting a COMMITTED .mdx partial + pytest freshness guard. RECOMMENDED. Reuses the existing Python generator + slug() (one script, one data model). Emits real markdown headings so Starlight owns rehype-slug anchors AND the right-hand TOC natively. Follows the established Amplify-can't-run-Python pattern: commit the artifact, guard freshness in pytest (mirror tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py / tests/test_spec_loader.py::test_pipeline_schema_in_sync).
 (b) Astro component reading the JSON (optionally via content collections + Zod). Gives type-safe access and no second generated file, and a component CAN emit <h3 id={anchor}> for exact manifest-owned anchors -- BUT Starlight builds the page TOC from the MDX markdown AST, not JSX component output, so component-rendered headings drop out of the right-sidebar TOC. That regresses the reference page's navigability. Flag as the fallback, not the default.
 (c) content collections + Zod schema over the manifest -- this is an access-layer detail orthogonal to (a)/(b), usable under either; not a standalone mechanism.

CURRENT vs stale: the RAMP directive half (::proto-enum / ::proto-message table generation) was DELIBERATELY DROPPED in Stage B (remark-api.mjs:12-16) precisely because reference content 'stays hand-written until Stage C generates it from the manifest.' Stage C is the sanctioned place to reintroduce generation -- but as codegen/partials, not remark directives.

## Relevant Code
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:92 slug() -- the anchor contract; reuse verbatim for heading generation.
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:258 _symbol_entry / :199 _declared_pydantic_fields / :301 _exception_hierarchy / :326 extract_lint_issue_kinds -- the four data sources already shaped for the four candidate sections.
- website/src/data/api-manifest.json -- committed data Stage C renders (do not re-derive).
- website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx -- the hand-written page to incrementally replace; keep the prose intro (lines 1-40) and per-symbol prose bullets hand-written, generate the signature block + field table + error tree + lint-kind table. Current hand-written error tree is an ASCII fence at lines 658-670; lint-kind table at lines 515-524; these are the lowest-risk first sections to generate (pure tabular, no prose).
- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:62-74 -- the heading-slug harvester; once headings become bare names its 'headings' set aligns with manifest anchors and SOFT/HARD linking becomes complete. remark-api.mjs:18-21 documents the seam Stage C removes.
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py -- the freshness-guard exemplar to copy for any newly committed generated .mdx partial.
- website/astro.config.mjs:11-13 -- remarkApi wiring; website/package.json:11 'npm test' runs node:test on plugins/*.test.mjs (run after any plugin-visible change).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Anchor collision on dedup: @node(...) already slugs to 'node'; a generated '### Node' heading also slugs to 'node' and github-slugger would dedup the second to 'node-1', breaking the manifest anchor. The @node decorator symbol name in the manifest is 'node' and the class is 'Node' -- BOTH slug(name) to 'node'. This is a REAL manifest-level anchor collision (two public symbols, same slug). Decide the disambiguation (e.g. keep @node prose hand-written and generate only the Node class section, or give one a distinct anchor in the generator) BEFORE generating both, or the freshness/link contract breaks. Prefix any resolution NEEDS USER INPUT if it changes the manifest anchor scheme (that touches the Stage A snapshot test).
- TOC regression under the Astro-component mechanism (b): component headings vanish from Starlight's right-sidebar TOC. Mechanism (a) avoids this.
- Generated-MDX churn (the design-doc-named failure mode, section 5 Stage C): keep generation strictly section-level; never regenerate prose. A whole-page generator would flatten the hand-written narrative bullets (api.mdx lines 78-99 etc.) that have no manifest equivalent.
- Staleness window inherited from Stage A: a committed generated partial is only as fresh as the last green pytest run; the freshness guard + the Stage B build-fail-on-dead-ref backstop are the mitigations (same contract as the manifest itself).
- 'missing'-kind symbols: generator emits a 'missing' entry if an __all__ name has no object (gen_api_manifest.py:293); Stage C rendering must handle/skip that kind (currently zero in the manifest, but the renderer must not crash if one appears).
- MDX-partial import + heading anchors: if mechanism (a) imports a partial as an MDX component, headings inside an imported component may NOT get rehype-slug IDs/TOC the way inline markdown does. Prefer generating INTO the page body (or an include mechanism that preserves markdown headings) over JSX import, or verify anchor+TOC survival with 'npm run build' before committing.
## Codebase Disease Scan (rfl7b)

Pattern: hand-written reference-doc sections that transcribe manifest-owned API data (per-symbol signatures, field tables, error-hierarchy tree, lint issue kinds) AND whose heading slugs drift from the manifest anchor for that symbol.

Scan method: bounded/enumerable content scan of the whole docs tree (website/src/content/docs). NOT the multi-agent semantic code-review — that scans src/ Python for dedup/consistency/layering anti-patterns and does not inspect MDX content; applying it here is a category error. The manifest-backed section shapes are a finite known set, enumerable by grep.

Scan commands (reproducible verbatim):
  grep -rcn 'NeographError (base)' website/src/content/docs --include='*.mdx'          # error-hierarchy trees
  grep -rlEn '^#{2,4} .*\(.*\)' website/src/content/docs --include='*.mdx'             # signature-in-heading (anchor-drift)
  grep -rln 'loop_condition_unregistered|template_placeholder_unresolvable' website/src/content/docs --include='*.mdx'  # lint-kind tables
Manifest shape verified: lint_issue_kinds = bare list of 10 name-strings (no severity/meaning); exception_hierarchy = 11 {name,parent,anchor,doc}; symbols[] carry signature+fields.

Total instances found: 6 dispositioned below.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | reference/api.mdx:~659 | error-hierarchy tree 'NeographError (base)' | MIGRATE | fully manifest-backed (exception_hierarchy, 11 entries); zero prose; anchor-owned |
| 2 | reference/api.mdx (31 headings, e.g. :482 lint(...)) | signature-in-heading '### name(sig...)' | MIGRATE | THE anchor-drift seam; heading slug embeds signature and diverges from manifest anchor. Emit bare-name heading + fenced signature from symbols[].signature |
| 3 | reference/api.mdx (14 symbols) | Pydantic field bullet blocks | MIGRATE | manifest symbols[].fields backs these; render from manifest |
| 4 | reference/api.mdx lint issue-kind listing | lint kinds | MIGRATE (name column only) | manifest lint_issue_kinds gives NAMES only; severity/meaning stay hand-written prose |
| 5 | concepts/lint.mdx:64-75 | lint-kind table (Kind+Severity+Meaning) | ALLOWLIST | editorial concept-page table; documents a DIFFERENT kind-set than manifest (from_input/template_/loop_/resource_ vs manifest's act_mode_/ask_human_/llm_kwargs_); manifest carries no severity/meaning, so it is NOT a manifest transcription and owns no Stage-B-validated anchor. Not the Stage-C disease. |
| 6 | node-api/*.mdx, concepts/*.mdx (prose 'raises ConstructError' etc.) | inline prose symbol refs | ALLOWLIST | prose mentions, not structured manifest renderings; Stage B remark-api already validates/autolinks these inline refs |

No DEFER rows: every found instance is either MIGRATE (within api.mdx, this ticket's scope) or ALLOWLIST (editorial/prose, not a manifest transcription). Scope unchanged from research plan: Stage C is a manifest renderer over reference/api.mdx.
## Architect Review

- [HIGH] Finding: The manifest has DUPLICATE anchors and the plan enumerates only ONE of them. Both `node`(fn)/`Node`(class) AND `tool`(fn)/`Tool`(class) slug to the same anchor (verified in api-manifest.json: two collisions, not one). The Core Invariant ('every generated heading's slug == the manifest anchor; manifest owns both ends') is UNSATISFIABLE when two distinct public symbols share one anchor on a single rendered page -- github-slugger dedups the 2nd heading to `node-1`, which is NOT in the manifest. Step 5's option-1 ('keep @node hand-written, generate only the Node class') does NOT preserve the invariant: the hand-written @node heading still slugs to `node` on the same page, forcing the generated `### Node` to `node-1`. The only invariant-preserving fix disambiguates the anchor SCHEME in gen_api_manifest.py -- which the plan itself gates as NEEDS USER INPUT (it mutates the Stage A snapshot-pinned contract that Stage B consumes). Note remark-api.mjs:64 already rests on a false premise ('manifest's Python slug is dedup-free (unique names)') -- names are unique, slugs are NOT. Suggestion: get a human decision on the anchor-disambiguation policy (e.g. kind-namespaced anchors) applied to BOTH pairs, update the Stage A snapshot in the same commit, before generating any per-symbol section.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The lint-issue-kind section is NOT a clean manifest render, contradicting step 4's claim it is 'already fully in the manifest' and 'pure-tabular, zero-prose'. The live table (api.mdx:515-524) has 3 columns (Kind/Severity/Meaning); the manifest carries bare NAMES only. Worse, the name-SETS diverge: the docs document from_input/from_config/from_input_model/from_config_model (4 DI kinds the manifest's AST-walk MISSES because they are constructed dynamically, not kind='literal'), while the manifest has 7 kinds the docs lack (act_mode_all_idempotent_tools, ask_human_in_mutating_node, llm_kwargs_missing, template_*, tool_requires_async_driver). Overlap is only 3. A 'name column only' migration would DELETE the 4 documented DI kinds, ADD 7 undocumented kinds with empty severity/meaning, and strip the Severity+Meaning columns that are the table's whole value -- a doc REGRESSION. Design-doc Open Question #3 (manifest behavioral metadata vs 'second implementation of the docs') is unresolved and governs this exact section. Suggestion: descope the lint-kind table from Stage C (keep hand-written), OR file a precursor ticket to enrich lint_issue_kinds with severity/meaning AND capture the DI kinds before migrating.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 4's premise that the error-hierarchy tree 'carries no hand-written narrative to lose' is only partly true. The live tree (api.mdx:658-670) embeds hand-authored annotations -- base-class notes like 'ConstructError (ValueError)' and per-node em-dash descriptions ('-- assembly-time validation failures'). The manifest exception_hierarchy carries {name,parent,anchor,doc} where doc is the docstring first-line; it does NOT carry the '(ValueError)' base note and the doc first-line may not match the curated descriptions. A pure-manifest render loses the base annotation and can reword descriptions. Suggestion: verify manifest `doc` fields reproduce the intended text before generating, or keep the annotation column hand-written.

- [LOW] Finding: Exception symbols appear in BOTH symbols[] (kind=exception, e.g. anchor `constructerror`) and exception_hierarchy[] with the SAME anchor. If Stage C generates per-symbol signature headings for all of symbols[] (disposition row #2 = all 31 signature headings, incl. the 10 exceptions) while also rendering the error tree, the tree MUST stay a fenced block (no headings) or the exception anchor is emitted twice. Currently the tree is a fence, so this is safe -- flag it so the renderer does not accidentally emit `### ConstructError` from both paths. Suggestion: assert single-heading-per-anchor in the Stage C freshness guard (step 6).

- [LOW] Finding: Reuse posture is correct and verified -- signatures/fields/exception_hierarchy are fully manifest-backed; step 1 (do not re-introspect) and step 8 (MDX-partial-import anchor/TOC risk) are sound. No concern; noted for completeness.

Overall: NEEDS_USER_INPUT
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_stage_c_reference.py::TestManifestAnchorUniqueness::test_all_symbol_anchors_are_unique (+ ::test_verified_name_class_collisions_are_disambiguated)

Observed: 2 manifest anchors shared by >1 symbol: node ['Node (pydantic_model)', 'node (function)'] and tool ['Tool (pydantic_model)', 'tool (function)']. slug-stable companion (::test_every_anchor_is_slug_stable) passes now and must keep passing after kind-namespacing.

## Implementation delivered (atom .7) — FOUNDATION of Stage C

DELIVERED (Part A, all green):
- Anchor disambiguation in scripts/gen_api_manifest.py (_KIND_ANCHOR_TAG + two-pass _disambiguate_anchors): colliding bare slugs get f'{base}-{kind_tag}'. The 4 changed anchors: node->node-function, Node->node-model, tool->tool-function, Tool->tool-model. All slug-stable + unique; only these 4 changed, mcp manifest byte-unchanged.

title: Fix sub-construct output extraction for Loop nodes
description:
## Problem
make_subgraph_fn scans sub_result.values() with isinstance(val, sub.output) but Loop nodes have list[T] from append-list reducer. Earlier non-loop nodes match first, returning wrong output.

## Fix
In factory.py make_subgraph_fn (~line 700-712):
1. Iterate sub_result values in REVERSE (later pipeline nodes take precedence)
2. Before isinstance check, unwrap lists: if val is list and val[-1] matches output type, use val[-1]

```python
for val in reversed(list(sub_result.values())):
    check_val = val
    if isinstance(val, list) and val:
        check_val = val[-1]
    if isinstance(check_val, sub.output):
        output_val = check_val
        break
```

## File
src/neograph/factory.py (make_subgraph_fn, ~line 700-712)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-djpi
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-djpi` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern. Use grep / AST search
   across the entire source tree (NOT just the cited files in the
   ticket). Concrete techniques:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Type-check: `mypy --strict` if relevant
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-djpi)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-djpi --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-djpi --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID:

```bash
bd label add neograph-djpi codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-djpi
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-djpi
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes.

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-djpi)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-djpi --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-djpi sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-0e9a
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-0e9a` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern. Use grep / AST search
   across the entire source tree (NOT just the cited files in the
   ticket). Concrete techniques:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Type-check: `mypy --strict` if relevant
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-0e9a)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-0e9a --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-0e9a --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID:

```bash
bd label add neograph-0e9a codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Write regression test for neograph-0e9a
description:
Write a failing test that defines the expected behavior for neograph-0e9a.
This is the TDD "red" step -- the test MUST exist and MUST fail before
any implementation begins.

## Instructions

1. Identify what to test from the implementation plan
2. Choose test level (prefer integration over unit when DB involved)
3. Write the failing test
4. Use test factories for test data (never inline model construction)
5. Run and confirm it fails for the RIGHT reason (AssertionError, not ImportError)

## BANNED Patterns

- `pytest.mark.xfail` is BANNED in regression tests
- AST-scanning / source-code pattern tests are BANNED **as a
  substitute for behavioral testing** — when the task changes
  behavior, the red test must exercise that behavior, not scan source.
- Direct DB session management in test code is BANNED

## Structural-disease tasks (no testable behavior)

Some tasks eliminate a NON-behavioral disease pattern (a casing/naming
wordmark, an import idiom, a helper-bypass that is type- or
text-shaped, not runtime-observable). For these, no behavioral failing
test exists — the only meaningful red artifact IS the structural guard
that `sweep-verify` will later require. In that case:
- Write that structural guard HERE, confirm it FAILS (the disease
  instances exist), and record it as the red artifact.
- The AST/source-text BAN above does NOT apply — it bans source scans
  used INSTEAD OF behavioral tests, not the structural guard that pins
  a structural invariant. The same guard satisfies `sweep-verify`.

## Verification: Paste the FAILED Output

You MUST see the word "FAILED" in pytest output.

## Store Test Reference

```bash
bd update neograph-0e9a --append-notes "## Regression Test
- Test: <test_path>::<test_name>
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step)
- Tests expected behavior: [one sentence]"
```
acceptance_criteria: Failing test exists. Test reference written to task notes.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-0e9a
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-0e9a
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes.

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-0e9a)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-0e9a --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-0e9a sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: arch: introduce typed LlmConfig; kill duplicated defaults + None-bypass bug class
description:
GAP at src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:354-360. Uses dict.get(key, default) which only returns default when key is MISSING. If a caller explicitly sets llm_config['budget_exhausted_message']=None or llm_config['budget_exhausted_message']='', those values are appended verbatim to messages instead of falling back to the hardcoded default.

Observed (via tests/modes/_scratch_v3/h5d7.py):
- {} (missing key) → default message used [OK]
- {'budget_exhausted_message': ''} → empty string appended [BUG]
- {'budget_exhausted_message': None} → None appended as content [BUG — real ChatModels may reject None]

Fix: change to
  budget_msg = llm_config.get('budget_exhausted_message') or _default

or explicit None/empty check. Tests in _scratch_v3/h5d7.py document current behavior; they must be updated (or moved to behavioral suite with flipped assertions) when fix lands.

Discovered via neograph-h5d7 test-gap closure (axis 10).
design:
## Core Invariant

The public dict-typed `llm_config` surface (Node.llm_config, Construct.llm_config, llm_factory(..., llm_config=dict) callback) is preserved verbatim; internal framework consumers read through a typed `LlmConfig` view normalized at the `invoke_structured` and `invoke_with_tools` entry, which rejects wrong types on known keys and resolves the one runtime-dependent default (`budget_exhausted_message`) via a helper.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Create `src/neograph/_llm_config.py`

```python
from typing import Any, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class LlmConfig(BaseModel):
    # Preserve provider-specific knobs (temperature, max_tokens, etc.) via
    # extra='allow'. The llm_factory callback reads these from the raw dict,
    # not from this model; LlmConfig is only used by internal consumers.
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')

    output_strategy: Literal['structured', 'json_mode', 'text'] = 'structured'
    max_retries: int = 1
    max_iterations: int = 20
    token_budget: int | None = None
    budget_exhausted_message: str | None = None

    def resolved_budget_exhausted_message(self, output_model_name: str) -> str:
        # `or` handles both None and '' -- the two rnjw-original bypass cases.
        return self.budget_exhausted_message or (
            'Your previous response contained tool-call markup. '
            'All tool budgets are exhausted. Do NOT invoke any more tools. '
            f'Produce the final response as a {output_model_name} object. '
            'No markup, no tool calls. Output ONLY the structured response.'
        )
```

### 2. Normalize at two entry points

**`invoke_with_tools`** (_tool_loop.py:154):
- After `llm_config = llm_config or {}` at :206, add:
  `cfg = LlmConfig.model_validate(llm_config)`
- Replace :207 `llm_config.get('max_iterations', 20)` -> `cfg.max_iterations`
- Replace :208 `llm_config.get('token_budget')` -> `cfg.token_budget`
- Replace :339 `llm_config.get('output_strategy', 'structured')` -> `cfg.output_strategy`
- Replace :340 `llm_config.get('max_retries', 1)` -> `cfg.max_retries`
- Replace :354-360 multi-line `.get(key, f-string)` -> `cfg.resolved_budget_exhausted_message(output_model.__name__)`

**`invoke_structured`** (_llm.py:680):
- After `llm_config = llm_config or {}` at :697, add:
  `cfg = LlmConfig.model_validate(llm_config)`
- Replace :698 `llm_config.get('output_strategy', 'structured')` -> `cfg.output_strategy`
- Replace :719 `llm_config.get('max_retries', 1)` -> `cfg.max_retries`

**`render_prompt`** (_llm.py:737) -- low-impact but consistent:
- After :775 `llm_config = getattr(node, 'llm_config', None) or {}`, add:
  `cfg = LlmConfig.model_validate(llm_config)`
- Replace :776 `llm_config.get('output_strategy', 'structured')` -> `cfg.output_strategy`

### 3. Keep raw dict at all public / callback surfaces

- Node.llm_config stays dict[str, Any] (node.py:100) -- no change.
- Construct.llm_config stays dict[str, Any] (construct.py:90) -- no change.
- `_get_llm` (_llm.py:169) keeps passing the raw dict to llm_factory -- no change.
- Construct's merge logic (construct.py:118-128) stays dict-level -- no change.
- compiler.py:163 CompileError validation stays (nicer UX than Pydantic ValidationError at runtime).

### 4. Tests (TDD order)

**Write failing first** (test the invariant in a behavioral shape):
- `test_budget_exhausted_message_none_falls_back_to_default` -- sets None, asserts default is appended (flip of existing pin test at test_llm_internals.py:3377)
- `test_budget_exhausted_message_empty_falls_back_to_default` -- sets '', asserts default is appended (flip of :3372)
- `test_llm_config_rejects_wrong_type_on_known_field` -- NEW: LlmConfig.model_validate({'max_retries': 'abc'}) raises pydantic.ValidationError
- `test_llm_config_preserves_unknown_keys` -- NEW: LlmConfig({'temperature': 0.7}).model_dump() contains 'temperature' (proves pass-through safe)

**After test red, implement**:
- Create _llm_config.py
- Wire cfg at the two entries
- Tests turn green

**Flip the gap-documenting class docstring** at test_llm_internals.py:3282-3296 to describe the fixed contract, not the old gap.

### 5. Quality gates

- `make quality` green (baseline restored in neograph-ownh; any regression is mine)
- All three API surfaces exercised: @node nodes, declarative Node(llm_config={...}), programmatic Node() | Modifier pipelines. Tests at test_composition.py:2155-2175 already cover this for llm_config propagation -- stays green.
- Follow-up ticket neograph-z8x5 (narrow behavioral pin) gets its tests landed in this same change.

## Out of scope for this ticket

- Typo protection on known-field misspellings (max_retires) -- would need `extra='forbid'` and break provider pass-through; deserves its own ticket with a warning/lint approach.
- Migrating compiler.py:163 to use LlmConfig for the CompileError -- UX regression risk.
- Documenting LlmConfig on the website -- it's an internal refactor, not a user-facing API.
