title: Systematic Agent Spec export/round-trip COVERAGE MATRIX: parametrize modifier x input-shape x round-trip (converge the surface, end the whack-a-mole)
description:
The Agent Spec export/round-trip surface has produced a sibling bug on every fix: ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3 -> hf505 -> neograph-3lk2l. All cluster in two root-cause families: (a) dict-form title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring, (b) type-identity loss on round-trip (synthesized AgentSpecType_ classes). The green suite misses them because export/round-trip tests use single-type-input WORKAROUND shapes, not the primary @node shapes (map_over=, dict-form, +context).

DELIVERABLE: a PARAMETRIZED export+round-trip test matrix over {no modifier, Each(map_over), Oracle(ensemble), Loop, Operator} x {single-type inputs, dict-form fan-in, +non-fan-out context input} x {export, round-trip}, all using the PRIMARY @node shapes. Run it to enumerate EVERY hole at once (do not fix one at a time). Then consolidate the fixes around the two root-cause families rather than per-symbol patches. This test becomes the permanent guard that the surface stays converged. ACCEPTANCE: the full matrix is green (or each red cell has a filed, wired blocker); 2ev48 does not close until this matrix passes.
design:
## Core Invariant
The Each fan-out receiver key is NOT a dict-form fan-in upstream — it is the iterated ELEMENT. Its Agent-Spec representation must round-trip to the SAME structural type as the producer's list element, and context (non-fan-out) inputs must lower to VALID MapNode 'iterated_'-prefixed inputs. One rule (the fan_out_param skip already in _check_fan_in_inputs) governs the split on BOTH export and import; never re-derive it per-symptom.

## Implementation Plan (consolidated, two families)

### Family A — export: context inputs -> valid MapNode iterated_ inputs (fixes hf505)
1. _agent_spec._lower_each: populate the inner sub-flow's StartNode.inputs with the inner node's input Properties (the context-input props), so MapNode._get_inferred_inputs yields iterated_{title}. (Fan-out-receiver-only case still exports — inputs may be unconnected.)
2. to_agent_spec dict-form DataFlowEdge loop (line ~774): when the destination item is Each-modified (MapNode), prefix destination_input with 'iterated_'. Detect via modifier_set.each is not None (the same node object is in scope).

### Family B — round-trip: fan-out receiver type identity (fixes 3lk2l)
3. _agent_spec._lower_each / EachSpec marker: record fan_out_param in _MARK_EACH_SPEC so import knows which dotted-prefix group is the element.
4. loader._reconstruct_each_node: un-prefix the fan-out receiver's dotted group ('item.v' -> 'v') before reconstructing, so the element type synthesizes to the SAME AgentSpecType_ hash as the producer's list element. Context groups stay dict-form fan-in.

### wqb5t (P2, do in same pass — cheap, prevents future sibling)
5. spec_types._fields_match: compare (name, _property/field type-signature) pairs, not names only.

## Verify
- Parametrized matrix test (write FIRST, RED): {no-mod, Each(map_over), Oracle(ensemble), Loop, Operator} x {single-type, dict-form fan-in, +context} x {export, round-trip}, PRIMARY @node shapes. Reproduce hf505/3lk2l as red cells first.
- Gate: uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest ; baseline 3476, zero regressions.
- Close hf505/3lk2l/wqb5t each only after its own repro passes under the consolidated fix.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-56d7f.2)

The whack-a-mole cluster (ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3/.4 -> hf505 -> 3lk2l -> wqb5t) reduces to ONE disease with two faces: neograph encodes fan-in/fan-out STRUCTURE in pyagentspec Property TITLES via three prefix conventions, and those conventions are applied INCONSISTENTLY between the export (title -> DataFlowEdge) side and the import (title -> reconstructed type) side. The green suite misses it because export/round-trip tests use single-type-input WORKAROUND shapes (Node.scripted(inputs=Tagged)) instead of the primary @node shapes (map_over=/dict-form/+context).

The three prefix conventions in play:
- dict-form: _properties_for() prefixes a dict-form inputs/outputs Property title with '{key}.' (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:167).
- Each fan-out receiver skip: the fan_out_param key is NOT an upstream edge; it is fed per-item by the MapNode sub-flow, so it is skipped (export loop already mirrors this).
- MapNode 'iterated_' prefix: pyagentspec MapNode INFERS its external input Properties from the inner sub-flow StartNode and PREFIXES every one with 'iterated_' (confirmed against installed pyagentspec MapNode docstring: 'complemented with the iterated_ prefix', type Union[inner, List[inner]]).

### Root-cause family A -- export title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring
- hf505: an Each node with BOTH a fan-out key AND a non-fan-out context key (inputs={'source':RawText,'cluster':ClusterGroup}, fan_out_param='cluster'). The dict-form fan-in loop skips 'cluster' and emits a DataFlowEdge to the MapNode with destination_input='source.text' -- but the MapNode's real inner property is 'iterated_source.text', so pydantic raises ValidationError ('does not have any property with that name'). The dest_node for an Each item IS the MapNode (_lower_construct_item:586 returns map_node as both primary and data_node). The fix locus is the destination_input line (currently f'{upstream_name}.{prop.title}') at _agent_spec.py:781, which must become 'iterated_{upstream_name}.{prop.title}' when the destination is a MapNode.

### Root-cause family B -- type-identity loss on round-trip (synthesized AgentSpecType_ classes)
- 3lk2l: a primary @node(map_over=) Each EXPORTS fine but FAILS round-trip with 'Each(over=...) element type mismatch: expected AgentSpecType_X, found list[AgentSpecType_Y]'. The Each element-type check (_validation_inputs.py:252 _check_each_path) compares the fanned-out RECEIVER input_type against the element_type of the producer's over-path list field via _types_compatible. On round-trip these must be the SAME synthesized class. They are NOT, because the inner Each node's fan-out receiver Property titles carry the dict-form '{key}.' prefix (from _properties_for), so on import _agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs) synthesizes a model whose FIELDS differ structurally from the producer's element model -> different _structural_type_name hash -> different class -> mismatch. Same disease as qtfof.4 (structural naming) and wqb5t (register_type).
- wqb5t: register_type's idempotency check _fields_match (spec_types.py:45-47) compares field NAMES only, never TYPES. Two structurally-different models with the same field-name set registered under the same explicit name silently collapse to the first (wrong) one. Must compare (field_name, field_type) pairs.

## Relevant Code (file:line)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:731-811 -- to_agent_spec's per-item DataFlowEdge loop; dict-form branch 739-784, fan_out_param skip 745-752 (already mirrors _validation_inputs). Family-A fix locus: destination_input at :781.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:410-437 -- _lower_each: MapNode wrapping single-node sub-flow; inner = _lower_node(node) so inner inputs = _properties_for(node.inputs) = dict-form '{key}.field' titles. This is where the 'iterated_' contract originates on the pyagentspec side.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:154-170 -- _properties_for: the '{key}.' dict-form title prefix (the shared convention).
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:157-159 -- the REUSE target: 'if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue' skip pattern the export loop already copies. fan_out_candidates() (imported from _ir_normalize) is the single shared fan-out-key rule.
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:197-260 -- _check_each_path; the element-type check at :252 that rejects the round-tripped Each (family B symptom site).
- src/neograph/loader.py:339-367 -- _reconstruct_each_node (inverse of _lower_each); inner reconstructed via _reconstruct_primitive_node then renamed; KEEPS inner inputs.
- src/neograph/loader.py:255-268 -- _reconstruct_primitive_node: inputs = _inputs_from_data_edges(...) or _agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs); the fallback path that synthesizes the divergent receiver type from prefixed titles.
- src/neograph/loader.py:80-97 -- _agent_spec_props_to_type: name = _structural_type_name(props); agent_spec_properties_to_types(props,name); the reuse mechanism intended to unify identical structures into ONE class.
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:45-47 -- _fields_match (wqb5t fix locus: compare (name,type) pairs).
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:244-301 -- _property_type_signature + _structural_type_name (structural hash; qtfof.4 recursion already lands here).
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:398-418 -- agent_spec_properties_to_types (explicit-name register path wqb5t warns can still collapse).

## Test infra / gap
- Extra gating: [agent-spec] optional extra (pyproject.toml:70, pyagentspec>=26.1.0,<27). All agent-spec test files module-gate with pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec') at top; run with 'uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest ...'. This is the correct import-guard pattern to copy.
- Existing tests use WORKAROUND single-type shapes: tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:103 Each via Node.scripted('each_step', inputs=Tagged, ...) | Each(...) -- NOT @node(map_over=). Loop via inputs=Draft (single type). The primary @node shapes (map_over=, dict-form fan-in from construct_from_functions, +context) are exactly what is untested.
- Helpers: tests/schemas.py:54-58 _producer/_consumer (Node.scripted single-type -- these are the workaround generators). Schemas RawText/Claims/ClusterGroup/Clusters/MatchResult available. build_test_compile_kwargs / register_scripted used for run-level round-trip.
- Existing structural guards live in tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py (TestDictFormFanInResolvesRealPropertyTitles, TestDictFormFanInSkipsFanOutReceiver) -- the permanent-guard home once the matrix is green.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- MapNode 'iterated_' prefix applies to ALL inferred inputs; when an Each node has ONLY the fan-out key (qtfof.1, already fixed) there are no context DataFlowEdges so the bug is invisible -- it only surfaces with a SECOND context input (hf505). The matrix's '+context' column is what forces this cell.
- Family B fix must keep the _structural_type_name + register_type reuse mechanism (do NOT add a parallel type synthesizer). The fix is to NORMALIZE the receiver's Property titles (strip the dict-form '{key}.'/'iterated_' prefix) BEFORE structural hashing on import, so the receiver hashes identically to the producer's element type. Alternatively resolve the receiver type from the over-path producer element. Prefer the prefix-normalization since it keeps ONE walker.
- wqb5t _fields_match change (names+types) could newly WARN/overwrite on legitimately-distinct same-name models -- ensure existing register_type idempotent callers (load_project_types) still no-op for genuinely identical schemas.
- Three-surface parity: agent-spec is IR-level free-function testing (to_agent_spec/from_agent_spec), exempt from the @node/declarative/programmatic triple per the roundtrip file's own stated exemption -- but the matrix SHOULD still drive the primary @node shape (map_over=/construct_from_functions) since that is the shape whose gap caused every bug.
- Do NOT fix cells one at a time: build the full matrix, run it, enumerate ALL red cells at once, then consolidate around the two families (per task acceptance).
## Findings (research neograph-56d7f.2)

The whack-a-mole cluster (ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3/.4 -> hf505 -> 3lk2l/wqb5t) reduces to ONE disease with two faces: the fan-in/fan-out prefix conventions that encode DAG structure in Agent-Spec Property TITLES are applied ASYMMETRICALLY between the export (title -> DataFlowEdge) and import (title -> reconstructed type) sides. Three title conventions are in play and each side must honor all three:
  1. dict-form fan-in prefix `{upstream_name}.{field}` (from `_properties_for`, _agent_spec.py:167)
  2. Each fan-out receiver SKIP (the `fan_out_param` key names no upstream node)
  3. MapNode `iterated_{...}` prefix -- pyagentspec MapNode INFERS its external inputs from the inner sub-flow StartNode and PREFIXES every one with `iterated_` (confirmed live against installed pyagentspec MapNode docstring: "The names of the inputs will be the ones of the inner flow, complemented with the `iterated_` prefix").

### Family A (export -- hf505, dict-form title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring)
For an Each node with BOTH a fan-out key AND a non-fan-out context key (`inputs={'source':RawText,'cluster':ClusterGroup}`, fan_out_param='cluster'), the export loop skips 'cluster' correctly but emits the context edge with `destination_input='source.text'` -- while the dest MapNode only exposes `iterated_source.text`. pyagentspec DataFlowEdge validation rejects it. The existing fan_out skip (already mirrors _check_fan_in_inputs) is CORRECT; the missing piece is the `iterated_` prefix when the destination data_node is a MapNode (Each combo).

### Family B (round-trip -- 3lk2l/qtfof.4/wqb5t, type-identity loss)
The primary `@node(map_over=...)` shape EXPORTS fine (qtfof.1) but FAILS `from_agent_spec` with "Each(over=...) element type mismatch: expected AgentSpecType_X, found list[AgentSpecType_Y]". Root: the Each inner node's fan-out receiver input Properties are titled with the dict-form prefix `item.<field>` (via `_properties_for`), so on import `_agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs)` synthesizes a model whose FIELD NAMES / structural signature include the `item.` prefix -- structurally DIFFERENT from the producer's element type (the same `Item` nested inside `prod.groups` reconstructs WITHOUT the prefix). Two different `_structural_type_name` hashes -> two different synthesized classes -> `_check_each_path`'s `_types_compatible(element_type, input_type)` (_validation_inputs.py:252) rejects. The intended dedup mechanism (`_structural_type_name` + `register_type` idempotency) never fires because the prefixed titles make the shapes genuinely diverge. wqb5t compounds this: `_fields_match` (spec_types.py:45-47) compares field NAMES only, so a same-named-different-typed collision under a reused explicit name silently keeps the WRONG class.

### Existing reuse targets (do NOT reinvent)
- Export fan_out skip: _agent_spec.py:745-752 already replicates `_validation_inputs.py:158` (`if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue`). The new context-key branch must ROUTE (not skip) with the `iterated_` prefix -- reuse `classify_modifiers(item)` / ModifierCombo.EACH (already imported) to detect a MapNode destination.
- Structural type dedup: `_structural_type_name` (spec_types.py:273) + `register_type`/`_fields_match` (spec_types.py:45-67) is the ONE canonical reuse-a-class mechanism. Family B fix = make the fan-out receiver reconstruct WITHOUT the dict-form prefix so its structural signature matches the producer element (then dedup fires for free), PLUS strengthen `_fields_match` to compare (name, type) pairs.
- Single JSON-Schema walker invariant: `_resolve_field_type` / `_property_to_field_type` are twins; keep any type change inside them, never a 3rd walker.

### Current-vs-workaround coverage gap (why green suite missed it)
The round-trip suite pins Each with a SINGLE-TYPE-input workaround: `Node.scripted("each_step", inputs=Tagged, ...) | Each(...)` (test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:103) -- NOT the primary `@node(map_over=..., map_key=...)` dict-form shape. `_producer`/`_consumer` (tests/schemas.py:54-59) are single-type too. So the dominant @node shape was never exercised for Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator x dict-form x round-trip.
## Findings (ground-truthed via repro + pyagentspec source)

### Reproduced holes (primary @node shapes)
- **3lk2l (round-trip)**: `@node(map_over='prod.groups') def ver(item: Item)` exports OK, round-trip FAILS: ConstructError Each element type mismatch, expected AgentSpecType_57730644 (consumer) vs found list[AgentSpecType_587752a5] (producer). Two synthesized classes for the SAME logical Item.
- **hf505 (export)**: Each node with context input (`verify(source: RawText, cluster: Item)`, map_over='clusters.groups') FAILS at to_agent_spec: pydantic ValidationError, DataFlowEdge dest 'source.text' not a property of MapNode 'verify'.

### Root cause A (export, hf505) — src/neograph/_agent_spec.py
- `_lower_each` (line 410) builds StartNode with NO inputs -> `MapNode._get_inferred_inputs()` returns [] (pyagentspec derives iterated_{title} from `subflow.inputs`, which comes from StartNode.inputs — confirmed in .venv/.../flows/nodes/mapnode.py:329 and startnode.py). So no data edge can target the MapNode.
- to_agent_spec dict-form loop (line 739-784) emits destination_input='{upstream}.{title}' (line 781). For a MapNode destination it must be 'iterated_{upstream}.{title}' (MapNode docstring + L2 example: even context inputs use iterated_ prefix, type Union[T, List[T]]).

### Root cause B (round-trip, 3lk2l) — src/neograph/loader.py + _agent_spec.py
- Export: `_properties_for` (line 154) dict-form-prefixes EVERY key incl. the fan-out receiver: `item: Item` -> StringProperty title='item.v'. (Confirmed via debug dump.)
- Import: `_reconstruct_primitive_node` -> `_agent_spec_props_to_type([Property('item.v')])` -> `_structural_type_name` hashes ('item.v','string') -> flat model {item.v} = AgentSpecType_57730644. Producer's nested Item hashes ('v','string') -> AgentSpecType_587752a5. Mismatch.
- `_structural_type_name` (spec_types.py:273) hashes (title, type-sig). The dotted title 'item.v' vs bare 'v' is the divergence.

### wqb5t (P2, latent) — spec_types.py:45
- `_fields_match` compares field NAMES only, not types. Independent latent bug; not on the 3lk2l/hf505 critical path (structural naming already separates different shapes). Fix: compare (name, type-signature) pairs.

### Reuse targets
- `_validation_inputs.py::_check_fan_in_inputs` (line 131,157-159): `fan_out_key = getattr(item,'fan_out_param',None)`; `if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue`. The to_agent_spec dict-form loop ALREADY mirrors this (line 745-752). The fan_out_param IS available on the node at export time.
- EachSpec marker (_MARK_EACH_SPEC) currently carries {over,key,on_error} — extend with fan_out_param so import can un-prefix the receiver group.

### Existing tests use workaround shapes
- test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:103 uses `Node.scripted(inputs=Tagged)` (single-type) — exactly the shape that hides these bugs. New matrix must use @node map_over= / dict-form.
## Disease scan (concentrated, not widespread)
Disease: 'the Each fan-out receiver is lowered/reconstructed like a dict-form fan-in (uniform {key}.{title} dotted prefix) instead of as the iterated element; and MapNode destinations get a bare (non-iterated_) destination_input.'

Disposition table (whole-src scan):
| Site | Pattern | Action |
|------|---------|--------|
| _agent_spec.py:167 (_properties_for) | uniform dotted prefix — generic, also used by Oracle/Loop | KEEP generic; handle fan-out-receiver at Each boundary only |
| _agent_spec.py:745-752 (to_agent_spec dict loop) | fan_out_param skip ALREADY here | REUSE — extend: iterated_ prefix for Each dest |
| _agent_spec.py:410 (_lower_each) | StartNode has no inputs | FIX — populate StartNode.inputs |
| loader.py:339 (_reconstruct_each_node) | keeps dotted inner inputs | FIX — un-prefix fan-out group |
| spec_types.py:45 (_fields_match) | name-only match | FIX (wqb5t) |
| loader.py:319,522 (merge/swarm reconstruct) | not Each fan-out path | NO CHANGE (out of scope) |

Conclusion: disease is confined to _agent_spec.py + loader.py + spec_types.py. No cross-file canonical-helper bypass backlog. The fan_out_param rule (getattr(node,'fan_out_param')) is the single shared discriminator — available at export; recorded into EachSpec marker for import.
## Review (adversarial, inline)
Rubric check on the plan:
- REUSE (LOW): reuses fan_out_param + the existing dict-loop skip; extends EachSpec marker rather than a parallel channel. Good.
- ROOT-CAUSE not per-symptom (LOW): both families traced to ONE cause — fan-out receiver mis-represented as dict-form fan-in. hf505(export) + 3lk2l(roundtrip) + wqb5t(latent) fixed by the same discriminator.
- REGRESSION RISK (MEDIUM, mitigated by test): (a) adding StartNode.inputs in _lower_each could disturb the fan-out-receiver-only export that currently passes — matrix test's Each(map_over) export cell guards this; (b) iterated_ prefix must be gated to Each(MapNode) destinations only, NOT Loop/Oracle — matrix covers Loop+Oracle export/round-trip; (c) import un-prefix must pick the correct group in the mixed case — driven by marker fan_out_param, and matrix +context round-trip cell guards it.
- TEST LOCUS (LOW): acceptance is behavior (export succeeds / round-trip Construct compiles + Each element types match) — the matrix drives to_agent_spec/from_agent_spec directly, the real surface. Behavior-level so robust to fix mechanism.
Verdict: ALL_LOW — proceed to write-test (RED).
## Triage: ALL_LOW -> proceed to write-test. No refinement, no user input needed.
## MATRIX RED-FIRST — full hole list (9 red / 16 cells) at HEAD 8bcb7fb
Test: tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py (2 classes: export, round_trip; 8 cells each).

EXPORT red (4) — all family A (dict-form DataFlowEdge wiring to a MODIFIER destination):
- each-context  [hf505] : MapNode dest needs iterated_ prefix + StartNode.inputs (MapNode infers iterated_{title} from subflow.inputs)
- oracle-single [NEW]   : dict-form edge targets Oracle MERGE node; external input must target the VARIANT nodes (which carry prod.a)
- oracle-dict   [NEW]   : same, two upstreams
- operator-single [NEW] : data_node returned is the CHECK BranchingNode (no props); must be the PRIMARY node

ROUND-TRIP red (5):
- each-single   [3lk2l] : family B — fan-out receiver 'item.v' reconstructs to flat {item.v} not Elem{v}; Each element-type mismatch
- each-context / oracle-single / oracle-dict / operator-single : CASCADE from their export failures

GREEN (7): none-single/none-dict (both ops), each-single EXPORT, loop-single (both ops).

Loop is FULLY GREEN with expression conditions -> Loop has no agent-spec-family bug. (Registered-NAME-condition round-trip is an orthogonal condition-parsing concern, not tested here.)

NEW bugs the sweep found beyond the wired blockers: Oracle dict-form fan-in export, Operator dict-form fan-in export. Both are family A (dict-form DataFlowEdge wiring).
## Implementation (consolidated, two families) — landed
Files: src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, src/neograph/loader.py, src/neograph/spec_types.py, tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py

### Family A — dict-form DataFlowEdge wiring to modifier destinations (one rule, no per-symptom)
- _lower_construct_item now returns a 6th value 'input_targets: list[(SpecNode, iterated:bool)]' — the modifier-aware answer to 'which node(s) receive this item's external inputs, and does it need the MapNode iterated_ prefix': BARE/LOOP/Construct/_BranchNode -> data_node; EACH -> MapNode (iterated); OPERATOR -> PRIMARY (not the property-less check); ORACLE -> EVERY variant.
- to_agent_spec: both the dict-form and single-type edge loops emit via one _emit_input_edges(...) helper using input_targets. iterated targets get 'iterated_{title}' (bare — pyagentspec forbids dots in json_schema titles, and MapNode infers iterated_{json_schema_title}).
- _lower_each: StartNode now declares the inner node's input Properties so MapNode._get_inferred_inputs yields iterated_{title} (fixes hf505: context-input edge now has a valid destination).
- OPERATOR data_node changed check->primary (also fixes it as an output SOURCE).

### Family B — type-identity loss on round-trip
- loader._dict_form_inputs_from_props: groups dotted-prefixed inner Properties ('cluster.v','source.c') back by key, strips the prefix, reconstructs each group's type -> fan-out receiver reconstructs to the SAME structural class as the producer's list element (3lk2l). Flat single-type shape (legacy) untouched.
- _reconstruct_each_node uses it for the inner node's inputs.
- _reconstruct_operator_item reads inputs from the PRIMARY node (mirrors the export target change).

### wqb5t
- spec_types._fields_match now compares (name, str(annotation)) pairs, not names only -> reused-explicit-name collision with different field types overwrites+warns instead of silently keeping the first.

### Guards fixed (self-inflicted): removed unused marker 'fan_out_param' key (tripped sole-IR-writer guard; import re-derives via normalizer), de-parenthesized a ticket ID in a comment.

title: CRITICAL: FromInput shadows upstream node — silent dependency drop
description:
When a @node param name matches both an upstream node AND has Annotated[T, FromInput], the DI classifier wins and the dependency edge is silently dropped. The pipeline executes in wrong order or skips type validation entirely.

Root cause: decorators.py line 639 — `if p.name in param_res: continue` unconditionally skips DI-classified params from the inputs dict. The adjacency builder at line 1249 does the same.

Fix: In _build_construct_from_decorated, after building the decorated dict (line 1149) and before adjacency wiring (line 1232), check if any DI param name collides with a node in the decorated dict or sub_by_field. Raise ConstructError on collision.

Fixture: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/di_from_input_shadows_upstream.py — move to should_fail/ when fixed.
close_reason: Fixed: DI param name collision with upstream node now raises ConstructError

title: Each/Oracle: single item failure crashes entire fan-out batch
description: When one item in an Each or EachOracle fan-out hits a retryable/transient error (e.g., 402 insufficient credits, 429 rate limit), the entire graph panics via _panic_or_proceed. All parallel items — including ones that could succeed — are killed. Should catch transient API errors per-item, mark that item as failed, and continue processing remaining items. Currently requires full re-run even if 14/15 items succeeded.
notes:
## Reproduce: CONFIRMED. One item RuntimeError kills entire fan-out batch. Test: test_each_item_failure_crashes_entire_batch. Fix requires per-item try/except in the node wrapper with sentinel results for failed items.
## Architect: NEEDS_USER_INPUT. This is a design decision: (1) wrap every Send-target in try/except, (2) add error_handling='continue' kwarg to Each, (3) use LangGraph RetryPolicy + custom error handler. Each approach has different tradeoffs for DX and debugging. Recommend approach 2: explicit opt-in via Each(on_error='continue') vs default 'raise'.
## Finding: LangGraph checkpoint already handles partial resume.
With checkpointer: run 1 dispatches 3 Send items. 'a' and 'b' succeed (checkpointed). 'bad' fails → panic. Resume: invoke(None, config) re-runs ONLY the failed 'bad' item. 'a' and 'b' results from checkpoint. All 3 succeed.

The fix is documentation + DX, not code:
1. Document: pass checkpointer= to compile() for fan-out resilience
2. Document: catch error, fix transient issue, resume with same config
3. Optional: add a helper like run_with_retry() that wraps this pattern
close_reason: Not a code bug: LangGraph checkpoint handles partial resume for Send failures. Needs documentation.

title: Relocate _strip_internals to a neutral module — kill the _subconstruct -> runner layer inversion
description:
Found by the three-layer audit (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md section 2.5.3). _subconstruct.py:63 does a function-local 'from neograph.runner import _strip_internals' inside make_subgraph_fn (used at _subconstruct.py:117). _subconstruct is compile-layer (builds node callables); runner is the run layer — a compile-layer module reaching into the run layer, with the function-local import existing only to dodge the circular import the inversion itself creates. That dodge is the tell.

FIX: _strip_internals (runner.py:27) is a pure result-shaping utility (drops neo_* keys). Move it to a neutral low-level module reachable from both layers — _state_keys.py is the natural home (it already centralizes StateKeys). runner.py and _subconstruct.py both import from there; the function-local import becomes module-level; update the function-local-import allowlist guard accordingly.

SEQUENCING: this folds naturally into the q8ec runner-verbs refactor (the finalize/finalize_chunk extraction touches the same helper) — q8ec depends on this ticket so the relocation lands first on clean ground. Keep the existing pinning tests green (test_composition.py:617-626 passthrough, test_invariants.py:528 prefix-strip, guard test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:149).
close_reason: Moved _strip_internals to _state_keys.py (neutral leaf). runner.py and _subconstruct.py now import it at module level; the compile->run function-local inversion is gone. Removed the allowlist entry (allowlist shrank). Full suite 2242 passed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-eoi8
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-eoi8` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-eoi8/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-eoi8
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-eoi8)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-eoi8/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-eoi8 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-eoi8
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-eoi8
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-eoi8`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-eoi8)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-eoi8 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: _check_fan_in_inputs silently skips ALL unmatched keys when Each modifier present
description:
In _construct_validation.py:_check_fan_in_inputs (lines 421-422), when a node has an Each modifier, ALL unmatched input keys are assumed to be fan-out item receivers and silently skipped. But a node should have at most ONE fan-out item key. Extra unmatched keys (typos, stale references) pass validation silently.

Repro:
  extract = Node(name='extract', outputs=Claims)
  # 'clams' is a typo for 'extract' — should be caught
  verify = Node(name='verify', inputs={'clams': Claims, 'item': SingleClaim}, outputs=Result) | Each(over='extract.items', key='text')
  Construct(name='test', nodes=[extract, verify])  # No error raised

At runtime, the 'clams' parameter resolves to None (no upstream produces it), causing a silent data loss bug.

Fix: when has_each is True, count the number of unmatched keys. Allow at most one (the fan-out receiver). If fan_out_param is set, only skip that specific key. If fan_out_param is not set (programmatic API), allow at most one unmatched key as the inferred fan-out receiver and reject additional unmatched keys.
close_reason: Fixed: Each allows at most 1 unmatched fan-in key

title: @node: mode='raw' escape hatch (replaces @raw_node for LangGraph power users)
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness). Surfaced by the Path A Dogfood epic.

## Problem

`@raw_node` (`src/neograph/node.py:151-175`) provides the LangGraph escape hatch — write a full `(state, config) -> state_update` function and let NeoGraph wire edges + observability around it. It's used for cases where the standard `mode='scripted'` / `mode='produce'` abstractions aren't enough: custom state manipulation, cross-node state reads, conditional updates driven by full state inspection.

Path A positioning says @node is THE public API. Having a separate `@raw_node` decorator splits the mental model: users learn @node for 95% of cases and have to context-switch to @raw_node for the escape hatch. Dogfooding examples will hit this when `examples/06_raw_node_escape_hatch.py` gets migrated.

## Proposed API

Fold @raw_node into @node via a new mode:

    @node(mode='raw', input=Claims, output=Claims)
    def filter_claims(state, config):
        \"\"\"Custom filtering logic with full state + config access.\"\"\"
        claims = None
        for field_name in state.__class__.model_fields:
            val = getattr(state, field_name, None)
            if isinstance(val, Claims):
                claims = val
                break
        if claims is None:
            return {'filter_claims': Claims(items=[])}
        filtered = Claims(items=[c for c in claims.items if c != 'b'])
        return {'filter_claims': filtered}

Signature constraint: `mode='raw'` functions must have exactly two parameters `(state, config)` — the LangGraph convention. Same shape as @raw_node today. They are NOT wired through parameter-name topology (the function body handles its own state access). The `input=` / `output=` kwargs still declare the node's typed contract for the validator and state builder.

`construct_from_module` discovers raw-mode @nodes via the sidecar but SKIPS the parameter-name adjacency pass for them — their parameters are fixed (state, config), not upstream names.

## Implementation sketch

In `src/neograph/decorators.py`:

    def node(
        fn=None,
        *,
        mode='produce',
        ...,
    ):
        def decorator(f):
            sig = inspect.signature(f)

            if mode == 'raw':
                # Raw mode: enforce (state, config) signature
                params = list(sig.parameters.values())
                if len(params) != 2:
                    raise ConstructError(
                        f\"@node(mode='raw') '{f.__name__}' must have exactly two \"
                        f\"parameters (state, config); got {len(params)}.\"
                    )
                if [p.name for p in params] != ['state', 'config']:
                    raise ConstructError(
                        f\"@node(mode='raw') '{f.__name__}' parameters must be \"
                        f\"named 'state' and 'config'; got {[p.name for p in params]}.\"
                    )
                # Param_names for raw mode: empty tuple — not used for topology.
                param_names = ()
            else:
                # Existing logic: reject *args/**kwargs, collect param names
                ...

            node_name = (name or f.__name__).replace('_', '-')
            # ... (existing output/input inference)

            n = Node(
                name=node_name,
                mode='scripted' if mode == 'raw' else mode,  # raw dispatches via raw_fn like @raw_node
                input=inferred_input,
                output=inferred_output,
                ...,
                raw_fn=f if mode == 'raw' else None,
            )

            _register_sidecar(n, f, param_names)
            # Stash the original mode so construct_from_module knows to skip
            # adjacency for raw nodes. Augment sidecar tuple with mode.
            return n

In `construct_from_module`, when building adjacency:
- For raw-mode @nodes (detectable via sidecar mode or `n.raw_fn is not None`), skip the parameter-name resolution loop. They have no upstream deps inferred from signature; they depend on whatever they choose to read from state.
- Raw-mode nodes are still included in the topological sort at their declaration point (since they have no incoming edges, they'll float to the start unless something else depends on them; use declaration-order tiebreaking).

## Acceptance criteria

- New tests in `TestNodeDecorator`:
  - `test_node_decorator_raw_mode_basic`: a `@node(mode='raw')` function reads a Claims value from state and returns a filtered update dict. End-to-end via compile+run.
  - `test_node_decorator_raw_mode_wrong_signature_raises`: three params, or wrong names ('s', 'c'), raises ConstructError at decoration time.
  - `test_node_decorator_raw_mode_with_downstream`: a raw @node produces output that a downstream scripted @node consumes by parameter name. Verifies the output=X kwarg is honored for topology.
  - `test_node_decorator_mixed_raw_and_scripted`: a pipeline with both raw and scripted @nodes in the same module.
- Existing `TestRawNode::test_raw_node_in_pipeline` (which uses the @raw_node decorator) still passes — @raw_node remains importable for back-compat within the codebase, but the Dogfood epic migrates the example to @node(mode='raw').
- @node docstring updated with a raw-mode section.
- Full suite stays green.

## Decision: deprecate @raw_node?

Option 1: keep @raw_node as an alias that calls @node(mode='raw') internally. No user-facing deprecation. Reader finds both in docs → confused.

Option 2: delete @raw_node from public API. Since no external users, this is safe. All internal usages migrate.

RECOMMENDED: Option 2 — delete @raw_node. This is the whole point of Path A. Documentation simplification wins.

Execute deletion as part of the Dogfood epic (migrate `examples/06_raw_node_escape_hatch.py` to @node(mode='raw') and drop @raw_node from `neograph/__init__.py`). This subtask only ADDS the @node(mode='raw') support; the deletion happens later so as not to break intermediate states.

## Dependencies

- No hard deps — can start immediately. The sidecar carryover (neograph-jyw) isn't needed because raw-mode nodes don't compose with modifiers in v1.

## Files to read

- `src/neograph/node.py:151-175` — @raw_node current implementation
- `src/neograph/decorators.py` — @node
- `src/neograph/factory.py::_make_raw_wrapper` — how raw_fn is dispatched at runtime (already handles the state-update-dict return shape)
- `tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py::TestRawNode::test_raw_node_in_pipeline` — reference test

## Non-goals

- Do NOT delete @raw_node in this subtask (deletion is part of Dogfood epic).
- Do NOT add support for raw mode combined with Each / Oracle / Operator modifiers — raw mode is the escape hatch, users manipulating state manually don't need framework modifiers.

title: 51m7 band-aid: recursive validator with ambient_producers; depth>=2 sub-constructs uncovered
description:
## Architectural property (the invariant)

Context-field producer validation must hold at compile time for inner Node.context references at ANY depth of sub-construct nesting (parent -> sub -> sub-sub -> sub-sub-sub ...). The validator must be recursive over construct topology, not a special case for depth-1.

The 'if it compiles, it runs' positioning depends on this invariant. Today (post commit 0330cea), the validator catches typos at depth 1 only and silently passes them at depth >= 2 — independent reviewer aa14ccfd confirmed.

## Anti-band-aid clause

IF YOUR FIX ADDS ANOTHER 'elif' BRANCH OR ANOTHER ENUMERATED CASE, STOP AND REDERIVE. The existing 'elif' branch at _construct_validation.py:312 MUST be REMOVED, not extended. The acceptance test is whether the new diff is NET NEGATIVE in special-case branches.

## Required architectural shape

Refactor _validate_node_chain to:

```python
def _validate_node_chain(
    construct: Construct,
    *,
    ambient_producers: list[Producer] | None = None,
) -> None:
```

Inner sub-constructs are validated by a recursive call:
```python
_validate_node_chain(item, ambient_producers=producers + [...])
```

The context-field check uses `known_fields = {p.field_name for p in (ambient_producers or []) + producers}` so inner nodes see both the sub-construct's own port AND the parent's producers. One code path. Arbitrary depth.

## Breadth/depth tests that MUST break a special-case implementation

1. **Depth-3 typo**: parent -> sub -> sub-sub where the sub-sub's inner Node.context=['typo'] — must raise ConstructError at Construct(parent, ...) time.
2. **Depth-2 happy path**: parent -> sub -> sub-sub where the deepest context is produced by the parent — compiles cleanly.
3. **Depth-2 forward reference**: parent has producer X AFTER the sub-construct in node order; sub-sub's context=['X'] — current architecture rejects forward refs at top level; the recursive validator must apply the same rule consistently.
4. **Mixed nesting**: parent contains [seed, sub_A, sub_B] where sub_B contains a sub-sub referencing a context produced by sub_A's output — verify the producer aggregation.

## Audit step (mandatory)

Before implementing: grep the codebase for OTHER 'construct.input is None' gates in validation logic. Each one is a potential band-aid sibling. Report findings in the bead notes.

## Independent-review gate (acceptance criterion)

After implementation, spawn a fresh feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with this exact prompt: 'Review the fix for neograph-ta43. Confirm with high confidence (>=90) whether this is a structural recursive solution or a band-aid that handles depth 1-2 only. Specifically test: does the validator catch a typo at depth 3? Does the implementation REMOVE the prior elif branch rather than extend it?' Paste the reviewer's verdict into the bead notes. If the reviewer reports band-aid, REOPEN the ticket.

## Out of scope

- Runtime _extract_context behavior (already correct via izo1-B)
- Changes to _subconstruct.py forwarding (the best-effort comment can be updated as part of this work since the contract is now compile-time-enforced)

## Acceptance

- The elif branch added in commit 0330cea is removed (line-count drop in _construct_validation.py for that block)
- 4+ depth-coverage tests in tests/test_validation.py::TestSubConstructContextFieldValidation (extend the existing class)

title: Branch-arm nodes invisible to iter_nodes tree walks (scripted shims, DI, fingerprints)
description:
Discovered while fixing neograph-faf8. iter_nodes (construct.py:57) deliberately SKIPS _BranchNode sentinels, so nodes inside branch arms (_BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes / false_arm_nodes) are invisible to every iter_nodes-based tree walk: _collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py), _collect_required_di, and node/schema fingerprint collection. 

Concrete symptom: a scripted @node placed inside a branch arm sub-construct fails to compile with 'Scripted function <name> not registered' because its _scripted_shim PrivateAttr is never collected into the per-compile scripted dict. Declarative Node.scripted(fn=...) works only because its fn is registered via the global decoration registry / per-compile scripted= dict, not via shim collection.

This is distinct from neograph-faf8 (checkpointer/conditions threading into arm sub-construct compile, now fixed). This bug is about tree-walk coverage of branch arms.

Scope decision needed: is the right fix to make iter_nodes descend into _BranchNode arms (broad — affects lint, DI, fingerprints uniformly), or targeted per-consumer? iter_nodes skipping _BranchNode is currently documented/relied-upon behavior, so changing it needs an audit of all consumers. Anti-band-aid: prefer the uniform fix over patching only _collect_scripted_shims.

Repro: @node scripted sub-construct (construct_from_functions) with a port param, placed in a programmatic _BranchNode true arm, compiled.
design:
## Root Cause
iter_nodes (construct.py:57-68) walks construct.nodes and handles only Construct (recurse) and Node (yield); _BranchNode is skipped by design ('matching the prior walks' isinstance(Node) gate'). But _BranchNode carries _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes / false_arm_nodes (list[Node | Construct]) that are real IR nodes. Three consumers walk iter_nodes and are therefore blind to arm contents:
  1. _collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py:255) -> arm @node shims uncollected -> 'not registered' at factory.py:61.
  2. _collect_required_di (compiler.py:271) -> arm DI params not surfaced in required-input validation.
  3. node/schema fingerprint collection (state.py compute_node_fingerprints) -> arm nodes excluded from checkpoint schema fingerprints.

## Fix Approach (uniform, anti-band-aid)
Make iter_nodes descend into _BranchNode arms: when item is a _BranchNode, iterate its branch_meta.true_arm_nodes + false_arm_nodes, recursing into Construct arm items and yielding Node arm items (same Node/Construct dispatch as the top level). This fixes all three consumers uniformly rather than patching only _collect_scripted_shims.

## Audit required (scope decision)
iter_nodes skipping _BranchNode is documented/relied-upon. Before changing, audit ALL iter_nodes callers to confirm descending is correct for each (shims YES, DI YES, fingerprints YES, lint placeholder checks — verify, validation walks use _construct_validation not iter_nodes — verify). Architect-review atom owns this scope call. Do NOT double-yield arm nodes that also appear elsewhere; _BranchMeta arms hold nodes that appear ONLY in that arm (per the field docstrings).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_branch_arm_iter_nodes.py::test_node_subconstruct_in_true_arm_compiles_and_runs (and _false_arm_)
- Observed RED: ConfigurationError: [Node 'gate'] Scripted function 'gate' not registered (factory.py:61)
- Root cause: iter_nodes (construct.py:57) skips _BranchNode sentinels, so _collect_scripted_shims(parent) never collects the shim of a @node inside a branch arm; the recursive arm compile inherits the parent's incomplete _scripted_lookup (_wiring.py threads _scripted_lookup=scripted_lookup down, never re-collects) -> shim missing -> factory.py:61 raises.
- Confirmed mechanism: faf8 tests pass only because they used Node.scripted+explicit scripted= dict; the @node shim-collection path (_scripted_shim PrivateAttr) is the one iter_nodes-skip breaks. Same skip also starves _collect_required_di (DI) and fingerprint collection for arm nodes.
## Trace-similar (same bug pattern elsewhere)
Pattern category: IR tree-walks blind to _BranchNode arm contents.

title: Auto-resume from schema divergence point via LangGraph time-travel
description: When a checkpoint exists but node output types changed, automatically rewind to the checkpoint before the earliest invalidated node and resume. Uses LangGraph get_state_history + update_state + invoke(None). Default auto_resume=True (Prefect model). Opt-out with auto_resume=False (raises CheckpointSchemaError). Requires: transitive descendant computation, earliest-invalidated-node finder, fingerprint injection at rewind point.
design:
## Test Strategy

### What we test (neograph contract, NOT LangGraph internals)
We test: given a construct + checkpoint state + schema change, what does run() do?
We do NOT test: does LangGraph correctly serialize channels, does MemorySaver persist correctly.

### The test matrix

**Axis 1: What changed between runs**

| Change type | Example | Expected behavior |
|-------------|---------|-------------------|
| Nothing | Same code, same types | Resume normally (skip completed nodes) |
| Field added to output model | score: float added | Rewind to changed node, re-run downstream |
| Field removed from output model | old_field removed | Same |
| Field type changed | str -> int | Same |
| Class renamed (same fields) | Claims -> EnrichedClaims | Same |
| Wrapper type swap | T -> ValidatedT(T) | Same |
| Node added to pipeline | New node E between C and D | Full re-run (topology change) |
| Node removed from pipeline | Node C removed | Full re-run (topology change) |
| Prompt changed (same types) | Different prompt string | NO change detected (schema fingerprint based on types, not prompts) |
| Logic changed (same types) | Different function body | NO change detected (Phase 4: source hash would catch this) |

**Axis 2: Pipeline topology**

| Topology | Why test it |
|----------|------------|
| Linear A->B->C->D | Basic: change C, rewind to C, re-run C+D |
| Fan-in A->C, B->C | Change A: does C re-run? (yes, it depends on A) |
| Fan-out A->B, A->C | Change A: both B and C re-run |
| Diamond A->B->D, A->C->D | Change B: C preserved, D re-runs |
| Sub-construct | Change inside sub: does parent handle it? |
| Single node | Degenerate case |

**Axis 3: Failure modes**

| Scenario | What we test |
|----------|-------------|
| Crash mid-pipeline (no schema change) | Normal resume, not auto-resume |
| Schema change + auto_resume=True | Rewind + continue (the happy path) |
| Schema change + auto_resume=False | CheckpointSchemaError raised |
| No checkpoint exists | Fresh run, no schema comparison |
| Checkpoint from before fingerprinting | Graceful: fresh run (cant compare) |
| Multiple nodes changed | Rewind to earliest changed |
| Root node changed | Everything re-runs |
| Leaf node changed | Only leaf re-runs |

### Hypothesis tests

| Property | What it verifies |
|----------|-----------------|
| For any topology, unchanged upstream nodes execute exactly once across both runs | Upstream preservation |
| For any topology, invalidated nodes always re-execute | No silent skip |
| The execution order respects DAG dependencies after rewind | Correctness |
| Fingerprint is deterministic (same model -> same fingerprint across runs) | Stability |
| Fingerprint changes iff the model shape changes | Sensitivity |

### What we explicitly do NOT test

- LangGraph MemorySaver correctness (their tests cover that)
- LangGraph serialization/deserialization (their serde tests)
- LangGraph scheduling algorithm (their _algo tests)
- Pydantic model validation (Pydantics tests)
- Corrupt checkpoint data (thats LangGraph infrastructure, not our contract)

### Test infrastructure needed

A helper that:
1. Creates a construct with N scripted nodes, each logging when executed
2. Compiles with MemorySaver
3. Runs once (populating checkpoint)
4. Optionally modifies one nodes output type
5. Re-compiles and runs again
6. Returns which nodes executed on each run

This helper parameterizes over topology and change type, enabling Hypothesis to generate random scenarios.

### Estimated test count
- 10-12 deterministic integration tests (topology x change type)
- 3-5 Hypothesis property tests
- 2-3 edge case tests (no checkpoint, pre-fingerprint checkpoint, auto_resume flag)
- Total: ~18-20 tests

## Testing Strategy

We test: given a construct + checkpoint state + schema change, what does run() do?
We do NOT test: MemorySaver correctness, LangGraph serde, scheduling algorithm, corrupt data.

### Test matrix (3 axes, ~20 tests)

**Axis 1: What changed between runs (10 scenarios)**

1. Nothing — normal resume, skip completed nodes
2. Field added to output model — rewind to changed node
3. Field removed — rewind
4. Field type changed (str -> int) — rewind
5. Class renamed (same fields) — rewind
6. Wrapper type swap (T -> ValidatedT) — rewind
7. Node added to pipeline — full re-run (topology change)
8. Node removed — full re-run
9. Prompt changed (same types) — NOT detected, resume (schema-based fingerprint)
10. Logic changed (same types) — NOT detected (future: source hash Phase 4)

**Axis 2: Pipeline topology (6 shapes)**

| Topology | What it tests |
|----------|--------------|
| Linear A->B->C->D | Basic: change C, rewind to C, re-run C+D |
| Fan-in A->C, B->C | Change A: C must re-run (depends on A) |
| Fan-out A->B, A->C | Change A: both B and C re-run |
| Diamond A->B->D, A->C->D | Change B: C preserved, D re-runs |
| Sub-construct | Change inside sub: parent handles rewind |
| Single node | Degenerate: change = full re-run |

**Axis 3: Failure modes (6 scenarios)**

| Scenario | Expected behavior |
|----------|-------------------|
| No checkpoint exists | Fresh run, no comparison |
| Checkpoint from pre-fingerprint era | Graceful: fresh run (cant verify) |
| auto_resume=True + schema change | Rewind + continue (happy path) |
| auto_resume=False + schema change | CheckpointSchemaError raised |
| Root node changed | Everything re-runs |
| Leaf node changed | Only leaf re-runs, all upstream preserved |

### Hypothesis property tests (5)

1. For any topology, unchanged upstream nodes execute exactly once across both runs
2. For any topology, invalidated nodes always re-execute on second run
3. Execution order after rewind respects DAG dependencies
4. Fingerprint determinism: same model -> same fingerprint across runs
5. Fingerprint sensitivity: model shape change <-> fingerprint change (bidirectional)

### Test infrastructure

Helper function that:
1. Creates a construct with N scripted nodes, each appending to an exec_log
2. Compiles with MemorySaver
3. Runs once (populating checkpoint)
4. Modifies one nodes output type (parameterized)
5. Re-compiles and runs again (same thread_id)
6. Returns (exec_log_run1, exec_log_run2, invalidated_nodes)

This helper parameterizes over topology and change type for both deterministic and Hypothesis tests.

### What we explicitly do NOT test

- LangGraph MemorySaver/SqliteSaver serialization correctness
- LangGraph channel scheduling algorithm
- Pydantic model validation/coercion
- Corrupt/truncated checkpoint data
- LangGraph get_state_history ordering
- Network failures to checkpoint store

### Estimated: 18-20 tests total
- 10-12 deterministic integration (topology x change type)
- 5 Hypothesis property tests
- 3 edge case tests (no checkpoint, pre-fingerprint, flag behavior)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-f7nt
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-f7nt` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-f7nt/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-f7nt
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-f7nt)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-f7nt --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-f7nt --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-f7nt/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-f7nt codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-f7nt/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in

   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |

   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

design:
## Core Invariant
Every construction site in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py that emits a pyagentspec primitive carrying neograph-authored ${var} prompt text — LlmNode.prompt_template, AgentNode via nested Agent.system_prompt, AND every _make_agent(...) call (which builds Agent(system_prompt=...)) — MUST be preceded, in the same enclosing function body, by a _translate_placeholders(/_node_translation( call, so no untranslated ${var} ever reaches the Agent Spec wire. The guard proves this PAIRING exhaustively (positive shape-guard), reusing the neograph-00447 registry as the single classification source (DERIVED, never hand-copied), and any KNOWN unpaired site rides a SHRINKING allowlist tagged with the tracking bug — never a silent skip.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per review kgbo0.12 — 2 MEDIUM resolved)
1. MEDIUM-1 FIX (derive, do not hardcode): in tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py add
   `PLACEHOLDER_PROMPT_EMITTING_CONSTRUCTORS = frozenset({n for n, f in NODE_FAMILIES.items() if f == "text_scan"}) | {"AgentNode"}`
   — DERIVED from NODE_FAMILIES text_scan members (NOT a hardcoded {LlmNode}; a future text_scan prompt-bearing primitive is then a LOUD add, not a silent miss) PLUS the AgentNode augmentation (AgentNode is `structural` to pyagentspec — NODE_FAMILIES faithfully mirrors _get_inferred_inputs, do NOT reclassify it — but placeholder-coupled in neograph EXPORT via nested Agent.system_prompt). Docstring names why: LlmNode = flow-node fed prompt_template; AgentNode = export-coupled; the OTHER text_scan members it collects (currently InputMessageNode) are narrowed by the req-3 exemption list, not hidden.
2. Create tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py. Always-on (pure `ast` + Tier-A dict import; NO importorskip). Parse _agent_spec.py once.
3. Collect TWO site families by AST walk:
   (a) NODE-construction sites: every ast.Call whose callee trailing name is in the derived set -> LlmNode :309/:504/:589, AgentNode :330/:544, InputMessageNode :812 (6 collected).
   (b) _make_agent CALL sites: every ast.Call to `_make_agent` -> :329, :539 (paired), :945 (Portal->Swarm, UNPAIRED). This family is what catches the mutual blind spot the AgentNode-only walk misses.
4. Req 2 pairing (post-cbpyx target = _translate_placeholders, the retired _check_placeholder_inputs is GONE per cbpyx 72fa5a1): for each collected site assert a _translate_placeholders(/_node_translation( Call exists in the SAME enclosing FunctionDef with lineno < site lineno. EXEMPTIONS (named, req-3):
   - InputMessageNode :812 — Portal routing-CHECK node, not prompt-bearing (no neograph ${var} text).
   - Agent() :370 inside _make_agent — receives an already-(or not)-translated system_prompt PARAM; pairing is enforced at its _make_agent CALL sites (family b), not here.
   ALLOWLIST (SHRINKING, req-4 escalation — do NOT paper over):
   - _make_agent :945 (_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm) is a CONFIRMED unpaired site: it ships raw ${var} to a foreign Swarm agent (empirically reproduced 2026-07-27). Tracked by BUG neograph-s7zt3.1. The guard asserts this ONE site is the sole allowlist entry, keyed to s7zt3.1, and a meta-assert that the allowlist has exactly 1 entry (so when s7zt3.1 is fixed, the entry is removed and the guard tightens). NOT a silent exemption — a documented, ticketed, shrinking allowlist.
5. Req 3 counts: assert collected node-sites == 6 AND _make_agent sites == 3; paired == 5 node-sites (InputMessageNode:812 exempt) + 2 _make_agent sites (:945 allowlisted). Drift comment: "if any count changes, a new placeholder-emitting/_make_agent site was added — verify paired _translate_placeholders OR named exemption OR ticketed shrinking-allowlist entry; never silent drift."
6. Req 4 reconciliation: assert the guards paired-site enumeration equals the matrixs 5 dispatch branches (_lower_node think+agent/act, _lower_oracle think-variant+agent/act-variant+merge_prompt), AND record that the Portal->Swarm path (:945) is the discrepancy req-4 surfaced — the matrix classifies Portal as per-node UNSUPPORTED so it never exercises the successful Swarm lowering; guard family (b) is what closes that mutual blind spot. Escalated as neograph-s7zt3.1, not papered over.
7. Meta-guard (positive+negative, plain-substring, mirrors tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py): feed a synthetic FunctionDef constructing an LlmNode (and one calling _make_agent) with NO preceding _translate_placeholders and assert the pairing check flags it — not vacuously green.
8. Do NOT touch src/ (the s7zt3.1 FIX is a SEPARATE bug/task — tjupj only ADDS the guard + allowlists the known site). Guard + registry-set only. Run: `uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py` AND core always-on `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py` (must pass WITHOUT the agent-spec extra).

title: Type registry: register_type + auto-generate Pydantic from JSON Schema
description:
## What
A registry that maps string type names to Pydantic models. Supports both:
1. Pre-registered Python types: register_type('Draft', Draft)
2. Auto-generated from project.neograph.yaml type definitions (JSON Schema → Pydantic via create_model)

## Approach
- _type_registry: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] in a new module (src/neograph/spec_types.py or extend factory.py)
- register_type(name, cls) — explicit registration
- load_project_types(project_config) — reads types section, generates Pydantic models via create_model
- JSON Schema type mapping: string→str, number→float, integer→int, boolean→bool, list[X]→list, nested→create_model

## Deliverable
