title: MCP tool-call resilience: per-call timeout + bounded retry on TRANSPORT errors (never on isError)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a transient TRANSPORT failure (connection reset, DNS blip, streamable-http 5xx/timeout) on an MCP tool call inside an agent/act ReAct loop is retried with bounded backoff, not fatal to the run — while a tool-level isError result is NEVER retried (it is a real result the model must see).

WHY: mcp_session ships timeout=30 + raises on isError, but the agent/act TOOL-LOOP path (factory-bound tools) has NO transport retry. LLM retry exists (_llm_retry) and does not cover MCP calls. One network blip on a remote tool fails the whole run.

SCOPE: bounded retry-with-backoff on TRANSPORT exceptions only, integrated with the existing retry-policy shape (single-responsibility retry — reuse, do not fork). Add a per-call timeout on the factory/tool-loop path (parity with the session timeout=30). Classify: transport/timeout -> retry; isError / tool-domain error -> surface immediately.

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT blanket-retry all exceptions — that would replay a mutating tool call (dangerous for act mode / non-idempotent tools). Retry only PRE-RESULT transport failures; respect the idempotent= flag — a non-idempotent tool that MAY have partially executed must NOT be silently retried. A retry is the same logical call — it does not consume tool budget twice.

ACCEPTANCE: a flaky-transport fake tool retries and succeeds within the bound; an isError result surfaces on first return (no retry); a non-idempotent tool is not replayed after an ambiguous failure; budget counts the logical call once. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
A retry re-issues ONLY a pre-result MCP TRANSPORT failure (and, for idempotent
tools, an ambiguous post-send one) as the SAME logical tool call — it never retries
an isError/tool-domain result, never replays a non-idempotent tool that may have
partially executed, and never lives in `src/neograph` (transport-classification
stays in the `neograph_mcp` battery; core stays MCP-free and retry_policy-free).

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/neograph_mcp/_client.py`, add `_with_transport_resilience(tool, *,
   timeout, max_attempts, idempotent)` that wraps `tool.coroutine` via the existing
   `tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine": ...})` pattern (copy `_inject_stdio_token`
   / `_wrap_output_model`). The wrapped coroutine loops up to `max_attempts`, each
   attempt inside `async with asyncio.timeout(timeout)` (mirror `_session.py:234`),
   with bounded exponential backoff between attempts (`asyncio.sleep`).
2. Classify inside the loop: re-raise `ToolException` (isError/tool-domain) and
   `asyncio.CancelledError` immediately; `_unwrap_single(exc)` (REUSE from
   `_session.py:174`; extract to a shared `neograph_mcp/_transport.py` or import it)
   then test a NARROW transport allowlist (ConnectionError, TimeoutError,
   `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`, connect-time errors). Anything not transport
   surfaces immediately. A `ValidationError` from the output-model wrap is NOT in the
   allowlist and surfaces.
3. Idempotency + pre/post-send split: pre-send failures (connect refused/DNS/connect
   timeout) retry regardless of `idempotent`; ambiguous post-send failures (call-time
   `TimeoutError`, mid-flight reset) retry ONLY when `idempotent=True`, else surface.
   Mirror the resource-replay gate posture (`di.py:180`/`NonIdempotentReplayError`);
   conservative default is non-idempotent.
4. Compose the wrap OUTERMOST in `_make_tool_factory` (`_client.py:252`) — after
   identity injection, rename, and `_wrap_output_model` — so a retry re-runs the
   whole transport call while result/domain errors still propagate.
5. Thread new params: `timeout: float = 30.0` (parity with `mcp_session`),
   `max_attempts`/backoff knobs, and `idempotent: bool = False` on `mcp_tool_factory`
   (:352); on `mcp_tool_factories` (:295) add `idempotents: dict[str, bool] | None`
   and a per-tool timeout mirroring the existing `output_models`/`parses` dict shape.
   Consumer sets `idempotent` to match their `Tool(idempotent=)`.
6. NO core change: budget-once and the async-only invoke path are already satisfied
   (`_agent_cycle.py` records one logical call; retry inside the coroutine is
   invisible to `ToolBudgetTracker`). Only ASSERT this in tests.
7. Tests (battery tier, keyless, deterministic fake double — copy `test_mcp_battery.py`
   style; TDD the four acceptance cases FIRST):
   (a) flaky-transport fake (raises transport error N< max then succeeds) -> succeeds
   within the bound; (b) isError/`ToolException` fake -> surfaces on first return, no
   retry; (c) non-idempotent tool + ambiguous (timeout) failure -> not replayed,
   surfaces; idempotent tool + same -> retried; (d) assert `ToolBudgetTracker` counts
   the logical call exactly once across a retried-then-succeeded call.
8. Update `website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx`: document MCP-tool
   transport retry as the tool-path arm of Layer 1 (the factory now bounds each call
   and retries transport-only), preserving the "never retry isError / never replay a
   non-idempotent tool" rationale. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
notes:
## Findings

REUSE TARGET — the resilience wrapper lives in the BATTERY, not core. Add a new
`_with_transport_resilience(tool, *, timeout, max_attempts, idempotent)` coroutine
wrapper in `src/neograph_mcp/_client.py`, applied as the OUTERMOST wrap in
`_make_tool_factory` (after identity injection, rename, and `_wrap_output_model`).
This is the SAME wrap-the-`.coroutine`-via-`tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine":...})`
pattern already used TWICE in that file: `_inject_stdio_token` (_client.py:175) and
`_wrap_output_model` (_client.py:207). Do NOT invent a new mechanism — copy that shape.

WHY the battery, not `src/neograph`: `tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py`
scans `src/neograph` ONLY and bans `import mcp` / MCP client lifecycle there; core
must stay MCP-free. Separately, `tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py`
(neograph-s5yk) enforces ZERO `retry_policy`/`RetryPolicy` references anywhere in
`src/neograph`. Both guards force transport-retry into `neograph_mcp`.

THE "single-responsibility retry" the task says to REUSE-not-fork is the three-layer
retry MODEL (doc `website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx`), NOT a
RetryPolicy class — that class was deliberately removed. This task adds the missing
piece of Layer 1 (transport) for the MCP-tool call path, which today has none. Frame
it in the doc's terms; do not resurrect `compile(retry_policy=)`.

CLASSIFICATION IS CLEAN BY CONSTRUCTION (the isError-never-retry guarantee):
- isError on the factory path raises `_MCPToolExecutionError`, a `ToolException`
  subclass (`langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:99`). With `handle_tool_errors=True`
  (the adapter default the battery preserves) langchain CATCHES it in `arun` and
  returns a normal error `ToolMessage` — so isError usually is not even an exception
  at our wrapper, and when it is, it is a `ToolException`.
- Transport failures are NOT `ToolException` subclasses — they propagate raw
  (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`, anyio
  `ExceptionGroup`).
  => The wrapper catches a NARROW transport allowlist and re-raises `ToolException`
  (and CancelledError) immediately. isError/tool-domain/ValidationError are never
  retried because they are never in the allowlist. This is the anti-band-aid.

REUSE `_unwrap_single` (`src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:174`) to normalise the anyio
`ExceptionGroup` wrapping BEFORE classifying — it already handles the nested-group
cases (refused port -> ExceptionGroup(ConnectError); dead stdio ->
ExceptionGroup(ExceptionGroup(McpError))). It currently lives in `_session.py`;
extract to a shared spot (e.g. a small `neograph_mcp/_transport.py`) or import it
into `_client.py`. Do not re-implement group-unwrapping.

PER-CALL TIMEOUT PARITY: `mcp_session`/`McpSession` already bound each call with
`timeout=30.0` default (`_session.py:32,323-324` via `read_timeout_seconds`, and the
connect via `async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout)` at `_session.py:234`). The
FACTORY path (`mcp_tool_factory`/`mcp_tool_factories`) passes NO timeout today, so a
bound tool inherits the adapter's 300s read timeout. Add a `timeout: float = 30.0`
factory param and enforce it by wrapping the coroutine in `async with
asyncio.timeout(timeout)` (mirror the session's connect line) — same default as the
session for parity.

BUDGET-ONCE IS FREE if the retry lives in the coroutine wrapper. The ReAct loop
calls the tool exactly once per logical call and records budget once:
`_agent_cycle.py` `_tool_call_precheck` -> `tracker.record_call` (sync path
`_record_tool_result` :450; async path pre-reserves at :668). A retry INSIDE the
wrapped `.coroutine` is invisible to `ToolBudgetTracker`, so the logical call counts
once automatically — no core change needed. Verify with an assertion, do not
re-plumb budgeting.

MCP TOOLS ARE ASYNC-ONLY: the adapter tool has no sync `.func`; the sync tools seam
raises via `_raise_sync_tool_async` (`_agent_cycle.py:365,638-639`). All MCP tool
execution goes through `_ainvoke_tool_timed` -> `tool_fn.ainvoke` -> `.coroutine`
(`_agent_cycle.py:454-461,670`). The wrapper only needs the async coroutine — which
is all `_client.py` ever wraps. No sync path to cover.

IDEMPOTENCY GATE precedent to mirror: the resource-replay path already refuses to
replay a non-idempotent producer — `di.py:180,209` gates on `producer_idempotent`,
raising `NonIdempotentReplayError` (`errors.py:288`); the flag originates on
`Tool.idempotent` (`tool.py:58`, conservative default False) and is read in core as
`idempotent_by_tool` (`_agent_cycle.py:533`). Apply the SAME conservative posture
here: an AMBIGUOUS post-send failure (read timeout / mid-flight reset — the call may
have partially executed) is retried ONLY when idempotent=True; a definitively
pre-send failure (connect refused / DNS / connect timeout) is safe to retry
regardless.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:175 `_inject_stdio_token` and :207 `_wrap_output_model` -- the exact coroutine-wrap pattern (`tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine": ...})`) to copy; :252 `_make_tool_factory` is where the new wrap is composed (outermost, after output_model); :295 `mcp_tool_factories` / :352 `mcp_tool_factory` get the new `timeout`/`idempotent`(+ dict form)/`max_attempts` params.
- src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:174 `_unwrap_single` -- REUSE for ExceptionGroup normalisation; :234 `asyncio.timeout(self._timeout)` and :323 `read_timeout_seconds` -- the timeout=30 parity precedent; :66 `McpToolCallError` -- the raw-session isError type (session path, not factory path).
- langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:99 `_MCPToolExecutionError(ToolException)` -- the isError type to EXCLUDE from retry.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:454 `_ainvoke_tool_timed` (single async invoke site), :450/:668 budget record-once, :533 `idempotent_by_tool`, :365/:638 sync-tool-async guard.
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx -- the three-layer model to align with (and update: MCP-tool transport retry is Layer 1 for the tool path).
- tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py + tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py:356 -- the two guards forcing this into neograph_mcp.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py -- battery test-harness style (fake tool double keeps the fast tier deterministic, keyless).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- WORKTREE COLLISION (from epic neograph-n34iy): this task overlaps sibling
  neograph-cnxlx (connection-reuse+reconnect) and neograph-32qtx (mcp test fakes) on
  `_client.py`/`_session.py`; the epic mandates a SEPARATE WORKTREE per child and
  sets execution order fakes(32qtx) -> reuse(cnxlx) -> resilience(uixi1). Expect to
  rebase onto their `_client.py` edits.
- The acceptance "flaky-transport fake tool" needs an async fake tool whose coroutine
  raises a transport error N times then succeeds. neograph-32qtx (MCP test fakes) is
  slated to land FIRST and may provide it; if not yet available, build a minimal
  langchain `StructuredTool`/`Tool` with a flaky `coroutine` directly in the test.
- Wrap ORDER matters: resilience must be OUTERMOST so a transport blip during the
  output-model call retries the whole transport call, but it must catch ONLY
  transport types so a `ValidationError` from `_wrap_output_model` (a result/domain
  error) surfaces, never retried.
- `asyncio.timeout` raises `TimeoutError` — treat as an AMBIGUOUS post-send failure
  (call may have executed): retry only if idempotent. Do not classify a call-time
  timeout as pre-send.
- Do NOT catch bare `BaseException`/`CancelledError` in the retry loop (the
  ReAct-loop cancellation path must propagate); catch the transport allowlist +
  re-raise `ToolException` first.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the idempotent flag is ALREADY declared on the neograph
  `Tool(idempotent=)` spec and known in core (`idempotent_by_tool`), but the
  tool-factory seam has no channel to receive it from core (the factory just returns
  a tool; the ownership invariant keeps core MCP-free). Recommended resolution: add
  an explicit `idempotent: bool = False` param to `mcp_tool_factory` (and an
  `idempotents: dict[str, bool] | None` to `mcp_tool_factories`, mirroring the
  existing `output_models`/`parses` dict params), conservative default False, which
  the consumer sets to match their `Tool(idempotent=)`. Confirm this duplication is
  acceptable vs. a more invasive core->battery idempotency channel.
## Codebase Disease Scan (uixi1)
Pattern: forked/duplicated retry logic — would a NEW transport-retry wrapper duplicate an existing retry helper (violating single-responsibility retry)?
Scan command: grep -rn 'retry|max_attempt|backoff|RetryPolicy' src/neograph/ src/neograph_mcp/
Total instances found: existing retries are ALL LLM-domain — _llm_retry (_ainvoke_json_with_retry / structured-output reparse) and compiler.py model.with_retry (transient API). NONE cover MCP transport.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph/_llm_retry.py (whole) | structured-output JSON reparse retry | ALLOWLIST | LLM-domain, not transport — correctly NOT reused; forcing MCP transport retry through it would be the wrong coupling |
| 2 | src/neograph/compiler.py:100 | model.with_retry(...) transient API | ALLOWLIST | LLM-provider transient retry, lives in core llm path; MCP transport is a different layer |
| 3 | (new) src/neograph_mcp/_client.py _with_transport_resilience | net-new coroutine wrapper | MIGRATE/ADD | transport retry is a genuinely NEW concern in the neograph_mcp battery (core stays MCP-free + retry_policy-free per invariant); reuse the tool.model_copy(coroutine=) wrapper PATTERN, not a core retry helper |

No duplication to migrate — the new wrapper is net-new in the right layer. BLOCKED pending idempotent-flag-plumbing decision (NEEDS_USER_INPUT).

GATE: PASS — research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present on the task labels.

VALIDATED (claims checked against code, all confirmed):
- Layering constraint is REAL: test_guards_function_local_imports.py:test_src_neograph_does_not_reference_retry_policy rglobs src/neograph and bans RetryPolicy/retry_policy; test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py rglobs SRC_DIR only and bans MCP lifecycle. Wrapper correctly forced into neograph_mcp.
- Reuse pattern REAL: _inject_stdio_token (_client.py:175) and _wrap_output_model (:207) both use tool.model_copy(update={'coroutine':...}); _make_tool_factory (:252) composes wraps outermost-last. New wrap slots in cleanly.
- _unwrap_single (_session.py:174) exists and handles nested ExceptionGroup; asyncio.timeout(self._timeout) at :234, default 30 — timeout parity precedent real.
- Budget-once: _agent_cycle records one call per logical call (record_call :450 sync, pre-reserve :668 async); retry inside coroutine is invisible to ToolBudgetTracker. Correct.
- isError classification is CLEAN BY CONSTRUCTION: verified _MCPToolExecutionError IS a subclass of langchain_core.tools.ToolException. Re-raising ToolException immediately => isError never retried. Anti-band-aid holds.
- Idempotency-gate precedent real: di.py:180 gates replay on producer_idempotent -> NonIdempotentReplayError; Tool.idempotent default False (tool.py:58); idempotent_by_tool in _agent_cycle:533.

FINDINGS:

- [HIGH] Finding: the NEEDS_USER_INPUT flag on idempotent-flag-plumbing is REAL and correctly raised, but UNDER-POSED. Verified the seam: core calls factory(config, tool_spec.config) (_tool_loop.py:318,343) — the factory receives Tool.config (a dict), NOT Tool.idempotent. So core knows idempotent but the battery factory has no channel for it: real gap. Two corrections to the framing so the human decides on accurate tradeoffs: (1) the alternative is NOT purely 'more invasive' — a channel PARTIALLY EXISTS (tool_spec.config is already threaded to the factory at call time), and Tool.idempotent is a GENERIC Tool field, not MCP-specific, so surfacing it does NOT breach the MCP-free ownership invariant (that guard bans MCP lifecycle/imports in core, not generic tool metadata). (2) The recommended duplication has a concrete SAFETY risk the framing omits: the Core Invariant is 'never replay a non-idempotent tool that may have partially executed'; declaring idempotent in BOTH Tool(idempotent=) and mcp_tool_factory(idempotent=) with no cross-check means a drift silently either replays a non-idempotent mutation (invariant violated) or needlessly refuses to retry a safe idempotent tool. That is exactly the drift class the anti-band-aid clause warns against. Suggestion: pose the human choice as (a) single-source — fold Tool.idempotent into the value passed as tool_config (or extend the call tuple) so the factory reads it at call time, no duplication; vs (b) keep the build-time param BUT add a compile/lint cross-check that fails loud on a Tool(idempotent=) vs factory-idempotent mismatch (mirrors the codebase's fail-loud posture). Do NOT ship bare duplication with no guard.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: internal contradiction between plan step 3 and the Risks section on connect-timeout classification. Step 3 lists 'connect timeout' as a PRE-SEND failure that retries regardless of idempotent; the Risks note says 'asyncio.timeout raises TimeoutError — treat as AMBIGUOUS post-send... Do not classify a call-time timeout as pre-send.' A single outer 'async with asyncio.timeout(timeout)' wrapping the whole attempt cannot distinguish a connect-phase timeout (safe, pre-send) from a call-phase timeout (ambiguous) — both surface as a bare TimeoutError. So step 3's 'connect timeout retries regardless of idempotent' is unrealizable without SEPARATE connect-scope vs call-scope timeouts, which the plan does not specify (and the factory does connect+call in one coroutine per the stateless-per-call session model). Suggestion: either accept the conservative Risks posture (ALL timeouts = ambiguous → drop 'connect timeout' from the pre-send bucket in step 3), or structure two timeout scopes so connect-timeout is distinguishable. Reconcile the two sections before implementing.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: coverage gap — the resilience wrapper wraps only tool.coroutine, but the factory's per-superstep client.get_tools() enumeration connect (inside _factory, _client.py:255-257) is a SEPARATE uncovered transport touchpoint. title: Design project.neograph.schema.json (project surface)
description:
## What
JSON Schema for the project surface file — types, tools, and models that pipeline specs reference.

## Schema must cover
- types: name → JSON Schema object (fields with types). Maps to Pydantic/Zod.
- tools: name → description + params schema. Tool implementations are language-specific.
- models: name → provider + model ID + optional config (temperature, etc.)

## Approach
- JSON Schema draft 2020-12
- Types use JSON Schema type definitions (string, number, integer, boolean, list, nested objects)
- Tool params are JSON Schema objects
- Model configs are freeform dicts with known keys

## Deliverable
src/neograph/schemas/project.neograph.schema.json + tests
design:

JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Three top-level properties: types (additionalProperties: JSON Schema object), tools (additionalProperties: {description, params}), models (additionalProperties: {provider, model, config}). File: src/neograph/schemas/project.neograph.schema.json

## Core Invariant
Every name referenced in a pipeline spec must resolve to an entry in the project surface.

title: Stage C: render error-hierarchy tree from manifest (DECISION 3: structure from manifest, curated annotations preserved)
description: Part B deferred from rfl7b's implement. exception_hierarchy[] (11 parent-linked entries) backs the tree STRUCTURE, but the live api.mdx tree carries curated content NOT in the manifest: the '(ValueError)' base note, em-dash descriptions, and a deliberate non-alphabetical lifecycle-phase sibling order referenced by the prose above it. CRUX to settle first: verify the MDX partial-include mechanism (Expressive-Code fenced-block rendering — the site has ZERO existing partial-import precedent) does not regress rendering, and design a hand-authored order+annotation sidecar so the manifest contributes a consistency check without rewording curated text. Keep the tree a fenced block (no headings) so exception anchors are not double-emitted. If the partial mechanism proves too risky, keep hand-written + add a manifest-vs-doc consistency test instead.
design:
## Core Invariant
The error-hierarchy tree stays a hand-authored FENCED block (no headings, so the 11 exception anchors are emitted exactly once — as manifest symbols, never doubled): the manifest contributes a STRUCTURE consistency check (class set + parent links), while curated content the manifest cannot express — the '(ValueError)' base note, em-dash descriptions, and the lifecycle-phase (non-alphabetical) sibling order that the prose narrates — is preserved verbatim.

## Implementation Plan
DECISION 3 realized as: keep hand-written tree + add a manifest-vs-doc CONSISTENCY test (the task's sanctioned fallback; generate-partial is DECLINED — see notes: no codegen/partial precedent, and the manifest lacks the curated order+annotations so a generator needs a hand-authored sidecar anyway = net-negative).

1. Leave api.mdx:688-708 UNCHANGED (do not regenerate; do not add headings; keep the fence). The block is already structurally consistent with the manifest.
2. Add a consistency test in tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py (the home of manifest-vs-artifact guards). Reuse the existing load patterns: _load_committed_manifest-style JSON read (copy from tests/test_stage_c_reference.py:42) for exception_hierarchy[], and read api.mdx text via a REPO_ROOT-relative Path.
3. Parse the fenced tree: locate the '### Error Hierarchy' section, take the first ``` fence after it, and recover (class_name -> parent) from the tree glyphs by indentation depth (├──/└── mark a child of the nearest shallower node; │ is a continuation rail). For each line strip the ' (ValueError)' parenthetical and the ' — description' em-dash tail to isolate the bare class name.
4. Assert STRUCTURE ONLY, three ways: (a) tree class-name SET == manifest name SET; (b) for every class the tree-derived parent == manifest parent (NeographError -> None/base); (c) no extra/missing nodes. Do NOT assert sibling ORDER and Do NOT assert description text (both are deliberately curated/divergent).
5. Add a focused assertion that the tree is a FENCED block and that NONE of the 11 class names appears as a markdown heading in api.mdx (reuses the fence-aware line scan mirroring remark-api.mjs:76-79) — pins the no-double-emit invariant so a future edit that promotes the tree to headings fails loudly.
6. Gate: `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py tests/test_stage_c_reference.py` green; then `cd website && npm run build` (and `npm test`) to confirm no rendering/autolink regression. No manifest regen needed (exception_hierarchy is already correct).
7. Three-surface / doc-parity note: this is docs-only; no IR change, so the three-API-surface rule does not apply. The parity that matters is manifest<->doc, enforced by the new test.
notes:
## Findings

CRUX SETTLED — RECOMMEND FALLBACK (consistency test), NOT generate-partial.

- The site has ZERO codegen-into-.mdx precedent AND zero MDX partial-import precedent — confirmed. api.mdx is 100% hand-authored; the ONLY manifest machinery is (a) scripts/gen_api_manifest.py which EMITS website/src/data/api-manifest.json, and (b) website/plugins/remark-api.mjs which VALIDATES/AUTOLINKS backticked refs against it. Nothing writes .mdx. remark-api.mjs:14 states outright: 'neograph reference content stays hand-written until Stage C generates it from the manifest' — Part B (this task) is where that could happen, and the recommendation is to NOT introduce a rendering pipeline.

- The fenced-block requirement is already SATISFIED and load-bearing. remark-api.mjs setup() collects reference-page heading slugs but SKIPS fenced content (the `if (fence) continue;` loop, remark-api.mjs:76-79). So the error-hierarchy tree, being a plain ``` fence, emits NO headings/anchors. The 11 exception classes already carry manifest anchors as SYMBOLS (symbols[] entries, anchors = slug(name)); if the tree were re-rendered as headings the anchors would double-emit and github-slugger would append `-1`, breaking the manifest-owns-both-ends invariant that test_stage_c_reference.py pins. Keeping the tree fenced is therefore mandatory, and any 'generate a partial' path must reproduce a fence (Expressive Code), not headings — extra risk for zero anchor benefit.

- The manifest CANNOT reproduce the curated tree. exception_hierarchy[] carries only {name, parent, anchor, doc}. The live tree adds three curated things absent from (or divergent from) the manifest: (1) the '(ValueError)' base-class note on ConstructError; (2) em-dash short descriptions that are NOT the manifest 'doc' first-lines (e.g. tree says 'assembly-time validation failures'; manifest doc = 'Assembly-time validation errors during Construct creation.'); (3) a deliberate NON-alphabetical, lifecycle-phase sibling order (ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError at top; PromptVarMissing, StateMissingError, NodeOutputError, NonIdempotentReplayError, ResourceExpiredError under ExecutionError) that the prose at api.mdx:690 explicitly references ('while the graph is executing / assembly / compile / configuration'). The manifest ships entries ALPHABETICALLY sorted (gen_api_manifest.py:359 `sorted(..., key=lambda c: c.__name__)`). So a generator would need a hand-authored order+annotation sidecar anyway — reintroducing the very hand-authored content the generation was meant to remove, with no net win.

- Structure is a perfect match TODAY: manifest 11 entries == tree 11 classes, and parent-links agree. So a consistency test passes immediately and only guards against future drift.

## Relevant Code
- website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx:688-708 — the '### Error Hierarchy' section: prose (690, references the lifecycle order), the FENCED tree (692-704, the curated content), CheckpointSchemaError bold note (706), importable-list (708). This is the block to preserve verbatim.
- website/src/data/api-manifest.json exception_hierarchy[] — 11 parent-linked {name,parent,anchor,doc}; NeographError has parent=null; alphabetical.
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:351-373 _exception_hierarchy() — introspects neograph._errors, sorts by __name__, one entry per NeographError subclass, parent = first NeographError base. slug() at module scope gives anchors.
- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:76-79 — the fence-skipping heading collector (proves fenced tree emits no anchors). remark-api.mjs:14-20 — 'hand-written until Stage C' + the accepted SOFT seam.
- tests/test_stage_c_reference.py — Stage C RED guard; Core Invariant 'heading slug == manifest anchor'; the reuse EXEMPLAR for reading the committed manifest (_load_committed_manifest) and for how anchors must stay unique/slug-stable.
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:56-74 (_load_gen_api_manifest via importlib), :45-49 path constants, :229 test_every_symbol_anchor_is_slug_of_its_name — the file where a manifest-vs-doc consistency test BELONGS and the load/parse patterns to copy.
- website/ build gate: `cd website && npm run build` (Astro+Starlight, ~2s, remark-api runs in-build so a broken ref FAILS build); `npm test` runs the plugin's node:test suite.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- If ever regenerated: alphabetical manifest order would silently reorder the tree and DESYNC the prose at api.mdx:690 (which narrates the lifecycle order). The consistency test must assert STRUCTURE ONLY (name set + parent map), NOT order and NOT description text, or it will fight the curated content.
- The consistency test must parse the fence by INDENTATION (├──/└──/│ tree-glyphs) to recover parent nesting, then compare the derived parent-map to manifest parent-links. Strip the '(ValueError)' parenthetical and the em-dash tail before extracting each class name.
- Do NOT add headings for the 11 errors to 'fix' SOFT-autolink inertness — that reintroduces the double-emit the fence exists to avoid (test_stage_c_reference invariant). Error autolink inertness is the accepted Stage B/C seam.
- generate-partial risk if pursued anyway: introduces first-ever .mdx codegen + first-ever partial import to a live-deploy (Amplify-on-push) site; Expressive Code fence rendering of an imported partial is unverified; the curated sidecar makes it net-negative. Declined.
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom uqy66.19)
Pattern: hand-authored error-hierarchy STRUCTURE (class set + parent links) that can silently drift from api-manifest.json exception_hierarchy[] with no guard; plus the no-double-emit invariant (an exception class must NOT appear as a markdown heading, else its anchor is emitted twice).
Scan commands: grep error-tree/exception enumerations across website docs; grep '^#+ .*<ErrorClass>' for class-name headings; locate existing manifest-vs-doc consistency tests.
Total: 1 tree instance + 0 double-emit violations.

| # | Locus | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | reference/api.mdx error-hierarchy fenced tree | hand-authored, no manifest guard | MIGRATE (add guard) | uorb4 adds structure-only consistency test; tree stays hand-written (curated order/annotations manifest can't express) |
| 2 | other website pages mentioning ConstructError/etc. | prose/code references, NOT a tree enumeration | ALLOWLIST | not structural duplication of the hierarchy |
| 3 | class names as markdown headings | NONE (3 grep hits are python '# comment' lines inside code blocks, not headings) | ALLOWLIST + PIN | no double-emit today; new guard's fence/heading assertion pins it going forward |

Reuse: tests/test_stage_c_reference.py (rfl7b Stage-C infra: manifest load + anchor tests) is the home/pattern for the new consistency test.
No generate-partial (declined in research); keep tree verbatim, guard structure only (not order, not descriptions).
## Architect Review

Reviewed the research findings, Core Invariant, and 7-step implementation plan against the live code (api.mdx:688-708, api-manifest.json exception_hierarchy[], remark-api.mjs:74-79, tests/test_stage_c_reference.py, tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py). Verified every load-bearing claim: manifest has exactly 11 parent-linked entries matching the tree's parentage; manifest is alphabetical + carries only {name,parent,anchor,doc} (cannot express order/annotations); the fence-skip heading collector is real; no class-name markdown headings exist today.

- [ENDORSED, not a finding] DECLINING generate-partial is CORRECT and well-justified. Verified independently: (a) zero .mdx-codegen and zero partial-import precedent — remark-api.mjs:14 states reference content 'stays hand-written until Stage C'; (b) the manifest genuinely cannot express the curated content — it is alphabetical (gen_api_manifest.py sorts by __name__) while the tree uses a deliberate lifecycle-phase sibling order the prose at api.mdx:690 narrates, and it lacks the '(ValueError)' note and the em-dash descriptions (which diverge from manifest 'doc' first-lines). A generator would need a hand-authored order+annotation sidecar = net-negative. The ticket explicitly sanctions this fallback. Not under-delivering.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: the plan's name-extraction strip-list (step 3 / Risks) enumerates ONLY ' (ValueError)' and the ' — desc' tail, but the tree ROOT line is 'NeographError (base)'. Implemented literally, the root class name is extracted as 'NeographError (base)', so assertion 4(a) (tree name-SET == manifest name-SET) fails on day one. Suggestion: generalize the parenthetical strip to 'any trailing ( ... ) group' (covers both '(base)' and '(ValueError)') rather than the literal '(ValueError)', OR special-case the root (glyph-less line -> parent=None) and strip its '(base)'. One-line plan edit; robust extraction = split on em-dash first, then rstrip any trailing '( ... )', then take the token.

- [LOW] Finding: step 5's no-double-emit check ('no class name appears as a markdown heading') does not specify exact-match vs substring. The invariant is slug(heading)==anchor double-emit, so the correct test is heading-text EQUALS a class name (exact/slug-equality), not 'contains'. A substring check would over-fire on a legitimate future heading like '### ExecutionError semantics'. Suggestion: assert exact heading-text equality (or slugger.slug(heading) == anchor) against the 11 names, fence-aware over the WHOLE file (as planned). Non-flaky today: verified no class-name headings exist; CheckpointSchemaError at :706 is bold prose, not a heading.

- [LOW] Finding: mild reuse duplication. test_guards_api_manifest.py ALREADY defines CORE_MANIFEST_PATH (line ~48) pointing at the committed api-manifest.json. Step 2 says to 'copy _load_committed_manifest from test_stage_c_reference.py:42' — copying that helper into a file that already has the path constant reinvents a one-liner. Suggestion: reuse the existing CORE_MANIFEST_PATH and json.loads(CORE_MANIFEST_PATH.read_text()); no cross-file helper copy needed. (test_stage_c_reference.py remains the conceptual exemplar.)

- [LOW] Finding: the indentation/glyph parser is inherently coupled to the current 2-space rendering (parent = nearest previous shallower glyph column; verified the algorithm resolves correctly for THIS tree, including the '│' rail disambiguating CheckpointSchemaError vs the ExecutionError leaves at the same column). A cosmetic reindent would false-positive. This is acceptable — the guard's PURPOSE is to fire on tree edits and force re-verification — but note the fragility so it is a deliberate choice, not a surprise.

Structure-only assertion (name set + parent links, NOT order, NOT descriptions) is correctly targeted: it catches a new/removed/reparented exception while allowing the curated order+annotation divergence. Confirmed sound.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Triage (atom uqy66.21)
Verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT (1 MEDIUM, 3 LOW). Routed: refine atom uqy66.53 (generalize parenthetical strip to any trailing '(...)' so 'NeographError (base)' + '(ValueError)' both parse); write-test (uqy66.22) now depends on it.
## Refinement (atom uqy66.53) — plan adjustments per review
- MEDIUM: generalize class-name extraction to strip ANY trailing parenthetical, not just ' (ValueError)'. The tree ROOT is 'NeographError (base)'; use re.sub(r'\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$','', name_after_glyphs_and_before_em_dash) so '(base)', '(ValueError)', and any future annotation all reduce to the bare class name. Verify the resulting SET == manifest name set on day one.
- LOW-1 (no-double-emit): assert EXACT heading-text equality (or slugger.slug(heading)==anchor) against the 11 exception names, fence-aware over the whole file — NOT substring (a substring check over-fires on a legit future '### ExecutionError semantics'). CheckpointSchemaError at api.mdx:706 is BOLD PROSE, not a heading — fine.
- LOW-2 (reuse): do NOT copy _load_committed_manifest from test_stage_c_reference.py. test_guards_api_manifest.py ALREADY has CORE_MANIFEST_PATH (~:48) -> reuse json.loads(CORE_MANIFEST_PATH.read_text()).
- LOW-3 (parser fragility): the ├──/└──/│ indentation parser is coupled to the current 2-space rendering; a cosmetic reindent would false-positive. ACCEPTED as deliberate — the guard's purpose is to fire on tree edits and force re-verification; document this in the test docstring so it is a known trade-off, not a surprise.
Structure-only assertion set (name set + parent links, NOT order/descriptions) confirmed correctly targeted. Research unchanged; approach adjustment only.
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestErrorHierarchyTreeConsistency::test_tree_class_set_matches_manifest_when_committed (+ ::test_tree_parent_links_match_manifest_when_committed, ::test_no_exception_class_is_a_markdown_heading)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-gf9g
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-gf9g` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-gf9g/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-gf9g
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-gf9g)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gf9g --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gf9g --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-gf9g/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-gf9g codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-gf9g
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-gf9g
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-gf9g`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-gf9g)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gf9g --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-gf9g sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-aiiz
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-aiiz` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-aiiz/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-aiiz
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-aiiz)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-aiiz --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-aiiz --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-aiiz/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-aiiz codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-aiiz/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-kec0k
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-kec0k` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-kec0k/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-kec0k
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-kec0k)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-kec0k --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-kec0k --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-kec0k/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-kec0k codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-kec0k/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-kec0k
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-kec0k
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-kec0k`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-kec0k)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-kec0k --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-kec0k sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-uorb4
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-uorb4
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-uorb4`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-uorb4)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>

   ```

     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.

exists:


     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.

       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.

   ```
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |

   ```

   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-cvjfm`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-cvjfm)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-wqzel
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-wqzel` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-wqzel/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-wqzel
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-wqzel)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wqzel --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wqzel --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-wqzel/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-wqzel codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-wqzel/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Implement neograph-wqzel
description:

then refactor.

1. **Green**: Write minimum code to make the failing test pass
2. **Verify**: Run the SAME test that FAILED -- must now PASS
3. **Refactor**: With passing tests as safety net
4. **Quality gate**: Run project quality command

## When EXISTING Tests Fail

1. STOP. Do NOT modify the failing tests.
2. Re-read the Core Invariant.
3. If your approach violates the invariant -> revert and rethink.
4. If the test has a genuine bug -> document WHY before modifying.

Sacred rule: NEVER adjust tests to match code without justification.

Close the original beads task:
```bash
bd close neograph-wqzel
```
acceptance_criteria: Quality command passes. Regression test passes. Original task closed.

title: Stage A precursor: enrich manifest lint_issue_kinds with severity/meaning + capture dynamically-constructed DI kinds
description:
Prerequisite for rfl7b's lint-kind reference section (design-doc Open Question #3, resolved: enrich-first). Today scripts/gen_api_manifest.py emits lint_issue_kinds as a bare list of ~10 NAME strings, and its AST-walk MISSES the dynamically-constructed DI kinds (from_input/from_config/from_input_model/from_config_model) that the docs document. The api.mdx lint table has 3 columns (Kind/Severity/Meaning) and its kind-set overlaps the manifest by only 3.

Scope:
1. Extend the manifest lint_issue_kinds entries from bare names to objects carrying {kind, severity, meaning} (or a parallel structure) sourced from the authoritative lint kind definitions in src/neograph/lint.py, so the Severity/Meaning columns are manifest-owned, not hand-authored.
2. Capture the DI kinds the current AST-walk misses (from_input/from_config + their _model forms) so the manifest kind-set is COMPLETE vs the docs.
3. Re-pin the Stage-A snapshot/freshness guard for the new shape.
Once done, rfl7b generates the lint-kind table from the enriched manifest (drift-checked) instead of hand-writing it. Until then, rfl7b keeps the lint section hand-written (excluded from Stage C rendering).
design:
## Core Invariant
The manifest's lint_issue_kinds set stays COMPLETE and zero-drift with what lint() actually emits: every kind emitted by src/neograph/lint.py (literal-emitted AND DI-variable-emitted) appears exactly once, and its severity follows the single canonical required->ERROR/WARN rule (__main__.py:199) -- no hand-authored kind list, severity, or meaning may silently diverge from the code.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add ONE authoritative registry constant to src/neograph/lint.py (e.g. LINT_KIND_META: dict[str, tuple[severity, meaning]] or a small frozen dataclass/list). It carries all 14 kinds with severity in {ERROR, WARN, WARN/ERROR, varies} and a one-line meaning. Source severity from the derivation in Findings (matches __main__.py:199 + the dual/varies cases the bool can't express); source meaning by MOVING the hand-authored strings out of api.mdx:540-548 into this registry (that is what makes Severity/Meaning 'manifest-owned'). This lives in lint.py because lint.py is the authoritative home for lint kinds (task scope 1).
2. In scripts/gen_api_manifest.py, EXTEND (do not replace) extract_lint_issue_kinds(): keep the AST walk to discover literal-emitted kinds, UNION in the 4 DI kinds from neograph.di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS (reuse the frozenset -> .value), then look up severity+meaning from the lint.py registry, and emit a list of {kind, severity, meaning} objects sorted by kind. Rename the fn if its list[str] contract changes (e.g. build_lint_issue_kinds()), update the module docstring at scripts line ~17.
3. Add a COMPLETENESS cross-check in the generator (or as a guard): (AST-literal kinds UNION DI kinds) == registry.keys(); raise loud on mismatch so adding a kind without a registry entry breaks regen. This preserves the zero-drift property the AST walk exists for.
4. Regenerate the snapshot: run scripts/gen_api_manifest.py (or its main()) to rewrite website/src/data/api-manifest.json with the 14-object enriched lint_issue_kinds (sort_keys=True/indent=2 already handled by _write_json).
5. Re-pin tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py: extend _KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR from 10 -> 14 (add the 4 DI kinds), update test_extracted_kinds_are_superset_of_known_floor to read kind from the object shape (item['kind']), and add an assertion that each entry carries non-empty severity+meaning and that severity is in the allowed set. Keep the superset/floor semantics (future kinds auto-picked-up). The TestApiManifestFreshness class already asserts committed==fresh-regen, so step 4 must be run before this passes.
6. Do NOT touch api.mdx in THIS task -- rfl7b (neograph-cvjfm) keeps the lint section hand-written and Stage-C-excluded until it consumes this enriched manifest. Removing the api.mdx table now would strand rfl7b; leave it, this task only makes the manifest the future source of truth.
7. Gates: uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py, plus mypy on lint.py + the generator. No website build needed (api.mdx unchanged).

It captures the 10 LITERAL kinds but STRUCTURALLY CANNOT see the 4 DI kinds because they are emitted as kind=kind_str where kind_str=binding.kind.value (a variable, lint.py:77). title: Batch 6: NeographError cleanup — eliminate 7 entries from NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST (Clusters 12+14)
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §5
- docs/design/any-audit-analysis-2026-05-20.md Clusters 12 + 14

## Maintainer decision on Cluster 14
Convert all 6 TypeError sites to \`ConstructError\`. The allowlist comment "tests assert TypeError" was self-reinforcing; tests update with the conversion. \`ConstructError\` (NeographError subclass deriving from ValueError) is the honest signal at the framework boundary for assembly-time misuse.

## Cluster 12: Scanner false positive

**Entry (1)**: \`_construct_validation.py:517\` — \`raise _build_no_producer_error(...)\` which returns a NeographError. Scanner can't see through the helper call.

**Fix**: inline the call (\`raise ConstructError.build(...)\` directly) OR improve the scanner to follow simple helper-call patterns. Inlining is simplest.

## Cluster 14: User-facing TypeError that COULD be ConstructError

**Entries (6)**: \`forward.py:121\`, \`forward.py:130\`, \`modifiers.py:317\`, \`modifiers.py:323\`, \`modifiers.py:330\`, \`modifiers.py:337\`.

**Hypothesis**: These raise \`TypeError\` for user mistakes in \`ForwardConstruct\` constructor/forward override misuse and in \`Modifiable.map()\` lambda content. Assembly-time misuse → \`ConstructError\`.

## Structural fix

```python
# forward.py:121, 130 (ForwardConstruct misuse)
raise ConstructError.build(...)  # was: raise TypeError(...)

# modifiers.py:317, 323, 330, 337 (Modifiable.map lambda misuse)
raise ConstructError.build(...)  # was: raise TypeError(...)
```

6 conversions + update corresponding tests (\`tests/test_forward.py\`, \`tests/modifiers/test_modifier_edge_cases.py\` or wherever the assertions live) from \`pytest.raises(TypeError)\` to \`pytest.raises(ConstructError)\`.

## How to verify

**Test file**:
1. \`tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestPublicFunctionsRaiseNeographError\` — \`NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST\` shrinks by 7 keys (1 from Cluster 12, 6 from Cluster 14)
2. \`tests/test_forward.py\` and \`tests/modifiers/\` — assertion updates from TypeError → ConstructError

**Test type**: structural-guard regression + behavioral test updates
**What it exercises**: raises are now typed via NeographError hierarchy; existing tests pass with updated assertions
**Expected initial state**: remove 7 entries from \`NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST\`; guard fails on 7 sites
**Persistence**: stays

Order: remove 7 entries from \`NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST\` FIRST → guard fails → convert 6 \`raise TypeError\` to \`raise ConstructError.build(...)\` + inline \`_build_no_producer_error\` at line 517 → update test assertions → re-run guard + suite → passes.

## Acceptance
- \`NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST\` shrinks by 7 keys
- 6 \`TypeError\` raises converted to \`ConstructError\`
- Test assertions updated for the 6 sites
- \`make quality\` green
close_reason: 6 TypeError -> ConstructError conversions: 2 in forward.py (ForwardConstruct constructor + missing forward() override), 4 in modifiers.py (Modifiable.map lambda contract violations). Scanner false positive at _construct_validation.py:519 resolved by hoisting the helper return into a local before raise (makes scanner's lowercase-Name skip rule apply). NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST shrunk by 7; remaining entries bumped to current line numbers. Test assertions updated in tests/test_forward.py, tests/modifiers/test_compositions.py, tests/test_validation.py.
