title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.4
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.4` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.4/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.4
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.4 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.4 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.4/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.4 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.4/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-w74k.2.4
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.4`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-w74k.2.4)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.4 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.

## Gate: Add Label

exists:


## Anti-Patterns

  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

  regressed.

title: Refine 2ur4 plan -- address NEEDS_REFINEMENT findings
description:
Refine 2ur4 implementation plan. Use existing research; do NOT re-research.

## Tasks (from architect review)

1. CostCallback Protocol shape: declare modern signature explicitly so mypy can catch arity bugs. Use __call__(self, *, tier: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, node_name: str = ..., mode: str = ..., duration_s: float = ..., **kw: Any) -> None. Legacy 3-arg fallback at _llm.py:77 stays as escape hatch.

2. MergePreProcess return type: change from dict[str, Any] to Any (or dict[str, Any] | BaseModel). Verify invoke_structured input_data annotation accepts both.

3. Move Protocols next to consumers (no _protocols.py module). LlmFactory/PromptCompiler/CostCallback go in _llm.py; merge hooks in modifiers.py; SkipPredicate/SkipValueFactory/RawNodeFn in node.py. Matches Renderer (renderers.py) and LlmConfig (_llm_config.py) precedent.

4. configure_llm() backward-compat: drop keyword-only params from LlmFactory Protocol (use *args, **kwargs catch) so documented 'Simple' form (lambda tier: ...) still satisfies. Rely on existing _accepted_params filtering at call site.

5. Add dedicated test that _validate_skip_callables still runs against Protocol-typed skip_when and rejects zero-arg lambdas.

6. Use typing.get_type_hints(configure_llm) for annotation tests (modules use from __future__ import annotations).

7. Three-surface parity tests must enumerate: (a) @node(skip_when=fn), (b) Node(skip_when=fn), (c) Node() | Oracle(merge_pre_process=fn) -- each compiles + executes one tick.

8. Document runtime_checkable as 'parity with Renderer, only test #8 isinstance is load-bearing.'

## Action

Append updated design to 2ur4 with --append-notes (bd has no --append-design). Verify Core Invariant unchanged.

## Acceptance

Refined plan written; all HIGH/MEDIUM findings addressed; Core Invariant intact.
close_reason: Refinements appended to 2ur4 notes: CostCallback explicit modern shape (catches arity bugs); MergePreProcess returns Any (matches invoke_structured); colocate Protocols with consumers (no _protocols.py); LlmFactory/PromptCompiler use *args/**kwargs catch to preserve documented Simple form; added _validate_skip_callables regression test; three-surface parity enumerated.

title: ARCH-4: migration completions (HIGH-01/02/08/09) — n2li globals + CompiledNeograph + factory shims + free import cycles
description:
## Architectural invariant

Three migrations declared complete in past tickets are made structurally complete:

1. **n2li registry migration** — `decorators.py` carries ZERO module-level mutable dicts. The per-compile `Registry` is the ONLY scripted/condition/tool-factory registration path. `tests/conftest.py:25-29` no longer needs `.clear()` calls between tests (because there's nothing to clear).

2. **CompiledNeograph typed facade** — `compile()` returns `CompiledNeograph` (a frozen dataclass), not LangGraph's `CompiledStateGraph` monkey-patched with 8 `_neo_*` attributes. The runner reads typed fields, not `getattr(graph, "_neo_*", None)`.

3. **Test-shim cleanup** — `factory.py` no longer exposes the ~20 `noqa:F401` test-only re-exports. Tests import from the actual modules.

4. **Import cycle hygiene** — the 3 cycles in `test_guards_sidecar_imports.py` allowlist whose justification comments are factually wrong (re-route through `decorators` for symbols that live in `_sidecar.py:73` / `_di_classify.py:237`) are deleted. Allowlist drops from 21 to 18.

## Source findings

Synthesis `.claude/code-review/020626_2218/synthesis.md`:
- **HIGH-01** — `decorators.py:87-89` keeps 4 import-time globals (`_decorator_scripted`, `_decorator_conditions`, `_decorator_tool_factories`, `_merge_fn_registry`); `conftest.py:25-29` clears them between tests. Smoking gun for incomplete migration.
- **HIGH-02** — `compile() -> Any`; 8 `_neo_*` attributes monkey-patched onto LangGraph object at `compiler.py:236-247`; cluster of `type:ignore` follows.
- **HIGH-08** — `factory.py:13-61` carries ~20 test-only re-export shims (10 `noqa:F401` blocks verified, 0 production consumers).
- **HIGH-09** — 21 cross-layer import cycles in `test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:64` allowlist; 3 illusory (the symbols live in leaf modules `_sidecar.py` / `_di_classify.py` but the allowlist justification names `decorators` as the source).

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (per molecule)

For each of the 4 sub-fixes, document:
1. The original ticket that claimed completion
2. What's actually in the code today
3. The COMPLETION INVARIANT that should have been tested at close time (e.g. "zero module-level mutable dicts in `src/neograph/`")
4. Why the completion invariant test doesn't exist today

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan (per molecule)

Disease pattern: "migration declared complete without a structurally-enforced completion invariant."

Scan:
1. n2li: `grep -nE '^_[a-z_]+: dict\[' src/neograph/*.py | grep -v test_` — should find zero. Today: finds 4.
2. CompiledNeograph: `grep -nE 'setattr\(.+, "_neo_' src/neograph/` — should find zero. Today: finds 8.
3. factory.py shims: `grep -nE '^from neograph\.[a-z_]+ import.+# noqa: F401' src/neograph/factory.py` — should find zero. Today: ~10 blocks.
4. Import cycles: read the allowlist + verify each justification comment by `grep`-ing the named symbol in the named module. The 3 illusory cycles' symbols live elsewhere.

Disposition table per disease.

## Phase 2 — Target design

Per disease:

1. **n2li completion** — Migrate the 4 decorator-side global dicts into the per-compile `Registry` (or attach via `_scripted_shim` PrivateAttr like the @node sidecar pattern). Delete `conftest.py:25-29` `.clear()` block. Structural guard: AST-scan `src/neograph/` for module-level mutable dicts; allowlist with documented reasons OR migrate.

2. **CompiledNeograph wrapper** — Define `class CompiledNeograph(frozen=True)` with typed fields: `graph: CompiledStateGraph`, `state_model`, `schema_fingerprint`, `node_fingerprints`, etc. `compile()` returns it. `runner.py` reads `result.schema_fingerprint` not `getattr(graph, "_neo_schema_fingerprint", None)`. Type-ignore cluster deleted.

3. **factory.py shims** — Walk every `noqa: F401` re-export. Find the 4 test files that import from `factory.py`. Repoint them to the real modules. Delete the shims. Structural guard: AST-scan `src/neograph/factory.py` for `noqa: F401` blocks.

4. **Illusory import cycles** — For each of the 3 cycles, follow the symbol: change the import in the consumer file to point to the leaf module (`_sidecar.py` / `_di_classify.py`). Verify nothing breaks. Remove from allowlist. Allowlist now 21→18.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until:
- All 4 disease scans return zero hits in src/
- `conftest.py` no longer needs `.clear()` between tests
- `compile()` returns `CompiledNeograph`; runner reads typed fields
- factory.py is leaner by ~50 LOC of test-only shims
- Allowlist drops 21→18

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO leaving any of the 4 decorator-side globals "for backward compat" — at 0.x there is no compat to preserve.
- NO accepting the CompiledNeograph wrapper if the runner still has `getattr(graph, "_neo_*", None)` anywhere — that's the migration's whole point.
- NO leaving even one `noqa: F401` shim in factory.py with a "future use" comment.
- NO leaving an illusory cycle in the allowlist with the wrong justification — fix the justification OR remove the entry. Don't lie in the allowlist.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification (per molecule)

Re-run all 4 disease scans. Zero hits in src/. New structural guards added (one per disease) with full meta-test discipline.

## Phase 6 — Independent review (per molecule)

Opus reviewer:
1. Are there OTHER migrations claimed complete that should have completion invariants? (e.g. is there a Q3+Q4+Q6+ epic claim that hides similar gaps?)
2. Does `CompiledNeograph` carry the right fields? Or is it just a renaming?
3. Did the factory.py shim removal break anything subtle that the test suite doesn't cover?

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- HIGH-01, HIGH-02, HIGH-08, HIGH-09 all resolved
- 4 new structural guards pinning completion invariants
- `compile()` returns `CompiledNeograph` (frozen dataclass); zero `_neo_*` `setattr` stashes; type-ignore cluster gone
- `conftest.py` `.clear()` block deleted; module-level mutable dicts in `decorators.py` gone
- factory.py shims deleted; tests repointed
- Allowlist 21→18
- `make quality` green
- Independent reviewer verdict ELEGANT ≥85
notes:
## Findings (research atom up1r.18)

### HIGH-01 — module-level mutable dicts in decorators.py
- decorators.py:87-89 = 3 globals: _decorator_scripted, _decorator_conditions, _decorator_tool_factories. (_merge_fn_registry already MOVED to _sidecar.py:69; _type_registry is spec_types.py:25 — a legit type registry, separate concern.)
- conftest.py:25-29 clears 5 dicts (_merge_fn_registry, _type_registry, _decorator_scripted/conditions/tool_factories).
- _scripted_shim PrivateAttr (node.py:219) ALREADY EXISTS and is the new per-node path: _construct_builder.py:710 attaches it; compiler._collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py:256) walks the construct. compiler.py:127 ALSO merges _decorator_scripted (legacy fallback). node.py:389/_sidecar.py:101 also read the globals.
- Registration call sites: register_scripted (decorators.py:201 inline body-merge, :770 @merge_fn legacy), register_condition (:628 inline interrupt_when -- ATTACHABLE to the node), register_tool_factory (tool.py:145 @tool -- STANDALONE, name-keyed, no node, no compile ctx).
- ARCHITECTURAL REALITY: scripted=already per-node; conditions=attachable per-node (interrupt_when binds to its node); tool_factories via @tool and @merge_fn are STANDALONE module-level decorators registering by name at import -- genuine chicken/egg. Full elimination needs the Tool object to CARRY its factory and nodes to carry Tool instances so compile() collects from the construct (a real redesign), OR an honest allowlist for the standalone case.

### HIGH-02 — compile() -> Any + 8 _neo_* monkey-patches
- compiler.py:235-247: 8 setattr with type:ignore: _neo_required_di, _neo_schema_fingerprint, _neo_node_fingerprints, _neo_construct, _neo_runtime, _neo_scripted, _neo_conditions, _neo_tool_factories.
- runner.py reads all via getattr(graph, '_neo_*', None) at L40/85/167/190/327/330.
- compile() result is consumed ONLY through graph.invoke()/get_state_history()/get_state()/checkpointer (runner.py) + the _neo_ getattr. So a CompiledNeograph(frozen) holding graph + 8 typed fields, delegating LangGraph methods via __getattr__, removes all 8 setattr + 8 type:ignore + 8 getattr. PUBLIC compile() return type changes (piarch consumes develop) -- breaking change (acceptable per project policy, but must update runner + all internal callers + tests that touch g._neo_* or g.invoke()).

### HIGH-08 — factory.py test-only re-export shims
- factory.py:13-60 re-exports ~20 symbols. MIXED: make_node_fn is DEFINED in factory.py (real); compiler.py:42 + _wiring.py:31 + node.py:334 import make_* FROM factory (production, comment L38 'so compiler imports stay stable'). The _dispatch/_execute/_input_shape/_state_write/_state_bus/di re-exports (ScriptedDispatch, _extract_input, _classify_input_shape, _build_state_update, adapt_state, _unwrap_*, etc.) are TEST-ONLY noqa:F401. Fix: repoint test importers to real modules; repoint compiler/_wiring imports of make_* to _oracle; delete test-only shims.

### HIGH-09 — import-cycle allowlist (test_guards_sidecar_imports.py)
- FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST has entries incl. ('_sidecar.py','neograph.decorators',{'_decorator_scripted'}) (L132), ('tool.py','neograph.decorators',{'register_tool_factory'}) (L187). The ticket's 3 illusory cycles: symbols live in _sidecar.py/_di_classify.py but allowlist names decorators as source. Coupled to HIGH-01 (removing globals changes these cycles).

## Risks
- HIGH-01 and HIGH-09 are COUPLED (globals removal reshapes the cycles).
- HIGH-02 is a public-API breaking change (compile() return) reaching piarch.
- HIGH-01 full 'zero module-level dicts' may be infeasible for standalone @tool/@merge_fn without a Tool-carries-factory redesign; honest options: (a) redesign, (b) allowlist-with-true-justification for the standalone case.
## Disposition Table (scan atom up1r.19)

### HIGH-01 (3 module-level dicts in decorators.py:87-89): _decorator_scripted/_decorator_conditions/_decorator_tool_factories. conftest.py:25-29 clears 5. scripted already per-node (_scripted_shim); conditions attachable; @tool/@merge_fn standalone (method -> architect atom). MIGRATE.
### HIGH-02 (8 _neo_* setattr at compiler.py:236-247, all type:ignore; read via getattr in runner.py:40/85/167/190/327/330). MIGRATE -> CompiledNeograph frozen dataclass.
### HIGH-08 (factory.py: 9 noqa:F401 import groups). Test-only re-exports (ScriptedDispatch/_extract_input/_classify_input_shape/_build_state_update/adapt_state/_unwrap_*/etc.) -> repoint tests to real modules + delete. PRODUCTION re-exports of make_* (compiler.py:42, _wiring.py:31/208, node.py:334 import make_node_fn/make_eachoracle_redirect_fn FROM factory) -> repoint to _oracle/keep make_node_fn (defined in factory). MIGRATE.
### HIGH-09 (import-cycle allowlist = 27 entries now, NOT 21; ticket figure stale post-ARCH-1). 3 illusory cycles import get_merge_fn_metadata/_resolve_merge_args FROM neograph.decorators though they live in leaf modules:
  - _construct_validation.py L83-87 (get_merge_fn_metadata) -> _sidecar

title: Public compile_prompt() for eval harnesses + template-source override — byte-identical prompts inside and outside the graph (survey R2/F4)
description:
From docs/design/prompt-surface-consumer-survey-2026-07-08.md (F4, the eval-parity discovery — the highest value-per-line finding). BOTH eval-running consumers rebuild prompts OUTSIDE the graph to eval them: ox-demo duplicates builders in evals/prompts/ (their comment: eval the REAL prompt, not a re-implementation — which is exactly what they end up not doing); piarch's evals hand-roll literal JSON-Schema strings + response_format — a DIFFERENT schema mechanism than its own pipeline, so its evals do not test the prompts production sends (split-brain, provider_classify.py:34-63).

SHIP: a public, documented compile_prompt(...) — promote the existing render_prompt/_compile_prompt inspection path into a first-class function callable STANDALONE (no compiled graph, no run) that produces byte-identical messages to what the graph sends: same renderer, same schema injection, same di_inputs layering, same strictness. Signature sketch: compile_prompt(template, input_data, *, output_model=None, output_schema=None, di_inputs=None, prompt_compiler=None, node_name='') -> list[dict]. Plus a TEMPLATE-SOURCE OVERRIDE (loader/template_text param) so eval harnesses can parameterize prompt VARIANTS (the filename-versioned convention both consumers use) without rebuilding rendering — this is the deliberate scope line from F5: neograph blesses the variant CONVENTION and gives evals the hook; registries/experiments/A-B stay out of scope (ecosystem territory), documented as such. ACCEPTANCE: an eval-side test proving compile_prompt output == the messages a compiled think node sends for the same inputs (the parity property, pinned); docs page 'Evaluating your prompts' with the promptfoo provider recipe. Anti-duplication: MUST be the same code path the graph uses (one compiler brain), not a parallel reimplementation — guard or test pinning the shared seam.

title: Replace modifiers: list[Modifier] with ModifierSet typed slots
description:
Phase 3 of architecture-v2.md section 2 (Type-Safe Modifiers). BREAKING CHANGE.

## What
Replace modifiers: list[Modifier] with ModifierSet typed slots.

## Design
See docs/design/architecture-v2.md section 2 (REVISED).

REVISED from review:
- ModifierSet.model_post_init rejects illegal combos (Each+Loop, Oracle+Loop)
- Every match block MUST end with case _ as unreachable: assert_never(unreachable) — HARD REQUIREMENT
- .map() must produce ModifierSet.with_each(Each(...)): self.model_copy(update={"modifier_set": ...})
- Sidecar invariant: model_copy produces new id(), sidecar must be re-registered on the copy. This is UNCHANGED from current list[Modifier] behavior — document it, dont break it.
- modifiers: list[Modifier] used in compile logging (compiler.py:80) and _BranchNode.has_modifier/get_modifier duck typing (forward.py:358). Both need migration.
- Programmatic API: Node(modifiers=[Oracle(), Each()]) must become pipe syntax. Clear error if someone passes modifiers= list.

## Migration (phased)
Phase 2 bridge: add modifier_set field, keep modifiers as computed property (backward compat)
Phase 3: remove modifiers property, all code uses modifier_set

## Impact
- 56 has_modifier/get_modifier calls → modifier_set.each / modifier_set.oracle
- 210 pipe-syntax tests: unchanged
- 2 check fixtures with modifiers=[...]: update
- Compile logging: log modifier_set.combo instead of modifier list
- _BranchNode: implement has_modifier/get_modifier on ModifierSet (always returns False/None)

## Verification
- All 1076+ tests pass
- assert_never in every match block
- grep -c "has_modifier\|get_modifier" src/neograph/ = 0
- mypy passes with no unhandled ModifierCombo variants
notes:
## Audit findings to incorporate (2026-04-10)

6a. This task needs a step-by-step migration plan:
Step 1: Add modifier_set: ModifierSet field to Modifiable (Node + Construct inherit)
Step 2: Rewrite __or__ to update modifier_set instead of appending to list
Step 3: Add computed property modifiers -> list[Modifier] from modifier_set (backward compat bridge)
Step 4: Rewrite .map() to use modifier_set.with_each()
Step 5: Rewrite has_modifier/get_modifier to delegate to modifier_set
Step 6: Update compiler.py logging (line 85-87) to log modifier_set.combo
Step 7: Update _BranchNode — it has modifiers=[] duck typing (forward.py:354). Either give it a ModifierSet(BARE) or keep a shim.
Step 8: Update 2 check fixtures that use modifiers=[...] syntax
Step 9: Remove computed property bridge (Phase 3 breaking change)

6c. _BranchNode.modifiers = [] is duck-typed. Under ModifierSet, _BranchNode needs modifier_set = ModifierSet() or a has_modifier/get_modifier shim that returns False/None.

2b. Keep _validate_node_chain belt-and-suspenders checks even after ModifierSet.model_post_init. Document as defense-in-depth (catches programmatic bypass of __or__).

title: Checkpoint auto-rewind can silently no-op — resume-from-tip skips invalidated nodes with no warning; per-node fingerprints too coarse (review 080726 PAT-03)
description:
From the 2026-07-08 full-tree review (.claude/code-review/080726_2001/synthesis.md, PAT-03 — VERIFIED by the reviewer; the highest-leverage fix: the durable/if-it-compiles-it-runs pitch is actively false on this path). TWO halves, one ticket:

(1) SILENT NO-OP: when schema fingerprints mismatch and _compute_invalidated_nodes returns a non-empty set, _auto_resume_from_divergence walks get_state_history for a snapshot whose .next intersects the invalidated set — and when NONE matches (runner.py:227-235 region), it no-ops WITHOUT WARNING and resumes from the tip, SKIPPING the changed nodes. A user trusting auto_resume gets stale results with no error. FIX (fail-loud house style): when invalidated is non-empty and no rewind point is found, do NOT silently resume — raise CheckpointSchemaError (with invalidated_nodes and a hint explaining why no rewind point exists: e.g. history pruned, nodes already past) OR at minimum log.warning auto_resume_no_rewind_point + document; the ticket owner decides raise-vs-warn WITH a written rationale, but silent is not an option. Both sync and async twins (the extracted _decide_checkpoint_schema/_auto_resume pair — keep extract-then-thin).

(2) FINGERPRINT COARSENESS compounds it: compute_node_fingerprints hashes only type.__qualname__ (state.py:373) — a field-level change to an output model with the same class name does not invalidate the node, so the rewind never even triggers. The richer annotation string is ALREADY COMPUTED for the schema fingerprint at state.py:415 — fold it into the per-node fingerprint. NOTE the migration consequence: existing checkpoints carry old-format node fingerprints; on first resume after upgrade every node looks changed — decide + document the behavior (probably correct-and-desired: one full re-run after upgrading) and pin it with a test.

TDD: failing repro first for the silent no-op (schema change + a history where no snapshot has the invalidated node in .next); regression for the coarse fingerprint (same class name, changed field type -> must invalidate). Cite the review synthesis. Gates y5ux.
notes:
v63o decisions (executor):

RAISE vs WARN -> RAISE. When auto_resume=True, the schema fingerprint mismatched, invalidated is non-empty, and NO checkpoint in get_state_history has an invalidated node pending in .next, we now raise CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) via a single-sited _raise_no_rewind_point(NoReturn) shared by the sync (_auto_resume_from_divergence) and async (_aauto_resume_from_divergence) twins. Rationale: silently resuming from the tip returns stale results with no signal -- the one spot where the durable/if-it-compiles-it-runs pitch is actively false. A crash at resume-time (BEFORE any stale node body re-executes) with an actionable message (why: history pruned or all invalidated nodes already ran; how to recover: new thread_id or invalidate the checkpoint) is strictly better than silent staleness, and matches the existing auto_resume=False contract that hands the caller invalidated_nodes as a setup signal. Empty invalidated stays a genuine no-op (nothing changed) -- no raise.

FINGERPRINT COARSENESS -> structural signature folded into BOTH fingerprints. New state._type_signature(typ) replaces qualname-only hashing: a Pydantic model now hashes module.Qualname + sorted (field, str(annotation)) pairs (one level, cycle-safe, matching schema-fp depth); generics (list[X]/dict[K,V]/Each's dict[str,X]) are unwrapped so a field change on the wrapped model is visible. CRITICAL: this had to go into compute_schema_fingerprint too, not just compute_node_fingerprints. Verified empirically that str(annotation) on a same-qualname model with a changed field is IDENTICAL, so the schema fingerprint (the GATE: _decide_checkpoint_schema returns None on a match) would never open and the enriched node fingerprint would be dead code. Both now move in lockstep. (Also fixed a latent bug: the dict-form branch hashed type(typ).__name__ = the metaclass name, collapsing all dict-form outputs to the same hash.)

MIGRATION -> correct-and-desired, pinned. Both fingerprint FORMATS change, so existing pre-v63o checkpoints show a schema mismatch on first resume after upgrade -> every node looks changed -> one full re-run. Better than trusting a coarser stale signature. Pinned by test_old_format_node_fingerprint_invalidates_on_upgrade (stores a hand-computed old qualname-only fp and asserts the node is invalidated).

THREE-SURFACE PARITY: fingerprint computation is surface-agnostic -- compute_node_fingerprints/_type_signature walk construct.nodes reading .outputs/.name/.output, identical for @node, declarative, and programmatic. The regression tests use the programmatic Node.scripted surface; the observability contract tests exercise the declarative surface end-to-end through run(). No per-surface branch touched.
close_reason: Fail-loud on no-rewind-point (raises CheckpointSchemaError instead of silent tip-resume); per-node + schema fingerprints now fold structural _type_signature so same-qualname changed-field invalidates; also fixed latent dict-form metaclass-hash bug. TDD, 9 new tests.

title: research: feasibility of typing run() input via Generics on compiled graph
description:
Child of ianf. Investigation-only ticket.

## The opportunity

```
src/neograph/runner.py:214  input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
```

The compiled graph knows its input type at compile() time (from Construct.input or the first Node's inputs annotation). If run() could return `CompiledGraph[InputT, OutputT]`, callers get static-typed input validation and IDE autocomplete:

```python
graph: CompiledGraph[MyInput, MyOutput] = compile(my_construct)
graph.run(input=MyInput(...))  # typed
graph.run(input={...})          # still works via Pydantic coercion
graph.run(input=WrongType(...)) # mypy error
```

## Challenges to research

1. Python Generics on compiled-graph-like objects -- does this compose with LangGraph's StateGraph type? StateGraph is generic on state only, not input/output.
2. Neograph's compile() returns a LangGraph StateGraph, not a neograph wrapper. A `CompiledGraph` wrapper would change the compile() return type (breaking change) OR add a thin generic wrapper class.
3. The input type isn't always a single Pydantic model -- for first-node-dict-form inputs, input is `dict[str, T]`. Typing this cleanly requires TypeVarTuple or similar (PEP 646, 3.11+).
4. Runtime: how does `Graph.run(input=X)` dispatch when X is a Pydantic instance vs a dict? Current code handles both; generics add static checking but the dynamic dispatch stays.

## Research deliverable

A short decision doc (in the bead notes) covering:

- Whether Generics compose cleanly with the current compile() return type
- Whether wrapping LangGraph's StateGraph in a neograph CompiledGraph class is worth the API surface cost
- Estimated effort (hours vs days)
- Whether the value proposition (static typed input) justifies the complexity
- Recommendation: do it, defer, or don't

## Decision gate

If research recommends 'do it', file a new implementation ticket with concrete design. If 'defer' or 'don't', close this ticket with the rationale written to the bead.

## Why P3

High complexity, speculative payoff. The ianf pattern is clear but this instance is harder than the others. Worth investigating but not urgent.

## Dependencies

Child of ianf. Should be tackled LAST among ianf children -- the lessons from pej0, l9qb, 2ur4 inform the right design here.
notes:
## Prep (atom yww4.5)

Read the task. v9qc is a research-only investigation. Deliverable is a decision doc in the bead notes, not code. The execute atom will write the doc; the commit atom is no-op.

Key facts:
- compile() at src/neograph/compiler.py:82 currently returns Any (LangGraph StateGraph instance from .compile())
- run() at src/neograph/runner.py:213 takes input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
- Construct has typed input/output ports (BaseModel | None) via construct.input / construct.output
- LangGraph StateGraph is generic on state only, not input/output

No production code changes -- the execute atom writes the decision doc.
## Decision (atom yww4.6) -- typing run() input via Generics

### Investigation summary

**Current state**:
- `compile(construct: Construct, ...) -> Any` (src/neograph/compiler.py:82) returns the LangGraph CompiledStateGraph; type-erased to Any.
- `run(graph: Any, input: dict[str, Any] | None, ...) -> Any` (src/neograph/runner.py:213) takes untyped input.
- `Construct` knows its input port: `input: type[BaseModel] | None` (construct.py:84).
- `Node.inputs: TypeSpec` is `None | type | dict[str, type]` (node.py:127).
- LangGraph's StateGraph is generic on the state schema, not on input/output. Subgraph compilation accepts an input_schema, but neograph's compile() does not surface it.

**Goal**: `compile(my_construct) -> CompiledGraph[InputT, OutputT]` so callers get static-checked `graph.run(input=MyInput(...))` and IDE autocomplete.

**Challenges**:

1. **Generics composition with the LangGraph return**. neograph's compile() returns a StateGraph instance directly. Adding Generics requires either:
   a. Wrapping the StateGraph in a neograph `CompiledGraph[I, O]` class with a `.invoke()`/`.run()` shim. Adds a wrapper and changes the return type contract for every existing caller.
   b. Returning the StateGraph itself but cast as `CompiledGraph[I, O]`. Preserves return-type backward compat but requires LangGraph to gain Generics it doesn't have.

2. **First-node-dict-form inputs**. When `Construct.input is None` AND the first Node has dict-form inputs (e.g., `inputs={"a": A, "b": B}`), the input type is naturally a TypedDict / dict[str, Any]. Typing this cleanly requires PEP 646 TypeVarTuple (3.11+) or fanned generics; the static surface gets ugly fast.

3. **Runtime dispatch invariance**. Today `run(graph, input=X)` accepts both Pydantic instances and dicts (Pydantic coerces at the entry boundary). Generics add static type-checking but don't change dynamic dispatch. The wrapper class would still need both code paths.

4. **piarch downstream**. piarch is the sole consumer. They build runtime-assembled pipelines (LLM-driven, JSON-spec) where the input type is dynamic at construct time. A static `CompiledGraph[InputT, OutputT]` doesn't help runtime-assembled pipelines because InputT isn't known statically there.

### Effort estimate

- **Wrapper approach (Option a)**: ~1 week. Define `CompiledGraph(Generic[InputT, OutputT])` wrapping LangGraph's CompiledStateGraph; change compile() return type; update run()/runner.py to take the wrapper; thread types through 19 examples + ~50 tests. Mostly mechanical but high blast radius. Three-surface parity tests + runtime dispatch retests required.

- **Cast approach (Option b)**: ~2 days. Just type-narrow at compile() return. But mypy's structural-checking won't follow the cast unless LangGraph types align; in practice this becomes "use TypeVar bound to BaseModel and rely on cast". Marginal gain vs effort.

### Value proposition

- **Static typed input** at the `run()` call site: caller writes `graph.run(input=MyInput(...))` and mypy verifies. Wrong type fails type-check.
- **IDE autocomplete** on the input parameter inside .run().
- **Documentation surface**: hover shows `CompiledGraph[Claims, Report]`.

But:
- piarch's runtime-assembled pipelines don't benefit (input type is dynamic at construct time).
- @node-driven pipelines already get input-type checking via the parameter annotation on the first node. The static-input gain is ONLY at the boundary `run(input=...)` call -- one site per user app.
- Pydantic coercion already turns `dict` input into `BaseModel` at the entry boundary, so wrong-type errors surface as ValidationError at run time. The gain is "1 second earlier feedback in IDE" vs "ValidationError on first run".

### Recommendation: **DEFER**

The complexity-to-benefit ratio is poor. The static-typed input gain materializes at exactly one site per user app (the run() call); the rest of the type story (node parameter annotations, Construct.input, dict-form fan-in) already has good ergonomics through @node decoration.

Concrete reasons:

1. **piarch (sole consumer) doesn't benefit**. Their LLM-driven runtime assembly path constructs pipelines where InputT is unknown statically.
2. **Pydantic coercion already provides wrong-type detection** at run time. mypy's earlier-feedback is a real gain but small.
3. **Effort is 1 week with high blast radius** (compile() return type change, runner.py changes, 19 examples, ~50 tests, three-surface parity validation). At 0.x with one downstream user, this is an expensive cosmetic upgrade.
4. **PEP 646 / TypeVarTuple territory** for dict-form first-node inputs adds non-trivial complexity to the Generics that doesn't fully resolve cleanly.
5. **The other ianf-children (pej0, l9qb, 2ur4, bha9) closed real bug classes**. v9qc closes nothing -- it's a static-checking ergonomic win.

### Conditions to re-open

This task should be re-opened (or its sibling implementation ticket filed) when:

- A second downstream consumer with statically-known input types appears.
- The neograph project ships its own `CompiledGraph` wrapper for unrelated reasons (e.g., a method like `graph.describe_input_schema()` that needs a typed surface).
- Python adds first-class TypeVarTuple support in a way that handles dict-form inputs cleanly without ergonomic ugliness.
- piarch shifts to a static-input-typed pipeline pattern.

### Disposition

Close v9qc as DEFERRED with this decision doc. Do not file an implementation ticket. The work is well-understood and can be re-evaluated when the conditions above change.
close_reason: DEFERRED. Audit + decision doc written in notes. Generics on compile()/run() carry high implementation cost (1 week, broad blast radius across compile/runner/examples/tests) for a thin gain (static typing at one boundary site per user app). piarch (sole downstream) doesn't benefit -- their LLM-driven runtime assembly has dynamic input types. Pydantic coercion already detects wrong-type input at run() boundary. PEP 646 TypeVarTuple for dict-form first-node inputs adds non-trivial complexity. Re-open if (a) a second downstream consumer with statically-known input types appears, (b) neograph ships a CompiledGraph wrapper for unrelated reasons, (c) piarch shifts to static-input pipelines. Per task description: 'If defer or don't, close this ticket with the rationale written to the bead.'

title: Normalize fan_out_param across all three API surfaces (remove runtime heuristic)
description: P1. CLAUDE.md claims all three surfaces produce identical IR; today @node sets node.fan_out_param but YAML/programmatic don't, forcing a runtime heuristic in _extract_fan_in_dict (added in zf8v commit 02181d3) that scans state.keys() to detect the fan-out key. Two consequences: (1) IR-parity claim is false; (2) duplicate detection logic with validator's _check_fan_in_inputs (same anti-pattern that caused neograph-8k3 / neograph-ayq). Fix: write fan_out_param back during validation OR at Construct __init__, then drop the runtime heuristic from _extract_fan_in_dict. Acceptance: structural guard test forbids the heuristic; node.fan_out_param has identical value across @node/YAML/programmatic for the same logical construct; existing tests pass.
design:
## Root Cause
fan_out_param is set as a side effect of @node decoration assembly in _construct_builder._build_construct_from_decorated:565 (`updates['fan_out_param'] = next(iter(skip))`). The YAML loader (loader.py:_apply_modifiers) and programmatic Node()|Each() (via Modifiable.__or__) never invoke this logic, so the IR Node has fan_out_param=None for those two surfaces.

The validator's _check_fan_in_inputs already detects fan-out keys at validation time (line 593: 'has_each and not _each_skip_used') — but only as a transient skip, never written back to node.fan_out_param.

## Fix Approach
Move fan-out detection to a Construct __init__ / post-validation pass so it runs ONCE for all three surfaces and writes node.fan_out_param. The validator becomes the single source of truth. The runtime band-aid in _extract_fan_in_dict (added in zf8v) gets removed.

Concrete steps:
1. In _construct_validation.py _check_fan_in_inputs: when has_each + unmatched key triggers the skip branch, set item.fan_out_param = upstream_name (idempotent: only if currently None).
2. Remove the runtime heuristic from _input_shape._extract_fan_in_dict.
3. Add a structural guard test forbidding state.keys()-based fan-out detection in _input_shape.py.

Core Invariant: 'all three API surfaces (declarative, @node, programmatic/YAML) produce identical Node IR after Construct construction.'
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/hypothesis/test_regression.py::TestFanOutParamIRParity (2 tests)
- Confirmed: YAML and programmatic Each surfaces both produce fan_out_param=None on the IR Node; only the @node path sets it via _construct_builder
- Root cause: fan_out_param assignment lives ONLY in _construct_builder._build_construct_from_decorated (the @node assembly path); loader.py and Construct.__init__ never invoke equivalent logic
## Trace
Scanned for the same anti-pattern (IR field set by one surface's assembly path only):
- node.fan_out_param: confirmed only @node sets it; fixed via Construct._normalize_fan_out_params
- node.scripted_fn: set by @node assembly only — but YAML uses string registration via scripted_fn= field on the spec directly. Verified by inspection: YAML loader sets it on spec parse. No drift.
- node.oracle_gen_type: set by Oracle modifier merge; programmatic + YAML go through same modifiers.py path. No drift.
- node.context: user-declared field, same across all surfaces. No drift.
No additional tickets to file.
## Architect Review
1. **Root cause correctness**: LOW risk. 2 GREEN regression tests confirm both YAML and programmatic surfaces now produce fan_out_param='item' on the IR Node.
2. **Fix minimality**: LOW. ~22-line normalization method + invocation + removed 11-line runtime band-aid + 1 structural guard. Net +33-15.
3. **Regression risk**: LOW. _normalize_fan_out_params is idempotent (only writes when fan_out_param is None). The @node decoration path runs _construct_builder post-Construct.__init__ which still sets fan_out_param via existing logic — both paths converge on the same value (verified by all 1891 tests passing including @node Each cases in tests/decorator/test_edge_cases.py).
4. **Architecture compliance**: LOW. Restores the three-surface IR-parity contract claimed in CLAUDE.md. Construct.__init__ is now the single source of truth; runtime extractor is dumb. Structural guard locks the contract.
5. **Similar bug scalability**: LOW. Traced 3 candidate fields (scripted_fn, oracle_gen_type, context) — none have the surface-divergence issue.
6. **Test coverage**: LOW. 2 IR-parity tests + 1 structural guard + behavior covered by existing TestEachKeyParityAcrossSurfaces (which was the originally-failing test).

ALL_LOW — implementation already complete.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for d5pvl
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show d5pvl` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/d5pvl/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" d5pvl
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (d5pvl)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/d5pvl/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add d5pvl codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/d5pvl/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for d5pvl
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on d5pvl
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" d5pvl`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (d5pvl)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add d5pvl sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Silent bug: multiple port params overwrite — should raise ConstructError
description:
In _build_construct_from_decorated (decorators.py:1078-1083), when a node has multiple params whose type matches construct_input, the dict rewrite loop executes filtered['neo_subgraph_input'] = v for each port param. The last one wins, earlier values are silently dropped.

Example:
  @node(outputs=Result)
  def bad(a: VerifyClaim, b: VerifyClaim) -> Result: ...

  construct_from_functions('x', [bad], input=VerifyClaim, output=Result)

Both 'a' and 'b' match construct_input. The rewrite writes neo_subgraph_input twice. Only the last param's type is kept. No error, no warning.

Fix: in the port_params identification loop (lines 917-935), if len(ports) > 1 for any node, raise ConstructError explaining the ambiguity. Add a test in TestNodeSubConstruct.

Also needs tests for:
- No matching param: construct_input set but no node param matches (silent no-op, should it warn?)
- Peer-priority edge case: param name matches both a peer @node AND construct_input type (code correctly prefers peer at line 927-928, but no test verifies)

File: src/neograph/decorators.py lines 917-935
Test: tests/test_composition.py
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test: tests/test_composition.py::TestPortParamErrors::test_raises_when_multiple_params_match_construct_input
- Status: FAILING (confirmed bug — DID NOT RAISE ConstructError)
- Two params of type VerifyClaim in one @node, construct_from_functions(input=VerifyClaim) silently accepts both, last one wins in the rewrite
- Peer priority test passes (line 928 'if pname in decorated: continue' works correctly)
## Trace Similar
- The port_params identification loop (decorators.py:920-935) is the only place where construct_input matching happens
- No similar pattern elsewhere in the codebase (fan_out_params identification at L921-933 has a different structure — it collects per-node, not per-type)
- The fix is localized: add a len(ports) > 1 check after the inner loop, raise ConstructError
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Fix location correct: decorators.py lines 934-935, after ports set is built, before storing in port_params dict
- [LOW] Error message should include the node name, the matching param names, and the construct_input type
- [LOW] Peer-priority edge case already handled correctly (line 928)

Overall: ALL_LOW

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for do0d9
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show do0d9` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/do0d9/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" do0d9
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (do0d9)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update do0d9 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update do0d9 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/do0d9/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add do0d9 codebase-scan:complete
```

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Refine nnds9 per review
description:
Resolve the 4 MEDIUM findings from the architect review (neograph-vihe7.12) recorded in nnds9's notes before write-test/implement proceed:

1. The static mesh-entry edge 'prev -> entry.name' (_wiring.py:783-786) must ALSO resolve through the entry-label map when the ENTRY member is agent/act (its real node is {entry}__agent). Step 4 of the plan only names the entry-label map for OTHER members' destinations=/goto= targets, never the static entry edge. Update the design to explicitly state the static entry edge resolves through the entry-label map too, and add a fixture/runtime test where the ENTRY member itself is agent/act (not just a peer) -- the existing planned fixture (scripted entry + agent peer) structurally dodges this case.

The actual pin is tests/test_portal_validation.py:249 test_agent_member_rejected (a unit test, not a check-fixture). Retarget step 7 at that real test (invert to assert-passes or delete). Also note tests/test_portal_addressability_doc.py:102 asserts the literal string 'D-MEMBER-MODES' remains in the doc -- step 8's doc update must keep that string when marking the decision resolved.

3. Recursion-floor step 6 flags but doesn't specify a formula. Pin the concrete floor calculation: an agent/act mesh member re-entered K times via mesh hops costs up to K*(max_iters*2+overhead) supersteps, not just K hop-supersteps -- update the design to state the floor must multiply an agent/act mesh member's per-cycle cost by that mesh's max_hops, so the implementer has a concrete formula and the checkpoint test can assert it.

4. Step 3 hedges on copying _add_agent_cycle wholesale ('refactor later if near-total duplication') -- it IS near-total duplication (only the parse node's registration + return diverge). Commit up front in the design to ONE shared internal wiring helper parametrized by (parse-body builder, destinations=) called by BOTH _add_agent_cycle and the new mesh path, rather than deferring the reuse decision.

Also reconcile the LOW finding: the Findings section says the entry-label map should be a graph-wide artifact while plan step 4 mandates mesh-local scope (deferred to do0d9) -- these are not contradictory in intent (mesh-local now, code-comment pointer to future graph-wide generalization) but the wording should be reconciled so it doesn't read as internally inconsistent.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for i3zsh
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show i3zsh` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/i3zsh/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" i3zsh
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (i3zsh)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update i3zsh --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update i3zsh --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/i3zsh/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add i3zsh codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/i3zsh/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.
close_reason: Disease scan complete: 0 instances of hand-rolled Agent Spec type walker found outside spec_types.py; codebase-scan:complete label added to i3zsh

title: Sweep verification for i3zsh
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on i3zsh
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" i3zsh`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (i3zsh)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update i3zsh --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add i3zsh sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.
