title: invoke_with_tools: DSML trailing-tool-call response crashes structured-output extraction when tool budget exhausted
description:
## What

After tool budget exhaustion in `invoke_with_tools`, NeoGraph asks the model for a final structured-output response (ExplorationResult, etc.). DeepSeek R1 (deepseek-reasoner via api.deepseek.com direct API) sometimes emits another round of native DSML tool-call markup in content instead of producing the JSON envelope:

```
<｜DSML｜tool_calls>
<｜DSML｜invoke name="search_nodes">
<｜DSML｜parameter name="query" string="true">coding agent BDD feature file improve input</｜DSML｜parameter>
</｜DSML｜invoke>
<｜DSML｜invoke name="search_nodes">
...
```

`_parse_json_response` correctly detects the XML-markup pattern and raises ExecutionError (line 501 of `_llm.py` — the existing safety net for "non-JSON after budget exhaustion" hint). The raise is caught nowhere in `invoke_with_tools` → the whole pipeline crashes.

## Why it matters + why we are just seeing it now

Before 2026-04-23 the GENERATOR role routed through OpenRouter which silently converted DSML-in-content to empty `tool_calls[]`. That caused a different bug (piarch-rkyd9.15: zero-tool-call silent 'new' verdicts) but ALSO masked this one — when the model wanted to keep calling tools, OpenRouter just ate the intent and the tool loop terminated with empty results.

Switching GENERATOR to DeepSeek direct (piarch-rkyd9.15 fix) now preserves the native DSML tokens, so the tool loop runs correctly for 39/40 explore calls but reveals this trailing-DSML edge case on the 40th. Visible now, invisible before.

## Evidence

- Rehearsal /Users/konst/projects/piarch-rehearse-rw/.derive-ensemble/rehearsals/rw-deepseek-direct
- Crash traceback at explore id `0b9aa4a6-2962-6840-587d-81fea5bdda28`, verify-claim `d609366f-7e7c-5b80-404f-e0971acf0c8b`
- Stack: `invoke_with_tools (_llm.py:1080) → _invoke_json_with_retry (_llm.py:644) → _parse_json_response (_llm.py:501)`
- 39 prior explore calls completed cleanly with OpenAI-compat tool_calls[] on the same run — the bug is tail-case only.

## Expectations after delivery

Two layers of remediation, both needed:

### Layer C (primary — single-pass fix)
When `_parse_json_response` raises "non-JSON content" with XML tool-call pattern detected, `_invoke_json_with_retry` should retry ONCE with a stronger directive in the retry message:

"Your previous response contained tool-call markup in content. The tool budget is exhausted — do NOT invoke any more tools. Respond with ONLY the JSON envelope for {model_name}. No DSML, no tool_calls, no XML. Output exactly the JSON object."

This targets the specific failure mode: model wanted another tool call, doesn't realize budget is over. A clear directive usually suffices for well-aligned models.

### Layer B (fallback — budget + DSML coercion)
If the retry in C fails too, coerce the DSML tool-call markup into a "give up, synthesize partial ExplorationResult from what we already have" path:

- Extract the model's accumulated tool_log (already available in the closure)
- Build a minimal ExplorationResult(summary="budget exhausted; tool loop terminated with partial research", candidate_node_ids=[from prior tool results])
- Log a warning; don't crash

This prevents full-pipeline aborts on a single misbehaving explorer. The score node downstream still gets a usable (if degraded) research packet.

### Bonus: budget visibility
Model emits DSML trailing tool-calls BECAUSE it thinks more tools are available. `_invoke_with_tools` could inject a system-level budget-remaining counter into each tool round's context ("you have N tool calls remaining; after that, produce the final JSON envelope"). Would reduce the frequency of this edge case upstream.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: tests/modes/test_invoke_with_tools_trailing_dsml.py — canned chat model that returns N successful tool calls then a final response with `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` markup in content. Assert:
  - Layer C: retry fires, model's next response is accepted as the final JSON.
  - Layer B: if retry also fails, invoke_with_tools returns ExplorationResult synthesized from tool_log, logs warning, does NOT raise.

**E2E**: rerun rw-process on BR-RW-035 through real DeepSeek direct. Assert run completes without ExecutionError raising from `_parse_json_response` trailing-DSML detection.

## Acceptance

- Layer C retry lands in `_invoke_json_with_retry` (or a new DSML-specific variant called from `invoke_with_tools`)
- Layer B fallback synthesizes partial result + logs warning
- Unit/integration test covers both paths
- piarch rehearsal on BR-RW-035 survives DSML trailing-tool-call tail case
notes:
## Analysis
File neograph/_llm.py is 1204 lines with four distinct concerns. Tool loop (~350 lines) extracted to _tool_loop.py before fixing the bug.

## Fix plan (in _tool_loop.py)
Layer C: DSML-aware retry with generic message ("Produce the final response")
Layer B: fallback — synthesize partial result from tool_interactions
Bonus: configurable budget-exhaustion message via llm_config["budget_exhausted_message"]
close_reason: Fixed: DSML trailing tool-call markup recovered via targeted retry + configurable budget message

title: lint: inspect actual template text for {placeholder} names and validate against rendered input keys

resolution) but never reads the actual template .txt files to extract

check but crash at runtime with KeyError.

This is the THIRD placeholder/data mismatch caught by runtime crash rather
than by neograph check in a single day:
1. {load_uc_composite} vs neo_subgraph_input (sub-construct remapping)
2. {research_packet} vs explore_internal_tool_log (bridge alias)
3. {existing_si} — field inside a rendered BAML blob, not a top-level key

All three passed neograph check. All three crashed after minutes of LLM
spend.

## Why

The lint operates on the construct graph (nodes, edges, DI bindings) but
never touches the template files that prompt_compiler will call
get_prompt() with. Template text is opaque to the linter. The
--known-vars mechanism is a consumer-side allowlist, not a verification.

With BAML rendering (neograph-qybn), models arrive as opaque strings keyed
by parameter name. Field-level placeholders ({existing_si}, {title},
{uc_id}) that worked when the bridge hand-flattened models are now
unresolvable. The lint must know about this.

## Direction

Extend lint to:

1. For each LLM-calling node, resolve the template file (node.prompt →
   prompt registry path). Read the template text. Extract all {placeholder}
   names via regex.
2. Compute the set of keys that will be available at runtime:
   - Fan-in parameter names (from node inputs)
   - Sub-construct remapped keys (neo_subgraph_input)
   - Standard vars (node_id, project_root, json_schema)
   - Context keys
   - known-vars from CLI
3. Diff: placeholders - available_keys = unresolvable. Report each as
   a lint ERROR.

This requires the linter to have access to the template registry (or
the template files on disk). The prompt_compiler is consumer-provided,
but template files are referenced by node.prompt and the consumer's
registry is loaded at check time via --setup.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: construct with a node whose template references
{field_inside_model}. Lint returns ERROR for that placeholder.

**Integration**: construct with a node whose template references only
valid parameter names. Lint returns no errors.

**E2E**: run neograph check on piarch's uc_derivation.py. Currently
write-si.txt has {existing_si} which is NOT a parameter name.
Lint must flag it.

## Acceptance

- Lint reads template text for every LLM-calling node
- Extracts {placeholder} names from template
- Compares against computed available keys
- Reports unresolvable placeholders as ERROR
- Catches all three classes of mismatch found today
design:
## Architecture

### lint() API change
```python
def lint(
    construct: Construct,
    *,
    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    known_template_vars: set[str] | None = None,
    template_resolver: Callable[[str], str | None] | None = None,
) -> list[LintIssue]:
```

### _check_template_placeholders changes
Currently handles inline prompts only. Extended:
- If prompt is inline: existing ${var} validation (unchanged)
- If prompt is template-ref AND template_resolver provided:
  1. text = template_resolver(node.prompt)
  2. If text is None: skip (resolver cant find template)
  3. Extract {placeholder} via string.Formatter().parse()
  4. Validate first segment of each against predicted_keys + known_vars
  5. Same issue kinds: template_placeholder_unresolvable (ERROR), template_placeholder_known_vars_only (WARN)

### __main__.py changes
In _load_config or new _load_template_resolver:
- If --setup module exports get_template_resolver(), use it
- Pass to lint(template_resolver=...)

### New issue kind
template_placeholder_unresolvable already exists. Reuse it for template-ref placeholders too.

Risk: LOW. Existing behavior unchanged when no resolver provided.
notes:
## Research

Core invariant: lint must validate template-ref prompt placeholders against runtime input keys when a template_resolver is provided.

### Design
1. lint() gains template_resolver: Callable[[str], str | None] parameter
2. For template-ref prompts (not inline), if resolver provided:
   a. Call resolver(node.prompt) to get template text
   b. Extract {placeholder} names via string.Formatter().parse()
   c. Validate each against predicted input keys + known extras + known_vars
3. __main__.py --setup module can export get_template_resolver() -> Callable
4. Template-ref uses Python str.format {placeholder} syntax, NOT ${var}

### Placeholder extraction
Use string.Formatter().parse(template) which yields (literal, field_name, format_spec, conversion) tuples. field_name is the placeholder name (may be dotted like "claim.text"). Take first segment.

### What counts as available keys for template-ref prompts
Same as inline prompts:
- Predicted input keys (from node.inputs dict)
- Framework extras (node_id, project_root, human_feedback)
- known_template_vars
- PLUS: config keys if config provided (prompt_compiler can access config)
- PLUS: node_name, output_model, etc. (prompt_compiler kwargs)

Actually, we should focus on input_data keys + known_vars. The prompt_compiler can access config separately — thats not part of template_vars. The consumer patterns show template.format(**data) where data = input_data dict.
close_reason: lint reads template text via template_resolver, extracts {placeholder} names, validates against input keys. Catches field-inside-model, sub-construct remapping, and bridge alias bugs.

title: Branch-arm bare Nodes skip validation, IR-normalization, lint, and verify walks
description:
Adjacent to neograph-tdbb (which scopes to scripted-shim/DI/fingerprint collection via iter_nodes). The disease-scan for tdbb found the SAME _BranchNode-blind-spot in FIVE more hand-rolled construct.nodes walks that do NOT go through iter_nodes, so the tdbb iter_nodes fix does not reach them:

1. _construct_validation.py:128 (_validate_node_chain producer registration) — bare arm Nodes (forward.py true_only/false_only are bare Node objects) are never producer-registered or type-validated at the parent level. Sub-constructs in arms self-validate at their own Construct.__init__; bare arm Nodes do not.
2. _ir_normalize.py:226 — 'if not isinstance(item, Node): continue' skips _BranchNode, so oracle_gen_type / fan_out_param normalization never runs for arm nodes. An Each/Oracle @node placed directly in a branch arm would miss IR normalization.
3. lint.py:214 (_walk) — _BranchNode falls through the 'if not isinstance(item, Node): return' guard, so DI-binding + template-placeholder lint never inspects arm nodes.
4. verify.py:90/163 (_walk + _has_llm_nodes) — arm nodes skipped by the verify tree-walk.
5. runner.py:206 (adjacency builder) — arm nodes contribute no edges to the adjacency map.

Root cause is identical to tdbb: _BranchNode sentinels carry _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes that every non-arm-aware tree walk ignores. Scope decision needed: after tdbb makes iter_nodes descend, migrate these five walks to route through iter_nodes (uniform), OR give each its own arm descent. Anti-band-aid: prefer routing through the single iter_nodes source of truth. Note the DEDUP opportunity: state.py compile_state_model (state.py:102/126-241) already hand-rolls a CORRECT arm walk; once iter_nodes descends, that manual walk can likely be retired too.

Blocked-by: neograph-tdbb (land the iter_nodes descent first, then migrate these consumers).
design:
## Root Cause
Five (documented) + six (scan-found) hand-rolled construct.nodes tree walks visit only top-level items and short-circuit on _BranchNode via isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guards (or, at __main__.py:166, a hasattr('modifiers') guard the empty-ModifierSet sentinel passes but classify_modifiers finds nothing in). Arm contents (_BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes) are reachable only via _neo_branch_meta, so they are invisible to: _construct_validation.py:128, _ir_normalize.py:226, lint.py:214, verify.py:90/163, runner.py:206, compiler.py:146/162/183, construct.py:170, __main__.py:165, _subconstruct.py:118. _wiring.py recursively _compile()s arm CONSTRUCTS (self-validating) but bare arm NODES go straight to make_node_fn, bypassing all compile-time guards.

## Fix Design (REFINED post-architect-review — VERDICT was NEEDS_REFINEMENT, 4 findings folded in)

### Primitives — home is _ir_branch.py (NOT construct.py) [FINDING 1, HIGH]
construct.py imports _validate_node_chain and normalize_ir from modules BELOW it; those modules would circular-import if they pulled the primitive from construct.py. _ir_branch.py already owns _BranchNode/_BranchMeta, is the neutral low-level IR home, and needs only item.nodes + _BranchNode + _neo_branch_meta.
- iter_with_arms(construct) -> Iterator[Node | Construct]: yield each item in construct.nodes; for each _BranchNode yield its arm items (true then false) IN PLACE OF the sentinel. ONE-LEVEL expansion — do NOT recurse into sub-constructs (arm Constructs yielded opaque so each caller's existing isinstance(item,Construct) recursion / _wiring recursive _compile handles them; recursing here would double-process).
- iter_item_slots(construct) -> Iterator[tuple[MutableSequence, int]]: yield (container_list, index) for every item slot incl. arm meta-list slots, so model_copy write-back targets the correct slot (top-level construct.nodes[i] OR meta.true_arm_nodes[j]/false_arm_nodes[j]).

### Read-only migrations (for item in construct.nodes -> iter_with_arms): sites 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,11.
### Write-back migrations (via iter_item_slots): site 2 (_ir_normalize) and site 9 (construct.py:170 llm_config/renderer inheritance).

### Known-limitation decisions [FINDINGS 2 & 3, MEDIUM]
- Site 1: registering conditional arm outputs as parent-scope producers is INTENDED (matches the state fields compile_state_model actually creates). Cross-arm leakage (false-arm node reading true-arm output) is NOT caught — not a regression (uncaught today); document in code comment + a pin test.
- Site 2: normalize_ir peer_field_names stays top-level-only for this fix; an arm Each reading an arm-SIBLING producer would misinfer fan_out_param. Document as a code-comment limitation (extending the peer set to arm producers is out of scope; no consumer needs it yet).

### state.py: LEAVE AS-IS + ALLOWLIST in the structural guard. Retiring its two arm walks needs re-expressing per-arm classify_modifiers (LOOP/ORACLE combos, loop-count fields) — file a separate low-priority follow-up, do NOT bundle.

### Test plan [FINDING 4, MEDIUM] — all RED before impl
- Keep the 5 existing RED tests (sites 1-5, true arm).
- Add RED per new site: 6 (bare arm Operator string cond unregistered -> ConfigurationError at compile), 7 (bare arm Operator + checkpointer=None -> CompileError 'requires a checkpointer' at COMPILE — highest-value), 8 (bare arm agent/act tool w/o factory -> CompileError at compile), 9 (bare arm LLM node inherits parent llm_config/renderer), 10 (CLI check auto-MemorySaver for arm Operator), 11 (sub-construct arm context node forwarded, not None).
- Add: idempotence (list(iter_with_arms(c)) == c.nodes when no _BranchNode); write-back-slot targeting (model_copy lands in meta.true_arm_nodes[j] AND meta.false_arm_nodes[j]); false-arm parity (extend _branch_parent to support false-arm placement — RED tests currently hardcode false_arm_nodes=[]); cross-arm-leakage limitation pin test.
- Structural guard (sweep-verify): every .nodes walk in src outside an allowlist must route through iter_nodes/iter_with_arms/iter_item_slots or be provably arm-aware. Model on tdbb TestIterNodesCoversBranchArms (behavioral pos/neg meta-test, NOT regex). Allowlist: state.py (documented), compiler.py:139 logging, loader.py spec-walks, testing.py codegen (neograph-gfoq), the primitives themselves, compiler.py:208 graph dispatch, iter_nodes.

### Core Invariant
Every walk over a Construct's node list that must observe conditionally-executed nodes routes through the single arm-descent primitive (iter_with_arms / iter_item_slots) or iter_nodes — no hand-rolled isinstance(item, Node/Construct) walk may silently skip _BranchNode arm contents.

## Triage (neograph-ala4.6): NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> refined inline (architect path was determinate, no user decision needed). Design above is the authoritative implementation plan for the fix atom.
notes:
## Reproduction (neograph-ala4.2)
- Failing test: tests/test_branch_arm_noniter_walks.py (5 tests, all RED)
  1. test_arm_node_input_type_mismatch_is_caught_at_assembly -- validation (_validate_node_chain): DID NOT RAISE on arm-node input type mismatch
  2. test_arm_each_node_gets_fan_out_param_normalized -- normalize_ir: arm Each node fan_out_param stays None (expected 'group')
  3. test_arm_node_di_binding_gap_is_linted -- lint._walk: arm FromInput binding never linted (0 issues)
  4. test_llm_node_in_arm_is_seen_by_has_llm_nodes -- verify._has_llm_nodes: returns False for arm-only LLM node
  5. test_arm_node_contributes_edge_to_adjacency -- runner adjacency: arm consumer contributes no seed->gate edge
- Root cause: Five hand-rolled construct.nodes walks short-circuit on _BranchNode sentinels because their isinstance(item, Node/Construct) guards do not recognize the branch sentinel, so nodes inside _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes are never visited. Identical root cause to neograph-tdbb (which fixed only the iter_nodes SoT walk).
## Trace-similar (neograph-ala4.3)
Bug pattern category: hand-rolled 'for item in construct.nodes' walk with an isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guard that short-circuits on _BranchNode, so bare arm Nodes (true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes) are skipped. Confirmed mechanism: _wiring.py:_add_branch_to_graph lowers arm CONSTRUCTS through a recursive _compile() (self-validating), but bare arm NODES go straight to make_node_fn -- bypassing every compile-time guard.

### Documented 5 (in ticket scope)
1. _construct_validation.py:128, 2. _ir_normalize.py:226, 3. lint.py:214, 4. verify.py:90/163, 5. runner.py:206. All reproduced RED in tests/test_branch_arm_noniter_walks.py.

### NEWLY FOUND same-pattern instances (NOT in original ticket scope)
6. compiler.py:146 -- Operator string-condition registration check (isinstance(item,(Node,Construct)) skips _BranchNode). A bare arm Node with Operator(when='unregistered-str') is never checked -> ConfigurationError not raised at compile.
7. compiler.py:161 -- has_operator checkpointer-requirement scan (top-level only). A bare arm Operator node -> has_operator False -> 'Operator requires a checkpointer' guard skipped -> runtime failure.
8. compiler.py:183 -- tool-factory registration check (top-level only). A bare arm agent/act Node with tools -> factory presence never validated -> runtime KeyError.
9. __main__.py:163 -- CLI 'neograph check' auto-MemorySaver supply, same has_operator top-level scan. Arm Operator -> no checkpointer auto-supplied -> false-negative check failure.
10. _subconstruct.py:118 -- runtime context-forwarding walk (for n in sub.nodes) within a sub-construct; a context node inside a branch arm of that sub-construct gets its context field forwarded as None.

### Recommendation
6-8 are the SAME compile-time-validation family as documented site 1 and share the identical arm-descent fix; strongly prefer folding them into this fix (anti-band-aid: one arm-descent primitive, all consumers). 9-10 are adjacent runtime/CLI instances -- architect atom (ala4.5) to decide fold-vs-file. Note: state.py (compile_state_model, compute_node_fingerprints) and compiler.py graph-build loop (208) and iter_nodes are ALREADY arm-aware -- they are the gold standard to mirror.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-ala4.4)

Pattern: a walk over a Construct's node list (`for _ in construct.nodes` / `.nodes`) whose isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guard short-circuits on _BranchNode, so bare arm Nodes in _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes are never visited.
Classification: SYNTACTIC/structural -- arm contents are reachable ONLY via _neo_branch_meta, so enumerating every .nodes walk AND every _neo_branch_meta access is provably complete (no semantic hiding places). Multi-agent fan-out not warranted.
Scan commands (reproducible):
  grep -rn 'for .* in .*\.nodes\|in construct\.nodes\|in self\.nodes\|in item\.nodes\|in sub\.nodes' src/neograph/*.py | grep -v 'arm_nodes\|for i in range\|lg_graph.nodes'
  grep -rn '_neo_branch_meta\|true_arm_nodes\|false_arm_nodes' src/neograph/*.py
Total .nodes-walk instances: 18 live walks (excl. loader spec-walks, emitted-code f-strings).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _construct_validation.py:128 | producer registration + type validation | MIGRATE | ticket site 1; RED test covers |
| 2 | _ir_normalize.py:226,228 | fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type inference + write-back | MIGRATE | ticket site 2; RED test; write-back into meta lists |
| 3 | lint.py:217 (_walk) | DI-binding + template lint | MIGRATE | ticket site 3; RED test |
| 4 | verify.py:91,163 | _walk + _has_llm_nodes | MIGRATE | ticket site 4; RED test |
| 5 | runner.py:206 | producer-consumer adjacency | MIGRATE | ticket site 5; RED test |
| 6 | compiler.py:146 | Operator string-condition registration check | MIGRATE | bare arm Operator condition never validated (found in trace-similar) |
| 7 | compiler.py:162 | has_operator -> checkpointer-required guard | MIGRATE | bare arm Operator skips checkpointer guard |
| 8 | compiler.py:183 | tool-factory registration check | MIGRATE | bare arm agent/act tools never validated |
| 9 | construct.py:170 | llm_config/renderer inheritance write-back | MIGRATE | bare arm LLM node misses parent llm_config/renderer inheritance (NEW -- not in trace-similar); write-back into meta lists |
| 10 | __main__.py:165 | CLI 'check' has_operator auto-MemorySaver | MIGRATE | arm Operator -> no auto-checkpointer -> false-negative check |
| 11 | _subconstruct.py:118 | runtime context forwarding within a sub-construct | MIGRATE | context node in an arm of the sub-construct forwarded as None |
| 12 | compiler.py:139,141 | compile_start logging node_names/modifiers | ALLOWLIST | display/telemetry only; no correctness impact |
| 13 | testing.py:72 (_collect_items) | test-scaffold codegen introspection | DEFER neograph-gfoq | tooling-only; arm nodes omitted from generated scaffolds |
| 14 | testing.py:90 (_collect_edges) | test-scaffold codegen introspection | DEFER neograph-gfoq | tooling-only; arm edges omitted from generated scaffolds |

title: Node.inputs/outputs typed as Any — largest type-safety gap in IR
description: Node.inputs: Any and Node.outputs: Any persist. Every consumer must isinstance-check. Comment says type[BaseModel] | dict[str, type] | None but annotation is Any. With Pydantic v2 BeforeValidator or TypeSpec Union, this could be properly typed. Single largest type-safety gap in the IR.
design:
## Architect Decision: SMALL ANNOTATION FIX

The validator was fixed in m91y — it rejects garbage at runtime. The remaining gap is:
- Static annotation type | dict[str, type] | None lies about what validator accepts
- Generic aliases (list[X]) and string dict values pass validation but fail type checking

Fix: Change TypeSpec to Annotated[Any, PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec)] with docstring listing valid forms. This is honest about the static limitation while the validator does real work.

Scope: 1 file change (node.py), ~5 lines. No behavioral change.
Triage: ALL_LOW — minimal, safe change.
notes:
## Research Findings

### Current state (already improved)
TypeSpec = Annotated[type | dict[str, type] | None, PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec)]
- _validate_type_spec is now a REAL validator (fixed in neograph-m91y)
- Rejects garbage: strings, ints, lists
- Accepts: None, type, generic aliases (list[X], dict[str,X], X|None), dict[str, type|str]

### The gap is static typing only
The static annotation type | dict[str, type] | None doesn't match what the validator accepts:
- Generic aliases (list[X]) are NOT type instances — they're GenericAlias
- Dict values can be str (decorator fallback, loader before resolution)
- Two # type: ignore[return-value] in _validate_type_spec evidence this

### PEP 747 TypeForm would solve this but isn't available yet

### Options
A. Widen annotation to include GenericAlias types — references typing._GenericAlias (private)
B. Use Any with PlainValidator — honest about static limits, validator does real work
C. Keep current — pragmatic, validator works, accept type: ignore comments

### Recommendation: Option B (Annotated[Any, PlainValidator])
- Honest: static annotation is Any (which it effectively already is)
- PlainValidator does the real validation at runtime
- Add docstring documenting valid forms
- Small, safe change

### Core invariant
PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec) is the single enforcement point. All three API surfaces pass through it at Node construction time.
close_reason: TypeSpec annotation fixed to Annotated[Any, PlainValidator]. Honest about static limits.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-jq2t
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-jq2t` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-jq2t/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-jq2t
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |

   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |

   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash

   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-jq2t/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash

```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Loop modifier: support multi-input produce+validate sub-constructs (input≠output type)
description:
## What

Loop modifier today requires a sub-construct whose input type matches its
output type — because Loop feeds each iteration's output back as the next
iteration's input. For the common "produce → validate → retry on errors"
pattern, this is too restrictive.

Typical consumer shape:

```python
@node(mode="think", outputs=Output, prompt="foo/produce")
def produce(
    a: SomeModel,  # 5 different upstream inputs
    b: Another,
    c: Third,
    d: Fourth,
    e: Fifth,
) -> Output: ...

@node(outputs=OutputValidated)
def validate(produce: Output, b: Another) -> OutputValidated:
    errors = [...]
    return OutputValidated(output=produce, errors=errors)

# Desired:
wrapped = construct_from_functions("produce-and-validate", [produce, validate]) | Loop(
    when=lambda v: v is None or bool(v.errors),
    max_iterations=5,
)
```

Today this fails construct_from_functions at compile time because input
type (UCComposite or one of the 5) doesn't match output (OutputValidated).

## Why

piarch has three produce+validate pairs filed (piarch-0dzjq, piarch-mbpxq,
piarch-szb6u) where validator errors should retry the producer with fresh
context. Each producer has 3-5 upstream inputs. Loop's input=output
constraint blocks all three.

Workarounds degrade the pattern:
- Collapse inputs into one bundle model — ugly DTO proliferation
- Fail loud without retry — no self-correction, bad output fails pipeline
- Manual retry @node with stateful counter — reimplementing Loop badly

## Direction

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

**(a) Decouple Loop input/output**: when a sub-construct's validator
has errors, re-execute the sub-construct with its ORIGINAL inputs,
not the output. Iteration state = error list + original fan-in inputs.
Requires Loop to remember the initial input tuple.

**(b) Explicit feedback channel**: the validator's errors become a
context entry visible to the producer on next iteration. Producer
template sees `{validation_errors}` (empty on first iteration, filled
on retry). No type constraint needed.

Either way, the pattern the user actually wants is: "retry the producer
with the SAME inputs, showing the LLM what the validator rejected."

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: Loop on a produce+validate sub-construct where producer
has 3 inputs and output is a Validated wrapper. First producer call
emits errors; Loop retries; second producer call emits clean output;
Loop exits. Verify the producer saw the validator's error list on
iteration 2.

**Integration**: max_iterations exhaust path — validator keeps emitting
errors; after N iterations, Loop raises ExecutionError.

**E2E**: piarch-0dzjq (brainstorm_extensions + at_step validator) wraps
in Loop without compile errors.

## Acceptance

- Sub-construct with input≠output can be wrapped in Loop
- Producer @node on retry sees validator errors (via context or
  template var)
- max_iterations + on_exhaust="error" still works
- piarch's three blocked tickets can all use Loop instead of fail-loud
design:
## Core Invariant
Loop feeds iteration output back as input; when input≠output on a sub-construct, re-read original inputs from parent state and deliver previous output as context feedback — one data flow, no type adapters.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Relax validate_loop_construct (_construct_validation.py:308-331)
Remove the _types_compatible check. Keep the requirement that both input and output are declared. The condition callable still evaluates the output type — that's correct and unchanged.

### 2. Change re-entry logic in make_subgraph_fn (factory.py:547-573)
Currently, iteration 2+ reads own_val[-1] and feeds as neo_subgraph_input. Change:
- If own_val[-1] is isinstance(sub.input) → existing path (input==output, backward compat)
- If own_val[-1] is NOT isinstance(sub.input) → skip own_val shortcut, fall through to parent state scan for original inputs. ALSO inject own_val[-1] into sub_input under the sub-construct's own field name (for context= access inside the sub-construct).

### 3. Add feedback field to sub-construct state (state.py)
When compiling a sub-construct with Loop and input≠output, add a state field for the feedback: the sub-construct's own field name with Optional[output] type, default None. This lets context= reference it.

### 4. Update ForwardConstruct._LoopCall (forward.py)
Allow input_type != output_type when building the sub-construct. Currently it infers both independently — just remove any validation that rejects the mismatch.

### 5. Update should_fail fixture → should_pass
Move the check fixture that tests input≠output rejection from should_fail/ to should_pass/. Add a new should_fail for the case where input OR output is None (that's still invalid).

### Files Changed
| File | Change | Risk |
|------|--------|------|
| _construct_validation.py | Remove type-compat check in validate_loop_construct | Low — targeted removal |
| factory.py:make_subgraph_fn | isinstance gate on re-entry path | Medium — core data flow |
| state.py | Optional feedback field for Loop+input≠output sub-constructs | Low — additive |
| forward.py | Allow mismatch in _LoopCall | Low — follows validation change |
| tests/test_loop.py | 3 new integration tests | N/A |
| tests/check_fixtures/ | Move/add fixtures | N/A |

### What Does NOT Change
- Loop on Node (self-loop) — unchanged, still requires input==output
- Loop condition evaluation — still receives output type
- Append-list state field — still uses output type
- _wiring.py — unchanged topology
- Existing tests — all pass (input==output path untouched)
notes:
## Findings

### Current Constraint
Loop on Construct requires `output` compatible with `input` (enforced at `|` time in `validate_loop_construct`, `_construct_validation.py:323`). At runtime, iteration N's output is fed back as iteration N+1's input via `make_subgraph_fn` (factory.py:547-553): `own_val[-1]` → `neo_subgraph_input`.

### Consumer Pattern
The user wants:
```python
@node(outputs=Output, prompt='foo/produce')
def produce(a: A, b: B, c: C) -> Output: ...

@node(outputs=OutputValidated)
def validate(produce: Output, b: B) -> OutputValidated:
    return OutputValidated(output=produce, errors=[...])

wrapped = construct_from_functions('p-v', [produce, validate]) | Loop(
    when=lambda v: v is None or bool(v.errors),
    max_iterations=5,
)
```
This fails because input=(A,B,C) and output=OutputValidated are different types.

### Key Files to Modify
1. `_construct_validation.py:validate_loop_construct` — relax type constraint
2. `factory.py:make_subgraph_fn` — change re-entry logic for input≠output
3. `_wiring.py:_construct_loop_unwrap` — condition evaluates output, not input
4. `state.py` — state field type stays as output (append-list of output type)
5. `modifiers.py` — Loop may need a `feedback` field for error injection

### Similar Implementations
- `Each` modifier's fan-out+barrier: `_add_each_to_graph` in `_wiring.py:256-321`. Uses a Send() pattern with per-item dispatch. Irrelevant to Loop.
- `Operator` interrupt/resume: rewires conditional edges but doesn't transform types between iterations.
- Node-level Loop dict-form inputs: `_extract_loop_reentry` in factory.py:420-455 already handles multi-key inputs where the self-referencing key gets the latest output and other keys read from state normally. THIS is the closest pattern.

### Critical Insight: Node-Level Loop Already Solves This
Node-level Loop with dict-form inputs handles the multi-input case:
```python
@node(output=Draft, loop_when=lambda d: d is None or d.score < 0.8)
def revise(context: Context, revise: Draft) -> Draft: ...
```
Here `context` reads from upstream state (constant across iterations), `revise` reads from own output. This works because `_extract_loop_reentry` routes self-referencing key to own output and other keys to state.

The Construct-level case is analogous: the sub-construct has 5 input params on its first node. On iteration 2+, the first node should still see the original upstream values PLUS the validator's output.

### Risk: Direction (b) from the task — Feedback Channel
The task suggests two directions. Direction (b) — explicit feedback channel where validator errors become context for the producer — is cleaner than (a) because:
- No need to decouple Loop input/output types
- The sub-construct's `input` stays as the producer's input type
- The sub-construct's `output` stays as the validator's output type
- A new state field carries validator errors into the next iteration
- The producer's prompt template sees `{validation_errors}` (empty on first, populated on retry)

BUT this requires the producer to declare errors as a DI param or input, breaking the clean function signature.

### Risk: Direction (a) — Decouple Input/Output
Direction (a) — re-execute sub-construct with original inputs — is simpler at the user level:
- Sub-construct re-runs from scratch each iteration
- Original upstream values preserved in parent state
- Only the validator output changes between iterations
- The Loop condition evaluates the OUTPUT (OutputValidated), not the input

The key change: on re-entry, `make_subgraph_fn` should NOT feed `own_val[-1]` (the OutputValidated) as `neo_subgraph_input`. Instead, it should fall through to the original input extraction logic (scan parent state for sub.input). The original inputs are still in parent state — they don't change.

This means: **on re-entry with input≠output, skip the own_val shortcut and let the sub-construct re-read its original inputs from parent state**.

### Edge Cases
1. What does the producer see on iteration 2+? Same inputs as iteration 1. The LLM gets a fresh prompt with the same context. Without feedback, it might produce the same bad output.
2. Solution: the validator's output (including errors) should be visible to the producer somehow. Two options:
   (a) Via `context=` on the producer node: add the validator's output field to the producer's context list. Then the prompt template shows prior errors.
   (b) Via a new Loop field (e.g., `feedback_field="validate"`) that injects the previous iteration's output into the sub-construct's state.
3. Temperature/sampling: even without feedback, retries with temperature>0 produce different results. This is the bare minimum.
## Architect Review

- [MEDIUM] Gap in context= feedback for Loop sub-constructs: parent state stores the sub-construct output as an append-list (Annotated[list[OutputValidated], _append_loop_result]). The context forwarding in make_subgraph_fn (factory.py:580-587) reads _state_get(state, ctx_field) which returns the raw list, not val[-1]. Fix: when forwarding context from a Loop sub-construct's own field, unwrap the append-list to val[-1].

- [MEDIUM] The _extract_context function (factory.py:79-90) also reads state fields raw for nodes within the sub-construct. Since the sub-construct's internal state is fresh each invocation (built from sub_input), the feedback field needs to be injected into sub_input with the unwrapped value, not the list. The internal state model's field for this should be Optional[OutputValidated], not list[OutputValidated].

- [LOW] Two check fixtures (mod_loop_construct_output_mismatch.py, loop_incompatible_types.py) need to move from should_fail/ to should_pass/. But we also need new should_fail fixtures for the cases that STILL fail: Loop on Construct with input=None or output=None.

- [LOW] ForwardConstruct._LoopCall: since it independently infers input_type and output_type and they can now differ, no code change needed — validate_loop_construct is the only gate, and it's being relaxed.

- [LOW] Design step 3 says "add feedback field to sub-construct state". Better approach: DON'T add a new framework field. Instead, inject the unwrapped previous output into sub_input under the sub-construct's own field_name. The sub-construct's internal state model already has context fields (from state.py context handling). If the producer uses context=["produce-and-validate"], the sub-construct state model gets a context field. The injected value flows through naturally.

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM items are implementation details with clear fixes, not design issues)
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_loop.py::TestLoopInputNotEqualOutput (3 tests)
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_compiles — produce+validate, 2 iterations, errors cleared
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_max_iterations — exhaust with on_exhaust=error
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_on_exhaust_last — exhaust with on_exhaust=last
- Status: FAILING (expected — TDD red step)
- Failure: ConstructError at validate_loop_construct:324 — 'Loop output type not compatible with input type for back-edge'
- Tests expected behavior: Construct|Loop with input!=output compiles and runs, re-reading original inputs on each iteration

title: §5: Audit Any in IR public APIs and dispatch layers; reduce to user-data boundaries only
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5 (Type and error discipline).

**Problem**: `Any` count in load-bearing modules (per senior review §W4):
- `_wiring.py`: 27
- `factory.py`: 17 (state: Any pattern at lines 54, 61, 79 — written before state model was typed)
- `_oracle.py`: 11
- `_construct_validation.py`: 11

Some `Any` is unavoidable (state is `dict | BaseModel`, user-declared input/output types). But many are not: `compile_state_model` produces a typed Pydantic model (`state.py:81`) and downstream code throws away the type information.

**Fix**: per file, walk every `Any` annotation. For each:
- Is the value at a user-supplied-data boundary? Keep `Any` (and add a comment naming the boundary).
- Is the value an internal framework type that was lazily annotated? Replace with the precise type.
- Is the value a polymorphic IR field (e.g., `Node.outputs`)? Replace with normalizer access (per §8).
- Is the value `RunnableConfig` or similar approved external type? Annotate with the precise external type.

**Acceptance**: each module's `Any` count drops to the value at the user-data boundary (which should be a single-digit count, much smaller than today). Each remaining `Any` has a one-line comment naming the boundary it represents.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5.

## How to verify

title: forward: compile() integration for traced ForwardConstruct
description:
Wire the traced `ForwardConstruct` end-to-end through the existing `compile()` pipeline and verify the resulting StateGraph behaves identically to the equivalent declarative `Construct(nodes=[...])`.

## Context

- Depends on the tracer subtask.
- Design: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` — "Emitted IR" section. The whole point of tracing into the existing IR shape is that this subtask should need **zero** changes to `compiler.py` or `state.py` for the MVP. If it does, that is a bug in the tracer, not an excuse to fork the compiler.

## Files

- Verify no changes needed to: `src/neograph/compiler.py`, `src/neograph/state.py`, `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py`, `src/neograph/factory.py`.
- If changes ARE needed, they should be additive guards only (e.g. skipping Proxies that leak into modifier fields) — get review before expanding scope.
- `tests/test_forward_construct_compile.py` — new end-to-end test file.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Build a `Pipeline(ForwardConstruct)` with two scripted Nodes chained straight-line in `forward()`. Compile it via `compile(pipeline)`. Assert the compiled graph's nodes match the declarative equivalent one-for-one (same node names, same topology).
2. Run the compiled graph with a seed input and verify the final state has the same shape as the declarative equivalent.
3. Run the declarative equivalent `Construct("pipeline", nodes=[decompose, classify])` through `compile()` and `invoke()`; assert the two runs produce equal final states given the same input.
4. `compile_state_model(pipeline)` returns a Pydantic model with the same fields in the same order as the declarative version.
5. The construct-level `_validate_node_chain` fires for a misconfigured ForwardConstruct (e.g. a classify node whose `input` type is incompatible with the decompose output). Same error, same source-location pointer.
6. Test uses only `Node.scripted(...)` nodes and fakes — no real LLMs.

## Out of scope

- Branching, looping, interrupt support.
- Modifiers on traced nodes. For now if a user attaches `Oracle` / `Each` / `Operator` to a class-attribute Node, it should pass through unchanged (they're attached to the Node, not the trace). Add one sanity test but do not expand the modifier story.
close_reason: Straight-line ForwardConstruct MVP complete. di0: base class with node discovery via __mro__ walk + Pydantic ignored_types fix. 3us: symbolic proxy tracer (_Proxy + _Tracer + _ForwardSelf + _NodeCall) wired into ForwardConstruct.__init__. vxv: zero compiler changes — tracer output is a plain nodes list that compile()/state-builder/factory consume unchanged. 10 new tests across 3 classes. 169/169 passing.

title: cgkl+godmodule followup: architectural analysis of factory.py split — change-axis clustering, not topical grouping
description:
## Context

`neograph-cgkl` closed with factory.py split from 601 → 290 lines into 4 topical modules:
- factory.py (290L) — `make_node_fn`, `make_subgraph_fn`, `_make_raw_wrapper`, `_execute_node`, `_type_name`
- `_state_io.py` (101L) — `_build_state_update`, `_inject_oracle_config`
- `_modifier_io.py` (201L) — `_apply_skip_when`, `_extract_input`, shape dispatch, `InputShape` enum
- `_observability.py` (24L) — `_extract_context` only

The split was mechanical. It grouped functions by topic, not by change-axis. `TestFactoryResponsibilityDiscipline` (the acceptance test) enforces a name whitelist and a 300-line budget — neither of which is testing architecture.

Same pattern as the vv05 Any-audit followup: surface-level wins masquerading as architecture. The maintainer's framing applies: "each violation is a code smell, not a problem itself. Analyze in detail and fix first; the symptom disappears as a side effect."

## Architectural questions the mechanical split didn't ask

1. **What is the CORE abstraction each new module represents?**
   - `_observability.py` is 24L (one function). Either a stub or the start of a namespace — which?
   - `_modifier_io.py` lumps "when to run this node" (`_apply_skip_when`) and "what input does it get" (`_extract_input`) under "modifier-aware". Two distinct change axes, one module.
   - `_state_io.py` — both functions write to state, but is it "state writeback" or "the state-bus boundary in the write direction"?

2. **Is factory.py still doing too much?**
   - `make_node_fn` + `make_subgraph_fn` — plausibly one responsibility
   - `_make_raw_wrapper` — raw escape-hatch path, different surface, different consumers
   - `_execute_node` — mode dispatch. **This may belong in `_dispatch.py`, not factory.** Factory is "build the callable"; execute is "drive the callable".
   - `_type_name` — type-name rendering for logs. Probably belongs in `_observability.py` (if that namespace is real) or as a private helper next to its only consumer.

3. **We deleted ad-hoc anti-drift guards at `tests/test_structural_guards.py:96-106`.** Those existed BECAUSE the boundary leaked. Did we replace them with something stronger, or just remove the guardrail?

4. **Forward-looking test**: "If we add a new execution mode, which files change?" "If we add a new modifier shape?" "If we change checkpoint state shape?" A clean architecture has small predictable answers.

## Out of scope

- NO code changes in this ticket
- NO module file moves
- NO test changes
- Deliverable is a written analysis only

## Deliverable

`docs/design/god-module-analysis-2026-05-20.md` — a written analysis covering current factory.py + the 3 spin-off modules. Sections:

### Section 1 — Per-function change-axis analysis

For each function across factory.py, _state_io.py, _modifier_io.py, _observability.py, _make_raw_wrapper, _execute_node, _type_name:

| Function | Current home | Callers | Change scenarios that touch it | Change-axis cluster |
|---|---|---|---|---|

"Change scenarios" examples:
- "New execution mode added (e.g., 'streaming')"
- "Modifier shape changes (new fan-out / fan-in pattern)"
- "Checkpoint state schema change"
- "New observability field added"
- "Raw escape-hatch contract changes"
- "Sub-graph dispatch semantics change"

"Change-axis cluster" — the family of related changes. Functions sharing a cluster should ideally share a module.

### Section 2 — Cluster identification

After per-function analysis, identify the actual change-axis clusters in the code (not the topical labels we already used). Expected 3-6 real clusters.

For each cluster:
- Name (semantic, not topical — what changes WHEN)
- Functions belonging to it
- Where they currently live
- The mismatch between current home and ideal home

### Section 3 — Proposed module layout (architectural, not topical)

Based on Section 2's clusters, propose a module layout where each module = one change-axis. For each proposed module:
- Module name (semantic)
- Functions inside
- Single responsibility statement (one sentence describing the change-axis)
- Imports it exposes / consumes
- Future-change scenarios it absorbs (small list)

### Section 4 — Diff from current state

For each function: stay-in-current-home | move-to-X | rename-current-home.

Specifically address:
- Does `_execute_node` belong in `_dispatch.py`?
- Is `_observability.py` a stub or a real namespace? If stub, fold where?
- Should `_modifier_io.py` split into `_skip.py` + `_input_extract.py`?
- Is `_state_io.py` correctly named? Or is it "state-bus write boundary"?
- Where should `_type_name` live?

### Section 5 — Architectural guard proposals

For each module in the proposed layout, what structural test catches drift?
- NOT line-count budgets (proxies, not metrics)
- NOT name whitelists (lock in current state, not architectural intent)
- INSTEAD: import-graph constraints, change-axis property tests, scenario walkthroughs

Example: a "scenario walkthrough" test could enumerate change scenarios (1.A, 1.B, ...) and assert each touches at most N files. If a scenario starts touching M>N, that's a drift signal.

### Section 6 — Acknowledged limits

Some splits won't be possible due to runtime constraints (e.g., circular dependencies that ANY split would reintroduce). Document them honestly.

## How to verify

**Test file**: N/A (analysis-only ticket; no test required)
**Test type**: review-deliverable
**What it exercises**: the written analysis. Maintainer reviews and grades:
- Does each function have a substantive change-axis analysis (not "topical: state-writing")?
- Are change-axis clusters real (testable via future-change scenarios) or rationalized?
- Are proposed moves specific (file + function + rationale)?
- Are proposed architectural guards stronger than name-whitelist / line-budget?

**Expected initial state**: document does not exist; produce it.
**Persistence**: stays in docs/design/ permanently; per-move tickets cite it.

## Acceptance

- `docs/design/god-module-analysis-2026-05-20.md` exists with all 6 sections above
- Per-function analysis covers ~10-12 functions across the 4 modules
- 3-6 change-axis clusters identified
- Specific stay/move/rename verdict per function
- At least one architectural-guard proposal per module (stronger than line budget)
- No code or test files modified by this ticket

## Source

- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §4 (Module and function responsibilities)
- Predecessor: neograph-cgkl (mechanical split, this analyzes the result)

Dependency chain: gm-2 → gm-1 → gm-3 → gm-4; gm-5 depends on all four.

title: forward: Python 'if' conditional branching via Proxy.__bool__
description:
Add Python `if` support to `ForwardConstruct.forward()` tracing by intercepting `Proxy.__bool__`. This is the subtask that actually kills `Operator(when='string_key')` dispatch — it's what the epic is pointing at.

## Context

- Depends on the end-to-end compile integration.
- Design: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` — "How control flow maps" (if section) and "How the Proxy type works". Note the open question about re-trace vs exception-rewind; this subtask needs to pick one and document the choice.
- Prior art: torch.fx's `concrete_args` re-trace pattern. Read torch/fx/proxy.py `TraceError` handling before starting.

## Files

- `src/neograph/forward.py` — add branch interception to `Proxy` and branch-recording state to `Tracer`.
- Potentially new IR: `BranchConstruct` or a modifier that lowers to `graph.add_conditional_edges`. This subtask gets to decide; the decision goes in a doc-comment with rationale.
- `src/neograph/compiler.py` — new lowering path for the branch IR to LangGraph conditional edges.
- `tests/test_forward_construct_branching.py` — new test file.

## Signatures

Sketch — the implementer may refine:

```python
class Proxy:
    def __lt__(self, other): return _ComparisonProxy(self, '<', other)
    def __gt__(self, other): return _ComparisonProxy(self, '>', other)
    # __le__, __ge__, __eq__, __ne__ similarly
    def __bool__(self):
        tracer = _active_tracer()  # contextvar
        return tracer.record_branch(self)  # returns True first, then False on re-trace
```

Strategy to pick (document in design-note comment):
- **Re-trace**: `Tracer.record_branch` returns True, runs forward() to completion, then resets and re-runs with False for that branch id. torch.fx approach.
- **Fork-on-demand**: single trace, on __bool__ spawn a cloned tracer that explores both arms. More complex, handles nested branches symmetrically.
Pick one; explain why in the module docstring.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `forward()` with `if self.classify(x).confidence < 0.7: self.decompose(x)` compiles to a StateGraph with a conditional edge after `classify`, same topology as the declarative `classify | Operator(when='low_confidence')` equivalent.
2. Both arms of the branch run correctly at runtime (test with seed inputs that take each arm).
3. Nested `if` works (at least two levels deep).
4. `elif` / `else` work.
5. Predicate supports: attribute chains (`x.confidence`), numeric comparisons (`<`, `>`, `==`), and `and`/`or` between comparisons. Short-circuit semantics documented.
6. A predicate that references a non-proxy value (e.g. `if some_constant:`) still works — don't over-intercept.
7. Failure mode: a predicate that we can't represent (e.g. calls a user function on a Proxy) raises `TracerError` with a pointer to the `forward()` line.

## Out of scope

- `for` loops, `try/except`, `while` — separate subtasks.
- Branch depth > 4 (bail with a clear error; 4 is arbitrary but bounded to keep re-trace cost sane).
- Interaction with `Oracle` / `Each` modifiers on nodes inside branches.
close_reason: Python if branching via Proxy.__bool__ + re-trace strategy. _Proxy gains __getattr__ (child proxies for attribute chains), 6 comparison dunders returning _ConditionProxy, __bool__ delegating to tracer. Re-trace strategy: run forward() with all branches True, then re-run with each branch flipped to False, diff traces to identify true-only/false-only/shared nodes. _BranchNode sentinel in node list carries _BranchMeta (condition spec + arm nodes). Compiler gains _add_branch_to_graph lowering _BranchNode to add_conditional_edges with a runtime router that navigates state field + attribute chain and applies the comparison. Join node for convergence. State builder extended for branch arm nodes. 18 new tests in tests/test_forward_construct_branching.py. 187/187 passing.

title: Phase 0 — dual-surface test harness + async fakes (scaffolding)
description:
SCAFFOLDING ONLY, co-evolving with Phase 1 (review M5) — do NOT gate Phase 1 on a 'complete' harness; the run/arun fixture can't be finalized against arun() semantics that don't exist yet.

Build: (1) a parametrized fixture that runs a behavioral test through both run() and arun() (and later astream); (2) async mirrors for the LLM fakes (ReActFake/StructuredFake/TextFake/GuardFake gain ainvoke/abind_tools) from ONE shared source of truth so sync/async fakes can't drift.

IMPORTANT (review M1/M7): parity is necessary but NOT sufficient — it proves plumbing, not concurrency/ordering/blocking/cancellation. The harness must also enable: real-concurrency tests (N runs on one loop), an event-loop-blocking watchdog, and cancellation E2Es. It is a 6-cell grid (3 API surfaces x sync/async), not a doubling; decide where full 6-cell is mandatory vs a representative subset.

Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §7. Ref architecture-review §M1/M5/M7.
design:
## Core Invariant
One compiled Construct, many drivers: every behavioral assertion holds identically under run() and (future) arun(), guaranteed structurally by making the sync invoke() itself the single source of truth — each fake's ainvoke() is a bare delegation that computes nothing, so sync and async fakes CANNOT drift.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review — scaffolding only, co-evolving with Phase 1; do NOT gate Phase 1 on completeness)

1. **Async mirrors by DELEGATION, not extraction (MED-2).** For each of the 8 shared deterministic fakes in tests/fakes.py (StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, TextFake, GuardFake, StubbornFake, FakeTool) add:
   - 'async def ainvoke(self, *a, **k): return self.invoke(*a, **k)'
   - 'def abind_tools(self, *a, **k): return self.bind_tools(*a, **k)'  (only fakes that HAVE bind_tools: ReActFake, StringArgsFake, GuardFake, StubbornFake)
   - StringArgsFake also: 'async def _agenerate(self, *a, **k): return self._generate(*a, **k)'
   invoke() stays the ONLY response logic. No _impl extraction (that conflated the per-fake sync/async mirror with the cross-fake _final_json_content rendering helper and added churn). ainvoke computes nothing -> drift structurally impossible.
   NOTE: the NEW awaitable-gated M1 primitive (step 5) is async-native and EXEMPT from this delegation invariant (it has no sync counterpart).

2. **Drift-guard is STRUCTURAL, not behavioral (MED-1).** The specified 'ainvoke output == invoke output' guard is unsound: invoke() mutates scripted state (ReActFake._call_idx, StringArgsFake._call_idx, GuardFake._call_counter, StubbornFake._call_count, FakeTool.calls) so sequential calls advance the script -> false mismatch; and AIMessage has no value __eq__. Instead add a guard in the tests/test_guards_* convention that inspects each fake's ainvoke via source/AST and asserts the body is a bare delegation to invoke (no response logic), and abind_tools delegates to bind_tools. This is the enforcement of the Core Invariant and is state-safe.
   Plus (LOW-3): add ONE executed 'asyncio.run(fake.ainvoke(...))' smoke assertion so ainvoke is EXERCISED (not merely inspected) in Phase 0, since the async driver cell skips today.

3. **Enable async collection.** Add asyncio_mode='auto' AND asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope='function' to [tool.pytest.ini_options] (pyproject.toml:103) — the loop-scope setting silences the pytest-asyncio deprecation warning and avoids a future warnings-as-error surprise (LOW). pytest-asyncio already a dep (pyproject:38); confirmed zero existing 'async def test' so 'auto' reclassifies nothing.

4. **Parametrized driver fixture (tests/conftest.py).** A sync fixture params=['sync','async'] yielding a callable driver(graph, **run_kwargs) that dispatches to run() or asyncio.run(arun(...)). The 'async' cell skip-guards on hasattr(neograph,'arun') so it is inert today and auto-activates when Phase 1 lands — NOT gated on nonexistent arun semantics (M5). Reuse build_fake_llm_kwargs / build_test_compile_kwargs / schemas._producer for the smoke pipeline. Keep the fixture SYNC (asyncio.run per call); real-concurrency (N runs on ONE loop) are separate explicit 'async def test' cases, NOT via this per-call fixture.

5. **Seed the parity-insufficient primitives (M1).** In tests/fakes.py: (a) an awaitable-gated fake whose ainvoke awaits an asyncio.Event (enables real-concurrency interleaving + cancellation-E2E parking) — async-native, exempt from step-1 delegation; (b) a small event-loop-lag watchdog helper (monotonic clock, GENEROUS threshold to avoid CI flakiness) for the blocking-detector test. Parity proves plumbing; these enable concurrency/blocking/cancellation tests parity structurally cannot. Full E2Es land with Phase 1; Phase 0 ships the primitives, kept assertion-light.

6. **Bake the 6-cell policy into the harness.** Document at the fixture: full 6-cell (3 API x sync/async) mandatory ONLY for IR-level behavioral changes; representative subset for execution-surface-agnostic logic; async doubling targeted at I/O-bearing (LLM/tool) tests, not pure/scripted nodes (M7). Also NOTE (do not implement) a Phase-1 obligation: re-triage the ~60 ALLOWLISTed inline fakes that are actually consumed by I/O-bearing tool-loop/LLM behavioral tests before finalizing the 6-cell subset, so the ALLOWLIST is not silently inherited as a Phase-1 blocker (LOW).

7. **Land green.** Phase 0 must pass make quality with the async driver cell skipped and no arun assertions — pure scaffolding co-evolving with Phase 1 (M5).
notes:
## Findings

### Reuse targets (extend, do NOT rebuild)
- **tests/fakes.py** is the single file to touch for async fakes. Fakes: StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, TextFake, GuardFake, StubbornFake, FakeTool. Each implements the same sync LLM contract: invoke(messages, **kwargs), bind_tools(tools), with_structured_output(model, **kwargs); StringArgsFake also has _generate().
- **THE single-source-of-truth pattern already exists**: _final_json_content (tests/fakes.py:47) is the shared helper ReActFake/StringArgsFake/GuardFake all funnel their final-turn rendering through. This IS the model to copy for 'sync/async cannot drift': factor each fake's response computation into ONE sync _impl method, then invoke returns it and 'async def ainvoke' returns the SAME call. Do not duplicate response logic into ainvoke.
- **tests/conftest.py** has exactly one autouse fixture (_clean_registries) and NO parametrized fixtures — the driver fixture goes here. It already imports reset_test_registry from tests.fakes.
- **Graph-construction plumbing to reuse in the fixture**: build_fake_llm_kwargs / configure_fake_llm (fakes.py:585/619), build_test_compile_kwargs (fakes.py:111), build_fake_runtime (fakes.py:632). tests/schemas.py:45/49 _producer/_consumer build minimal Node chains.

### run()/arun() status
- run() exists at src/neograph/runner.py:270 (exported from neograph.__init__, line 82). It wraps graph.invoke() for three modes (new / resume / crash-recovery).
- **arun() does NOT exist. Zero async in src/**: grep 'async def|await|ainvoke|astream|arun' src/neograph/ returns nothing. arun/async-checkpointer are Phase 1. Phase 0 MUST NOT assert or gate on arun semantics (review M5).
- Fake consumption sites that get async twins in Phase 1 (context only, not Phase 0 work): _tool_loop.py:77/91/252/266 (bind_tools().invoke() via _CoercingToolWrapper), :324 tool_fn.invoke(); _llm.py with_structured_output path.

### Test-infra state
- pytest-asyncio>=0.23 is already a project dep (pyproject.toml:38) BUT there is NO asyncio_mode set in [tool.pytest.ini_options] (pyproject.toml:103). Default is 'strict' → async tests/fixtures need explicit markers. There are currently ZERO async tests in tests/.
- LangGraph runs sync nodes in a threadpool under ainvoke — so a purely-sync fake 'works' under a future arun via threadpool. That masks whether the async vertical is truly exercised. The event-loop-blocking watchdog (M1) is the ONLY thing that catches a fake/tool that blocks the loop; parity cannot.

### 6-cell grid (M7) — mandatory vs representative
- 3 API surfaces (@node / declarative / programmatic) x 2 exec surfaces (sync/async) = 6 cells per IR-level behavioral change. Three-surface is already the top bug source (AGENTS.md).
- Policy from design §7 / review M7: full 6-cell mandatory ONLY for IR-level behavioral changes; representative subset for execution-surface-agnostic logic (rendering/validation, e.g. describe_type, lint). Target the async doubling at I/O-bearing (LLM/tool) tests, NOT pure/scripted nodes (LangGraph threadpools those → near-zero async signal).

### Parity is necessary but NOT sufficient (M1) — primitives Phase 0 must ENABLE
Parity proves plumbing only. The three tests parity structurally cannot be need fake primitives Phase 0 seeds:
1. Real-concurrency (N runs on one loop, assert interleaving/isolation) → needs an awaitable-gated fake whose ainvoke awaits an asyncio.Event/sleep so interleaving is observable.
2. Event-loop-blocking watchdog (slow sync call under arun trips a loop-lag detector) → needs a loop-lag measurement helper.
3. Cancellation E2E (cancel mid-astream, assert session close + checkpoint consistency) → needs the same awaitable-gated fake so the run can be deterministically parked and cancelled.
These are mostly exercised in Phase 1+, but the fake primitives belong with the async-fakes work here.
## Relevant Code
- tests/fakes.py:47 _final_json_content -- EXISTING shared source-of-truth helper; the exact pattern to replicate so ainvoke/invoke cannot drift.
- tests/fakes.py:171-533 the fake classes (StructuredFake/ReActFake/StringArgsFake/TextFake/GuardFake/StubbornFake) -- each needs a sync _impl extraction + async ainvoke/abind_tools mirror.
- tests/fakes.py:111 build_test_compile_kwargs, :585 build_fake_llm_kwargs -- compile-kwargs plumbing the driver fixture splats into compile().
- tests/conftest.py:7 _clean_registries autouse fixture -- sibling location for the new parametrized driver fixture; no existing parametrized fixtures.
- tests/schemas.py:45/49 _producer/_consumer -- minimal Node builders for harness smoke pipelines.
- src/neograph/runner.py:270 run() -- the sync driver the fixture wraps; arun() will mirror it in Phase 1.
- src/neograph/__init__.py:82 'run' export -- arun/astream will be added here; the async fixture cell skip-guards on hasattr(neograph,'arun').
- pyproject.toml:103 [tool.pytest.ini_options] -- add asyncio_mode='auto' (pytest-asyncio already dep at line 38).
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:81 _CoercingToolWrapper -- Phase-1 async twin consumer of fake.ainvoke (context only).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **asyncio_mode unset**: pytest-asyncio defaults to strict; without asyncio_mode='auto' async tests/fixtures are silently not collected as async. Set it in pyproject as part of Phase 0.
- **Do NOT gate on arun (review M5)**: arun() does not exist. The async driver cell MUST skip-guard on hasattr(neograph,'arun') so the harness ships green today and lights up automatically when Phase 1 lands. Phase 0 is scaffolding co-evolving with Phase 1 — not a 'complete' harness.
- **Drift is the whole threat**: if ainvoke re-implements response logic instead of calling the shared sync _impl, sync/async silently diverge. Add a drift-guard test asserting ainvoke(...)==invoke(...) for identical fake state (analogous to the structural-guard suite).
- **Threadpool masking**: under a future arun, a purely-sync fake still works via LangGraph's sync-node threadpool, so parity green does NOT prove the async vertical is awaited. Only the loop-blocking watchdog catches a blocking call. Do not let parity create false confidence (M1).
- **Wall-clock (review M7/§9.5)**: blanket 6-cell doubling is a suite-time sink. Gate full 6-cell to IR-level behavioral changes; representative subset elsewhere; target doubling at I/O-bearing tests only.
- **Driver fixture shape**: keep the fixture SYNC, yielding a callable that internally does asyncio.run for the async branch (one loop per run() call). Real-concurrency tests (N runs on ONE loop) are separate explicit 'async def test' cases using arun directly — they do NOT go through the per-call driver fixture.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.1)

Pattern: LLM/tool fake response logic lives inline in invoke()/_generate() with NO shared sync method a future ainvoke() can reuse -> sync/async fakes will silently drift when async mirrors are added.
