title: Phase 1 — async foundation (arun, driver-selected async, async checkpointer)
description:
The keystone. Add async execution as a DIMENSION (dual sync/async, never a flip).

Core (review H2 — the load-bearing correction): async-ness is chosen by the DRIVER (run vs arun), NOT by the node body. think/agent/act have EMPTY bodies — there is no async def to detect. Under arun() the LLM/tool/MCP vertical (_execute_node->_dispatch->_tool_loop) awaits llm.ainvoke()/tool.ainvoke(); under run() it stays sync. The body's async-ness governs ONLY how a scripted body is invoked (await vs threadpool). Getting this wrong is SILENT (tests pass; prod still blocks the loop).

Scope: dual-path factory emitting an async node_wrapper twin; async scripted-shim (await async body); async twins for the custom seams (_CoercingToolWrapper/abind_tools _tool_loop.py:251; think-mode structured-output/coercion path — review L3/L4); async checkpointer (AsyncSqliteSaver/AsyncPostgresSaver). DI resolution is pure dict lookup — no await (review L3).

Phase-1 acceptance MUST include (review M6): (a) observability survives await (trace/contextvars across await — Langfuse example); (b) mixed-driver checkpoint resume (sync SqliteSaver thread resumes under AsyncSqliteSaver, same thread_id) — resolve, don't leave open; (c) a performance gate (async adds no per-call overhead beyond threshold; exercises within-run MCP session reuse per §5/H1).

Depends on Phase 0. Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.1, §4, §9.
design:
## Core Invariant
One compiled Construct, two drivers over ONE shared execution core: async is a DRIVER-selected
dimension (run->func / arun->afunc on a single RunnableLambda node), never a body-detected flip — the
sync and async paths share every pure preamble/postamble/rendering/parse helper and diverge ONLY at the
terminal `await llm.ainvoke()/tool.ainvoke()`, so they cannot silently drift and the sync surface is
never rewritten.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; extend existing seams, do not rebuild)

1. **Dual-path node registration via RunnableLambda (the spine).** Change `factory.make_node_fn`
   (factory.py:22) to return `RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)`. `node_wrapper` stays
   the current sync shell; `anode_wrapper` is a new async shell calling `_aexecute_node`. All add_node
   sites in _wiring.py stay unchanged. Raw wrapper (_make_raw_wrapper): await raw_fn only if it is a
   coroutine function, else call sync.

2. **Async twin of the execution core, reusing every pure helper.** Add `_aexecute_node` in _execute.py
   that reuses adapt_state / _inject_oracle_config / _extract_input / _apply_skip_when /
   _extract_context / NodeInput shaping / _build_state_update verbatim and only `await
   dispatch.aexecute(...)`. Add `async def aexecute` to the ModeDispatch Protocol (_dispatch.py) and the
   three classes: ScriptedDispatch (await async body via inspect.iscoroutinefunction, else sync call —
   this is the ONLY place body async-ness matters, review H2); ThinkDispatch -> `_llm.ainvoke_structured`;
   ToolDispatch -> `_tool_loop.ainvoke_with_tools`. Reuse _render_input / _resolve_primary_output /
   budget-tracker / oracle-override setup unchanged.

3. **Async twins for the custom LLM/tool seams (review L3/L4).** In _tool_loop.py add
   `ainvoke_with_tools` (keep bind_tools sync; await `_CoercingToolWrapper.ainvoke` and
   `tool_fn.ainvoke(args)`); give `_CoercingToolWrapper` an `ainvoke` + async `_agenerate` recovery
   mirror of the sync string-args coercion. In _llm.py add `ainvoke_structured`; in _llm_dispatch.py add
   `_acall_structured` (await the structured adapter + async json-retry); in _llm_structured_compat.py add
   an async adapter method awaiting `structured.ainvoke` through the same Parsed/Raw/Failed
   classification; in _llm_retry.py add async twins only where the LLM is invoked (_parse_json_response
   stays shared). _get_llm and _compile_prompt stay sync (no I/O). DI resolve stays sync (L3).

4. **arun() runner + async checkpoint helpers.** Add `arun` in runner.py mirroring run() and reusing
   _inject_input_to_config / _preflight_di_check / _strip_internals verbatim; `await graph.ainvoke(...)`.
   Add async twins of _has_existing_checkpoint / _verify_checkpoint_schema / _auto_resume_from_divergence
   using `aget_tuple` / `aget_state_history`. Add ainvoke/aget_state/aget_state_history/astream explicit
   delegations to CompiledNeograph (_compiled.py). Export `arun` from neograph.__init__ — this lights up
   the Phase-0 conftest async cell automatically.

5. **Async checkpointer wiring.** compile() already passes checkpointer through to graph.compile()
   unchanged — no compiler change needed; an async saver just works. For tests use InMemorySaver (has
   both sync + async surfaces) for parity/unit; decide on langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite (AsyncSqliteSaver)
   for the true cross-driver mixed-resume E2E (see NEEDS USER INPUT in notes).

6. **Three mandatory acceptance areas (review M6), each an E2E/guard:**
   (a) Observability survives await — pass `config` into every `.ainvoke(messages, config=config)`;
       assert a Langfuse-style callback/trace span propagates across the await boundary.
   (b) Mixed-driver checkpoint resume — a thread started under a sync saver resumes under the async
       saver on the same thread_id (arun's async checkpoint helpers).
   (c) Performance gate — benchmark asserting the async path adds no per-call overhead beyond a
       threshold; forward-references §5/H1 within-run session reuse (fully realized in Phase 3).
   Plus the M1 non-parity trio using Phase-0 primitives: real-concurrency (N runs, one loop,
   GatedAsyncFake), event-loop-lag watchdog (catches a silent blocking twin), cancellation E2E.

7. **Lock the invariants with structural guards.** "Every LLM mode exposes BOTH a sync and an async
   dispatch path" (no sync-only mode); async twins live in the SAME module as their sync counterpart
   (no async-only module importing decorators.py — respects the layer-discipline guards). Land each
   step green through the dual-surface harness; 6-cell coverage is MANDATORY for the IR-level changes
   in steps 1-2 (@node / declarative / programmatic x sync / async).

## Scope judgment — DECOMPOSE (do NOT run as one implement atom)
This epic spans 8 source files, 6 distinct async-twin seams, an async checkpointer path, and 3
mandatory acceptance E2Es plus 3 non-parity concurrency tests. It is far past a single implement atom
and the review flagged the silent-failure mode as the central hazard. Recommended child atoms, ordered:
  1. Dual-path factory + _aexecute_node + ModeDispatch.aexecute (steps 1-2) — the IR spine, 6-cell tested.
  2. Async scripted shim (await async body vs threadpool) — three-surface parity.
  3. Async LLM+tool seams (_llm / _tool_loop / _llm_dispatch / _llm_structured_compat / _llm_retry) (step 3).
  4. arun() + async checkpoint helpers + CompiledNeograph async delegations + __init__ export (step 4).
  5. Async checkpointer wiring + mixed-driver resume E2E (steps 5, 6b).
  6. Observability-across-await E2E (6a) + performance gate (6c) + M1 concurrency/watchdog/cancellation.
  7. Structural guards locking the dual-path invariant (step 7).
See notes "NEEDS USER INPUT" on the sqlite-async test dependency before atom 5.
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher, l7js.2)

### The keystone reuse target — RunnableLambda(func, afunc=...) for dual-path node registration
LangGraph accepts any LangChain Runnable as a graph node and dispatches by driver:
`graph.invoke()` calls the node's `.invoke` (func); `graph.ainvoke()` calls `.ainvoke` (afunc).
`RunnableLambda(sync_func, afunc=async_func)` is the ONE primitive that gives "one Construct, many
drivers" with ZERO duplication at the registration seam (verified: RunnableLambda.__init__ takes
`afunc=`; instance has both invoke+ainvoke). So `factory.make_node_fn` should return
`RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)` instead of a bare function — every add_node call
site (_wiring.py:209/454/458/577/578) stays UNCHANGED (they pass one object to add_node). This is the
reuse-first spine of the whole phase: do NOT register two nodes or branch the wiring.

### The shared-core / thin-shell split (reuse-over-reinvention)
`_execute_node` (_execute.py:55) is preamble -> `dispatch.execute()` -> postamble. EVERYTHING except
the single `dispatch.execute()` middle call is pure, sync, I/O-free and REUSED VERBATIM by an async
twin: adapt_state, _inject_oracle_config, _extract_input, _apply_skip_when, _extract_context,
NodeInput shaping, _build_state_update, the two structlog lines, timing. So `_aexecute_node` is a
~10-line async twin that reuses the same helpers and only `await dispatch.aexecute(...)`. The
ModeDispatch Protocol (_dispatch.py:79) gains an `aexecute` method; the three dispatch classes get
async twins that reuse ALL their sync setup (rendering, output-model resolution, budget tracker,
oracle override) and differ ONLY in the terminal LLM/tool call. Same pattern one layer down: the
LLM/tool orchestrators (`invoke_structured`, `invoke_with_tools`) are long but only a handful of lines
touch the network — those get awaited; prompt compile / parse / usage-summing / logging are pure and
reused.

### DI resolution is pure dict lookup — NO await needed (review L3 CONFIRMED)
`DIBinding.resolve` (di.py:132) and `scripted_shim` (_scripted_registry.py:47) only read
`config['configurable'][...]` and construct Pydantic models. Zero I/O. The scripted shim body needs an
async twin ONLY to `await fn(*args)` when the user body is `async def` (detect via
`inspect.iscoroutinefunction`), else call sync (LangGraph threadpools a sync body under ainvoke). This
is the ONLY place body async-ness matters — review H2's load-bearing point.

### Driver chooses async, not the body (review H2)
think/agent/act have empty bodies (`...`) — there is no `async def` to detect. Async-ness of the
LLM/tool/MCP vertical is selected by which driver (run vs arun) invoked the graph, which selects
func vs afunc on the RunnableLambda automatically. Getting this wrong is SILENT: if the async node
just threadpools the sync vertical, tests pass but the loop still blocks and MCP (async-only) can't
bind. The afunc MUST route to the awaiting vertical.

### Async infra already present in installed deps
- CompiledStateGraph exposes ainvoke/astream/astream_events/aget_state/aget_state_history (verified).
- InMemorySaver supports BOTH sync (get_tuple/put) and async (aget_tuple/aput) — the test reuse target
  for mixed-driver resume without needing a new package.
- `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` is NOT installed (AsyncSqliteSaver import fails). Real AsyncSqliteSaver/
  AsyncPostgresSaver live in separate packages and expose ONLY the async API (sync get_tuple raises).
- Zero async in src/neograph today (grep count = 0). No async-body detection exists yet.

### Phase-0 harness to build on (w74k.1, landed)
- tests/conftest.py `run_driver` fixture params=['sync','async']; the async cell skip-guards on
  `hasattr(neograph,'arun')` and auto-activates the moment arun is exported from neograph.__init__.
- tests/fakes.py: all 8 shared fakes have bare-delegation `ainvoke`/`abind_tools`/`_agenerate`;
  GatedAsyncFake (awaitable-gated, for real-concurrency + cancellation) + event_loop_lag_watchdog
  (blocking detector) primitives exist.
- pyproject asyncio_mode='auto' set. Structural drift-guard tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py locks it.

- src/neograph/_execute.py:55 _execute_node -> add _aexecute_node twin; REUSE every helper (preamble/postamble pure). Only line :91 `dispatch.execute(...)` becomes `await dispatch.aexecute(...)`.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- SILENT-FAILURE risk (H2): an async node twin that just calls the sync vertical passes every parity test but never awaits — loop still blocks, MCP can't bind. The event-loop-lag watchdog + a GatedAsyncFake concurrency test (Phase-0 primitives) are the ONLY guards that catch this; parity cannot. A structural guard "every LLM mode has both a sync AND async dispatch path" (design §7) must be added.
- Observability across await (M6a): neograph threads `config` (carrying LangChain callbacks) into every llm.invoke(messages, config=config). The async twins MUST pass the SAME config into every `.ainvoke(messages, config=config)` — callbacks propagate via config, and contextvar-based tracers (Langfuse @observe) propagate across `await` natively (unlike threadpooled sync nodes). Dropping config on any async hop silently breaks the trace. Acceptance = a Langfuse observable_pipeline span survives the await boundary.
- Mixed-driver resume (M6b): sync SqliteSaver thread resumed under AsyncSqliteSaver same thread_id. Data is compatible (same DB). The real work is that arun()'s checkpoint helpers must call aget_tuple/aget_state_history (AsyncSqliteSaver's sync methods raise). InMemorySaver (both surfaces, same process) is the cheap unit-test vehicle; a TRUE cross-process/cross-saver E2E needs langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite which is NOT currently a dependency. NEEDS USER INPUT below.
- Perf gate (M6c): async adds no per-call overhead beyond threshold; must exercise within-run MCP session reuse (§5/H1) — but MCP is Phase 3. In Phase 1 the perf gate can only assert the async node/LLM vertical adds no per-call overhead vs sync; the session-reuse dimension is a forward-reference to Phase 3, not fully testable here. - Three-surface x sync/async = 6-cell (M7): IR-level changes here (factory/_execute/_dispatch) are exactly the "full 6-cell mandatory" category. The scripted-body async path (await async def) must be tested through @node, declarative Node.scripted(), AND programmatic surfaces (three-surface parity rule; neograph-ts7 class of bug).

## Core Invariant
The async node path is DRIVER-selected off a single RunnableLambda (graph.invoke->node_wrapper, graph.ainvoke->anode_wrapper) that shares the entire pure _execute_node preamble/postamble and every ModeDispatch setup helper VERBATIM, diverging only at the terminal 'await dispatch.aexecute()' — so sync and async cannot silently drift, and no add_node wiring, no sync surface, and no pure helper is rewritten.

## Implementation Plan (1a ONLY — reconciled to the disease-scan correction; single source of truth)

REVIEW-CONFIRMED SOUND (do not re-litigate): RunnableLambda(fn).invoke(state,config) forwards config to 2-arg (state,config) closures (accepts_config satisfied — DI/observability survive); RunnableLambda is NOT directly callable (migration mandatory); ainvoke routes to afunc with config intact; sync invoke calls func (no regression).

description: Research plan step 2 (ScriptedDispatch async path). The ONLY place body async-ness matters (review H2): the scripted shim async twin awaits fn(*args) when the user body is 'async def' (inspect.iscoroutinefunction), else calls sync (LangGraph threadpools sync bodies under ainvoke). design:
## Core Invariant
A scripted/raw async body is awaited by DETECTING the awaitable at the call boundary (`inspect.isawaitable(result)` AFTER invoking self.fn / raw_fn), NOT by inspecting the function object — because for @node the user body is hidden behind a synchronous shim (`scripted_shim` returns an un-awaited coroutine), so `iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` is blind to it; one call-then-isawaitable check works identically across @node, declarative, and programmatic surfaces, so sync and async scripted paths share the exact same shim/registry/compiler machinery and cannot drift.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; touch ONLY _dispatch.py + factory.py)
1. ScriptedDispatch.aexecute (_dispatch.py:126-137): add `import inspect` to the module; change the body to
   `result = self.fn(input_data.value, config)` -> `if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result` -> `return NodeOutput(single=result)`. DELETE the `# noqa: RUF029` on line 126 (the conditional await now satisfies RUF029). Reuse the EXISTING `scripted_shim` unchanged — it already returns `fn(*args)` which is a coroutine when the sidecar body is `async def`, and returns the raw value otherwise. Do NOT add per-surface branches, do NOT thread the sidecar into ScriptedDispatch, do NOT touch _scripted_registry.py / decorators.py / compiler.py / node.py.
2. Raw async twin (factory.py): add an async raw wrapper mirroring `_make_raw_wrapper` (:86-108) — same node_start/node_complete logging + timing, but `result = raw_fn(state, config); if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result` (conditional await; no noqa needed). Wire it in make_node_fn raw branch (:53-54): `return RunnableLambda(_make_raw_wrapper(node), afunc=<async_twin>(node))`. `raw_fn = node.raw_fn` is the user fn directly (no shim), so isawaitable-on-result also handles the async-raw case; keep detection identical to scripted to avoid drift. Factor shared log/timing if it reads cleanly, else a small twin is fine (matches the _execute_node/_aexecute_node a-prefix twin convention).
3. Tests — extend tests/test_async_dual_path.py (reuse `_sync_async_node_thread` harness, register_scripted, Claims/RawText). Add async-body cells for THREE surfaces driven under graph.ainvoke only (sync driver + async body is out of scope):

## Findings (dp-researcher — Phase 1b: async scripted shim + async raw twin)

### THE CRUX — the shim HIDES the async body (iscoroutinefunction(self.fn) is WRONG for @node)
ScriptedDispatch.fn (_dispatch.py:123/136) is `self.fn(input_data.value, config)`. What `self.fn` IS differs by surface, and this is the whole ballgame:
- @node surface: `self.fn` = the `scripted_shim` closure built by `_register_node_scripted` (_scripted_registry.py:47-68). That shim is ALWAYS a plain `def` (sync) — it ends `return fn(*args)` (line 68) where `fn` is the user`s ORIGINAL function pulled from the sidecar (`fn, param_names = _get_sidecar(n)`). If the user wrote `async def`, `fn(*args)` returns an UN-AWAITED coroutine and the sync shim returns it. So `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` == False for EVERY @node scripted node, async body or not. The async-ness is hidden one layer down in the sidecar.
- declarative `Node.scripted(name, fn="x")` (node.py:267) + programmatic `Node()|Modifier`: `scripted_fn` is a STRING; the actual callable is registered via `register_scripted(name, actual_fn)` (_runtime_registry.py:32) and looked up into the per-compile scripted dict. Here `self.fn` IS the user`s registered `(input_data, config)` fn directly — so `iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` WOULD be correct for these two surfaces, but NOT for @node.

### THE UNIFORM DETECTOR (reuse-first — zero shim/registry/compiler changes)
Do NOT branch per-surface and do NOT thread the sidecar into ScriptedDispatch. CALL first, then `inspect.isawaitable(result)`:
- @node: `self.fn(...)` (sync shim) returns `fn(*args)` = coroutine when body is async -> isawaitable True.
- declarative/programmatic async fn: `self.fn(...)` (async fn) returns coroutine -> isawaitable True.
- any sync body (all three surfaces): returns a BaseModel/dict -> isawaitable False -> no await.
Creating a coroutine does NOT run it (no loop needed), so `result = self.fn(...)` never blocks/errors even for async bodies. ONE check covers all three surfaces. This is strictly better than iscoroutinefunction (which needs the sidecar for @node) and matches the epic Core Invariant "one shared core".

### @node ALLOWS async def scripted bodies TODAY (nothing rejects/mishandles them at decoration)
- Mode inference (decorators.py:344-350) ignores async-ness: `async def` with no prompt/model infers `scripted`.
- The dead-body AST walk (decorators.py:373-402) already handles `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (line 377) but is gated to LLM modes only (line 355) — scripted bodies are never inspected. So an async scripted body gets NO warning, NO rejection.
- Sidecar stores `f` verbatim (`_register_sidecar` _sidecar.py:34 `n._sidecar = (fn, param_names)`), async preserved.
Net: async @node scripted bodies are constructible today but currently BROKEN on both drivers (shim returns an un-awaited coroutine). 1b fixes the ASYNC driver; the sync-driver case is out of scope (see Risks).

### RAW path — no shim, so raw_fn IS the user fn (async twin deferred from 1a)
factory.make_node_fn raw branch (factory.py:53-54) returns `RunnableLambda(_make_raw_wrapper(node))` with NO afunc. `_make_raw_wrapper` (factory.py:86-108) -> `raw_node_wrapper` calls `raw_fn(state, config)` (line 101) where `raw_fn = node.raw_fn` is the user fn DIRECTLY (no shim hiding it). 1b: add an async twin wrapper + `afunc=`. Same isawaitable-on-result pattern (or equivalently `iscoroutinefunction(node.raw_fn)` since there is no shim — both correct for raw; prefer isawaitable to keep raw+scripted detection identical).

### Async spine already wired (1a) — 1b only fills the terminal await
`_aexecute_node` (_execute.py:99-140) awaits `dispatch.aexecute(...)` at line 135 and reuses every pure helper. Once ScriptedDispatch.aexecute awaits the awaitable, an async body flows through end-to-end. make_node_fn normal path already returns `RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)` (factory.py:83). ONLY the raw path lacks an afunc.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py:126-137 ScriptedDispatch.aexecute — the 1b edit site. Currently `result = self.fn(...)` (sync-call form, `# noqa: RUF029` at :126). Change to: `result = self.fn(input_data.value, config); if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result; return NodeOutput(single=result)`. The conditional `await` satisfies RUF029 -> DELETE the `# noqa: RUF029`. Add `import inspect` (module has none today).
- src/neograph/_scripted_registry.py:47-68 scripted_shim — the sync `def` that returns `fn(*args)`; UNCHANGED (it already produces a coroutine when the sidecar fn is async). This is why no shim/registry/compiler plumbing is needed.
- src/neograph/factory.py:53-54 make_node_fn raw branch — add `afunc=`; :86-108 _make_raw_wrapper — add an async twin (async raw_node_wrapper: same log/timing, `result = raw_fn(state, config); if isawaitable(result): result = await result`).
- src/neograph/decorators.py:344-350 (mode inference, async-agnostic), :373-402 (dead-body walk, LLM-only, already AsyncFunctionDef-aware) — confirms async scripted bodies are permitted, untouched by 1b.
- src/neograph/_sidecar.py:34 `n._sidecar=(fn,...)` verbatim async fn; node.py:392-394 (@node self.fn = _scripted_shim); _runtime_registry.py:32 register_scripted (declarative/programmatic self.fn = user fn).
- src/neograph/_execute.py:135 `await dispatch.aexecute` — the spine that carries the awaited result. UNCHANGED.
- tests/test_async_dual_path.py — 1a harness to EXTEND. `_sync_async_node_thread` drives graph.invoke then asyncio.run(graph.ainvoke); build_test_compile_kwargs/register_scripted/Claims/RawText reused. Add async-body cells here.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- SHIM-HIDES-ASYNC TRAP (headline): using `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` detects nothing for @node (shim is sync) — async @node bodies would silently NOT be awaited (coroutine written to state, tests may pass on `is not None`). MITIGATION: detect via `inspect.isawaitable(result)` AFTER calling, not on the function object.
- SYNC-DRIVER + ASYNC-BODY = OUT OF 1b SCOPE (but real): under `run()` (graph.invoke -> ScriptedDispatch.execute :123) an async scripted body returns an un-awaited coroutine -> silently wrong output. Task scopes 1b to `aexecute` + raw async twin ONLY. Nothing in mode inference rejects async scripted bodies, so this latent footgun remains after 1b. Recommend a follow-up: either a decoration-time guard (async scripted body requires arun) or await-in-sync via a loop — do NOT do it in 1b. Flagging so it is not mistaken for done.
- SYNC BODY UNDER ainvoke IS CORRECT AS-IS: `result = self.fn(...)` returns a BaseModel, `isawaitable` False, no await — LangGraph`s ainvoke already threadpools nothing extra here (the node runs inline on the loop via the afunc; the sync body just executes). No regression, matches task ("call it sync").
- RUF029: the current 1a `# noqa: RUF029` on ScriptedDispatch.aexecute (:126) MUST be removed once the conditional `await` lands (the function now has an await). Leaving it is a dead-noqa lint failure under repo ruff. Same for the new async raw twin — it has a conditional await, so no noqa needed.
- THREE-SURFACE PARITY (neograph-ts7 class): async body must be exercised via @node (`async def f(x)->Y`), declarative Node.scripted(fn registered as `async def g(input_data,config)`), AND programmatic Node()|Modifier. The async-body cell can only be driven under graph.ainvoke (sync driver + async body is the out-of-scope footgun above), so assert the ainvoke result is the real Out (NOT a coroutine object) on all three; a body doing `await asyncio.sleep(0)` + flag proves it ran to completion, not left pending.
- isawaitable false-positive: a sync scripted body returning a Future/awaitable is theoretically mis-awaited. Not a real neograph case (scripted nodes return Pydantic models/dicts). Acceptable; note in a comment.
- LAYER DISCIPLINE: the fix stays in _dispatch.py (ScriptedDispatch) + factory.py (raw twin) — NO change to _scripted_registry.py / decorators.py / node.py / compiler.py. The shim is reused as-is; this respects "no @node-layer logic in low-level modules" and the sidecar-import guards.

## Core Invariant
Each sync LLM/tool orchestrator gets a THIN async twin in the SAME module: the pure preamble/render/parse/classify/budget/usage/logging bookends are EXTRACTED into shared helpers that BOTH sync and async call, so the twin adds only the awaited network seam (.invoke -> await .ainvoke, _generate -> await _agenerate) and the interleaving-await control flow — sync and async cannot drift, and config threads into every .ainvoke hop so observability survives the await.

## Implementation Plan (EXTRACT-then-THIN, bottom-up; pure refactors first, sync behavior unchanged)

STEP 0 — pure extractions (refactor SYNC path, no behavior change, run quality after each):
- _llm_structured_compat.py: extract the pure result-classification (lines ~97-108 and ~150-159) into a shared classify helper; sync invoke() calls it. Async ainvoke() will call the same.
- _llm.py invoke_structured (~151-192): extract the pure preamble (log.bind + usage_info assembly) and postamble (llm_log.info + _notify_cost) into shared helper(s) that invoke_structured calls; the awaited seam is _call_structured (~179).
- _tool_loop.py invoke_with_tools: extract the PURE preamble (~186-262 setup) and the PURE usage-summation+logging postamble (~439-471) into shared helpers; sync invoke_with_tools calls them. The ReAct while-loop (~264-380) and fallback tail (~400-437) interleave awaits and are NOT extracted.

IncludeRawCompatDecorator.ainvoke awaits self._inner.ainvoke(...) plus await structured.ainvoke where sync does. DsmlClassifierDecorator.ainvoke awaits self._inner.ainvoke(...) then pure reclassify. ## Core Invariant
The async driver (arun/graph.ainvoke) must preserve BEHAVIORAL and OBSERVABILITY parity with the sync driver over one shared pure core — every awaited network hop threads the SAME RunnableConfig (so callbacks/tracers survive the await), runs cooperatively on the event loop (never blocking it), and tears down cleanly on cancellation — WITHOUT the async path adding per-call overhead beyond a generous bound.

(Mostly TESTS. One conditional SOURCE FIX only if an E2E finds a dropped-config hop — code review says the LLM/think/agent vertical is already threaded, so expect zero LLM source fixes.)

### Perf gate — non-flaky formulation
- asyncio.run creates+tears a loop PER call: that is fixed per-RUN, not per-NODE. To isolate PER-CALL (per-node) overhead, amortize loop setup across many nodes: build a K-node chained scripted pipeline (e.g. K=20), measure median run() time and median single asyncio.run(arun()) time over M repeats (warm up first). Gate on per-node delta: (arun_median - run_median)/K < generous absolute bound (e.g. 20ms/node) OR arun_median < max(run_median*5, run_median+0.100s). Absolute floor prevents ratio flakiness when sync is trivially fast; the ratio catches pathological regressions (accidental per-node loop creation). Use time.perf_counter, median-of-M (M>=5), no wall-clock in CI-parallel asserts beyond the generous bound.
- PARTIAL COVERAGE (flag): within-run MCP session reuse (H1/§5) is Phase 3 — the 1f gate can only assert the async node/LLM vertical adds no per-call overhead. Document that the gate does NOT cover MCP session-reuse amortization.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- PERF-GATE FLAKINESS (highest): ratio-only gates flake when sync run is sub-ms; MUST include an absolute floor and use median-of-M with a warmup. Keep bounds generous (documented rationale). Prefer per-node-amortized delta over per-run comparison (asyncio.run loop setup is a fixed per-run cost that would otherwise dominate and falsely inflate "async overhead").
- WATCHDOG vs THREADPOOL: LangGraph threadpools a TRULY-SYNC node under ainvoke, which MASKS a blocking body (the watchdog would NOT trip). To trip it deterministically, the blocking body must run inline on the loop thread — use an async-def scripted body that calls time.sleep (stays on the loop) OR confirm via thread-identity (test_async_dual_path.py pattern) that the sync scripted afunc runs inline post-1a. Assert post-cancel the saver is reusable (re-arun the same thread_id resumes cleanly) — that both proves clean teardown AND checkpoint consistency. title: Phase 1g: structural guards locking the dual-path invariant
description: Research plan step 7. Guard: 'every LLM mode exposes BOTH a sync AND an async dispatch path' (no sync-only mode) — the structural counter to the H2 silent-failure hazard. Guard: async twins live in the SAME module as their sync counterpart (no async-only module importing decorators.py — respects layer-discipline guards test_guards_sidecar_imports / assembly import DAG). AST-based, positive+negative meta-tests. Depends on Phase 1a, 1c, 1d.
design:
## Core Invariant
Every LLM-mode dispatch class exposes BOTH a sync `execute` AND an async `aexecute` (with `aexecute` being `async def`), and every async twin is defined in the SAME module as its sync counterpart — so no PR can silently reintroduce a sync-only execution path (the H2 silent-failure mode).

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW FILE `tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py`, pure-AST (zero `re` → auto-exempt from the regex-slip meta-guard), mirroring tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py structure (module-level `ast.parse` of the target source, a small collector, per-class asserts, a not-vacuous slip meta-test).

2. GUARD A — dual-path dispatch completeness.
   - Detector: parse src/neograph/_dispatch.py; a "dispatch class" = any top-level ClassDef whose body defines a method named `execute`. This enrolls ModeDispatch (Protocol) + ScriptedDispatch + ThinkDispatch + ToolDispatch and excludes NodeInput/NodeOutput. Do NOT key on the `*Dispatch` suffix.
   - Assertion: every dispatch class also defines `aexecute`, AND its `aexecute` node is `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (blocks a sync stub), AND `execute` is a plain `def` (`ast.FunctionDef`).
   - Sanity assert: the detected dispatch-class set on today's source == {ModeDispatch, ScriptedDispatch, ThinkDispatch, ToolDispatch} (catches detector drift / a future non-dispatch class sprouting an execute).
   - Meta-tests (mandatory, mirror test_delegation_detector_is_not_vacuous):
       * POSITIVE: synthetic `class X: def execute(...); async def aexecute(...)` → detector treats X as a dispatch and passes.
       * NEGATIVE 1: synthetic `class X: def execute(...)` (no aexecute) → flagged.
       * NEGATIVE 2: synthetic `class X: def execute(...); def aexecute(...)` (sync aexecute) → flagged.
       * EXCLUSION: synthetic class with only a `value` property → NOT a dispatch (not flagged).

3. GUARD B — async-twin co-location, scoped to the gap ONLY.
   - Delegate the 4 LLM-vertical twins to test_guards_llm_runtime.py ALLOWED_NAMES (document this in the docstring; do NOT re-assert them).
   - Assert same-module co-location for the twins NOT covered by ALLOWED_NAMES, as a `{module: [(sync, async), ...]}` table:
       _execute.py: (_execute_node, _aexecute_node)
       _tool_loop.py: (invoke_with_tools, ainvoke_with_tools)
       runner.py: (run, arun), (_has_existing_checkpoint, _ahas_existing_checkpoint), (_verify_checkpoint_schema, _averify_checkpoint_schema), (_auto_resume_from_divergence, _aauto_resume_from_divergence)
       factory.py: (_make_raw_wrapper, _make_araw_wrapper)
     For each pair: both names are top-level defs in that module's AST (async one is AsyncFunctionDef). A twin migrating to an async-only module fails this.
   - Meta-tests: POSITIVE (both defs present in one synthetic module → passes); NEGATIVE (async twin missing / moved to a second synthetic module → flagged).
   - Do NOT add a new decorators-import-DAG guard: no async-only module exists (Phase 1a-1f co-located every twin), so there is nothing to police; the existing sidecar/import guards remain sufficient. Note this decision in the file docstring.

4. Run `pytest tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py -q` (expect all green — this is a lock over already-correct 1a-1f code, not a red TDD test). Also run tests/test_guards_meta.py to confirm the new file trips no regex-slip / near-duplicate discipline.

## Findings (Phase 1g research — neograph-46vu.2)

### State after 1a-1f (verified)
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py: ModeDispatch Protocol (lines 80-102) declares BOTH `execute` (sync, l.88) and `aexecute` (`async def`, l.96). All 3 concrete dispatch classes define both:
  - ScriptedDispatch: execute l.116, aexecute l.127 (isawaitable-at-call-boundary async)
  - ThinkDispatch: execute l.156, aexecute l.186 (awaits _llm.ainvoke_structured)
  - ToolDispatch: execute l.265, aexecute l.276 (awaits _tool_loop.ainvoke_with_tools)
  Dual-path invariant currently HOLDS; guard should be TDD-green on write (this is a lock, not a red test — unlike Phase 0's test_guards_async_fakes which shipped red).

### GUARD A detection rule (robust, NOT name-based)
A "dispatch class" = any top-level ClassDef in _dispatch.py whose body defines a method named `execute`. This catches the ModeDispatch Protocol AND the 3 concrete classes, and EXCLUDES NodeInput/NodeOutput (they only have a `value` @property, no execute). Do NOT key on the `*Dispatch` suffix — a rename would silently disable the guard, and the Protocol is named `ModeDispatch` (also ends in Dispatch but is the Protocol, not a concrete class). Keying on presence-of-`execute` is the invariant of BEING a dispatch: a future 4th mode class must define execute, so it is auto-enrolled; if it adds execute but forgets aexecute → guard FAILS (exactly the H2 sync-only reintroduction). Strengthen: assert aexecute is `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (blocks a sync `def aexecute` stub) and execute is a plain `def`.

### GUARD B — redundancy analysis (scope precisely, do NOT duplicate)

title: Phase 3 — MCP client (per-step bind, stateless auth, compile-time lint)
description:
Make neograph a first-class MCP client. Reuses Tool specs (MCP tools are not special); mcp_servers= typed config + factory transport; mcp_tool('server','tool',budget=) per-step named subset = the lintable per-step filter; mandatory namespacing server.tool; the LINTER validates bindings at compile time (the differentiator — no other MCP client does this).

Binding obeys the TWO-LIFETIME rule (§5/H1): provider/factory across checkpoints; live MCP session CACHED per (process,loop) within a run and invalidated on resume (NOT open-initialize-call-dispose per tools/call — that breaks stateful sessions and adds per-call handshake latency). Discovery decoupled from live session; linter holds no runtime session.

MCP requires arun() (review M4): async does not 'remove' the sync bridge, it requires the async driver; lint an MCP tool under a run()-driven graph. Session disposed at run end or on cancellation (H3).

Depends on Phase 1. Parallelizable with Phase 2 (review M5). Later: resources/prompts/sampling (MVP tools-only). Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.3. MCP landscape: ox-troubleshooting-demo/docs/research/mcp-client-landscape.md.

Only remaining child is neograph-w74k.3.1 (token-provider auth FR, unchanged/separate) — epic stays open pending it. Docs follow-up: neograph-04dz.

title: FR — per-run MCP identity via token-provider hook (on-behalf-of, no passthrough)
description:
config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] = provider(run_ctx) -> bearer JWT; static headers= stays the default, provider is the per-run escape hatch. On-behalf-of: neograph CARRIES identity, never DECIDES (ADR-0009; enforcement is the tool server's Permify check).

Cadence (review M2): provider invoked once per run, cached for the run, RE-MINTED on resume (fresh process -> cache miss). Cache lives OUTSIDE checkpoint state (live secret, never persisted). Provider may be async (blocking broker must not stall the loop); sync provider via threadpool.

Audience binding (review H4): DECLARED client-side, ENFORCED server-side. The audience URI is what the provider is expected to bind (RFC 8707); the tool server validates aud on receipt. neograph does NOT parse the token (carries-not-decides). No verbatim upstream-token forwarding. HTTP->bearer; stdio->env (no OAuth).

Guards: token never enters checkpoint state, schema fingerprint, OR any log / ToolInteraction (review L2); a structural guard that neograph never parses token contents.

Verification: integration — two run-context identities, assert each tools/call carried the correct per-identity token at a stub server, no-auth default path unaffected. E2E — one tool call resolves different server-side authz under two operators.

Depends on Phase 3 (neograph-w74k.3). Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.3.1.
design:
## Core Invariant
neograph CARRIES per-run identity and never DECIDES it: an async tool factory on the arun() path reads config['configurable'] and returns per-run tools whose per-request auth is minted by the ecosystem's httpx.Auth — neograph owns NO MCP session, parses NO token, and never lets a token reach checkpoint state, schema fingerprint, log, or ToolInteraction.

## Implementation Plan (refined 2026-07-06 per architect review)

1. **Twin the ONE sync factory line, don't rebuild the loop.** In src/neograph/_tool_loop.py factor the tool-instantiation loop (L266-275) out of _prepare_tool_loop into a shared helper, then add an async twin (_aprepare_tool_loop) co-located in the SAME module. Sync path fail-loud ORDER MATTERS (LOW-4): first `if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(factory): raise ...` BEFORE calling (avoids creating an un-awaited coroutine and re-emitting the 'coroutine never awaited' RuntimeWarning); only if not a coroutine function, call `result = factory(config, tc)` then `if inspect.isawaitable(result): raise ...`. Both raises use ConfigurationError.build (LOW-3: NOT ExecutionError — driver/config mismatch, convergent design-doc §3 + exemplar _agent_cycle.py:352 + research) with the 4-field shape: expected='an async driver (arun())', found='sync run() driving an async tool factory', hint=..., node=node.name. Async path: `inst = factory(config, tc); inst = await inst if inspect.isawaitable(inst) else inst`.

2. **Route the 3 async bodies through an async prep.** Add _abuild_turn_prep in _agent_cycle.py (async twin of _build_turn_prep, L96) that awaits _aprepare_tool_loop; wire aagent_body/atools_body/aparse_body (L272/375/444) to it. Leave the 3 sync bodies on the sync prep unchanged. Node-level RunnableLambda(sync, afunc=async) twin at _wiring.py:755-757 already selects by driver — no wiring change.

3. **Fix lint introspection (item 2), reuse existing kind.** In src/neograph/lint.py _resolve_tool_object (L556) / _check_async_only_tools (L443): if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(factory) BEFORE calling factory({}, spec.config), emit the EXISTING LintIssue kind 'tool_requires_async_driver' (L470) without invoking. Silences the current 'coroutine never awaited' RuntimeWarning. Extend tests/test_lint_mcp.py with an async-factory fixture (assert no RuntimeWarning).

4. **Extend GUARD B TWIN_TABLE — co-location alone does NOT lock the new twins (MEDIUM-1).** GUARD B (tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py:293-308) is TABLE-DRIVEN and checks only what TWIN_TABLE names. Add: _tool_loop.py list += ('_prepare_tool_loop','_aprepare_tool_loop'); NEW key '_agent_cycle.py': [('_build_turn_prep','_abuild_turn_prep')]. Without these rows the anti-band-aid 'no async-only module' clause is UNENFORCEABLE for exactly these twins.

5. **Three NEW guards (item 3) — a+b as ONE runtime-sentinel test, not vacuous AST (MEDIUM-2).**
   - Guards (a) token-never-in-checkpoint/fingerprint/log/ToolInteraction AND (b) never-passthrough: ONE runtime-sentinel test. Inject a known token sentinel via a stub httpx.Auth; run() AND arun() a tool-bearing agent with a real (file-backed) checkpointer; assert the sentinel string appears in NONE of: the checkpoint state dump, the _neo schema fingerprint, captured structlog output, ToolInteraction.args/result. The ToolInteraction/outbound-args assertion doubles as never-passthrough (sentinel must not reappear verbatim in outbound tool args). This avoids the codebase's vacuous-guard hazard (a NEGATIVE-about-runtime-values assertion has no AST signature).
   - Guard (c) neograph contains NO MCP session-lifecycle code: structural grep — assert no 'client.session('/persistent-session ownership / ClientSession under src/neograph/ (locks the kill-nmb2 verdict). Include a non-vacuity meta-assertion (the grep matches a planted positive control).

6. **6-cell tests (item 4), copy tests/test_async_dual_path.py:79 shape.** 3 API surfaces (@node(tools=) / declarative Node(tools=) / programmatic Node()|Modifier) × run/arun via conftest.py:66 run_driver fixture. Explicitly (LOW-5): fail-loud-under-run() asserted on ALL 3 SYNC surface cells (not once) with the 3 async cells succeeding — shared async-factory fixture. Plus integration: two run-context identities each carry the correct per-identity token at a stub httpx.Auth/stub server; no-auth default path unaffected.

7. **Zero new config surface, zero new publics.** Async factory reads config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] (or any consumer-chosen key) and returns MultiServerMCPClient tools carrying auth: httpx.Auth. The optional mcp_tool_factory() convenience + docs/website MCP recipe are a SEPARATE optional ticket, not this atom. mcp>=1.28 deprecates transport-level headers=/auth= — auth belongs on httpx.AsyncClient; adapter 0.3.0 already does this.

## Anti-band-aid clause
Do NOT resurrect the deleted invoke_with_tools monolith, do NOT add an async-only module (GUARD B rows in Step 4 enforce this), do NOT add @node-layer logic to _tool_loop.py/lint.py beyond the factory-await twin, do NOT cache the live tool/session across supersteps (re-mint per superstep from fresh config IS the resume-correct behavior). Guards (a)+(b) must be a runtime-sentinel test, never a signature-free AST assertion.
notes:
BLOCKED (found 2026-07-04): not implementable as specified. The token-provider hook needs neograph to OWN the MCP session lifecycle so it can stamp/re-mint Authorization: Bearer per tools/call. Today neograph does not create MCP sessions (Phase 3 re-scoped mcp_servers=/session-factory out); users pass pre-built BaseTools in tools= with the session captured in the tool closure -> no hook point. Now depends on neograph-nmb2 (neograph-owned MCP session + mcp_servers= config). Re-run once nmb2 lands. See design 6.3.1.
RE-SCOPE 2026-07-05 (per the architect review that killed prerequisite nmb2 — docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md). The FR is satisfied by ONE neograph change plus ecosystem-native auth. Scope:

1. ASYNC TOOL FACTORIES on the arun() path: twin the single sync-only site (_tool_loop.py ~L275 factory(config, tool_spec.config) in shared prep) — async prep awaits coroutine factories; sync run() path FAILS LOUD with a clear async-factory-requires-arun ExecutionError (khff pattern, mirroring the async-only-tool error at _agent_cycle.py:352). Zero new config surface: an async factory reads config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] (or any key the consumer chooses) and returns per-run tools built with MultiServerMCPClient connections carrying auth: httpx.Auth — per-request token minting is then NATIVE (httpx.Auth.auth_flow per request; SDK ships OAuthClientProvider/ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider/PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider). Version note for docs/example: mcp 1.28.x deprecates transport-level headers=/auth= — auth belongs on httpx.AsyncClient; adapter 0.3.0 already does this correctly.
2. LINT: classify a coroutine factory as tool_requires_async_driver WITHOUT calling it (current lint would misintrospect the returned coroutine — fix the introspection).
3. GUARDS (cheap, still required by the original FR): token-never-in-checkpoint/fingerprint/log guard; never-passthrough structural guard; NEW guard asserting neograph contains NO MCP session-lifecycle code (no client.session()/persistent ownership in src/) — locks the review verdict against future drift.
4. TESTS: 6-cell (factory reachable from @node/declarative/programmatic x run/arun); integration: two identities -> correct per-identity token observed at a stub server; no-auth path unaffected; fail-loud on run(); lint fixture.
5. OPTIONAL sugar, file separately if wanted (NOT a blocker): documented recipe or tiny mcp_tool_factory(server_config, auth=provider) convenience wrapping MultiServerMCPClient().get_tools() — owns NO session.
6. DOCS: the on-behalf-of recipe on the MCP page; latency note (stateless = ~3 POSTs/call vs 1 on a consumer-managed persistent session — consumer's opt-in via the adapter, not neograph's).

Two-lifetime rule status: across-checkpoint half ALREADY satisfied (factories re-invoked every superstep, config read fresh — resume re-mints automatically); within-run caching is a consumer latency option via the adapter. Audience binding: declared client-side in the provider config, enforced server-side — unchanged from the original FR.
## Findings (research neograph-0u4l.2, 2026-07-06)

### REUSE TARGETS (do not rebuild)
- **The single sync-only factory site**: `src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:275` inside `_prepare_tool_loop` — `tool_instances[tool_spec.name] = factory(config, tool_spec.config)`. This is THE one un-twinned line the re-scope names. `_prepare_tool_loop` (L210-290) is shared VERBATIM by sync and async paths. The fix: factor tool-instantiation into a helper OR add `_aprepare_tool_loop` twin so the async path can await coroutine factories; sync path fails loud on a coroutine factory.
- **Fail-loud exemplar to mirror**: `src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:352-363` — on `NotImplementedError` from `tool_fn.invoke`, raises `ConfigurationError.build(msg, expected=..., found=..., hint=..., node=node.name)`. NOTE: this is `ConfigurationError.build`, NOT `ExecutionError` (the re-scope prose says 'ExecutionError' but design doc §3 L126 correctly says ConfigurationError). Mirror the ConfigurationError.build 4-field shape for 'async-factory-requires-arun'.
- **is_async_only_tool**: `src/neograph/tool.py:67` — the existing runtime introspection for async-only *tool objects* (StructuredTool coroutine-only / BaseTool _arun-only). Distinct from the NEW need: detecting async *factories* (coroutine functions) BEFORE calling.

### Call graph (both drivers converge on the same prep)
- `_wiring._add_agent_cycle` (`src/neograph/_wiring.py:728-757`) registers `RunnableLambda(agent_sync, afunc=agent_async)` etc. LangGraph picks the async twin under `arun()`. So the node-level twin ALREADY exists.
- Sync bodies `tools_body`/`agent_body`/`parse_body` and async bodies `atools_body`(L375)/`aagent_body`(L272)/`aparse_body`(L444) ALL call the SAME sync `_build_turn_prep` (`_agent_cycle.py:96-134`) which calls `_prepare_tool_loop`. The async bodies already await `caller.ainvoke`/`tool_fn.ainvoke` — only the factory that BUILDS the tool is still sync. So the change is: add an async `_abuild_turn_prep` (awaits `_aprepare_tool_loop`) called by the 3 async bodies; the 3 sync bodies keep the sync prep.
- The monolithic `invoke_with_tools`/`ainvoke_with_tools` are GONE (deleted in m6d3.3, f81ff12); only docstring references remain in _tool_loop.py. The agent-cycle is the ONLY tool-loop path. Do not resurrect the monolith.

### Item 2 — lint introspection fix

Four independently-shippable stages, each catching a drift class the previous cannot: A manifest+guard (any public-surface delta fails pytest), B remark validation (prose refs to dead/renamed symbols, dead anchors, zero page edits), C generated reference sections (signature/field-table drift), D snippet testing (snippets that resolve but no longer run). title: Compiler drops edges: nodes after first chain terminate at __end__
description:
## Bug Summary

The NeoGraph compiler fails to wire dependency edges between nodes when constructing a LangGraph StateGraph. Only the first linear chain of nodes gets connected -- all subsequent nodes that depend on earlier outputs are disconnected and the graph terminates prematurely at __end__.

## Reproduction

Minimal example with 3 sequential nodes where step_b depends on step_a and step_c depends on step_b (via parameter names matching function names):

Expected edges: __start__ -> step-a -> step-b -> step-c -> __end__
Actual edges: __start__ -> step-a -> __end__

step_b and step_c are compiled as graph nodes but have no incoming edges.

## Real-world impact

The UC derivation pipeline in piarch has 19 nodes across 4 phases. When compiled, only the first 3 nodes execute (read-graph-context -> read-draft -> research-comparable -> __end__). The remaining 16 nodes (write-si Oracle x3, validate, lint, review, write-overview Oracle x3, write-mss, brainstorm-extensions, write-extensions Each, derive-business-rules Each, validate-completeness Operator, lint-artifacts, register-and-activate, create-downstream-nodes, impact-cascade) have no incoming edges.

The RW ingestion pipeline (8 nodes) has the same bug -- only first 3 nodes connected.

## Root cause hypothesis

The compiler resolves dependencies from function parameter names (e.g. def step_b(step_a: dict) means step_b depends on step_a). Either the dependency resolver only processes the first node outputs and stops, or the edge builder only connects the linear chain from __start__ and marks everything else as terminal.

## Environment

neograph 0.2.0.dev0, Python 3.12, LangGraph latest, macOS Darwin 25.2.0

## Severity

P0 blocker -- no multi-node construct can execute beyond the first chain. Makes NeoGraph unusable for any real pipeline.
design:
## Root Cause
_wire_oracle and _wire_each in compiler.py call graph.add_conditional_edges(prev_node, router) without a path_map argument. The router functions return Send() objects (not string node names). LangGraph's get_graph() requires either type hints on the router return value or a path_map to determine static edge targets. Without these, the visualization shows source -> __end__ and drops all downstream edges.

## Fix Approach
Pass path_map=[gen_name] to add_conditional_edges in _wire_oracle (line ~403) and path_map=[fan_name] in _wire_each (line ~464). This tells LangGraph what nodes the Send() dispatches target, making the edges visible in get_graph().
notes:
## Update: get_graph() display bug, NOT execution bug

The execution actually works correctly. The pipeline ran through 14+ nodes including Oracle parallel (x3), merge, Each fan-out (x18 extensions). The get_graph().edges output is misleading — it shows only 4 edges, but the actual LangGraph execution correctly follows all dependency chains.

The pipeline failed at write-extensions because the LLM returned wrong schema (file_content instead of ExtensionHandling fields) — a prompt/model issue, not a compiler issue.

Downgrade from P0 to P3: get_graph() visualization is inaccurate but execution works.
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py::TestGetGraphEdges::test_oracle_edges_visible_in_get_graph and test_each_edges_visible_in_get_graph
- Root cause: _wire_oracle and _wire_each call add_conditional_edges(source, router) without path_map. LangGraph's get_graph() cannot resolve Send() targets statically, so it shows source -> __end__ and drops all downstream edges.

title: Guard integrity: make IR-field-write scanner exhaustive (or honest) + clarify sibling scanner
description:
From code review of 185c322 (synthesis.md MED-01 + DRY-05). The structural guard TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter is the enforcement of the epic's core invariant ('normalize_ir is the only assembly-time writer of fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type'). Two issues:

## MED-01 (the real one): scanner claims exhaustiveness it doesn't have
tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter._scan_ir_field_writes detects only attribute-assign, subscript-assign, dict-literal key, and setattr/__setattr__. Reproduced misses (all return empty set):
- node.fan_out_param += x            (ast.AugAssign)
- node.fan_out_param: str = x        (ast.AnnAssign, instance target)
- node.fan_out_param, y = a, b       (tuple-unpack target)
- node.model_copy(update=dict(fan_out_param=x))   (dict() kwarg form)
The docstring says it scans 'EVERY syntactic form'. The self-test test_scanner_detects_every_write_form only feeds the 4 handled forms, so it passes by construction and falsely implies exhaustiveness. The realistic regression vector among the misses is the dict()-kwarg model_copy idiom.

Fix (preferred): extend _scan_ir_field_writes to cover ast.AugAssign, ast.AnnAssign (instance attribute targets only — NOT class-body field declarations), tuple/list assignment targets, and dict(...) keyword-arg calls; ADD each new form to the mutation self-test so the self-test actually proves coverage. Acceptable alternative: downgrade the docstring from 'EVERY syntactic form' to the explicit enumerated list. Prefer extending.

## DRY-05 (cleanup): disambiguate the two AST scanners
TestNoNodeMutationInAssembly (test_structural_guards.py ~1328) and the new _scan_ir_field_writes overlap on field names but enforce DIFFERENT invariants (in-place-mutation-only-in-builder vs IR-field-written-only-at-sanctioned-sites). No parallel-update hazard. Action: add a one-line docstring note to TestNoNodeMutationInAssembly clarifying it is 'in-place attribute mutation only' and is NOT the IR-field-write authority (that is TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter), so a future reader doesn't conflate them.

## Acceptance
- Scanner detects all four currently-missed forms (add a repro/parametrized test), OR docstring no longer claims exhaustiveness.
- Self-test exercises every form the scanner claims to support.
- TestNoNodeMutationInAssembly docstring disambiguated.
- make quality green.

## Prep
- Files to modify: tests/test_structural_guards.py only (the _scan_ir_field_writes classmethod, its self-test test_scanner_detects_every_write_form, the docstring; + TestNoNodeMutationInAssembly docstring note for DRY-05).
- Approach: factor a _check_target(target) helper that recurses Attribute/Subscript/Tuple/List elts; call it from ast.Assign.targets, ast.AugAssign.target, ast.AnnAssign.target. CRITICAL: ignore bare ast.Name targets in AnnAssign so class-body field declarations (node.py 'fan_out_param: str | None = None', '_NORMALIZERS: list[...] = [...]') do NOT false-positive. Add dict() keyword-arg detection (ast.Call func Name 'dict', kw.arg in IR_FIELDS). Update self-test to feed all forms incl. AugAssign/AnnAssign/tuple/dict(). Update docstring to enumerate honestly. Add one-line note to TestNoNodeMutationInAssembly clarifying it is in-place-attr-mutation-only, not the IR-write authority.

title: gate_tools_when: deny is silently ignored — the gated tool runs anyway (approval checkpoint, not a gate)
description:
Found by independent verification of neograph-m6d3.4 (commit 43b5605). The gate node pauses correctly BEFORE the tools superstep (approve-before-side-effects holds, keystone green 4 ways), but the resume value is written to human_feedback (_wiring.py:781) and NEVER READ: grep shows zero routing consumers of HUMAN_FEEDBACK in src, and _wiring.py:794 adds an UNCONDITIONAL gate -> tools edge. Consequence: a user who resumes with a deny/reject payload gets the tool executed anyway. That is WORSE than no gate — it manufactures a false sense of a safety control. No deny test exists because deny is not implemented.

INVARIANT: a human gate that accepts a decision must honor the decision — approve routes to tools; deny must NOT execute the pending tool calls and must feed a denial back to the agent so the loop can continue reasoning (ToolMessage per pending tool_call, standard LangGraph review-tool-calls pattern), not crash or hang.

SCOPE (design decision first, then TDD): (1) define the resume contract — suggested {approved: bool, reason?: str} minimum; document whether edit-args is in scope or explicitly deferred; (2) gate -> conditional edge reading the resume decision: approve -> {node}__tools; deny -> back to {node}__agent with denial ToolMessages appended to neo_agent_messages so the LLM sees why; (3) failing tests FIRST: deny -> tool counter stays 0 AND the agent receives the denial and produces a final answer; approve path unchanged; both drivers; (4) docs: human-in-the-loop.mdx currently says approve-before-side-effects (accurate) — extend with the deny contract when built; until then the page must not imply deny works.

ANTI-BAND-AID: no in-body if-approved check inside the tools node (invisible to the checkpointer, wrong layer) — the decision belongs in Layer-1 topology (conditional edge), same as the rest of the agent cycle. Cite docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md.
design:
## Root Cause
_add_agent_cycle (_wiring.py:766-794) inserts a gate node on the router's tools arm. The gate interrupts BEFORE the tools superstep (approve-before-side-effects holds), and on resume writes the human decision to StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK. But nothing reads HUMAN_FEEDBACK for routing — line 794 is an unconditional edge gate_name -> names.tools. Deny is never implemented, so the tool always runs after resume.

## Fix Approach (minimal, Layer-1 topology)
Resume contract: {approved: bool, reason?: str} minimum. Edit-args EXPLICITLY DEFERRED (document as out of scope).

1. Replace the unconditional gate -> tools edge with a conditional edge:
   graph.add_conditional_edges(gate_name, gate_decision_router, path_map=[names.tools, names.agent])
   where gate_decision_router reads the resume decision from state: approved truthy -> names.tools; deny -> names.agent.
2. On DENY, append one denial ToolMessage per pending tool_call to neo_agent_messages_{field} so the LLM sees the rejection and can finalize (standard LangGraph review-tool-calls pattern). The pending tool_calls are on the last AIMessage in the messages channel. This synthesis belongs in the agent cycle (where msgs_key + pending tool_calls live), mirroring _agent_cycle._limit_messages — NOT an in-body if-approved check in the tools node (anti-band-aid; cite docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md).
3. Gate body must WRITE the decision to a routable channel (reuse HUMAN_FEEDBACK) AND, when deny, emit the denial ToolMessages on msgs_key. Because the gate needs msgs_key/field knowledge, build it via make_agent_cycle_bodies (agent-cycle layer) rather than inlining channel names in _wiring.py.

## Layer discipline
Decision-reading for routing = Layer-1 conditional edge (topology). Denial-message synthesis = Layer-2 agent-cycle body. No if-approved check inside the tools node body.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_tool_gating.py::TestToolGatingDenyKeystone::test_deny_does_not_run_tool_and_agent_finalizes (4 params: {run,arun} x {node,programmatic})
- All 4 FAIL: on resume with {approved: False}, side-effecting 'record' tool ran 1x (expected 0). 'DENY VIOLATION'.
- Root cause: the tool-gate's resume decision is written to HUMAN_FEEDBACK (_wiring.py:781) but never read for routing; _wiring.py:794 adds an UNCONDITIONAL gate -> {node}__tools edge, so any resume value (approve OR deny) falls through to the tools superstep and executes the pending tool.
## Trace-similar (same bug pattern elsewhere?)
Pattern category: a decision-bearing interrupt whose resume value is written to StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK but never READ for routing, followed by an unconditional downstream edge.

Two interrupt sites write HUMAN_FEEDBACK; NEITHER is read for routing anywhere in src (grep: zero routing consumers):
1. _wiring.py:781 — tool-gate (THIS bug, whq0). Contract IS to gate tool execution on the decision -> unconditional gate->tools edge is a real bug.
2. _wiring.py:823 — _add_operator_check (Operator modifier). Contract per modifiers.py:484 is 'pause graph for human review' = acknowledge-and-continue; the compiler continues linearly (compiler.py:487,544) regardless of decision. Operator does NOT promise to route on the decision, and human_feedback remains readable on the state bus for downstream nodes. So NOT the same bug — but it shares the write-and-never-read shape and would silently ignore a {approved: False} if a user expected it to skip. Noted, not filed: Operator's approve/deny semantics are a separate design question, out of scope for whq0.

No other unconditional-edge-after-decision-interrupt instances. whq0 is the only site where the gate's stated purpose (gate tool side effects) is contradicted by the topology.
## Codebase Disease Scan (whq0)

Pattern: a decision-bearing interrupt() whose resume value must gate downstream routing, but is followed by an UNCONDITIONAL edge that runs the gated work regardless of the decision.
Scan command: grep -rn 'interrupt(' src/neograph/ && grep -rn 'add_edge|add_conditional_edges' src/neograph/_wiring.py
Method: SYNTACTIC (exact-form enumeration of interrupt sites + their outgoing edges) — no fan-out needed.
Total instances found: 1 (the motivating site)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _wiring.py:780->794 | gate interrupt + unconditional gate->tools edge | MIGRATE | THE bug (whq0). Fix replaces 794 with a conditional edge reading the decision. |
| 2 | _wiring.py:822->827 (_add_operator_check) | operator interrupt + linear continuation | ALLOWLIST | Operator contract (modifiers.py:484) is pause-for-review = acknowledge-and-continue, NOT gate. Decision remains readable on the state bus (human_feedback). Not a gate promise -> not the disease. |
| 3 | hitl.py:56 (ask_human) | interrupt() passthrough inside a Layer-2 tool | ALLOWLIST | Resume value is returned to tool code (typed via resume_model), not a topology routing decision. N/A to this disease. |

Conclusion: the fix addresses the single MIGRATE instance. No other sites need the conditional-edge treatment.
## Architect Review (fix design)

1. Root cause correctness — LOW (correct). Verified: HUMAN_FEEDBACK written at _wiring.py:781, zero routing readers in src, unconditional edge at 794. Reproduction fails exactly as predicted (tool runs 1x on deny).

2. Fix minimality — LOW. Replacing one unconditional edge with a conditional edge + a deny message-emit is the minimal change. No IR/schema change; HUMAN_FEEDBACK channel already exists.

3. Architecture compliance — LOW. Matches three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md: routing decision = Layer-1 topology (conditional edge); interrupt already sits at a checkpointer-visible boundary node (sec 1.2 purity test); denial ToolMessage synthesis is node-boundary output built in the agent-cycle layer where msgs_key lives. No in-body if-approved check in the tools node.

4. Regression risk — LOW/MEDIUM. Approve path: existing TestToolGatingKeystone resumes {approved: True} and must stay green (conditional edge routes approved->tools). Verify no-gate path (else branch, line 795-799) is untouched. Operator/ask_human paths untouched.

5. FINDING (MEDIUM) — router must read a FRESH per-visit decision, NOT a persistent stale channel. HUMAN_FEEDBACK is a single overwritten channel; a multi-turn agent whose gate fires on turn 1 (approve) then does NOT fire on turn 3 would leave a stale 'approved' in HUMAN_FEEDBACK. The gate router must distinguish three cases on EACH visit: (a) gate fired + denied -> route to agent (deny msgs appended); (b) gate fired + approved -> route to tools; (c) gate condition falsy / did not fire -> route to tools (proceed). Recommend the gate body emit an explicit per-visit routing signal (or the router key off freshly-appended deny ToolMessages) rather than reading a persistent HUMAN_FEEDBACK that can go stale across turns. The fix atom MUST handle case (c) and the stale-across-turns case.

6. FINDING (MEDIUM) — fail-closed default. A gate is a SAFETY control: any resume value that is not explicitly {approved: True} (missing key, non-dict, malformed) should be treated as DENY, not approve. Make the approved-check explicit and fail-closed.

7. Test coverage — LOW/MEDIUM. Reproduction covers deny keystone (tool==0 + finalize) x {run,arun} x {node,programmatic}. ## Triage decision
Verdict: PROCEED to fix (no HIGH, no NEEDS_USER_INPUT). Two MEDIUM findings are concrete implementation requirements, not design ambiguities requiring human direction, so NOT NEEDS_REFINEMENT/NEEDS_USER_INPUT. Folded into the fix contract below. Proceeding to atom .7 (fix).

## Fix must-address (from review, binding on the fix atom)

title: Typed MCP tool results on the agent path: output_model= on neograph_mcp factories
description:
## What
Add `output_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None` (+ `parse=`) to `mcp_tool_factory` / `mcp_tool_factories` (dict form `output_models=`). When declared, the factory wraps the discovered adapter tool so the TOOL RESULT IS the rehydrated Pydantic model: the adapter coroutine returns `(content, artifact)` under response_format='content_and_artifact'; take `artifact['structured_content']` (MCPToolArtifact is a TypedDict — use .get, not getattr), `output_model.model_validate` it (via `parse` if given), return the model, and reset response_format='content' on the copied tool. Mirrors `resource_reader(output_model=, parse=)` — same layer, same names.

## Why (user direction 2026-07-10 — THE primary deliverable of the MCP typed-results design, not an optional follow-up)
The agent-bound MCP path structurally DROPS structuredContent today: neograph's tool loop invokes with plain args (_agent_cycle.py:459) and langchain attaches the artifact only on the ToolCall->ToolMessage path. So typed_result is a raw content-block list, the next ReAct turn's ToolMessage gets str(list-of-dicts), and demos compensate with shortcuts (example 23's _parse_mcp_json). Per MCP spec 2025-06-18 the text block accompanying structuredContent is a BACKWARDS-COMPAT MIRROR — a structured-aware client must treat structuredContent as the single source of truth, not consume both. The framework mechanism already exists: _render_tool_result_for_llm (_tool_loop.py:50) renders Pydantic-model results via renderer/describe_value (BAML-style) into the ToolMessage — it just never receives a model on the MCP path. PROBED end-to-end 2026-07-10: wrapped crm_search -> ainvoke returns the model -> _render_tool_result_for_llm emits the typed block. ZERO core changes; src/neograph stays MCP-free (nmb2).

Full design: docs/design/mcp-session-api-2plcl-2026-07-10.md §4bis (rejected variants: core Tool spec output=, outputSchema-derived auto-models, raw-dict default — see doc).

## Semantics
- output_model declared + structuredContent present -> model (parse= hook optional); ValidationError propagates untouched.
- output_model declared + NO structuredContent -> typed error naming the tool and the server-annotation fix.
- isError=True -> adapter's existing error path, unchanged.
- No output_model -> behavior unchanged (content blocks); type channel is opt-in by declaration.
- Naming alignment battery-wide: `output_model=` on factory, factories, AND McpSession.call (supersedes the session design's earlier `output=`).

## Demos de-shortcut (same bead)
Example 23 beat 5: declare output_model on reader factories, DELETE _parse_mcp_json, assert model attributes. Example 25: gateway-renamed tool declares output_model. Demo server already emits structuredContent (crm_search returns CrmSearchResult — landed 2026-07-10).

## Verification — integration & E2E only
Integration (tests/test_mcp_battery.py, @requires_mcp): factory with output_model -> awaited tool ainvoke returns the model instance; missing-structuredContent (get_deal + output_model) -> typed error; ValidationError propagates. E2E: agent run via compile()+arun() — assert ToolInteraction.typed_result IS the model AND the ToolMessage content in message history is the describe_value rendering (not a JSON/repr of blocks). Examples harness green after 23/25 de-shortcut.

## Acceptance
- output_model= public on both factories (+ output_models dict form), documented; zero src/neograph changes; session-ownership guard green.
- Example 23 has no _parse_mcp_json; typed_result carries models.
- Website MCP pages updated (typed results section: structuredContent as source of truth, BAML rendering into the next turn).
design:
## Core Invariant
The MCP typed-result channel is opt-in-by-declaration and lives ENTIRELY in the neograph_mcp battery package: declaring output_model= makes the wrapped adapter tool return the rehydrated Pydantic model as the tool result, and every downstream mechanism (ToolInteraction.typed_result, _render_tool_result_for_llm BAML rendering) already handles a model with ZERO changes to src/neograph.

## Implementation Plan (refined per architect review neograph-8w6a9.4/.12)

1. EXTEND src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:_make_tool_factory with output_model: type[BaseModel]|None=None, parse: Callable[[dict],BaseModel]|None=None. At the END of the _factory closure (AFTER _inject_stdio_token :208-209 and rename :210-211, BEFORE return :212), when output_model is set, wrap:
     orig = tool.coroutine
     async def wrapped(**kw):
         content, artifact = await orig(**kw)   # isError RAISES here (see invariant) — propagates, NOT caught
         sc = artifact.get('structured_content') if artifact else None
         if sc is None:
             raise ValueError(\"MCP tool '<tool_name>' declared output_model=<Name> but the server returned no structuredContent — the server tool likely has a bare '-> dict'/'-> list' annotation; use '-> dict[str, Any]' or a Pydantic return type.\")
         return parse(sc) if parse else output_model.model_validate(sc)
     tool = tool.model_copy(update={'coroutine': wrapped, 'response_format': 'content'})
   Let ValidationError propagate untouched (it IS the type-mismatch signal).

   isError MECHANISM (corrected — the plan's earlier tuple-return rationale was WRONG): against langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:258-283, a SERVER isError=True does NOT return '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' — it RAISES _MCPToolExecutionError (ToolException subclass, raise :274) from inside orig(). The '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' returns at :260-265 fire ONLY for INTERCEPTOR-returned messages, which the battery NEVER wires. Therefore:
   - NO isError guard is needed: the ONLY None-artifact case the wrapper ever sees is a genuine missing-structuredContent (a bare -> dict/list server annotation). The interceptor ToolMessage/Command path is dead-for-battery (document this caveat in the wrapper; do not add a branch for it).
   - LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT (state it in the code comment): model_copy(update={coroutine, response_format:'content'}) PRESERVES handle_tool_errors (True), and the wrapper MUST let the _MCPToolExecutionError PROPAGATE — do NOT try/except-convert it. langchain's arun catches the ToolException via the preserved handle_tool_errors and surfaces it as a self-correcting error ToolMessage (the adapter-native path). A catch here would break that.

2. THREAD the params through the two public delegators: mcp_tool_factory gains output_model=/parse= (pass straight down). mcp_tool_factories gains output_models: dict[str,type[BaseModel]]|None and parses: dict[str,Callable]|None (keyed like the returned factory dict — namespaced/bare key), looked up per tool inside the build loop and passed to _make_tool_factory. Mirror resource_reader() docstrings (src/neograph/tool.py:336-361) for the new params.

3. NO new public symbol — output_model rides the already-exported mcp_tool_factory/mcp_tool_factories in neograph_mcp/__init__.__all__. No __init__ edit.

4. DE-SHORTCUT example 23: define client output models for BOTH readers.
   - crm_search client model: shape its 'hits' field as list[Deal] (the existing example Deal model) so 'search.typed_result.hits[0]' IS a Deal directly. This DROPS the old line 333 'deal = Deal(**hit)' (which would break — cannot ** a BaseModel once hits[0] is a model).

description:
## Architectural invariant

`src/neograph/testing.py` (640 LOC) and `src/neograph/forward.py` (889 LOC) are audited for the same "canonical helper exists, majority of call sites bypass it" disease pattern that ARCH-3 (`neograph-gf9g`) closed in the runtime IR layer. Every bypass found is migrated, allowlisted, or deferred per the codebase-scan disposition discipline. New helper monopolies discovered in these two files get structural guards with full meta-test coverage. Outcome: either a meaningful LOC reduction (10-20% per file) or a documented finding that "these files are minimum-viable size for what they do."

## Why this is filed (and why it's P3)

Two of the three remaining files >700 LOC (`_construct_validation.py` is the third, addressed in its own ticket). The Jun-2026 sprint closed runtime-layer helper monopolies (ARCH-2/3/4). These two files were OUT OF SCOPE of that sprint but live in the same codebase and may carry the same disease. The audit is preventive — surface the diseases now, fix what's contained, file the rest.

NOT a release blocker. Pure architectural housekeeping.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

For EACH of the two files separately, inventory:

**`testing.py` (640 LOC)** — likely concerns:
- Fake LLM infrastructure (`StructuredFake`, `TextFake`, `ReActFake`)
- Test compile-kwargs builders (`build_test_compile_kwargs`, `build_fake_llm_kwargs`)
- Test-side registries (`register_scripted`, `register_condition`, `register_tool_factory` test helpers)
- Mock state/config builders
- Convenience exports
Output: list of top-level functions/classes, grouped by concern, with LOC per concern.

**`forward.py` (889 LOC)** — likely concerns:
- `ForwardConstruct` base class
- `_Proxy` symbolic-tracer (the heaviest piece)
- `_BranchNode` sentinel
- Path-parse utilities (`out_of_<node>` and similar — MED-02 in synthesis flagged `_Proxy` `out_of_<node>` path parse duplicated at lines 286, 421)
- Loop/if/try tracing
- Compilation hooks
Output: same grouping format.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern (per file): "Inline repetition of logic that should live in a single helper within this file." Specifically scan FOR:

1. **In `testing.py`:**
   - Repeated patterns across `*Fake` classes that should be a base class or mixin
   - Repeated kwarg-bundle construction across `build_*_kwargs` helpers
   - Test-side registry init/clear logic duplicated across test files (cross-file scan)

2. **In `forward.py`:**
   - The MED-02 finding (path-parse duplicated at lines 286, 421) — verify currency, migrate if still present
   - Repeated `_Proxy` attribute access / setattr patterns
   - Repeated tracer-frame construction across `_BranchNode` variants

Both files: cross-reference against `_state_bus.py` / `_ir_normalize.py` / `_oracle.py` patterns. Is there a runtime-layer helper either file could be consuming but isn't (e.g., `snapshot_state`, `output_field_name`, `normalize_outputs.primary`)? Disposition table per finding.

## Phase 2 — Target design

For each file, one of three outcomes:

(a) **Migration plan** — a list of helper monopolies to introduce + MIGRATE rows to apply. Estimated LOC delta. New structural guards required.

(b) **Decomposition plan** — split the file into 2-3 focused modules along the concern lines from Phase 1. Same shape as the `_construct_validation.py` ticket but smaller.

(c) **"Minimum-viable" finding** — document that this file is already as small as it can honestly be. Cite the inventory and explain why each chunk pulls weight. Close the ticket as INFO-ONLY with the analysis attached.

Outcome (c) is acceptable but only after Phase 1b shows zero meaningful disease instances. Don't manufacture work.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + DRY. Iterate until ALL of:

- Every MIGRATE row from Phase 1b is applied OR explicitly DEFERRED with a filed follow-up.
- If decomposition was chosen (outcome b), no new file exceeds 400 LOC.
- New helpers (if any) have ONLY THE NEW SITE'S CALL SITES — no existing call sites left bypassing the helper.
- If outcome (c) was chosen, the bead notes contain a clean rationale-per-chunk that a future maintainer can read.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO collapsing the five fake LLM classes into one branching function (the Jun-2026 architectural review explicitly rejected this — they encode five real LLM contracts).

title: §5: Audit arbitrary_types_allowed=True usage; require per-use justification
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5 (Type and error discipline).

**Problem**: `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` appears on `Node`, `Construct`, `ForwardConstruct`, `Oracle`. Some are justified (`Renderer | None`, `Callable | None`, `_BranchNode` sentinel). Some are habitual.

**Fix**: for each Pydantic model with `arbitrary_types_allowed=True`:
1. Inventory which fields actually need it
2. If the answer is "just one field that's a `Callable`", consider whether the field can be moved off the model (e.g., into a `PrivateAttr` sidecar — the `Node._sidecar` pattern)
3. If `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` stays, add a module-level comment naming each field that requires it and why

**New uses require sign-off** per the spec — but that's a future-process rule, not implementation work for this ticket. The implementation work is auditing today's uses.

**Acceptance**: every `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` in `src/neograph/` is paired with a comment naming the field(s) requiring it. Habitual uses are removed.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §5.

## How to verify

**Test file**: `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestArbitraryTypesJustified` (new test class)
**Test type**: structural-guard, mutation-verified
**What it exercises**: regex-scan `src/neograph/**/*.py` for `arbitrary_types_allowed\s*=\s*True`; for each hit, assert (a) the model is in an explicit ALLOWLIST set inside the test, and (b) the line immediately above or below contains a justification comment (`# arbitrary_types_allowed: field X requires it because ...`). Mutation case: temp module with `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` and no comment, scanner detects, file removed.
**Expected initial state**: failing — current `Node`, `Construct`, `ForwardConstruct`, `Oracle` use it without paired comments.
**Persistence**: stays in suite; new uses require allowlist update + comment.

Order: write the failing structural guard FIRST → run it → must fail → audit, remove habitual uses, add justification comments for the rest → run again → must pass.
