title: Cross-linking capstone: reference-anchor coverage guard — every autolinkable symbol has a rendered heading (turn silent-inert into loud-fail)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: for every symbol the remark-api plugin CAN autolink (present in api-manifest.json with an anchor, per the tiered-confidence rule), the rendered reference page MUST contain exactly one heading whose github-slugger slug == that anchor.

WHY (from Stage-C verification, 2026-07-10): today the plugin declines to emit a link when no matching heading exists (remark-api.mjs:161). That prevents dead anchors — but it ALSO means a prose reference to node/Node/tool/Tool (and any symbol whose reference section is not rendered) SILENTLY stays inert instead of linking. The cross-linking invariant is therefore 'satisfiable but not satisfied': nothing fails loud when a symbol's section is missing. This ticket flips silent-inert -> loud, making full prose->symbol cross-linking a permanent, drift-checked property.

SCOPE: once kec0k/cvjfm/uorb4 render the sections, add a guard (pytest over the parsed reference page + manifest, and/or an Astro-build assertion) that FAILS when any autolinkable manifest symbol lacks a rendered heading with slug==anchor.

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT satisfy the guard by hand-adding headings. The headings must be the manifest-generated ones from kec0k/cvjfm/uorb4 — the guard asserts GENERATION IS COMPLETE (every public symbol has a home), not that a human patched gaps. Scope the autolinkable set to the manifest symbols the plugin actually links (exclude the intentionally-inert bare lowercase tokens); enumerate any deliberate exclusions IN the guard with a reason (self-documenting, like the self-cleaning ignore file).

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for 3my4x
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show 3my4x` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/3my4x/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" 3my4x
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (3my4x)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update 3my4x --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update 3my4x --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/3my4x/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add 3my4x codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/3my4x/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for 3my4x
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on 3my4x
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" 3my4x`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (3my4x)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update 3my4x --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add 3my4x sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for rfl7b
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show rfl7b` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/rfl7b/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" rfl7b
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (rfl7b)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update rfl7b --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update rfl7b --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/rfl7b/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add rfl7b codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/rfl7b/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for rfl7b
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on rfl7b
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" rfl7b`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (rfl7b)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update rfl7b --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add rfl7b sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: _extract_json silently returns inner dict when outer array truncated — zero-artifact pipeline
description:
## What
In `src/neograph/_llm.py::_extract_json`, when input begins with `[` but is truncated before the closing `]` (common with LLM max_tokens cap), the function:
1. Tries array extraction: `_extract_balanced` walks depth, never returns to 0 → returns None
2. Falls back to object extraction: walks text for first balanced `{...}` → returns the FIRST inner dict
3. json_repair parses the inner dict
4. `_parse_json_response` sees `isinstance(parsed, dict)`, applies null defaults, passes to `model_validate_json`
5. Target model (e.g. ClassificationResult{classified_claims: list[...] = default_factory=list}) validates — fields from inner item (claim_id, statement, reasoning, classification) are IGNORED as extras (Pydantic v2 default) → empty list default → VALID empty result

Result: silent zero-artifact output. Caller sees `ClassificationResult(classified_claims=[])`, no exception.

## Repro

```python
from neograph._llm import _parse_json_response
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Item(BaseModel):
    id: str
    value: str

class Result(BaseModel):
    items: list[Item] = Field(default_factory=list)

# Truncated array (no closing ]) — extract_json falls back to first inner {}
truncated = '''[
  {"id": "A", "value": "alpha"},
  {"id": "B", "value": "beta"},
  {"id": "C", "value": "gam'''
r = _parse_json_response(truncated, Result)
assert r.items == []  # BUG: should raise ExecutionError
```

## Why

Production bug in piarch (filed as piarch-{id}): 62-claim classify call hit V3.2 max_tokens=8192, output truncated, NeoGraph returned ClassificationResult(classified_claims=[]). Pipeline silently ran to completion, cost $0.21, created 0 artifacts.

This class of silent failure contradicts the retry contract: when json_mode can't parse valid output matching the schema, it should raise (which _invoke_json_with_retry catches and retries with schema-aware feedback).

## Expectations after delivery

- Truncated arrays raise ExecutionError (or at least the array-to-object fallback is guarded so it only triggers when target model accepts the inner shape).
- Retry mechanism sees the failure, appends schema, LLM corrects to envelope form or smaller response.
- No silent empty-result path for list-valued target models.

## Options

**Option A** (conservative): In `_extract_json`, if the first non-whitespace char is `[` and array extraction fails, do NOT fall back to object extraction — return the raw text and let json_repair handle. If json_repair yields a dict when the target model is list-typed, validation catches it.

**Option B** (strict): In `_parse_json_response`, after extraction + parse, if parsed is a dict AND target model has exactly one required list field AND the parsed dict's keys match that list field's inner-model shape (not the target model's fields), raise ExecutionError ("got inner item, expected envelope with '{field}'").

**Option C**: Compile-time: require bare-array-list-envelope models to declare tolerance via a marker, and log warnings at runtime when the fallback is triggered.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: tests/test_json_mode_truncation.py — truncated array, list-field target → assert raises ExecutionError, not silent empty.

## Acceptance
- Truncated list responses raise ExecutionError (or trigger retry path)
- Existing envelope-parsing tests still pass
- Companion issue in piarch repo references this fix
design:
## Root Cause
_extract_json: when [ comes first and _extract_balanced fails (truncated), falls through to { extraction. Returns the FIRST inner dict object. _parse_json_response sees a dict, applies null defaults, Pydantic validates against target model (extras ignored, list field gets default []).

## Fix (Option A)
When first char is [ and array extraction fails, return text.strip() instead of falling through to object extraction. Let json_repair handle truncation recovery.
notes:
## Reproduction
- test_truncated_array_raises_not_empty_result: FAILS — silent empty Result(items=[])
- test_truncated_array_extract_json_does_not_return_inner_dict: confirms _extract_json returns inner dict
- Root cause: _extract_json line 360-363 falls through to object extraction when array is truncated
## Trace Similar
Only one code path: _extract_json lines 360-363. The fallback from [ to { extraction. No other similar pattern in the codebase.

## Architect Review
- [LOW] Option A (stop fallback to {}) is the right fix. 3-line change.
- [LOW] json_repair handles truncated arrays well — it closes the bracket and parses what it can.
- [LOW] Risk: if json_repair also fails, the retry path fires. Correct behavior.
Overall: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Fixed: truncated arrays recovered by json_repair instead of falling through to inner dict extraction

title: Batch 5b: LangGraph approved types (RetryPolicy/RunnableConfig) — eliminate 5 Any entries from Cluster 10
description:
## Source
- docs/design/architecture-decisions.md §1
- docs/design/any-audit-analysis-2026-05-20.md Cluster 10

## RetryPolicy stability verified

\`langgraph.types.RetryPolicy\` is a stable public export at the pinned LangGraph range (\`>=1.1,<2.0\`). Verified:
- \`from langgraph.types import RetryPolicy\` works
- \`RetryPolicy\` listed in \`dir(langgraph.types)\` (no underscore)
- Same module \`langgraph.types\` is already used elsewhere in src/neograph/ for \`Send\`, \`Command\`, \`interrupt\`

Per §1 ("LangGraph public API is approved"), this is pure tightening.

## Cluster 10: LangGraph approved types declared as Any

**Entries (5)**: \`_wire_oracle:retry_policy\`, \`_wire_each:retry_policy\`, \`_add_each_oracle_fused:retry_policy\`, \`_add_loop_back_edge:retry_policy\`, \`_merge_one_group:config\`.

**Hypothesis**: Four \`retry_policy\` parameters and one \`RunnableConfig\` parameter typed as \`Any\`. The allowlist comments framed RetryPolicy as "LangGraph internal" — verifiably wrong; \`langgraph.types.RetryPolicy\` is public. The \`_merge_one_group:config\` allowlist said "not statically typed at this boundary" — also wrong; every other call site DOES type it as \`RunnableConfig\`.

## Structural fix

```python
from langgraph.types import RetryPolicy
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig  # already in widespread use

def _wire_oracle(..., retry_policy: RetryPolicy | None = None): ...
def _merge_one_group(..., config: RunnableConfig) -> ...: ...
```

5 annotation updates. Trivial.

## How to verify

**Test file**: \`tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoAnyInIRPublicAPIs\` — \`ANY_ALLOWLIST\` shrinks by 5 entries
**Test type**: structural-guard regression
**What it exercises**: existing \`_wiring.py\` tests pass; allowlist shrinks
**Expected initial state**: remove 5 entries from \`ANY_ALLOWLIST\`; guard fails on 5 sites
**Persistence**: stays

Order: remove 5 entries from \`ANY_ALLOWLIST\` FIRST → guard fails → update 5 annotations to \`RetryPolicy | None\` / \`RunnableConfig\` → re-run → passes.

## Acceptance
- \`ANY_ALLOWLIST\` shrinks by 5 entries
- \`_wiring.py\` tests pass
- \`make quality\` green
close_reason: 5 RetryPolicy/RunnableConfig annotations tightened; ANY_ALLOWLIST shrunk by 5 entries

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-2s2o6
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-2s2o6` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-2s2o6/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-2s2o6
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-2s2o6)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2s2o6 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2s2o6 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-2s2o6/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-2s2o6 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

The IR node-tree walk, the LLM-node collection, and the declared-output extraction each have exactly one implementation; consumers call the shared helper rather than re-inlining the recursion or the field-selection.

## Implementation Plan

title: Inline prompt ${var.field} broken after BAML default rendering
description: After neograph-qybn fix, _render_input BAML-renders dict values before _compile_prompt runs. Inline prompts with dotted access (${claim.text}) get getattr on a BAML string instead of a Pydantic model, silently returning empty string. This was already broken WITH a renderer configured, but the fix extended it to the no-renderer default path. Fix options: (A) resolve vars before rendering, (B) render after var substitution, (C) make _resolve_var BAML-aware. Option A is simplest — pass raw input_data to _substitute_vars for inline prompts, then render only the substituted result.
design:
## Root Cause
_render_input (in _dispatch.py) calls render_input which now BAML-renders Pydantic models even when renderer=None (neograph-qybn fix). The rendered dict goes to invoke_structured -> _compile_prompt -> _substitute_vars -> _resolve_var. For dotted paths like seed.text, _resolve_var does getattr(baml_string, 'text') which returns ''.

## Fix Approach
Option A: In _compile_prompt, when the prompt is inline, do var substitution on RAW input_data FIRST, then render. This requires passing raw input through to _compile_prompt alongside rendered input.

Option B: In _dispatch.py ThinkDispatch/ToolDispatch, detect inline prompts and skip rendering, letting _compile_prompt handle everything. Simpler but leaks prompt knowledge into dispatch.

Option C: In _render_input, for inline prompts with dotted vars, defer rendering. Same layer leak as B.

Option D: Render AFTER var substitution. Change _compile_prompt so that for inline prompts, it receives raw data, does var substitution, then renders the final string values. For non-inline (template ref), render first then pass to prompt_compiler.

Recommended: Option D — cleanest separation. _compile_prompt becomes the decision point: inline prompts get raw data + var substitution; template refs get rendered data + prompt_compiler.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_inline_prompts.py::TestInlinePromptThroughFullDispatch::test_dotted_var_resolves_through_full_pipeline
- Root cause confirmed: _render_input BAML-renders dict values, _resolve_var does getattr on string -> ''
- The prompt sent to LLM is 'Judge this claim: ' (empty where field value should be)
- Warning log: prompt_var_missing segment=text var=seed.text
## Trace Similar
Pattern isolated to _resolve_var in inline prompts. Non-inline prompts use prompt_compiler which receives dict values by key — BAML strings are correct for that path. No similar patterns elsewhere.
## Architect Review
Core tension: rendering must happen AFTER var substitution for inline prompts (dotted access needs raw models) but BEFORE prompt_compiler for template refs (compiler expects rendered strings).

Chosen approach: Don't render in _dispatch.py when prompt is inline. Inline prompt path in _resolve_var BAML-renders BaseModel leaf values. Template ref path renders input before calling prompt_compiler.

Implementation:
1. _render_input gains prompt parameter. When _is_inline_prompt(prompt), return raw input_data unchanged.
2. _resolve_var: at the str(obj) step, if obj is a BaseModel, use describe_value instead.
3. No changes to renderers.py (the neograph-qybn fix stays).

Risk: LOW. Only inline prompts are affected. Template ref path unchanged.
Verdict: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Fixed: inline prompts skip rendering, _resolve_var BAML-renders BaseModel leaf values. describe_value promoted to top-level in _llm.py.

design:

## Implementation Plan

Reuse btqzq's existing offline seam and the quick-start 'Complete Example' self-contained pattern (quick-start.mdx:121). Do NOT build new test machinery. Mostly Stage A/C doc edits + one small harness delenv.

1. **Re-label ALL 8 honestly (highest value, do first).** Replace the false 'runs a live-model...' marker on each of the 8 with its real category, mirroring the on-page 'illustrative fragment: references `X`...' convention. This alone corrects btqzq's finding even for snippets that stay skipped.

2. **FIX the 4 cheap forward-ref snippets → self-contained + un-skip:**
   - llm-configuration.mdx:33 — add 'from neograph import compile, node, construct_from_module' + a minimal 1-node @node pipeline + a my_compiler lambda; keep the block compile-only (no run). Factory lambda is never invoked at compile → no LLM.
   - llm-configuration.mdx:54 — either self-contained or rely on page-threading from the now-runnable :33 (same page, later in source order); ensure MODELS/ChatOpenAI/pipeline/my_compiler resolve. Compile-only.
   - retry-semantics.mdx:28 — self-contained: define MODELS + tiny pipeline + my_compiler; compile-only.
   - observability.mdx:120 — stub 'class Report(BaseModel)', 'class Claims(BaseModel)', 'class LangfuseTracer' (with a no-op span() contextmanager) inline; decoration-only, no run.

3. **FIX :186 (observe=True) — requires a 2-line harness change FIRST (TDD-order):**
   a. In tests/test_docs_snippets.py::_seed_offline_llm add LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY + LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY to the delenv set so observe=True is a DETERMINISTIC no-op regardless of ambient env (closes the ImportError-by-env risk).
   b. Then make observability.mdx:186 self-contained: define pipeline, compile+run it with observe=True; runs offline via the fake.

4. **:157 — choose per churn-budget:** either add ONE small self-contained pipeline/graph setup block earlier on observability.mdx and page-thread :157 off it (define langfuse_tracer/my_limiter as plain stub objects passed via config), OR keep it skipped with the honest 'illustrative fragment' reason. Default to keep-skipped-honestly given the task is Low priority; upgrade to FIX only if step 3's setup block already yields a reusable graph.

## Findings

btqzq's research is confirmed: ALL 8 snippets carry a FALSE skip reason. The marker on every one says 'runs a live-model/observability pipeline (needs OPENAI_API_KEY...)', but btqzq's offline seam (_seed_offline_llm) already neutralizes the LLM. The REAL obstacle for each is a forward-reference NameError or a langfuse-extra import — NOT the model. The highest-value correction is honest re-labeling; recovery is a bonus for drift detection.

Two categories of obstacle, per-snippet disposition:

### (a) Forward-reference NameError — RECOVERABLE by a self-contained doc edit
- **llm-configuration.mdx:33** (Simple factory) — undefined: pipeline, compile, my_compiler (MODELS + ChatOpenAI ARE defined in-block). compile() NEVER invokes the factory lambda, so no LLM is reached even when run. FIX (cheap): add compile import + a tiny 1-node pipeline + my_compiler lambda.
- **llm-configuration.mdx:54** (Advanced factory) — undefined: MODELS, ChatOpenAI, pipeline, my_compiler. Compile-only, factory never called. FIX: threads off :33's namespace (page runs blocks in SOURCE ORDER sharing acc) once :33 is un-skipped, or self-contained.
- **retry-semantics.mdx:28** (Layer 1) — undefined: MODELS, pipeline, my_compiler. Compile-only; the with_retry factory is never invoked at compile. FIX self-contained.
- **observability.mdx:120** (@node summarize) — undefined: Report, Claims, LangfuseTracer (annotation-resolution NameError at decoration; get_type_hints). Decoration-only, no run. FIX: stub the 3 classes inline (LangfuseTracer can be a bare 'class LangfuseTracer: ...').
- **observability.mdx:186** (observe=True) — undefined: pipeline. observe=True is a VERIFIED clean no-op offline: runner.py:661/664 gate the langfuse import behind _langfuse_keys_present() (needs BOTH LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY+LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY). run() executes offline via the fake. FIX: define pipeline; ALSO delenv LANGFUSE_* for determinism (see Risks).
- **observability.mdx:157** (config['configurable']) — undefined: run, graph, langfuse_tracer, my_limiter. No langfuse import (langfuse_tracer is just a name/stub). Needs a full compiled graph + run(). RECOVERABLE but higher-churn; recommend page-thread off a single added pipeline/graph block, else keep-skipped honestly.

### (b) langfuse-extra import — MUST STAY SKIPPED (honest reason)
langfuse is the optional [langfuse] extra (pyproject.toml:35), NOT in the dev extra (pyproject.toml:60). Stage D runs 'uv run --extra dev pytest' → langfuse is absent. The per-page threading model has NO per-block importorskip; the ONLY per-block skip is the test-skip marker.

title: 269 Agent Spec tests silently skip under the project's own gate (pyagentspec not in any dev group)
description:
Found during neograph-tjpn4's architect review (atom neograph-dw76v.4, 2026-07-28) and then
verified decisively against a clean environment.

## The seam

269 tests -- the ENTIRE Agent Spec surface -- are `pytest.importorskip("pyagentspec")`-gated
across 14 files, but `pyagentspec` is declared ONLY in `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec`.
It is in neither `[project.optional-dependencies].dev` nor `[dependency-groups].dev`.

Therefore the project's own gate does not run them:
- `make quality` runs bare `uv run pytest -q` -> `[dependency-groups].dev` only -> no pyagentspec.
- The AGENTS.md-documented `uv run --extra dev pytest` -> no pyagentspec either.

Proof (not inference):
```
$ uv run --isolated --extra dev python -c "import importlib.util as u; print(u.find_spec('pyagentspec') is not None)"
Installed 86 packages in 196ms
False
```
The suite passes 3751/3751 on THIS machine only because the local `.venv` retains pyagentspec
from an earlier `--extra agent-spec` run. On a clean checkout the same command reports a green
run with ~269 fewer tests collected -- and nothing announces the difference, because a skipped
importorskip module is not a failure and the collected count is not compared against anything.

## Why it matters beyond bookkeeping

There is NO CI test workflow. `.github/workflows/` contains only `publish.yml`. So the local
gate is the ONLY gate, and the local gate is blind to 269 tests on any environment that has not
happened to install the extra.

Concretely, this bit during neograph-tjpn4: every artifact proving that task's
zero-behaviour-change claim (`test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py` byte-snapshot,
`test_agent_spec_export.py`, `test_agent_spec_matrix.py`, `test_agent_spec_construct_member.py`)
is importorskip-gated. A clean-env run would have landed that migration with its proof never
executed and the gate still green. That is precisely the "single silent seam" the project's
north star names as an existential defect rather than deferrable polish.

The same shape exists for the MCP extras (`importorskip("mcp")` x3,
`importorskip("langchain_mcp_adapters")` x2) -- but that one is DOCUMENTED and deliberate:
AGENTS.md explicitly states "no-key != no extra" and gives the
`uv run --extra dev --extra mcp-examples pytest` command, and the guard that keeps `src/neograph`
MCP-free depends on the extra staying optional. The Agent Spec case has no such documentation and
no such structural reason -- `_agent_spec.py` ships in `src/neograph` and its tests are the
primary proof surface for an actively-developed epic (neograph-s7zt3).

## Options (pick one; they are not equivalent)

1. **Move `pyagentspec` into `[dependency-groups].dev`** (auto-installed by `uv run pytest`),
   mirroring what was already done for `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` and `pytest-examples` --
   both of which have an in-file comment explaining they live there specifically "so the file
   collects under the bare test command". This is the established precedent and the smallest
   change. Keep the `agent-spec` extra as the consumer-facing optional dependency.
2. **Make the skip loud**: a session-scoped conftest check that FAILS (not skips) when a
   pyagentspec-gated module is deselected unless an explicit opt-out env var is set. Preserves
   the optional install but converts silence into noise.
3. **Assert a collected-count floor** in a guard test. Cheapest, but brittle and it does not
   actually run the tests.

Recommendation: (1), with (2) as a follow-up if the optionality must be preserved for packaging
reasons. (1) alone closes the hole for the default gate.

## Acceptance

- `uv run --isolated --extra dev pytest --collect-only -q` collects the SAME number of tests as a
  run with `--extra agent-spec` (i.e. 269 no longer vanish).
- `make quality` on a clean checkout runs the Agent Spec suite.
- AGENTS.md's test-conventions section states the resulting gate command, and says plainly which
  extras are still required for which suites (the MCP note is the model to copy).
- A note in the file(s) explaining WHY the dep sits where it does, matching the
  `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` / `pytest-examples` comment precedent.

title: Typed tool results: tools return models, not strings
description:
Typed tool results: tools return models, not strings. Parent epic for the implementation.

## The problem
_llm.py:367 does result=str(result) — tool returns a Pydantic model but it gets stringified into ToolInteraction.result: str. The original 1bp design says 'tool results should stay typed, renderer converts at the last mile.' The implementation threw away the types at the first mile.

## The fix
1. ToolInteraction gets typed_result: Any = None (keeps result: str for backward compat)
2. invoke_with_tools stores the original object in typed_result, renders with model_dump_json for ToolMessage
3. Downstream nodes receive list[ToolInteraction] with both .result (str) and .typed_result (original model)
4. Tests prove typed_result is preserved end-to-end

## Files affected
- src/neograph/tool.py (ToolInteraction model)
- src/neograph/_llm.py (invoke_with_tools)
- tests/test_pipeline_modes.py (existing tool tests)
- tests/test_composition.py (e2e tests)
- tests/test_fakes.py (ToolInteraction assertions)
notes:
## Lineage

This feature was designed as part of neograph-1bp (Node.outputs refactor epic, now closed). The full design is in neograph-1bp's DESIGN and NOTES fields — multiple design decisions documented:

1. 'Demand-Driven Collection' — tool results collected ONLY when downstream declares dependency
2. 'Renderer Pipeline for Tool Results' — same rendering as any input, describe_type + XmlRenderer/etc
3. 'N Named Outputs' — dict[str, type] mirrors dict[str, type] inputs
4. 'Why NOT Message History' — typed end-to-end, not prose-level ToolMessage strings

The implementation shipped 7 subtasks (1bp.1 through 1bp.7) but the typed tool result part was never completed:
- 1bp.6 collected ToolInteraction but with result=str (stringified)
- The design says 'tool results should stay typed, renderer converts at the last mile'
- The implementation does str(result) at the first mile (_llm.py:367)

This issue completes the original 1bp design — the last missing piece.

Cross-reference: bd show neograph-1bp for full design context (DESIGN + NOTES fields).

title: FR: optional neograph[mcp] DX battery — ship the client-side stitching as a shipped, overridable helper (DefaultPromptCompiler precedent)
description:
## What
Ship an OPTIONAL, consumer-side MCP-client DX battery — a thin `neograph[mcp]` extra (outside the guarded `src/neograph` core) that turns a typed server config into the consumer-owned `tool_factories` + resource-fetcher that `compile()` already accepts. This GRADUATES the client-side stitching demonstrated by the MCP examples (neograph-g4q9/qb7q/3m6g) from copy-me-per-consumer boilerplate into a shipped, overridable helper — following the exact `PromptCompiler` Protocol + `DefaultPromptCompiler` seam-plus-battery precedent already in the codebase.

Sketch (names illustrative — the shape is the proposal, not the identifiers):

```python
# lives in the optional extra (e.g. src/neograph_mcp/ or neograph.contrib.mcp),
# NOT src/neograph — imports langchain-mcp-adapters, so the no-session-ownership
# guard (which scans src/neograph only) stays green, same exemption as mcp-examples.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StdioServer:
    command: str
    args: list[str]
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None

def mcp_tool_factories(
    servers: dict[str, StdioServer | HttpServer],
    *,
    token_provider: Callable[[dict], Awaitable[str] | str] | None = None,  # per-run identity (config["configurable"])
    namespace: bool = True,                                                # ADR §4.5 server::tool namespacing
) -> dict[str, ToolFactory]:
    """Build the {name: async factory} dict for compile(tool_factories=...).
    The MultiServerMCPClient / session is created and OWNED inside the returned
    factories (consumer-held) — never by neograph core. token_provider mints
    per-request auth (httpx.Auth) from config['configurable'] on the arun() path."""

def mcp_resource_fetcher(servers, *, token_provider=None):  # for FromResource(ref=/uri=)
    """Return the mcp_resource_fetcher (+ replayer) callables the consumer drops
    into config['configurable'] so FromResource hydration works out of the box."""
```

The consumer wires MCP in a handful of lines:

```python
factories = mcp_tool_factories({"crm": StdioServer(sys.executable, [".../server.py"])}, token_provider=exchange)
compiled = compile(construct, tool_factories={**graph_factories, **factories})
```

Use the default, or hand-roll your own factory — identical opt-in/override story as `DefaultPromptCompiler`.

## Why
The client-side stitching (MultiServerMCPClient + stdio/http transport config + the token-provider seam → a `tool_factory`) is genuinely consumer-side — g4q9's thesis is correct, it *needs* no framework code. But "needs no framework code" is not the same as "should be re-hand-rolled per consumer." It is IDENTICAL boilerplate across every adopter:
- agent-stark (ADR-0014) is the anticipated **second consumer** and is about to hand-roll exactly this in its `bridge.py::build_tool_factories`; ox-troubleshooting-demo is the first. That is two copies of the same MultiServerMCPClient/token-provider glue, drifting independently.
- The `DefaultPromptCompiler` precedent already settles the philosophy: a prompt compiler also "needs no framework code" (agent-stark in fact overrides it), yet neograph ships a `PromptCompiler` Protocol (seam) + `DefaultPromptCompiler` (battery) so adopters get DX out of the box and override only for house rules. The MCP client wiring is the same shape and deserves the same treatment.
- The examples (g4q9) already build the reference stitching + the `mcp-examples` extra. This FR asks: rather than have every consumer copy the example, expose that stitching as a supported helper the examples themselves consume (dogfood).

Net: a new adopter goes from "read the example, re-derive the MultiServerMCPClient + auth + namespacing glue" to "call `mcp_tool_factories(config)` and pass the result to `compile()`."

## Non-goals / invariant respect (this does NOT reopen nmb2)
- Does NOT move session lifecycle into core. The `MultiServerMCPClient`/`ClientSession` is created and disposed INSIDE the returned factory, which the CONSUMER holds — neograph core never creates/holds/disposes it. The latency + async-cancellation-cleanup surface the nmb2 verdict removed stays removed.
- `src/neograph` stays MCP-free; the battery lives in the optional extra (outside the guard's scan scope), exactly like the `mcp-examples` extra precedent. The no-session-ownership guard stays green.
- The seam is unchanged and already in core: `compile(tool_factories=...)`, the `Tool` spec, `resource_reader`, StructuredTool recognition. This adds only an optional, overridable default on top of that seam.

## Verification
- The g4q9 examples (23/24) are rewritten to CONSUME `mcp_tool_factories` / `mcp_resource_fetcher` instead of inlining the MultiServerMCPClient stitching — proving the helper covers the real selective-binding + FromResource + per-operator-identity + gated-mutation beats end-to-end against the real FastMCP demo server, offline.
- `test_guards_mcp_session_ownership` stays green (helper is in the extra, not `src/neograph`).
- A one-consumer smoke: bind one tool from a stdio server via the helper → compile passes, lint validates the binding, an arun() call succeeds, and swapping the factory for a recorded-real double keeps the fast tier deterministic.
- Extra-gated: `uv run` without the extra imports neograph core with zero MCP deps (skipif in the harness).

## Acceptance
- An optional extra ships `mcp_tool_factories(...)` (+ a resource-fetcher builder) returning consumer-owned factories for `compile(tool_factories=...)`, with a per-run `token_provider` seam and opt-in server::tool namespacing.
- The default is overridable (hand-rolled factory still works) — the `DefaultPromptCompiler` story.
- Examples g4q9/qb7q/3m6g consume the helper (dogfood); `src/neograph` MCP-free; no-session-ownership guard green.
- API shape signed off by the maintainer (this is an FR — the interface is the deliverable to agree first).

## Relationship / provenance
Raised by agent-stark (the ADR-0014 second consumer, task stark-63q.54 — external tool surface → MCP) after mapping the shipped MCP client + FromResource: the "no node rewrite" claim held, doublability held, but each consumer must build the MultiServerMCPClient adapter itself. Builds on / generalizes neograph-g4q9 (shared demo server + mcp-examples extra); would be consumed by the qb7q + 3m6g examples. Maintainer's call given the explicit "client-side stitching needs no framework code" thesis — this FR argues the DX/dedup case for an OPTIONAL battery that honors it.
notes: DONE 2026-07-08 (team run, commit db80b22). MAINTAINER-PENDING DECISIONS TAKEN AUTONOMOUSLY (user away at ask-time; adjust on diff review): (1) PACKAGE LOCATION = separate top-level src/neograph_mcp (second hatch wheel+sdist target), NOT neograph.contrib.mcp -- keeps src/neograph trivially MCP-free (0 imports, guard green) with no lazy-import discipline. (2) Built to the pinned API shape directly rather than proposal-first. API: StdioServer/HttpServer dataclasses; mcp_tool_factories(servers,*,token_provider=,namespace=True,stdio_token_arg='token')->dict[str,ToolFactory]; mcp_resource_fetcher(servers,*,token_provider=)->(fetcher,replayer). ONE deviation from sketch: added stdio_token_arg kwarg (stdio has no headers so identity rides a tool arg; default 'token' matches demo server). nmb2 invariant preserved: MultiServerMCPClient created+owned inside per-superstep factory/fetcher/replayer closures, adapter imports function-local. Guard: session-ownership green + new battery-import assertion (adapter allowed, langgraph/run-layer banned, with non-vacuity slip test). SCOPE: battery+smoke only; examples 23/24 remain qb7q/3m6g. Gates: battery 6 passed (--extra mcp); full suite 2716 passed/2 skipped; mypy+ruff clean on new files.
close_reason: Completed via team run; two per-task commits, all gates green (full suite 2716 passed).

title: R4: replace id(f) shim naming in decorators.py:151 with secrets.token_hex
description:
Per `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2 (compile() reads inputs from kwargs).

**Bug**: `decorators.py:151` generates body-as-merge shim names via `f"_body_merge_{node_label}_{id(f):x}"`. `id()` returns a memory address; addresses are reused across function lifetimes. If a lambda is decorated, garbage collected, and a different lambda is decorated with the same address, both register under the same name in the global registry — the second silently overwrites the first.

**Failure mode**: long-running test sessions with many `@node` decorations of similarly-shaped lambdas can produce cross-test contamination. No test asserts the boundary today.

**Fix**: replace `id(f):x` with `secrets.token_hex(8)`. Shim names need to be unique, not reproducible.

**TDD**: write a failing test that decorates two lambdas in sequence, forces gc of the first, decorates a third lambda, asserts both shims resolve correctly. Verify red (or document that current behavior could fail under address reuse), fix, verify the fix structurally prevents the issue.

**Note**: §2 epic (`neograph-n2li`) closes this transitively — the per-compile `@node` lookup makes `id()` collisions structurally impossible. Ship this first so the bug doesn't survive in the wild while the larger refactor is in flight.

**Source**: `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §2.
close_reason: Replaced id(f):x with secrets.token_hex(8) in decorators.py shim-name generation (body-merge line 151 + interrupt_when line 592); TDD test class TestBodyMergeShimNameUniqueness added in tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py (3 tests, all green). grep 'id(f)' src/neograph/decorators.py returns zero hits. 1707 tests pass.

title: forward: try/except support in forward() tracing
description:
Add `try/except` support to `ForwardConstruct.forward()` tracing. Maps Python exception handling to retry/fallback topology in the compiled StateGraph.

## Context

- Depends on conditional branching (uses the same re-trace / predicate machinery).
- Design: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` — "How control flow maps" (try/except section). Flagged as needing its own design pass; this subtask MUST start with a short design note in `src/neograph/forward.py`'s module docstring explaining the chosen mapping before implementation.

## Files

- `src/neograph/forward.py` — add try-scope recording.
- `src/neograph/compiler.py` — lowering path for try-IR to conditional edges driven by "node raised exception X".
- `tests/test_forward_construct_try_except.py` — new test file.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `try: self.a(x) except SomeError: self.fallback(x)` compiles to a topology where `a` is followed by a conditional edge that routes to `fallback` iff `a` raised `SomeError`.
2. Multiple except clauses work (match order, first-wins).
3. `except Exception:` bare catch works.
4. `try/except/else` works — the `else` branch executes only when no exception was raised.
5. `finally:` works — nodes in `finally` always run regardless of arm.
6. A `try` with no handler for a raised exception re-raises at runtime.
7. A `try` whose body has no Node calls is accepted (traces to empty try-scope, no topology change).

## Out of scope

- Exception chaining (`raise ... from ...`).
- Catching exceptions raised by the framework itself (`ConstructError`, `TracerError`); these bypass user handlers.
- Retry semantics (that's a separate modifier / subtask).

description: Comment documents variants (CONSTANT: any value; FROM_INPUT: bool; MODEL: tuple[type, bool]) but type is object. Access by index (self.payload[0]) with runtime asserts. Proper tagged union via dataclass subclasses or @overload would catch errors at mypy time.
notes:
## Research
### Current state:
- DIBinding.payload: object — 5 construction sites, 4 different value shapes
- resolve() uses isinstance(self.payload, tuple) + self.payload[0] indexing
- Payload semantics: CONSTANT→any, FROM_INPUT/CONFIG→bool(required), MODEL→tuple(type,bool), FROM_STATE→type

### Construction sites (4 files):
1. _di_classify.py:212 — MODEL: payload=(inner_type, required)
2. _di_classify.py:218 — FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG: payload=required (bool)
3. decorators.py:791 — CONSTANT: payload=p.default (any)
4. decorators.py:797 — FROM_STATE: payload=hint (type)
5. _construct_builder.py:353 — CONSTANT: payload=p.default (any)

### Consumers of payload:
1. di.py:152-154 — MODEL: assert isinstance(tuple), payload[0], payload[1]
2. di.py:188 — CONSTANT: return self.payload
3. di.py:193 — FROM_STATE: passed to _unwrap_loop_value as expected_type

### Observation:
- FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG payload is redundant — it's just a copy of self.required
- MODEL payload duplicates (model_cls=inner_type, required=self.required)
- The ONLY payload that carries unique info is CONSTANT (the default value)
- FROM_STATE payload is inner_type (already stored in self.inner_type field!)

### Fix approach:
1. Add model_cls: type | None = None field for MODEL kinds
2. Add default_value: Any = None field for CONSTANT kind
3. Remove payload field
4. Update 5 construction sites + 3 resolve() access sites
5. Core invariant: DI resolution semantics must not change — same values, same errors
## Architect Review
- Risk: LOW. Mechanical replacement of untyped field with typed fields.
- The payload field is redundant for FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG (copies required) and FROM_STATE (copies inner_type).
- Only CONSTANT and MODEL carry unique data.
- Approach: add default_value (for CONSTANT) and model_cls (for MODEL). Drop payload.
- Edge case: lint.py reads DIBinding — check it doesn't access payload.
- Triage: ALL_LOW — straightforward refactor.
close_reason: payload: object replaced with typed default_value + model_cls fields

title: pej0 follow-up: pin typo rejection at invoke_structured/invoke_with_tools dict boundary
description:
Follow-up to neograph-pej0 (commit 1743cca). Reviewer agent flagged that `_coerce_llm_config` accepts raw `dict` at the internal entry points (`invoke_structured`, `invoke_with_tools`, `_get_llm`), routing through `LlmConfig(**...)` which raises on typos. Behavior is correct, but there's no explicit regression test that pins this -- if the dict-acceptance shim ever stops calling `LlmConfig.model_validate`, typos would silently re-enter via the direct-call path.

## Scope

Add explicit regression tests asserting that `invoke_structured(..., llm_config={'max_retires': 5})` raises `pydantic.ValidationError` (or its `ConfigurationError` wrapper, depending on how `_coerce_llm_config` surfaces it).

Repeat for:
- `invoke_with_tools(..., llm_config={...typoed...})`
- `render_prompt(node)` where `node.llm_config` was constructed (somehow) with a typoed dict

## Why this matters

Two layers of typo protection:
1. **Construction-time** (Node/Construct field validation) -- already covered by `test_typo_on_known_field_raises_at_node_construction`.
2. **Direct-call boundary** (when something bypasses Node and calls `invoke_structured` with a dict) -- NOT pinned. If `_coerce_llm_config` is ever 'optimized' to skip validation for performance, the typo hole reopens for direct callers (tests, custom dispatch, future LLM-driven runtime construction paths).

## Tests

- `test_invoke_structured_rejects_dict_with_typo` -- via `tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py` patterns; mock the LLM to never get called; assert raise happens before LLM
- `test_invoke_with_tools_rejects_dict_with_typo` -- analogous
- `test_render_prompt_rejects_dict_with_typo` -- analogous

## Effort

~1 hour. Mostly mechanical -- mirror existing patterns from `TestBudgetExhaustedMessageFallbackPostRnjw` setup.

## Out of scope

Removing dict acceptance entirely from these entry points. That would require migrating internal callers and is its own design decision.
notes:
## Prep (atom 4cf3.5)

Targets: tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py -- add 3 regression tests in TestCallbackProtocols (or new TestDictCoercionTypoRejection class) asserting:
- invoke_structured(llm_config={'max_retires': 5}) raises ValidationError before LLM call
- invoke_with_tools same
- render_prompt(node) raises (or _coerce_llm_config raises directly)

Patterns to mirror: TestBudgetExhaustedMessageFallbackPostRnjw setup + monkeypatch the LLM to never get called.

_coerce_llm_config in _llm.py raises pydantic ValidationError directly (no wrap). Tests assert ValidationError.

For render_prompt -- the typed Node field already rejects typoed dicts at construction. The remaining gap is when render_prompt receives a Node-like with a raw dict llm_config. The render_prompt path coerces via _coerce_llm_config too.
close_reason: 3 regression tests added in tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py::TestDictCoercionTypoRejection: invoke_structured / invoke_with_tools / _coerce_llm_config all reject typoed dicts at the _coerce_llm_config boundary. Tests pin that LLM/tool factory is never reached when a typo is present (called[0] sentinel). Ensures pej0's typo protection holds for the direct-call path even if some future optimization tries to skip validation. 1704 total green; lint+mypy clean.

title: PROC-1 follow-up: decide task-fix.yaml sweep discipline (DEFER from neograph-ruqm)
description:
## Context
Filed as the DEFER disposition from neograph-ruqm (PROC-1) codebase-scan over the dev-practices formulas directory.

## Problem
task-fix.yaml emits PRODUCTION code changes (implement atom) via a 'fix the specific weakness' step, but has NO codebase-scan / sweep-verify gate. It is therefore vulnerable to the exact disease ARCH-SWEEP fights: an executor routes a single instance of a repeated pattern through task-fix and fixes only the motivating site.

## Why DEFER and not MIGRATE-now
Blindly adding codebase-scan + sweep-verify (which mandates a structural guard with meta-tests) would push task-fix from 4N+2 to 6N+2 atoms — nearly task-execute (7N+2) — collapsing the lightweight tier and defeating the formula taxonomy. The correct resolution is a DESIGN decision, not a mechanical atom-paste.

## Options to decide
1. Scope-narrow: add explicit 'Use when ... NOT when the fix is one instance of a repeated pattern — route to task-execute' clause to task-fix description + skill formula-selection table. (cheapest; preserves tiers)
2. Light gate: add codebase-scan ONLY (disposition table, no mandatory structural guard) so task-fix surfaces multi-site patterns and escalates, without the full sweep weight.
3. Deprecate task-fix in favor of task-execute with a 'skip-research' flag.

## Acceptance
- One option chosen with rationale recorded.
- task-fix.yaml and/or the execute skill formula-selection table updated.
- Pushed to agentic-toolkit.
notes:
## Resolved — MIGRATE (not deferred)
Decision: task-fix emits production code -> gets the full sweep discipline. Added codebase-scan (after prep) + sweep-verify (after verify) atoms. Chain: prep -> codebase-scan -> implement -> verify -> sweep-verify -> commit (6N+2). Guard required for repeated patterns; single-instance one-offs record why no guard applies. Committed agentic-toolkit 25ee5cc. Dry-run cooks 8 atoms, gates wired (implement<-codebase-scan, commit<-sweep-verify).

title: ta43 hardening: ConstructLike Protocol + ValidationMode sentinel + producer OrderedDict
description:
P2 architectural hardening from independent review (agentId a8987166183d7be43, confidence 85). The ta43 recursive validator is sound but not best-in-class.

Three improvements:
1. Replace 'cast(Any, item)' at _construct_validation.py:342 with a ConstructLike Protocol in _ir_protocols.py. Eliminates the runtime cast and restores type safety on the recursive call site. Breaks the import cycle structurally rather than via TYPE_CHECKING + cast.
2. Replace 'context_checkable = ambient_producers is not None or construct.input is None' with an explicit ValidationMode enum (STANDALONE vs IN_CONTEXT) OR split into _validate_construct_standalone() and _validate_construct_in_context() functions. The boolean encodes two orthogonal states implicitly.
3. Replace 'list[Producer]' with 'OrderedDict[str, Producer]' keyed by field_name. Drops the O(N²) scan in _check_fan_in_inputs's repeated dict reconstruction; makes the ordering contract explicit at the type level.

Acceptance: structural guard test forbids 'cast(Any' in _construct_validation.py recursive call sites; ValidationMode enum (or split functions) replaces context_checkable; Producer collection changes type; all existing tests still pass.
design:
## Core Invariant
The recursive validator has exactly ONE walker (_validate_node_chain) and ONE producer-side type authority (effective_producer_type); hardening must preserve identical validation behavior across all three API surfaces while removing the runtime cast, naming the validation mode explicitly, and keying producers by field_name — no new validation semantics.

## Implementation Plan
1. RED guard-first: add structural guard in test_guards (cast(Any forbidden at _construct_validation recursive call; ValidationMode present; OrderedDict[str, Producer] used) — fails now.
2. PART 1: add ConstructLike Protocol (name, input, nodes) to _ir_protocols.py; add _is_construct_like TypeGuard; retype _validate_node_chain(construct: ConstructLike); replace inline is_sub_construct + cast(Any) with the TypeGuard. Drop TYPE_CHECKING Construct import if no longer referenced (keep for other Construct-typed helper sigs).
3. PART 2: introduce ValidationMode enum; derive at entry; rewrite context_checkable explicitly.
4. PART 3: producers list -> OrderedDict[str, Producer] across the 6 fns; index directly in _check_fan_in_inputs (drop the per-call rebuild). 
5. GREEN: full make quality (1958+) must pass unchanged; guard passes; mypy clean (no cast, type-safe recursion).
6. Three-surface parity: rely on existing fanin/parity suites; add a focused deep-recursion + many-producer fan-in characterization test if coverage gap found.
notes:
PARTIALLY SUBSUMED. The ConstructLike Protocol part may be addressed naturally by EPIC 1 (which restructures the validator's interaction with Construct). The ValidationMode sentinel and OrderedDict[str,Producer] parts remain standalone hardening; defer until after the three epics land to re-evaluate.
SCOPE CONFIRMED 2026-06-02 (user): proceed with ALL 3 parts. Deferral gate cleared — no validator epics remain open in beads. Re-evaluation findings: Part 1 still live — cast(Any, item) still at _construct_validation.py:342; scaffolding already exists as ConstructItem protocol in _ir_protocols.py (NOTE: named ConstructItem, not ConstructLike as ticket says) but NOT wired into the recursive call site. Part 1 = wire ConstructItem into the recursive call + remove cast(Any). Parts 2/3 (ValidationMode enum-or-split, OrderedDict[str,Producer]) proceed as written. Structural guard must forbid 'cast(Any' at recursive call sites in _construct_validation.py.
## Findings (2026-06-02)
PART 1 (cast(Any) -> Protocol): _construct_validation.py already imports ConstructItem (line 28, aliased NodeItem) and uses it on the per-item helpers. The remaining cast is at line 342: recursive _validate_node_chain(cast(Any, item)). Root cause: _validate_node_chain is typed (construct: Construct) but the recursion passes 'item' (a ConstructItem from construct.nodes), and ConstructItem lacks .input/.nodes. Fix: add a richer ConstructLike Protocol to _ir_protocols.py declaring the attrs the walker reads off a construct (name, input, nodes); retype _validate_node_chain(construct: ConstructLike); replace the inline is_sub_construct bool + cast with a TypeGuard '_is_construct_like(item) -> TypeGuard[ConstructLike]' so narrowing is type-safe with NO cast. Construct satisfies ConstructLike structurally (called from construct.py:158).

PART 2 (ValidationMode): context_checkable = 'ambient_producers is not None or construct.input is None' conflates (a) called in-context vs standalone with (b) is-this-a-subconstruct-boundary. Fix: ValidationMode enum {STANDALONE, IN_CONTEXT} derived from ambient_producers at entry; context_checkable = mode is IN_CONTEXT or construct.input is None (orthogonality now explicit/named).

PART 3 (OrderedDict producers): producers: list[Producer] threaded through 6 fns. O(N^2): _check_fan_in_inputs rebuilds 'producer_by_name = {p.field_name: ... for p in producers}' every call. Switch to OrderedDict[str, Producer] keyed by field_name. field_names are unique within a chain's LOCAL producers (dict-form keys distinct via output_field_name; single output via field_name_for; SUBGRAPH_INPUT port) so no info loss. _check_* helpers only ever receive LOCAL producers (ambient is used only for context checks + recursion in _validate_node_chain). Edit sites: append->assign, 'for p in producers'->'.values()', '{p.field_name for p}'->set(producers), ambient+local list-concat -> {**ambient, **local}.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py: Producer (38), _validate_node_chain (253, cast at 342, context_checkable 313), _check_item_input (514), _check_fan_in_inputs (587, O(N^2) at 614), _check_each_path (669), _build_no_producer_error (859), _suggest_hint (886)
- src/neograph/_ir_protocols.py: add ConstructLike beside ConstructItem
- entry: construct.py:158 _validate_node_chain(self) with real Construct

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Behavior-preserving refactor: full suite (1958) is the safety net. Three-surface parity covered by existing TestThreeSurfaceFanInParity + test_fanin_validation.
- TypeGuard import: typing.TypeGuard (3.10+) — confirm Python floor. Use typing_extensions if needed.
- Don't change _check_* to receive ambient — keep current local-only contract.
## Architect Review (2026-06-02)
- [LOW] ConstructLike attrs: declare name: str, input: Any, nodes: Sequence[ConstructItem]. Use Sequence (covariant) not list (invariant) so Construct.nodes (list[Node|Construct|_BranchNode]) assigns cleanly. Do NOT mark runtime_checkable — narrowing is via the _is_construct_like TypeGuard (manual getattr), never isinstance(ConstructLike), so no runtime overhead.
- [LOW] Retype the internal walk helpers (_check_item_input, _check_fan_in_inputs, _check_each_path, _build_no_producer_error) construct param to ConstructLike too — they only read construct.name. This lets the TYPE_CHECKING 'from neograph.construct import Construct' import be kept ONLY for validate_loop_construct (separate entry), removing Construct reliance from the walker chain entirely. Resolves the import-cycle structurally (ticket goal).
- [LOW] _BranchNode is a ConstructItem but not construct-like (no .input/.nodes); the TypeGuard returns False for it, exactly matching today's is_sub_construct guard. No behavior change.
- [LOW] TypeGuard: typing.TypeGuard OK (requires-python >=3.11). assert_never already used in this codebase, so modern typing is in-house style.
- [MEDIUM] Behavior-preservation is the whole risk surface. Mitigation: the change introduces ZERO new validation semantics; the 1958-test suite + TestThreeSurfaceFanInParity + test_fanin_validation are the regression net. If ANY existing test changes outcome, revert — that means a semantic drift, a Core-Invariant violation. Add one focused deep-recursion + many-producer characterization test only if a coverage gap is found.

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM is a process discipline, resolvable autonomously via the existing suite).
## Triage (2026-06-02)
Verdict ALL_LOW. Proceeding to write-test (guard-first) then implement. No refine/user-input needed.
## Write-test RED (2026-06-02)
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py::TestValidatorHardening — 4 guard-first tests, all FAIL: no-cast(Any), ValidationMode enum exists, OrderedDict[str,Producer] (not list[Producer]), ConstructLike Protocol exists.
- Behavioral safety net: existing test_context_validation.py already has test_depth_3_typo_rejected/happy + test_depth_4_typo_rejected (recursion) + TestThreeSurfaceFanInParity (test_fanin_validation) — refactor must keep all 1958 green. No new characterization test needed.
## Implement GREEN (2026-06-02)
PART 1: added ConstructLike Protocol (name/input/output + read-only 'nodes' property for covariance) to _ir_protocols.py + _is_construct_like TypeGuard in _construct_validation.py. Retyped _validate_node_chain + the 4 walk helpers to ConstructLike. Recursive call now passes the TypeGuard-narrowed item — cast(Any) GONE. TYPE_CHECKING Construct import kept only for validate_loop_construct.
PART 2: ValidationMode{STANDALONE,IN_CONTEXT} enum derived at entry; context_checkable rewritten as 'mode is IN_CONTEXT or construct.input is None' (orthogonality explicit).
PART 3: producers list[Producer] -> ProducerMap = OrderedDict[str, Producer] across all 6 fns; append->keyed assign; iterations ->.values()/set(producers); ambient merge via dict update. _check_fan_in_inputs no longer rebuilds producer_by_name per call (O(N^2) drop) — indexes 'producers' directly.
- Guard TestValidatorHardening: 4/4 pass. make quality: 1962 passed (1958+4), 0 failed; ruff clean; mypy clean (no cast, type-safe recursion). All existing validation/fanin/context/parity tests unchanged -> invariant held, zero semantic drift.
- mypy variance fix: ConstructLike.nodes is a read-only @property (covariant) so Construct.nodes: list[...] satisfies Sequence[ConstructItem].
