title: ARCH: loader.py:230 auto-fan-in assigns raw prev_node.outputs as input type (dict-form upstream mismatch)
description: Found by neograph-my84 codebase disease scan (DEFER row). loader.py:230 (_load_construct auto-inputs wiring) sets inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs for each prior node in a YAML sub-construct. When prev_node.outputs is dict-form, this (a) assigns a dict where a single type is expected (same class as neograph-my84 part 1), AND (b) keys the fan-in entry by prev_field, but a dict-form producer registers per-key fields prev_field_{key} (the base prev_field is not itself a producer). So normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary alone is insufficient — the KEY must also map to the per-key producer field (output_field_name(prev_field, primary_key)). Needs its own analysis + a should_fail/should_pass fixture for a dict-form upstream in a YAML sub-construct. Deferred from neograph-my84 (which scopes to forward.py + the 4 primary-field micro-pattern sites) because this requires validator-wiring semantics verification beyond a .primary swap. Low confidence any current YAML pipeline hits dict-form sub-construct auto-wiring.
design:
## Core Invariant
Sub-construct auto-fan-in must wire each upstream producer to the EXACT state-bus field the validator registers, via the monopolized normalize_outputs/primary_output_field helpers -- so a dict-form producer maps to {prev}_{primary_key}: primary_type, never the raw outputs dict at the base field.

## Fix Approach
loader.py:230 -> inputs_dict[primary_output_field(prev_field, prev_node.outputs)] = normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary. Import both from neograph._normalize. Behavior-preserving for single-type (the only YAML-reachable form today); correct for dict-form. Test via direct _build_sub_construct call with a synthesized dict-form node (YAML cannot express dict-form outputs).
notes:
## Findings
- loader.py:227-231 (_build_sub_construct auto-fan-in): for each prior node in a YAML sub-construct it does inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs. Two defects when prev_node.outputs is dict-form:
  (a) assigns the raw dict where a single type is expected;
  (b) keys by the BASE prev_field, but the validator registers a dict-form producer ONLY at output_field_name(prev_field, key) (per-key), never the base field -> fan-in finds no producer.
- REACHABILITY: NodeSpec.outputs is typed `str` (_spec_schema.py:84) and _build_node sets outputs = lookup_type(str) (loader.py:175) -> a YAML-spec node can NEVER have dict-form outputs. So this branch is currently UNREACHABLE via load_spec. The bug is latent/defensive (confirms the ticket DEFER note). No current YAML pipeline can hit it.
- Validator producer registration (_construct_validation.py:195-208): dict-form Node -> producers[output_field_name(field, key)] per key; single-type/Construct -> producers[field]. Fan-in (_check_fan_in_inputs) looks up producers by the inputs-dict KEY. So the auto-wired key MUST equal the registered producer field.
- Monopolized helpers (_normalize.py): normalize_outputs(outputs).primary = primary type (single type for both forms); primary_output_field(base, outputs) = base for single-type, output_field_name(base, primary_key) for dict-form. These already exist and are the single source of truth.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/loader.py:226-231 -- the buggy auto-fan-in assignment (fix site).
- src/neograph/_normalize.py:58-125 -- normalize_outputs / primary_output_field (use these).
- src/neograph/naming.py:12 -- output_field_name(base, key).
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:188-220 -- producer registration (per-key for dict-form).
- src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:84 -- NodeSpec.outputs: str (reachability root cause).
- tests/test_spec_loader.py -- spec-loader test patterns (~26 tests).

## Fix shape
Replace inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs with:
  inputs_dict[primary_output_field(prev_field, prev_node.outputs)] = normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary
Behavior-IDENTICAL for single-type (primary_output_field->prev_field, primary->the type); correct for dict-form.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Cannot write a pure-YAML should_fail/should_pass (NodeSpec.outputs is str). The test must drive _build_sub_construct directly with a synthesized all_nodes containing a dict-form-output Node -> assert the later node`s inputs wires {SUBGRAPH_INPUT: input, output_field_name(prev, key): primary} and the Construct compiles. RED before (raw dict / wrong key -> ConstructError), GREEN after.
- Keep auto-wiring to the PRIMARY output only (matches single-type heuristic); secondary dict keys are not auto-exposed.
- Three-surface parity: this is loader-only (YAML surface); declarative/@node/programmatic do not auto-wire inputs, so parity N/A here (note in test).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-z3ie)
Disease: fan-in / producer-field auto-wiring that uses raw Node.outputs instead of the monopolized primary_output_field (field name) + normalize_outputs(...).primary (type). Drift here mismatches the per-key producer fields the validator registers for dict-form outputs.

Scan command (SYNTACTIC + manual classification; small, no fan-out):
  grep -rnE "\.outputs\b" src/neograph/ | (exclude _normalize/_declared_output/primary_output_field/docstrings)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | loader.py:230 | inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs (auto-fan-in) | MIGRATE | THE bug; fix uses primary_output_field + .primary |
| 2 | _wiring.py:324 | output_model = node.outputs (oracle merge arg) | ALLOWLIST | passed to _merge_variants/invoke_structured which normalize dict-form internally (first key = primary) |
| 3 | compiler.py:512 | make_oracle_merge_fn(..., node.outputs, ...) | ALLOWLIST | merge fn normalizes internally (CLAUDE.md) |
| 4 | _validation_modifiers.py:41,119 | output_type = node.outputs (modifier validation) | ALLOWLIST | validation reads raw type; effective_producer_type handles modifier effects |
| 5 | _ir_normalize.py:72,170 | state builder per-key + gen-type compare | ALLOWLIST | builder already emits {base}_{key} per dict key (correct); :170 is oracle gen-type inference, not fan-in |
| 6 | _dispatch.py:261 | docstring/gen-type override | ALLOWLIST | not fan-in wiring |

Only loader.py:230 is the fan-in-field disease. neograph-my84 already swept forward.py + the 4 primary-field micro-pattern sites and DEFERRED this one (this ticket). No DEFER rows remain after this fix.
SYNTACTIC -> single grep + manual classification sufficient; no multi-agent fan-out, so .claude/code-review/neograph-z3ie/ not required.
## Architect Review (neograph-z3ie)
Inline review (well-bounded loader-internal fix; validator-wiring semantics verified by direct code reads).

1. Root cause correctness [LOW]: confirmed -- validator registers dict-form producers only at output_field_name(field,key); loader keyed fan-in by base field + assigned raw dict. Both wrong for dict-form.
2. Fix minimality [LOW]: one-line swap to primary_output_field(prev_field, outputs) -> normalize_outputs(outputs).primary. Imports from _normalize (the monopoly module). Behavior-IDENTICAL for single-type (the only YAML-reachable form). Aligns with neograph-my84 micro-pattern cleanup.
3. Regression risk [LOW]: single-type path bit-identical; dict-form path is currently unreachable via YAML (NodeSpec.outputs: str). Full suite + a focused unit test guard it.
4. Architecture compliance [LOW]: enforces the documented monopoly (no raw .outputs for producer-field/primary selection; use normalize_outputs/primary_output_field). Reduces drift class that caused neograph-8k3/ayq.
5. Similar-bug scalability [LOW]: disease-scan shows loader.py:230 is the LAST fan-in-field site using raw .outputs; others normalize internally.
6. Test coverage [MEDIUM->LOW]: YAML cannot express dict-form outputs, so the test drives _build_sub_construct directly with a synthesized dict-form Node (RED: raw dict at wrong key -> ConstructError; GREEN: {prev}_{key}: primary, compiles). Also add a single-type _build_sub_construct test asserting behavior-unchanged.

Design decisions confirmed:
- Wire PRIMARY output only (matches single-type heuristic; secondary keys like tool_log are framework-collected, not auto-exposed). Per ticket.
- Do NOT extend NodeSpec.outputs to dict-form (out of scope; gated on protocol widening per neograph-8cqd S9.4). The fix is defensive/consistency, valuable regardless of current reachability.

VERDICT: ALL_LOW -> proceed to write-test + implement.
## Write-test (TDD red)
- tests/test_spec_loader.py::TestSubConstructAutoFanInDictForm::test_dict_form_upstream_wires_primary_per_key_field -- RED: ConstructError "declares inputs[prev]={result,log} but no upstream named prev; available: neo_subgraph_input, prev_log, prev_result". Confirms both defects (raw dict + wrong base-field key).
- test_single_type_upstream_wiring_unchanged -- GREEN now (behavior-preservation guard for the single-type path; must stay green after fix).
Drives _build_sub_construct directly with a synthesized dict-form Node (YAML cannot express dict-form). Loader-only surface; three-surface parity N/A (noted in test docstring).
## Implement (TDD green)
loader.py:226-231 -> uses neograph._normalize.primary_output_field + normalize_outputs(...).primary:
  producer_field = primary_output_field(prev_field, prev_node.outputs)
  inputs_dict[producer_field] = normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary
Dict-form test GREEN (was RED); single-type guard stays GREEN. Full gate: 2126 passed, ruff + mypy clean.
Two guards fired during implement (resolved): TestNoTicketIdsInComments (removed (neograph-z3ie) from the src comment) and ruff import-order (auto-fixed _normalize import position).
## Sweep Verification (neograph-z3ie)
Re-scan command: grep -rnE "\.outputs\b" src/neograph/ (+ manual fan-in-field classification)
Pre-fix fan-in-field instances: 1; Post-fix: 0.

| # | Phase 1b content | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|------------------|-------------|----------------|----------|
| 1 | loader.py: inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs | MIGRATE | now primary_output_field(prev_field, outputs) + normalize_outputs(outputs).primary | YES |
| 2 | _wiring.py:324 output_model = node.outputs | ALLOWLIST | unchanged; merge path normalizes internally (false-positive reason holds) | YES |
| 3 | compiler.py:512 make_oracle_merge_fn(..., node.outputs) | ALLOWLIST | unchanged; merge fn normalizes internally | YES |
| 4 | _validation_modifiers.py:41,119 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged; raw type read for modifier validation | YES |
| 5 | _ir_normalize.py:72,170 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged; per-key state builder + gen-type compare | YES |

## Structural Guard
- File: tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py
- Class: TestNoRawOutputsInFanInWiring
- AST-based (regex-free): bans SUBSCRIPT assignment whose value is `<expr>.outputs` across all src/neograph/*.py (the fan-in disease signature: inputs_dict[k] = node.outputs). Legitimate raw reads (plain `x = node.outputs`, call args) are not flagged.
- Meta-tests: positive (d[k]=node.outputs flagged); negative (normalize_outputs(...).primary not flagged); negative (plain assign + call-arg not flagged).
- All 4 pass; real-src scan green post-fix. Class-level guard -> catches the pattern in ANY future src module, not just loader.py.

title: structured output strategy: no re-prompt retry on Pydantic ValidationError (parity with json_mode)
description:
_llm_dispatch._call_structured (and _acall_structured): the 'structured' strategy handles Parsed|Raw|Failed with DSML recovery, but has NO re-prompt retry when the provider returns structurally-valid JSON that fails Pydantic model validation (a schema/constraint violation). json_mode routes through _invoke_json_with_retry(max_retries=...) and re-prompts; structured surfaces the ValidationError and kills the node/round.

This bites on providers whose constrained-decode does NOT truly enforce the schema (e.g. z-ai/glm-5.1 via OpenRouter): ~13% of structured agent-node calls emit an output that fails validation. Observed in ox-troubleshooting-demo GLM full-corpus run: 5 round-fatal ValidationErrors across HypothesisSet, Evidence, RoundState, Diagnosis (all output_strategy=structured), each failing a cascade scenario that would otherwise pass. Errors seen: 'ExecutionError: Validation failed for RoundState', 'ValidationError: 1 validation error for {HypothesisSet,Evidence,Diagnosis}'.

Ask: give the structured path the same bounded re-prompt-on-ValidationError retry json_mode has (honor max_retries; feed the validation error back as a repair hint), so a single weakly-enforced structured decode doesn't fail the whole node. Consumers currently work around it by switching hot nodes to json_mode, losing constrained-decode's guarantees on well-behaved providers.
notes:
2026-07-08 MAINTAINER-SIDE ANALYSIS (claims verified against develop HEAD). CONFIRMED: ValidationError from a weakly-enforced constrained decode surfaces as Failed(error=ValidationError) from the compat adapter chain (_llm_structured_compat.py:153,164 — the decorators catch validation exc and wrap); the structured strategy's Failed arm raises immediately with NO retry, while json_mode routes through _invoke_json_with_retry's bounded re-prompt loop (_llm_retry.py:292, honoring max_retries; LlmConfig.max_retries exists at _llm_config.py:44). The machinery for parity EXISTS — the structured path just never engages it for validation failures.

TWO SITES to cover (both bitten by the consumer): (1) the think-mode primary structured path (invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured -> adapter chain -> Failed handling in _llm.py) and (2) the agent-mode structured fallback (_call_structured/_acall_structured Failed arms, _llm_dispatch.py:129 + async twin). Fix at the SHARED seam so both inherit — post-ykun the error builders are already module-level; the retry loop must follow the same extract-then-thin discipline (a structured-flavored bounded retry pair sharing a pure repair-hint-message builder with the existing DSML/json retry builders in _llm_retry — do NOT re-inline the loop per twin; TWIN_TABLE + thinness guard apply).

FIX SHAPE: on Failed(error=ValidationError) (discriminate: retry ONLY validation failures — TypeError/provider-rejection Failed arms keep their current handling), re-invoke the SAME structured adapter with the validation error appended as a repair-hint message (the model sees what constraint it violated), bounded by cfg.max_retries; after exhaustion raise the existing ExecutionError with attempts count in the message. Constrained decode stays engaged on retries (that is the point — keep structured guarantees on well-behaved providers, repair on weak ones). Zero behavior change for Parsed-on-first-try and for json_mode/text.

TESTS: fake emitting invalid-then-valid structured results (StructuredFakeWithRaw sequence or a Failed-then-Parsed adapter fake) — assert exactly one re-prompt, repair hint present in the retry messages, max_retries honored (exhaustion -> ExecutionError), sync+async cells for BOTH sites (think primary + agent fallback), first-try-Parsed makes zero extra calls. Consumer scenario pin: an agent node with output_strategy=structured surviving a single weak decode.

WAVE PLACEMENT: Wave 9 FOURTH SEAT — region (_llm.py/_llm_dispatch.py/_llm_retry.py/compat + tests/modes) is disjoint from 12dc (errors.py/di.py), hhlr (_run_cache/runner), fdyy (_dispatch.py carrier/guards). Gated on y5ux and blocks m0tv (reformat stays last).
close_reason: Already shipped as 'structured retry parity' (commit 8722666) — _call_structured now re-prompts on Failed(ValidationError) bounded by max_retries. Verified in the installed editable neograph; the ox-demo agent nodes reverted to structured to use it. Duplicate of shipped work.

title: izo1-B: Migrate 24 .get() call sites — 8 REQUIRED to get_required, 16 OPTIONAL annotated
description:
## Context

Second of 4 subtasks under epic neograph-izo1. izo1-A established `get_required` and `StateMissingError`. This subtask audits and migrates every existing `.get()` call site on a StateBus-typed expression to either `.get_required(...)` (the REQUIRED 8) or `.get(key, default)` with a `# StateBus.get optional: <reason>` comment (the OPTIONAL 16).

This is the bulk of izo1's work hours; mostly mechanical but each site requires reading to verify classification.

## Source of truth

- `docs/design/state-bus-required-getter-2026-05-20.md` Section 1 (per-site classification table) + Section 4 step 2 (migration plan with line numbers)
- `docs/design/architecture-decisions.md` §7

## Scope

### EDIT (per the audit doc, by file)
- `src/neograph/_input_shape.py`
- `src/neograph/_execute.py`
- `src/neograph/_wiring.py`
- `src/neograph/_oracle.py`
- `src/neograph/_subconstruct.py`
- `src/neograph/_state_write.py`

### DO NOT TOUCH
- `src/neograph/_state_bus.py` (izo1-A handled it)
- `src/neograph/errors.py` (izo1-A handled it)
- Validator (`_construct_validation.py`) — izo1-C
- Structural guard (`tests/test_structural_guards.py`) — izo1-D
- Tests not affected by the migration (only test fix-out IF Phase E exposure surfaces)

## The 24 call sites

Per the audit doc Section 1, classified by sub-category:

**8 REQUIRED** — switch to `.get_required(key, node_label=node.name)` so missing → raise:
The exact file:line for these is in the audit doc. Read each site, confirm REQUIRED classification still holds, apply migration.

**16 OPTIONAL** — keep `.get(key, default)` and add `# StateBus.get optional: <reason>` comment:
- 5 sites: `OPTIONAL-loop-bootstrap` ("loop counter not yet initialized on first entry")
- 4 sites: `OPTIONAL-framework` ("framework-internal field; not present until first run")
- 4 sites: `OPTIONAL-loop-counter` ("loop counter; absent → treat as 0 before first iteration")
- 1 site: `OPTIONAL-context` ("context forwarding to sub-construct; absent → no parent context")
- 2 sites: per audit (specific reasons in research doc)

## Implementation

Walk the audit doc Section 1 file-by-file:

1. Open file
2. Locate each `.get()` site by line number from the audit doc
3. Apply the verdict (REQUIRED → migration, OPTIONAL → annotation)
4. Run the file's tests after each cluster (2-3 sites at a time)

```bash
uv run pytest tests/modes/ tests/modifiers/ -x 2>&1 | tail -10
```

If any existing test starts failing, enter Phase E triage (see below).

## Phase E — Test fix-out (included in this subtask)

Existing tests may rely on silent-None for fields now classified REQUIRED. When a test starts raising `StateMissingError`, triage:
- **Was masking a bug?** → fix the test fixture/pipeline so the required field is populated
- **Legitimately optional?** → the audit miscategorized this site; reclassify as OPTIONAL with a comment and document the reclassification
- **Unclear?** → flag in the bd ticket notes and surface to maintainer before proceeding

Estimated 5-10 tests may need attention; could be zero.

## How to verify

**Test file**: existing tests across `tests/modes/`, `tests/modifiers/`, `tests/test_validation.py` — they cover the touched code paths
**Test type**: regression — no new tests written in this subtask; the existing surface IS the contract
**What it exercises**: every REQUIRED migration is a fail-loud upgrade; every OPTIONAL site stays silent-by-justification

**Expected initial state**: zero new test failures EXCEPT in Phase E cases (genuine bugs masking; document and fix the fixture, not the code)

**Persistence**: migration is permanent; OPTIONAL annotations stay as code documentation

Order:
1. Apply REQUIRED migrations file-by-file (2-3 at a time)
2. Run that file's tests; Phase E if needed
3. Apply OPTIONAL annotations (same file)
4. Re-run
5. Move to next file
6. After all 6 files done, run `make quality`

## Acceptance

- 8 REQUIRED call sites use `.get_required(key, node_label=node.name)` (or equivalent context)
- 16 OPTIONAL call sites carry `# StateBus.get optional: <reason>` comments with the categorized reason
- Any tests requiring fix-out resolved per Phase E triage
- `make quality 2>&1 | grep -E "passed|failed|error"` green
- Live `_execute.py:46` bug becomes either: (a) `_extract_context` now uses `.get_required` and fails loud OR (b) still uses `.get` but izo1-C will close the door at compile time. Pick whichever fits the call site better.

## Effort

~3h + 0-2h contingent Phase E = 3-5h.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **izo1-A** (needs `get_required` to exist)

## Out of scope

- `StateMissingError` subclass (izo1-A)
- Validator tightening for node.context (izo1-C)
- Structural guard preventing future `.get()` regressions (izo1-D)

  _input_shape.py:60(#3), 96(#5), 106(#6), 109(#7), 124(#8)
  _execute.py:46(#9)

description:
Follow-up to stark-h46 (shipped 0.7.2). The spec addendum framed the gap as '_is_stringly_null coerces scalar Optional inner types but not list/BaseModel inner types'. Empirically that framing is WRONG on main@0.7.2: _is_stringly_null already returns True for list[str]|None, list[Model]|None, and Model|None, so the DIRECT top-level cases ({"langs":"null"} where langs: list[str]|None) already coerce to None and pass.

The ACTUAL incompleteness is in the RECURSION DESCENT of _apply_null_defaults (src/neograph/_llm_retry.py:161). It only recurses into a nested model when isinstance(annotation, type) and issubclass(annotation, BaseModel), and into list items only when get_origin(annotation) is list. When the field is Optional-wrapped -- parent: Company|None or products: list[Product]|None -- the annotation is a Union, so BOTH recursion branches are skipped and stringly-null sentinels on the INTERIOR fields never get normalized.

Empirically confirmed failing on main@0.7.2:
- {"parent": {"langs": "null"}} where parent: Company|None -> ValidationError list_type (interior never reached)
- {"products": [{"price": "null"}]} where products: list[Product]|None -> ValidationError int_parsing (interior never reached)

Passing already (regression-guard, must stay green): direct top-level list[X]|None / list[Model]|None / Model|None = 'null'; nested inside NON-optional list[Model]; legit list/model values preserved; non-Optional 'null' still fails loud.

Fix: teach the two recursion branches to see through the Optional wrapper -- unwrap Union-with-None to the single inner type before the BaseModel / list-origin checks. Centralize the 'inner model type of this annotation' derivation so scalar/optional-scalar/model/optional-model/list-of-model/optional-list-of-model are all driven by one annotation walker rather than the current inline hand-rolled introspection (the reason the Optional cases were missed).

Also: chaos/Hypothesis property test across random Optional/list/nested topologies asserting no bare pydantic crash on stringly-null and no destruction of legit values. Review for wrong-layer plumbing (inline type introspection in _llm_retry that duplicates the type-structure walking centralized elsewhere).

Worktree: ../neograph-073 on branch fix/stringly-null-containers off main. Target release 0.7.3.
notes:
FIXED in worktree ../neograph-073 (branch fix/stringly-null-containers).

Root cause (empirically pinned, spec framing corrected): _is_stringly_null ALREADY returned True for direct list[X]|None / list[Model]|None / Model|None on main@0.7.2, so the direct top-level cases the spec named already worked. The real defect was the RECURSION DESCENT in _apply_null_defaults, which hand-enumerated only two container shapes (bare BaseModel field, bare list[BaseModel]) and silently skipped every other shape. Confirmed-failing shapes on main: Optional-wrapped model (Company|None), Optional-wrapped list-of-models (list[Product]|None), dict-of-models (dict[str,Product]), list-of-optional-models (list[Product|None]).

Fix: replaced the per-shape branch list with ONE recursive shape classifier -- _unwrap_optional (peels a single X|None) + _descend_null_defaults (dispatches on runtime value: model dict -> recurse; list[...] -> recurse each element; dict[K,V] -> recurse each value; re-peels Optional at every level). Kills the whole missing-shape bug family, not just the 2 spec cases. tuple[...] intentionally out of scope (LLM structured output doesn't emit heterogeneous tuples).

Layer verdict: NOT wrong-module -- _apply_null_defaults correctly lives on the LLM-JSON-repair axis in _llm_retry.py; reusing the IR-layer _validation_types walker would be a layer violation. The defect was wrong-SHAPE plumbing (hand-enumeration) not wrong-layer. Single-caller (only _parse_json_response), no parallel normalizer, so no three-surface/DRY duplication.

Tests: 5 deterministic regressions in TestParseJsonResponseLenientParsing (optional-model, optional-list-of-models, dict-of-models, list-of-optional-models, legit-preservation) + Hypothesis TestStringlyNullChaosAcrossTopologies (200 examples x 2 props over randomized Optional/list/dict/optional-element topologies). Mutation-verified all 6 descent tests fail without the fix. Guards updated: allowed-names (+_unwrap_optional,+_descend_null_defaults), line budget 615->665, version sync. Full suite 3078 passed. Bumped to 0.7.3 + CHANGELOG.
close_reason: Fixed via shape-driven descent (_unwrap_optional + _descend_null_defaults). Merged to main (ef6bed5), tagged v0.7.3, publish workflow triggered. Full suite 3078 passed.

title: Propagate RunnableConfig into tool .invoke in the ReAct loop (astream_events tool visibility)
description:
## What
neograph's agent/ReAct loop invokes tools WITHOUT the run's RunnableConfig: _agent_cycle.py:346 tool_fn.invoke(tc['args']) and :397 await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args']) — no config=config. Pass the node's config through so LangChain callbacks propagate and on_tool_start/on_tool_end appear in the compiled graph's astream_events.
## Why
Consumers (agent-stark) build live activity feeds over astream_events; today tool calls are invisible at the event stream (only the LLM/node events fire), so a UI can't show 'agent called search_graph(...)' live without scraping state. Relates to neograph-q8ec (custom stream events) — same goal, different mechanism.
## Verify
Integration: an agent node with a tool; drive compiled.astream_events(version='v2'); assert on_tool_start/on_tool_end fire with the tool name + args + result. Both sync and async tool paths.
## Acceptance
- tool .invoke/.ainvoke receive the node RunnableConfig; on_tool_start/end visible via astream_events; existing tool-loop tests green.
notes:
Fixed: threaded node RunnableConfig into tool execution at both agent-cycle call sites in src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py — tools_body line 351 (tool_fn.invoke(tc['args'], config=config)) and atools_body line 402 (await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args'], config=config)). _tool_loop.py did NOT need the fix: it no longer contains a tool-execution site (tool exec was moved into the agent cycle bodies); its .invoke/.ainvoke calls are all LLM calls via _CoercingToolWrapper. Verified only these two sites execute tools via grep.

TDD: tests/test_agent_tool_config_propagation.py (new, 3 tests). Core regression = config-capturing tool asserting the tool receives a non-None config at BOTH sync (run/graph.invoke) and async (graph.ainvoke) call sites — both RED before the fix (captured config was None), GREEN after. NOTE: an astream_events(v2) on_tool_start/on_tool_end assertion was NOT a valid RED test on its own — langchain_core 1.4.0 propagates callbacks via the var_child_runnable_config contextvar, so a real StructuredTool already fires those events without explicit config=. The explicit config= is still the documented-correct fix (contextvar propagation is fragile across thread/executor/context boundaries). Kept one astream_events test as an end-to-end visibility check.

Fake fallout (expected, reported): passing config= broke tool fakes whose invoke(self, args) had no config kwarg (real LangChain BaseTools accept config; the fakes modeled the old config-less contract). Updated FakeTool (tests/fakes.py) + inline tool fakes in tests/test_hitl.py, test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py, test_tool_gating.py, test_lint.py, test_composition.py, test_guards_ir_compiler.py, tests/modes/test_output_strategies.py, test_llm_internals.py to accept config=None, **kwargs. Consistent with the test_guards_async_fakes.py guard (ainvoke delegates to invoke).

Gates: ruff clean (src/ tests/). tests/modes/ + tests/ -k 'tool or agent or react' = 176 passed. New test file 3/3 pass. Full suite: 2389 passed, 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this task (test_guards_any_audit::test_no_bare_stdlib_raises flags modifiers.py:420/:495 bare ValueError — foreign uncommitted working-tree changes from a parallel agent; not touched by this task, passes on clean HEAD).
close_reason: Fixed: config=config threaded into both tool-exec sites in _agent_cycle.py; on_tool_start/end now visible via astream_events. Fakes + example tools updated to the real BaseTool config signature. Landed 89b063c. Follow-on: fixed the example-tool regressions (02/10/13/14) in the same commit.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-9epk
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-9epk` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-9epk/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-9epk
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-9epk)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-9epk --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-9epk --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-9epk/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-9epk codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-9epk/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Write regression test for neograph-9epk

- The AST/source-text BAN above does NOT apply — it bans source scans

title: Sweep verification for neograph-9epk
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-9epk
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-9epk`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-9epk)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-9epk --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-9epk sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-z3ie
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-z3ie` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-z3ie/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-z3ie
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out:
     - Pattern grep: `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`
     - AST scan: `python -c "import ast; ..."` for syntactic patterns
     - Dual-name search: `git grep -E '_(is)?_?instance_safe'`

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-z3ie)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-z3ie --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-z3ie --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-z3ie/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-z3ie codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-z3ie/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in

title: ForwardConstruct parity RATCHET is tautological — REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES derives from the corpus it checks (no teeth)
description:
## Invariant the ratchet is supposed to enforce
A declarative capability that ships WITHOUT a forward() parity twin must FAIL LOUD (the 'parity ratchet' — e9zse's permanent anti-drift guard). A silently-deleted parity row must also fail loud.

## The defect (confirmed 2026-07-11, adversarial verify of e9zse + reconfirmed directly)
tests/test_forward_parity.py:766: REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS) — the 'required' set is DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS IT CHECKS. test_every_required_capability_has_a_corpus_row (:798) then computes covered = {row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS} and asserts REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES - covered == empty. Both sides come from the SAME list, so the difference is ALWAYS empty — tautological. The module docstring claims the opposite contract ('a new declarative capability is added here FIRST; the coverage test fails loud until its forward() twin row lands') but that intent is not realized.

PROOF (verifier, reverted): commenting out the loop_in_loop corpus row dropped the file to 19 passed and TestParityRatchet stayed 3 passed GREEN — a load-bearing parity twin silently deleted with ZERO ratchet response. It is weaker than even a hardcoded assert len(rows) >= N (which would at least catch a deletion).

## Scope / impact
NOT a correctness defect in the shipped feature: the IR-equality helper assert_ir_identical (:169-229) is genuinely DEEP (verified — catches Each key/over/on_error, Loop when-identity/max_iterations/on_exhaust, Oracle params+hook identity, Operator.when, boundary ports, recursive nesting; three valid-IR mutation probes each went RED). The rows that EXIST enforce IR-identity for real. The hole is ONLY in the forward-looking guard: future declarative capabilities can ship without a forward() twin, and existing twins can be deleted, with no failure.

## Fix (anti-band-aid: the ratchet must have an INDEPENDENT source of truth)
REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES must NOT be derived from PARITY_CORPUS. Two options:
  A. Hardcoded independent frozenset of capability names — adding a name without a corpus row fails; deleting a row fails. Minimal.
  B. (Preferred) ENUMERATE the declarative modifier/composition surface from neograph itself — the modifier classes (Each, Loop, Oracle, Operator) + composition capabilities (sub-construct nesting, fan-in, multi-output dict, branch/cap) — and assert each maps to >=1 covered corpus row. This makes a NEW declarative modifier that lacks a forward() twin fail loud automatically (the ratchet's actual stated purpose), and is the real 'parity ratchet' the epic promised.

## Guard-first / TDD
1. Failing test FIRST: delete/comment a corpus row (or add a REQUIRED capability with no row) -> the ratchet must go RED. Verify it currently stays GREEN (the bug).
2. Implement independent enumeration until the deletion/omission is caught.
3. Meta-test: assert the ratchet itself is non-tautological (e.g. REQUIRED source is not ).

## Acceptance
- Deleting any corpus row -> ratchet RED.
- A declarative modifier/capability with no forward() twin -> ratchet RED (mutation-proven).
- The self-referential derivation is gone; independence pinned by a meta-test.

Found in the e9zse post-ship adversarial verification (7/8 claims CONFIRMED; this was the one REFUTED). Design context: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md ('permanent guard = a property test ... so a new declarative capability lacking a forward() path FAILS LOUD (the parity ratchet)') — that promised guard is the thing this bug says is not yet real.
design:
## Root Cause
REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS) — both sides of test_every_required_capability_has_a_corpus_row come from the same list; deletion of a row or shipping a capability without a twin can never fail.

## Fix Approach (post-review, final)
1. Replace derivation with a HARDCODED literal frozenset of the 14 capability names. Change the coverage test to assert set EQUALITY (covered == REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES) so a deleted row AND an unregistered new row both fail loud.
2. Surface-enumeration ratchet: required modifier types = {r.mod_type for r in neograph.modifiers._SLOT_RULES} (the production registration table — NOT Modifier.__subclasses__, which is process-global and pollutable). Exercised types = walk every PARITY_CORPUS row's declarative_nodes() IR recursively (Node/Construct .modifier_set slots, recurse into Construct.nodes), collect type(mod) per occupied slot. Assert required <= exercised.
3. Meta-guard already landed (RED): AST check that REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES assignment does not reference PARITY_CORPUS.
4. Mutation proofs (transient, reverted): (a) comment out loop_in_loop row -> equality test RED; (b) simulate a new modifier in _SLOT_RULES (or drop a row so a modifier loses sole coverage) -> enumeration test RED.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_forward_parity.py::TestParityRatchet::test_required_capabilities_is_independent_of_corpus (structural meta-guard — the bug is a structural disease of the ratchet itself, no behavioral repro exists per execute-skill structural-disease clause)
- Verified RED: 1 failed, 3 passed — REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES assignment AST references PARITY_CORPUS
- Root cause: test_forward_parity.py:766 derives REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES via comprehension over PARITY_CORPUS, so the coverage test compares the corpus to itself — always empty diff, zero teeth.
## Trace-similar (atom 3)
Pattern category: self-referential coverage ratchet (required-set derived from the corpus it validates).
Searched: all derived frozensets over test collections (grep 'frozenset(...for...' + REQUIRED_/EXPECTED_/coverage-set guards).
- test_guards_api_manifest.py:_DI_KIND_NAMES derives from neograph.di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS (production source, checked against lint()'s actual emissions) — two INDEPENDENT sources, not tautological.
- api-manifest coverage authority (_autolinkable) checks manifest vs plugin regex literals vs enumerated exclusions — independent sources.
- test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:250 frozenset is a local AST comparison, not a ratchet.
VERDICT: test_forward_parity.py:766 is the only instance of the disease. No new beads filed.
## Codebase Disease Scan (zrcln)

Pattern: a coverage/ratchet 'required' set built by comprehension over the SAME collection the coverage assertion checks (tautological self-derivation).
Scan commands (reproducible):
  grep -rnE '(frozenset|set)\(\s*[a-z_]*\.?[a-z_]+ for ' tests/ src/neograph/ --include='*.py'
  grep -rnE '\{ *[a-zA-Z_.]+(\[[^]]+\])? for [a-z_]+ in [A-Z_]+' tests/ src/neograph/ --include='*.py'
Total instances found: 1 (of 14 comprehension hits, 13 compare against an INDEPENDENT source)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | tests/test_forward_parity.py:766 (+ :799 consumer) | REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS) | MIGRATE | The motivating bug — required set and covered set share one source |
| 2 | tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:431 | _DI_KIND_NAMES from di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS | ALLOWLIST | Derived from PRODUCTION source, checked against lint() emissions — independent sides |
| 3 | tests/test_di.py:49,61,607 | {k.value for k in DIKind} vs hardcoded expected | ALLOWLIST | Enum vs literal expected set — independent |
| 4 | remaining hits (guards_examples:528, guards_ir_compiler:435, guards_llm_runtime:472, fanout_oracle before/after) | filesystem/registry snapshots | ALLOWLIST | Snapshot-vs-snapshot or fs-vs-manifest comparisons, not self-derived ratchets |

## Architect review (atom 5, inline)

1. Root cause correctness: CONFIRMED (HIGH confidence). :766 derivation makes :798's set-difference structurally empty; mutation proof in the ticket (deleted loop_in_loop row stayed GREEN).
2. Fix minimality: OK. Both parts (hardcoded literal set with EQUALITY assertion + surface-enumeration ratchet) are required by the acceptance criteria — the literal set alone cannot make a NEW modifier fail loud.
3. Regression risk: test-only change, zero production surface. ONE finding:
   - MEDIUM: plan proposed Modifier.__subclasses__() for surface enumeration. __subclasses__() is process-global — any test module defining a throwaway Modifier subclass would pollute the required set and flake. RESOLUTION (incorporated): enumerate from modifiers._SLOT_RULES ({r.mod_type for r in _SLOT_RULES}) — the production registration table every |-appliable modifier MUST join (with_modifier raises for unknown types). Independent of the corpus, stable, and a new modifier lands there by construction.
4. Architecture compliance: OK — matches guard-first convention; AST source-scan is sanctioned for structural-disease guards (existing test_guards_* precedent).
5. Similar-bug scalability: LOW — disease scan found exactly 1 instance; a codebase-wide anti-tautology guard is not warranted for n=1. The AST meta-guard pins this file permanently.
6. Test coverage sufficiency: OK — fix atom must mutation-prove both directions (comment out a corpus row -> RED via equality; register a fake _SlotRule/modifier -> RED via enumeration) and revert.

Findings: 1 MEDIUM (resolved in-plan, design updated), 1 LOW (no action). VERDICT: ALL_LOW after incorporation — proceed to fix.
## Fix (atom 7)
tests/test_forward_parity.py only (+93/-1):
1. REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES: derivation replaced with a hardcoded literal frozenset of the 14 capability names (independence documented in-comment).
2. test_every_required_capability_has_a_corpus_row: now also asserts covered - REQUIRED == empty (set EQUALITY) — an unregistered new row fails loud too.
3. NEW test_every_slot_rule_modifier_is_exercised_by_corpus: required modifier types from production modifiers._SLOT_RULES; exercised types collected by recursive IR walk over every corpus row's declarative_nodes() modifier_set slots; asserts required <= exercised.
4. Meta-guard test_required_capabilities_is_independent_of_corpus (from repro atom): AST-verifies the assignment references no PARITY_CORPUS.

title: Checkpoint resume does not work — graph restarts from beginning despite existing checkpoint
description:
## Problem
When a pipeline crashes and is rerun with the same thread_id and SqliteSaver checkpoint DB, LangGraph should resume from the last completed superstep. Instead, it restarts from the beginning (all scripted + research nodes re-execute).

## Evidence
Run 1ba5bff6: runner detects existing checkpoint DB, logs 'resume', but execution starts from read-graph-context (the first node) instead of write-overview (the crash point).

## LangGraph behavior
Per LangGraph docs, calling graph.invoke(input, config={'configurable': {'thread_id': 'same-id'}}) with the same thread_id and existing checkpoints should automatically resume. NeoGraph's run() wraps this but may interfere.

## Suspects
1. NeoGraph run() re-injects input fields into config via _inject_input_to_config — this might cause LangGraph to see it as a new execution
2. The input dict might differ between runs (e.g., different object IDs for Pydantic models) causing LangGraph to treat it as a new thread
3. NeoGraph's compile() might produce a different graph ID between runs

## Expected
Rerun with same thread_id + checkpoint DB should skip all completed nodes and resume from the failed one.
design:
## Fix
1. Remove the ValueError guard when both input and resume are None
2. When input=None and resume=None: call graph.invoke(None, config=config) — LangGraph resumes from checkpoint
3. Keep _inject_input_to_config for the input= path (new execution)
4. File separate bug for _neo_input persistence across process restarts
5. Add test: compile with MemorySaver, run halfway, run again with input=None + same thread_id → resumes
notes:
## Reproduce: CONFIRMED

### Root cause
run() always passes input dict to graph.invoke(). LangGraph's _first() method (pregel/_loop.py:633) checks is_resuming = self.input is None or input_is_command or run_id matches. When input is a dict, all three are False → LangGraph starts fresh.

### Why Operator resume works
resume= passes Command(resume=...) → input_is_command=True → is_resuming=True

### Fix
Option B (cleanest): When input=None and resume=None and config has thread_id, pass None to graph.invoke(). Remove the ValueError guard. 'No input + existing thread = resume from checkpoint.'

### Secondary issue
_neo_input DI stash is in-memory only. Won't survive process restarts. Needs to be persisted in checkpoint metadata. File as separate bug.

### Core invariant
run(graph, input=None, config={'configurable': {'thread_id': X}}) with existing checkpoints must resume, not restart.
## Reopened (2026-04-13)

Still not resuming. Two consecutive runs:
- logs/66ce18fd.jsonl: killed mid-run at brainstorm-extensions (step 35)
- logs/5d2070c2.jsonl: rerun — logs 'neograph_uc_develop_resume' but starts from read-graph-context (step 0)

Both have same thread_id 'neo-uc-develop-BR-UC-001'. SqliteSaver checkpoint DB exists at .derive-ensemble/checkpoints/neo-uc-develop-BR-UC-001.db between runs.

The scripted nodes (read-graph-context through read-draft) complete in <1s so they LOOK like they're replaying, but the research Oracle x3 nodes re-execute full LLM calls (50+ minutes), proving no checkpoint resume.
## Reproducible test case (2026-04-13)

```python
"""Minimal reproduction: checkpoint resume after crash.

Run this script. It should:
1. First run: execute node-a, node-b, crash at node-c
2. Second run: skip node-a and node-b, resume from node-c
"""
import sqlite3
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
from neograph import node, construct_from_functions, compile as neo_compile, run


call_log = []


@node(outputs=str)
def node_a() -> str:
    call_log.append("a")
    return "result-a"


@node(outputs=str)
def node_b(node_a: str) -> str:
    call_log.append("b")
    return f"result-b({node_a})"


crash_count = 0


@node(outputs=str)
def node_c(node_b: str) -> str:
    global crash_count
    call_log.append("c")
    crash_count += 1
    if crash_count == 1:
        raise RuntimeError("Simulated crash on first attempt")
    return f"result-c({node_b})"


construct = construct_from_functions("test-resume", [node_a, node_b, node_c])

db_path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "checkpoint.db"
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "test-thread-1"}}

# Run 1: should crash at node_c
print("=== Run 1 (should crash at node_c) ===")
call_log.clear()
with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(str(db_path)) as checkpointer:
    graph = neo_compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer)
    try:
        run(graph, input={}, config=config)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Crashed as expected: {e}")
    print(f"Nodes called: {call_log}")
    assert "a" in call_log and "b" in call_log and "c" in call_log, "All nodes should have been called"

# Run 2: should resume from node_c (skip a, b)
print("\n=== Run 2 (should resume, skip a and b) ===")
call_log.clear()
with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(str(db_path)) as checkpointer:
    graph = neo_compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer)
    result = run(graph, input={}, config=config)
    print(f"Nodes called: {call_log}")
    print(f"Result: {result}")

if "a" in call_log or "b" in call_log:
    print("\n❌ FAIL: node_a or node_b were re-executed — checkpoint resume not working")
else:
    print("\n✅ PASS: only node_c re-executed — checkpoint resume works")
```

Output:
Run 1: crashes at node_c as expected (a, b, c all called)
Run 2: a, b, c ALL re-called — checkpoint not honored

Expected Run 2: only c called (a and b skipped from checkpoint)

Same SqliteSaver DB file, same thread_id, same compiled graph.
LangGraph docs say invoke() with same thread_id should auto-resume.
close_reason: Fixed for real: _has_existing_checkpoint detects saved state, routes to invoke(None) for resume while keeping input in config for DI. Test passes with input={} on resume.

title: neograph check: support get_known_template_vars() in --setup module
description:
## What

Extend the `--setup` module contract for `neograph check` with a third
optional function: `get_known_template_vars() -> set[str]` that returns
the bridge-supplied template variable names. Mirror the existing
`get_template_resolver()` pattern.

Today the setup module exports up to 2 functions:
- `get_check_config() -> dict`
- `get_template_resolver() -> Callable[[str], str | None]`

Proposed: add a third, loaded by `__main__._load_known_template_vars()`:
- `get_known_template_vars() -> set[str]`

When present, its return value is merged with (or replaces) the
`--known-vars` CLI flag's set.

## Why

Consumers with non-trivial bridges (piarch's neograph_bridge) synthesize
template vars that aren't @node inputs:

- Standard vars: `json_schema`, `node_id`, `project_root`, `domain_briefing`,
  `max_tool_calls`
- Legacy aliases: `research_packet` (from `explore_tool_log`)
- Context flattening for match-verify (`id_allowlist`, `claim_id`,
  `claim_statement`, etc. flattened from `neo_subgraph_input` view models
  via bridge-side context flattening — invisible to lint)

Today piarch has to pass:

    --known-vars domain_briefing,max_tool_calls,id_allowlist,claim_id,
      claim_statement,claim_classification,context_quote,bm25_candidates,
      research_packet,json_schema

Every time, on a Makefile line, in CI, etc. That list doesn't belong on a
command line — it belongs in Python next to the bridge code with comments
explaining each entry.

## Expectations after delivery

- `--setup` module may optionally export `get_known_template_vars()`.
- If present, the function is called and its return (coerced to `set[str]`)
  is used as `known_template_vars` in `lint()`.
- If both `--known-vars` CLI and `get_known_template_vars()` are supplied,
  their union is used.
- If neither is supplied, behavior unchanged (no known vars).
- Consumer code stays as a single Python module, not split across
  CLI flags + setup module.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/test_cli.py::test_known_template_vars_from_setup_module`
— write a fake setup module exporting both `get_check_config()` and
`get_known_template_vars()`. Run `cmd_check()` without `--known-vars`.
Assert the vars from `get_known_template_vars()` suppress placeholder
errors for those names.

**Integration**: same test file — setup module exports both, and user
also passes `--known-vars`. Assert the union is used (CLI vars + module
vars).

**E2E**: piarch's `scripts/neograph_check_config.py` adds
`get_known_template_vars()` returning the 10 bridge-supplied vars. Running
`neograph check src/derive_ensemble/constructs/rw_ingestion.py --setup
scripts/neograph_check_config.py` (without `--known-vars` on CLI) shows
warnings but no errors — same result as today's `--known-vars` flag.

## Acceptance

- `__main__._load_known_template_vars()` implemented, mirroring
  `_load_template_resolver()`.
- Called in `cmd_check()`, merged with `--known-vars` CLI flag (union).
- `cmd_check()` passes the merged set to `lint(known_template_vars=...)`.
- CLI `--known-vars` flag continues to work standalone.
- Setup module with only `get_check_config()` continues to work (no
  regression).
- Documented in the lint skill / neograph check help.
close_reason: --setup module now supports get_known_template_vars(). Merged with --known-vars CLI flag (union).

title: _add_subgraph has no Each×Oracle fusion path for Constructs
description: In compiler.py _add_subgraph(), when a Construct has both Oracle and Each modifiers (Construct | Oracle(...) | Each(...)), the 'if oracle:' branch fires first and handles it as pure Oracle — the Each modifier is silently ignored. Compare with _add_node_to_graph() which has an explicit 'if oracle and each:' check (line 305) that routes to _add_each_oracle_fused(). There is no equivalent Each×Oracle fusion implementation for Constructs. Confirmed with live test: Construct with [Oracle, Each] modifiers compiles a graph with only Oracle merge nodes and no Each barrier nodes. Options: (1) implement fusion for Constructs, or (2) reject the combination at __or__ time with a clear error. Given the complexity of M×N fusion on sub-constructs, option 2 is safer.
close_reason: Fixed: clear CompileError instead of silent drop
